# EB Scripting Guide

The EB docs in one file, for an AI helper that writes EB scripts: For AI helpers, Quick start, Helper scripts, Instances, Fights, Quests, Tasks, Crew and group, Nav and travel, Combat and cast stacks, Items, merchants and broker, Harvesting, Loot, Dialogs, UI windows, Events, Settings, every tested example in full, and the reference (the complete scripts, the Lua library, the TLOs and the console commands). Built from the EB website's docs and EB's reference of 2026-11-25.

Repository: https://github.com/Jiimboeq2/EB-Docs. This file: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jiimboeq2/EB-Docs/main/EB_Scripting_Guide.md. The website: https://eb.jiimbo.dev/docs.html.

## How to use this file

- A helper script is one Lua 5.4 file in InnerSpace's `Scripts` folder, run by ISXLUA beside EB for InnerSpace: `lua <name>` starts it, `endlua <name>` stops it. It hands EB the line you would type after `eb`, once per decision and 40 words at most: `IS.Execute("luacall EBISX_cmd all pause")`.
- Never attach an event that can bring more than 42 arguments (`EBISX_QuestUpdate`, never `EQ2_onQuestUpdate`; `EBISX_State2`, never `EBISX_State`). A handler only queues; the main loop works and waits (`wait`, `waitframe`), and reads the game in few batched reads (several `${...}` in one `IS.Parse` are one read).
- Let EB do the walking (`walk x,y,z`, `marks go <mark>`, `goto <zone>`): EB moves a character only on the zone's mesh.
- Use only what this file lists: its commands, functions, events and TLO members. A complete script runs as it is. A snippet shows its script, then how it was tested: the offline stand-in for the game and the checks exist only on EB's test world, so a real script leaves them out, and any line of the script that uses `DOCS`, `w.` or `a.` too.
- Give the player each file with the place it goes, the line that starts it and what it needs.
- Read [For AI helpers](#for-ai-helpers) first: it is the whole of these rules, with the reasons.

## For AI helpers

Give your AI helper all of EB in one file, ask for the script you want in the right shape, and check what it wrote before you run it.

### For AI helpers: What this page is for

An AI helper (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot or any other) can write an EB script for you, if it knows EB. Out of the box it does not, so it guesses: it makes up functions, borrows another bot's commands, moves the character with its own code, waits the wrong way, or reads the game every frame.

This page fixes that. Give your AI the files below, ask in the shape this page shows, and check what it wrote before you trust it.

#### The short version

1. Give your AI the whole guide in one file, [EB_Scripting_Guide.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jiimboeq2/EB-Docs/main/EB_Scripting_Guide.md): paste it into its instructions, attach it, or give it the link ([how](#for-ai-helpers-give-your-ai-everything)).
2. Copy [the prompt](#for-ai-helpers-how-to-ask), fill in your setup and what you want, and send it.
3. Check what it wrote, [step by step](#for-ai-helpers-check-what-your-ai-wrote-step-by-step): on one box, in a quiet spot, with the stop line ready.
4. When something is off, send it the script and the exact console lines, and ask for the smallest fix.

#### First: which kind of script

EB runs three kinds of script of your own. Each has its own folder, its own start line and its own tools, and the tools never mix. Tell your AI which kind you want, or ask it to pick the smallest kind that does the job.

| Kind | What it is | Where it goes, and how it starts | Its tools |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EB Script | A Lua file for EB's Scripts window. Its header lines (`-- ebscript …`) become options, buttons and pages. It runs inside EB, in a sandbox, on both EB builds. | The `scripts` folder in EB's data folder. `eb script run <Name>`, `eb script stop <Name>`. | The `script` object only: `script.me()`, `script.eb(line, who)`, `script.wait(seconds)` and the rest of [rule 3](#for-ai-helpers-the-rules-every-eb-script-follows). |
| Helper | A Lua file beside EB, run by ISXLUA in its own Lua state. EB for InnerSpace only. | InnerSpace's `Scripts` folder. `lua <name>`, `endlua <name>`. | `IS.Parse` to read, `IS.Execute` to act, `IS.AttachEvent` to listen, `echo` and `wait`; it talks to EB with `luacall EBISX_cmd <line>`. |
| Data file | An instance (`instance.lua` and its `encounters/`) or a quest pack. Pure data: it only returns a table, and EB runs it. | Your own folders in EB's folder: `data/ebic/authored/instances/<folder>/` (`eb ic run authored/<folder>`) and `data/ebquests/authored/` (`eb ql start <quest>`). | None: `return { schema = "eb.ic/1", … }` or `return { schema = "eb-quest/1", … }`. |

The [Lua library](#lua-library) is a fourth thing, and not a kind you write: it is EB's own code. Its examples show EB's modules at work on an offline stand-in for the game. An EB Script cannot load them, and a helper loads only the few that read no game ([the library at a glance](#for-ai-helpers-the-eb-library-at-a-glance)).

The [Scripts](#scripts) page has the tested complete scripts. EB's Scripts window has the shipped EB Script examples: Hello EB, Ability Board, My First Page, Kit Tour, File Tools, Health Watch, My First Test and Reads Check.

### For AI helpers: Give your AI everything

The more of EB your AI has, the less it guesses. Give it the guide every time, and the rest when the job needs it.

| Give it | Where | What is in it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The whole guide | [EB_Scripting_Guide.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jiimboeq2/EB-Docs/main/EB_Scripting_Guide.md) (raw, one file) | The whole of these docs as one Markdown file: the three kinds, the rules, the commands, the game reads, the events and the file places. Give it first, every time. |
| The git repo | [EB-Docs on GitHub](https://github.com/Jiimboeq2/EB-Docs) | The guide, plus `commands.md` (every console command EB ships), `examples/` (every tested example as its own `.lua` file, with a header that says where it goes and how it runs; `examples/README.md` lists them) and `reference/lua_api.json`. Clone it for an assistant that works in a folder. |
| The site's AI files | [llms.txt](https://eb.jiimbo.dev/llms.txt) and [llms-full.txt](https://eb.jiimbo.dev/llms-full.txt), at this site's root | `llms.txt` is a short map of these docs with a link to each page, the file AI tools look for on a site. `llms-full.txt` is all of the docs in one plain text file. |
| The full reference | [assets/lua_api.json](https://eb.jiimbo.dev/assets/lua_api.json) on this site, or [reference/lua_api.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jiimboeq2/EB-Docs/main/reference/lua_api.json) in the repo | Every module and function of the Lua library, every TLO and member, and every tested example with its exact code. Nearly 3 MB: give it to an assistant that can search a file (a project, a code editor). It is too big to paste into a chat. |
| The commands | [commands.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jiimboeq2/EB-Docs/main/commands.md) (raw), or the [Commands](#commands) page | Every command EB ships, grouped, with the words it takes and the crew words it accepts. |
| One tested example | For example [examples/script-bagwatch.lua](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jiimboeq2/EB-Docs/main/examples/script-bagwatch.lua) (raw) | The tested script closest to what you want, as a model ([pick one](#for-ai-helpers-how-to-ask)). Each file is named by its example id. |
| The EB Scripts guide | `EB_Scripts_Guide.txt` in your EB folder, at `data/eb/scripts/examples` | The guide EB ships with its Scripts window: the header, the fifteen option kinds, the `script` object, pages and their 44 parts. Its section 18 is written for AI helpers. Give it too when you want an EB Script. |

#### How to give it to your assistant

- **As standing instructions.** Most assistants have a place that every chat in it reads first: a project's files or instructions, a custom assistant, a rules file in a code editor. Put `EB_Scripting_Guide.md` there once, and every chat there starts with EB's facts.
- **As an attached file.** Open the raw link, save the file, and attach it to your first message with [the prompt](#for-ai-helpers-how-to-ask).
- **As a link.** An assistant that can open web pages reads the raw link itself. Ask it first to list the three kinds of EB script, so you know it read the file. When it cannot open links, attach the file instead.
- **In a code editor.** Clone the repo (`git clone https://github.com/Jiimboeq2/EB-Docs`) next to your scripts, and point the editor's assistant at it. It can then search the whole reference and every example.

- Start a new chat for a new script, with the guide in it. A long chat drifts away from EB's facts.
- The files are made again when EB changes. Give your AI the current copy, not one you saved months ago.
- Nothing here needs your account, your characters or your PC's folders. Never paste a password, a character name or a full folder path into a chat: put a made-up name in its place.

### For AI helpers: How to ask

Copy this prompt, fill in the brackets, and send it with the guide. It tells your AI what you run, what you want, and the rules it must keep.

The prompt:

```
Read this first, all of it: the EB guide for AI helpers, in one file:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jiimboeq2/EB-Docs/main/EB_Scripting_Guide.md
(If you cannot open links, say so, and I will attach the file or paste it below this prompt.)

You are helping me write a script for EB, a Lua bot for EverQuest II. Use ONLY what that guide and the files I give you list: EB's commands, its Lua functions, the game members in its TLO reference, its events and its file places. If what I want needs something that is not there, tell me plainly and stop. Never invent a function, a command, a game member, an event, a setting or a file.

MY SETUP
- EB build: [EB for InnerSpace | EB Boxer (NON-ISX)]
- What eb version answered: [paste]
- The first line of eb status: [paste]
- EB's console word on my PC: [eb | ebi]
- Server type: [live | TLE] (no server name)
- The character it is for: class [for example warden], level [..], role [tank | healer | dps | support]
- My crew: [how many] boxes, sessions [is1, is2 ...]; the tank is [isN]; the box I play by hand is [isN | none]
- Where it should run: [this box only | my group | every box]

WHAT I WANT
- In one sentence: when [this happens], [this box | the crew] should [do this].
- When it should stop by itself: [...]
- What it must never do: [...]
- The kind of script: [a helper beside EB: one .lua file in InnerSpace's Scripts folder, started with lua <name> | an EB Script for EB's Scripts window: -- ebscript header lines and the script object | an instance run with its fight files | a quest pack | not sure: pick the smallest kind that does it, and tell me why]

FACTS FROM MY GAME (copied, never retyped)
- Names exactly as the game shows them: NPCs and mobs [..], abilities with their rank [..], items [..], doors and objects [..]
- Spots: for each one, what eb marks set <name> answered: [..]
- What eb help <command> says, for each command the script should send: [paste]
- The tested example closest to what I want, copied whole: [paste, or none]
- If this is a fix: the script as it is now, and the exact console lines, names replaced: [paste]

RULES FOR WHAT YOU WRITE
1. Lua 5.4 only: no ffi, jit, bit, unpack, loadstring, setfenv, table.getn or math.pow, and no != or +=. No os.time, os.execute or io.popen: time comes from socket.gettime() in a helper and script.now() in an EB Script.
2. Every loop waits: wait(seconds) or waitframe() in a helper, script.wait(seconds) in an EB Script. Event handlers only note what happened; the main loop acts.
3. Few game reads: every member a round needs in ONE IS.Parse, a few rounds a second, and only members the TLO reference lists. Answers are text ("TRUE", "NULL", "87"). Never poll a loot window, an effect's name or a window's children by number.
4. Talk to EB only with luacall EBISX_cmd <line> (a helper) or script.eb(line, who) (an EB Script), using only commands eb help lists. Send a line once per change, never every round.
5. Never move the character yourself. Every move is EB's walk on the zone's mesh: eb walk x,y,z, eb marks go <mark>, eb follow <name>, eb goto <zone> (script.moveTo and script.travel in an EB Script). No held movement keys, no straight-line walking, no fast travel. If EB finds no route, report it; never work around it.
6. EB runs without any other bot: no other bot's commands, functions or files, no MacroQuest mq.*, no LavishScript .iss.
7. Never start a fight, click a yes/no window, accept a reward or attack a guard: fights belong to EB's cast stack. Tell me what to switch off in EB first, so the two never do the same job (eb cures off, eb loot off ...).
8. Never attach a Lua handler to EQ2_onQuestUpdate or to EB's old EBISX_State: they can crash the game. Use EBISX_QuestUpdate and EBISX_State2.
9. Clean chat text and names before they go into any console line (drop ${, line breaks and quotes). No hard-coded folders. No real character, guild or server names: placeholders only.
10. Instance, fight and quest files are data only (return { ... }) with the guide's schema: eb.ic/1 or eb-quest/1.

WHAT TO GIVE ME BACK
- Every file complete and ready to save, with nothing left out as "...".
- For each file: its exact name and folder, the line that starts it and the line that stops it.
- What to switch off or set in EB before I run it.
- Every eb command, game member and event the script uses, in a list, so I can check each one (eb help <command>, eb tlocheck <member>).
- A short test plan: one box, a quiet spot, what I should see in the console, and how to stop it.
- Anything you are not sure of, as a plain question for me instead of a guess.
```

#### The same prompt, filled in

Here is a real request: pause EB when the bags are full. Only these parts change; the opening, the rules and *What to give me back* stay as they are. [The worked example](#for-ai-helpers-a-worked-example) shows the tested script that answers it.

Filled in:

```
MY SETUP
- EB build: EB for InnerSpace
- What eb version answered: [the line it printed]
- The first line of eb status: [the line it printed]
- EB's console word on my PC: eb
- Server type: live
- The character it is for: class fury, level 60, role healer
- My crew: 4 boxes, sessions is1 to is4; the tank is is1; the box I play by hand is none
- Where it should run: this box only, or every box when I add a word

WHAT I WANT
- In one sentence: when this box's bags drop under 3 free slots, EB on this box should pause (with the word crew: the whole crew), and go on once there is room again.
- When it should stop by itself: never; I stop it with endlua.
- What it must never do: pause or go on twice for one change, flip back and forth at the mark, move the character, or touch an item.
- The kind of script: a helper beside EB: one .lua file in InnerSpace's Scripts folder, started with lua <name>.

FACTS FROM MY GAME (copied, never retyped)
- Names exactly as the game shows them: none needed.
- Spots: none.
- What eb help <command> says, for each command the script should send: [what eb help pause and eb help resume printed]
- The tested example closest to what I want, copied whole: none that I know of; tell me if there is one.
```

#### Ask well

- **One script, one job.** Ask for one thing, try it, then ask for the next. A small script is easy to check.
- **Say the kind.** A helper, an EB Script or a data file: [the kinds](#first-which-kind-of-script) say which fits.
- **Copy every name from the game.** Abilities with their rank, NPCs, items and doors, exactly as the game shows them. For a spot, stand on it and type `eb marks set <name>`.
- **Say what must never happen.** "Never pause twice", "never move the character": an AI keeps a rule it is given.
- **Ask for its questions first.** "Before you write, list what you are not sure of." Answer them, then let it write.
- **Never let it fill a gap with a guess.** "If the guide does not list it, say so and stop" is in the prompt for that reason.

### For AI helpers: The rules every EB script follows

Every rule here comes from EB's own code or its tested examples. Each one says why, and where you can see it. Point your AI at a rule by its number: "rule 47 says one line per change".

#### The checklist

1. **Pick the kind, and use only its tools.** An EB Script has the `script` object, a helper has `IS`, a data file has nothing. [Rules 1 to 6](#for-ai-helpers-the-rules-every-eb-script-follows).
2. **The right folder and the right name.** [Rules 7 to 11](#for-ai-helpers-the-rules-every-eb-script-follows).
3. **The right start and stop lines.** `eb script run` and `lua <name>`. [Rules 12 to 17](#for-ai-helpers-the-rules-every-eb-script-follows).
4. **Plain Lua 5.4.** No LuaJIT, no Lua 5.1, no other language's syntax. [Rules 18 to 21](#for-ai-helpers-the-rules-every-eb-script-follows).
5. **Every loop waits, in seconds.** [Rules 22 to 27](#for-ai-helpers-the-rules-every-eb-script-follows).
6. **Few game reads, batched, of listed members only.** [Rules 28 to 41](#for-ai-helpers-the-rules-every-eb-script-follows).
7. **Only EB's own commands, through its door, once per change.** [Rules 42 to 50](#for-ai-helpers-the-rules-every-eb-script-follows).
8. **EB moves the character, never fast travels, and starts no fight of its own.** [Rules 51 to 58](#for-ai-helpers-the-rules-every-eb-script-follows).
9. **The crew: crew words, and EBISX_State2 keyed by the box.** [Rules 59 to 64](#for-ai-helpers-the-rules-every-eb-script-follows).
10. **A handler only notes; no event wider than 40 arguments.** [Rules 65 to 71](#for-ai-helpers-the-rules-every-eb-script-follows).
11. **A page's parts match its script, in EB's colours.** [Rules 72 to 78](#for-ai-helpers-the-rules-every-eb-script-follows).
12. **Settings with `eb set`; `boot.json` is read only.** [Rules 79 to 83](#for-ai-helpers-the-rules-every-eb-script-follows).
13. **Files only in your own places, and never a second EB.** [Rules 84 to 92](#for-ai-helpers-the-rules-every-eb-script-follows).
14. **Instances and quest packs are data, and the tank leads.** [Rules 93 to 99](#for-ai-helpers-the-rules-every-eb-script-follows).
15. **One box first, and no real names.** [Rules 100 to 103](#for-ai-helpers-the-rules-every-eb-script-follows).

#### All the rules, by subject

Open a subject to read its rules.

**The three kinds and their tools rules 1 to 6**

1. **Say which kind of script it is.** An EB Script, a helper or a data file ([the kinds](#first-which-kind-of-script)). `IS` is nil inside an EB Script, `script` is nil in a helper, and a data file that runs code is refused. *Why:* mixing them is the first mistake an AI makes.
2. **What an EB Script has.** Lua's `string`, `table` and `math` (its own copies), `utf8`, `pairs`, `ipairs`, `next`, `select`, `type`, `tostring`, `tonumber`, `error`, `assert`, `pcall`, `xpcall`, `rawget`, `rawset`, `rawequal`, `rawlen`, `setmetatable`, `getmetatable`, `print`, its own `_G`, `_VERSION` and `script`. Nothing else: no `io`, `os`, `require`, `load`, `dofile`, `debug`, `coroutine`, `IS`, `socket` or `cjson`. *Why:* any other name is nil and stops the script; files, time, the game and EB are reached only through `script` (EB Scripts guide 16.1).
3. **The `script` object, exactly:** `start running stopping wait stem name args now unix opt on num int count item has x y z set setMine say live liveClear panel eb travel moveTo pick page pageClose sound soundStop speak speakStop banner fileName folderOf fileExists readFile listFolder writeFile appendLine testStart check expect expectNum expectValue mayBeEmpty skip testDone me target group`. *Why:* an invented member is nil and stops the script, and EB's own tests hold the guide to this list (EB Scripts guide 5).
4. **What a helper has.** ISXLUA gives it `IS`, `echo`, `wait`, `waitframe`, `waituntil`, `waitforevent`, `await`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, `clearTimer`, `Exists`, `ISXLUA`, `args` and `io`, with `require("socket")` and `require("cjson.safe")` built in (cjson needs the ISXLUA 2026-09 build or newer). The `IS` calls EB and its tested scripts lean on: `Execute`, `Parse`, `GetVar`, `SetVar`, `CallAtom`, `AttachEvent`, `AttachEventTyped`, `DetachEvent`, `FireEvent`, `Register`, `Unregister`, `Relay` and `RelayEvent`. `IS.CallAtom` forwards no arguments: stage them with `IS.SetVar` first. Print with `echo(...)`. *Why:* these are the tools a tested helper uses; an AI must not assume others.
5. **A data file is data.** An instance folder and a quest pack only `return { … }`. EB loads and runs them itself, and refuses a file it cannot honour, with the reason. [script-ic-instance](#complete-script-a-whole-instance-file-hub-door-route-camp-spots-pulls-loop).
6. **Helpers are for EB for InnerSpace only.** EB Boxer, the NON-ISX build, has no InnerSpace and no ISXLUA, so an `IS.*` script cannot run there. EB Scripts and data files work the same on both builds. The first line of `eb status` names the build: ask before you write.

**Places and names rules 7 to 11**

7. **An EB Script is one `.lua` file directly in your scripts folder**: the folder named `scripts` in EB's data folder (`boot.json`'s `data`; by default the EB Boxer folder in your Windows user's local app data). Its name is its file name without `.lua`: letters, digits, `-` and `_`, starting with a letter, 60 characters at most, any case. A file in a folder below, or with another name, is never listed; one of yours with an example's name takes the example's place. `eb script new <Name>` writes a starter there. *Why:* EB lists only those files (EB Scripts guide 2).
8. **A helper is one `.lua` file in InnerSpace's `Scripts` folder**, for example `Scripts/eb_bagwatch.lua`. Never in `Scripts/EBIS` (EB's own folder: its `boot.json`, its start file and its key guard), never named `eb.lua` (EB Setup's launcher behind `lua eb start`), and never with one of EB's file names. *Why:* EB Setup owns those files, and a clash breaks how EB starts. [script-bagwatch](#complete-script-pause-eb-when-the-bags-are-full).
9. **Your own instances and quest packs live in your own folders.** An instance: `data/ebic/authored/instances/<folder>/` in EB's folder, run with `eb ic run authored/<folder>`. A quest pack: `data/ebquests/authored/`, found by its file name with `eb ql start <quest>`. *Why:* EB's updates never touch those folders, while `data/eb` is EB's own shipped data, which an update may replace. (The tested instance example names a folder under `data/eb/ic`; put a file of your own in the authored folder.)
10. **Never change a shipped example where it is.** Copy it first: *Copy to my scripts* in the Scripts window, or `eb script copy <Example> [new name]`. *Why:* an update puts the examples back as shipped, and an edit there is lost. Your scripts folder is yours: EB's updates and EB Setup never write or delete there.
11. **A script runs only where its file is.** A run sent to another box or PC needs the script in that PC's own scripts folder; a PC without it answers *no script called …*. Copy your scripts folder, with its `options` and `sounds`, to each PC.

**Starting and stopping rules 12 to 17**

12. **EB Script lines.** `eb script` opens the Scripts window; `eb script list` and `eb script info <Name>` show them. `eb script run <Name> [me|group|irc|all] [words]` (or just `eb script <Name>`) runs one, and `eb script stop <Name>` or `eb script stop all` stops. Also `eb script test <Name>`, `eb script results <Name>`, `eb script set <Name> <key> <value> [for me|all|<character>]`, `eb script unset <Name> <key>` and `eb script reload`. A line with no Who word runs on this box only. *Why:* these are the only start and stop lines (EB Scripts guide 15).
13. **Helper lines.** `lua <name> [words]` starts it in that session's console, and `endlua <name>` stops it. A helper in a folder below `Scripts` is `lua <folder>/<name>`. A word in double quotes is one argument. *Why:* the run and stop lines of every tested helper. [script-autocure](#complete-script-auto-cure-watcher).
14. **A helper's words arrive as `...`** (`local a, b = ...`). Some ISXLUA builds hand them in the global `args` instead, so fall back to it when `...` is empty. Check every word; on a bad one, print a usage line and `return`. *Why:* without the fallback a helper sees no words on some builds, and a bad word should end it with its usage, not run it wrong. [script-bagwatch](#complete-script-pause-eb-when-the-bags-are-full).
15. **A run reads its file fresh.** After you save, stop it and start it again. EB reads the scripts folder again every 8 s while the Scripts window is up, every 60 s otherwise, and at once on `eb script reload`; it lists 400 scripts at most. *Why:* a running script keeps the text it started with.
16. **A helper that sends EB lines needs EB in its session.** Game reads and game commands work without EB. `luacall EBISX_cmd` needs EB running there: EB registers `EBISX_cmd` only while it runs, and until the character is in the world EB answers only its own few start words (such as stop, status, version and help); every other line answers that it works once EB is up in the world. *Why:* a pause-the-crew helper does nothing where EB is down. Each tested script's Needs line says which it needs.
17. **When EB ends, its EB Scripts end.** `eb stop`, typed in a session's console, ends EB there and every EB Script it runs. A script starts only while EB is signed in on that box. A run or a header button sent from another box is refused on a box played by hand (EB paused) or where EB is stopped (*… is not started here*).

**Lua 5.4 rules 18 to 21**

18. **Plain Lua 5.4.** Both EB builds run Lua 5.4. Never `setfenv`, `getfenv`, `loadstring`, `module`, `table.getn`, `table.maxn`, `math.pow`, `math.atan2`, `math.log10`, `math.mod`, the global `unpack`, `bit32`, `require("bit")`, `require("ffi")` or `require("jit")`. Write `table.unpack`, `load`, `#t`, `x ^ y`, `math.atan(y, x)`, `math.log(x, 10)`, `math.fmod(a, b)` and Lua 5.4's own `& | ~ << >>`. *Why:* those are Lua 5.1 and LuaJIT names: nil in Lua 5.4, they stop the script with *attempt to call a nil value*.
19. **No syntax from other languages.** Not `!=`, `+=`, `++`, `&&`, `||`, `!x`, `continue`, `a ? b : c` or `x?.y`: write `~=`, `x = x + 1`, `and`, `or`, `not`, `goto continue` with a `::continue::` label, `if … then … else … end`, and a plain nil check.
20. **Whole numbers for `%d`.** `string.format("%d", x)` raises unless `x` is whole: use `math.floor(x + 0.5)` first, or `%.1f` (health can be 87.5). `tostring(3.0)` is `"3.0"`: hand LavishScript whole numbers with no `.0`. [data-compat-numbers](#snippet-print-numbers-the-same-way-everywhere).
21. **Never join nil into text.** `"hp " .. nil` stops the script: write `tostring(v)` or `v or ""`. A list option is a Lua table (`#list`, `list[1]`).

**Waiting and timing rules 22 to 27**

22. **Every loop waits.** A helper waits with `wait(seconds)`, `waitframe()`, `waituntil(fn, seconds)` (it answers true or false) or `waitforevent(name, seconds)`; an EB Script with `script.wait(seconds)`. *Why:* a helper runs on the game thread and is resumed once a frame, so a loop with no wait freezes the game; an EB Script that runs 50 ms without a wait is ended (*it ran too long without waiting*), and its own `pcall` cannot keep it alive.
23. **Seconds, not tenths.** ISXLUA's `wait` and `script.wait` take seconds (`wait(0.5)` is half a second); `script.now()` counts milliseconds. LavishScript's `wait 10` (tenths of a second) is not Lua. *Why:* a wait in the wrong unit waits ten or a thousand times too long.
24. **The EB Script loop.** `script.start()` first (it fills the `var=` variables), then one loop: `while script.running() do … script.wait(n) end`. Code after the loop runs once Stop is pressed. On Stop the wait answers false at once and `script.running()` turns false; a script still running 8 s later is ended, and its file calls then answer *the script is stopping*. Write what you must keep inside the loop (EB Scripts guide 5.1).
25. **Wait in short steps.** A wait's length is fixed when it starts. Wait about a second at a time, and do the work when it is due (`script.now() - last >= every * 1000`). *Why:* one 60-second wait notices Stop, a button or a changed option a minute late.
26. **Tell time the tested way.** In a helper, `require("socket").gettime()` (seconds, with a fraction). In an EB Script, `script.now()` (milliseconds that only go forward) and `script.unix()` (the PC clock's whole seconds). Never `os.time`: an EB Script has no `os`, and `os.time` has thrown inside ISXLUA. [script-groupready](#complete-script-group-ready-checker).
27. **A watching helper keeps running.** Its event handlers and registered functions go when the script ends, so it keeps a main loop that waits until `endlua <name>`. A one-shot helper may end by itself, as script-groupready does. [script-eventwatch](#complete-script-event-watcher).

**Reading the game rules 28 to 41**

28. **An EB Script reads the game through `script.me()`, `script.target()` and `script.group()` only.** `script.me()`: `inGame` (false out of the world, and then nothing else is there), `name`, `level`, `class`, `archetype`, `zone`, `health` and `power` (percent), `dead`, `combat`, `moving`, `x`, `y`, `z`. `script.target()`: nil, or `id`, `name`, `health`, `level`, `distance`, `type`, `dead`, `named`. `script.group()`: a list of `name`, `zone`, `dead`, `distance`, `class`. Read once a round, keep the table, and check `me.inGame` first. *Why:* these are EB's own counted reads; an EB Script never touches the game itself (EB Scripts guide 5.8).
29. **A helper reads with `IS.Parse("${…}")`, and only members the [TLO reference](#tlos) lists.** A member EB holds back as not verified (for example `Me.Archetype`) is not one to lean on. Try any member first with `eb tlocheck Me.Level`: it answers the value and how long the read took, or why EB holds it back. *Why:* an untested member has printed errors on screen and once crashed a client. [tlo-getvar-not-verified](#snippet-what-getvar-does-with-a-member-that-is-not-verified-yet).
30. **One batched read a round.** Put every member a round needs into one `IS.Parse`, joined by a separator no value holds (`~^~` for names and text, `|` for numbers and flags), and split the answer. Keep to a few rounds a second (the tested scripts check every 0.25 to 5 s), and cap list reads (they read 5 to 20 rows): `IS.Parse` answers nil past 8 KB. *Why:* every read runs on the game thread; EB keeps itself to about 8 reads a frame, and a helper's reads come on top of EB's. [tlo-me-batched-read](#snippet-read-several-me-members-in-one-read).
31. **Every answer is text.** Numbers come as text (`"123"`, `"1.500000"`), flags as `TRUE` or `FALSE`, a missing object or member as `NULL` (a chain off NULL stays NULL, with no error), and `(exists)` as `TRUE` or `NULL`, never `FALSE`. Member names ignore case. Compare with `== "TRUE"`, convert with `tonumber()`, and guard nil: `tostring(IS.Parse(…) or "")`. [tlo-exists-and-text](#snippet-true-or-null-and-numbers-as-text).
32. **Never poll a server request.** `Ability[…].ToAbilityInfo`, `Equipment[…].ToItemInfo`, `Inventory[…].ToItemInfo`, `Effect[n].ToEffectInfo.Name` and an effect's first `.ID` go to the game's server: read each once per id and keep it. *Why:* read every round, they flood the server. [tlo-effect-info-server](#snippet-effect-names-are-server-requests---never-poll-them).
33. **Read a window after its event.** `LootWindow` only after `EQ2_onLootWindowAppeared`; a merchant only while `MerchantWindow.IsVisible` is `TRUE`. *Why:* asking with no window up is slow, and gets slower in a long session. [script-lootall](#complete-script-take-loot-windows-by-your-rules).
34. **Read the zone after the load.** `Zone.Name` and `Zone.ShortName` name the new zone as soon as a load starts. Read them after `EQ2_FinishedZoning`, or once `EQ2.Zoning` reads 0 and `Me.InGameWorld` is `TRUE`. `EQ2.Zoning` is a number, -1 at character select. EB keys zones by the short name. [tlo-zone-name-flips-early](#snippet-zonename-changes-at-the-start-of-a-zone-load).
35. **Read the right member.** A fight on you is `Me.IsHated` (`Me.InCombat` stays lit after a fight). `Me.Group[0]` is you and `Me.Group[1]` to `Me.Group[5]` the others; a member in another zone reads ID 0 and has no distance, so check `InZone` first. `Me.Health` and `Me.Power` are percent already. The class is `Me.SubClass` (`Me.Class` is "druid" for a warden). An ability's name lives in `.ToAbilityInfo.Name`, never on the ability. Worn gear is `Me.Equipment[<slot>]`, bag items `Me.Inventory[ExactName,"<name>"]`. One known actor is `Actor[id,<id>]`. [The Me TLO](#tlo-me), [script-autocure](#complete-script-auto-cure-watcher).
36. **Known bad, never used:** `ability.Name`, `ability:Cast` (use `:Use`), `Me.IsMounted`, `Mounted`, `Coin`, `NumBagSlots`, `NumInventorySlots`, `actor.IsInteractable`, `IsTargetable`, `NumVerbs`, `Verb`, `IsInSameEncounter` as a member (it works only as a query term) and `groupmember.Zone`. **Not tested yet:** `actor:DoFace`, `Me:DoTarget`, `Me.Archetype`, and `groupmember.Power` (read `CurrentPower` and `MaxPower`, as script-groupready does). *Why:* they read wrong, read nothing, or are not in the game.
37. **Search actors the tested way.** Run `EQ2:QueryActors[<YourIndex>, <query>, "ByDist"]` into an `index:actor` variable of your own (`:Clear` it first), then read `<YourIndex>.Used` and the rows in one batch. Strings compare with `==`, flags with `= TRUE` or `= FALSE`; terms join with `&&`, `||`, `!` and brackets; NPCs are `Type == "NPC" || Type == "NamedNPC"`. Use only tested members as terms, and query about once a second at most. *Why:* a query that names an unverified member is refused by EB's checks, and another form may match nothing. [script-namedwatch](#complete-script-say-when-a-named-spawns).
38. **Read a game window by its full name:** `EQ2UIPage[<window>,<page>].Child[<type>,<full.name>]`. Never walk children by type (`ChildType`), or by number under a tabbed pane. *Why:* such a read once took InnerSpace and every session on the PC down, and EB's guard refuses it. The speech bubble's reply rows are the one tested read by number (script-hailreply). [tlo-ui-page-by-name](#snippet-read-an-interface-element-by-its-full-name).
39. **Probe before you read another extension.** `${Extension[<name>](exists)}` first; a stand-alone helper waits for `${ISXEQ2.IsReady}` before it reads anything. Never read EB's own extension TLOs (`EBNav`, `EBDiag`) from a script: they are for EB's own code. *Why:* reading an unloaded extension's TLO prints an error on screen. [tlo-isxeq2-ready](#snippet-check-that-the-game-extension-is-ready).
40. **Never click a yes/no window or a reward.** EB does not press ChoiceWindow buttons on this release, and accepting a RewardWindow is not verified: say what is asked, and let a person answer. For a buy of your own, `eb purchase expect "<item>"` answers the game's purchase question Yes only when it names exactly that item. *Why:* a script that waits on a popup it thinks it answered hangs. [script-choicealert](#complete-script-tell-me-when-a-yesno-question-waits).
41. **Answer an NPC by the words of its replies.** The speech bubble's rows are `EQ2UIPage[ProxyActor,Conversation].Child[composite,replies].Child[n]`, picked with `:LeftClick`. In the classic window, list `ReplyDialog.Replies:GetOptions[<YourIndex>]` into an `index:collection:string` (an `index:string` is refused) and pick with `ReplyDialog:Choose[n]`. No match: list the replies and stop. Never click a guess. [script-hailreply](#complete-script-hail-and-answer-an-npc).

**Sending commands rules 42 to 50**

42. **A helper's one door to EB is `IS.Execute("luacall EBISX_cmd <line>")`.** Crew words go inside the line: `luacall EBISX_cmd all pause`. Never type the console word from a script: beside another Lua bot it is `ebi`, and `eb` is then the other bot's. EB registers only `EBISX_cmd`. *Why:* the tested door works whatever word the install picked. [script-bagwatch](#complete-script-pause-eb-when-the-bags-are-full).
43. **An EB Script's door is `script.eb(line, who)`.** `eb` in front is optional; `who` is `"me"` (the default), `"group"`, `"irc"` or `"all"`. The line is checked against EB's commands first (*not an EB line*) and may be 500 characters at most; it answers ok and words. `script.moveTo(x, y, z)` is `eb walk x,y,z`, and `script.travel(zone)` is `eb goto <zone>` (EB Scripts guide 5.4).
44. **Only EB's own commands.** The verb, after an optional crew word, must be in the [Commands](#commands) list. `eb help <command>` shows the words it takes and whether it takes a crew word; type a line once by hand before a script sends it. Words in double quotes stay together. EB answers anything else in plain words: *'x' is not an eb command (eb help lists them)*, a bad value names its choices, a missing word is named. [commands-refusals](#snippet-what-a-refused-line-tells-you).
45. **40 words at most in a luacall line.** luacall hands ISXLUA one argument per word, and past 42 the game crashes before EB sees the line. *Why:* the console word joins a typed line into one argument; a script's own luacall does not.
46. **There is no reply.** EB queues the line (64 at most; past that the oldest is dropped), takes 8 queued lines a frame, and answers as an `[eb]` line on the console. Learn what happened from the game (`Me.IsMoving`, the target, the buff) or from the crew's next state. *Why:* a script that waits for an answer never gets one. [script-patrol](#complete-script-patrol-between-saved-marks).
47. **One line per change, never every round.** Remember what you sent, and send again only when the state flips, with a margin so it never flips back and forth (script-bagwatch goes on only two slots past the mark). *Why:* a repeated line floods every box it reaches, and a line sent to `all` runs on every box, this one too. [script-namedwatch](#complete-script-say-when-a-named-spawns).
48. **`stop` alone ends EB.** `luacall EBISX_cmd stop`, like `eb stop` typed in a session, ends EB in that session. To halt runs, walks and goals while EB and the fight go on, send `stopall` (this box) or `all stop` (the crew). `pause` and `resume` hold and free them; `end <system>` ends one thing (`quest`, `ic`, `nav`, `hunt`, `craft`, `harvest` or `all`). [commands-core-family](#snippet-pause-resume-status-and-the-kill-switch).
49. **Never put game text or typed text into a line raw.** Strip `${` and line breaks from chat text (LavishScript would run a data sequence), keep a name to letters, digits and `'` (`gsub("[^%w']", "")`), and refuse an item or ability name that holds a double quote or a backslash. In an EB Script, never build a line from what a player typed: keep it as an option, and let a function of the script use it. *Why:* unclean text changes what the line means. [script-tellreply](#complete-script-answer-tells-while-you-are-away).
50. **Game commands: only the ones the tested scripts use.** `eq2execute hail`, `eq2execute gsay`, `eq2execute tell`, `Actor[id,<id>]:DoTarget` and `:DoubleClick`, `Me.Ability["<exact name>"]:Use`, `Me.Equipment[<slot>]:ToggleAutoConsume`, `MerchantWindow.MyInventory["<name>"]:Sell[n]`, `LootWindow:LootAll`, `ReplyDialog:Choose[n]`, an element's `:LeftClick`, `EQ2:QueryActors[…]`, `<YourIndex>:Clear` and `declarevariable`. When EB answers *held back until it is proven live*, script around it (tell the player, wait), and never send EB's proof words from a script: they change, for the whole session, what EB lets out. [script-selljunk](#complete-script-sell-junk-at-a-merchant).

**Moving and fighting rules 51 to 58**

51. **EB has one mover: the zone's mesh.** Every move is an EB command: `eb walk x,y,z` (or a mark, a route, a map point), `eb marks go <mark>`, `eb follow <name> [dist]`, `eb poi <name>`, `eb gtgm <member>`, `eb leash …`, `eb goto <zone>`, `eb hub`, `eb zoneout`; `script.moveTo` and `script.travel` in an EB Script; `MM x,y,z` in a quest pack and `path` steps in an instance. *Why:* EB's walker plans on the mesh and keeps a character off walls, ledges and lava. [script-patrol](#complete-script-patrol-between-saved-marks), [Nav and travel](#nav-and-travel).
52. **Never steer by hand.** No held movement keys (InnerSpace's press commands, `eb key … hold`), no face-and-run loop, no straight line the mesh did not route, no auto-run, no fly keys. *Why:* a held key outlives the script (EB lets go only of the keys it held itself), and a walk with no route runs into walls and off ledges.
53. **No route, no walk.** EB does not walk to a spot the mesh has no way to: it says why (*no route on the .nav: …*, *no mesh: …*), and the character stays. A script that asks for a walk watches it start (`Me.IsMoving` within a few seconds) and handles *no walk*. Never fall back to walking straight. [nav-no-route](#snippet-a-walk-the-mesh-has-no-route-for-fails-and-says-why).
54. **Never fast travel.** An instance step that names it is refused when the file loads. A quest pack never fast travels (`SmartTravelTo` goes the ground way, `FastTravel` is refused) and never flies (`FlyUp` and `FlyDown` stop the step). `eb ft` is a press of your own only, and is refused while a quest line, a power-level route or an instance run is going. Travel with `eb goto <zone>`; `eb route <zone>` shows the hops without moving. [quest-no-fast-travel](#snippet-packs-never-fast-travel).
55. **Never move a character someone plays.** EB never moves a box it is paused on (a box played by hand), and refuses the crew lines that would. A script must not try either.
56. **A zone load ends a follow.** After `EQ2_FinishedZoning`, wait about 3 s for the others to load, then send `luacall EBISX_cmd others follow <you>` again. [script-followme](#complete-script-crew-follow-me).
57. **Never start a fight.** A helper that targets for a fight picks only a mob that already fights (an NPC or a named, alive, in combat mode), the way script-assist follows the tank's choice. Pulls belong to EB's combat and the cast stack (`eb assist tank`, `eb engage`). EB never fights a guard. [combat-never-a-guard](#snippet-guards-are-never-pulled-or-splashed).
58. **When a script does a job EB also does, switch EB's off.** Cures: `eb cures off`, or the cast stack's own cures off. Buffs: leave them out of the cast stack. Loot: `eb loot off`. *Why:* two casters or looters on one target or window act over each other. Each tested script's Needs line says what to switch off. [script-lootall](#complete-script-take-loot-windows-by-your-rules).

**The crew rules 59 to 64**

59. **Crew words.** `all` (every box, this one too), `others` (every box but this one) and `to <who>`: a box (`is2`), a character, a class, an archetype (`fighter`, `priest`, `mage` or `scout`), an `@role`, or several joined by commas (`to is2,is3`). No word: this box only. `eb relay <word> <line>` adds `here`, `awake`, `stagger [s]` and `mygroup`. Some commands take no crew word: `eb help <command>` says. [commands-crew-scopes](#snippet-send-a-command-to-the-crew), [Crew and group](#crew-and-group).
60. **A crew line runs once, and goes no further.** A received line is never sent on (one that carries a crew word is refused), each box acts on a message id once, and a crew line over 1800 bytes is refused, never cut. Prefer EB's crew words to InnerSpace's raw `relay is2 <line>`, which types the line into is2 unchecked. *Why:* no echo storms.
61. **Read the crew from the relay event `EBISX_State2`.** Every EB box sends it every 2 s, and a box not heard for 9 s has dropped out. Key each row by the box id (`is1`, `is2` …, from `${Session}`), never the character name. Its arguments start `v, box, name, zone, mode, hp, pw, combat, target, lastAct, tickMs`; it carries at most 40, and from the 40th on the fields ride packed in the 40th. Decode a row with EB's own `decodeState(args)` from `eb.relay.wire`; new fields only ever go on the end. [script-crewboard](#complete-script-crew-status-board), [what travels between boxes](#crew-and-group-what-travels-between-boxes).
62. **Never attach EB's old `EBISX_State`.** An older EB sends it with 47 arguments, and under ISXLUA an event wider than 42 arguments crashes the game in every session that has a handler on it. EB's crew state rides `EBISX_State2` (at most 40 arguments).
63. **Listen to `EBISX_Cmd`; never fire it.** `EBISX_Cmd` (v, mid, from, scope, who, relayed, line) is EB's crew command. Send your own lines with `luacall EBISX_cmd`: EB runs a crew line only from a box that has said who it is, and drops a repeat by its mid. *Why:* a hand-made EBISX_Cmd is refused, or runs twice.
64. **No other bot's lines.** No oc lines, no other bot's console word, atoms or variables. EB runs without any other bot, and such a line runs only in a session where that bot is loaded. In a mixed group, `eb ocdo <oc line>` runs EB's own version of an oc line's commands, and lists back the ones it has no version of.

**Events rules 65 to 71**

65. **A handler only notes; the main loop acts.** ISXLUA runs event handlers, `setTimeout` and `setInterval` callbacks and `IS.Register` functions in one go: a wait or an await inside one raises (*wait() cannot be used inside an event/timer/callback handler*). A handler records a small item (a queue entry, a counter, a flag) and returns. *Why:* heavy work there runs inside the game's own callback. [script-eventwatch](#complete-script-event-watcher).

66. **No event wider than 40 arguments.** A Lua handler must never attach ISXEQ2's `EQ2_onQuestUpdate`: it carries 5 arguments plus one per progress line, and past 42 ISXLUA overruns the handler and the game crashes. For quest progress attach `EBISX_QuestUpdate` instead: always 7 arguments (ID, Name, CurrentZone, Category, Description, the newest progress line, the number of lines), fired while EB runs. Any event or luacall of your own carries 40 arguments at most, and a relayed event 1800 bytes at most.

67. **The game's events, by name.** These are the names and argument orders EB itself attaches. Every argument arrives as text. Never invent another (there is no EQ2_onTell and no EQ2_onDeath).

    | Event | Arguments | When it fires |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | `EQ2_onIncomingChatText` | ChatType, Message, Speaker, Target, SpeakerIsNPC, ChannelName, SpeakerID, TargetID | A chat line arrives. |
    | `EQ2_onIncomingText` | Text, Type | Other text the game shows. |
    | `EQ2_StartedZoning` | none | A zone load begins. |
    | `EQ2_FinishedZoning` | TimeInSeconds | The new zone has loaded. |
    | `EQ2_ReplyDialogAppeared` | ID | An NPC conversation opens. |
    | `EQ2_onChoiceWindowAppeared` | ID | A yes/no window opens. |
    | `EQ2_onLootWindowAppeared` | ID | A loot window opens. |
    | `EQ2_onRewardWindowAppeared` | ID | A reward window opens. |
    | `EQ2_onQuestOffered` | Name, Description, Level, StatusReward | An NPC offers a quest. |
    | `EQ2_onAnnouncement` | Text, SoundType, Timer | A center-screen announcement. |
    | `EQ2_onLevelChange` | OldLevel, NewLevel | The character levels. |
    | `EQ2_onGroupMembershipChange` | Prev, New | The group changes. |
    | `EQ2_onRaidMembershipChange` | Prev, New | The raid changes. |
    | `EQ2_ActorSpawned` | ID, Name, Level, Type | An actor appears; a crowd of them at each zone-in. |
    | `EQ2_ActorDespawned` | ID, Name | An actor goes. |
    | `EQ2_ExamineItemWindowAppeared` | ItemName, WindowID | An item's examine window opens. |
    | `EQ2_onInventoryUpdate` | none | The bags change. |
    | `EBISX_QuestUpdate` | ID, Name, CurrentZone, Category, Description, the newest progress line, the number of lines | EB's safe quest update, while EB runs. |
    | `EBISX_State2` | v, box, name, zone, mode, hp, pw, combat, target, lastAct, tickMs, and more | A box's state, every 2 s (rule 61). |

    [Events](#events) covers them, and EB's own names for code inside EB.

68. **Attach as few event names as you need.** ISXLUA allows 64 distinct event names per game process, shared by every script in it; EB keeps up to 48 for itself, and a name EB already attaches costs nothing more. *Why:* past 64 the next attach fails, and it may be someone else's. script-eventwatch attaches four.

69. **A window event carries only an id.** Read the window once, after the event, in the main loop: its text and its buttons are not in the event. [script-choicealert](#complete-script-tell-me-when-a-yesno-question-waits).

70. **De-duplicate chat.** The game often repeats a chat line once per chat window: keep the last line and its time, and skip the repeat. A tell to you is a chat line whose Target is your own name, with no ChannelName, from a speaker who is not an NPC and not you. [script-tellreply](#complete-script-answer-tells-while-you-are-away), [events-dedupe](#snippet-the-same-line-twice-is-delivered-once).

71. **Leave the actor events' switch alone.** `EQ2_ActorStanceChange` stays silent until `ISXEQ2:EnableActorEvents`, a switch every script shares and EB holds. A zone-in fires a crowd of `EQ2_ActorSpawned`, so its handler only queues.

**Pages and windows rules 72 to 78**

72. **A window of your own is an EB Script page.** An `.html` file beside the script (or in a folder below it), named in a header line: `-- ebscript page "Title" file=<name>.html [w= h= x= y= …]`. 20 pages a script, 4 MB a file. Open it with `script.page(n)` or `eb script page <Name> [n]`, and close it with `script.pageClose(n)`; a page opens whether the script runs or not. An add-in (`-- ebscript addin "Title" file=<x>.html in=<window word>`) puts your HTML inside another EB window, and a page with the flag `hud` covers the game while clicks go through it. A helper cannot add a window to EB (EB Scripts guide 7 and 12).
73. **Parts and names must match.** A page is built from elements with `data-eb-part="<part>"` (44 parts) and their settings as `data-eb-<setting>`. Every `data-eb-key` is an option of the header, every `data-eb-live` a name the script sends with `script.live`, and every `data-eb-call` a global function of the script. *Why:* a part with a wrong name shows its words but no value, and a press does nothing (EB Scripts guide 8).
74. **A function a button or page calls is global, and above the loop.** `function Name() … end`, not `local function`; its name is letters, digits and `_`, 40 at most. It runs inside the script's next wait, and 20 calls wait at most. In it, read a value that just changed with `script.opt("key")`. *Why:* a local function, or one below the loop, does not exist yet (*has no function X*) (EB Scripts guide 16.2).
75. **A page's look.** No drop-down lists (use the pick part). Colours only through EB's tokens: `var(--og-text)`, `var(--og-bright)`, `var(--og-dim)`, `var(--og-mute)`, `var(--og-heading)`, `var(--og-highlight)`, `var(--og-accent)`, `var(--og-good)`, `var(--og-warn)`, `var(--og-bad)`, `var(--og-panel)`, `var(--og-field)`, `var(--og-well)`, `var(--og-btn)`, `var(--og-line)`, `var(--og-line-soft)`, `var(--og-hover)`. No text under 12 px, and never a state by colour alone. A page's own JavaScript uses `EBUI.page()` and its `J`. *Why:* every theme must read, and Black and White is the default (EB Scripts guide 7.4 and 9).
76. **A page's EB line carries no crew word.** `data-eb-line` runs one line its author wrote, and the page's Who says where it goes, so never `all`, `others`, `to` or `relay` in it. Nothing a player types on a page ever becomes a command line: keep it as an option (`J.set`), and let a function of the script use it (`J.call`) (EB Scripts guide 7.3 and 9).
77. **Open EB's own windows with EB lines.** `eb windows` lists them by their words, and `eb windows <word>` opens one; also `eb ui`, `eb mcp`, `eb mini` and `eb console open`. EB for InnerSpace's start also answers `eb overlay`. A window is a this-box thing: these take no crew word. [UI windows](#ui-windows).
78. **The panel.** `local p = script.panel()`, then `p:title`, `p:text`, `p:note`, `p:good`, `p:warn`, `p:bad`, `p:divider`, `p:row(label, value)`, `p:bar(label, value, max)`, `p:ability(name, line)`, `p:item(name, picture, line)`, `p:icon(spec, a, b)` and `p:button("Label", "GlobalFn")`, then `p:show()` draws it in one go. 200 items, 300 characters each (EB Scripts guide 5.3).

**Settings rules 79 to 83**

79. **Change an EB setting with `eb set <key> <value>`.** From a helper `luacall EBISX_cmd set <key> <value>`, from an EB Script `script.eb("set <key> <value>")`. `eb set <key>` reads one, `eb set` alone lists them, and `eb all set …` reaches the crew. A key is letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`; a value is on or off, a number, or plain words, never quotes, braces, brackets or a backslash. *Why:* `eb set` keeps the value, saves it, and applies it now where EB can. [commands-utility-commands](#snippet-the-utility-commands-in-this-release).
80. **Never invent a setting key.** Keys, their kinds and ranges come from EB's settings catalog (`eb.ui.settings.settings`); `eb set` lists what is set. An unknown key does nothing. [platform-settings-catalog](#snippet-read-the-settings-catalog).
81. **EB's settings file: by hand only with EB stopped.** `eb-settings.json`, in EB's folder, holds the settings of every box of the install. EB reads it once, and its saves write back only the keys it changed; a hand edit made while EB runs is not seen until EB starts again. Use `eb set`. A script that must edit the file stops EB first and checks EB's heartbeat, as [script-setting](#complete-script-change-an-eb-setting) does.
82. **`boot.json` is EB Setup's file.** `Scripts/EBIS/boot.json` says where EB lives (`root`), its console word (`console`: `eb` or `ebi`) and its data folder (`data`). A helper may read it with `cjson.safe`, and never writes it. *Why:* a bad edit stops EB from starting; EB refuses the whole file when `root` is missing or the word is not eb or ebi. [script-crewboard](#complete-script-crew-status-board), [Settings](#settings).
83. **An EB Script's option values** live in `options/<name>.json` in your scripts folder (a lower-case name). A script reads this character's own value, else every character's, else the header's default. Set them in the Scripts window, with `script.set` (every character) or `script.setMine` (this one), or with `eb script set …`. Delete the file to reset them; rename it along with the `.lua` to keep them (EB Scripts guide 4.4).

**Files and globals rules 84 to 92**

84. **An EB Script's paths are relative to a place.** With no word, your scripts folder: the only place a script or a page writes. `examples:`, `logs:` and `exports:` are EB's, read only. No drive, no leading slash, never above its place with `..`; a backslash reads as a slash; 1000 characters at most, and each name one Windows takes. *Why:* any other path is refused in words (EB Scripts guide 10.1).
85. **An EB Script's file calls:** `script.readFile` (4 MB at most), `script.writeFile`, `script.appendLine`, `script.listFolder` and `script.fileExists`. Each is a job for EB's file worker: the script waits a moment, the game never does. Read a file once and keep its text (EB Scripts guide 10.2).
86. **A helper's file work runs on the game thread.** Read a file once at start, and write rarely. Build every path from `${LavishScript.HomeDirectory}` or boot.json's `root` (turn `\` into `/`, strip the last `/`), never a folder typed into the script. *Why:* a hard-coded folder breaks on another PC. [script-crewboard](#complete-script-crew-status-board).
87. **Never write EB's own files while EB runs:** its `eb-*` files in EB's folder, and its shipped data under `data/eb`. Your own folders (your scripts folder, `data/ebic`, `data/ebquests`, `data/huntlists`) are never laid over or pruned by an update.
88. **Your own LavishScript variables.** Declare them `declarevariable <Name> <type> global`, in that word order (the other order quietly makes a plain string), with a prefix of your own (the examples use `EBH_`); `squelch` keeps *already declared* off the console. Never name one after a TLO or a game object (it hides that object from every script), and never use EB's `EBX_` or `EBISX_` names. [script-harvest](#complete-script-harvest-the-nodes-in-reach).
89. **EB's heartbeat is read only.** EB rewrites the LavishScript global `EBISX_Beat` (milliseconds) every 250 ms and sets it to 0 when it stops: read it twice, a second apart, to know EB runs. Never write it or EB's other globals, and never register a function named `EBISX_cmd` or any `EBISX_` name. *Why:* EB refuses to start while the beat looks fresh, and a second `EBISX_cmd` steals EB's door. [script-setting](#complete-script-change-an-eb-setting).
90. **Never run a second EB inside a helper.** A helper loads only EB modules that read no game: `eb.relay.wire` (crew states) and `eb.ui.settings.settings` (the settings catalog). Put `<root>/lua/?.lua` and `<root>/lua/?/init.lua` in front of `package.path`, as EB's own start does. Never start EB's pulse, game layer, events or relay there. *Why:* EB's pulse writes EB's heartbeat and zeroes it when it stops, so EB then refuses to start; a second event layer also takes names from the 64. [script-crewboard](#complete-script-crew-status-board).
91. **Never call `IS.Share` or `IS.Shared`.** Keep state that scripts share in a LavishScript global variable (declare it, set it, read it with `IS.Parse`). *Why:* a shared table crashed a live client inside ISXLUA, and EB refuses the call.
92. **Never start other programs:** no `os.execute`, no `io.popen`. *Why:* a helper runs on the game thread, so a call that blocks there blocks the game.

**Instances and quest packs rules 93 to 99**

93. **Instance and quest files are data only:** `return { … }`, with no functions, loops, `require`, text building, files or game reads. Nothing runs when EB loads them, and a file EB cannot honour is refused at load with the reason, never half-run. [script-ic-instance](#complete-script-a-whole-instance-file-hub-door-route-camp-spots-pulls-loop).
94. **The schema.** `schema = "eb.ic/1"` in instance and fight files; `schema = "eb-quest/1"` in a quest pack, with `quest_name` exactly as the journal shows it. Every route step has a unique `id`, and every spot is three numbers, `{ x, y, z }`. [ic-load-checks](#snippet-what-runnerload-refuses).
95. **Route steps the runner knows.** Each step's `act` has its own fields: `path` (`spots = { { x, y, z }, … }`), `campspot` (`spot`, `who`), `encounter` (`name`: the fight file), `interact` (`actor`, `verb`), `wait` (`seconds`), `wait_actor_dead` (`name`), `loot` (`op`), `announce` (`message`), `zoneout` (`via`), and `swim`, `evac` and `lootmethod`. An act the runner does not know is refused at load. *Why:* a step the runner once skipped walked a group past a named. [ic-route-step-kinds](#snippet-one-route-step-of-each-kind), [Instances](#instances).
96. **The hub route is the tank's alone.** It holds only `path`, `campspot` (`who = "me"`), `wait`, `interact` and `wait_group`: no camp spot for the group, and no path that brings the group along. Every box gets to the hub zone by its own travel (`eb hub`, `eb all hub <instance>`); the box the run is typed on leads as the tank, walks to the door and zones the group in; inside, the others hold on the tank's camp spots. [ic-tank-zones-group-in](#snippet-the-tank-zones-the-group-in).
97. **A fight file**, one per fight in `encounters/`: `name`, `kind`, `spot`, a gate (`when`), `phases` (`{ id, do_ = { … } }`), reactions (a phase with `when` and `repeat_ = true`, or `once = true`), a win test (`done`) and `on_death`. A gate that fails skips the step; with no win test the verdict is *FAILED:done-test*. Conditions are EB's own only: `actor_present`, `actor_dead`, `actor_count`, `actor_type`, `health_below`, `health_above`, `mob_health_below`, `mob_casting`, `in_combat`, `near_spot`, `timer_expired`, `detriment_present`, `chat_seen`, `has_item`, `all`, `any` and `not_`. An unknown one is refused, and one EB cannot read in the session counts as false. [script-named-fight](#complete-script-a-named-fight-with-a-gate-phases-a-reaction-and-a-win-test), [Fights](#fights).
98. **Try a new instance alone first.** `eb ic load <file>` says what EB will not run of it. Then `eb ic run <name>` on one box, `eb ic status` and `eb ic stop`. Then `eb all ic run <name>`, typed on the tank. [ic-dry-run](#snippet-dry-run-an-instance-file).
99. **A quest pack** is `{ schema = "eb-quest/1", quest_name = "…", steps = { … } }`; each step is `{ type = "command", command = "<Verb> <args>", completed = "<journal text>" }` or `{ type = "comment", description = "…" }`. Reach a zone with `CheckZone`, walk with `MM x,y,z`, and gate each objective on the journal's own text (`CheckQuestStep "<journal text>"`). A verb EB does not handle stops the pack (*not handled*); it is never guessed or skipped. Run it with `eb ql start <line or quest>` and end it with `eb ql cancel`. [recipe-quest-pack](#snippet-recipe-a-quest-pack-with-stages-hails-and-clicks), [Quests](#quests).

**Testing and sharing rules 100 to 103**

100. **Test an EB Script with its test calls:** `script.testStart()`, `check`, `expect`, `expectNum`, `expectValue`, `mayBeEmpty`, `skip` and `testDone()`. Run it as a test with `eb script test <Name> [who]`, and read the rows with `eb script results <Name>`. The examples My First Test and Reads Check show how (EB Scripts guide 13).
101. **One box first.** A quiet spot, out of a fight, on a box nobody plays by hand, with the stop line ready. Then two boxes, then the crew. See [Check what your AI wrote](#for-ai-helpers-check-what-your-ai-wrote-step-by-step).
102. **No real names.** No real character, player, guild, account or server names in a script, its pages or its comments: made-up ones only. Take names from the script's words or options. *Why:* scripts get shared.
103. **Nothing from your PC.** No drive letters, no Windows user folders, no passwords, no account names, in a script or in a chat with your AI. Paths come from EB's own places (rules 84 and 86).

### For AI helpers: The EB library at a glance

The [Lua library](#lua-library) is EB's own code, module by module. Its examples run EB's modules on an offline stand-in for the game (the lines that use `DOCS` build that world and check the result). Read it to learn how EB works and what a command does, not as a menu of calls for your script:

- An EB Script cannot load a module (it has no `require`). It uses `script`, whose calls go through these modules for it.
- A helper loads only modules that read no game: the tested ones are `eb.relay.wire` (script-crewboard) and `eb.ui.settings.settings` (script-setting).
- The rest runs inside EB's own Lua state. A helper reaches it through `luacall EBISX_cmd`, and a `commands.*` module says which line does what.

| Module | What it is for |
| --- | --- |
| [`game`](#module-game) | The game layer: you, your target, actors near you, abilities, effects, items and the game's windows, read in batches and acted on. |
| [`eb.platform`](#module-ebplatform) | One script, both EB builds: which build this is, the clock, the frame pulse (jobs and tasks), files, settings and the log. |
| [`settings`](#module-settings) | EB's settings store: a value with a default, a change for this session, one save. |
| [`eb.events`](#module-ebevents) | Game events under EB's own names (ChatLine, ZoningFinished, LootOpened …), and how a handler reacts. |
| [`eb.registry`](#module-ebregistry) | The one table of eb commands: run a line as if typed, send it to the crew, read the help. |
| [`commands.core`](#module-commandscore) | The commands every box answers: help, status, stop, end, pause, resume, afk and reload. Each `commands.*` module covers one area the same way. |
| [`eb.relay`](#module-ebrelay) | Lines between boxes (all, others, to \<who>), every box's short state, and what the crew sends, run once. |
| [`eb.relay.wire`](#module-ebrelaywire) | The crew line format: crew words, to-lists, message ids and the state fields, with `decodeState`. Reads no game: a helper may load it. |
| [`eb.relay.group`](#module-ebrelaygroup) | Group verbs: wait for everyone at a mark, read the group, and who drives an instance (the tank). |
| [`eb.nav`](#module-ebnav) | EB's one mover: walk the zone's mesh to a point, a saved spot, after an actor or to another zone, and stop cleanly. |
| [`eb.navd`](#module-ebnavd) | The mesh router under the walker: is the mesh ready, one route, the nearest mesh point, lava and water under a point. |
| [`eb.nav_travel`](#module-ebnav_travel) | Trips to other zones over the game's own travel network (bells, spires, druid rings, the guild hall, pads), never fast travel. |
| [`eb.zone`](#module-ebzone) | The zone you are in, by the short name EB keys its mesh, travel and saved spots by. |
| [`eb.combat`](#module-ebcombat) | The combat engine: one decision per step from the cast stack. |
| [`eb.app.combat`](#module-ebappcombat) | The combat plane EB builds once per box: the cast stack, the engine, and the answers every part of EB asks. |
| [`eb.caststack.jsonstack_live`](#module-ebcaststackjsonstack_live) | The live cast stack: switch one row, or every row with a tag, during a fight (from a script: `eb tag`). |
| [`eb.coord.arbiter`](#module-ebcoordarbiter) | "Only one of us does this": one box cures or rezzes, and the next takes over if it fails. |
| [`eb.coord.rules`](#module-ebcoordrules) | Crew rules in plain words: when this happens, that box does that. |
| [`eb.ic`](#module-ebic) | The instance runner: load an instance file, and run it once or in a loop. |
| [`eb.app.ic`](#module-ebappic) | `eb ic` on a running box: start a run or a loop, its status, stop. |
| [`eb.quest`](#module-ebquest) | The quest-pack runner: load a pack, start or resume it, one step per tick, on the journal's own text. |
| [`eb.brain`](#module-ebbrain) | The autonomy brain: one goal at a time, with interrupts for death, a fight, being stuck, full bags and the rest. |
| [`eb.world`](#module-ebworld) | The one world snapshot: you, your state and your group, built once a frame and shared. |
| [`eb.economy`](#module-ebeconomy) | Bags, selling, repair, depots, the bank, mail, the broker, loot, crafting and the ledger, as one object. |
| [`eb.economy.confirm`](#module-ebeconomyconfirm) | The purchase question: Yes only when it names exactly the item you are buying. |
| [`eb.ui.settings.settings`](#module-ebuisettingssettings) | The settings catalog: every key with its label, kind, unit, range and step. Reads no game: a helper may load it. |
| [`ebkit.window`](#module-ebkitwindow) | An EB window's Lua side: the whole state it shows, and the verbs a click may run. |
| [`ebkit.jsontable`](#module-ebkitjsontable) | Plain tables to JSON and back, for files, crew messages and window states. It never raises on bad input. |
| [`ebkit.lua_fmt`](#module-ebkitlua_fmt) | Write a table as a Lua data file (`return { … }`), the format of EB's quest and instance files. |
| [`eb.compat`](#module-ebcompat) | The same output on every EB build: one number formatter (3, never 3.0), stable key order, and the 32-bit bit operations. |

The [TLO reference](#tlos) lists every game member a helper may read, with what each read costs, and the [Scripts](#scripts) page every tested complete script.

### For AI helpers: Mistakes AI helpers make, and what to write instead

These come up again and again. Search your AI's answer for them before you save a file. The rule numbers point into [the rules](#for-ai-helpers-the-rules-every-eb-script-follows). The first two groups are open; open the others by subject.

**Made-up names, and the wrong kind of script mistakes 1 to 8**

| # | The AI writes | Write this instead |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `IS.Parse`, `IS.Execute`, `echo` or `wait` in an EB Script; `script.*` in a helper; code in an instance, fight or quest file. | Pick the kind first and use only its tools ([the kinds](#first-which-kind-of-script), rules 1 to 6). |
| 2 | EB functions that do not exist: `eb.cast()`, `eb.moveTo()`, `eb.target()`, `eb.wait()`, `EB.Pause()`. | In a helper every action is an EB line: `IS.Execute("luacall EBISX_cmd <line>")`. In an EB Script: `script.eb(line, who)`, `script.moveTo`, `script.wait`, `script.say`. |
| 3 | Members `script` does not have: `script.cast`, `script.follow`, `script.sleep`, `script.log`, `script.read`. | Only the members of rule 3. Anything else is an EB line: `script.eb("cast <row>")`, `script.eb("follow <name>")`. |
| 4 | Commands EB does not have: *eb attack*, *eb move*, *eb heal*, *eb wait*, *eb loot all*. | Only what `eb help` lists (rule 44). Often meant: `eb walk x,y,z`, `eb tgt <id or name>`, `eb cast <row of the cast stack>`, `eb assist tank`, `eb loot now`, `eb hail`, `eb say group <text>`. |
| 5 | Game members that do not exist or are held back: `${Me.Archetype}`, `IsNamed` in a query, `${Me.Ability["X"].Name}`, `${Me.PctHPs}`, `${Target.HP}`. | Members the [TLO reference](#tlos) lists: `Me.Health` and `Me.Power` are percent; a named is `Type == "NamedNPC"`; the class is `Me.SubClass`; an ability's name is `.ToAbilityInfo.Name`. Try one with `eb tlocheck` (rules 29 to 36). |
| 6 | Event names that do not exist (`EQ2_onTell`, `EQ2_onDeath`), or EB's own names in `IS.AttachEvent` (`ChatLine`). | A helper attaches the names in rule 67. A tell is a chat line whose Target is you, with no ChannelName, from a speaker who is not an NPC. |
| 7 | Another bot's code: a LavishScript `.iss` (`function main`, `wait 10`), MacroQuest-style Lua (`mq.TLO`, `mq.cmd`, `mq.delay`), oc lines, another bot's console word. | EB's scripts are Lua 5.4 of their own. Reads are ISXEQ2 members read as text with `IS.Parse`; actions are `IS.Execute` lines or EB lines (rules 42 and 64). |
| 8 | The Lua library's examples pasted into a script: `require("eb.platform").game()`, `pulse.spawn`, `eb.delay`, `eb.dispatch`, the `DOCS` lines. | Those show EB's own modules on the offline test world. A helper reads with `IS.Parse` and acts with `luacall EBISX_cmd`; an EB Script uses `script`. A helper may load only `eb.relay.wire` and `eb.ui.settings.settings` (rule 90). |

**Lua, time and loops mistakes 9 to 14**

| # | The AI writes | Write this instead |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 9 | Lua 5.1 or LuaJIT: `unpack`, `loadstring`, `setfenv`, `table.getn`, `math.pow`, `math.atan2`, `require("bit")`, `require("ffi")`. | `table.unpack`, `load`, `#t`, `x ^ y`, `math.atan(y, x)`, Lua 5.4's own `& \| ~ << >>` (rule 18). |
| 10 | Other languages: `!=`, `+=`, `++`, `&&`, `\|\|`, `continue`, `a ? b : c`. | `~=`, `x = x + 1`, `and`, `or`, `not`, `goto continue` with a `::continue::` label, `if … then … else … end` (rule 19). |
| 11 | `string.format("%d", x)` on a number with a fraction: health 87.5, a distance, a spot. | `math.floor(x + 0.5)` first, or `%.1f`; write a spot for `eb walk x,y,z` with `%.1f` (rule 20). |
| 12 | `os.time()`, `os.clock()` or `os.date()`; `os.execute` or `io.popen`. | `require("socket").gettime()` in a helper; `script.now()` and `script.unix()` in an EB Script. Nothing starts another program (rules 26 and 92). |
| 13 | A loop that never waits, or a wait in the wrong unit: `wait(500)` meant as half a second. | Every loop waits, in seconds: `wait(0.5)`, `waitframe()`, `script.wait(1)`. A few checks a second is plenty (rules 22 and 23). |
| 14 | A wait, or the real work, inside an event handler or a registered function. | The handler notes a small record and returns; the main loop reads the game and acts (rule 65, [script-eventwatch](#complete-script-event-watcher)). |

**Reading the game mistakes 15 to 22**

| # | The AI writes | Write this instead |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 15 | One `IS.Parse` per member, every frame. | One `IS.Parse` a round with every member, joined by a separator, a few rounds a second (rule 30, [script-groupready](#complete-script-group-ready-checker)). |
| 16 | Answers used as Lua values: `if IS.Parse("${Me.IsDead}") then`, maths on text, `(exists)` compared with `FALSE`. | `== "TRUE"`, `tonumber()`, and `(exists)` reads `TRUE` or `NULL`; guard nil with `tostring(IS.Parse(…) or "")` (rule 31). |
| 17 | A batch split on `\|` where a value can hold one (a name, a chat line), or a batch past 8 KB. | `~^~` for names and text, a check of the number of pieces, and 10 to 20 rows at most (rule 30). |
| 18 | An effect's name, `ToItemInfo` or `ToAbilityInfo` read every round. | The plain fields each round (`CountEffects`, `Effect[n].Type`), a name once per new id kept in a table, and `Me.Maintained[n].Name` for maintained spells (rule 32, [script-buffkeeper](#complete-script-buff-keeper)). |
| 19 | `LootWindow`, `MerchantWindow` or `RewardWindow` read while no window is open; `${Zone.Name}` acted on while a zone loads. | Read a window after its event; read the zone after `EQ2_FinishedZoning` (rules 33 and 34). |
| 20 | `EQ2UIPage[…].Child[3]` or `ChildType` to find a button. | The element by its full name: `EQ2UIPage[<window>,<page>].Child[<type>,<full.name>]` (rule 38). |
| 21 | `Me.InCombat` as "a fight is on"; `Me.Group[0]` as another member; a member's ID or distance in another zone; `Me.Inventory` for worn gear. | `Me.IsHated`; `Me.Group[1]` to `[5]`; `InZone == "TRUE"` first; `Me.Equipment[<slot>]` (rule 35). |
| 22 | `EQ2:QueryActors` every frame, into a variable named like a game object (`Target`, `Actor`), with an untested term. | About once a second, into an `index:actor` of your own (an `EBH_` name, declared once with `squelch`, cleared first), tested terms only, 10 to 20 rows in one batch (rule 37, [script-namedwatch](#complete-script-say-when-a-named-spawns)). |

**Commands, the crew and events mistakes 23 to 30**

| # | The AI writes | Write this instead |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 23 | The console word typed from a script: `IS.Execute("eb pause")`. | `IS.Execute("luacall EBISX_cmd pause")`: the word may be `ebi` (rule 42). |
| 24 | `IS.Execute`'s return read as EB's answer, or a command assumed to have worked. | EB answers on the console. Check the result in the game (`Me.IsMoving` after `marks go`) or in the crew's next state (rule 46, [script-patrol](#complete-script-patrol-between-saved-marks)). |
| 25 | An EB line sent every round: pause, follow, walk. | Once per change, with a margin so it never flips back and forth (rule 47, [script-bagwatch](#complete-script-pause-eb-when-the-bags-are-full)). |
| 26 | A luacall line of more than 40 words, or one that carries chat text. | Short lines, and chat text never (rules 45 and 49). |
| 27 | Chat text, typed text or a name put straight into a line: `IS.Execute("eq2execute tell " .. speaker .. " " .. text)`. | Clean it first: drop `${` and line breaks, keep a name to letters, digits and `'`, refuse a quote or a backslash (rule 49, [script-tellreply](#complete-script-answer-tells-while-you-are-away)). |
| 28 | Every event forwarded to the crew, or `all` where this box must not act too. | One deliberate line per decision: `others` leaves this box out, `to is2` reaches one box (rule 59, [script-followme](#complete-script-crew-follow-me)). |
| 29 | The crew keyed by character name; real names in a script. | Key boxes by the session id (`is1`, `is2`: EBISX_State2's box); made-up names only (rules 61 and 102). |
| 30 | A handler on an event a script must not attach: `EQ2_onQuestUpdate`, or EB's old `EBISX_State`. | `EBISX_QuestUpdate` (7 arguments) for quest progress; `EBISX_State2` for the crew, decoded with `decodeState` (rules 61, 62 and 66, [script-crewboard](#complete-script-crew-status-board)). |

**Moving, fighting and popups mistakes 31 to 37**

| # | The AI writes | Write this instead |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 31 | The character moved by the script itself: held keys, a face-and-run loop, `eb.move`, a straight line to a point. | Every move handed to EB: `eb walk x,y,z`, `eb marks go <mark>`, `eb follow <name>`, `eb goto <zone>`, `script.moveTo`; then watch `Me.IsMoving` (rules 51 and 52). |
| 32 | "Then walk straight there" when EB finds no route. | No route means no walk: report it, try another spot the player marked, or stop (rule 53). |
| 33 | Travel that skips the walk: `eb ft` in a script, `FastTravel` or `FlyUp` in a pack, a teleport step in an instance. | `eb goto <zone>` (bells, spires, druid rings, the guild hall, zone lines, doors); in a pack `CheckZone` and `MM x,y,z`. EB never fast travels on its own (rule 54). |
| 34 | A helper that starts fights: it targets the nearest NPC and casts at it. | Fights belong to EB's combat and the cast stack: follow the tank's choice onto a mob that already fights, or `eb assist tank`. EB never fights a guard (rule 57, [script-assist](#complete-script-follow-and-assist-the-tank)). |
| 35 | A helper that does a job EB also does (cures, buffs, loot), so the two act on one target or window. | Switch EB's off first: `eb cures off`, the buffs left out of the cast stack, `eb loot off` (rule 58). |
| 36 | Target and cast in one breath, or a cast with no check that it can go. | One read of dead, casting and `IsReady`; `Actor[id,<id>]:DoTarget`; wait until `${Target.ID}` is that id (`waituntil(fn, 1)`); then `:Use`, wait for the cast bar, and go back to the old target ([script-autocure](#complete-script-auto-cure-watcher)). |
| 37 | A yes/no window or a reward clicked by the script; a reply picked by its number blindly. | Say what is asked ([script-choicealert](#complete-script-tell-me-when-a-yesno-question-waits)); `eb purchase expect "<item>"` for your own buy; pick a reply by its words, and stop when none matches (rules 40 and 41). |

**Places, files, data files and testing mistakes 38 to 50**

| # | The AI writes | Write this instead |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 38 | A helper that attaches its events and then ends. | A main loop that waits, until `endlua <name>` (rule 27). |
| 39 | A helper saved in `Scripts/EBIS` or EB's own folder, or started with `runscript`. | InnerSpace's `Scripts` folder, started with `lua <name>`; `runscript` is for LavishScript files (rule 8). |
| 40 | An EB Script in a folder below the scripts folder, with a name EB does not take, or an example changed where it is. | `eb script new <Name>`, or a `.lua` directly in the scripts folder; `eb script copy <Example> [new name]` before a change (rules 7 and 10). |
| 41 | Functions a button or page calls written `local`, or below the loop; `var=` names that are Lua words or sandbox names. | Global functions above the loop; `var=` names of letters, digits and `_`, never `script`, `string`, `table`, `math`, `print` or another sandbox name (rule 74). |
| 42 | `script.target().name` with nothing targeted; `me.health` out of the world; a page's `data-eb-line` with a crew word. | `local t = script.target()` may be nil; `if me.inGame then … end`; no crew word in a page's line: its Who says where it goes (rules 28 and 76). |
| 43 | Hard-coded folders: a drive letter, a Windows user folder. | A helper builds paths from `${LavishScript.HomeDirectory}` or boot.json's `root`; an EB Script's paths are relative to its scripts folder (rules 84 and 86). |
| 44 | EB's settings, marks or places files edited by hand while EB runs. | `eb set <key> <value>`, `eb marks set\|del <name>`, `eb bl` and `eb gl`; for a file edit, `eb stop` first (rules 79 and 81). |
| 45 | Coordinates, zone names or names of NPCs, doors, abilities and items guessed. | `eb marks set <name>` on each spot; names copied exactly, abilities with their rank; anything missing asked of the player. |
