| 46 | An instance or quest file with code in it, no schema, a step with no id, an act EB does not have, or a spot that is not three numbers. | `return { … }` with `schema = "eb.ic/1"` or `"eb-quest/1"`, unique step ids, known acts and `{ x, y, z }` spots (rules 93 to 95). |
| 47 | The group walking the hub route, or each box zoning itself in. | Every box travels to the hub zone; the tank alone walks to the door and zones the group in; inside, the group holds on the tank's camp spots (rule 96). |
| 48 | A named fight with no gate and no win test; quest steps that never check the journal. | `when = { { actor_present = "<name>" }, { in_combat = false } }` and `done = { { actor_dead = "<name>" } }`; `CheckQuestStep "<journal text>"` after each objective (rules 97 and 99). |
| 49 | An ISXLUA helper written for an EB Boxer player. | An EB Script or a data file: ask which build first, from the first line of `eb status` (rule 6). |
| 50 | A new script tried first on every box, in a fight, or on the box played by hand; *held back until it is proven live* worked around with raw game lines. | One box, a quiet spot, then two boxes, then the crew; script around a held-back call, and send only the game lines of rule 50 (rules 50 and 101). |

### For AI helpers: Check what your AI wrote, step by step

1. **Read the answer before you save anything.** Each file must say where it goes, and how it starts and stops:
   - a helper: `InnerSpace/Scripts/<name>.lua`, `lua <name>` and `endlua <name>`;
   - an EB Script: the scripts folder in EB's data folder, `eb script run <Name>` and `eb script stop <Name>`;
   - an instance: `data/ebic/authored/instances/<folder>/`, `eb ic run authored/<folder>` and `eb ic stop`;
   - a quest pack: `data/ebquests/authored/`, `eb ql start <quest>` and `eb ql cancel`.
2. **Search it for what must not be there.** Send the answer back if you find any of these:
   - `os.time`, `os.execute`, `io.popen`, `ffi`, `require("bit")`, `unpack(`, `!=` or `+=` (rules 18, 19, 26 and 92);
   - `press -hold`, `eb key … hold`, `FastTravel`, `FlyUp` or `eb ft` (rules 52 and 54);
   - an oc line, another bot's word, `mq.` or a LavishScript `.iss` (rule 64);
   - `DoChoice`, `AcceptReward` or a click on a ChoiceWindow (rule 40);
   - a handler on `EQ2_onQuestUpdate` or on EB's old `EBISX_State`: a helper must never attach either (rules 62 and 66);
   - `IS.Share`, a drive letter, a Windows user folder, or a real name (rules 91, 102 and 103).
3. **Check that EB is up where it will run.** `eb status` answers (its first line names the build), and `eb version` says which EB it is. A helper that sends EB lines needs EB running in that same session.
4. **Check every command it sends.** `eb help <command>` prints its words and whether it takes a crew word. Then type the line once by hand, and read EB's answer. *Is not an eb command* or *does not answer on this box yet* means the line is wrong, or not switched on here.
5. **Check every game member it reads.** `eb tlocheck Me.InventorySlotsFree` (with or without `${ }`) answers the value and how long the read took, or that EB holds it back, that it is known bad, or that EB does not know it. A member the [TLO reference](#tlos) does not list is one EB has not checked: ask your AI for another way.
6. **Get ready on one box.** A quiet spot, out of a fight, on a box you are not playing by hand. Switch off the part of EB the script does itself (`eb cures off`, `eb loot off` …). Keep the stops ready: `endlua <name>` or `eb script stop <Name>` ends the script; `eb all stop` halts every box's runs, walks and goals while the fight goes on; `eb freeze` also stops casting; `eb resume` goes on.
7. **Start it the way its kind starts.**
   - A helper: save it in InnerSpace's `Scripts` folder and type `lua <name> [words]` in that session's console. Its `echo` lines and its errors show there.
   - An EB Script: `eb script reload`, then `eb script info <Name>` (it lists any header line EB could not read, with its line number and why), `eb script test <Name>` when it has tests, then `eb script run <Name>` (this box only).
   - An instance: `eb ic load <file>`, then `eb ic run <name>` on one box; `eb ic status` says how it stands.
   - A quest pack: `eb ql start <quest>`, then `eb ql status`.
8. **Read the console while it runs:** the script's own lines, EB's `[eb]` answers to what it sent, and any error. [What EB prints](#for-ai-helpers-check-what-your-ai-wrote-step-by-step), below the steps, says what each line means.
9. **Watch EB's side as well.** `eb status` for this box, `eb status crew` for every box (zone, mode, health, power, fighting), `eb status nav` for a walk, `eb status combat` for the cast stack, and `eb status goal` or `eb ic status` for a run.
10. **Make it happen on purpose.** Cause what it watches for (a tell, full bags, a named in range, a mark to walk to) and check that it acts once. Take the cause away and check that it settles. Cause it again and check that it acts again.
11. **Check the frame rate.** `eb fps` with the script running and without it; `eb fps reads` lists the game reads by kind. A clear drop means too many reads, or a loop that waits too little: give your AI those numbers.
12. **Change zone once with it running.** Nothing should happen during the load, and it should pick up again in the new zone.
13. **Leave it running for 15 minutes or so.** No line repeated over and over, no console that keeps filling, and a steady frame rate.
14. **Then two boxes, then the crew.** `eb to is2 <line>` or the Scripts window's Who; for an instance, `eb all ic run <name>` typed on the tank, with `eb all stop` ready.
15. **Stop it and check nothing is left behind.** `endlua <name>`, `eb script stop <Name>` or `eb ic stop`; `eb status nav` shows no walk; `eb resume` if it paused the crew; switch back on what you switched off.
16. **When something is wrong, send it back.** Give your AI the script, the exact console lines (character names replaced) and what you saw happen, and ask for the smallest change that fixes it, not a rewrite ([the message](#what-to-send-back-when-it-fails)). Then test again from step 3.

**What EB prints, and what it means 15 lines**

| You see | What it means, and what to send back |
| --- | --- |
| `[Name] stopped on a mistake: Name:12: …` | An EB Script hit a Lua error on that line. Send the line and the script. |
| `it ran too long without waiting` | An EB Script loop with no `script.wait` in it (rule 22). |
| `has no function X` | A button or page calls a function that is local, below the loop, or missing, or the script is not running (rule 74). |
| `not an EB line` | `script.eb`, a header button or a page's line names a command EB does not have: try it with `eb help <word>` (rule 44). |
| `a page's EB line carries no crew word` | A page's `data-eb-line` has all, others, to or relay in it (rule 76). |
| `no script called …` | That PC's scripts folder does not have the script (rule 11). |
| `… is not started here` | That box is paused (played by hand), or EB is stopped on it (rule 17). |
| A Lua error naming the helper's file and line | The helper called something ISXLUA or Lua 5.4 does not have (*attempt to call a nil value*), or did maths on text. Send the error line. |
| `refused: '…' is not an eb command` | The line's verb does not exist (rule 44). |
| `refused: eb … does not answer on this box yet` | The part of EB behind that command did not start on this box; `eb status bot` lists what did. |
| `refused: eb … runs on this box only` | That command takes no crew word (rule 59). |
| `held back until it is proven live` | EB refused, on purpose, a game read or click it has not proven yet. Script around it (rule 50). |
| `no route on the .nav: …` or `no mesh: …` | The walk was not made: the mesh has no way there, or this PC has no mesh for the zone yet (rule 53). |
| `the IC did not load: …` | An instance file was refused at load; the rest of the line says why (rules 93 to 96). |
| No `[eb]` answer to a luacall line | EB is not running in that session, so no `EBISX_cmd` is registered there (rule 16). |

#### What to send back when it fails

Send this back:

```
The script you wrote does not work yet. Fix only what is wrong, and keep the rest as it is.

The whole script, as I ran it:
[paste the file]

The line I typed to start it:
[for example: lua eb_bagwatch free=3]

What the console said, from the start line to the error (character names replaced):
[paste the lines exactly]

What I saw in the game:
[for example: nothing paused, or it paused and went on every two seconds]

Use only what the EB guide lists. Say what was wrong, then give me the whole fixed file.
```

### For AI helpers: A worked example

The request filled in under [How to ask](#for-ai-helpers-how-to-ask), answered by a complete tested script: save it and run it as its card says.

#### Complete script: Pause EB when the bags are full

A drop-in script that pauses EB (this box, or the whole crew) when your bags drop under a number of free slots, and resumes it once there is room again.

**Where it goes:** `InnerSpace/Scripts/eb_bagwatch.lua`

**Get the file:** [examples/script-bagwatch.lua](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jiimboeq2/EB-Docs/main/examples/script-bagwatch.lua) (save it as eb_bagwatch.lua)

**Run it:**

```text
lua eb_bagwatch free=3
lua eb_bagwatch free=3 crew
endlua eb_bagwatch
```

**Needs:**

- EB for InnerSpace running in this session (eb status answers)

**Tested:** Pauses EB once when the free slots fall under the mark and resumes it once when you made room.

**Verified:** tested offline: run end to end on EB's offline stand-in for the game; not run in the live game yet, so try it on one box first

```lua
-- eb_bagwatch.lua - stop EB filling bags it cannot empty. Every two seconds it reads how many bag slots are free (one
-- read). Under the mark it sends EB "pause" through EB's console word - "all pause" with the word crew, so every box
-- stops - and once you made room (two slots past the mark, so it does not flip back and forth) it sends "resume".
-- EB answers in the console; a script hears no reply.
--
--   lua eb_bagwatch [free=<slots>] [crew]      start it (free: default 3)
--   endlua eb_bagwatch                         stop it

local low, crew = 3, false
for _, a in ipairs({ ... }) do
    local n = tostring(a):match("^free=(%d+)$")
    if n then
        low = tonumber(n)
    elseif a == "crew" then
        crew = true
    else
        echo("usage: lua eb_bagwatch [free=<slots>] [crew]")
        return
    end
end

local paused = false
echo(("eb_bagwatch: pausing %s under %d free bag slot(s) - endlua eb_bagwatch stops it"):format(
    crew and "the crew" or "EB", low))
while true do
    local free = tonumber(IS.Parse("${Me.InventorySlotsFree}"))
    if free then
        if not paused and free < low then
            IS.Execute(crew and "luacall EBISX_cmd all pause" or "luacall EBISX_cmd pause")
            echo(("eb_bagwatch: %d bag slot(s) free - paused"):format(free))
            paused = true
        elseif paused and free >= low + 2 then
            IS.Execute(crew and "luacall EBISX_cmd all resume" or "luacall EBISX_cmd resume")
            echo(("eb_bagwatch: %d bag slot(s) free - resumed"):format(free))
            paused = false
        end
    end
    wait(2)
end
```

#### How it keeps the rules

- **The kind is a helper:** one file, `InnerSpace/Scripts/eb_bagwatch.lua`, started with `lua eb_bagwatch free=3` and stopped with `endlua eb_bagwatch` (rules 8 and 13).
- **It checks its words** (`free=<slots>` and `crew`), and on a bad one prints its usage line and returns (rule 14).
- **One read a round:** `${Me.InventorySlotsFree}`, a member the TLO reference lists, turned into a number with `tonumber`, and skipped when it is not one (rules 29 and 31).
- **Its loop waits** two seconds every round, with ISXLUA's `wait`, which takes seconds (rules 22 and 23).
- **It talks to EB only through its door:** `luacall EBISX_cmd pause`, or `luacall EBISX_cmd all pause` with the word crew (rules 42 and 59).
- **Once per change:** a `paused` flag, and it goes on only two slots past the mark, so it never flips back and forth (rule 47).
- **It expects no reply:** EB answers on the console, and the script says what it did with `echo` (rule 46).
- **It leaves the rest alone:** no `os.time`, no movement, no item touched, no other bot, no names.

#### Try it

1. On the card, press *Download as file*, and save the file in InnerSpace's `Scripts` folder as `eb_bagwatch.lua`.
2. In a session where EB runs (`eb status` answers), type `lua eb_bagwatch free=3`, or `lua eb_bagwatch free=3 crew` for the whole crew.
3. Fill your bags until fewer than 3 slots are free. The console says `eb_bagwatch: 2 bag slot(s) free - paused`, and EB pauses.
4. Make room for 5 free slots. It says `… - resumed`, and EB goes on.
5. Type `endlua eb_bagwatch` to stop it.

## Quick start

Get EB playing your characters, learn the first commands, and save your first script. The other guides are about writing your own.

### Quick start: What EB is

EB is a private EverQuest II bot for a small group of testers. It plays your characters for you: each one fights with its own cast stack, and the whole crew can quest, run instances and travel together.

This page takes you from an account to EB running in the game, then to your first script.

EB comes in two builds that share one Lua codebase:

- **EB for InnerSpace** runs inside InnerSpace, on ISXEQ2 and ISXLUA (Lua 5.4). It is the stable, recommended build, on Windows and on Linux, and the one EB Setup picks for you.
- **EB Boxer** is EB's own standalone engine, the NON-ISX build. It doesn't need InnerSpace. It is still in testing: EB Setup installs it only after you tick *I understand EB Boxer is still in testing*.

These docs are written for EB for InnerSpace. Where a window opens on one build only, `eb windows all` says so, and why.

### Quick start: The short version

1. Get an EB account from your admin.
2. Download EB Setup from the [Download page](https://eb.jiimbo.dev/download.html) and open it. On Linux, make the file executable first.
3. Press *Set it all up for me*, sign in, and let the update finish.
4. Add your characters' logins, then press *Play* next to one.
5. Wait for the character to reach the world, and look at that session's InnerSpace console.

**You should see** `[eb] EB for InnerSpace is up - 'eb status', 'eb stop'`

Now type `eb status crew` in that console. It shows this box and every other box it hears: the zone, health and power of each, and whether it is fighting.

Each step is explained below. Then save [your first script](#quick-start-your-first-script).

### Quick start: What you need

- A PC with Windows 10 or 11, or Linux with EverQuest II under Wine.
- EverQuest II.
- For EB for InnerSpace: InnerSpace with the ISXEQ2 extension. If your InnerSpace has no ISXLUA, EB Setup adds it, and ISXIM too (only EB IRC needs that one). It never replaces a copy you already have.
- An EB account with an active subscription.

EB Setup's Version step checks what your PC has, and says what is missing and how to fix it. On Linux it checks the game's Wine prefix too: see [On Linux](#on-linux).

### Quick start: Your account

1. Ask your admin for an account. Accounts are invite-only: you get a username and a password.
2. Sign in on [your account page](https://eb.jiimbo.dev/account.html). Its Account tab shows your role and whether your subscription is active. Updates need an active one.
3. Optional: press *Link Discord* on the Account tab. From then on, *Sign in with Discord* works on the sign-in page.

A sign-in on this website lasts at most a day. EB Setup keeps its own sign-in, for as long as you choose.

### Quick start: Install with EB Setup

EB Setup is one file. It installs EB, keeps it up to date, and starts your characters.

#### Get it

1. Download EB Setup from the [Download page](https://eb.jiimbo.dev/download.html), or from your account's Download tab: `EB-Setup-<version>.exe` for Windows, `EB-Setup-<version>-linux-x86_64` for Linux.
2. Open it. If Windows SmartScreen warns the first time, press *More info*, then *Run anyway*. On Linux, make the file executable first, as [On Linux](#on-linux) says.

#### Go through its seven steps

The rail on the left of EB Setup shows the steps, with the one you are on lit.

1. **Welcome.** Press *Set it all up for me*. It makes the usual choices for you and goes straight on to Sign in, stopping at Version only when something is missing. *Let me choose* shows every choice first.
2. **Version.** Keep *EB for InnerSpace*, the recommended one. Its card lists what it needs, with the fix for anything missing.
3. **Folders.** Check your EB folder, EverQuest II and InnerSpace. Each one is found and checked for you.
4. **Sign in.** Type your EB username and password, and pick how long EB Setup keeps you signed in: *A day*, *A week*, *A year* or *Don't sign me out*.
5. **Update.** Wait while EB Setup downloads EB: only the files that changed, each one checked before it replaces anything. Then press *Continue*.
6. **Characters.** Import the logins you already saved on this PC, or press *Add a login*. Tick each character that should start with *Play ticked*. An account name or a password is never shown again.
7. **Play.** Press *Play* next to a character. EB opens the game, logs that character in, and starts in the world.

> [!NOTE]
> **InnerSpace can stay open.** EB gets its own game profile, *EverQuest 2 EB*, and no other profile is changed. With no game running, EB Setup restarts InnerSpace by itself to put the profile in, and says so. With a game running, the profile goes in the next time InnerSpace starts: EB Setup never closes a game.

#### The Play page

Besides a *Play* button per character and *Play ticked* (every ticked character, one after another), the Play page has one *Play team* button per ISBoxer team. Its *Windows and shortcuts* tab picks a monitor per character, keeps game windows off the main monitor, and makes desktop shortcuts that play without opening EB Setup. Its *What got set up* tab lists what EB Setup did on this PC.

An ISBoxer team needs one change in ISBoxer before *Play team* works. Until then the team shows *! One change in ISBoxer first*.

1. In ISBoxer Toolkit, open Characters, and set the Game Profile of each of the team's characters to *EverQuest 2 EB*.
2. Press *Export All to Inner Space*.
3. Back in EB Setup, press *Check again*.

#### Zone maps

EB walks each zone on its map (a nav mesh). While EB Setup is open, it gets every zone's map in the background, and *Play* never waits for them. If a character reaches a zone whose map is not here yet, EB asks EB Setup for that map first. *Zone maps…*, on the Update and Play steps, lets you untick groups of zones to save disk space. In the game, `eb nav status` says whether this zone's map is in.

#### On Linux

On Linux, EverQuest II runs under Wine (plain Wine, Lutris, Bottles or Steam's Proton), and EB runs inside the game's own Wine prefix: EB Setup finds it. After downloading, make the file executable (`chmod +x`, or Properties → Permissions → Allow executing) and open it.

The same seven steps follow, with the same choice as on Windows: EB for InnerSpace (recommended), with InnerSpace installed inside that prefix, or EB Boxer (NON-ISX). For EB for InnerSpace, the Version step checks the prefix and has a button for each fix:

- **InnerSpace.** EB Setup never downloads it for you. Download InnerSpace yourself, then press *Run the installer you downloaded…* to install it into the prefix. Its first start asks for your own InnerSpace sign-in, which EB Setup never sees.
- **.NET 3.5 SP1**, which ISXLUA runs on: *Install .NET 3.5 SP1* puts it in with winetricks (about 230 MB to download, and around 15 minutes).
- **InnerSpace's .NET parts**: *Put them in* adds them.

ISBoxer teams and picking a monitor are Windows only.

### Quick start: First launch

Each character plays in its own InnerSpace session, and each session runs its own EB.

1. Press *Play* next to a character in EB Setup.
2. Wait. The session logs that character in, and EB starts by itself once the character is in the world.
3. Read that session's InnerSpace console. EB says whether every part of it started (`… - every part started`, or `… but 1 part did NOT start:` with the reason), then gives a `cast stack:` line and a `windows:` line.
4. Then comes `[eb] EB for InnerSpace is up - 'eb status', 'eb stop'`: EB is ready.
5. Start your other characters the same way, or press *Play ticked* to start every ticked one, one after another.

#### When you target a mob

When you target a mob this box can fight, within 30 m, EB starts the fight at once with this character's cast stack. In a group, the boxes EB drives fight what the group's lead targets. This is `eb engage`, on by default and kept per character.

- It never starts a fight in a city or a guild hall, unless you turn that on: `eb engage cities on`.
- A box EB is paused on (one you play by hand) never starts a fight by itself.
- `eb engage off` turns it off for this character. `eb engage status` says why it last did or did not start a fight.

#### A session you open yourself

You can also launch EverQuest II from InnerSpace with the game profile *EverQuest 2 EB*. Which character a session plays comes from the box list, by the session's name: with no box list of your own, your ticked characters play `is1`, `is2` and so on, in turn, and the first one leads. Once they are all in the world, the lead box groups the others up.

- `eb login boxes` shows the box list.
- `eb login <box>`, typed in a session that has not logged in yet, makes it play that box.

To start EB by hand in a session you opened some other way, type these two lines in its console. That session needs ISXEQ2 loaded too: EB waits for it.

```text
ext isxlua
lua eb start
```

If EB Setup said `lua eb start` isn't set up on this PC (InnerSpace already had its own `eb.lua`), type `lua EBIS/eb_isx_boot now` instead.

### Quick start: The eb console

You talk to EB with lines that start with `eb`, typed in a session's InnerSpace console or on EB Console's command line. EB answers in the same console.

Try these three in one session:

1. `eb help` lists EB's command groups and opens the EB Help window.
2. `eb pause` holds this box where it is. The fight goes on.
3. `eb resume` lets it go on.

#### Commands to know first

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `eb help` | Lists the command groups and opens EB Help. `eb help ic` lists one group; `eb help pause` shows one command: what it takes, and which crew words it accepts. `eb help list` only prints. |
| `eb status` | A few lines on EB in this session: whether it runs, its events, movement and windows. |
| `eb status bot` | The full report: which parts of EB started, any that did not and why, the crew, the cast stack and what this box is doing. |
| `eb status crew` | This box and every box it hears: zone, what it is doing, health, power, and whether it is fighting. |
| `eb status goal` | The instance run and the goal this box is on. `eb status nav` shows the walk, and `eb status combat` the cast stack. |
| `eb pause` | Holds quests, instance runs, walking and goals where they are. The fight goes on. `eb resume` goes on. |
| `eb freeze` | Stops everything at once, the cast going now too, and nothing is cast until `eb resume`. |
| `eb stopall` | The kill switch: stops quests, instance runs, walking and goals on this box. The fight goes on, so the character stays alive. EB stays loaded, and `eb resume` starts again. |
| `eb end ic` | Ends one thing and leaves the rest: `quest`, `ic`, `nav`, `hunt`, `craft`, `harvest` or `all`. |
| `eb reload` | Loads EB again in this session; the game and the character stay. A box in a run reloads once the run is over (`eb reload cancel` drops that). |
| `eb stop` | Typed in a session's console, ends EB there. The game and the character stay. `lua eb start` starts it again. |

In the game, `eb help` always matches the EB you run. On the web, the [Commands](#commands) page lets you browse and search EB's commands.

### Quick start: Your crew

Every EB tells the other InnerSpace sessions who and where it is, every two seconds: together they are your crew. A box is named by its InnerSpace session (`is1`, `is2` …), and a box that goes quiet for nine seconds drops out.

To send a line to the crew, put a crew word in front of the command:

| You type | Who runs it |
| --- | --- |
| `eb pause` | This box only (the default). |
| `eb all pause` | Every box, this one too. |
| `eb others pause` | Every box but this one. |
| `eb to is2 pause` | The boxes the list names: a box (`is2`), a character, a class (`warden`) or an archetype (`priest`). Separate several with commas: `eb to is2,is3 pause`. |
| `eb relay mygroup pause` | This character's group, this box too. |
| `eb all stop` | The crew's kill switch: every box halts, as `eb stopall` does. `eb all resume` lets them go. |

- A line that reaches another box runs there once, and is never sent on again.
- To type into one session from another, use InnerSpace's own relay: `relay is2 eb mini`. It works for commands that run on one box only. Careful: `relay is2 eb stop` ends EB in is2, while `eb to is2 stop` only halts it.
- To play a character yourself, pause EB on it first. EB never moves a character it is paused on, and never starts a fight on it by itself. `eb all resume` resumes it too, so use `eb others resume` for the rest.
- For instance runs, the box you type the run on leads, and the others follow it: see [Instances](#instances).
- Boxes on several PCs can be one crew, with `eb crew link` (off until you set it up).

[Crew and group](#crew-and-group) has every crew word, and how leads and followers work.

### Quick start: EB's windows

On a crew, EB's windows open by themselves only on the lead box: the lowest session EB hears (`is1` in a team), or a box that runs alone. There the mini, EB Console, EB Main and the MCP open once EB is up. The other boxes open nothing by themselves, and say so:

`windows: nothing opens by itself on this box - is1 leads the crew and has the windows (eb mini / eb console open / eb ui / eb mcp, or Control + ~, open one here)`

Window commands run on one box only. To open a window on such a box:

1. Go to that box's own console.
2. Type `eb mini`, `eb ui`, `eb mcp` or `eb console open`, or press `Control` + `~` for EB Console.

From another session, `relay is2 eb mini` does the same. To have every box open its own windows from its next start, type `eb all set ui.open_on_load all` once (`lead` is the default; `off` keeps EB Main and the MCP shut until you open them).

#### The four you meet first

- **EB mini** (`eb mini`): this character's switches (EB, Pause, Follow, Move, Camp, DPS, Combat, Buffs, Pet, Loot), with EB Main, the MCP and *Stop group* one click away. A switch changes this character only, unless the mini's *Group* button is lit: then it flips on every box of your group. *Stop group* and *Go on* always reach the whole group. The mini's X keeps it closed on this character until `eb mini`.
- **EB Main** (`eb ui`): the crew at a glance, *Start*, *Pause* and *Stop all* for every box, and the way into every EB window.
- **EB Console** (`Control` + `~`): chat with the crew, type EB's commands, and see every command EB runs, with who started it.
- **The MCP**, the Master Control Panel (`eb mcp`): a button for every EB command, for the whole crew or one box.

A press on a window does what the matching typed line does. The windows are drawn by EB Overlay Host, a small program EB starts beside the game.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `eb windows` | Lists every EB window by what it is for, with the line that opens each. |
| `eb windows main` | Opens one window by its word: EB Main's is `main`, the mini's `mini`. Add `hide` to close it, or `toggle`. |
| `eb windows all` | Every window, with the reason one does not open on this box. |
| `eb windows reset` | Puts this character's EB windows back at their default place and size. |

More on each window in [UI windows](#ui-windows).

### Quick start: Updates

1. Open EB Setup again. If you signed in before, it skips the first-time steps and goes straight to the update.
2. If a newer EB Setup is out, it replaces itself first and says *EB Setup updated to* the new version.
3. It updates EB, only the files that changed, then opens the Play page. Nothing starts until you press *Play*.

- Sessions already running take the new EB by themselves: EB Setup tells each one to `eb reload`. A session in the middle of a run reloads once the run is over.
- Files EB writes for you (settings, learned data, your own files) are never part of an update, so an update leaves them alone.
- Releases come on two channels: Stable (EB for InnerSpace) and NON-ISX (EB Boxer). Your account's Download tab shows the newest on each. EB Setup takes the channel of the build you picked, so there is nothing to choose.

### Quick start: Your first script

A script is a small Lua file beside EB. It sends EB the same lines you type. This one makes your crew follow the character you drive.

1. On the card below, press *Download as file*, and save the file in InnerSpace's `Scripts` folder as `eb_followme.lua`.
2. In the session of the character you drive, type `lua eb_followme 4`. The 4 is how close, in metres, the others keep.
3. Watch the other boxes start to follow. After each zone load, the script tells them again.
4. To stop, type `endlua eb_followme`, then `eb others follow off` to end the follow itself.

#### Complete script: Crew, follow me

A drop-in script for the box you drive by hand: it tells every other EB box to follow you, and tells them again after each zone load, so the boxes that came through with you pick the follow back up.

**Where it goes:** `InnerSpace/Scripts/eb_followme.lua`

**Get the file:** [examples/script-followme.lua](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jiimboeq2/EB-Docs/main/examples/script-followme.lua) (save it as eb_followme.lua)

**Run it:**

```text
lua eb_followme 4
endlua eb_followme
```

**Needs:**

- EB for InnerSpace running on this box and on the crew's boxes (eb status crew lists them)
- the crew in your group, in the same zone as you

**Tested:** Sends eb others follow \<you> at start and again after a zone load; this box itself never follows.

**Verified:** tested offline: run end to end on EB's offline stand-in for the game; not run in the live game yet, so try it on one box first

```lua
-- eb_followme.lua - the crew follows the box you drive.
--
--   lua eb_followme [metres]     start it on YOUR box: how close they keep (EB's own follow distance if left out)
--   endlua eb_followme           stop re-sending (each box keeps following until its EB stops or walks elsewhere)
--
-- It sends ONE crew line - `eb others follow <your name> [metres]` - through this box's EB, which carries it to
-- every other box (the "others" scope: never this one). A zone load ends a follow, so after each one it waits three
-- seconds for the boxes that came along to finish loading, and sends the line again.

local dist = tonumber((...))
local me = tostring(IS.Parse("${Me.Name}") or ""):gsub("[^%w']", "")
if me == "" then echo("eb_followme: start it in the world"); return end

local function callCrew(why)
    IS.Execute("luacall EBISX_cmd others follow " .. me .. (dist and (" " .. dist) or ""))
    echo("eb_followme: the crew follows " .. me .. " (" .. why .. ")")
end

local zoned = false
IS.AttachEvent("EQ2_FinishedZoning", function() zoned = true end)   -- only a flag: the loop acts

callCrew("start")
while true do
    if zoned then
        zoned = false
        wait(3)
        callCrew("after a zone load")
    end
    wait(0.5)
end
```

[Helper scripts](#helper-scripts) explains how a script talks to EB and reads the crew, and [Scripts](#scripts) has more complete scripts to save and run.

### Quick start: When something is off

EB says what is wrong in the session's console. Find the start of the line below.

#### When EB starts

| You see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `EB is already running in this session` | One EB runs per session. Type `eb stop` first if you meant to start it again, or `eb reload` to load it again in one go. |
| `EB for InnerSpace is not installed` `boot.json has no root` `the EB tree at … is incomplete` | The session cannot find EB, or EB's own files are missing or damaged. Run EB Setup again: its update puts back every file that differs. InnerSpace can stay open. |
| `autostart is off in boot.json` | Type the line it names: `lua eb start`, or `lua EBIS/eb_isx_boot now` on a PC where `lua eb start` isn't set up. |
| `EB does not know which box … plays` | This session has no character to log in, and the brackets say why. Type `eb login <box>` in it, or log in by hand. |
| `… works once EB is up in the world` | EB is still starting: the character is at character select, or loading. Wait for the up line, then type it again. |
| `this ISXLUA has no cjson` | Your ISXLUA is too old: EB needs the ISXLUA 2026-09 build or newer. Put a newer one into your InnerSpace. |
| ISXLUA fails with a .NET initialization error | Another extension that hosts .NET loaded first. Keep ISXLUA right after ISXEQ2 in the game profile, as *EverQuest 2 EB* has it: `ext isxeq2`, `ext isxlua`, then `lua EBIS/eb_isx_boot`. |
| `cast stack: none` | EB found no cast stack for this character, and the line says why. `eb status combat` shows it again. See [Combat and cast stacks](#combat-and-cast-stacks). |
| `windows are off: …` | EB runs, but its windows could not start; the rest of the line says why. Commands still work, and `eb reload` tries again. |
| `windows: nothing opens by itself` | Normal on a crew: only the lead box opens windows by itself. See [EB's windows](#quick-start-ebs-windows). |
| `nav <zone>: no mesh for it` | From `eb nav status`: this PC has no map of the zone yet, and EB walks a zone only on its map. EB asks EB Setup for it by itself; type `eb nav status` again to see when it is in. |
| EB Setup: subscription ended | Ask your admin to extend it, then run EB Setup again. |

#### When EB refuses a line

A line EB will not run comes back as `refused:` and the reason.

| You see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `'…' is not an eb command` | A typo, or a word EB does not have. `eb help` lists them. |
| `… is one of …` | A word that command does not take. The line names the ones it does. |
| `… needs …` | A word is missing: `eb end` needs what to end, for example. `eb help end` shows what a command takes. |
| `eb <command> does not answer on this box yet` | The part of EB behind that command did not start on this box; the rest of the line says why. `eb status bot` lists what started. |
| `eb <command> runs on this box only` | That command takes no crew word. Type it in the session you mean, or use InnerSpace's relay: `relay is2 eb <command>`. |
| `eb <command> goes to the crew with …` | That command takes only some crew words, and the line names them. |

### Quick start: FAQ

#### Will EB log my characters out or restart the game?

Not by itself, and it never relaunches a client. The one exception is an option you turn on yourself: EB Craft's *Camp when done* camps a character to character select after a craft run finishes. `eb stop` ends EB, not the game.

#### How does EB get around?

Inside a zone, EB walks the zone's own map. Between zones it takes bells, wizard spires, druid rings, zone lines, doors and the guild hall: `eb goto <zone>` picks the way. `eb bell`, `eb spire` or `eb druid` with no place says where this zone's one goes.

EB never uses fast travel on its own. `eb ft` does it on your press, and it is refused while a quest line, a power-level route or an instance run is going.

#### Can EB run next to another Lua bot?

Yes, and there is nothing to choose. EB starts from its own game profile, *EverQuest 2 EB*, so another bot's profiles, startup line and files stay as they are. In EB's sessions, EB answers to `eb`.

#### How do I play one character myself?

Pause EB on it: `eb pause` in its console, or the mini's Pause switch. EB then never moves it and never starts a fight on it. Type `eb resume` there when you are done.
