```lua
}

-- offline stand-in: a three-box group; the healer's box is still in another zone
local env, world = require("instances.lib.icworld").make({
    group = { { id = "is2", role = "healer", zone = "fixture_market" }, { id = "is3", role = "dps" } } })
env.loadInstance = function() return INSTANCE end

local runner = require("eb.ic").new(env)
local inst = assert(runner:load("fixture_hollow"))
local ctx = runner:newCtx(inst, {})              -- the run state: role, group, options
local ok, why = runner:zoneIn(ctx)               -- the entry alone (runner:run starts with it)
for _, l in ipairs(world.lines) do if l:find("not everyone", 1, true) then print(l) end end

DOCS.check(ok, "zoned in: " .. tostring(why))
DOCS.eq(world.did("sendTravel"), 1, "the straggler was re-sent its OWN travel, once")
local _, door = world.first("door")
DOCS.eq(door[2], "a fixture rift", "the tank used the door")
DOCS.eq(door[4], "group", "one door use takes the whole group")
DOCS.eq(world.did("door"), 1, "nobody else used it")
for _, m in ipairs(env.brain.group()) do DOCS.eq(m.zone, "fixture_hollow", "inside: " .. m.id) end
```

Tested too: [A hub route the tank walks alone](#snippet-a-hub-route-the-tank-walks-alone).

### Instances: Route steps

Every step is a table with an `id` and an `act`. The id is a short label of its own: options, announces and the console lines name the step by it. The other fields depend on the act.

| `act` and fields | What the tank does |
| --- | --- |
| `path { spots, group }` | Walks the points in `spots`, a list of `{x,y,z}`, on the mesh. With `group = "hold"`, the default, the group stays camped; `"follow"` brings it along, into a boss room. |
| `campspot { name, spot, who }` | Sets a camp spot at `spot`. `who` says who camps there: the tank alone when left out. See [Camp spots](#instances-camp-spots). |
| `encounter { name }` | Runs `encounters\<name>.lua`. How it ended (`killed`, `cleared`, `skipped:gate` ...) is the step's verdict. |
| `loot { op }` | `"chest"`: opens every chest within 75 m, nearest first, up to 8. No chest is not a failure. `"shinies"` takes nothing yet. |
| `announce { message }` | Says the line. `{{verdict.<id>}}` fills in how the encounter or loot step `<id>` ended (`?` for any other step). |
| `interact { actor, verb }` | Walks to the object (a lever, a ride) and uses it: no verb or `"use"` double-clicks, `"hail"` hails, any other verb is applied by its name. |
| `wait { seconds }` | Waits. A stop ends the wait. |
| `wait_actor_dead { name, seconds }` | Waits until that mob is dead, `seconds` at most (300 when left out). |
| `swim { dir, who }` | `"up"` holds swim-up for a fight in water, `"stop"` lets it go. `who`: `"group"`, the default, or `"me"`. The end of the run lets it go. |
| `evac` | Once the fight is clear, evacuates the group to the entrance, inside the copy: the tank's class evac, else a member's, else an evac item. An evac that does not take stops the run. |
| `lootmethod { method, rarity }` | Sets the group's loot method from here on, with the words of `loot_method`. It never stops the run. |
| `zoneout { via }` | `via = "exit"`: takes the group out by the exit door. See [the way out](#instances-deaths-a-member-down-and-the-way-out). |

Any step can also carry a gate, `when = { ... }`: see [Options and step gates](#instances-options-and-step-gates). The route is the tank's: a follower holds on `path`, `campspot` and `interact` steps, and the tank's camp spots move it.

Tested: [One route step of each kind](#snippet-one-route-step-of-each-kind).

### Instances: Camp spots

Inside, the group stands where the tank camps it, and only the tank sets camp spots. A `campspot` step's `who` says who goes to the spot:

| `who` | Who goes there |
| --- | --- |
| `"group"` or `"all"` | Everyone: the tank walks to the spot, and every follower camps on it. |
| `"me"`, the default | The tank alone. A camp spot without `who` moves only the tank. |
| `"others"` | Every follower. The tank stays where it is. |
| `"tank"`, `"healer"`, `"dps"` | Each box of that role. A fighter is a tank, a priest a healer, any other class dps, and the box that leads counts as the tank. |
| A subclass, archetype, character or box | Those boxes: `"templar"`, `"priest"` (or `"fighter"`, `"mage"`, `"scout"`), a character's name or a box id, or several with commas. The tank stays where it is. |

A role word works only on its own. In a list, `"healer"` names nobody: `"healer,scout"` reaches the scouts alone, so write `"priest,scout"`.

Besides camp spots, the group moves only along a `path` with `group = "follow"`, to the exit (camped 3 m short of the door), with an `evac` step, on a fight's own camp spots (see [Actions](#fights-actions)), and to the Guild Hall Mender for the `repair` chore.

### Instances: Fights and loot

An instance file never writes a fight inline. Each fight is a file in `encounters\`, run by an `encounter` step, and the pull is part of that file: `pull` starts the fight from the tank, `engage` fights one named to the end, `clear_area` clears a pack. The [Fights](#fights) page covers the file in full.

- Every fight the route names must load. A missing or broken fight file stops the whole folder from loading, with the step and the reason.
- A fight whose gate does not hold is skipped: its verdict is `skipped:gate`, and the run goes on.
- A `loot` step opens every chest within 75 m, nearest first, up to 8, then the tank walks back to where it stood. Only the tank loots.
- Before each `path` step the tank also takes any chest that has appeared since, within 75 m. At the zone's end it takes every chest left within 100 m.

### Instances: Options and step gates

**Options** are parts of the route a run can skip. Each one is `{ id, label, default, skip_steps }`. When an option is on, the steps in its `skip_steps` are skipped.

- `default = true` in the file: on unless set off.
- `eb ic option <instance> <id> off` (or `on`) keeps it so on this PC, for the next runs.
- `<id>=off` or `<id>=on` on the run line is for this run only, and comes first. `yes`/`no`, `true`/`false` and `1`/`0` work too.
- `eb ic options <instance>` lists them: on or off for the next run, and what each skips.

```text
eb ic run authored/my_hollow skip_bonus=off
```

- Make an id of letters, digits and `_`, starting with a letter or `_`. Any other id cannot be typed on the run line.
- A `skip_steps` entry that names no route step is refused when the file loads, so a typo can never quietly run a fight you meant to skip.
- A word for an option the file does not have is said and ignored.

**Step gates.** Any route step can carry `when = { ... }`: conditions that must all hold. A step whose gate does not hold is skipped, and the console says `SKIP` and why. The conditions are the ones fights use: see [Triggers](#fights-conditions-triggers).

#### Snippet: Instance options and step gates

An instance declares an option that skips its bonus named by default; a run flips it with skip_bonus=off. A route step with its own when gate runs only when the gate holds. A skipped step is said and never run.

**Tested:** The default run skips the bonus named and the gated chest; the run with skip_bonus=off fights it.

**The script:**

```lua
local INSTANCE = {
    schema = "eb.ic/1", zone = "Fixture Hollow", short = "fixture_hollow",
    options = { { id = "skip_bonus", label = "skip the bonus named", default = true, skip_steps = { "bonus" } } },
    route = {
        { id = "bonus", act = "encounter", name = "bonus_named" },
        -- a step gate: loot the chest only when the bonus named is dead
        { id = "bonus.loot", act = "loot", op = "chest", when = { { actor_dead = "Old Fixturo" } } },
    },
}
local BONUS = { schema = "eb.ic/1", name = "Old Fixturo", kind = "named",
                phases = { { id = "pull", do_ = { { engage = "Old Fixturo" } } } } }

local function runWith(flags)
    local env, world = require("instances.lib.icworld").make({ start = "copy", alive = { ["Old Fixturo"] = 100 },
        drops = { "an old chest" } })
    env.loadInstance = function() return INSTANCE end
    env.loadEncounter = function() return BONUS end
    local runner = require("eb.ic").new(env)
    local inst = assert(runner:load("fixture_hollow"))
    local options = runner.parseOptionFlags(flags)       -- "skip_bonus=off" -> { skip_bonus = false }
    local ok, _, report = runner:run(inst, { options = options })
    return ok, report, world
end

local ok1, rep1, w1 = runWith("")
for _, l in ipairs(w1.lines) do if l:find("option skip_bonus", 1, true) then print(l) end end
local ok2, rep2, w2 = runWith("skip_bonus=off")

DOCS.check(ok1 and ok2, "both runs complete")
DOCS.eq(rep1.verdicts.bonus, nil, "default: the bonus named is skipped (no verdict)")
DOCS.eq(w1.did("chest"), 0, "default: its gate does not hold, so no chest step")
DOCS.eq(rep2.verdicts.bonus, "killed", "skip_bonus=off: the bonus named is fought")
DOCS.eq(rep2.verdicts["bonus.loot"], "an old chest", "and its gated chest is looted")
local flags, rest = require("eb.ic").parseOptionFlags("fixture_hollow 30 skip_bonus=off")
```

**Offline lines:** the lines that use `DOCS`, `require("instances.lib` are EB's offline test world, which exists only where the example was tested: in a real script, leave them out or let the game do that part.

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
DOCS.eq(flags.skip_bonus, false, "parseOptionFlags takes the option words out")
DOCS.eq(rest, "fixture_hollow 30", "and hands back the rest of the line")
```

### Instances: Deaths, a member down, and the way out

- **The tank dies, or the group wipes.** The fight file's `on_death` actions run first. The run waits for the group to be revived (2 minutes at most), walks back from the nearest step with a spot, skipping loot, and fights the step it died on again.
- **A member dies.** The run holds between steps, and fights are waited out. Every minute it asks for the rez run: a rezzer runs to each body. After 4 minutes the member releases and walks back along the route. After 8 minutes the run goes on without them, and says so.
- **Stuck.** Freeing a wedged box is EB's mover's job, as on any walk. The run evacuates only at an `evac` step.
- **Off the route.** A tank more than 60 m off the route that has not come closer for 45 s, out of a fight, goes on from the step nearest to it, at most twice a step and four times a run.
- **The way out.** A `zoneout` step needs the exit door within 80 m. The group camps 3 m short of it; the tank and each follower walk up and click it, and every box picks the same copy. After 3 tries that leave the group inside, the run stops.
- **Fail closed.** A step the run cannot do stops the run and says why: the next step assumes the last one happened. These never stop it: a chest that is not there, a step or fight whose gate does not hold, a loot method that cannot be set, a chore that cannot be done.

For a member down: `eb ic catchup` walks this box back to the tank along the route, `eb ic rezmember <name>` sends one rezzer to that member, `eb ic gatherremains` casts Gather Remains here, and `eb ic acceptrez` takes a rez offer on a dead box.

Tested: [Death in an instance: revive, walk back, pull again](#snippet-death-in-an-instance-revive-walk-back-pull-again).

### Instances: Commands

`<instance>` is the instance's name: its folder's name, as `eb ic list` shows it, or `authored/<folder>` for one of yours.

#### Run and watch

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `eb ic list` | The instance collections EB ships, with some of each one's instances. |
| `eb ic run <instance> [difficulty]` | One run, led by this box. The file is read fresh each time. |
| `eb all ic run <instance>` | The same, sent to every box; one outside the tank's group stays out. |
| `eb ic loop <instance> [minutes] [difficulty]` | Runs it again and again: see [Loops](#instances-loops-and-the-instance-queue). |
| `eb ic rerun <instance> [difficulty]` | One more run: out, a reset from outside, back in. No reset today. |
| `eb hub <instance>` | Takes this box to the hub zone; `eb all hub` every box, each its own way. |
| `eb ic entrance <instance>` | In the hub zone: walks this box to the door. It never takes the door. |
| `eb ic status` | The run: lead or follower, the step it is on, its last line. |
| `eb status goal` | The run and EB's goal together. |
| `eb ic goto <step>` | On the tank: the run goes on from that step now. |
| `eb pause` | Holds the run where it is; fights go on. `eb resume` goes on. |
| `eb ic stop` | Ends the run and every wait in it. On the tank, it ends the followers' runs too. |
| `eb all stop` | Stops runs, quests, walks and goals on every box. Fights go on. |

**Words on the run line:** a difficulty after the name (`[Heroic I]`; on a loop, after the minutes), `<id>=on|off` for an option, `solo`, `merc=on`, `loot=<method>`, `from=<step>` to start at a step, `laps=<n>` to end a loop after n laps, and the chores `tse`, `repair` and `maintenance`.

#### Build and debug

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `eb ic new [3boss\|5boss\|raid] [name]` | A template as a new folder of yours, named after the name (else the zone you stand in) with `_heroic` or `_raid`. Its walks and fights wait to be filled in. It never writes over a folder you have. `eb ic templates` lists them. |
| `eb ic save <instance> [name]` | Copies an instance into a folder of yours, with the fight files its `encounters` names. `eb ic export` is the same. |
| `eb creator ic` | Opens the Instance Builder. Your folders are under Open > Mine. |
| `eb ic near <instance> [n]` | The n steps nearest to you (5 when not given), with their numbers. |
| `eb ic teststep <instance> <step>` | That one step now, on this box: no way in, no zone's end. `eb ic nextstep` runs the next one. |
| `eb ic runnear <instance>` | Inside the instance: runs it from the step nearest to you. |
| `eb ic rundirect <instance> [difficulty] [step]` | Runs it from that step, like `from=<step>`. |
| `eb ic options <instance>` | Its options: on or off for the next run, and what each skips. |
| `eb ic checkitems [items]` | What this box lacks: of the items named, else of `required_items`. |
| `eb ic stats [instance]` | Run times, nameds, deaths and the best time. `eb ic stats csv` writes a row a run to `eb-instance-timing.csv`, beside the install. |

#### Lockouts and the queue

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `eb lockouts` | The zones this character is saved to; `check <zone>` for one, `fleet <zone>` asks every box. Held back today. |
| `eb resetzone one <zone>` | Asks the game to reset that zone's lockout, from outside it; `all` resets every zone this box is saved to. Held back today. |
| `eb iqueue add <instance>` | Adds it to the queue; `start [row]`, `stop`, `pause`, `resume` and `status` do as they say. |
| `eb ic looplist [runs] [minutes]` | The whole queue again and again; `0` or none is no cap. |
| `eb ic ignorelock on` | The queue runs a zone this box is saved to anyway; `off`, the default, skips it. |

While a run goes, the console shows one line per step: its id, its act, and how it went. A skipped step says `SKIP` and why; a loop marks each lap (`--- lap 2 ---`) and its end (`=== loop over ... ===`). A file that does not load answers `the IC did not load:` and the reason, naming the step at fault.

##### Snippet: The instance commands from the console

Boot EB offline and type the instance commands the way you would in game: eb ic status, eb lockouts and eb resetzone. Each answers at once; a run itself is an EB task that eb ic status reports on. Resetting a zone (and reading which zones you are saved to) is held back until EB has proven that call in the game: the answer names the zone and says so.

**Tested:** eb ic status says the runner is idle, eb lockouts answers, and eb resetzone names the zone and says its reset is held back until it is proven live; with no zone it asks which.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script: lines exactly as you type them
local status = a.console("eb ic status")
local locks = a.console("eb lockouts")
local reset = a.console("eb resetzone one fixture_hollow")
print(status)
print(reset)
```

**Offline lines:** the lines that use `a.console` are EB's offline test world, which exists only where the example was tested: in a real script, leave them out or let the game do that part.

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
-- offline stand-in: the whole of EB for InnerSpace booted by its real boot
local a = DOCS.app()
```

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.has(status, "ic: idle", "no run is going")
DOCS.has(locks, "lockouts:", "eb lockouts answers")
DOCS.has(reset, "the reset of fixture_hollow", "eb resetzone names the zone it was asked for")
DOCS.has(reset, "held back until it is proven live", "and says the reset is held back for now")
DOCS.has(a.console("eb resetzone"), "which zone?", "with no zone it asks which")
a.stop()
```

### Instances: Today on EB for InnerSpace

Some reads and calls are held back until EB has proven them in the game. EB's own answers say so.

- **A loop runs one lap.** The reuse timer cannot be read yet, so `eb ic loop` runs one lap and ends inside the cleared copy.
- **No zone reset.** `eb resetzone` answers that the reset is held back until it is proven live, and `eb ic rerun` runs the copy as it is. Reset a zone yourself between runs for now.
- **No lockout read.** `eb lockouts` says its read is held back, and shows this PC's last record. The queue skips no zone for a lockout yet, so `eb ic ignorelock` changes nothing.
- **The loop's own time.** `eb ic loop` never uses the file's `max_minutes`: type the minutes on the line.
- **The word solo.** A run typed on a grouped box still goes to the group's other EB boxes, also with `solo` and with `eb ic teststep`: a box that is not inside travels to the hub and waits there until the run ends. For a true solo run, use a character with nobody else in its group.
- **Copies.** EB does not read which copy each box is in. It relies on every box picking the same row of the door's list.
- **Far chests.** The tank walks to every chest: calling a far chest over is held back.

### Instances: If something goes wrong

EB says what stopped a run, in the console of the box it ran on. The usual ones, in the order you meet them:

| EB says | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `no IC called '<name>'` | Check the name with `eb ic list`. For one of yours, put `authored/` first. |
| `the IC did not load: ...` | The reason names the step or key at fault, as in the card below. A fight file must be `encounters\<name>.lua`, named as its step names it. |
| `is not a step the runner knows` | A typo in `act`: see [Route steps](#instances-route-steps). |
| `this box lacks <item>` | Put the file's `required_items` in the tank's bags. |
| `not in my group` | That box's character is not in the tank's group. Invite it, then start again. |
| `no '<door>' in reach` | A follower waits more than 300 m from the door: gather the crew at the door first ([Alone or with your group](#instances-alone-or-with-your-group)). |
| `no '<door>' within 60 m` | The tank's walk ends too far from the door, or `door.actor` is not its exact name. |
| `could not get within <n> m of the door` | The tank cannot reach `entrance.loc`: move it onto open ground, or raise `tolerance`. |
| `someone is still saved to <zone>` | A member is saved to another copy, and EB's reset is held back today: reset it yourself, or wait out the lockout. |
| `the evac did not take` | The group is still at the last fight. Take it out yourself, then start again. |
| `could not leave <zone> after 3 tries` | The `zoneout` step ran too far from the exit: end the path before it near the door. |
| `every named ... was already gone` | The copy was still the cleared one. Reset it, then start again. |
| `an IC run is going` | A box runs one instance at a time: `eb ic stop` first. |

#### Snippet: What runner:load refuses

The loader checks an instance file before anything runs: its schema, a hub route that would move the group, an option that skips a step the route does not have, and an encounter file that will not load. Each refusal says why.

**Tested:** Four broken files are refused with their reasons; the fixed file loads with its encounter attached.

**The script:**

```lua
local IC = require("eb.ic")
local env = require("instances.lib.icworld").make()           -- offline interfaces (the loader needs none of them)

local function try(inst, encounters)
    env.loadInstance = function() return inst end
    env.loadEncounter = function(_, name)
        local e = encounters and encounters[name]
        if not e then error("encounters/" .. name .. ".lua is missing") end
        return e
    end
    return IC.new(env):load("fixture_hollow")
end

local base = function()
    return { schema = "eb.ic/1", zone = "Fixture Hollow", short = "fixture_hollow",
             hub = { zone = "fixture_docks", door = { actor = "a fixture rift", verb = "enter" } },
             route = { { id = "n1", act = "encounter", name = "captain_fixturo" } } }
end
local ENC = { captain_fixturo = { schema = "eb.ic/1", name = "Captain Fixturo", kind = "named", phases = {} } }

-- 1. not an eb.ic/1 file
local bad1 = base(); bad1.schema = "something/else"
local _, why1 = try(bad1, ENC)
-- 2. a hub route step that walks the group along (the tank walks the hub route ALONE)
local bad2 = base()
bad2.hub.route = { { id = "h1", act = "path", spots = { { 1, 0, 1 } } },
                   { id = "h2", act = "path", spots = { { 9, 0, 9 } }, group = "follow" } }
local _, why2 = try(bad2, ENC)
print("refused: " .. why2)
-- 3. an option that skips a step id the route does not have
local bad3 = base(); bad3.options = { { id = "skip_bonus", default = true, skip_steps = { "bonus" } } }
local _, why3 = try(bad3, ENC)
-- 4. a route step that calls an encounter with no file
local _, why4 = try(base(), {})

local inst = try(base(), ENC)
```

**Offline lines:** the lines that use `require("instances.lib` are EB's offline test world, which exists only where the example was tested: in a real script, leave them out or let the game do that part.

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
DOCS.has(why1, "unknown schema", "the schema is checked")
DOCS.has(why2, "the tank walks the hub route alone", "a hub step may not move the group")
DOCS.has(why3, "which is not a route step", "an option must name real route steps")
DOCS.has(why4, "will not load", "a missing encounter refuses the load")
DOCS.eq(inst and inst._enc.captain_fixturo.name, "Captain Fixturo", "the good file loads with its encounter")
```

Tested too: [eb ic from the console and from a script](#snippet-eb-ic-from-the-console-and-from-a-script), [Spot a reset that did not take](#snippet-spot-a-reset-that-did-not-take).

## Fights

A fight file tells the tank when a fight applies, what to do in it, how to answer its mechanics, and what counts as won.

### Fights: What a fight file is for

A fight file scripts one fight of an instance run: a named, a boss, a trash pack or a mechanic. It says when the fight applies, what the tank does, how EB answers the fight's mechanics, and what counts as won. What each character casts still comes from its own cast stack.

> [!NOTE]
> **Only the tank runs the file:** the box you typed the run on. The other boxes fight beside it. They assist its target, stand on its camp spots and act on the orders its actions send. So "my health" or "in my bags" in a condition means the tank's.

### Fights: Quick start: a trash pack

The shortest complete fight file is a trash pack: a gate, a pull, a clear and a win test. It is tested end to end with its instance file, the [worked example on the Instances page](#instances-worked-example). The card's **Show the script** button shows the file.

#### Complete script: A trash pull encounter

encounters/hollow_skitters.lua of the complete instance: a gate that skips the step when no pack is up, a pull that brings the pack to the group's camp spot, then a clear of whatever is left within reach.

**Where it goes:** `EB/data/eb/ic/<collection>/fixture_hollow/encounters/hollow_skitters.lua`

**Get the file:** [examples/script-ic-trash-pull.lua](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jiimboeq2/EB-Docs/main/examples/script-ic-trash-pull.lua) (save it as hollow_skitters.lua)

**Run it:**

```text
eb ic run fixture_hollow
```

**Needs:**

- the instance file fixture_hollow/instance.lua beside its encounters folder

**Tested:** With four skitters up, the pack is pulled once and cleared; with none up, the step is skipped by its gate.

**Verified:** tested offline: run end to end on EB's offline stand-in for the game; not run in the live game yet, so try it on one box first

```lua
-- fixture_hollow/encounters/hollow_skitters.lua - conditions -> actions, as data. The route's "trash" step runs it.
return {
    schema = "eb.ic/1",
    name = "a hollow skitter",
    kind = "trash",
    spot = { 0, 0, 5 },                                   -- where the tank fights it from
    -- the gate: no skitter up = nothing to do (the verdict says "skipped:gate" and the run goes on)
    when = { { actor_count = { query = "a hollow skitter", cmp = ">=", value = 1 } } },
    phases = {
        { id = "pull", do_ = { { pull = "a hollow skitter" } } },                  -- bring the pack to the camp spot
        { id = "clear", do_ = { { clear_area = "a hollow skitter", radius = 30 } } },
    },
    done = { { actor_count = { query = "a hollow skitter", cmp = "==", value = 0 } } },
}
```

1. Save the file as `encounters\hollow_skitters.lua` in your instance's folder. The card puts it beside the instances EB ships; your own instances live in the EB folder's `data\ebic\authored\instances\`, one folder each.
2. In `instance.lua`, call it from a route step whose `name` is the file's name without `.lua`. The tested instance file has that step: `{ id = "trash", act = "encounter", name = "hollow_skitters" }`.
3. On the tank's box, start the run: `eb ic run authored/fixture_hollow`, with your folder's name after `authored/`.
4. Watch the console. `encounter 'a hollow skitter' (trash)` says the gate held, and the step ends with `verdict cleared`.

For your own zone, put its mob's name and the spot the tank fights from in place of the fixture's.

### Fights: Step by step: script a named

The [worked example](#fights-worked-example) below is a complete named fight. These steps build one like it.

1. Stand where the tank should fight the named and type `eb marks set boss1`. EB answers `marked 'boss1' at x,y,z in <zone>`: the three numbers are the fight's spot.
2. In the instance's `encounters` folder, create a file named for the fight: `boss1.lua`.
3. Give it the fields at the top of the worked example: `schema = "eb.ic/1"`, the mob's exact `name`, `kind = "named"` and the `spot` from step 1.
4. Add a gate in `when`, so the fight runs only when the named is up: an `actor_present` condition with its name.
5. Add the fight: one phase whose `do_` holds an `engage` of the named. The tank fights it to the end.
6. Add a reaction for each mechanic, as the [next section](#fights-answer-a-mechanic-mid-fight) shows.
7. Add the win test in `done`: an `actor_dead` condition with the named's name.
8. In `instance.lua`, call it from the route with an `encounter` step whose `name` is `"boss1"`, and list it in `encounters`.
9. Put a `loot` step after it when the named drops a chest.
10. Try the fight on its own with `eb ic teststep`, as [Try one fight on its own](#fights-try-one-fight-on-its-own) shows.

### Fights: Answer a mechanic mid-fight

A mechanic is answered by a **reaction**: a phase with a `when` and `repeat_ = true`. EB checks it while the fight runs and does its `do_` list each time the condition holds.

1. Pick the condition that shows the mechanic: `chat_seen` for an emote, `actor_count` for adds, `mob_health_below` for a health mark, `timer_expired` for a timer, `mob_casting` for a big cast.
2. Add a phase with an `id`, that condition in its `when`, and `repeat_ = true`.
3. Put the answer in its `do_`: `clear_area` for adds, `campspot` to a safe spot and back, `cast` for a burn.
4. Add `once = true` when it should fire only once per pull, like an enrage or a burn.
5. For a mechanic that comes back, make sure its condition clears between two of them: give `chat_seen` a `since`, and put `reset_timer` first in a timer's `do_`.
6. Run it and look for `reactive '<id>' fires` in the console each time it answers.

Step 5 matters because a condition that stays true fires its reaction again and again. `chat_seen` with no `since` stays true for the rest of the fight once the line was seen, and `timer_expired` stays true once its time is up.

The tested snippet below is a boss whose adds surface mid-fight. The reaction clears them each time they are up, while the step phase fights the boss.

#### Snippet: A mechanic mid-fight: a reactive phase

An encounter whose boss calls in adds: a phase with when + repeat\_ is checked on every fight tick and between phases, and clears the adds whenever they are up, while the main phase fights the boss.

**Tested:** The reactive phase fires once the adds surface, clears them, and the boss is killed.

**The script:**

```lua
local INSTANCE = {
    schema = "eb.ic/1", zone = "Fixture Hollow", short = "fixture_hollow",
    route = { { id = "boss", act = "encounter", name = "mire_queen" } },
}
local MIRE_QUEEN = {
    schema = "eb.ic/1", name = "Mire Queen Fixtura", kind = "boss",
    phases = {
        { id = "burn", do_ = { { engage = "Mire Queen Fixtura" } } },
        -- REACTIVE: when + repeat_ = checked on every fight tick; it fires whenever its condition holds
        { id = "adds", repeat_ = true,
          when = { { actor_count = { query = "a mire spawn", cmp = ">=", value = 1 } } },
          do_ = { { clear_area = "a mire spawn", radius = 25 } } },
    },
    done = { { actor_dead = "Mire Queen Fixtura" } },
}

-- offline stand-in: engaging the queen surfaces three adds
local env, world = require("instances.lib.icworld").make({ start = "copy",
    alive = { ["Mire Queen Fixtura"] = 100 }, adds = { on = "Mire Queen Fixtura", name = "a mire spawn", count = 3 } })
env.loadInstance = function() return INSTANCE end
env.loadEncounter = function() return MIRE_QUEEN end

local runner = require("eb.ic").new(env)
local inst = assert(runner:load("fixture_hollow"))
local ok, _, report = runner:run(inst)
for _, l in ipairs(world.lines) do if l:find("reactive", 1, true) then print(l) end end
```

**Offline lines:** the lines that use `require("instances.lib` are EB's offline test world, which exists only where the example was tested: in a real script, leave them out or let the game do that part.

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
DOCS.check(ok, "the run completes")
DOCS.eq(report.verdicts.boss, "killed", "the boss")
DOCS.eq(world.did("clear"), 1, "the adds were cleared once, when they surfaced")
DOCS.eq(env.combat.count("a mire spawn"), 0, "no add left up")
```

When exactly reactions are checked is under [Phases](#fights-phases).

### Fights: Try one fight on its own

You do not need a whole run to try an edit. `eb ic teststep` runs one route step now, from this box.

1. Go inside the instance and stand near the fight.
2. Type `eb ic near authored/fixture_hollow`, with your folder's name. EB lists the steps nearest to you, with their numbers.
3. Type `eb ic teststep authored/fixture_hollow 5`, with your fight's step number. This box walks to the fight's spot and runs the fight.
4. Read the console lines, fix the file and save it.
5. Type the same `eb ic teststep` line again. Each test reads the folder fresh.
6. Type `eb ic nextstep` to go on to the step after it.

A test takes no way in and no zone's end, and it does not count in `eb ic stats`.

### Fights: Use a fight file with no run going

A boss's fight file also works outside a run, for a named you pull yourself. EB lays it on each box for that boss's fight.

1. Go to the boss's zone.
2. Type `eb encounter fights`. EB lists the fight files its instance library holds for this zone, each in plain words: its kill order, the fight rules a box answers here, and the moves left to a run.
3. Type `eb all encounter fight` and the boss's name. Each box lays the file on. With no name, it takes the named it fights, else the nearest one.
4. Fight the boss as you would.
5. Type `eb encounter status` to see what is laid on, and `eb encounter off` to take it off. Leaving the zone takes it off too.

- While the boss fights, the file's kill order and `combat_override` hold for the whole fight, the adds too.
- Each box answers the file's reactions whose actions move nobody: `cast`, `cure`, `dispel`, `announce`, `ability_tag` and `reset_timer`. A reaction that moves, pulls or clears is left to a run.
- A box EB is paused on, one you play by hand, answers none.
- EB finds the files by the zone's name, among the instances it ships: a folder named after the zone, in lower case, with each run of spaces and punctuation as `_`. Your own folders under `authored` are not looked in.

#### Encounter setups

An encounter setup is a smaller file: combat settings for one named, with no phases. Each one is a JSON file in the EB folder's `data\eb\encounters\`, holding `name`, an optional `zone`, `mob` (a part of the named's name) and `directives` (the same keys as [combat_override](#combat_override-keys)). While that named is the mob, its directives are laid over the cast stack.

- `eb encounter list` lists yours. EB ships none.
- `eb encounter load <name>` lays one on. With no name it takes the setup for the named this box fights, else the nearest named's.
- `eb flag autosetups on` lays every installed setup on by itself, each while its named is the mob.
- `eb setups raid on` does that in every raid zone and takes them off again elsewhere; `eb setups heroic on` does the same for every other zone. Both are off until you switch one on.

### Fights: Worked example

A complete named fight, tested end to end with its instance file. Its parts, from the top:

| Part | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `when` | The gate: the named is up and nobody is fighting yet. |
| phase `fight` | The tank engages the named and fights it to the end. |
| phase `floor` | Once per pull, on the emote: the group steps onto the safe ledge, waits 6 seconds and comes back. |
| phase `adds` | Each time a spawn is up: clear it. |
| phase `burn` | Once, under 30% health: cast the finisher. |
| `done` | The win test: the named is dead. |
| `on_death` | After a wipe here: a line in the console, before the walk back in. |

#### Complete script: A named fight with a gate, phases, a reaction and a win test

encounters/overseer_of_fixtures.lua of the complete instance: the fight starts only when the named is up and nobody is fighting; the tank fights it to death while reactive phases answer its emote (the group steps onto a safe ledge and back), clear its adds and cast the finisher under 30%; the fight counts as won only when it is dead.

**Where it goes:** `EB/data/eb/ic/<collection>/fixture_hollow/encounters/overseer_of_fixtures.lua`

**Get the file:** [examples/script-named-fight.lua](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jiimboeq2/EB-Docs/main/examples/script-named-fight.lua) (save it as overseer_of_fixtures.lua)

**Run it:**

```text
eb ic run fixture_hollow
```

**Needs:**

- the instance file fixture_hollow/instance.lua, whose route step "boss" names this file
- Fixture Burst (or your own finisher's name) in the tank's knowledge book

**Tested:** The emote moves the group to the safe ledge once and back, the adds are cleared, the finisher is cast once under 30%, and the verdict is killed; with the named not up, the gate skips the fight.

**Verified:** tested offline: run end to end on EB's offline stand-in for the game; not run in the live game yet, so try it on one box first

```lua
-- fixture_hollow/encounters/overseer_of_fixtures.lua - one named fight as conditions -> actions. The phases without a
-- "when" run in order; a phase with "when" + "repeat_ = true" is a REACTION, checked between phases and on every tick
-- of the fight; "once = true" fires a reaction one time per pull.
return {
    schema = "eb.ic/1",
    name = "Overseer of Fixtures",
    aka = { "the Overseer" },
    kind = "named",
    spot = { 12, 0, 42 },                                 -- where the tank fights it from

    -- the GATE: the named is up and nobody is fighting yet (else the verdict is "skipped:gate")
    when = { { actor_present = "Overseer of Fixtures" }, { in_combat = false } },

    phases = {
        -- the fight: the cast stack fights the Overseer to death; the reactions below fire on its ticks
        { id = "fight", do_ = { { engage = "Overseer of Fixtures" } } },

        -- REACTION to the emote: the floor burns - the group steps onto the safe ledge, waits it out, comes back
        { id = "floor", repeat_ = true, once = true,
          when = { { chat_seen = { match = "the floor will burn" } } },
          do_ = {
              { campspot = { name = "safe ledge", spot = { 25, 0, 50 }, who = "group" } },
              { wait = 6 },
              { campspot = { name = "boss room", spot = { 12, 0, 38 }, who = "group" } },
          } },

        -- REACTION to adds: whenever spawns are up, clear them
        { id = "adds", repeat_ = true,
          when = { { actor_count = { query = "a fixture spawn", cmp = ">=", value = 1 } } },
          do_ = { { clear_area = "a fixture spawn", radius = 25 } } },

        -- the BURN: under 30% health, cast the finisher once
        { id = "burn", repeat_ = true, once = true,
          when = { { mob_health_below = { name = "Overseer of Fixtures", pct = 30 } } },
          do_ = { { cast = "Fixture Burst" } } },
    },

    -- the WIN TEST: the fight only counts as won when the Overseer is dead (else "FAILED:done-test")
    done = { { actor_dead = "Overseer of Fixtures" } },

    -- a wipe here: say so before the walk back in
    on_death = { { announce = "the Overseer of Fixtures wiped us - walking back in" } },
}
```

Its gate is read at the fight's spot. If something is already fighting the tank there, `in_combat = false` fails and the fight is skipped.

### Fights: How a fight runs

1. A route step names the file. In the tested instance file: `{ id = "boss", act = "encounter", name = "overseer_of_fixtures" }`.
2. When the run starts, EB loads and checks every fight file the route calls. A missing file, a Lua error or an unknown key stops the load and names the step.
3. On the walk to the fight (a `path` step before it), the fight's names go first on the kill-first list: its `kill_order` and `extra_targets`, or its own name for a named or a boss. If the group is fighting just then, this waits until it is clear.
4. At its step, the tank walks to `spot`, to within 4 metres, and reads the gate there. If the gate does not hold, the step ends as `skipped:gate` and the run goes on.
5. When the gate holds, the kill-first list goes on, the fight clock starts (what `timer_expired` and `chat_seen` count from) and `combat_override` goes on. Then the phases run.
6. After the phases, `done` decides: `killed` (`cleared` for trash), or `FAILED:done-test`.
7. A failed action in a step or gate phase ends the fight as `FAILED:` with the reason, and the run stops at that step.
8. If the tank is dead, the fight ends as `DIED:` and the recovery runs: `on_death` first, then EB waits up to 2 minutes for the rez, walks back from the nearest step with a spot (skipping loot) and runs the fight again.
9. The override goes off on every way out. A route `announce` can quote how the fight ended: the tested instance file writes `{{verdict.boss}}`.

**A fight met on the way.** While the tank walks the route and the group is fighting, a living mob of one of the next two fights brings that fight's `combat_override` and kill-first names on, for this fight only. A mechanic never does.

The tested snippet below shows the recovery: the tank dies on the first pull, the group is revived, the tank walks back and wins the second pull.

#### Snippet: Death in an instance: revive, walk back, pull again

The tank dies on the first pull of a named. The runner waits for the group to be revived, walks back from the nearest positioned step before the fight (skipping loot), and runs the encounter again. Nothing is ever moved any other way.

**Tested:** The second pull kills the named, the catch-up walk re-walks the path step, and the run completes.

**The script:**

```lua
local INSTANCE = {
    schema = "eb.ic/1", zone = "Fixture Hollow", short = "fixture_hollow",
    route = {
        { id = "camp", act = "campspot", name = "entry", spot = { 0, 0, -30 }, who = "group" },
        { id = "walk", act = "path", spots = { { 0, 0, 10 }, { 15, 0, 40 } } },
        { id = "n1", act = "encounter", name = "captain_fixturo" },
    },
}
local CAPTAIN = { schema = "eb.ic/1", name = "Captain Fixturo", kind = "named",
                  phases = { { id = "pull", do_ = { { engage = "Captain Fixturo" } } } } }

-- offline stand-in: the first pull of the captain kills the tank
local env, world = require("instances.lib.icworld").make({ start = "copy",
    alive = { ["Captain Fixturo"] = 100 }, dieOnFirst = "Captain Fixturo" })
env.loadInstance = function() return INSTANCE end
env.loadEncounter = function() return CAPTAIN end

local runner = require("eb.ic").new(env)
local inst = assert(runner:load("fixture_hollow"))
local ok, _, report = runner:run(inst)
for _, l in ipairs(world.lines) do if l:find("RECOVERY", 1, true) then print(l) end end
```

**Offline lines:** the lines that use `require("instances.lib` are EB's offline test world, which exists only where the example was tested: in a real script, leave them out or let the game do that part.

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
DOCS.check(ok, "the run completes after the recovery")
DOCS.eq(report.verdicts.n1, "killed", "the second pull kills the named")
DOCS.eq(world.attempts["Captain Fixturo"], 2, "two pulls: the wipe, then the kill")
DOCS.eq(world.did("revived"), 1, "the runner waited for the group to be revived")
DOCS.eq(world.did("walk"), 4, "the path step was walked again (2 waypoints, twice)")
```

### Fights: The fight file

A fight file is plain Lua that only returns a table, saved as `encounters\<name>.lua` in the instance's folder. Its fields:

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `schema` (required) | `"eb.ic/1"`. The Instance Builder and `eb encounter fight` check it. |
| `name` | The mob the fight is about, as the game names it. |
| `aka` | Other names the mob goes by. The Instance Builder links a fight by them; the run does not read them. |
| `kind` | `"named"`, `"boss"`, `"trash"` or `"mechanic"`. A trash fight ends as `cleared` and the others as `killed`; every kind but trash counts as a named in `eb ic stats`. When every named and boss of a loop's lap is skipped by its gate, the loop ends: the copy came back cleared. |
| `spot` | `{x, y, z}`: the tank walks there before the gate is read. |
| `search` | How far `actor_present` and `actor_dead` look from the tank, in metres. 60 when not set. |
| `when` | The gate: every condition must hold, or the fight is skipped (`skipped:gate`) and the run goes on. A bonus named that did not spawn is skipped this way. |
| `phases` | The fight itself. See [Phases](#fights-phases). |
| `done` | The win test, after the phases. If it does not hold, the fight ends as `FAILED:done-test` and the run stops. |
| `on_death` | Actions run first after a wipe in this fight; the usual recovery follows them. Use actions that move nobody, such as `announce`. |
| `kill_order` | Names to kill first, in order. They go on the kill-first list when the fight starts, and already on the walk toward it. |
| `extra_targets` | More kill-first names, after `kill_order`. |
| `no_autotarget` | `true` keeps this fight's names off the kill-first list. |
| `combat_override` | Combat settings for this fight only: on when it starts, off on every way out. Its keys are [below](#combat_override-keys). |
| `override_priority` | When two overrides set the same key, the higher priority wins. 50 when not set. |
| `loot` | What the fight drops, for people reading the file: `{ "chest" }`. The route's `loot` step does the looting. |

The kill-first list orders a fight that is on; it starts none. EB picks from it only after the mob the tank is pointed at, so to kill the adds before the named, use `trashFirst` below. A `target` action in a phase sets the list instead of `kill_order` and `extra_targets`.

#### combat_override keys

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `trashFirst` | `true`: kill the adds before the named, even over the mob the tank is pointed at. |
| `disableAE` | `true`: no area attacks. `disableMez` and `disableHO` do the same for mez and heroic opportunities. |
| `tags` | A table of cast-stack tags: `true` forces a tag on, `false` off. |
| `interruptAll` | `true`: interrupt any cast that can be stopped, not only the listed ones. |
| `interruptList` | A list of cast names: the casts to interrupt. |
| `cureScope` | `"group"`: only group cures fire. `"single"`: only single-target cures. |
| `pause` | `true` holds every cast. |
| `autoTarget` | `{ enabled, oocScan, list, scanRadius }`: the kill-first list's switches. `oocScan = true` lets it start on a calm mob in range. |
| `positioning` | Where the boxes stand in the fight: `"behind"`, `"range"`, `"stack"` or `"melee"`. |
| `losGate` | `true` or `false`: the line-of-sight check before an attack. |
| `ttkMax` | In milliseconds: the longest a kill may look like taking before EB gives it up. `ttkGrace`: how long EB fights before it judges. |
| `forceAssist` | A player's name: assist that player's target. |
| `lockTarget` | An actor's id: a hard target lock. |
| `stack` | Names another cast-stack profile. EB does not switch to it yet. |

No key can make EB fight a guard, or keep on with a fight it cannot win.

### Fights: Phases

A phase is a table with an `id` and a `do_` list of actions, run in order. Its other fields decide what kind it is:

| Kind | The phase has | When it runs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Step | no `when` | Once, in order with the other step and gate phases. |
| Gate | `when` | In order. It waits up to 2 minutes for its condition, while reactions keep firing. After that it runs anyway. |
| Reaction | `when` and `repeat_ = true` | Each time its condition holds, at the moments listed below. This is how a mechanic is answered. |
| One-shot reaction | a reaction with `once = true` | The first time its condition holds, then not again in that fight. A new pull after a wipe arms it again. |

Reactions are checked:

- on every tick of an `engage`;
- as each step or gate phase starts, and every half second while a gate phase waits;
- after each phase, every half second while one is still armed, for at most 60 passes.

They are not checked while `clear_area`, `wait`, `wait_combat` or `wait_actor_dead` runs.

A failed action in a reaction is only reported with `[FAILED]`: the fight goes on.

`repeat_`, `do_`, `not_` and `until_` end in `_` because `repeat`, `do`, `not` and `until` are Lua words.

### Fights: Conditions (triggers)

Conditions are what `when`, `done`, `until_` and route step gates hold. A list means every one must hold. Each condition is a table with one key:

| Key | Its value | Holds when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actor_present` | a name | A living one of that name is in reach: the fight's `search`, 60 m when not set. |
| `actor_dead` | a name | No living one of that name is in reach. One that walked out of reach reads as dead. |
| `actor_count` | a table: `query`, `cmp`, `value` | The living mobs whose name holds `query`, within 60 m, compared with `value`. `cmp` is `>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<` or `==` (`>=` and 1 when not set). A corpse never counts. |
| `actor_type` | a table: `name`, `type` | The actor with that exact name shows as that type, such as `NamedNPC`, in any case. |
| `health_below` | a percent | The tank's own health is under it. |
| `health_above` | a percent | The tank's own health is over it. |
| `mob_health_below` | a table: `name`, `pct` | That mob's health is under `pct` percent. |
| `in_combat` | `true` or `false` | The tank is, or is not, in a fight. |
| `near_spot` | a table: `spot`, `within` | The tank is within `within` metres of `spot`, a `{x, y, z}`, measured flat (5 when not set). |
| `timer_expired` | a table: `seconds`, `name` | That many seconds have passed since the pull, or since `reset_timer` last restarted that named timer. |
| `chat_seen` | a table: `match`, `since` | A chat or emote line, or an on-screen announcement, holds that text in any case: since the pull, or in the last `since` seconds. |
| `mob_casting` | a table: `mob`, `ability`, `since` | That mob is casting it now: its cast bar, else the game's own "begins casting" line in the last `since` seconds (5 when not set). `mob` and `ability` are parts of the names; `ability` may be the cast's number. |
| `detriment_present` | a table: `who`, `type`, `name`; or `true` | A curable detriment is up: `type` is arcane, noxious, elemental, trauma or cursed, and `true` means any. It never holds on EB for InnerSpace today. |
| `has_item` | an item's name | That item, by its exact name, is in the tank's bags. |
| `all`, `any`, `not_` | a list, or one condition | `all`: every one holds. `any`: at least one holds. `not_`: that condition does not hold. |
| a function | `function(w) ... end` | Your own test, for anything else. It returns true or false. |

**How a name finds its mob.** A name means the actor with exactly that name, in any case, a living one first. Only when nothing carries the exact name does it match the nearest living NPC whose name holds it. `actor_count` counts every living mob whose name holds the words.

> [!NOTE]
> **A typo stops the load.** A condition key EB does not know refuses the whole folder when the run starts, and the answer names the step, the fight file and the key: `route step 'boss' calls encounter 'overseer_of_fixtures': its gate: unknown condition 'actor_presnet'`. An unknown action key is refused the same way. Only a condition EB cannot read in this session answers false.

The tested snippet below reads conditions directly: single keys, the combinations and a function. Its last check is the answer at run time to a key EB does not know, which is false. A fight file with such a key never gets that far.

#### Snippet: Encounter conditions, and how they fail closed

Evaluate when / done conditions against the runner's world facade: actor_present, actor_dead, actor_count, health_below, the all / any / not\_ combinators, and a function. A condition the runner does not know is always false.

**Tested:** Each condition reads the fake world as expected; the misspelled one is false, never a silent true.

**The script:**

```lua
local env = require("instances.lib.icworld").make({ start = "copy",
    alive = { ["Captain Fixturo"] = 100 }, packs = { ["a hollow skitter"] = 2 } })
local runner = require("eb.ic").new(env)
local w = runner:worldFacade()                 -- what an encounter's conditions read through

local function holds(cond) return runner.evalCond(cond, w) end

DOCS.check(holds({ actor_present = "Captain Fixturo" }), "the named is up")
DOCS.check(not holds({ actor_dead = "Captain Fixturo" }), "so it is not dead")
DOCS.check(holds({ actor_count = { query = "a hollow skitter", cmp = ">=", value = 2 } }), "two skitters")
DOCS.check(not holds({ health_below = 40 }), "my health is not under 40%")
DOCS.check(holds({ any = { { health_below = 40 }, { actor_present = "Captain Fixturo" } } }), "any = one of them")
DOCS.check(not holds({ all = { { health_below = 40 }, { actor_present = "Captain Fixturo" } } }), "all = every one")
DOCS.check(holds({ not_ = { actor_present = "a missing mob" } }), "not_ flips one condition")
DOCS.check(holds(function(facade) return facade.actorCount("a hollow skitter") == 2 end), "a function reads the facade")
-- a `when` list means AND: every entry must hold
DOCS.check(runner.evalWhen({ { actor_present = "Captain Fixturo" }, { health_above = 50 } }, w), "a when list")

local misspelled = holds({ actor_presnet = "Captain Fixturo" })
print("unknown condition -> " .. tostring(misspelled))
```

**Offline lines:** the lines that use `DOCS`, `require("instances.lib` are EB's offline test world, which exists only where the example was tested: in a real script, leave them out or let the game do that part.

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
DOCS.eq(misspelled, false, "an unknown condition is false: a typo never pulls a boss")
```

### Fights: Actions

An action is a table with one main key. `do_` and `on_death` are lists of them, run in order. Every move is a walk on the mesh: a fight file that asks for any other kind of move is refused when the run loads.

#### Fighting

| Key | Its value | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pull` | a name; `opts`: `range` | The tank targets that mob, looking 60 m (`range`), and opens the fight. A mob that already lies dead is a success: `is down already`. |
| `engage` | a name; `opts`: `seconds`, `range` | Fights it to the end: when one of that name is down, the next. It is done when none is left alive in reach (`range`, 60 m) and the fight is over, so a name that is not there ends it as soon as no fight is on. After `seconds` (20 minutes when not set) it fails. Reactions are checked on every tick. |
| `clear_area` | a name or `true`; `radius` | With a name: pulls and kills every living mob of that name within `radius` (30 m), one after another, calm ones too: at most 24, each within 3 minutes. Then it waits until the fight is over. With `true`: it kills only mobs already fighting within the radius. |
| `target` | a list of names | Sets the kill-first list. A name matches by part of a mob's name, in any case. |
| `cast` | an ability; `who` | Casts the ability. `who` says who casts it, never on whom: `me`, `group` (or `all`, `raid`), `tank`, `healer`, `dps`, a class (`druid` means warden and fury), a subclass or an archetype. Any other word means the box whose ability book has it. With no `who`, the tank casts it. A cast the game refuses is reported, and the fight goes on. |
| `cure` | a table: `who`, `type`, `name`; or `true` | Casts nothing itself today: it answers `cure deferred to rotation`. Each box's cast-stack cure rows do the curing. |
| `dispel` | a table: `mob`, `name`; or `true` | Strips that mob's buff with a dispel ability from the cast stack. With none in the stack, nothing happens and the fight goes on. |
| `ability_tag` | a table: `tag`, `seconds`, `mode`; `who` | For `seconds`, opens (`mode = "allow"`) or holds back (`mode = "embargo"`) the cast-stack rows with that tag. `who = "group"` does it on every box. |
| `wait_ready` | a table: `ability`, `who`, `seconds`, `fallback` | Waits until that box has the ability ready, and it casts it then; else the `fallback` goes to every box that has it ready. It never fails the fight. |

#### Moving

| Key | Its value | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `campspot` | a table: `name`, `spot`, `who` | Sets a camp spot at `spot`, a `{x, y, z}`, as a route step does. `who = "group"` camps the group there; with no `who`, only the tank goes. |
| `move_to` | `{x, y, z}` | The tank walks there. |
| `anchor` | a label or `true` | Keeps the spot where the tank stands now. |
| `to_anchor` | a label or `true`; `who`, `within` | Walks back to that kept spot, to within `within` metres (4). With `who = "group"`, the default, the group camps there too. The spot is then used up. With none kept, it says so and the fight goes on. |
| `interact` | a table: `actor`, `verb` | Walks to an object and uses that verb on it. |
| `verb_now` | a table: `actor`, `verb` | Uses that verb on the object now, from where the tank stands. The verb `Move` picks up a house item. |
| `click_now` | a table: `actor`, `exact` | Double-clicks the nearest object whose name holds the words. `exact = true` takes that name only. |
| `place_item` | a table: `item`, `spot`, `camp`, `heading`, `height` | Camps the group at `camp` when given, then the tank steps onto the spot, faces `heading` and puts down the house item on its cursor, `height` metres over the spot. Pick the item up first with `verb_now` and the verb `Move`. |
| `swim` | `"up"` or `"stop"`; `who` | Holds swim-up, or lets it go. It is let go when the run ends. |

#### Items and waiting

| Key | Its value | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `use_item` | an item; `on`, `who`, `until_`, `tries`, `seconds`, `every` | Uses the item, on that mob when `on` is given. Without `until_` it is used once, and no such item in the bags fails the fight. With `until_` it is used again every `every` seconds (1) until those conditions hold, at most `tries` times (20) or for `seconds` (60). Reaching the cap is no failure. |
| `wait` | seconds | Waits that long. |
| `wait_combat` | seconds | Waits until the fight is over, at most that long (300). A mob in a fight that nobody fights holds the wait and is handed to the fight; a bare combat flag lets go after 5 seconds. Reaching the cap is no failure. |
| `wait_actor_dead` | a name; `seconds` | Waits until no living one is in reach. After `seconds` (300) the fight fails. |
| `reset_timer` | a timer's name | Restarts that fight timer, for a mechanic that comes every N seconds. |

#### Saying, looting and your own Lua

| Key | Its value | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `announce` | a line of text | Writes `ANNOUNCE:` and the line to EB's console, with `{{verdict.<step id>}}` filled in. Nothing goes to the game's chat. |
| `loot` | `"chest"` or `"shinies"` | `"chest"`: the tank takes every chest within 75 m, nearest first (up to 8), then walks back. No chest is a success. `"shinies"` takes nothing yet. |
| `fn` | `function(ctx) ... end` | Your own Lua, for anything else. `ctx` holds `w` (what conditions read), `verdicts` and `opts`. It returns true, or false and the reason. |

### Fights: Commands and console lines

A fight runs as a step of its instance run: start the run as the [Instances](#instances-commands) page says. In these commands, `<ic>` is the instance's name: `authored/<folder>` for one of your own.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `eb ic run <ic>` | Runs the instance. It reads the folder and every fight file it calls as it starts, so an edit counts from the next run. |
| `eb ic loop <ic> [minutes]` | Loops it. The files are read once, when the loop starts. |
| `eb ic near <ic> [n]` | The `n` steps nearest to where you stand (5), with their numbers. |
| `eb ic teststep <ic> <step>` | Runs that one step now, from this box: no way in, no zone's end, not counted in `eb ic stats`. |
| `eb ic nextstep` | Runs the step after the last one tested. |
| `eb ic status` | The run: lead or follower, what it is doing, the step (n/N and its id) and the last line. |
| `eb ic stop` | Stops the run. Every wait ends; nobody is moved. |
| `eb encounter fights` | This zone's fight files from EB's instance library, in plain words. |
| `eb encounter fight [<named>]` | Lays one on this box with no run going. See [Use a fight file with no run going](#fights-use-a-fight-file-with-no-run-going). |
| `eb encounter status` | What is laid on. `eb encounter off` takes it off. |
| `eb status combat` | What EB loaded of this box's cast stack, as counts, or `cast stack: none` and why. |
| `eb claim status` | Which box holds which cure, rez or group action. |

While a fight runs, the console shows these lines. Every line of the run starts with `[ic]`.

- `encounter '<name>' (named)`: the gate held and the fight starts. The kind is in brackets.
- `encounter '<name>' gate not met - skipping`: the gate did not hold. The step ends as `skipped:gate`.
- `kill-first: <names>`: the kill-first list is on.
- `combat override on for '<name>'`: the fight's `combat_override` is on.
- `phase '<id>'`: a step or gate phase starts. Each action follows on its own line.
- `reactive '<id>' fires`: a reaction's condition held, with `(once)` for a one-shot.
- `[FAILED]` after an action: in a step or gate phase, the fight ends there and the run stops. In a reaction it is only reported.
- `a reactive phase of '<name>' is still armed after 60 passes - going on`: a reaction's condition never cleared after a phase.
- `step <id> encounter verdict <verdict>`: how the fight ended.
- `<names> first from here (the fight at step N)`: the walk toward a fight put its names first.
- `a fight on the way with <name>` ...: a mob of a later fight joined a fight on the way, so that fight's rules are on for this fight.
- `RECOVERY (death at step N)`: the tank died in the fight, and the recovery starts.
- `on_death: <note>`: one line for each `on_death` action.
- `ANNOUNCE: <text>`: an `announce` action or step.

### Fights: The cast stack

A fight file says what happens when. What each character casts comes from its own cast stack: one profile per character. The Combat page covers the file and its rows: [the cast-stack file](#combat-and-cast-stacks-the-cast-stack-file).

- `eb status combat` shows what EB loaded, as counts, or `cast stack: none` and why.
- A character with no profile file of its own starts from its archetype's template. EB ships one per archetype (fighter, priest, scout, mage) in the EB folder's `data\eb\stacks\templates\`. To make it the character's own, copy it into the profiles folder's `Main` folder as `<Server>_<Character>.json` and put the character's real abilities in.
- A character with profiles on two servers loads the one the setting `caststack.server.<character>` pins, else the one for the server this session is on. With neither known, EB names the servers and loads none.
- `eb reload stack` reads the stack again now. Otherwise EB looks for a change every 30 seconds.
- A heal, ward, cure, rez or power row that EB's class facts cannot complete is held back, never guessed. `eb anal fix` lists the rows EB will not cast.
- `eb cs profile <name>` picks which profile of the file EB casts from.

### Fights: If something goes wrong

When a folder does not load, `eb ic run` answers `the IC did not load:` and the reason, naming the step and the fight file. The rest shows in the run's console lines.

| Problem | What EB says | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A typo in a condition | `unknown condition '<key>'` | Fix the key. See [Conditions](#fights-conditions-triggers). |
| A typo in an action | `unknown action { ... }`, with the phase and the action's number | Fix the key. See [Actions](#fights-actions). |
| The file is not found | `calls encounter '<name>' that will not load` | Save it in `encounters` as the step's `name` plus `.lua`, and check it for a Lua error. |
| A bad spot | `its fight spot is not { x, y, z }` | Write three numbers. |
| Skipped, mob is there | `encounter '<name>' gate not met - skipping` | The gate is read at the spot, as far as `search` reaches. Move the spot closer, raise `search`, or leave out `in_combat = false` when a fight may already be on there. |
| The win test fails | `FAILED:done-test`, and the run stops | Use the mob's exact name in `done`, and remember that a mob out of reach reads as dead. Try it with `eb ic teststep`. |
| The mob is refused | `refused: guard`, `refused: epic` or `refused: tooStrong (benched this session)` | EB refuses that mob, and the fight fails. A mob with a guard word in its name is fought only outside a city, when the file names that mob. An epic that is already fighting is refused, and so is a mob benched as too strong, until EB starts again. |
| Nothing to target | `could not target <name> (none in reach)` | No living mob of that name is within 60 m of the tank. Check the name and the spot, or give `pull` a larger `range`. |
| Engage runs out | `engage <name>: still fighting after N s` | Give it more `seconds`, or check that the name is the mob that is fighting. |
| A reaction never stops | `a reactive phase of '<name>' is still armed after 60 passes` | Its condition stays true. Add `once = true`, a `since`, or `reset_timer` as its first action. |
| A reaction never fires | No `reactive '<id>' fires` line | Check the text `chat_seen` waits for, and remember that the condition reads the tank. `detriment_present` never holds today. |
| A cast does not go | `precast <ability> was not cast here` and why | The game refused it: not in that book, or still on its reuse. The fight goes on. Check the name and `who`. |
| An edit does nothing | The loop runs the old file | A loop keeps the files it read when it started. Stop it with `eb ic stop` and start the loop again. |

### Fights: Today on EB for InnerSpace

- `detriment_present` never holds: no detriment read reaches a fight yet, so a reaction gated on it never fires. Let the cast stack's cure rows cure.
- The `cure` action casts nothing itself: it answers `cure deferred to rotation`, and each box's cast-stack cure rows do the curing. With the crew relay up, the claims give each cure, rez and dispel to one box. `eb claim status` shows who holds what.
- `loot = "shinies"` takes nothing yet.
- `engage` reads only `seconds` (or `ms`) and `range` from its `opts`. Other keys some files carry are not read.
- `clear_area = true` kills only mobs that are already fighting within the radius, and pulls nothing new. Name the mob to clear a calm pack.
- Epic mobs: `pull`, `engage` and a named `clear_area` refuse an epic only when it is already fighting within 60 m. A calm epic is not read as one, so the fight goes ahead.
- Heroic opportunities are not answered yet: EB for InnerSpace cannot read the wheel. See [Combat](#combat-and-cast-stacks-today-on-eb-for-innerspace).

### Fights: Mechanics in Lua

A fight file covers most fights. For scripters who work in Lua, the [Lua library](#lua-library) has tested snippets of the same mechanics, written with EB's own modules. Each link opens one:

- [React to a boss emote](#snippet-react-to-a-boss-emote): the handler only notes the cue, and a task acts on it. In a fight file: `chat_seen`.
- [Time a mechanic from an announcement](#snippet-time-a-mechanic-from-an-announcement): act just before an on-screen timer runs out. In a fight file, `chat_seen` matches on-screen announcements too.
- [Step out to a safe spot and back](#snippet-step-out-to-a-safe-spot-and-back), on the mesh. In a fight file: `campspot`, or `anchor` and `to_anchor`.
- [Change phase at a health mark](#snippet-change-phase-at-a-health-mark). In a fight file: `mob_health_below` with `once = true`.
- [Interrupt the boss's big cast yourself](#snippet-interrupt-the-bosss-big-cast-yourself). In a fight file: `mob_casting` and a `cast`.
- [Who is in the fight](#snippet-who-is-in-the-fight): one read says how many mobs are on you and whether a named is engaged.

## Quests

A quest pack is one Lua file per quest: the steps you would play, in order. EB runs them one at a time and checks the quest journal as it goes.

### Quests: What a quest pack is

A quest pack tells EB how to do one quest. It is a Lua file that lists the steps you would play, in order: walk here, hail this NPC, click that, kill those.

EB runs the steps one at a time. It hands zone travel, fights and loot to its own travel, combat and looting, and it moves on when the quest journal shows that a part is done.

Several packs in one folder make a **quest line**. EB runs a line's quests in order, from the first to the last.

An errand that is not a journal quest, such as a token buy or a language primer, is a task: the same kind of file, on the same runner. See [Tasks](#tasks).

### Quests: Quick start

Run a quest EB already has. Type these in the InnerSpace console of the character's session:

1. Find it: `eb ql list <words>`. EB lists the quest lines and quests whose names hold those words.
2. Start it: `eb ql start <line or quest>`. A quest's name runs that one quest; a line's name runs the whole line.
3. Watch it: `eb ql status` names the quest, the step it is on and what it waits for.
4. Stop it: `eb ql cancel`.

The first time you ask, EB reads its quest folders for a few seconds, says so, and then answers. The Quest Runner window does the same with buttons: `eb windows quests`.

**Your own pack** runs the same way. Save it in the `data\ebquests\authored` folder inside your EB folder (make the folders if they are not there yet), named after the quest: `the_fixture_errand.lua`. Then type `eb ql start the fixture errand`. EB finds a pack by its file name, whatever the case, spaces or punctuation.

### Quests: Step by step: write a quest pack

1. Create the file in `data\ebquests\authored`, named after the quest: `the_fixture_errand.lua`.
2. Make it return one table: `return { ... }`.
3. In the table, write `schema = "eb-quest/1"` and `quest_name`: the quest's name exactly as the journal shows it.
4. Add `steps = { ... }`, one table per step, in the order you would play them.
5. Open each part of the quest with a comment step: `{ type = "comment", description = "Stage 1: take the errand" }`.
6. Start each part with `CheckZone "<zone>"`, so EB travels there first when the character is somewhere else.
7. Write what you would do, one step each: `MM x,y,z` walks, `HailActor <npc>,1` talks, `ClickActor "<name>"` clicks, `KillMobs "<mob>","",30,5` fights.
8. On a step that repeats until the journal ticks a line (clicks, kills, gathering), add `completed = "<journal text>"`.
9. After each part, check the journal: `CheckQuestStep "<journal text>"` goes on when the journal shows that text, so a part that did not work stops the run there. `eb qsteps <quest>` prints the texts the journal shows.
10. Finish with the hand-in, `HailActor <giver>,1`, then `QuestComplete`, which checks that the quest left the journal.
11. Run it: `eb ql start the fixture errand`, and watch `eb ql status`.

The tested pack [Recipe: a quest pack with stages, hails and clicks](#snippet-recipe-a-quest-pack-with-stages-hails-and-clicks) is this recipe end to end. It is the first snippet under [Worked example](#quests-worked-example), and its `PACK` table is what your file returns.

The Quest Builder writes the same file with a form per step, and makes steps from where you stand and what you target: `eb creator quest`.

### Quests: Step by step: make a quest line

1. Make a folder for the line in `data\ebquests\authored`, named after the line: `Fixture Line`.
2. Put a file named `questline.lua` in it that returns `{ schema = "eb-questline/1", name = "Fixture Line" }`. That file is what makes the folder a line.
3. Put the line's quests beside it, numbered in play order: `001-the_fixture_errand.lua`, `002-the_fixture_reeds.lua`. EB runs them in file-name order.
4. Start the line by the folder's name: `eb ql start fixture line`.
5. To run several lines one after another, queue each with `eb queue add <line or quest>`, then type `eb queue start`.

- Each quest of a line still runs alone by its own name, and a line never runs on into another line.
- A quest skipped on purpose (a sibling held, a prerequisite not met, a quest already done) counts as done: the line goes on.
- A queued line that stops also stops the queue; `eb queue start` goes on with the rest.

### Quests: Step by step: test and fix a pack

1. Read the texts your checks need: `eb qsteps <quest>` lists the quest's steps as the journal shows them.
2. Go where a step starts: `eb nav <NPC name>` walks to an NPC on the mesh, `eb nav x,y,z` to a spot.
3. Try one line before it goes in the file: `eb action HailActor Warden Fixturo,1` runs that one step now, by the same rules as a pack.
4. Run the pack: `eb ql start <quest>`, or from a later step: `eb ql start <quest> step=<n>`.
5. Watch the console: `[quest] waiting: <reason>` says what a step waits for.
6. Fix the file and start the quest again. EB reads the file each time the quest starts, so an edit needs no restart.

Step numbers count every entry of `steps`, comment steps too. Journal steps such as `CheckQuestStep` read the pack's own quest, so test them in the pack, not with `eb action`.

### Quests: Worked example

The topic's complete scripts come first, then its tested snippets. Today its one complete script is a hail helper: it hails your target and answers the conversation by words, the job a `HailActor` step does inside a pack. The first snippet after it is a whole quest pack, run end to end on the offline stand-in for the game.

#### Complete script: Hail and answer an NPC

A drop-in script that hails your target and walks a conversation by the words of each reply you want, in the speech bubble or the classic conversation window, then ends.

**Where it goes:** `InnerSpace/Scripts/eb_hailreply.lua`

**Get the file:** [examples/script-hailreply.lua](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jiimboeq2/EB-Docs/main/examples/script-hailreply.lua) (save it as eb_hailreply.lua)

**Run it:**

```text
lua eb_hailreply "hollow" "help"
```

**Needs:**

- EB for InnerSpace's session (ISXEQ2 and ISXLUA loaded); EB itself does not have to run
- the NPC targeted and close enough to hail

**Tested:** Hails, picks the reply containing each wanted word in turn (bubble and classic), and reports what it chose.

**Verified:** tested offline: run end to end on EB's offline stand-in for the game; not run in the live game yet, so try it on one box first

```lua
-- eb_hailreply.lua - hail your target and answer its conversation by words.
--
--   lua eb_hailreply "<words>" ["<words>" ...]    hail, then for each step pick the reply that contains <words>
--                                                 (case does not matter); it ends after the last step
--
-- An NPC talks in the speech bubble (read by its reply rows' text) or in the classic conversation window (its
-- replies listed into this script's own LavishScript index, EBH_Replies). Each step waits up to five seconds for the
-- conversation, clicks the matching reply, and waits for that reply to take. A step with no match lists the replies
-- it saw and stops - it never clicks a guess.

local wants = { ... }
if #wants == 0 then
    echo('usage: lua eb_hailreply "<words of the reply>" ["<words of the next reply>" ...]')
    return
end

local SEP = "~^~"
local function split(s)
    local out, i = {}, 1
    s = tostring(s or "")
    while true do
        local j = s:find(SEP, i, true)
        if not j then out[#out + 1] = s:sub(i); return out end
        out[#out + 1] = s:sub(i, j - 1)
        i = j + #SEP
    end
end

local BUBBLE = "EQ2UIPage[ProxyActor,Conversation].Child[composite,replies]"
local VAR = "EBH_Replies"
IS.Execute("squelch declarevariable " .. VAR .. " index:collection:string global")

-- the conversation as it stands: { kind = "bubble" | "classic", options = { texts } } or nil
local function conversation()
    local seq = {}
    for i = 1, 8 do
        seq[#seq + 1] = "${" .. BUBBLE .. ".Child[" .. i .. "].GetProperty[visible]}"
        seq[#seq + 1] = "${" .. BUBBLE .. ".Child[" .. i .. "].GetProperty[LocalText]}"
    end
    seq[#seq + 1] = "${ReplyDialog(exists)}"
    seq[#seq + 1] = "${ReplyDialog.IsVisible}"
    local s = split(IS.Parse(table.concat(seq, SEP)))
    local options = {}
    for i = 1, 8 do
        if s[2 * i - 1] ~= "TRUE" then break end
        options[i] = s[2 * i]
    end
    if #options > 0 then return { kind = "bubble", options = options } end
    if s[17] == "TRUE" and s[18] ~= "FALSE" then
        IS.Execute(VAR .. ":Clear")
        IS.Execute("ReplyDialog.Replies:GetOptions[" .. VAR .. "]")
        local n = math.min(tonumber(IS.Parse("${" .. VAR .. ".Used}")) or 0, 12)
        local rows = {}
        for i = 1, n do
            rows[#rows + 1] = "${" .. VAR .. "[" .. i .. "].FirstKey}" .. SEP .. "${" .. VAR .. "[" .. i .. "].CurrentValue}"
        end
        local r = n > 0 and split(IS.Parse(table.concat(rows, SEP))) or {}
        for i = 1, n do options[i] = r[2 * i] or "" end
        return { kind = "classic", options = options }
    end
    return nil
end

local function choose(c, n)
    if c.kind == "bubble" then IS.Execute(BUBBLE .. ".Child[" .. n .. "]:LeftClick")
    else IS.Execute("ReplyDialog:Choose[" .. n .. "]") end
end

if (tonumber(IS.Parse("${Target.ID}")) or 0) <= 0 then echo("eb_hailreply: target the NPC first"); return end
IS.Execute("eq2execute hail")
for step, want in ipairs(wants) do
    local c
    waituntil(function() c = conversation(); return c ~= nil end, 5)
    if not c then echo(("eb_hailreply: step %d - no conversation opened"):format(step)); return end
    local pick
    for i, text in ipairs(c.options) do
        if tostring(text):lower():find(want:lower(), 1, true) then pick = i; break end
    end
    if not pick then
        echo(("eb_hailreply: step %d - no reply with '%s' (replies: %s)"):format(step, want, table.concat(c.options, " / ")))
        return
    end
    local chosen = c.options[pick]
    choose(c, pick)
    echo(("eb_hailreply: step %d - %s"):format(step, chosen))
    -- the reply takes when the conversation closes or changes
    waituntil(function()
        local now = conversation()
        return now == nil or now.kind ~= c.kind or table.concat(now.options, SEP) ~= table.concat(c.options, SEP)
    end, 5)
end
echo("eb_hailreply: done")
```

**Snippets:** 33 shorter tested pieces of the same topic.

#### Snippet: Recipe: a quest pack with stages, hails and clicks

Write a quest pack, bind the quest runner, and drive it to completion the way EB's brain does: travel by the zone's own transit, walk, hail the giver through its dialog, click the quest objects until the journal updates, kill and loot, then hand in. Each stage advances on the journal's own text.

**Tested:** The pack runs to complete; the journal shows each stage in turn and the quest leaves the journal at the hand-in.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script: bind the runner to its adapters, start the pack, and drive it one step per tick
local quests = require("eb.quest").bind(deps)
local run = quests.start({ quest = PACK, name = QUEST }, {})
local trace, status, info = {}, nil, nil
for _ = 1, 100 do
    status, info = quests.step(run)
    trace[#trace + 1] = status
    if status == "complete" or status == "blocked" then break end
    -- the brain's part: the runner hands travel, fights and loot back, and the brain does them
    if status == "need_travel" then deps.nav.travelTo(info, { pack = true })
    elseif status == "need_combat" then deps.combat.engage(info); world.hated = false
    elseif status == "need_loot" then deps.economy.lootGrab({}) end
    world.tick(5000)
end
print(status .. ": " .. tostring(info))
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
-- the pack: what a quest file returns (pure data; each step is one command line)
local PACK = {
    schema = "eb-quest/1",
    quest_name = "The Fixture Errand",
    no_smart_travel = true,                  -- a pack never fast travels (this is also the default)
    steps = {
```
