```lua
        { type = "comment", description = "Stage 1: take the errand from the warden" },
        { type = "command", command = 'CheckZone "Fixture Vale"' },           -- the zone's own transit, never fast travel
        { type = "command", command = "MM 12,0,30" },                         -- walk the mesh to the warden
        { type = "command", command = "HailActor Warden Fixturo,1,1" },       -- hail, then dialog picks 1 and 1
        { type = "command", command = 'CheckQuestStep "Collect three fixture lanterns"' },
        { type = "comment", description = "Stage 2: the lanterns and the thief" },
        { type = "command", command = 'DoubleClickActorUntilUpdate "a fixture lantern"',
          completed = "Collect three fixture lanterns" },                     -- click until the journal ticks it
        { type = "command", command = 'KillMobs "a lantern thief","",30,5', completed = "Defeat the lantern thief" },
        { type = "command", command = "LootAll" },
        { type = "comment", description = "Stage 3: back to the warden" },
        { type = "command", command = 'CheckQuestStep "Return to Warden Fixturo"' },
        { type = "command", command = "HailActor Warden Fixturo,1" },         -- the hand-in
        { type = "command", command = "QuestComplete" },                      -- verified: the quest left the journal
    },
}

-- offline stand-in: a scripted world (in game the journal, the NPCs and the fights are real)
local QUEST = PACK.quest_name
local lanterns = 0
local deps, world = require("quests.lib.questworld").make({
    onHail = function(npc, picks, w)
        if not w.quests[QUEST] and not w.completed[QUEST] then
            w.journal.give(QUEST, { "Collect three fixture lanterns", "Defeat the lantern thief" })
        elseif w.quests[QUEST] then w.journal.complete(QUEST) end            -- the hand-in
    end,
    onClick = function(spec, w)
        lanterns = lanterns + 1
        if lanterns >= 3 then w.journal.check(QUEST, "Collect three fixture lanterns") end
    end,
    onKill = function(target, w) w.journal.check(QUEST, "Defeat the lantern thief"); w.lootPending = true end,
    onLoot = function(w) w.journal.stage(QUEST, { "Return to Warden Fixturo" }) end,   -- stage 3 shows up
})
```

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(status, "complete", "the pack ran to its end")
DOCS.check(world.completed[QUEST], "the quest left the journal at the hand-in")
DOCS.eq(world.did("travel"), 1, "one trip, by the zone's own transit")
DOCS.eq(world.did("hail"), 2, "two hails: the giver and the hand-in")
DOCS.eq(lanterns, 3, "clicked until the journal ticked the lanterns")
DOCS.eq(world.did("engage"), 1, "one pull for the thief")
DOCS.eq(world.did("loot"), 1, "one loot pass")
local seen = table.concat(trace, " ")
DOCS.has(seen, "need_travel", "travel was handed to the brain")
DOCS.has(seen, "need_combat", "the fight was handed to the brain")
DOCS.has(seen, "need_loot", "the loot was handed to the brain")
```

#### Snippet: Hail an NPC

Target the NPC with TargetActor(id), then send the game's own hail with Execute("eq2execute hail"). Execute sends one console line as written: use it only for commands EB knows to work.

**Tested:** The quest giver is targeted and the hail goes out to the game.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local npc = game.NearestActor('Type == "NPC"', 10, "Questfixture")
if npc and game.TargetActor(npc.id) then
    game.Execute("eq2execute hail")
    print("hailed " .. npc.name)
end
```

#### Snippet: What quests.step answers, and what to do with it

quests.step(run) does one bounded bite and returns at once with a status: working, step_done, need_travel (a zone), need_combat (a target), need_loot, complete or blocked (a reason). The runner never waits; the caller acts on the need\_\* statuses and calls again.

**Tested:** The trace shows each status once in order; the walk, the trip, the fight and the loot each happened once.

**The script:**

```lua
local PACK = {
    schema = "eb-quest/1", quest_name = "Fixture Basics",
    steps = {
        { type = "command", command = 'CheckZone "Fixture Vale"' },
        { type = "command", command = "MM 4,0,9" },
        { type = "command", command = 'Pull "a fixture beetle"' },
        { type = "command", command = "LootAll" },
    },
}
local deps, world = require("quests.lib.questworld").make({ onKill = function(_, w) w.lootPending = true end })
local quests = require("eb.quest").bind(deps)
local run = quests.start({ quest = PACK, name = PACK.quest_name }, {})

local trace = {}
for _ = 1, 40 do
    local status, info = quests.step(run)
    trace[#trace + 1] = status
    if status == "need_travel" then print("need_travel " .. info); deps.nav.travelTo(info, { pack = true })
    elseif status == "need_combat" then deps.combat.engage(info)
    elseif status == "need_loot" then deps.economy.lootGrab({})
    elseif status == "complete" or status == "blocked" then break end
    world.tick(5000)
end
```

**Offline lines:** the lines that use `require("quests.lib` are EB's offline test world, which exists only where the example was tested: in a real script, leave them out or let the game do that part.

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
DOCS.eq(trace[1], "need_travel", "CheckZone hands the zone change back")
DOCS.eq(trace[#trace], "complete", "the last status")
DOCS.has(table.concat(trace, " "), "need_combat", "a pull is handed back as need_combat")
DOCS.has(table.concat(trace, " "), "need_loot", "a loot pass is handed back as need_loot")
DOCS.has(table.concat(trace, " "), "step_done", "a finished step says step_done")
DOCS.eq(world.did("walk"), 1, "the MM step walked")
```

#### Snippet: Save where a quest is, and resume there

After a step finishes, quests.pointer(run) is the resume point to keep: { step, zone, x, y, z }. quests.resume(handle, pointer) starts a fresh run at that step, so a restart never repeats the steps already done.

**Tested:** The pointer after two steps is step 3; the resumed run walks only the last waypoint.

**The script:**

```lua
local PACK = {
    schema = "eb-quest/1", quest_name = "Fixture Rounds",
    steps = {
        { type = "command", command = "MM 1,0,1" },
        { type = "command", command = "MM 2,0,2" },
        { type = "command", command = "MM 3,0,3" },
    },
}
local handle = { quest = PACK, name = PACK.quest_name }

local deps, world = require("quests.lib.questworld").make()
local quests = require("eb.quest").bind(deps)
local run = quests.start(handle, {})
quests.step(run); quests.step(run)                -- two steps done
local pointer = quests.pointer(run)               -- keep this (write it OFF the game thread)
print("resume at step " .. pointer.step)

-- later (a reload, a new session): a fresh world and a fresh runner
local deps2, world2 = require("quests.lib.questworld").make()
local quests2 = require("eb.quest").bind(deps2)
local resumed = quests2.resume(handle, pointer)
local status
repeat status = quests2.step(resumed) until status == "complete" or status == "blocked"
```

#### Snippet: Skip a step on a condition or on the journal

A step's condition is read before it starts: false plus skip_if_condition_false skips it. SkipIfJournal "\<line>",N skips the next N steps when the journal already shows that line done, so a pack resumed mid-quest does not redo work.

**Tested:** The level-gated walk is skipped at level 100, and the two steps behind SkipIfJournal are skipped because the line is done.

**The script:**

```lua
local PACK = {
    schema = "eb-quest/1", quest_name = "Fixture Conditions",
    continues_later = true,              -- the quest is still in the journal when these steps end, on purpose
    steps = {
        { type = "command", command = "MM 1,0,1", condition = "${Me.Level} >= 120", skip_if_condition_false = true },
        { type = "command", command = 'SkipIfJournal "Gather the fixture reeds",2' },
        { type = "command", command = "MM 2,0,2" },
        { type = "command", command = 'ClickActor "a fixture reed"' },
        { type = "command", command = "MM 3,0,3" },
    },
}
local deps, world = require("quests.lib.questworld").make({ level = 100 })
world.journal.give("Fixture Conditions", { "Gather the fixture reeds" })
world.journal.check("Fixture Conditions", "Gather the fixture reeds")      -- that part is already done

local quests = require("eb.quest").bind(deps)
local run = quests.start({ quest = PACK, name = PACK.quest_name }, {})
local status
for _ = 1, 20 do status = quests.step(run); if status == "complete" or status == "blocked" then break end end
print("walks: " .. world.did("walk"))
```

#### Snippet: Wait for the journal to move on

WaitForQuestStep "\<quest>","\<line>",\<seconds> holds the pack (status working, never a blocking wait) until the journal shows that line, or ticks it. At the time limit the step is blocked, or with -continue it says so and goes on.

**Tested:** The wait reports working until the escort NPC's line shows up 15 s in, then the pack goes on; a wait that never sees its line is blocked at its limit.

**The script:**

```lua
local PACK = {
    schema = "eb-quest/1", quest_name = "Fixture Escort", continues_later = true,
    steps = {
        { type = "command", command = 'WaitForQuestStep "Fixture Escort","Speak to the ferryman",60' },
        { type = "command", command = "HailActor a fixture ferryman" },
    },
}
local deps, world = require("quests.lib.questworld").make()
world.journal.give("Fixture Escort", { "Escort the ferryman to the pier" })

local quests = require("eb.quest").bind(deps)
local run = quests.start({ quest = PACK, name = PACK.quest_name }, {})
local waited, status = 0, nil
for _ = 1, 30 do
    status = quests.step(run)
    if status ~= "working" then break end
    waited = waited + 1
    world.tick(5000)
    if world.now >= 15000 then world.journal.add("Fixture Escort", "Speak to the ferryman") end   -- the escort arrives
end
repeat status = quests.step(run) until status == "complete" or status == "blocked"
print(("waited %d tick(s) for the journal"):format(waited))

-- a wait whose line never comes: blocked at its limit (10 s here)
local deps2, world2 = require("quests.lib.questworld").make()
world2.journal.give("Fixture Escort", { "Escort the ferryman to the pier" })
local q2 = require("eb.quest").bind(deps2)
local run2 = q2.start({ quest = { schema = "eb-quest/1", quest_name = "Fixture Escort", steps = {
    { type = "command", command = 'WaitForQuestStep "Fixture Escort","Speak to the ferryman",10' } } },
    name = "Fixture Escort" }, {})
local st2, why2
for _ = 1, 10 do st2, why2 = q2.step(run2); if st2 ~= "working" then break end; world2.tick(5000) end
```

#### Snippet: Packs never fast travel

Inside a pack the destination is always reached the ground way: SmartTravelTo hands the zone back as need_travel (the zone's own transit), FastTravel is refused with the reason, and a flight-only step (FlyUp) stops because EB never flies: it walks the zone's mesh and nothing else.

**Tested:** SmartTravelTo answers need_travel; FastTravel and FlyUp are blocked with their reasons (EB never flies).

**The script:**

```lua
local function once(line)
    local deps = require("quests.lib.questworld").make({ zone = "Fixture Docks" })
    local quests = require("eb.quest").bind(deps)
    local run = quests.start({ quest = { schema = "eb-quest/1", quest_name = "Fixture Travel",
        steps = { { type = "command", command = line } } }, name = "Fixture Travel" }, {})
    return quests.step(run)
end

local s1, info1 = once('SmartTravelTo "Fixture Vale"')
local s2, info2 = once('FastTravel "Fixture Vale"')
local s3, info3 = once("FlyUp")
print("FastTravel -> " .. s2)
```

#### Snippet: A pack's own way into a zone

zone_routes names how this pack gets into a zone: each way is a list of steps run as a sub-sequence when CheckZone needs that zone. A way that fails moves on to the next; only when every written way is spent does CheckZone hand the zone to the zone's allowed transit.

**Tested:** The first way's ride fails, the second way (walk to the bell, ring it) is taken, and the pack arrives without a need_travel.

**The script:**

```lua
local PACK = {
    schema = "eb-quest/1", quest_name = "Fixture Crossing",
    zone_routes = {
        ["Fixture Vale"] = {
            { why = "via the ferry", steps = { { type = "command", command = 'Transit "Vale Landing | a fixture ferryman"' } } },
            { why = "via the pier bell", steps = {
                { type = "command", command = "MM 30,0,5" },
                { type = "command", command = 'TravelBell "Fixture Vale"' } } },
        },
    },
    steps = { { type = "command", command = 'CheckZone "Fixture Vale"' } },
}
local deps, world = require("quests.lib.questworld").make({ zone = "Fixture Docks" })
deps.act.transit = function() return "blocked", "the ferry is not running" end    -- the first way fails
local quests = require("eb.quest").bind(deps)
local run = quests.start({ quest = PACK, name = PACK.quest_name }, {})

local trace, status, info = {}, nil, nil
for _ = 1, 40 do
    status, info = quests.step(run)
    trace[#trace + 1] = status
    if status == "working" and tostring(info):find("running route", 1, true) then print(info) end
    if status == "need_travel" then deps.nav.travelTo(info, { pack = true }) end   -- the bell's ride
    if status == "complete" or status == "blocked" then break end
    world.tick(5000)
end
```


#### Snippet: Read a quest's journal lines

eb.quest.journal reads the quest tracker the way packs need it: lineState(text, quest) answers open, done, gone (the quest is up but its stage moved on) or nil (not on the tracker). A line matches its text inside the objective, else word by word with small typos forgiven.

**Tested:** The open, done and gone lines read as such; a slightly misspelled line still matches; an untracked quest reads nil.

**The script:**

```lua
local Journal = require("eb.quest.journal")

-- a reader: the game's quest tracker rows (EB's game layer supplies these in game)
local reader = {
    trackerRows = function()
        return { { name = "The Fixture Reeds", parts = {
            { text = "Gather three fixture reeds", progress = { current = 1, total = 3 } },
            { text = "Speak to Warden Fixturo", progress = { complete = true } } } } }
    end,
}
local J = Journal.new(reader)

local open = J:lineState("Gather three fixture reeds", "The Fixture Reeds")
print("Gather three fixture reeds -> " .. open)
```

#### Snippet: A pack's gates: level, a held sibling, a zone's wing

Before the first step the runner checks the pack's gates: level_required stops a character that is too low (with the reason), skip_if_holding skips the quest while a sibling from the same giver is held. Zone names compare the hub-aware way: a hub is never its own instance wing.

```lua
    local quests = require("eb.quest").bind(deps)
    return quests.step(quests.start({ quest = pack, name = pack.quest_name }, {}))
end

    skip_if_holding = { "Fixture Chore A" }, steps = { { type = "command", command = "MM 1,0,1" } } }, {}, "Fixture Chore A")

local G = require("eb.quest.gates")
```

#### Snippet: Add your own pack verb

eb.quest.verbs.register(keys, fn, about, group) adds a verb every pack can use. The handler gets the step's context: ctx.cmd (the parsed line), ctx:zone(), ctx.state (this step's own scratch table) and answers with ctx:done, ctx:work, ctx:travel, ctx:combat, ctx:loot, ctx:block or ctx:stop. It must return at once and never wait.

**Tested:** The custom verb waits two ticks while it rings, then the pack goes on and completes.

**The script:**

```lua
local verbs = require("eb.quest.verbs")
verbs.register({ "ringgong", "gong" }, function(ctx)
    local times = tonumber(verbs.csv(ctx.cmd.rest)[1]) or 1
    ctx.state.rung = (ctx.state.rung or 0) + 1                 -- per-step scratch, kept across ticks
    if ctx.state.rung < times then return ctx:work("ringing (" .. ctx.state.rung .. "/" .. times .. ")") end
    return ctx:done(("rang the fixture gong %d times in %s"):format(times, tostring(ctx:zone())))
end, "ring the fixture gong N times (a docs example verb)", "act")

local PACK = { schema = "eb-quest/1", quest_name = "Fixture Gong", steps = {
    { type = "command", command = "RingGong 3" },
    { type = "command", command = "MM 1,0,1" } } }
local deps, world = require("quests.lib.questworld").make()
local quests = require("eb.quest").bind(deps)
local run = quests.start({ quest = PACK, name = PACK.quest_name }, {})
local trace, msg = {}, nil
for _ = 1, 10 do
    local st, info = quests.step(run)
    trace[#trace + 1] = st
    if st == "step_done" and tostring(info):find("gong", 1, true) then msg = info end
    if st == "complete" or st == "blocked" then break end
end
print(msg)
```

```lua
    name = "Fixture Patrol" }, {})

local first = quests.step(run)
stop = true
```

#### Snippet: A pack verb that reads the journal and the world

A verb's handler gets the step's context. Besides the statuses it can answer, the context reads for it: ctx:completedDone() (the step's completed line is done in the journal), ctx:truth(condition), ctx:zoneEqual, ctx:groupCount() and ctx:inGuildHall(); ctx:log writes a line to the run's log.

**Tested:** The verb lights the lantern once, waits for the journal, and its step is done when the journal says so.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local quests = require("eb.quest").bind(deps)
local run = quests.start({ quest = PACK, name = PACK.quest_name }, {})
local trace = {}
for _ = 1, 6 do
    local st = quests.step(run)
    trace[#trace + 1] = st
    if st == "complete" or st == "blocked" then break end
    world.tick(1000)
end
print(world.lines[1])
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
local verbs = require("eb.quest.verbs")
verbs.register("lightlantern", function(ctx)
    if ctx:completedDone() then return ctx:done("the journal says the lantern is lit") end
    if ctx:truth("${Me.Level} >= 20") ~= true then return ctx:stop("too low for the lantern") end
    if not ctx:zoneEqual(ctx:zone(), "Fixture Docks") then return ctx:travel("Fixture Docks") end
    if not ctx.state.clicked then
        ctx.state.clicked = true
        ctx.dep.act.click({ name = "a fixture lantern", double = true })
        ctx:log("lit the lantern in %s (level gate passed, %s)", ctx:zone(), ctx:groupCount() == 1 and "solo" or "grouped")
    end
    return ctx:work("waiting for the journal")
end, "light the fixture lantern (a docs example verb)", "act")

local PACK = { schema = "eb-quest/1", quest_name = "Fixture Lanterns", continues_later = true, steps = {
    { type = "command", command = "LightLantern", completed = "Light the fixture lantern" } } }

-- offline stand-in for the game: the journal holds the line; clicking the lantern ticks it on the next tick
local deps, world = require("quests.lib.questworld").make({
    onClick = function(spec, w) w.journal.check("Fixture Lanterns", "Light the fixture lantern") end })
world.journal.give("Fixture Lanterns", { "Light the fixture lantern" })
```

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(world.did("click"), 1, "the lantern was clicked once")
DOCS.eq(trace[1], "working", "then the step waited for the journal")
DOCS.eq(trace[#trace], "complete", "and the pack completed once the journal said so")
DOCS.has(world.lines[1], "Fixture Docks", "ctx:log wrote to the run's log")
```

#### Snippet: The verb registry's parsers and its refusals

The helpers every verb's arguments go through: flags takes the -flag words out of a hail, splitFields keeps a \${...} condition whole, isComment spots a note line. dispatch runs one parsed line through its verb and turns a refused verb, or one nobody registered, into a final "blocked" with the reason - a pack is never guessed at.

**Tested:** The hail's -peaceful flag is found, the wait's condition stays one field, and both an unknown and a refused verb stop with a reason.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local rest, found = verbs.flags("-peaceful,Warden Fixturo,1")
print(("hail args: %s (%s)"):format(rest, found.peaceful and "peaceful" or "-"))
local fields = verbs.splitFields('${If[${Me.X} < 400,TRUE,FALSE]},60')
local unknown, uwhy = verbs.dispatch({ cmd = verbs.parse("DanceWithFixtures 3") })
local refusedRow = verbs.refusedList()[1]
local ctx = { cmd = verbs.parse(refusedRow.verb .. " Fixture Vale") }
local refused, rwhy = verbs.dispatch(ctx)
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
require("eb.quest")                                   -- loads every verb family into the registry
local verbs = require("eb.quest.verbs")
```

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(rest, "Warden Fixturo,1", "the flag word is taken out")
DOCS.check(found.peaceful, "and reported")
DOCS.eq(#fields, 2, "the condition is one field, the seconds another")
DOCS.check(verbs.isComment("# a note in the pack"), "a # line is a comment")
DOCS.eq(unknown, "blocked", "a verb nobody registered stops the pack")
DOCS.has(uwhy, "not handled", "and says so")
DOCS.eq(refused, "blocked", "a refused verb stops the pack")
DOCS.check(ctx.final == true, "for good, not as a block to recover from")
DOCS.has(rwhy, refusedRow.why, "with the reason it is refused")
```

#### Snippet: Is a quest on the tracker?

A journal view reads the quest tracker through any reader with trackerRows(). J:rows() gives every tracked quest and its objectives; J:questHeld(name) says whether a quest is tracked - and answers nil, not false, when the tracker reads empty and it cannot tell.

**Tested:** The tracked quest is held, another is not, and an empty tracker cannot tell.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local Journal = require("eb.quest.journal")
local J = Journal.new(deps.journal)
for _, row in ipairs(J:rows()) do print(("tracked: %s (%d line)"):format(row.name, #row.parts)) end
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
-- offline stand-in for the game: the quest tracker
local deps, world = require("quests.lib.questworld").make()
world.journal.give("Fixture Lanterns", { "Light the fixture lantern" })
```

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(J:questHeld("Fixture Lanterns"), true, "the quest is tracked")
DOCS.eq(J:questHeld("Fixture Bells"), false, "another one is not")
world.journal.complete("Fixture Lanterns")
DOCS.eq(J:questHeld("Fixture Bells"), nil, "an empty tracker cannot tell")
DOCS.eq(Journal.new(nil):questHeld("Fixture Lanterns"), nil, "nor can a view with no reader")
```

#### Snippet: Run a pack on the runner's core, with only your own verbs

eb.quest.quests is the runner without the verb families loaded: register the verbs you want, bind the core to your adapters, and step a pack. Here a two-step pack of one custom verb runs to completion, and stepTarget reads a move step's point without running it.

**Tested:** Both chime steps finish, the pack completes, and stepTarget names the move step's point.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script

local run = api.start({ quest = PACK, name = PACK.quest_name }, {})
local status
for _ = 1, 6 do status = Q.step(run); if status == "complete" or status == "blocked" then break end end
print(("chimed %d times, then: %s"):format(chimes, status))

local moveRun = api.start({ quest = { quest_name = "Fixture Walk", steps = { { command = "MM 4,0,5", zone = "Fixture Docks" } } } }, {})
local x, y, z, zone = Q.stepTarget(moveRun)
```

```lua
    { type = "command", command = "Chime" }, { type = "command", command = "Chime" } } }
```

#### Snippet: Read a pack's condition text yourself

eb.quest.cond reads the \${...} conditions packs carry, over a world snapshot: expand fills the terms, truth decides true, false or unknown, conditionExpr normalizes a bare condition first. A term EB cannot read is UNKNOWN - never a guess - and show() makes it readable (question marks).

**Tested:** The level and zone terms fill in, the comparison is true, and an unreadable term comes back unknown.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
print(cond.expand("level ${Me.Level} in ${Zone.ShortName}", env))
local ok = cond.truth("${Me.Level} >= 20", env)
local wrapped = cond.conditionExpr("${Me.Level} >= 20")
local unknown = cond.truth("${Me.GetGameData[Self.Fixture].Label} == 3", env)
local kept = cond.expandKnown("go to ${Me.GetGameData[Self.Fixture].Label}", env)

-- the same reader a run uses, built over its journal and adapters
local deps = require("quests.lib.questworld").make()
local run = require("eb.quest.quests").bind(deps).start({ quest = { quest_name = "Fixture Walk", steps = {} } }, {})
local renv = require("eb.quest.quests").condEnv(run, snap)
```

**Offline lines:** the lines that use `require("quests.lib` are EB's offline test world, which exists only where the example was tested: in a real script, leave them out or let the game do that part.

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
local cond = require("eb.quest.cond")

-- a world snapshot, as the runner hands one to every step
local snap = { level = 100, zone = "fixture_docks", x = 10, y = 0, z = 20 }
local env = { snap = snap }
```

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(ok, true, "the comparison holds")
DOCS.has(wrapped, "If[", "a comparison is wrapped before it is read")
DOCS.eq(unknown, nil, "an unreadable term is unknown, not false")
DOCS.eq(kept, nil, "expandKnown refuses a text with an unknown in it")
DOCS.check(not cond.show("a " .. cond.UNKNOWN .. " b"):find("\1", 1, true), "show() leaves no marker in the text")
DOCS.eq(cond.truth("${Me.Level} >= 20", renv), true, "the run's own reader answers the same")
```

#### Snippet: Pick a letter for OpenMail

The mail verbs pick a letter by its subject (and, when given, by the sender's whole name) at the nearest mailbox. The rules are pure: parseArgs reads the verb's arguments, shown takes the game's hidden key off a field, and pick finds the first letter that fits and counts how many do.

**Tested:** The second letter fits the subject; the take word is read; the hidden key is taken off.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script: OpenMail "fixture lantern",take
local a = mail.parseArgs('"fixture lantern",take', false)
local index, fits = mail.pick(a, rows)
print(("letter %d of %d that fit"):format(index, fits))
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
local mail = require("eb.quest.verbs.mail").mail       -- loading it registers the verbs; .mail holds the rules

-- the inbox rows, in the order the mailbox lists them (offline: invented letters)
local rows = { { subject = "Fixture Fair results" }, { subject = ":47541fd6e0da31d6:Your fixture lantern" },
               { subject = "Fixture Fair tickets" } }
```

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(a.subject, "fixture lantern", "the subject")
DOCS.eq(a.take, true, "the take word")
DOCS.eq(index, 2, "the letter that fits")
DOCS.eq(mail.shown(rows[2].subject), "Your fixture lantern", "the game's hidden key is taken off")
DOCS.eq(mail.pick(mail.parseArgs('""', false), rows), nil, "no subject and no sender picks nothing")
```

#### Snippet: Open one letter by its subject and take what it carries

A letter is picked by a part of its subject, by its sender's WHOLE name, or both - a part of a name never matches. The game may put a key in front of a subject (":\<key>:"); it is never part of it. mail.pick is the pure rule; eco.mail:open(subject, sender, take) opens the first letter that fits and, with take, takes its attachments. A quest letter opened this way starts its quest.

**Tested:** The keyed subject is matched, "Fix" does not match the sender "Fixwell", and the lantern oil reaches the bags.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script: the pure rules first
DOCS.eq(Mail.shown(":0123abcd:The Fixture Lantern"), "The Fixture Lantern", "the key is not part of the subject")
DOCS.eq((Mail.pick("lantern", nil, W.mail.inbox)), 2, "a part of the subject matches")
DOCS.eq((Mail.pick(nil, "Fix", W.mail.inbox)), nil, "a part of a name never matches")
DOCS.eq((Mail.pick(nil, "fixwell", W.mail.inbox)), 1, "the whole name, any case, does")

-- open it and take the attachment
local status
for _ = 1, 20 do
    status = eco.mail:open("lantern", nil, true)
    if status ~= "working" then break end
end
print("opened: " .. Mail.shown(W.mail.inbox[2].subject))
```

**Offline lines:** the lines that use `DOCS` are EB's offline test world, which exists only where the example was tested: in a real script, leave them out or let the game do that part.

#### Snippet: Write a Lua data file

ebkit.lua_fmt writes a table as a stable "return { ... }" file that load() reads back with no environment.

**Tested:** The document starts with return, keeps the chosen key order, and loads back to the same values.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local LF = require("ebkit.lua_fmt")
local route = { name = "a test hall", steps = { { kind = "walk", at = { 12.5, 0, -40 } }, { kind = "camp", at = { 30, 0, -12 } } } }
local text = LF.document(route, { order = function(t) return { "name", "kind" } end })   -- these keys first
print(text:match("^return {"))
local back = assert(load(text, "route", "t", {}))()        -- a data file needs no globals at all
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.has(text, 'name = "a test hall"', "a bare key where Lua allows one")
DOCS.has(text, "at = {12.5, 0, -40}", "a short number list stays on one line")
DOCS.eq(back.steps[2].kind, "camp", "it loads back")
DOCS.eq(LF.document(route, { order = function() return { "name", "kind" } end }), text, "the same table writes the same text")
DOCS.eq(LF.num(150.0), "150", "numbers are minimal: never 150.0")
```

#### Snippet: Which collection pieces you still miss

eco.collections:journal() reads the journal's collections; scope(rows, word) picks the incomplete ones a word names (an exact category wins, else a name that contains the word; "all" = every incomplete one); missing(word) answers the piece names still needed and the ones that cannot be acted on.

**Tested:** "fixture isle" is a category (two collections), "feathers" matches a name, "all" gives the three incomplete ones; the missing pieces are cleaned of their "(...)" tag and the placeholder rows are set aside.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local Collections = require("eb.economy.collections")
local rows = eco.collections:journal()
local isle, how = Collections.scope(rows, "fixture isle")
local feathers, how2 = Collections.scope(rows, "feathers")
local all = Collections.scope(rows, "all")
local names, unresolved = eco.collections:missing("all")
print("missing: " .. table.concat(names, ", "))
for _, u in ipairs(unresolved) do print(("set aside: %s (%s)"):format(u.name, u.why)) end
```

```lua
local world = CW.world({ journal = {
    { name = "Fixture Shells", category = "Fixture Isle", level = 10, have = { "a pink shell" }, missing = { "a blue shell", "[12345]" } },
    { name = "Fixture Bones", category = "Fixture Isle", level = 12, missing = { "a fixture rib" } },
    { name = "Fixture Coins", category = "Fixture Mainland", level = 20, missing = {} },
    { name = "Fixture Feathers", category = "Fixture Mainland", level = 20, missing = { "a gray feather (Shiny)", "?" } } } })
local eco = CW.economy(world)
```

*The checks:*

```lua
DOCS.eq(#feathers .. " " .. how2, "1 collection", "a name")
DOCS.eq(#all, 3, "every incomplete collection (the complete one is never picked)")
DOCS.eq(#names, 3, "three pieces to find")
DOCS.eq(#unresolved, 2, "a placeholder and an unknown row are set aside")
DOCS.eq(Collections.clean("a gray feather (Shiny)"), "a gray feather", "clean drops the trailing tag")
DOCS.eq(Collections.usable("[12345]"), false, "a placeholder is not usable")
```
