### Quests: Rules every pack keeps

- **No fast travel.** A pack reaches every zone in the world: its own zone routes first, then the zone's bells, spires, druid rings, the guild hall, doors and exits. `FastTravel` stops the step; `SmartTravelTo`, `TravelTo` and `FastTravelFirst` are taken the ground way instead. Tested: [Packs never fast travel](#snippet-packs-never-fast-travel).
- **EB never flies.** `FlyUp` and `FlyDown` stop the step. `FlyTo` walks the mesh to where its points end, and `FlyDownInto` reaches its zone on the ground.
- **One mover: the mesh.** Every walk is a walk on the zone's mesh. `ClimbWall`, and a `Press` of a key that moves the character, stop the step and say so.
- **Refused, never skipped.** A line whose verb EB does not have, or refuses, stops the run with the reason. A skipped kill would be a pull nobody fought.
- **Instances are runs of their own.** Every box reaches an instance's hub by its own travel. In a group, a member whose `CheckZone`, `ZoneDoor` or `ZoneOut` goes into or out of an instance waits in the hub while the tank zones the group (tested: [A quest that goes into an instance, in a group](#snippet-a-quest-that-goes-into-an-instance-in-a-group)). `RunIC` and `TeamRunIC` are refused: run the instance on its own (see [Instances](#instances)). `QueueMissionIC <table>,mark` before a mission giver's hail, and `QueueMissionIC <table>[,run]` after it, put the new mission's instance run in the instance queue (`run` starts the queue).
- **No grouping steps.** `GroupUp`, `Disband` and `InviteToGroup` are refused. Grouping belongs to the crew.

### Quests: The quest file

A pack file is plain Lua that returns one table. It may use local functions, build strings and read files of its own (`dofile`, a read-only `io.open`), the way EB's big packs put themselves together from a `<name>.parts` folder beside them. It has no `require` and no `os`, and it cannot write files.

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `schema` | `"eb-quest/1"`. Write it in every pack: it says the file is a quest. |
| `quest_name` (required) | The quest's name exactly as the journal shows it. EB loads a file without it, but then no journal step can find the quest. |
| `steps` (required) | The body, in play order: see [Steps](#quests-steps). EB refuses a file without it: `quest has no steps[] list`. |
| `start_zone` | Where the quest starts. The Quest Runner window shows it. |
| `level_required` | The adventure level it needs (`ts_level_required`: the tradeskill level). A lower character stops: `level 60 required, I am 20`. No gate for a quest already in the journal, for 200 (a quest that scales), or with `scales_with_level = true`. |
| `skip_if_holding` | `{ "<quest>", ... }`: skip this quest while the journal holds one of these, for a giver who hands out one at a time. |
| `continues_later` | `true`: the steps may end with the quest still in the journal, because a later quest finishes it (`repeatable = true` allows the same). Otherwise steps that end with the quest still held stop the run. |
| `zone_routes` | Your own ways into a zone: see [Your own way into a zone](#your-own-way-into-a-zone). |
| `fallback_travel` | Steps that reach the quest's start zone. `CheckZone` uses them only when `zone_routes` has no entry for that zone, and only when they go there. |
| `step_validation` | Where a fresh start begins when the journal shows a later part: see [Stages and journal texts](#quests-stages-and-journal-texts). |
| `no_smart_travel` | On unless a pack says `false`. A pack never fast travels either way. |
| `stay_mounted` | `true`: EB gets on the mount before each `MM` walk. |
| Notes | `function_name` (the Quest Builder names the file after it), `quest_line`, `category`, `order`, `starter_npc`, `starter_loc`, `prerequisites`, `max_repeats`, `no_flight` and a quest-level `optional` are notes for people and tools; the runner does not act on them. To gate on another quest, use `CheckPreReqs`. `faction_required`: see [Today](#quests-today-on-eb-for-innerspace). |

Tested: [A pack's gates: level, a held sibling, a zone's wing](#snippet-a-packs-gates-level-a-held-sibling-a-zones-wing).

#### Your own way into a zone

`zone_routes = { ["<zone>"] = { <way>, ... } }`, each way `{ why = "<a note>", from = { "<zone>", ... }, steps = { ... } }`.

- `CheckZone` tries the ways in the order written. A way whose step fails ends, and the next is tried; when all are spent, the zone goes to EB's own travel.
- `from` limits a way to a box standing in one of those zones (`"@guildhall"`: any guild hall; `"any"`: anywhere). With no `from` a way fits everywhere.
- A way may also name `side = "good"` or `"evil"`, and `bind = "<words>"`: both wait for facts EB cannot read yet.

Tested: [A pack's own way into a zone](#snippet-a-packs-own-way-into-a-zone), where the first way's ride fails and the second way is taken.

### Quests: Steps

A step is a table. A command step runs its line; a comment step is a header for people, and EB skips it. Step numbers count every entry, comments too: a skip of 2 skips the next two entries.

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `type` | `"command"` or `"comment"`. |
| `command` | The line EB runs: a verb and its arguments, for example `HailActor Warden Fixturo,1,1`. Older packs call it `target`; EB reads that the same way. |
| `description` | A note for people; on a comment step, the header text. |
| `completed` | `"<journal text>"`: the journal line that says this step's work is done. `KillMobs` and `KillQuestMobs` fight again, and the `…UntilUpdate` clicks click again, until the journal ticks it; `HarvestQuestItem`, `GatherMultipleUntilComplete` and `EscortActor` end when it does. Without it, `KillMobs` fights one pull and an `…UntilUpdate` click happens once. |
| `condition` | Read before the step starts, for example `${Me.Level} >= 120`. A false condition skips the step only with `skip_if_condition_false = true`; without it the step runs anyway, and so does a condition EB cannot read. |
| `optional` | `true`: the step may fail. It gets one try (unless `max_retries` says more), EB says so in the run's log, and the run goes on. A trip it asks for is made by the runner itself, so a refused trip passes the step by. |
| `max_retries` | How many tries a step gets in all: 3 when not set, 1 when optional. It counts the failures a step tries again by itself (a follow, a zone exit, a hand-in); after the last, the step is blocked `(after 3 tries)`. |
| `zone` | The zone the step belongs to, for maps and planners. |
| Notes | `stage`, `branch`, `action`, `action_target`, `quota`, `waypoints` and `partial_ok` are notes for tools; the runner does not act on them. |

#### Game facts in a line: \${...}

A step's arguments may hold `${...}` terms. EB fills them in from what it already knows of the world, just before the step runs; nothing is sent to the game. It reads:

- `${Me.<member>}` for X, Y, Z, Loc, Name, Level, Class and SubClass (both the class you play), Archetype, InCombat and IsDead; `${Me.Ability["<name>"].IsReady}`; `${Me.Inventory["<item>"](exists)}` and its Quantity.
- `${Zone.ShortName}` (Zone.Name reads the short name too), `${QuestJournalWindow.ActiveQuest["<quest>"](exists)}` and CompletedQuest, and `${Actor["<name>"](exists)}` with its X, Y, Z, Loc, Distance and Name.
- `${If[...]}`, `${Math.Distance[...]}` and `${Math.Calc[...]}`, the text members Equal, Find, Length, Upper and Lower, and the number members Int, Ceil and Round.

Any other term is unknown, and the line is used exactly as written. `WaitFor` and `SkipIf` keep their `${...}` and read it as their condition. Tested: [Skip a step on a condition or on the journal](#snippet-skip-a-step-on-a-condition-or-on-the-journal).

### Quests: Stages and journal texts

A quest moves through stages, and the journal shows a line of text for each part: open while you work on it, ticked once it is done. A pack moves on by those texts.

A text matches when it is part of the journal's line; failing that, EB matches it word by word and forgives small typos. Copy the texts from `eb qsteps <quest>`. Tested: [Read a quest's journal lines](#snippet-read-a-quests-journal-lines).

| Step | How to write it, and what it does |
| --- | --- |
| `CheckQuestStep` | `CheckQuestStep "<journal text>"`. Goes on when the journal shows the text, open or done, and when the quest is already completed. A missing text gets one more look 3 seconds later, then the step is blocked: the steps before it did not do their job. A quest that is not in the journal blocks at once. When the journal cannot see the quest at all, it says `NOT CONFIRMED` and goes on. |
| `SkipIfJournal` | `SkipIfJournal "<journal text>",N`. Skips the next N steps when that text is done, or gone because its stage is past; runs them while it is open. |
| `WaitForQuestStep` | `WaitForQuestStep "<quest>","<journal text>",<seconds>`. Waits until the text shows up or is ticked; a text open when the wait began must move on (300 seconds when not set). At the limit it is blocked, or with `,-continue` at the end it goes on. Tested: [Wait for the journal to move on](#snippet-wait-for-the-journal-to-move-on). |
| `WaitForJournalStep` | `WaitForJournalStep "<quest>","<journal text>",<seconds>`. Waits until the text is done (30 seconds when the number is 0). At the limit it says so and goes on: it never fails the step. |
| `RepeatUntilJournal` | `RepeatUntilJournal "<journal text>",<back>[,<loops>]`. While the text is open, goes back `<back>` steps and runs them again, at most `<loops>` times (12 when not set), then goes on. |
| `RepeatUntilQuest` | `RepeatUntilQuest "<quest>",<back>[,<loops>]`. While the quest is not in the journal yet, goes back and runs the steps again (kill until the item that starts it drops). Still not taken after the loops: blocked. |
| `CheckCompletedQuest` | `CheckCompletedQuest "<quest>"`. Ends this quest as skipped when that quest is already completed; otherwise goes on. |
| `QuestComplete` | Checks that the quest left the journal after the hand-in. Still there after 1.5 seconds, it tries again; after 3 tries it is blocked: the turn-in may not have succeeded. |
| `MakeCurrentQuest` | `MakeCurrentQuest "<quest>"`. The journal steps after it read that quest; with no name, this pack's quest again. |

#### Starting where the journal is

`step_validation = { check_quest_steps = { { text = "<journal text>", step = N }, ... } }`

When a quest starts fresh (`eb ql start`, or its turn in a line), the furthest step whose text the journal shows, open or done, is where it begins: a character halfway through does not redo the first half. `eb ql resume` and `step=<n>` begin where they say instead.

### Quests: Verbs

The first word of a command line is its verb; case does not matter. Talking and clicking are under [Hails and clicks](#quests-hails-and-clicks), the journal under [Stages and journal texts](#quests-stages-and-journal-texts). These are the others a pack uses most:

| Verb | How to write it, and what it does |
| --- | --- |
| `MM` | `MM x,y,z` walks the zone's mesh to the point; `MM x,y,z\|x,y,z\|...` walks each point in order, and `-exact` at the end stops on the spot itself. |
| `MoveToActor` | `MoveToActor <name>` walks to the nearest NPC or object of that name (looked for within 150 m); it waits while none is in range. |
| `CheckZone` | `CheckZone "<zone>"`: already there, done; otherwise your `zone_routes`, then EB's own travel by bell, spire, druid ring or the guild hall. |
| `TravelBell` | `TravelBell "<zone>"`, `TravelSpires` and `TravelDruid` hand the zone to EB's travel, as `CheckZone` does with no route: EB picks the way. |
| `ZoneDoor` | `ZoneDoor "<door>"` uses a door or zone line by its name and waits for the new zone (30 seconds). |
| `ZoneOut` | `ZoneOut [<words>]` walks to the zone's exit (the one the words name, within 80 m) and leaves by it. |
| `KillMobs` | `KillMobs "<mob>","",<range>,<pulls>` pulls the mob, and EB's combat fights it with the cast stack. With a `completed` line it pulls again until the journal ticks it, at most `<pulls>` times (60 when not set), then is blocked; without one it fights one pull. |
| `Pull` | `Pull "<name>"` fights the nearest one, once. |
| `LootAll` | Loots the corpse or chest; done when nothing is left to loot. |
| `HarvestQuestItem` | `HarvestQuestItem "<item>",<qty>` harvests a quest item; `HarvestQuestItem "<node>,!<journal text>,<max>"` harvests a node until the text is ticked (40 times at most when not set). |
| `SkipIf` | `SkipIf <condition>,N` skips the next N steps when the condition reads true; one EB cannot read skips nothing. `SkipIfQuestActive "<quest>",N` skips them while that quest is in the journal. |
| `CheckPreReqs` | `CheckPreReqs -Completed "<quest>"` (or `-Active`, `-NotActive`) skips this quest when the check fails; `-ITEMQTY "<item>" <n>` stops the run when the bags are short. |
| `WaitFor` | `WaitFor <condition>[,<seconds>][,-continue]` waits until the condition reads true (30 seconds); one EB cannot read waits its time and goes on. `Wait <seconds>` just waits. |

A wait that takes `-continue` is blocked at its limit; with `-continue` at the end of the line it says so and goes on.

#### More verbs

- **Moving:** `FollowActor "<npc>"[,x,y,z]` follows an NPC on the mesh, 5 m behind (with x,y,z it ends when the NPC gets there); `FaceActor <name>`, `Mount`, `Dismount` (or `LandMount`), `StopMovement`.
- **Travel:** `CallGH` (to the guild hall); `WaitForZoning` (a zone load, then on after 60 seconds); `WaitForZone "<zone>"[,<seconds>][,-continue]` (60 seconds).
- **Fights:** `KillQuestMobs`, like `KillMobs` but it goes on at its pass limit (20); `Leash x,y,z[,<radius>]`, `Leash here` and `Leash off`, which keep the run's fights within 20 m of a spot; `AvoidArea <name>,x,y,z,<radius>`, a circle no walk crosses and no pull is taken from, and `AvoidAreaClear [<name>]`.
- **Gathering:** `GatherMultipleUntilComplete "<item>"`, until the step's `completed` line is done (then on after 60 seconds).
- **Skips:** `SkipIfHaveItems "<item>",<qty>,N` and `SkipIfMissingItems`; `SkipIfActorWithin "<name>",<range>,N`; `SkipIfGuildHall N` and `SkipIfNoGuildHall N`.
- **Waits:** `WaitForActorSpawn "<name>"` (30 seconds); `WaitForActorNear "<name>"[,<range>][,<seconds>]` (30 m, 60 seconds, then blocked); `WaitForActorDeath "<name>"` (300 seconds); `EventWaitForChat "<text>"` (60 seconds, counting the 10 before it began); `WaitForCombat` (on after 60 seconds).
- **Errands:** `Linguist <language>` learns Halasian, Oggish, Ratongan, Stout or Ykeshan from the character's Linguist, primer bought and used (30 minutes at most); `Special` clicks the nearest special object, a glowing thing a zone wants clicked.
- **Economy:** `MerchantBuy`, `BrokerBuyItem`, `CraftItem`, `ScribeRecipe`, `DumpAllToDepots`, `RemoveFromDepot`, `OpenMail` and more.

Every verb with what it does, and the ones EB refuses with the reason: the tested example [What a pack can say: the verb list](#snippet-what-a-pack-can-say-the-verb-list).

### Quests: Hails and clicks

#### HailActor

`HailActor <npc>,<reply>,<reply>...` hails the nearest NPC of that name within 30 m and clicks its replies in order, for example `HailActor Warden Fixturo,1,1`.

- `1,3` picks the first reply, then the third; `1.1.1` picks the first reply three times. A talk that ends sooner is done.
- A name with `|` in it lists choices (`a guard|a sentry`): the nearest of them is hailed.
- No NPC of that name in reach: `no '<npc>' within 30 m to hail`. No talk within 6 seconds: `no conversation opened with '<npc>'`.
- Before a hail, EB reads the journal. When work is still open that an earlier step names after a `!` (as `HarvestQuestItem "<node>,!<journal text>,<max>"` does), the run goes back to that step first, at most twice a quest, so it does not hand in unfinished work.
- Old flags such as `-nocaststack`, `-peaceful` and `-zoomout` are accepted and ignored, so older packs load unchanged.

#### Talking and clicking

| Verb | How to write it, and what it does |
| --- | --- |
| `HailThrough` | `HailThrough <npc>[,<rounds>]` hails and clicks the first reply each round until the talk ends (12 rounds when not set, 30 at most); a reward it opens is taken. |
| `ReplyDialog` | `ReplyDialog <reply>[,<reply>...]` answers the open conversation: a number, `LAST_ENTRY`, or words the reply holds, a second apart (`wait=<tenths of a second>` changes the gap). Words no reply holds block the step and list the replies. |
| `ChoiceWindow` | `ChoiceWindow 1` or `2` presses a yes/no popup's first or second button. Never a purchase, trade, summon, money, invite or rez popup, nor one that asks the character to forsake a faith. |
| `AcceptQuest` | Takes the quest offer on screen; it waits 8 seconds for one. |
| `AcceptReward` | `AcceptReward [<n>]` takes the reward (`<n>`: the nth of a pick-one window); it waits 8 seconds for the window. |
| `OK_Button` | Presses the OK of the window that is up; with none in 4 seconds, it goes on. |
| `ClickActor` | `ClickActor "<name>"` (or `DoubleClickActor`) clicks the nearest object or NPC of that name within 30 m, the way you would. `InteractNearby "<name>"` is the same click. |
| `ClickActorAtLoc` | `ClickActorAtLoc x,y,z[,<radius>]` clicks the object nearest that spot, within the radius (8 m when not set): for things with no name. |
| `…UntilUpdate` | `ClickActorUntilUpdate "<name>"` and `DoubleClickActorUntilUpdate`, with `completed = "<journal text>"` on the step, click until the journal ticks the line; still open after 20 seconds: blocked. Without `completed` they click once. |
| `ApplyVerb` | `ApplyVerb "<name>","<verb>"` uses one of an object's right-click choices by its name. |
| `UseItem` | `UseItem "<item>"` uses an item from the bags; `ExamineItem "<item>"` examines one, for a quest that starts from an item. |
| `EscortActor` | `EscortActor "<npc>"`, with a `completed` line, follows the NPC on the mesh until the journal ticks it (10 minutes at most). |

While a line runs, a reward with nothing to pick and the quest offer a talk puts up need no step: EB takes them when it can (see [Today on EB for InnerSpace](#quests-today-on-eb-for-innerspace)).

### Quests: Commands

Type these in the character's InnerSpace console. The quest line commands take a crew scope: `eb all ql start <line>` runs the line on every box (see [Crew and group](#crew-and-group)). Every command is on the [Commands](#commands) page too.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `eb ql list <words>` | Lists the quest lines, then the quests, whose names hold the words (25 at most). |
| `eb ql start <name>` | Runs a line or a quest as EB's goal: a quest's name runs that quest, a line's name runs the line to its last quest. `eb ql start <quest> step=<n>` starts at step n. `eb ql load <name>` picks one, and a bare `eb ql start` then runs it. |
| `eb ql status` | The line, the quest and step it is on, and what it waits for. |
| `eb ql pause` | Holds the line. `eb ql resume` goes on; with nothing running, it starts the last line again where it got to. |
| `eb ql cancel` | Stops the line. `eb ql skip` skips the quest in hand and goes on with the next. |
| `eb queue add <name>` | Queues a line or quest; `eb queue start`, `stop` and `clear` run, stop and empty the queue, and `eb queue` lists it. |
| `eb lang <language>` | Runs that language's quest line; `eb lang` lists the languages. |
| `eb action <step>` | Runs one pack step now, by the same rules as a pack; what EB was doing goes on after it. |
| `eb actor <name> [verb]` | Hails or clicks an NPC or object by name, or uses one of its right-click choices. |
| `eb qsteps <quest>` | The quest's steps as the journal shows them; `eb queststep <quest>` the one it is on. |
| `eb dialog` | Reads the open conversation and its replies; `eb dialog reply <n>`, `choice <n>`, `ok` or `close` answers it. |
| `eb nav <NPC name>` | Walks there on the mesh (a place or `x,y,z` too). `eb nav bell` walks up to this zone's bell and never rides it; `spire`, `druid` and `transit` (the nearest of the three) work the same way. |
| `eb bell <place>` | Rides this zone's bell to a place; `eb spire` and `eb druid` ride its wizard spire and druid ring. With no place, each says where it goes. |
| `eb windows quests` | The Quest Runner window: pick a line or a quest, start it now or later, queue it, and watch its step. |
| `eb creator quest` | The Quest Builder: a form per step, steps from where you stand and what you target, a step tested, the file saved in your own folder. |
| `eb windows pull` | The Quest Pull window: pick one of EB's packs, see its stages, and pull it into the Quest Builder as a copy of your own. |

The Quest Builder never saves a quest that names fast travel: an old travel or walk word in a pack it opens becomes its in-world twin (`NavigateToZone`, `MM`), and it says so. Tested: [The quest commands from the console](#snippet-the-quest-commands-from-the-console).

#### Questing by hand

- `eb questhelper on`: a conversation with one reply gets it picked; standing still with no conversation up, a quest giver within 10 m is hailed and a quest object within 5 m is clicked. Never in a fight or a guild hall.
- `eb engage`, on by default: a mob you target that this box can fight is engaged at once, as if you started the fight. `eb engage off` turns it off.
- `eb hail [who]` hails an NPC by name within 30 m, or the nearest one to talk to within 15 m. `eb special` clicks the nearest special object within 30 m.

#### Driving the runner from Lua

A script can run a pack itself with `require("eb.quest")`: see [eb.quest](#module-ebquest) in the Lua library. Each step answers `working`, `step_done`, `complete`, `blocked` with the reason, or `need_travel`, `need_combat` or `need_loot` for the caller to act on. An EB quest line answers those by its in-world travel, its combat and a loot pass. It ends at once on a refused or unknown verb or a stop, and after 30 seconds on any other block. Tested: [What quests.step answers, and what to do with it](#snippet-what-questsstep-answers-and-what-to-do-with-it) and [Load a quest pack from its file](#snippet-load-a-quest-pack-from-its-file).

### Quests: Today on EB for InnerSpace

- **Offers, rewards and popups.** EB does not click a quest offer, a reward window or a yes/no popup by itself here yet. `AcceptQuest`, `AcceptReward` and `ChoiceWindow` stop and say why, and a running line leaves an offer or a reward up for you to take by hand.
- **Lifts and rides.** `RideLift`, `UseLift` and `Transit` have nothing to ride with yet. The lift steps find no lift, try again, then stop. `Transit` hands its post to EB's travel as if it were a zone, and the line ends when that travel has no way there. Write the way around them for now.
- **Books and bare spots.** `ReadBook` and `ClickLoc` stop the step: EB cannot read a book or click a bare spot here yet.
- **Facts EB cannot read yet:** the character's side (good or evil), bind point, faction standing and deity. So `SkipIfAlignment` skips nothing, a zone route's `side` limits nothing and one with `bind` never fits, `faction_required` never gates a quest, and `${Me.GetGameData[Self.Deity].Label}` is unknown. So are `${Me.TSLevel}`, `${Me.IsSwimming}`, `${Me.IsClimbing}`, `${Me.FlyingUsingMount}` and `${EQ2UIPage[...].IsVisible}`.
- **Clicks and languages.** `InteractNearby` reads no range or keyword yet: it clicks the nearest match within 30 m. `UseItemOnActor` uses its item without targeting the actor. `SkipIfKnowsLanguage` cannot ask the game yet: after 5 seconds it runs the steps.
- **New pack files.** EB reads its quest folders once, the first time you ask. A pack file added after that is found once EB starts again in that session; an edit to a file EB already knows needs no restart.

### Quests: If something goes wrong

| What happened | What EB says, and what to do |
| --- | --- |
| No pack by that name | `no quest line or quest called '<name>'`. The file is not in `data\ebquests\authored`, or its name is spelled another way: `eb ql list <words>` shows what EB has. A file added after EB first read its folders is found once EB starts again. |
| The name fits several | `'<name>' names 3 packs - say which: ...`. Type one of the paths it lists, such as `authored/the_fixture_errand`. |
| The file does not load | `the quest file did not load (<file>): <reason>`: a Lua error, `quest file did not return a table`, or `quest has no steps[] list`. |
| A verb EB lacks | `<Verb> is not handled by the EB quest runner yet`, or `is refused by the EB quest runner: <why>`. A typo, or a verb EB does not have or refuses: see [Verbs](#quests-verbs). |
| A step waits | `[quest] waiting: <reason>`. EB keeps at it; still blocked after 30 seconds, the line stops with that reason. |
| A journal check fails | `... has no line like '<text>' - the steps before it did not do their job`. The part before it did not finish, or the text differs: compare it with `eb qsteps <quest>`. |
| The quest was not taken | `'<quest>' is not in the journal`. Check the NPC's name and the replies of `HailActor`, or take the offer by hand. |
| An offer or reward waits | `[quest] the quest offer waits: ...` or `[quest] the reward waits: ...`. EB did not click it (see [Today](#quests-today-on-eb-for-innerspace)): take it by hand. |
| The hand-in failed | `... still in the journal after QuestComplete - the turn-in may not have succeeded`. Check the giver's name and the replies of the last `HailActor`. |
| The steps ran out | `the steps ran out but the journal still holds '<quest>' - check the pack`. The hand-in is missing; or, when a later quest finishes it, add `continues_later = true`. |
| No NPC in reach | `no '<npc>' within 30 m to hail`. Walk closer first (`MM` or `MoveToActor`), or fix the name. |
| A kill or click goes on | `objective still open after 5 pulls`, or `the journal did not update within 20s`. The `completed` text differs from the journal's line, or the target is wrong. |
| No way to a zone | `could not travel to <zone> by bell, spire, ring or the guild hall`. Write the way in with `zone_routes`. |
| FastTravel in a pack | `... packs never fast travel ...`. Write `CheckZone "<zone>"` instead, with a zone route when EB's travel has no way. |

## Tasks

Errands that are not journal quests, such as a token buy, a language primer or a mission pickup: run a task file, line steps up in a task list, and let EB's chores do the daily rounds.

### Tasks: What tasks are for

A task is an errand that is not a journal quest: a token buy, a language primer, a mission pickup. EB does it for you, walking the zone's mesh and travelling by bells, spires, druid rings, doors and the guild hall, never by fast travel. You can run one task, line several up, or let EB's own chores do the daily rounds.

- **Task files** are files of steps that came with EB, or that you write. `eb taskfile run` runs one.
- **Task lists** are your own lists of steps for one character, made in the Tasks window: run a quest line, run an instance, run a command, or wait.
- **Chores** are EB's own rounds: the overseer missions, the writs, the trainer, the mercenary and the collections. `eb tasks` shows how each stands.

### Tasks: Quick start

EB comes with task files. Type these in the InnerSpace console of a session where EB runs:

1. List them, by folder:

   ```text
   eb taskfile list
   ```

2. Run one:

   ```text
   eb taskfile run <file>
   ```

   Name the file by its folder and name (`Examples/Library_of_Erudin_Heroic`) or by its file name in words (`grab tso daily double`).

3. Watch it with `eb ql status`, and stop it with `eb ql cancel`.

**Where the files are.** In the EB folder, under `data\eb\tasks\`, in the one folder EB ships there: the *task folder*. Each folder inside it is a category.

Typed alone, `eb tasks` opens the Tasks window. Its *Task files* tab shows the same files, and every step of each.

### Tasks: Run a task file

1. Find it: `eb taskfile list` lists every task file by folder. Add words to list only the paths that hold them, such as `eb taskfile list roc`.
2. Run it: `eb taskfile run <file>`, with its path under the task folder or its file name in words. A word that fits two files is answered with both, so add a word.
3. Watch it: `eb ql status` shows the step it is on and what it waits for.
4. Hold it with `eb ql pause`, and go on with `eb ql resume`.
5. Stop it with `eb ql cancel`, or `eb end quest`.

- A task runs as a quest line of its own, and one quest line runs at a time. While another one or an instance run is going, EB says which to end first: `eb ql cancel` or `eb ic stop`.
- A task keeps no place. Run it again and it starts at its first step.
- The *Task files* tab shows each task's steps, so you can read what one does before you run it. It does not run them.

### Tasks: Write a task file

A task file is a Lua file that returns one table: a few fields about the task, then its steps. It has the shape of a [quest pack](#quests), runs on the same runner with the same verbs, and is done when its steps run out. Every field is listed under [The task file](#tasks-the-task-file).

1. Make a file `<Name>.lua` in a category folder of the task folder. A new folder there is a new category.
2. Start the table with `schema = "eb-task/1"`, `is_task = true`, a `task_name` for people to read and a `function_name` in snake_case.
3. Say what the task does in `method_summary`. The *Task files* tab shows its first sentence.
4. Add `steps`, in order. A step with `type = "comment"` labels a part. A step with `type = "command"` does one thing, written in its `command` as a verb and its arguments.
5. Move the EB way: `CheckZone <zone>` gets to a zone, and `MM x,y,z` walks the zone's mesh.
6. Use only verbs the runner has: see [the verbs a task uses most](#verbs-a-task-uses-most), and the full list on [Quests](#quests-verbs).
7. Check that EB finds it: `eb taskfile list <words>` names it, and the *Task files* tab shows its steps, or why it could not read it. If the tab was open, press *Read again* first.
8. Run it with `eb taskfile run <file>`, and watch it with `eb ql status`.

#### From a script

A verb the runner does not have stops the task at that step, with the reason. It is never guessed or skipped. `eb.quest` answers which verbs it has:

##### Snippet: What a pack can say: the verb list

eb.quest knows every verb a pack may use. supported(verb) answers yes or no, ported() lists each verb with what it does and its group, refused() lists the verbs EB refuses on purpose with the reason. A line with a verb nobody handles stops the run with a clear reason; it is never guessed or skipped.

**Tested:** HailActor is supported, a made-up verb is not, and running it stops the pack with "not handled".

**The script:**

```lua
local Q = require("eb.quest")
local ported, refused = Q.ported(), Q.refused()
local groups = {}
for _, v in ipairs(ported) do groups[v.group] = (groups[v.group] or 0) + 1 end

local deps = require("quests.lib.questworld").make()
local quests = Q.bind(deps)
local run = quests.start({ quest = { schema = "eb-quest/1", quest_name = "Fixture Verbs",
    steps = { { type = "command", command = 'FrobnicateLever "a fixture lever"' } } }, name = "Fixture Verbs" }, {})
local st, why = quests.step(run)
print("FrobnicateLever -> " .. st)
```

**Offline lines:** the lines that use `require("quests.lib` are EB's offline test world, which exists only where the example was tested: in a real script, leave them out or let the game do that part.

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
DOCS.check(Q.supported("HailActor"), "HailActor is a pack verb")
DOCS.check(Q.supported("mm"), "verbs match in any case")
DOCS.check(not Q.supported("FrobnicateLever"), "a made-up verb is not")
DOCS.check(#ported > 200, "hundreds of verbs are ported")
DOCS.check(groups.npc and groups.travel and groups.quest, "grouped by concern: npc, travel, quest ...")
DOCS.check(#refused > 5, "the refused ones are listed with their reason")
DOCS.eq(st, "blocked", "an unknown verb stops the run")
DOCS.has(why, "not handled", "and says why")
```

A task file loads like a quest pack: `quests.load(path)` hands back a handle to start, or `nil` and the reason. A data file that is not a task still loads, but its run is blocked with what it is:

##### Snippet: Load a quest pack from its file

quests.load(path) reads a pack file as pure data (it may not run code) and hands back a handle to start. A file that is a quest line index, not a quest, still loads, but its run is blocked with what it is.

**Tested:** The pack loads with its name and five steps and runs to complete; the line index loads as not runnable.

**The script:**

```lua
local deps, world = require("quests.lib.questworld").make()
local quests = require("eb.quest").bind(deps)

local handle = assert(quests.load("tests/eb/docs_examples/quests/lib/packs/fixture_lanterns.lua"))
print(("loaded %s: %d steps"):format(handle.name, #handle.quest.steps))
local run = quests.start(handle, {})
local status
for _ = 1, 30 do
    status = quests.step(run)
    if status == "complete" or status == "blocked" then break end
    world.tick(1000)
end

-- a quest LINE index (the order of a line's quests) is data too, but it is not a quest
local index = { quest = { schema = "eb-questline/1", name = "Fixture Line" }, name = "Fixture Line",
                notRunnable = "an eb-questline/1 index (the order of a quest line), not a quest: run the line's quests" }
local st, why = quests.step(quests.start(index, {}))
```

**Offline lines:** the lines that use `require("quests.lib` are EB's offline test world, which exists only where the example was tested: in a real script, leave them out or let the game do that part.

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
DOCS.eq(handle.quest.quest_name, "The Fixture Lanterns", "the handle carries the pack")
DOCS.eq(status, "complete", "the pack ran to its end")
DOCS.eq(world.did("click"), 2, "both lanterns were clicked")
DOCS.eq(st, "blocked", "an index file is not run")
DOCS.has(why, "not a quest", "and says what it is")
```

### Tasks: Make a task list

A task list is your own list of steps for one character, run one after another. You make it in the Tasks window.

1. Open the Tasks window with `eb tasks` (or `eb windows tasks`) and pick the *Task lists* tab.
2. Press *+ New list*, then *Rename* to name it.
3. Press *+ Add a step* for each step, in order: *Run a quest line*, *Run an instance*, *Run a command* (pick one, or type your own) or *Wait*.
4. Press *Run this list*. *Status* says how it stands, and *Stop the task* stops it.

From the console, `eb tasklist run <list>` runs a list whole, `eb tasklist status` says where it is, and `eb tasklist stop` ends it.

- *Run this list* puts a list of quest lines only on EB's quest queue, and a list of instances only on the instance queue. A list that mixes kinds runs with `eb tasklist run <list>`.
- A command EB refuses is said and skipped, and the list goes on. An instance run that stops ends the list.
- A command step never fast travels: the list refuses one when you add it, and again when it runs. For a trip, use `eb goto <zone>`, or one way only, such as `eb goto <zone> spire` (`bell` and `druid` work too). `eb spire <place>` and `eb druid <place>` ride this zone's own spire or druid ring.
- `eb tasklist stop` ends the wait in hand and an instance run the list started. A quest line it started runs on until `eb ql cancel`. `eb stopall` ends the list too.
- A list can run by itself when the character logs in, when it zones in or every few hours, and it can be kept to some levels: see [Commands](#tasks-commands).
- For the crew, `eb all tasklist run <list>` runs each box's own list of that name, never on a box played by hand.

### Tasks: Chores

EB has five chores of its own: the overseer's daily missions, the errands (the writs), the trainer, the mercenary and the collections. Each has its own command (`eb overseer`, `eb errands`, `eb trainer`, `eb mercenary`, `eb collections`), and `eb tasks` shows them all in one place.

1. Type `eb tasks status`. Each chore says running, done, stopped or idle, why it last stopped, and what it needs on this box.
2. For a night's round, make a task list called `overnight` with the chores you want as command steps, such as `eb overseer run` and `eb errands run`.
3. Type `eb tasks run`. It runs your list called overnight, or the overseer's daily missions (`eb overseer run`) when you have none.

- A chore is one pass. It says when it is done, and when it cannot go on it says why and stops.
- A chore whose part is not on this box does not start, and its command says what it needs.

#### From a script

A chore is a goal you hand to EB's brain:

##### Snippet: Hand the brain a chore loop

eb.loops builds a chore loop as a brain goal: overseer, errands, trainer, mercenary or collections. Give it an activities provider (the window driver it acts through) and set it on the running brain; the brain advances it one bite per tick between its own interrupts. A trainer only ever spends points on abilities YOUR list names.

**Tested:** The brain runs the trainer pass on the booted box: it trains the listed ability with both points, claims finished research, and leaves the unlisted one alone.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local Loops = require("eb.loops")
local brain = a.app.brain
brain:setGoal(Loops.new({ kind = "trainer", params = { act = { trainer = provider }, trainList = { "Fixture Ward" } } }))
a.w.runFor(5000)                                   -- the brain ticks about 4 times a second
for _, l in ipairs(a.app.brainLog) do if l:find("done", 1, true) then print(l:match("goal .*")) end end

DOCS.eq(#trained, 2, "both points were spent")
DOCS.eq(trained[1], "t1", "on the listed ability")
DOCS.eq(trained[2], "t1", "and only on it")
DOCS.check(claimed, "finished research was claimed (free, safe)")
DOCS.eq(brain:activeGoal(), nil, "the goal finished and left the brain idle")
a.stop()
```

**Offline lines:** the lines that use `DOCS`, `a.app`, `a.stop`, `w.runFor` are EB's offline test world, which exists only where the example was tested: in a real script, leave them out or let the game do that part.

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
-- offline stand-in: EB booted on the offline world; the provider below stands in for the trainer window driver
local a = DOCS.app()
local points, trained, claimed = 2, {}, false
local provider = {
    near = function() return nil end,                          -- nil: no trainer NPC needed for these upgrades
    points = function() return { training = points, aa = 0 } end,
    trainable = function() return { { id = "t1", name = "Fixture Ward", kind = "training" },
                                    { id = "t2", name = "Fixture Bloom", kind = "training" } } end,
    train = function(id) trained[#trained + 1] = id; points = points - 1; return "done" end,
    researchClaim = function() claimed = true; return "done" end,
    researchStart = function() return "done" end,
    researchNext = function() return nil end,
}
```

### Tasks: Chores between instance runs

An instance run or loop can do three chores between runs. Each is off until you name it on the run's line, after the zone:

| Word | What it does, and when |
| --- | --- |
| `tse` | Sell and tidy: every box cleans its bags by its saved rules (EB's T.S.E, `eb tse saved`). It runs at the zone's end, inside. In a group, each member first hands its pick to the leader. |
| `repair` | When the leading box's gear is under 90%, the group goes to the guild hall and repairs at its mender. It runs once the group is out. |
| `maintenance` | The leading box runs its character's task list called `maintenance`, from its first step, for 20 minutes at most. It runs once the group is out. |

1. Make a task list called `maintenance` with the steps you want done between runs. *Run a command* offers EB's usual ones: repair, clean the bags, the depot, the overseer, the errand run, the trainer and a call to the guild hall.
2. Name the chore on the run: `eb ic loop <ic> [minutes] maintenance`, or `eb ic run <ic> maintenance` for one run.
3. For the instance queue, put it on the row: `eb iqueue add <ic> [minutes] maintenance`. In the Instance Runner window, tick *Maintenance between runs*.
4. Check it: `eb tasklist lists` marks that list as the one that runs between instance runs.

- *Once the group is out* means after a single run's exit; in a loop, after the wait for the zone's timer, the exit and the reset; and when the loop ends.
- A chore that cannot be done is said and skipped. It never stops the run.
- If EB goes down while the maintenance list runs, the list is not picked up again by itself.

Loops themselves are on the [Instances](#instances-loops-and-the-instance-queue) page.

### Tasks: Worked example

The tested complete script of the tasks and loops topic. Its card says what it does, where the file goes and how to run it. The shorter tested examples sit with the steps they show, above.

#### Complete script: Loop an instance once the group is ready

A drop-in script for the tank's box: it waits until every member is in this zone, alive, healthy and rested, then types eb ic loop for you and ends. EB runs the loop: each run ends inside the cleared copy, the tank waits out the reset timer there, leaves by the exit, resets the copy from outside and goes back in.

**Where it goes:** `InnerSpace/Scripts/eb_icloop.lua`

**Get the file:** [examples/script-ic-loop-task.lua](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jiimboeq2/EB-Docs/main/examples/script-ic-loop-task.lua) (save it as eb_icloop.lua)

**Run it:**

```text
lua eb_icloop fixture_hollow 120
endlua eb_icloop
eb ic stop
```

**Needs:**

- EB running on every box of the group; start this on the tank's box (the box that types the loop leads it)
- the instance installed (the complete instance file fixture_hollow and its encounters)
- every box already in the hub zone (fixture_docks)

**Tested:** It waits while a member is hurt, starts eb ic loop fixture_hollow 120 the moment the group is ready, and ends; the loop then runs two laps with the reset wait inside the copy.

**Verified:** tested offline: run end to end on EB's offline stand-in for the game; not run in the live game yet, so try it on one box first

```lua
-- eb_icloop.lua - start an instance loop when the group is ready: everyone in this zone, alive, health at least 90%
-- and power at least 50%. Then it types `eb ic loop <instance> <minutes>` for you (through EB's console word) and
-- ends. EB runs the loop; `eb ic stop` ends it.
--
--   lua eb_icloop fixture_hollow 120      the instance's short name and the loop's minutes (0 = until eb ic stop)
--   endlua eb_icloop                      stop waiting, before the loop has started

local zone, minutes = ...
zone = tostring(zone or ""):gsub("[^%w_/%-]", "")         -- an instance name: letters, digits, _ - /
if zone == "" then
    echo("usage: lua eb_icloop <instance> [minutes]")
    return
end
minutes = math.max(0, math.floor(tonumber(minutes) or 0))
local MIN_HEALTH, MIN_POWER = 90, 50

local function split(s)
    local out = {}
    for v in (tostring(s or "") .. "|"):gmatch("(.-)|") do out[#out + 1] = v end
    return out
end

-- one read: me, then the other five group slots (Me.Group[1] .. [5]; an empty slot reads NULL)
local function groupReady()
    local seq = { "${Me.IsDead}", "${Me.Health}", "${Me.Power}", "${Me.GroupCount}" }
    for slot = 1, 5 do
        local g = "Me.Group[" .. slot .. "]"
        seq[#seq + 1] = "${" .. g .. ".Name}|${" .. g .. ".InZone}|${" .. g .. ".IsDead}|${" .. g .. ".Health}|${" ..
            g .. ".CurrentPower}|${" .. g .. ".MaxPower}"
    end
    local s = split(IS.Parse(table.concat(seq, "|")))
    if s[1] == "TRUE" then return false, "you are dead" end
    if (tonumber(s[2]) or 0) < MIN_HEALTH then return false, "you are hurt" end
    if (tonumber(s[3]) or 0) < MIN_POWER then return false, "you are low on power" end
    for slot = 1, math.min(5, (tonumber(s[4]) or 1) - 1) do
        local at = 5 + (slot - 1) * 6
        local name, inZone, dead = s[at], s[at + 1], s[at + 2]
        local hp, pw, maxPw = tonumber(s[at + 3]) or 0, tonumber(s[at + 4]) or 0, tonumber(s[at + 5]) or 0
        if inZone ~= "TRUE" then return false, name .. " is not in this zone" end
        if dead == "TRUE" then return false, name .. " is dead" end
        if hp < MIN_HEALTH then return false, name .. " is hurt" end
        if maxPw > 0 and pw * 100 / maxPw < MIN_POWER then return false, name .. " is low on power" end
    end
    return true
end

echo(("eb_icloop: waiting for the group to be ready for %s"):format(zone))
local said
while true do
    local ok, why = groupReady()
    if ok then break end
    if why ~= said then echo("eb_icloop: not yet - " .. why); said = why end
    wait(2)
end
IS.Execute("luacall EBISX_cmd ic loop " .. zone .. " " .. minutes)
echo(("eb_icloop: the group is ready - started eb ic loop %s %d (eb ic stop ends it)"):format(zone, minutes))
```

### Tasks: The task file

A task file is read as pure data: it returns one Lua table, `return { ... }`, and nothing else. EB reads it from the task folder.

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `steps` (required) | The task's steps, in order (see [Steps](#steps)). A file with no `steps` is not read as a task. |
| `schema` | `"eb-task/1"`, the format's name. |
| `is_task` | `true`. |
| `task_name` | The name EB shows: in `eb ql status`, in the *Task files* tab and on the run's lines. Without one, EB shows the `function_name`. |
| `function_name` | A stable key in snake_case, unique in its folder. |
| `method_summary` | What the task does. The *Task files* tab shows its first sentence. |
| `start_zone` | The zone it starts in, by its short name, or empty. |
| `destination` | Where it goes. |
| `notes` | Anything worth knowing. |
| `expansion` | The expansion it belongs to. |
| `estimated_time` | About how long it takes. |
| `complexity` | How hard it is. |
| `category` | What kind of errand it is. The *Task files* tab groups tasks by their folder, not by this field. |

The last six are for people choosing a task: EB does not read them. A task can also carry a quest pack's other fields, such as its gates and its own ways into a zone, and they work the same way: see [Quests](#quests).

#### Steps

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `type` | `"command"` runs the step's line. `"comment"` is a label and runs nothing. |
| `command` | The line: a verb and its arguments, such as `MM 12,0,30`. A command step with no line is passed by without a word. |
| `description` | A note. On a comment step it is the label, such as `"Step 2: walk to the merchant"`. |
| `optional` | `true`: when the step cannot be done, the task goes on without it and says so once. |
| `max_retries` | How many tries a step that has to try again gets: 3 unless it says, 1 for an optional step. |
| `condition` | A test read before the step starts. When it reads false and the step has `skip_if_condition_false = true`, the step is skipped. |

Every step field is on the [Quests](#quests) page.

#### Verbs a task uses most

| Verb | The line, and what it does |
| --- | --- |
| `CheckZone` | `CheckZone <zone>` gets to the zone the ground way: the task's own ways in first, then bells, spires, druid rings, docks and doors. |
| `MM` | `MM x,y,z` walks to the spot on the zone's mesh. `MM x,y,z\|x,y,z` walks to each in turn. |
| `TravelBell` | `TravelBell <zone>` goes by bell only. `TravelSpire` and `TravelDruid` go by wizard spire or druid ring only. |
| `CallGH` | Calls to the guild hall. |
| `HailActor` | `HailActor <npc>,<reply>,<reply>...` hails the NPC and walks its dialog, picking those replies. |
| `BuyFromMerchant` | `BuyFromMerchant <merchant>,<item>[,qty]` buys from the named merchant nearby. |
| `Wait` | `Wait <seconds>` waits that long. |

#### Files in the task folder that are not tasks

EB never lists or runs these. A data file of these kinds handed to the runner is refused with what it is.

| Name | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `tasks_manifest.lua` | An index of the tasks (`eb-index/1`). EB does not read it: `eb taskfile list` and the *Task files* tab read the folders, so a new file shows up on its own. |
| `maintenance_cycle.lua` | An operation list (`eb-config/1`) that nothing in EB runs. The chores between instance runs are your task list called `maintenance`: see [Chores between instance runs](#tasks-chores-between-instance-runs). |
| `_missions\` | Mission tables (`eb-missions/1`): the missions one NPC gives, and the instance run of each. The step `QueueMissionIC <table>[,mark][,run][,wait=<seconds>]` reads one and puts the instance run of the mission the NPC just gave in the instance queue. *Grab TSO Daily Double* uses it. |
| `<name>.parts\` | The rest of a long task's steps, read back in order by the `<name>.lua` beside it. EB's own long tasks are split this way; a task of yours can stay one file, however long. |
| `_` or `.` first | A file or folder whose name starts with either is skipped. |

### Tasks: Commands

#### Task files

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `eb taskfile list` | Lists the task files by folder. Words after it list only the paths that hold them. `eb taskfiles` is the same command. |
| `eb taskfile run <file>` | Runs one as a quest line of its own, from its first step. Name it by its path under the task folder or by its file name in words. A word that fits two files is answered with both; a path with `..` or a drive is refused. |
| `eb ql status` | The running task: its step and what it waits for, or how the last one ended. |
| `eb ql pause` | Holds the task at its step. `eb ql resume` goes on. |
| `eb ql cancel` | Stops it. `eb end quest` does the same. |
| `eb pause` | Holds quest lines (a task too), instance runs, walks and goals where they are; the fight goes on. `eb resume` goes on. |
| `eb stopall` | The kill switch: stops quest lines, instance runs, walks, goals and task lists on this box; the fight goes on. `eb resume` lets EB run again. |

#### Task lists

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `eb tasklist run <list>` | Runs one of this character's task lists whole, step after step. `eb task` is the same command. |
| `eb tasklist status` | Where the running list is, or how the last one ended. |
| `eb tasklist stop` | Ends the list, the wait in hand and an instance run it started. A quest line it started runs on (`eb ql cancel` ends it). |
| `eb tasklist lists` | This character's lists and how many steps each has. The list called `maintenance` is marked as the one that runs between instance runs. |
| `eb tasklist trigger add` | Runs a list by itself: `<list> login` when the character logs in, `<list> zonein [<zone words>]` when it zones in, or `<list> every <hours>` (`90m` and `1h30m` work too). Kept across restarts. A trigger never starts over another run or on a box played by hand, and a fight holds it. |
| `eb tasklist triggers` | Lists the triggers. `trigger on <n>`, `off <n>`, `remove <n>` and `test <n>` (run it now) manage them; `all` works for on and off. |
| `eb tasklist level` | `level <list> <min>[-<max>] [adv \| ts]` sets the levels a list is for: a character under or over them skips it and says so. `level <list> off` takes the limit off. |
| `eb tasklist resume` | Picks up a list EB went down in the middle of, at its step. When EB is back within ten minutes it does this by itself. `eb tasklist forget` drops that place. |
| `eb all tasklist run <list>` | Each box runs its own list of that name, never on a box played by hand. Add `stagger <seconds>` and each box starts that long after the one before. |
| `eb teams runlist <list>` | Runs a list on this box, or shares its instance steps out across your teams: see [Crew and group](#crew-and-group). |

#### Chores

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `eb tasks` | Typed alone, opens the Tasks window. `eb windows tasks` does too. |
| `eb tasks status` | Each chore (overseer, errands, trainer, mercenary, collections): running, done, stopped or idle, why it last stopped, and what it needs on this box. |
| `eb tasks list` | The same, and this character's task lists. |
| `eb tasks run` | Runs the task list called `overnight`, or the overseer's daily missions (`eb overseer run`) when there is none. `eb chores` is the same command. |
| `eb errands` | `run` (the default) starts the writs. `list` says whether this box can run the craft writs and the city writs. `plan`, `go`, `stop` and `status` drive the errand run (the class trainer's wares, the port spell, a first mount), and `city` picks the city its errands go to. |

#### Between instance runs

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `eb ic loop <ic> ...` | Loops an instance: `[minutes] [difficulty]`, then any of the chore words `tse`, `repair` and `maintenance`. |
| `eb ic run <ic> ...` | One run, with the same chore words after the zone. |
| `eb iqueue add <ic> ...` | A row of the instance queue: `[minutes] [difficulty]` and the chore words. |

### Tasks: The Tasks window

Open it with `eb tasks`, typed alone, or `eb windows tasks`. Every *Run*, *Status* and *Stop* press there is an `eb` line, and the window shows EB's own answer.

| Tab | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| *Tonight* | Each character's night chores as switches (the pack pony, the garden, overseer missions, a gather route, rush writs, sell and repair, the depot), and its *Start hour*. |
| *Errands* | This character's errand run (what it would do, *Go* and *Stop*, where it is, what it spent, its city and budget) and its writs. |
| *Task lists* | Your task lists: *+ New list*, *Rename*, *Copy*, *Send to* (another of your characters), *Delete*, *+ Add a step*, *Run this list*, *Status* and *Stop the task*. A step's own *Run* runs that one step now. |
| *Task files* | The task files that came with EB, by category, with counts: each task's name, the first sentence of its `method_summary`, and its number of steps. Click a task to see every step. A file EB cannot read says *It could not be read as a task*, and why. |
| *Timers* | EB's timers: what is counting down. Add one, or clear one. |

On the *Task files* tab, the *x* on a task or a category takes it out of your lists on this PC, after asking. *Deleted*, at the end of the list, shows what you took out, with *Bring back*. EB's own files are never removed. *Read again* reads the folder again.

### Tasks: If something goes wrong

| You see | What it means, and what to do |
| --- | --- |
| `no task file called '...'` | No file has that path or file name. `eb taskfile list` shows what EB finds. A file outside the task folder, or under a name that starts with `_` or `.`, is never found. |
| `'...' names 2 task files` | The words fit more than one file. Add a word, or use one of the paths the line shows. |
| `a quest line is running` | A task is a quest line, and one runs at a time. End the other one with `eb ql cancel` first. |
| `an instance run is going` | End it with `eb ic stop`, or let it finish, then run the task. |
| `EB is stopped (eb stopall)` | Type `eb resume`, then run it again. |
| `[quest] waiting: ...` | A step cannot go on yet, for the reason on the line. After 30 seconds of that, the task stops with it. |
| `... is not handled ...` | The step's verb is one the runner does not have, often a typo. The task stops at that step. Check the verb against the list on [Quests](#quests-verbs). |
| `... packs never fast travel ...` | A step asks for fast travel, which a task never does. Write the way in instead: `CheckZone <zone>`, or a bell, spire or druid ring. |
| `... is refused ...` | A verb EB refuses on purpose. The line says why. |
| `the quest file did not load` | The file has a Lua mistake, or does not return a table. The rest of the line says what. |
| `quest has no steps[] list` | The table has no `steps`. |
| `not a quest: ...` | The file is an index, an operation list or a mission table, not a task: see [Files that are not tasks](#files-in-the-task-folder-that-are-not-tasks). |
| `could not travel to ...` | No bell, spire, druid ring or guild-hall way reaches that zone from here. Start nearer, or give the task its own way in (see [Quests](#quests)). |
| A step is passed by without a word | It has no `command` line. Check the key's spelling. |
| `optional step ... did not work` | That step has `optional = true`, so the task went on without it. |
| `no task list called '...'` | Task lists belong to one character. `eb tasklist lists` on that box shows its lists; the Tasks window makes them. |
| `... eb tasklist stop first` | A list is running on this box already. Stop it, or wait for it to end. |
| `never a step of a list` | The command fast travels, which a list never does. For a trip, use `eb goto <zone>`, a quest line or an instance. |
| `step ... skipped - ...` | EB refused that step's command, said why, and the list went on. |
| `maintenance between runs: ...` | The maintenance chore could not run, and the line says why. Most often the character has no task list called `maintenance`. |
| `the chore loops are not running` | That part of EB did not start on this box, so `eb tasks` has nothing to show. |

#### Limits in this build

- EB reads task files from its task folder only. Keep a copy of your own files outside the EB folder too: an EB update lays EB's own task files down again.
- A task keeps no place. Stopped or ended, it starts again at its first step.
- A task list has no task-file step. A command step can type `eb taskfile run <file>`, but the list waits only while a walk, a zone change or the chore a command started (cleaning the bags, a repair, the depot) is going, not for the task to end. Make it the list's last step.
- The *Task files* tab shows tasks; it does not run them.

## Crew and group

Every EB you start is a box. Put a crew word in front of a command and the other boxes run it too.

### Crew and group: What the crew is for

Every InnerSpace session that runs EB is a **box**. All your boxes together are the **crew**.

The boxes hear each other, so a command you type on one box can run on all of them. That is how you play several characters as one group: follow, walk and fight together, and run an instance with the tank in the lead.

- **A box is named by its session:** `is1`, `is2` and so on, never by its character.
- **The boxes find each other by themselves.** Each one says who and where it is every two seconds. A box not heard for nine seconds drops out.
- **A crew word sends a command.** `eb all pause` pauses every box. Each box runs the line once and never sends it on.
- **A box you play by hand stays where you put it.** Pause EB on it with `eb pause`: a crew line never moves a paused box.

### Crew and group: Quick start

Start EB in two or more sessions first (the [getting-started guide](#quick-start) shows how). Then type these in the InnerSpace console of the box you play:

1. `eb status crew` lists this box and every box it hears: its id, zone, mode, health and power. Right after a start it says it is still listening: ask again a few seconds later.
2. `eb all pause` pauses every box, this one too. A fight that is on goes on.
3. `eb all resume` lets every box go on from where it stopped.

A script sends the same line with `luacall EBISX_cmd all pause`. The crew board in the [worked example](#crew-and-group-worked-example) is a complete script that does it when a box goes quiet. Save it as `InnerSpace/Scripts/eb_crewboard.lua` and start it with `lua eb_crewboard 15`.

### Crew and group: Move together

#### Have the others follow you

1. On the box you play, type `eb follow me`. It answers `the others follow me`.
2. Each other box starts after you. It says `issued: follow` and your character's name in its own console.
3. Walk, ride or change zones as you like. The others follow you over zone lines and through doors.
4. To end it, type `eb others follow off`.

#### Walk to one spot together

1. Find the spot: stand on it and type `eb grab`. It prints `loc`, then the three numbers of the spot.
2. Type `eb relay here walk x,y,z` with those numbers. Every box in this zone walks there on the zone's mesh, this one too.
3. The boxes spread out as they arrive: where the mesh allows, each other box takes its own place about 3 m from the spot, and the box you typed on stands on it.

A box in another zone, or one EB is paused on, is left out. `eb all walk x,y,z` works too; a box in another zone then answers that the spot is in another zone.

#### Go through a doorway one at a time

1. Type `eb all stagger on`. Each box keeps its own switch, so send it to all of them.
2. A walk or a follow that a crew line starts now waits its turn: the leader goes first, then the others one second apart.
3. Change the gap with `eb all stagger delay 2000` (in milliseconds), or make your group's tank the leader with `eb all stagger leader auto`.
4. Turn it off with `eb all stagger off`.

#### Travel to another zone together

- `eb relay mygroup goto <zone>` takes your group there, each box its own way. A member you play by hand is left out.
- `eb all goto <zone>` sends every box of the crew.
- `eb all spire <place>` takes every box there by its zone's wizard spire, and `eb all druid <place>` by its druid ring.
- `eb nav` moves this box only, in all its forms: it takes no crew word.

The tested example below follows a crew member by name, the way each box runs `eb follow`.

##### Snippet: Follow a crew member with eb follow

eb follow \<name> starts a follow over the mesh and answers "issued" at once; the follow re-plans as the other moves, and a script on that box ends it with eb.nav.stop().

**Tested:** The command answers at once; a few seconds later you stand near Tankard; nav.stop() ends the follow.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local nav = require("eb.nav")
local ok, text = reg:dispatch("eb follow Tankard")  -- never blocks: the follow runs on the pulse
print("follow: " .. tostring(text))
w.runFor(6000)
local near = math.sqrt((w.self.x - 24) ^ 2 + (w.self.z - 10) ^ 2)
local wasWalking = nav.stop("the docs example is done")
w.runFor(300)
```

### Crew and group: Group up and fight together

1. On the box that leads, type `eb invite`. It invites every crew character that is not in its group yet, one every 1.5 seconds, up to a full group.
2. Each EB box accepts the invite by itself, since it comes from one of your own characters. A box EB is paused or stopped on answers no invite: you decide there.
3. On the tank's box, type `eb go tank`. That character is now the tank on every box, and a fighter takes its defensive stance.
4. Type `eb relay mygroup assist tank follow`. Every box of your group follows the tank and fights what it fights. A box you play by hand is left out.
5. To put the whole crew on one mob, target it and type `eb all tgt ${Target.ID}`. InnerSpace puts in your target's id, and a spawn id is the same on every box in the zone.

A box that assists a lead also engages what that lead targets, even before the lead starts the fight. A box you play by hand never starts a fight by itself. `eb engage status` says how it stands on a box, and `eb all engage off` turns it off on every box. Each character keeps its own switch.

**Cures and rezzes need no setup.** When two healers want the same cure, group cure, rez or dispel, the boxes settle it between them: one box acts, the same one on every box, and the others stand down. If its cast never lands, another box takes over. `eb claim` shows who holds what.

### Crew and group: Run an instance together

1. Group up first: `eb invite` on the tank's box.
2. On the tank's box, type `eb ic run <zone>`. The tank leads, and it sends the run to every EB box whose character is in its group.
3. Each other box travels to the hub zone its own way and waits there.
4. The tank walks the way in alone and zones the whole group in.
5. Inside, the others hold on the tank's camp spots and assist it in every fight.
6. To end the run, type `eb ic stop` on the tank. The others' runs end with it.

[Leads and followers](#crew-and-group-leads-and-followers) lists the rules each box keeps, and [Instances](#instances-alone-or-with-your-group) covers the run itself.

### Crew and group: Pause, stop and go on

1. `eb all pause` holds every box where it is: its run, its goal, its walk or follow. Fights go on.
2. `eb all resume` lets every box go on from there.
3. `eb all stop` is the crew's kill switch: every box ends its runs, walks and goals. Fights still go on, so nobody dies of it.
4. `eb all resume` starts the boxes again after a stop too.

- For one box, leave the crew word off: `eb pause`, `eb resume`, and `eb stopall` for its kill switch.
- Typed alone in the InnerSpace console, `eb stop` ends EB itself in that session. To halt a box and keep EB running, type `eb stopall`.
- `eb freeze` stops a box at once and cancels the cast that is going. Nothing is cast until `eb resume`.
- `eb relay mygroup freeze` does that for your whole group, and `eb relay mygroup resume` lets it go on. It is the *Stop group* button of the mini and of EB's Master Control Panel.
- `eb all resume` also resumes a box you paused to play by hand. Typed on that box, `eb others resume` leaves it paused.

#### Snippet: Pause, resume, status and the kill switch

The core commands every box answers, typed in the console and run from a script with eb.dispatch: help's usage line, pause and resume, status goal, and eb stopall halting the brain.

**Tested:** pause freezes the brain and resume frees it; a script's eb.dispatch takes the same path; stopall halts the brain while EB stays loaded.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script: lines as typed, then the same from code
local usage = a.console("eb help pause"):match("eb pause[^\n]*")
local paused = a.console("eb pause")
local wasPaused = a.app.brain.paused
local okR, resumed = eb.dispatch("eb resume")              -- a script runs a line exactly as if typed
local goal = a.console("eb status goal")
local halted = a.console("eb stopall")
print(("%s | %s | %s | %s"):format(usage, paused:match("EB paused"), resumed, halted:match("the brain is halted")))
```


*The checks:*

```lua

DOCS.check(wasPaused == true, "eb pause froze the brain")
DOCS.check(okR and a.app.brain.paused == false, "eb.dispatch ran eb resume")
DOCS.has(goal, "brain:", "eb status goal names the brain's state")
DOCS.check(a.app.brain.halted == true, "eb stopall halted the brain")
```

### Crew and group: Reach some of the boxes

1. Name one box: `eb to is2 pause`. Only is2 pauses. This box does not, unless it is is2.
2. Name several, with commas: `eb to is2,is3 pause`. A space after a comma is fine.
3. Name a character, a class or an archetype the same way: `eb to priest rebuff` reaches every box whose character is a priest.
4. Mark the characters you want to pick: `eb marked on` on a box, or `eb to <name> marked on` from yours. The mark is kept, and the crew sees it.
5. Reach every marked box with `eb to marked rebuff`. `eb all marked off` takes every mark off.
6. Give a box a role word once with `eb alias @healer is3`. From then on, `eb to @healer pause` reaches it.

To see which character plays on which box, type `eb crew status`.

Three reach words go after `eb relay` and pick the boxes for you:

- `eb relay here <command>`: this box, and every box in its zone that EB is not paused on.
- `eb relay awake <command>`: every box EB is not paused on.
- `eb relay mygroup <command>`: this character's group, this box too.

### Crew and group: From a script

- **A script of your own** runs beside EB and sends a crew line the way you type one: `luacall EBISX_cmd all pause`, run with ISXLUA's `IS.Execute`. The complete scripts in the [worked example](#crew-and-group-worked-example) do exactly this.
- **Code inside EB** passes the same line to `eb.dispatch`. Crew words work just as they do at the console.
- **An event handler** that wants the crew to act sends one deliberate line with `events.crew`. Events never reach the other boxes by themselves.
- **To watch the crew**, listen to the state every box sends every two seconds. [Read the crew's state](#helper-scripts-read-the-crews-state) lists its fields.

The tested example below turns an event into one crew line.

#### Snippet: Turn an event into one command for the crew

Events never travel to the other boxes by themselves: a handler that wants the crew to act sends ONE deliberate eb line with events.crew().

**Tested:** The announcement of a named makes the handler send exactly one "eb pause" line to every box.

```lua
-- your script
events.on("Announcement", function(ev)
    if ev.text:find("Overseer of Fixtures", 1, true) then
        events.crew("all", "eb pause")       -- one line, on purpose; every box runs it once
    end
end)

w.frame(2)
w.host:fire("EQ2_onAnnouncement", "A fixture brute wanders off.", "", "0")
w.frame(2)
```

#### Snippet: Read your group and find who is hurt

Group() answers the other members of your group (slots 1 to 5) in one batched read: health and power in percent, in the zone or not, distance, dead.

**Tested:** Finds the most hurt member in the zone and skips the one out of the zone.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local worst
for _, m in ipairs(game.Group()) do
    if m.inZone and not m.isDead and (not worst or m.healthPct < worst.healthPct) then worst = m end
end
if worst then print(("most hurt: %s at %d%%"):format(worst.name, worst.healthPct)) end
```

#### Snippet: Call out in group chat and send a tell

Say("group" | "raid", text) speaks in group or raid chat once EB has proven that call in the game - until then it sends nothing and answers false with the reason; Tell(name, text) whispers one player. Text is sent as plain words, never evaluated.

**Tested:** The tell goes out with the text as written (a "\${" defused); the group line is held back: Say answers false and says why.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local groupHeld
for _, m in ipairs(game.Group()) do
    if m.healthPct < 40 then
        -- group and raid chat are held back until EB has proven them in the game: Say answers false, and why
        local sent, why = game.Say("group", m.name .. " is low!")
        if not sent then groupHeld = why end
        game.Tell(m.name, "drink a potion, ${not code}")       -- a "${" in text is defused, never run
    end
end
print(("sent %d chat line; group chat: %s"):format(#w.world.chatOut, groupHeld and "held back" or "sent"))
```

#### Snippet: Send a command to the crew

A leading all / others / to \<who> hands the line to the crew relay; the registry decides where it also runs.

**Tested:** all runs here and goes out; others only goes out; to is2 runs here only when this box is is2.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local reg = assert(require("eb.registry").default({ root = ".", fresh = true }))
local ranHere = 0
reg:attach("core.pause", function() ranHere = ranHere + 1; return true, "paused" end, { owner = "my_helper" })

-- ctx.relay carries a crew line (EB sets it to the crew relay; here it just records what would go out)
local sent = {}
local ctx = {
    relay = function(scope, who, line) sent[#sent + 1] = { scope = scope, who = who, line = line }; return true end,
    isMe = function(who) for _, w in ipairs(who or {}) do if w == "is1" then return true end end return false end,
}

reg:dispatch("eb all pause", ctx)              -- goes out AND runs here
print(("sent %s: %s"):format(sent[1].scope, sent[1].line))
reg:dispatch("eb others pause", ctx)           -- goes out, never runs here
reg:dispatch("eb to is2 pause", ctx)           -- goes out; is2 is not this box
reg:dispatch("eb to is1,is3 pause", ctx)       -- goes out; is1 IS this box, so it runs here too
local ok, why = reg:dispatch("eb all help")    -- help runs on one box only
```

#### Snippet: Two boxes, one crew

eb.relay carries scoped lines between boxes: all reaches everyone once, others skips the sender, to names who.

**Tested:** all runs once on each box, others only on the other one, to is2 only on is2.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script: one relay per box; onLocal is what a box does with a line meant for it
local Relay = require("eb.relay")
local function box(id, name, subclass)
    local ran = {}
    local R = Relay.new({ box = id, name = name, subclass = subclass, transport = bus.box(id) })
    R.onLocal(function(line, env) ran[#ran + 1] = line end)
    R.join()                                   -- opt in: nothing is sent or heard before join()
    return R, ran
end
local tank, tankRan = box("is1", "Tankard", "guardian")
local heal, healRan = box("is2", "Mendwell", "templar")

tank.send("all pause")                         -- everyone, the sender included (it acts at once)
tank.send("others stop")                       -- everyone but the sender
tank.send("to is2 follow is1")                 -- only box is2
print(("is1 ran: %s | is2 ran: %s"):format(table.concat(tankRan, ", "), table.concat(healRan, ", ")))
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
-- offline stand-in: an offline relay bus between two boxes (in game each box's relay rides InnerSpace's own)
local bus = require("eb.relay.events").bus()
```

*The checks:*

```lua
DOCS.eq(table.concat(healRan, ","), "pause,stop,follow is1", "the other box ran each line meant for it, once")
local dec = tank.send("to is2 all pause")
DOCS.eq(dec.ok, false, "a line may carry only one scope word")
```

#### Snippet: Split a typed line into scope and command

wire.parseScope reads the one leading scope word of a line: local, all, others or to \<who>.

**Tested:** Each line splits into its scope, who and the command left over; a bare line is local.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local wire = require("eb.relay.wire")
local scope, who, rest = wire.parseScope("to is2,is3 follow Tankard")
print(("%s | %s | %s"):format(scope, who, rest))
local s2, _, r2 = wire.parseScope("others pause")
local s3, _, r3 = wire.parseScope("pause")
local s4, w4, r4 = wire.parseScope("to")                  -- "to" with nobody after it is NOT a broadcast
```

#### Snippet: A line heard twice runs once

Every crew line carries a message id; a box acts on an id once, however many times the line arrives.

**Tested:** The same message id is new the first time and a duplicate after; a different id is new again.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local wire = require("eb.relay.wire")
local seen = wire.seenSet(64)              -- a bounded set: it forgets the oldest ids past 64
local first = seen.add("is1#41")
local again = seen.add("is1#41")
local next = seen.add("is1#42")
print(("first %s, again %s, next %s"):format(tostring(first), tostring(again), tostring(next)))

-- a whole command line on the wire: encode, decode, and the id it carries
local fields = wire.encodeCmd({ from = "is1", seq = 43, scope = "to", who = "is2", line = "eb follow is1" })
local env = wire.decodeCmd(fields)
```

#### Snippet: Wait for the group at a mark

group.barrier(name) is non-blocking: call it each tick until every member here has reached the same mark.

**Tested:** The barrier waits while one member is missing, is ready once both marks are in, and times out on its own.

**The script:**

```lua

local G = Group.new({ world = world, me = { box = "is1", name = "Tankard", subclass = "guardian" },
    clock = function() return t.now end,
    broadcastMark = function(name) end,                       -- (offline: EB puts the mark on the crew relay)
    peerMarks = function() return peerMarks end })
local seen = {}
seen[#seen + 1] = G.barrier("door", { timeoutMs = 15000 })   -- nobody else has reached it yet
peerMarks.mendwell = "door"
seen[#seen + 1] = G.barrier("door", { timeoutMs = 15000 })   -- one of two
peerMarks.sparkwick = "door"
seen[#seen + 1] = G.barrier("door", { timeoutMs = 15000 })   -- everyone here
print("barrier: " .. table.concat(seen, ", "))

G.resetBarrier()                                              -- the next objective starts fresh
peerMarks = {}
G.barrier("boss", { timeoutMs = 5000 })
t.now = 6000
local late = G.barrier("boss", { timeoutMs = 5000 })
```

#### Snippet: Give the followers an order

The lead sends an order with crew.order, a follower answers it with crew.onOrder; boxes hear each other.

**Tested:** The follower gets the lead's camp order with its arguments and the sender's box id; each box hears the other. A crew line from a box that has not said who it is waits for that box's state, so each box ticks first.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local Relay, Crew = require("eb.relay"), require("eb.app.crew")
local function box(id, name)
    local R = Relay.new({ box = id, name = name, transport = bus.box(id), clock = function() return t.now end })
    local crew = Crew.new({ relay = R, now = function() return t.now end,
        me = function() return { name = name, zone = "a_test_hall", mode = "idle", hp = 100, pw = 100 } end })
    R.join()
    return crew
end
local lead, follower = box("is1", "Tankard"), box("is2", "Mendwell")
local got
follower.onOrder("camp", function(args, env) got = { args = args, from = env.from } end)

lead.tick(t.now); follower.tick(t.now)                     -- EB runs tick() as a pulse job: each box says who it is
lead.order("to is2", "camp", { "12.5", "0", "-40" })      -- travels as a crew line, never as an eb command
print(("is2 got camp %s from %s"):format(got and got.args or "?", got and got.from or "?"))
```

#### Snippet: Drive the console from a script

eb.console is the console window's model: scoped lines through the relay, history, search and completion.

**Tested:** A scoped line goes to the crew and the other box's dispatcher runs it; history and search see it.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local Relay, Console = require("eb.relay"), require("eb.console")
local function box(id, name)
    local ran = {}
    local R = Relay.new({ box = id, name = name, transport = bus.box(id) })
    local C = Console.new({ relay = R, box = id, name = name,
        dispatch = function(line) ran[#ran + 1] = line; return true, "ran " .. line end })
    R.join()
    return C, ran
end
local c1, ran1 = box("is1", "Tankard")
local _, ran2 = box("is2", "Mendwell")
local _, answer = c1.run("others pause")

local hits = c1.search("pause")
local comp = c1.complete("to ")
```
