#### Snippet: Call the group back, evacuate, read the group

eb.relay.group's calls over a real relay: send a line, read the group from the world snapshot, record a member's mark, call stuck members back (catchup) and evacuate (evac); then leave the relay.

**Tested:** The healer's box hears the pause, the catch-up order and the evacuation order; the group lists the healer with its role; leave marks the relay as no longer joined.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local Relay = require("eb.relay")
local Group = require("eb.relay.group")
local tank = Relay.new({ box = "is1", name = "Tankard", subclass = "guardian", transport = bus.box("is1") })
local healer = Relay.new({ box = "is2", name = "Mendwell", subclass = "templar", transport = bus.box("is2") })
local heard, notes = {}, {}
healer.onLocal(function(line) heard[#heard + 1] = line end)
tank.note(function(text) notes[#notes + 1] = text end)        -- lines the console shows but does not act on
tank.join(); healer.join()

local G = Group.new({ relay = tank, world = world, me = { box = "is1", name = "Tankard", subclass = "guardian" },
    clock = function() return 0 end })
G.send("others", "eb pause")
local back = G.catchup("is2")                 -- the first answer to a member who fell behind
local out = G.evac()                          -- the evacuation chain, then a totem - only ever by spell
local gs = G.groupState()
G.recordMark("Mendwell", "door")
print(("heard: %s; %s is the %s"):format(table.concat(heard, " | "), gs.members[1].name, gs.members[1].role))

tank.leave()                                  -- in game: the transport leaves the relay group join() joined
```

#### Snippet: Share a route: the scrub and the short code

eb.plroutes.share makes a route safe to hand to a friend: scrubForShare replaces a camp puller's character name with "me" (roles stay) and says what it removed; shortCode gives the same PL- code for the same plan every time, so two copies of a plan can be told apart from two different plans.

**Tested:** The puller's name is scrubbed to me, the code is stable, and changing one step changes the code.

**The script:**

```lua
local Share = require("eb.plroutes.share")
local Route = require("eb.plroutes.route")

local route = {
    schema = "eb-plroute/1", name = "Fixture camp",
    steps = { { kind = "hunt", zone = "Fixture Vale", where = "camp", at = { x = 1, y = 0, z = 2 },
                goal = { kind = "level", value = 30 },
                pull = { mode = "camp", puller = "Fixturo", target_order = "closest" } } },
}
local clean, removed = Share.scrubForShare(route)
print("scrubbed: " .. removed[1])

local code1, code2 = Share.shortCode(route), Share.shortCode(route)
local other = Route.normalize(route)
other.steps[1].goal.value = 40
local code3 = Share.shortCode(other)
```

#### Snippet: The T.S.E hand-over: a member gives its pick to the leader

At the zone's end, inside, each member hands its T.S.E pick to the leader before the leader's pass: twelve items to a trade, leaving out what cannot change hands and anything wished for in a loot roll. The give is a pollable job; when it ends the member's answer tells the leader it is finished.

**Tested:** The heirloom and the wished-for mantle stay; the two tradeable lines go in one trade; the member answers done.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script: the member's side (call give every tick until it is not "working")
local tse = eco.tse
local wished = { ["a wished-for mantle"] = true }
local status
for _ = 1, 5 do
    status = tse:give({ to = "Leaderio", items = bags, wished = wished })
    if status ~= "working" then break end
end
local answer = tse:answer()
print(("gave %d line(s) to Leaderio: %s"):format(answer.given, answer.state))
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
local TSE = require("eb.economy.tse")                        -- its plan helpers; the pillar itself comes from the economy

-- offline stand-in for the game's side of the economy: the bags, the trade window, the group (every name invented)
local bags = {
    { id = 1, name = "a fixture bracer", qty = 1 }, { id = 2, name = "a fixture ring", qty = 2 },
    { id = 3, name = "a fixture heirloom", qty = 1, heirloom = true }, { id = 4, name = "a wished-for mantle", qty = 1 },
}
local added = {}
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({                      -- EB builds this once per box; the T.S.E is eco.tse
    cfg = {}, now = function() return 1000 end, log = function() end,
    relay = { groupState = function() return { members = { { name = "Leaderio" }, { name = "Memberino" } } } end },
    drive = {
        ["bags.items"] = function() return bags end,
        ["trade.near"] = function(to) return to == "Leaderio" end,
        ["trade.open"] = function() return "done" end,
        ["trade.add"] = function(id, qty) added[#added + 1] = id .. "x" .. qty end,
        ["trade.accept"] = function() return "done" end,
        ["trade.state"] = function() return { theyAccepted = true } end,   -- the leader accepted (a gone trade is never counted)
    },
})
```

#### Snippet: Give a drop to a role: @priest, @fighter ...

An "assign" rule's "to" may name a role with @ (fighter, priest, scout, mage, a class or a subclass). On a need-or-greed window each box rolls need when it fits the role and passes when it does not.

**Tested:** The templar box needs the priest item and the guardian box passes on it.

```lua

local d = LR.parse({ rules = { { match = "exact", item = "Fixture Censer", act = "assign", to = "@priest" } } })
local item = { { name = "Fixture Censer" } }
local healer = LR.decideWindow(d.rules, d.opts, item, "nbg", { me = "Healfixture", sub = "templar" })
local tank = LR.decideWindow(d.rules, d.opts, item, "nbg", { me = "Tankfixture", sub = "guardian" })
print(("templar: %s, guardian: %s"):format(healer.items[1].verb, tank.items[1].verb))
```

#### Snippet: What this box does with each drop

eco.loot:classify(item) is the simple per-drop rule: a rule for the item's name first (cfg.loot.rules), then the always-take list (cfg.loot.autoTake), then a quota a group member still wants (cfg.loot.quotas, counted against cfg.loot.owned), then the group's loot method. A full loot-rules document (cfg.loot.rulesDoc, see eb.economy.lootrules) replaces this path when it is on.

**Tested:** need for the gem, take for the pouch, to:Tankard for the shard, greed for the rest (need before greed).

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = Fake.drive(W), me = W.me, relay = relay, cfg = { loot = {
    rules = { ["fixture gem"] = "need" },
    autoTake = { "Fixture Coin Pouch" },
    quotas = { ["fixture shard"] = { tankard = 2 } },        -- the tank wants two shards ...
    owned = { Tankard = { ["fixture shard"] = 1 } },         -- ... and holds one
    method = "nbg",
} } })
local loot = eco.loot
print("shard: " .. loot:classify({ name = "Fixture Shard" }))
```

#### Snippet: Give a gear drop to the member who gains the most

The Resolve auction (opt-in: cfg.loot.resolveAuction = true): an equipment drop in a leader's loot window goes to the member who gains the most Resolve over what they wear in that slot. Each member's bid comes from the group's gear exports. auction.bid / auction.winner are the pure rule; eco.auction:award(item, roster) picks the winner from the exports.

**Tested:** The tank gains 40 Resolve, the healer 10: the breastplate goes to the tank. With the auction off, nobody.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script: the pure rule
local A = require("eb.economy.auction")
DOCS.eq((A.bid(drop, exports.Tankard)), 40, "the tank gains 40")
DOCS.eq((A.bid(drop, exports.Healwell)), 10, "the healer gains 10")
DOCS.check(A.qualifies(drop, {}), "equipment with Resolve goes to auction")

-- the live call the leader's loot window makes
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = Fake.drive(W), me = W.me,
    cfg = { loot = { resolveAuction = true, exports = exports } } })
local who = eco.auction:award(drop, { "Tankard", "Healwell" })
print(("%s -> %s (+%d)"):format(drop.name, who, A.bid(drop, exports[who])))
```

#### Snippet: When the tank shouts, the healer reacts

Two boxes, two rules: the tank's cast fires a tag to the group, the healer's own rule turns the tag into a cast intent - one relay message, one reaction.

**Tested:** The tank sends one tag; the healer's box gets exactly one cast intent and the tank's gets none.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script: one coordination engine per box, each with the rules for its own abilities
local Coord = require("eb.coord.rules")
local Link = require("eb.coord.relaylink")
local function box(id, name, role)
    local link = Link.new({ box = id, transport = bus.box(id) })
    local coord = Coord.new({ me = { box = id, name = name, role = role }, link = link, clock = function() return now end })
    link.join()                                   -- nothing is heard before join()
    local intents = {}
    coord:onIntent(function(it) intents[#intents + 1] = it end)   -- in game: hand it to the caster
    return coord, intents
end
local tank, tankIntents = box("is1", "Tankard", "tank")
local healer, healIntents = box("is2", "Mendwell", "healer")

tank:add({ id = "burn-on-shout", trigger = { kind = "cast", who = "tank", ability = "Rallying Shout" },
           action = { kind = "firetag", tag = "Burn" }, scope = "group" })
healer:add({ id = "heal-on-burn", trigger = { kind = "tag", tag = "Burn" },
             action = { kind = "cast", ability = "Fixture Mend", target = "PartyTank" }, scope = "self" })

-- the tank's box sees its own cast (in game EB's combat feeds this)
tank:feed({ kind = "cast", actor = "Tankard", name = "Tankard", role = "tank", ability = "Rallying Shout", isMe = true })
local it = healIntents[1]
print(("healer casts %s on %s (rule %s)"):format(it.ability, it.target, it.rule))
```


#### Snippet: Hold an ability for a while

An embargo rule puts an ability on hold for 20 seconds when a line is said; the cast stack asks holdsCast before casting, and the hold ends on its own.

**Tested:** Fixture Blast is held after the warning line, still held at 19 s, free again at 21 s; a lift ends a hold early.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local Coord = require("eb.coord.rules")
local now = 0
local coord = Coord.new({ me = { box = "is1", name = "Fixturae", role = "mage" }, clock = function() return now end })
coord:add({ id = "no-blast", trigger = { kind = "chat", match = "reflects all spells" },
            action = { kind = "embargo", ability = "Fixture Blast", durationMs = 20000 }, scope = "self" })
coord:add({ id = "blast-again", trigger = { kind = "chat", match = "shield shatters" },
            action = { kind = "liftembargo", ability = "Fixture Blast" }, scope = "self" })

coord:feed({ kind = "chat", text = "The Overseer of Fixtures reflects all spells!" })
local a = coord:holdsCast("Fixture Blast")
now = 19000; coord:tick(); local b = coord:holdsCast("Fixture Blast")
now = 21000; coord:tick(); local c = coord:holdsCast("Fixture Blast")
print(("held: %s at 0 s, %s at 19 s, %s at 21 s"):format(tostring(a), tostring(b), tostring(c)))

-- a second warning, then the lift line ends it early
coord:feed({ kind = "chat", text = "It reflects all spells again" })
local up = #coord:activeEmbargoes()
coord:feed({ kind = "text", text = "Its shield shatters." })
```

```lua
DOCS.eq(coord:holdsCast("Fixture Strike"), false, "other abilities are never held")
```

#### Snippet: A rule that listens to the game

bindEvents feeds a rules engine from eb.events: a tell or an emote line triggers a crew rule, and the intent becomes one eb command line.

**Tested:** The emote line in chat triggers the rule; its crew intent carries "eb all pause".

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local P = require("eb.platform")
local Coord = require("eb.coord.rules")
local coord = Coord.new({ me = { box = "is1", name = "Fixturae", role = "tank" }, clock = P.now })
local lines = {}
coord:onIntent(function(it) if it.kind == "crew" then lines[#lines + 1] = it.line end end)
coord:add({ id = "pause-on-roar", trigger = { kind = "chat", match = "lets out a deafening roar" },
            action = { kind = "crew", line = "eb all pause" }, scope = "self" })
coord:bindEvents(events)
P.pulse().every("coord.tick", 100, function(now) coord:tick(now) end)   -- delays, gates and embargo expiry

-- the game delivers the emote (offline: the fake host fires ISXEQ2's chat event)
w.host:emitChat({ chatType = 15, speaker = "Overseer of Fixtures", speakerIsNPC = true,
                  message = "The Overseer of Fixtures lets out a deafening roar!" })
w.frame(3)
print("crew line: " .. tostring(lines[1]))
```

#### Snippet: Exactly one box cures

Two healers want the same cure: each lays a bid, the claim window closes, the same winner is picked on both boxes, the winner casts and reports it landed.

**Tested:** is1 waits out the claim window; is2 has already heard the better bid and stands down; then is1 gets go.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script: one arbiter per box, on a relay link
local Arb = require("eb.coord.arbiter")
local Link = require("eb.coord.relaylink")
local function box(id, rank)
    local link = Link.new({ box = id, transport = bus.box(id) })
    local arb = Arb.new({ box = id, role = rank, link = link, clock = function() return now end })
    link.join()
    return arb
end
local a, b = box("is1", 10), box("is2", 20)
local cure = { action = "cure", target = "1234", scope = "group" }    -- the member being cured

local first = { a:request(cure), b:request(cure) }       -- both bid; is2 hears is1's better bid at once
now = 200                                                 -- the 150 ms window has passed
local ra, rb = a:request(cure), b:request(cure)
print(("is1 %s, is2 %s"):format(ra, rb))
if ra == "go" then a:acted(cure) end                      -- the winner casts and says so
local whileActing = b:statusOf("cure", "1234")
a:done(cure, true)                                        -- the cure landed: everyone clears it
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua

local bus = require("eb.relay.events").bus()
local now = 0
```

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(first[1], "wait", "is1 waits while the window is open")
DOCS.eq(first[2], "standdown", "is2 already knows a better box wants it")
DOCS.eq(ra, "go", "the lower rank wins")
DOCS.eq(rb, "standdown", "the other box stands down")
DOCS.eq(whileActing, "standdown", "while is1 casts, is2 keeps standing down")
DOCS.eq(a:statusOf("cure", "1234"), "idle", "done cleared the claim")
```

#### Snippet: When the winner never finishes

The box that won a rez casts it but never reports it landed; after the failover time the next box takes the rez, so a member is never left lying.

**Tested:** is1 wins and acts, then goes silent; 2.5 s later the rez is open again, is2 bids anew and, once its bid's short window has passed, its request answers go.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local Arb = require("eb.coord.arbiter")
local Link = require("eb.coord.relaylink")
local function box(id, rank)
    local link = Link.new({ box = id, transport = bus.box(id) })
    local arb = Arb.new({ box = id, role = rank, link = link, clock = function() return now end })
    link.join()
    return arb
end
local a, b = box("is1", 10), box("is2", 20)
local rez = { action = "rez", target = "5678", scope = "group" }

a:request(rez); b:request(rez)
now = 200
local won = a:request(rez)
b:request(rez)
a:acted(rez)                                  -- is1 starts the rez ... and its box dies before it lands
now = 1000; b:poll()
local early = b:request(rez)
now = 3000; b:poll()                          -- past the 2.5 s with no word from is1: the rez is open again
b:request(rez)                                -- is2 bids anew (a new round: its bid has a short window of its own)
now = 3200
local late = b:request(rez)
print("is2 takes over: " .. late)
```

#### Snippet: The coordination messages and the tie-break

A tag and a claim as relay fields and back, the one claim key, and the tie-break every box computes the same way.

**Tested:** Both messages survive the round trip; the lower rank wins, a tie goes to the smaller box id.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local W = require("eb.coord.cowire")
local tag = W.decodeTag(W.encodeTag({ from = "is1", seq = 7, scope = "group", phase = "raise", tag = "Hold Fire",
    data = "20000" }))
local claim = W.decodeClaim(W.encodeClaim({ from = "is2", seq = 3, role = 5, scope = "raid", action = "Cure",
    target = "1234", phase = "bid" }))

local bids = { { from = "is1", role = 10 }, { from = "is2", role = 5 }, { from = "is3", role = 10 } }
local best = W.winner(bids)
local tie = W.winner({ { from = "is3", role = 10 }, { from = "is1", role = 10 } })
local key = W.claimKey("Cure", "1234", "raid")
print(("winner %s (rank %d) | tie goes to %s | key %s"):format(best.from, best.role, tie.from, key))
```

```lua
DOCS.eq(tag.mid, "is1#7", "every message carries <box>#<seq>")
DOCS.eq(claim.role, 5, "the rank comes back as a number")
DOCS.eq(claim.action, "cure", "actions are lower case on the wire")

```

#### Snippet: Keep a set of rules

Add a saved set of rules at once, look one up, switch it off and on, remove it, and list what is left - what a rules window does.

**Tested:** Three rules load; a switched-off rule does not act; the removed one is gone from the list.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local Coord = require("eb.coord.rules")
local coord = Coord.new({ me = { box = "is1", name = "Fixturae", role = "healer" }, clock = function() return 0 end })
local acted = 0
coord:onIntent(function() acted = acted + 1 end)
local ids = coord:addAll({
    { id = "ward-on-flames", trigger = { kind = "chat", match = "flames" },
      action = { kind = "cast", ability = "Fixture Ward" }, scope = "self" },
    { id = "hold-on-root", trigger = { kind = "chat", match = "roots you" },
      action = { kind = "embargo", ability = "Fixture Leap", durationMs = 5000 }, scope = "self" },
    { id = "crew-on-wipe", trigger = { kind = "event", event = "GroupChanged" },
      action = { kind = "crew", line = "eb all pause" }, scope = "self" },
})

coord:enable("ward-on-flames", false)
coord:feed({ kind = "chat", text = "Fixture flames rise" })
local whileOff = acted
coord:enable("ward-on-flames", true)
coord:feed({ kind = "chat", text = "Fixture flames rise" })
local afterOn = acted
local rule = coord:get("ward-on-flames")
coord:remove("ward-on-flames")
local left = {}
for _, r in ipairs(coord:all()) do left[#left + 1] = r.id end
print(("loaded %d, acted while off: %d, after on: %d, left: %s"):format(#ids, whileOff, afterOn, table.concat(left, ", ")))
```

```lua
DOCS.eq(rule.action.kind, "cast", "with its action")

DOCS.eq(coord:get("ward-on-flames"), nil, "the removed rule is gone")
```

#### Snippet: Hand a claim over at once

A box that cannot cast at all calls fail() and the next box takes the cure straight away; a box whose need went away calls release(); claims can also be carried over your own transport with onClaim.

**Tested:** After is1 fails, is2's next request is go; release clears the key; a claim fed by hand makes this box stand down.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local Arb = require("eb.coord.arbiter")
local Link = require("eb.coord.relaylink")
local W = require("eb.coord.cowire")
local function box(id, rank)
    local link = Link.new({ box = id, transport = bus.box(id) })
    local arb = Arb.new({ box = id, role = rank, link = link, clock = function() return now end })
    link.join()
    return arb
end
local a, b = box("is1", 10), box("is2", 20)
local cure = { action = "cure", target = "1234", scope = "group" }
a:request(cure); b:request(cure)
now = 200
a:request(cure)
a:fail(cure)                                    -- out of power: give the claim up now
local next = b:request(cure)
b:release(cure)                                 -- the member was cured by something else
local cleared = b:statusOf("cure", "1234")

-- a third arbiter with no link: carry a claim to it yourself (your own transport decoded it)
local c = Arb.new({ box = "is3", role = 30, clock = function() return now end })
c:onClaim(W.decodeClaim(W.encodeClaim({ from = "is9", seq = 1, role = 1, scope = "group", action = "rez",
    target = "77", phase = "bid" })))
local hand = c:request({ action = "rez", target = "77", scope = "group" })
print(("is1 failed -> is2 %s | released -> %s | hand-fed bid -> %s"):format(next, cleared, hand))
```


```lua
DOCS.eq(cleared, "idle", "release cleared this box's claim")
DOCS.eq(hand, "standdown", "a better bid carried by hand makes this box stand down")
```

#### Snippet: Share a fight with the crew

A box sends the crew one short summary per fight, never its raw lines; the shared service hands every window the same monitor.

**Tested:** The summary line round-trips; the service answers the monitor it was given.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local Feed = require("eb.ui.monitor.parse_feed")
local Parser = require("eb.ui.monitor.parser")
local service = require("eb.ui.monitor.service")
local parser = Parser.new({ me = "Fixturae" })
parser:ingest({ t = 0, kind = "hit", src = "Fixturae", dst = "a fixture brute", amount = 600 })
parser:ingest({ t = 1000, kind = "heal", src = "Fixturae", dst = "Fixturae", amount = 250 })
parser:ingest({ t = 4000, kind = "hit", src = "Fixturae", dst = "a fixture brute", amount = 300 })

local line = Feed.crewLine("is1", parser:export())     -- send this over the crew relay
local back = Feed.parseCrewLine(line)                  -- what the lead reads from it
print(("%s -> %s did %d"):format(line, back.box, back.dmg))

service.setMonitor(parser)                              -- the one monitor every window reads
local shared = service.monitor()
service.publish({ app = { monitor = parser } })
```

#### Snippet: Share gear exports across the crew

Each box's gear feed builds its own export and publishes it on the crew relay; every box takes in its peers' and holds the group table a loot or gear decision reads. Here two feeds are joined by a tiny in-memory transport standing in for EB's relay, and a tick on each shares both exports.

**Tested:** Each box ends up with both exports, a re-tick with nothing changed sends nothing, and the roster lists both.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local a = gearfeed.new({ transport = transport(), box = "is1", me = "Fixturae", now = now,
    gearOpts = { host = host("Fixturae", "guardian") } })
local b = gearfeed.new({ transport = transport(), box = "is2", me = "Tankard", now = now,
    gearOpts = { host = host("Tankard", "berserker") } })
a:tick(); b:tick()
local names = {}
for name in pairs(a:exports()) do names[#names + 1] = name end
table.sort(names)
print("is1 holds: " .. table.concat(names, ", "))
clock = clock + 1000
local again = a:tick()
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
local gearfeed = require("eb.exports.gearfeed")

-- a transport pair standing in for EB's relay (in game pass opts.relay = the crew relay)
local listeners = {}
local function transport()
    return { kind = "test",
        publish = function(cmd, payload)
            for _, fn in ipairs(listeners) do fn(payload) end
            return true
        end,
        subscribe = function(fn) listeners[#listeners + 1] = fn end }
end
local function host(name, sub)
    return { identity = function() return { name = name, class = "warrior", subClass = sub, level = 100 } end,
             worn = function() return { chest = { name = "a fixture breastplate", stats = { stamina = 90 } } } end,
             bags = function() return {} end }
end
local clock = 0
local now = function() return clock end
```

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(#names, 2, "box 1 holds both exports")
DOCS.check(b:exports()["fixturae"] ~= nil, "box 2 holds box 1's, by name in any case")
DOCS.eq(again, "held", "nothing changed: nothing sent")
DOCS.eq(#a:boxes(), 2, "the roster lists both boxes")
DOCS.eq(a:peerCount(), 1, "one peer heard")
DOCS.check(a:decode(a:encode(a:build())) ~= nil, "a payload round-trips")
```

### Crew and group: Scopes: who runs a line

A crew word, or scope, goes right after `eb`. A line carries one crew word at most.

| You type | Who runs it |
| --- | --- |
| `eb pause` | This box only: the line never leaves it. `eb local pause` is the same. |
| `eb all pause` | Every box, this one too. |
| `eb others pause` | Every box but this one. |
| `eb to is2 pause` | The boxes the list names (below). This box too, when the list names it. |

#### What a to list can name

| Entry | Reaches |
| --- | --- |
| `is2` | That box, by its session name. A box on another PC is `<pc>/<box>`; an EB Boxer box is `eb` and a number. |
| a character | The box that plays it, in any case. |
| a class | Every box whose character has that class, for example `warden`. |
| an archetype | `fighter`, `priest`, `mage` or `scout`, with or without `@` in front. |
| `all` | Every box. |
| `marked` | Every box whose character is marked (`eb marked on`). |
| `@me` | The box that sent the line. |
| `@healer` | A role word of your own: the one box or character that `eb alias @healer <who>` names. With no such alias it reaches nobody. |

Separate entries with commas. An entry that matches nothing reaches nobody, and nothing answers.

#### Reach words

| You type | Who runs it |
| --- | --- |
| `eb relay here <command>` | This box, and every box standing in its zone that EB is not paused on. |
| `eb relay awake <command>` | Every box EB is not paused on, this one too when it is not paused. |
| `eb relay stagger <command>` | Every box that is not paused, each in its turn: this one at once, then the others 2 seconds apart. Put a number of seconds first to change the gap, up to 30: `eb relay stagger 5 <command>`. |
| `eb relay mygroup <command>` | This character's group, this box too. With no group, this box only. A member you play by hand is left out. |

Not every command takes a crew word: `eb help <command>` says *for the crew* or *this box only*.

##### Snippet: Address boxes by box, name, class or archetype

A to \<who> list may name a box id, a character, a class or an archetype; wire.shouldHandle decides who acts.

**Tested:** to priest reaches the templar, to @fighter the guardian, to is3 only is3, and others never the sender.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local wire = require("eb.relay.wire")
local boxes = {
    { box = "is1", name = "Tankard", subclass = "guardian" },
    { box = "is2", name = "Mendwell", subclass = "templar" },
    { box = "is3", name = "Sparkwick", subclass = "wizard" },
}
local function who(scope, list, from)
    local out = {}
    for _, me in ipairs(boxes) do
        if wire.shouldHandle({ scope = scope, who = list, from = from or "is1" }, me) then out[#out + 1] = me.box end
    end
    return table.concat(out, ",")
end
print("priest -> " .. who("to", "priest"))
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(who("to", "priest"), "is2", "an archetype")
DOCS.eq(who("to", "@fighter"), "is1", "@archetype")
DOCS.eq(who("to", "templar,is3"), "is2,is3", "a class and a box id together")
DOCS.eq(who("to", "sparkwick"), "is3", "a character name, any case")
DOCS.eq(who("others", ""), "is2,is3", "others never reaches the sender")
DOCS.eq(who("all", ""), "is1,is2,is3", "all reaches everyone")
DOCS.eq(wire.archetype("dirge"), "scout", "the archetype of a class")
```

### Crew and group: Commands

Every command below takes a crew word unless it says otherwise. The [Commands](#commands) page has their arguments.

#### See the crew

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `eb status crew` | This box and every box it hears: id, zone, mode, health, power, and `FIGHTING` while in a fight. This box only. |
| `eb crew status` | One line per box, with the character it plays. This box only. |
| `eb crew` | Opens At a Glance, the crew board. This box only. |
| `eb waiting` | Who the crew is waiting on: what each box is doing, and this box's goal. This box only. |

#### Talk to the crew

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `eb all\|others\|to <who> <command>` | Sends a command to the crew (see [Scopes](#crew-and-group-scopes-who-runs-a-line)). |
| `eb relay <word> <command>` | The spelled-out form, with the crew word after `relay`: `eb relay all pause` is `eb all pause`. It also takes the reach words here, awake, stagger and mygroup. With no crew word, `eb relay pause` runs on this box only. |
| `eb announce <text>` | Every box says `announced:` and the text in its console. It reaches every box on its own. |
| `eb marked on\|off` | Marks this character, so `eb to marked <command>` picks it. The mark is kept and the crew sees it; `status` says which boxes are marked. |
| `eb alias @<role> <who>` | A role word for one box or character, for `eb to @<role>`. This box only. |

#### Move together

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `eb follow me` | Typed on your box, the others follow you, over zone lines too. In a crew line, `me` is the box that sent it. `eb others follow off` ends it. |
| `eb relay here walk x,y,z` | Every box in this zone walks to the spot, each to its own place about 3 m from it. |
| `eb stagger on\|off` | Crew-started walks and follows go one box at a time: the leader first, then the others a second apart. Off by default; each box keeps its own switch. Also `delay <ms>`, `leader <who>` (`auto` is the group's tank) and `reset`. |
| `eb relay mygroup goto <zone>` | Your group travels to that zone, each box its own way. `eb all goto <zone>` sends every box. |
| `eb all spire <place>` | Every box travels by its zone's wizard spire. `eb all druid <place>` takes the druid ring. |
| `eb all hub <instance>` | Every box travels to that instance's hub zone, each its own way. |

#### Group up and fight

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `eb invite` | Typed on the leader: invites every crew character not in its group yet, up to a full group, in the order set in Settings > Group first. A crew line asking for it is refused. `eb invite <name>` invites one character; `eb all invite disband` breaks the group up. |
| `eb go tank` | This character is the tank on every box. `eb go dps` on that box lifts it. |
| `eb assist tank follow` | This box fights what the tank fights and goes with it. `tank` is the group's tank; a name, `me` (in a crew line, the box that sent it) and `off` work too. |
| `eb relay mygroup assist tank follow` | Your group follows the tank and fights what it fights: the *Follow + assist tank* button of the Master Control Panel. |
| `eb engage on\|off` | On by default, per character: a box starts fighting a mob as soon as it is targeted, and in a group it fights what its lead targets. A box you play by hand never starts a fight by itself. Also `status`, `range <metres>` (5 to 50) and `cities on\|off` (off by default). |
| `eb all tgt <id>` | Every box targets that actor. On one box, `eb tgt` also takes a name, `me` or `none`. |
| `eb all mentor <name>` | Every box above that member's level mentors it; `eb all unmentor` stops. Held back until the game's own mentor line is proven live: the answer says so. |

#### Work together

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `eb claim` | Who holds a cure, a rez or a group action, so two boxes never do the same one. `eb claim release` lets this box's claims go. This box only. |
| `eb rules` | Crew rules in plain words: when something happens, do something, for someone. `eb rules builder` opens the Coordination window. This box only. |
| `eb tags` | The cast stack's ability tags, so the boxes time things together: `eb tags set <tag> on\|off` switches every row that carries it. |

#### Pause and stop

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `eb pause` | Holds runs, goals, walks and follows where they are. The fight goes on; `eb set pauseHoldsCasting on` makes a pause hold casting too. |
| `eb resume` | Goes on after a pause or a stop. |
| `eb all stop` | The crew's kill switch: every box ends its runs, walks and goals, and keeps fighting. `eb stopall` (or `eb abort`) is the same for one box. |
| `eb freeze` | Stops at once: the walk, the follow and the run end, the cast that is going is cancelled, and nothing is cast until `eb resume`. `eb relay mygroup freeze` does it for your group. |

#### Instances

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `eb ic run <zone>` | Typed on the tank: it leads and calls in every EB box of its group. `eb ic stop` there ends the others' runs too. |
| `eb iqueue tankdrives on\|off` | On by default: an instance queue started on a box whose character is no fighter goes to the group's fighter, when that fighter's box runs EB. |
| `eb teams list` | Run teams: each box's team and role. `eb teams form <team>` groups a team up. |

### Crew and group: Leads and followers

In an instance run, the box you type the run on is the **lead**, and it plays the tank. It walks the hub route and the instance route alone, zones the group in, pulls, loots and takes the group out.

The lead calls its group in: every EB box whose character is in its group gets the run and becomes a **follower**. A follower:

- follows only a lead whose character is in its own group, and says so when it refuses;
- travels to the hub its own way and holds there until the lead's door takes it in;
- inside, moves only on the lead's camp spots and assists the lead's character in every fight;
- acts on crew orders from that lead only;
- ends its run when the lead's run ends.

Roles, as EB sees a group: a fighter is the tank, a priest the healer, and everyone else a member. An instance queue started on a box whose character is no fighter goes to the group's fighter; `eb iqueue tankdrives off` keeps it with whoever starts it.

### Crew and group: Relay settings

The `relay` block of [boot.json](#settings-bootjson) decides how far a box's crew lines reach. Give every EB for InnerSpace box of the crew the same values.

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `target` | `"all"` | `"all"` reaches every session on the relay. A group name narrows it to the sessions in that relay group. |
| `join` | `false` | `true` joins the relay group named in `target`. With a group, every box must join, or it hears nothing. |
| `filebus` | `"off"` | `"on"` or `"auto"` (the same today) also carries the crew over a shared folder, for a crew that mixes EB Boxer and EB for InnerSpace boxes on one PC. The folder is boot.json's `bus` key, by default the `bus` folder in EB's data folder. |

#### Several PCs in one crew

`eb crew link` joins several PCs into one crew. It is off until you turn it on, and it runs on each box by itself (no crew word):

1. On the PC that keeps the crew hub, type `eb crew link host on`.
2. On every PC, name that PC the same way: `eb crew link hub <address:port>`.
3. On one PC, type `eb crew link key new`. It makes the crew key in a file of that PC's own: copy the file to the same folder on each other PC. The key is never shown.
4. Type `eb crew link on` on each box, and `eb crew link status` to see how it stands.

Another PC's boxes show as `<pc>/<box>`, and `eb to <pc>/<box> pause` reaches one of them. Only crew lines and box states cross PCs, and a box you play by hand still never moves for them.

### Crew and group: What travels between boxes

On EB for InnerSpace the boxes talk over InnerSpace's relay, with event names of EB's own. A script can listen to them; it sends its own lines with `luacall EBISX_cmd`.

| Event | Arguments, in order | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `EBISX_State2` | v, box, name, zone, mode, hp, pw, combat, target, lastAct, tickMs | A box's state, every two seconds. More fields follow these eleven (where it stands, whom it follows, its level and others), 47 in all. An event carries at most 40 arguments, so the 40th to the 47th arrive packed together in argument 40. `mode` is `idle`, `paused`, `ic-lead:<zone>` or `ic-follow:<zone>`. |
| `EBISX_Cmd` | v, mid, from, scope, who, relayed, line | A crew line. `mid` is its message id; `line` is last and keeps its spaces. |
| `EBISX_Inbound` | line | A line handed to EB from outside it. |

EB's coordination adds two more on the same relay. `EBISX_Tag` (v, mid, from, scope, phase, tag, data) carries a fired tag, a hold raised or lifted, or a rule change. `EBISX_Claim` (v, mid, from, role, scope, action, target, phase, seq, ttl) carries a cure or rez claim.

- Each argument travels on its own, so no value needs quoting. One event carries at most 1800 bytes: a longer line is refused, never cut.
- A box acts on each message id once, however often the line arrives.
- EB's own crew orders (a lead's camp spots, its door, its exit and the like) ride the same wire as lines that start with two underscores. They are EB's, not commands to type.
- A script that reads states should use the first 39 arguments and leave argument 40 alone. The crew board decodes them with EB's own `wire.decodeState`.

The [helper guide](#helper-scripts-read-the-crews-state) lists the state's first arguments one by one.

### Crew and group: If something goes wrong

Each box answers in its own console: the box you type on shows only its own answer. `eb status crew` shows what each box is doing now.

| You see | What it means, and what to do |
| --- | --- |
| `listening for the other boxes` | EB has just started and the others have not spoken yet. Ask `eb status crew` again in a few seconds. |
| `0 other boxes heard` | This box hears nobody. Start EB on the other boxes, and check that every box has the same [relay settings](#crew-and-group-relay-settings). |
| `relay off: …` | The relay could not start in this session; the rest of the line says why. |
| `paused (played by hand) - not moved` | Said by a box a crew line tried to move: a crew line never moves a box EB is paused on. Type the line on that box, or `eb resume` there first. |
| `EB is stopped on this box` | That box was halted with `eb stopall`, so a crew line does not move it. `eb resume` there starts it again. |
| `which is not in the crew` | A line came from a box that has not said who it is yet: it just started, or its relay settings differ. Send the line again in a few seconds. |
| `EB is still starting on this box` | That box got the line while EB was starting. Send it again in a second. |
| `runs on this box only (no 'all')` | That command takes no crew word; `eb help` and `eb nav` are two of these. Type it in the session you mean. |
| `one crew word per line` | A reach word was followed by a crew word, as in `eb relay here all pause`. Use one of them. |
| `a crew line does not invite` | `eb invite` with no name went out to the crew. Type it on the leader alone. |
| `not following its run` | That box's character is not in the lead's group. Group up first (`eb invite` on the lead), then start the run again. |
| `a spot in another zone` | That box stands in another zone, where the spot means nothing. `eb relay here walk x,y,z` reaches only the boxes in your zone. |
| `held back until it is proven live` | EB sends the game only what it has proven to work, and nothing was sent. A raid invite or mentoring may answer this today. |
| A box you play by hand moved | InnerSpace's own `relay is2 eb walk x,y,z` runs the line on is2 as if it were typed there, so the crew's rules do not apply: send `eb to is2 walk x,y,z` instead. `eb all resume` also resumes a paused box: type `eb others resume` on that box instead. |
| Nothing happened, and no box answered | A to list that names nobody reaches nobody, quietly. Check the names with `eb crew status`; an `@` word needs its `eb alias` first. |

## Nav and travel

Walk to a spot, follow someone, go back to a saved place, or travel to another zone. Every walk is a route on the zone's mesh.

### Nav and travel: What nav and travel do

EB moves your character one way only: it plans a route on the zone's **mesh**, EB's own map of the ground a character can walk on, and walks it with your movement keys.

That one walker takes you to a spot, follows someone, brings you back to places you saved, and travels to other zones by bells, wizard spires, druid rings, the guild hall and the zones' own pads.

A spot the mesh has no way to is never walked to: EB says why, and your character stays where it is.

### Nav and travel: Quick start

Save a spot, walk off, and let EB bring you back. Type each line in the InnerSpace console of your character's session, where every `eb` command goes ([set EB up first](#quick-start)). Each line answers at once.

1. Stand where you want to come back to, and save the spot:

   ```text
   eb marks set home
   ```

   EB answers `marked 'home' at x,y,z in <zone>`.

2. Walk away. Change zone too, if you like.

3. Go back:

   ```text
   eb marks go home
   ```

   EB answers `issued: goto home` and walks back on the mesh. From another zone it first travels to the mark's zone.

To stop it on the way, type `eb walk stop`.

Rather run a script? The [worked example](#nav-and-travel-worked-example) is a complete one, `eb_patrol.lua`, that walks you between your marks. Its card says where the file goes (InnerSpace's `Scripts` folder) and how to run it (`lua eb_patrol alpha beta laps=2`).

### Nav and travel: Step by step

The everyday jobs, a few console lines each. Every command answers at once, and the walk goes on by itself.

#### Walk to a spot in this zone

1. Type `eb walk` and the spot's three numbers: `eb walk 120,4,-88`. Spaces work too: `eb walk 120 4 -88`. EB answers `issued: walk`.
2. Or name the place instead of numbers: something in sight (`eb walk broker`), a mark, a map point, or a route you recorded.
3. See how it goes with `eb nav`: the waypoint it is on and the metres to go.
4. Stop early with `eb walk stop`. Only the walk ends; the rest of EB carries on.

On the Map window (`eb map`), a right-click on a spot walks there too. The Trip window shows a walk or a trip as it goes, with a Stop button; it pops up by itself while EB's windows are on (on the crew's lead box, or a box on its own).

#### Save places and go back to them

1. Stand on the spot and type `eb marks set camp1`. A mark remembers its zone.
2. List your places with `eb marks`. They are numbered and grouped by category.
3. Go to one by its name or its number: `eb marks go camp1`, or `eb marks go 3`. For a place in another zone, EB travels there first, then walks.
4. Delete one with `eb marks del camp1`.

#### Follow someone

1. Type `eb follow <name>`. A name of several words goes in quotes. EB answers `issued: follow <name>`.
2. EB walks up to them, stops 4 m away, and sets off again whenever they move on. A crew member is followed across zones too.
3. Change the gap a metre at a time with `eb closer` or `eb farther`.
4. Stop following with `eb follow off`.

Anyone outside your crew is followed by name. Out of sight for 15 s, the follow ends and says why.

#### Have the crew follow you

1. On the box you play, type `eb follow me`. EB answers `the others follow me`, and every other box follows you, across zones too.
2. To end it on every other box, type `eb others follow off`.

#### Travel to another zone

1. See the way first: `eb route <zone>`, with the zone's short name or its name. It lists each hop and moves nothing.
2. Go: `eb goto <zone>`. EB answers `issued: travel <zone>`.
3. EB walks to each bell, spire or ring on the mesh, rides it, and plans again from where it lands.
4. Check the hops still ahead with `eb itinerary status`.
5. Hold the trip with `eb travelcancel pause`, go on with `eb travelcancel resume`, or cancel it with `eb travelcancel`.

To ride one way only, add it: `eb goto <zone> spire` (or `bell`, `druid`). To take your group along: `eb relay mygroup goto <zone>`. Every box: `eb all goto <zone>`.

#### Ride this zone's pads

1. List the zone's griffons, sokokars and flight pads: `eb transit`.
2. See how each one opens and where it flies: `eb transit info`.
3. Ride to a station: `eb transit <station>`. EB walks to each pad on the mesh, rides it, and plans again from each landing.

#### Keep walks out of a bad spot

1. Stand in the spot (a hole walks fall into, a corner they wedge in) and type `eb bl`. That puts a 6 m circle there; `eb bl 12` makes it 12 m.
2. From the next walk on, routes go round the circle.
3. Changed your mind? Stand over its middle and type `eb gl`. The greenlight lifts it.
4. List this zone's circles with `eb bl list`. `eb bl clear` removes them all.

#### Record a route and walk it again

1. Stand where the route starts and type `eb record start patrol`.
2. Walk the route by hand. EB keeps a point every few metres, and on sharp turns, climbs and drops.
3. Type `eb record stop`. The route is saved as patrol.
4. Walk it with `eb walk patrol`. `eb walk patrol,3` walks it three times; `eb walk patrol,loop` keeps going until `eb walk stop`.

#### From a Lua script

A helper script sends the same lines through EB's console word, for example `luacall EBISX_cmd walk 120,4,-88` (see [Helper scripts](#helper-scripts)). Lua that runs inside EB walks with [eb.nav](#module-ebnav) itself, on EB's pulse. Tested examples to start from: [walk to a point over the mesh](#snippet-walk-to-a-point-over-the-mesh), [stop a walk cleanly](#snippet-stop-a-walk-cleanly), [follow an actor](#snippet-follow-an-actor) and [plan a trip to another zone](#snippet-plan-a-trip-to-another-zone). The [worked example](#nav-and-travel-worked-example) has the rest.

### Nav and travel: Worked example

Complete scripts come first: save one and run it as its card says. Shorter tested snippets of the same topic follow, a few at a time.

> [!NOTE]
> **Tip:** to have the crew follow you, type `eb follow me` on your own box. Every other box follows you, across zones too.

#### Complete script: Patrol between saved marks

A drop-in script that walks you between marks you saved with eb marks set, for as many laps as you ask: it hands each walk to EB (eb marks go) and watches you arrive before it sends the next.

**Where it goes:** `InnerSpace/Scripts/eb_patrol.lua`

**Get the file:** [examples/script-patrol.lua](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jiimboeq2/EB-Docs/main/examples/script-patrol.lua) (save it as eb_patrol.lua)

**Run it:**

```text
eb marks set alpha
eb marks set beta
lua eb_patrol alpha beta laps=2
endlua eb_patrol
```

**Needs:**

- EB for InnerSpace running in this session (eb status answers)
- each mark saved first with eb marks set \<name>, standing on the spot, in this zone
- a mesh for this zone (EB walks the mesh and nothing else: a mark the mesh has no route to is not walked to)

**Tested:** Walks to each mark in turn for the laps asked, says where it is after each walk, and ends on the last mark.

**Verified:** tested offline: run end to end on EB's offline stand-in for the game; not run in the live game yet, so try it on one box first

```lua
-- eb_patrol.lua - walk between your saved marks. For each mark it sends EB the line "marks go <mark>" through EB's
-- console word (luacall EBISX_cmd: EB answers in the console, a script hears no reply), then watches you: the walk has
-- started once you move, and it is over once you stood still for a second. Then the next mark, lap after lap.
--
--   lua eb_patrol <mark> <mark> [<mark> ...] [laps=<n>]      start it (laps: default 1)
--   endlua eb_patrol                                           stop it (a walk EB has started finishes on its own)

local marks, laps = {}, 1
for _, a in ipairs({ ... }) do
    local n = tostring(a):match("^laps=(%d+)$")
    if n then
        laps = tonumber(n)
    elseif tostring(a):match("^[%w_%-]+$") then
        marks[#marks + 1] = a
    else
        echo("eb_patrol: a mark name is one word: " .. tostring(a))
        return
    end
end
if #marks < 2 then
    echo("usage: lua eb_patrol <mark> <mark> [<mark> ...] [laps=<n>]")
    return
end

local START_WAIT = 4          -- seconds to see the walk start
local WALK_MAX = 180          -- seconds one walk may take
local function moving() return IS.Parse("${Me.IsMoving}") == "TRUE" end

-- one walk: EB walks it; this only watches you start and stop
local function walkTo(mark)
    IS.Execute("luacall EBISX_cmd marks go " .. mark)
    if not waituntil(moving, START_WAIT) then
        echo("eb_patrol: no walk to " .. mark .. " (already there, no such mark in this zone, or the mesh has no way to it - EB says which in its console)")
        return
    end
    local still, spent = 0, 0
    while still < 1 and spent < WALK_MAX do
        wait(0.25)
        spent = spent + 0.25
        if moving() then still = 0 else still = still + 0.25 end
    end
end

echo(("eb_patrol: %d mark(s), %d lap(s) - endlua eb_patrol stops it"):format(#marks, laps))
for lap = 1, laps do
    for _, mark in ipairs(marks) do
        walkTo(mark)
        echo(("eb_patrol: lap %d, at %s"):format(lap, mark))
    end
end
echo("eb_patrol: done")
```

#### Snippet: Turn to face an actor or a point

FaceActor(id) turns you toward an actor; Face(x, z) toward a point on the ground.

**Tested:** Both turns go out as face commands with the actor's and the point's X and Z.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
game.FaceActor(230)                 -- turns toward the lever's own X / Z
game.Face(12.5, 30)                 -- turns toward a spot: x, z (the height does not matter)
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
w.addActor({ id = 230, name = "a fixture lever", type = "NoKill NPC", x = 40, y = 2, z = -15, distance = 6 })
```

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check: the fake world recorded each turn the game was told to make
local faces = {}
for _, a in ipairs(w.world.actions) do if a.kind == "face" then faces[#faces + 1] = a end end
DOCS.eq(#faces, 2, "two turns")
DOCS.eq(faces[1].x, 40, "toward the lever's X")
DOCS.eq(faces[1].z, -15, "...and Z")
```

#### Snippet: A walk the mesh has no route for fails and says why

The same for a zone with no mesh at all - even a six metre step.

**Tested:** A spot 60 m away when the mesh ends 20 m out answers false "no route on the .nav ... the mesh has no way to this spot" and nothing moves; a spot the mesh reaches is walked to; a zone with no mesh answers false "no mesh: ..." even for a 6 m step.

#### Snippet: Where the mesh joins two floors: one jump tap

Some routes cross a gap the mesh itself bridges with a link: a take-off corner, then the landing. The walk goes to the take-off, faces the landing, taps the jump key ONCE and walks on from the landing - the same goPoint, no other mover. A drop needs no key at all. EB never flies: a link is a jump, a climb, a drop or a door, never a flight.

**Tested:** The walk over a jump link arrives; the jump key was pressed exactly once, near the take-off and facing the landing; nav.onLink was told it was a jump.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local nav, move = require("eb.nav"), require("eb.move")
local told, where = {}, nil
nav.onLink = function(kind, landing)                      -- told each time a jump or a climb key goes out
    told[#told + 1] = kind
    local x = move.pos()
    where = { x = x, off = math.abs(move.turnDelta(move.heading(), move.headingTo(landing.x, landing.z))) }
end
local ok, why = w.task(function() return nav.goPoint(40, 0, 0) end)

local taps = 0
for _, line in ipairs(w.host.log.exec) do if line == "press space" then taps = taps + 1 end end
print("jump key taps: " .. taps)
print("nav.onLink told: " .. table.concat(told, ", "))
```

**Offline lines:** the lines that use `w.host`, `w.task` are EB's offline test world, which exists only where the example was tested: in a real script, leave them out or let the game do that part, and start the work a w.task(...) runs as a task of your own, with P.pulse().spawn(...).

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the mesh is real): a mesh whose way east crosses
-- a gap at x 20..22 by a jump link - the take-off at x 19.5, the landing at x 25
local w = DOCS.world({ me = { x = 0, y = 0, z = 0, heading = 90 } })
local mesh = require("nav.lib.navworld").attach(w, { zone = "fixture_hollow" })
mesh.pathChained = function(fx, fy, fz, tx, ty, tz)
    local route
    if fx < 22 then
        route = { { x = 19.5, y = 0, z = 0, offmesh = true },       -- the take-off: a corner navd flags as a link
                  { x = 25, y = 0, z = 0, kind = 2 },               -- the landing; kind 1 drop, 2 jump, 3 door, 4 climb
                  { x = tx, y = ty, z = tz } }
    else
        route = { { x = tx, y = ty, z = tz } }
    end
    route.why, route.partial = "", false
    return route
end
```

```lua
DOCS.near(w.self.x, 40, 2.5, "and ends on the goal")

DOCS.eq(told[1], "jump", "nav.onLink says what kind of link it was")

DOCS.check(where and where.off <= nav.FACE_TOL, "facing the landing")
DOCS.eq(nav.LINK_TAKEOFF, 1.5, "a take-off counts as reached within this many metres across")
DOCS.eq(nav.FLY, nil, "there is no flight mode to switch on: EB never flies")
```

#### Snippet: Ask the mesh service directly

Load a zone's mesh in the background with eb.navd.ready, then ask it for one route, the nearest mesh point, a straight line's clearance and the floor height - each one request.

**Tested:** ready() answers "loading" until the mesh is in, then true; the route reaches the goal; the reports read back.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local navd = require("eb.navd")
local frames = 0
local ok, why = navd.ready("fixture_hollow")             -- the first ask starts the load and answers at once
while not ok and frames < 20 do                            -- in a task you would eb.delay(0) between asks
    w.frame(1); frames = frames + 1
    ok, why = navd.ready("fixture_hollow")
end
print(("mesh ready after %d frames (%s)"):format(frames, tostring(navd.source())))

local route = navd.pathChained(0, 0, 0, 30, 0, 40, 1.0)   -- ONE request for the whole walk
local last = route[#route]
local mx, my, mz, off = navd.nearest(12, 5, 12)           -- snap a point onto the mesh
local clear = navd.clear(0, 0, 0, 10, 0, 0)               -- can the straight line be walked?
local floor = navd.height(3, 2, 3)
print(("route: %d corners to %.0f,%.0f; nearest floor y %.1f; straight line clear: %s"):format(
    #route, last.x, last.z, my, tostring(clear)))
```

```lua
    return true
end }
for _, d in ipairs(doors.forZone("fixture_hollow")) do
    print(("door '%s' at %.0f,%.0f: verb %s (%s)"):format(d.name, d.x, d.z, tostring(d.clickVerb), d.src))
end

local again, why = nav.tryDoor(8, 0, 5, 6, trip)          -- the same door moments later
```

```lua
-- your script
```

```lua
        }
```

#### Snippet: Read a zone's pads and plan a pad trip

EB's pad data per zone: the pads, their networks, what each offers, the nearest one; then the pad graph - the fewest hops from where you stand to a station, the time it takes, and the flights that cross a zone line.

**Tested:** Two griffon hops reach the far tower; one flight crosses into the next zone; the rides add up to 75 s.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local data, graph = require("eb.transit_data"), require("eb.transit_graph")
local pads = data.forZone("fixture_hollow")
local near = data.nearest(data.forNetwork("fixture_hollow", "griffon"), 5, 0, 5)
local offers = data.destinations("fixture_hollow", "griffon")
local g = graph.build()
local plan = graph.planInZone(g, "fixture_hollow", 5, 0, 5, "Fixture Tower")
local crossing = graph.crossZoneEdges(g)
print(("plan: %s -> Fixture Tower (%d hops, %d s)"):format(plan.start.name, #plan.hops, graph.cost(plan.hops)))
require("eb.transit").resetGraph()            -- after new pad data: the next trip builds its graph again
```

#### Snippet: Catch health lost out of combat and back out

Run the walker's hazard watch over your own samples: health falls 15 points in three seconds with no fight on, the watch calls it a hazard, and the way back to the last safe spot is the track walked in reverse.

**Tested:** The losing rule fires; the safe spot is the last dry, unhurt sample at least 6 m back; the way back leads to it.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local hazard = require("eb.nav_hazard")
local mon = hazard.new()
local hp = { 100, 100, 100, 100, 100, 98, 94, 90, 85 }          -- health, one sample every 500 ms while walking east
local hz
for i, h in ipairs(hp) do
    local t = 10000 + i * 500
    hazard.sample(mon, { t = t, x = i * 2, y = 0, z = 0, hp = h, swim = false, combat = false, lava = false })
    hz = hz or hazard.check(mon, t, { lethalZone = false })
end
print("hazard: " .. tostring(hz and hz.what))
local losing, was = hazard.losing(mon.track, 10000 + #hp * 500, hp[#hp])
local safe, k = hazard.safeSpot(mon, hz.x, hz.z, hz.was)
local back = hazard.wayBack(mon, k)
print(("back out to %.0f,%.0f over %d points"):format(safe.x, safe.z, #back))
```


*The checks:*

```lua

DOCS.eq(losing, true, "the losing rule on its own agrees")
DOCS.eq(was, 100, "the most health this stretch held")
DOCS.check(hz.x - safe.x >= hazard.BACK, "the safe spot is at least 6 m back")
DOCS.check(safe.hp >= hz.was - 2, "and you were unhurt there")
DOCS.eq(back[#back].x, safe.x, "the way back ends at the safe spot")
```

#### Snippet: Never swim where the liquid kills

The zones whose liquid kills are a list you can set; swimming in one is a hazard at once, unless the walk says it has to go in (a quest step) with allowLethal.

**Tested:** Swimming in a listed zone is a hazard; the same sample with allowLethal is not; another zone is not.

```lua
-- your script

hazard.setLethalZones("fixture_magma, fixture_cinders")
local function swimSample(ctx)
    local mon = hazard.new()
    hazard.sample(mon, { t = 1000, x = 5, y = -2, z = 5, hp = 100, swim = true, combat = false, lava = false })
    return hazard.check(mon, 1000, ctx)
end
local inLethal = swimSample({ lethalZone = hazard.lethalZone("fixture_magma") })
local allowed = swimSample({ lethalZone = true, allowLethal = true })      -- a quest step that has to go in
local safeZone = swimSample({ lethalZone = hazard.lethalZone("fixture_hollow") })
print("hazard in fixture_magma: " .. tostring(inLethal ~= nil))
```

#### Snippet: Read a zone's mesh corrections

#### Snippet: Remember what a bell's map offers

A bell's travel map may offer less than the network on file, and a city bell offers its reader's own side only. Keep each ring in a bell map memory per side, ask it before ringing, and judge an open map read by read.

**Tested:** For a good character the port's bell offers the steppe and lacks the isle; a character of no known side gets no verdict; the open map is a miss for the isle and offers the steppe.

**The script:**

```lua

local s = bellmaps.new()
bellmaps.recordSide(s, "Fixture Server", "Fixturae", "good", 1000)    -- the side her guild hall globe showed her
bellmaps.record(s, { server = "Fixture Server", zone = "fixture_port", bell = "bell", bind = "side:good",
    labels = { "Fixture Hollow", "Fixture Steppe" }, complete = true, asked = "Fixture Isle", now = 1000 })
local ctx = { server = "Fixture Server", zone = "fixture_port", me = "Fixturae", now = 5000 }
local steppe = bellmaps.verdict(ctx, "Fixture Steppe", s)

    "Fixture Isle", s)
print("isle from the port's bell: " .. isle)

-- an open map, read twice (two reads that agree make a whole map)

bellmaps.mapShown(m, 100)
bellmaps.addRead(m, { "Fixture Hollow", "Fixture Steppe" }, 900)
bellmaps.addRead(m, { "Fixture Hollow", "Fixture Steppe" }, 1700)
```

#### Snippet: Swim corners, the water's surface and no dive in a fight

The swim corner decision is pure: climb toward a higher corner, dive toward a lower one - but never dive while a fight is on. The mesh's liquid surface says whether you are under water. A goal under the surface that the mesh has no route to is NOT swum to: the walk fails, saying the spot is in open water the mesh does not reach.

**Tested:** A corner below is a dive; the same dive in a fight holds; you are under the surface; a goal under the water is said to be in open water the mesh does not reach - and never swum to straight.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local swim, swimout, nav = require("eb.nav_swim"), require("eb.nav_swimout"), require("eb.nav")
local corner = { px = 70, py = -2, pz = 0, wx = 80, wy = -12, wz = 0, surfaceY = 1 }
local calm = swim.want(corner)                                   -- no fight: dive toward the lower corner
corner.inCombat = true
local fight = swim.want(corner)                                  -- a fight on: hold at the surface
print("dive in a fight: " .. tostring(fight.reason))
nav.swimDeps = { surfaceY = function() return 1 end, swimming = true }    -- the reads, swapped for this example
local surface = swim.surfaceY(nav, 70, -2, 0)
local inWater = swim.swimming(nav, 70, -2, 0)
local openWater = swimout.inOpenWater(nav, 70, -2, 0, 78, -6, 4)     -- words only: it moves nothing
nav.swimDeps = nil
```

#### Snippet: Turn a typed word into a zone

```lua
print(zw.explain("fixture", candidates))
```

#### Snippet: Marks and blacklists from the console

eb marks set / list / go / del keep named spots, and eb bl / eb gl blacklist or greenlight the spot you stand on - the same work eb.nav_marks and eb.nav_places do, as console lines a script can send.

**Tested:** The mark is set and listed, eb marks go walks back to it, eb bl puts a circle where you stand, eb gl lifts it.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local okSet, setText = reg:dispatch("eb marks set camp")
print("marks set: " .. tostring(setText))
local _, listText = reg:dispatch("eb marks list")
w.self.x, w.self.z = 30, 30                             -- you walked off (offline: the world moves you)
local okGo, goText = reg:dispatch("eb marks go camp")  -- a walk back, on the pulse
w.runFor(6000)
local backAt = math.sqrt((w.self.x - 4) ^ 2 + (w.self.z - 4) ^ 2)
local okBl = reg:dispatch("eb bl add 5")                -- a 5 m circle where you stand
local circles = #require("eb.nav_places").listBlacklist("fixture_hollow")
local okGl = reg:dispatch("eb gl add")                  -- greenlight the same spot
local inForce = #require("eb.nav_places").avoidCircles("fixture_hollow")
reg:dispatch("eb marks del camp")
```

**Offline lines:** the lines that use `w.runFor`, `w.self` are EB's offline test world, which exists only where the example was tested: in a real script, leave them out or let the game do that part.

```lua
require("eb.nav").stop("the docs example only shows the trip start")
```

#### Snippet: Step out to a safe spot and back

On a cue, walk to the fight's safe spot over the mesh, wait out the mechanic, and walk back to where you fought.

**Tested:** The task leaves its fighting spot, stands at the safe spot during the wait, and is back within 3 m afterwards.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local nav, move = require("eb.nav"), require("eb.move")
local SAFE = { x = -18, y = 0, z = 12 }
local atSafe
local ok = w.task(function()
    local hx, hy, hz = move.pos()                          -- where we fight from
    if not nav.goPoint(SAFE.x, SAFE.y, SAFE.z) then return false end
    atSafe = { move.pos() }
    eb.delay(4000)                                         -- the mechanic's length
    local back = nav.goPoint(hx, hy, hz)
    if back then print("back to fighting") end
    return back
end)
```

**Offline lines:** the lines that use `w.task` are EB's offline test world, which exists only where the example was tested: in a real script, leave them out or let the game do that part, and start the work a w.task(...) runs as a task of your own, with P.pulse().spawn(...).

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

```lua
require("nav.lib.navworld").attach(w, { zone = "fixture_lair" })
```

*The checks:*

```lua
DOCS.check(math.sqrt((atSafe[1] - SAFE.x) ^ 2 + (atSafe[3] - SAFE.z) ^ 2) <= 2.5, "it stood at the safe spot")
DOCS.check(math.sqrt((w.self.x - 4) ^ 2 + (w.self.z - 2) ^ 2) <= 3, "and is back where it fought")
```

#### Snippet: A hub route the tank walks alone

hub.route lists the tank's own steps from the hub to the door: a walk, its own camp spot (who = "me"), a click on a lever. A wait_group step loads but is skipped: the group holds in the hub and the door takes it in.

**Tested:** The tank walks, camps itself, pulls the lever and uses the door; the wait_group step is skipped and said.

**The script:**

```lua
local INSTANCE = {
    schema = "eb.ic/1", zone = "Fixture Hollow", short = "fixture_hollow",
    hub = {
        zone = "fixture_docks", difficulty = "[Heroic I]",
        route = {                                             -- wins over hub.approach when both are given
            { id = "h1", act = "path", spots = { { 5, 0, 5 }, { 12, 0, 18 } } },
            { id = "h2", act = "campspot", name = "dock", spot = { 12, 0, 18 }, who = "me" },
            { id = "h3", act = "interact", actor = "a rusted fixture lever", verb = "pull" },
            { id = "h4", act = "wait_group" },
        },
        entrance = { loc = { 12, 0, 18 }, tolerance = 8 },
        door = { actor = "a fixture rift", verb = "enter" },
    },
    route = { { id = "inside", act = "wait", seconds = 1 } },
}

local env, world = require("instances.lib.icworld").make({ group = { { id = "is2", role = "healer" } } })
env.loadInstance = function() return INSTANCE end
local runner = require("eb.ic").new(env)
local inst = assert(runner:load("fixture_hollow"))
local ctx = runner:newCtx(inst, {})
local ok, why = runner:zoneIn(ctx)
for _, l in ipairs(world.lines) do if l:find("no wait for the group", 1, true) then print(l) end end

DOCS.check(ok, "in: " .. tostring(why))
DOCS.eq(world.did("walk"), 2, "the tank walked the hub route's two waypoints")
local _, camp = world.first("camp")
DOCS.eq(camp[3], "me", "the hub camp spot is the tank's own")
local _, lever = world.first("interact")
```

#### Snippet: Run a power-level route, step by step

A power-level route is a list of STEPS: travel, hunt, actions and instance. Bind the route runner to its adapters, load a route table, and call runner:step(run) once per tick; like the quest runner it answers working, step_done, need_combat, need_loot, need_travel, complete or blocked. Travel and walks are mounted on the mesh, pulls are closest first, and a route never mentors down.

**Tested:** The route travels mounted, hails the camp master, then hunts with closest-first pulls until level 12 and completes.

**The script:**

```lua
local ROUTE = {
    schema = "eb-plroute/1", name = "Fixture warm-up", level_of = "lowest",
    breaks = { hp = 50, power = 30, resume = 90, dead = true },
    steps = {
        { kind = "travel", name = "To the vale", zone = "Fixture Vale" },
        { kind = "actions", name = "Check in", actions = {
            { kind = "go", at = { x = 10, y = 0, z = 12 } },
            { kind = "click", actor = "a fixture camp master", how = "hail" },
            { kind = "wait", secs = 5 } } },
        { kind = "hunt", name = "Hunt to 12", zone = "Fixture Vale", levels = { 10, 20 },
          goal = { kind = "level", value = 12 }, pull = { mode = "single", target_order = "closest" } },
    },
}

local PL = require("loops.lib.plworld")
local deps, world = PL.make({ zone = "Fixture Docks", level = 10 })

local routes = require("eb.plroutes")
local runner = routes.bind(deps)
-- a hand-written route is normalized first: every option gets its default, every step its full shape
local handle = assert(runner:load(require("eb.plroutes.route").normalize(ROUTE)))
local run = runner:start(handle, {})
local status = PL.drive(runner, run, deps, world, 100)       -- the brain's part (need_combat -> the fight, ...)
print(("route %s at level %d"):format(status, world.level))

DOCS.eq(handle.check, "", "the route needs nothing filled in")
DOCS.eq(status, "complete", "the route ran to its end")
DOCS.eq(world.level, 12, "the hunt's goal: level 12")
local travel
for _, c in ipairs(world.calls) do if c[1] == "travel" then travel = c end end
DOCS.eq(travel[3], true, "travel is mounted")
for _, c in ipairs(world.calls) do if c[1] == "engage" then DOCS.eq(c[2], "closest", "pulls are closest first") end end
```

**Offline lines:** the lines that use `DOCS`, `require("loops.lib` are EB's offline test world, which exists only where the example was tested: in a real script, leave them out or let the game do that part.

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
DOCS.eq(world.did("hail"), 1, "the actions step hailed the camp master")
```

#### Snippet: Run a gather route

eco.harvest:runRoute(route) walks to each stop on the mesh, harvests every wanted node in reach, leaves the rest (it never clicks a node it leaves, and remembers it), and moves on. A named route comes from your config (cfg.harvest.routes).

**Tested:** Two stops: the ore and the wood are gathered, the blacklisted weed is never clicked and never looped on, and the route answers done.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script: a saved route by name, polled to the end
local status = CW.poll(function() return eco.harvest:runRoute("fixture loop") end)
local gathered, left = 0, 0
for _, node in ipairs(world.nodes) do
    if world.harvested[node.id] == "gathered" then gathered = gathered + 1 else left = left + 1 end
end
print(("route %s: %d gathered, %d left"):format(status, gathered, left))
```
