#### Snippet: Where to stand, and line of sight

Ask the engine to position behind the mob: every decision then carries where it would stand - EB does not move in a fight for it yet (moves = false, said once in the console). A positional entry waits for its angle when the angle can be read, and the line-of-sight gate holds casts through a wall.

**Tested:** The decision says it would stand "behind" at 3 m and that nothing moves the box (moves = false); an unreadable angle never blocks; with the angle read as "front", a behind-only art waits; with the line blocked and the gate on, nothing is cast.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local Combat = require("eb.combat")
local strike = { name = "Fixture Strike", ability = "Fixture Strike", group = "dps", tags = "CA", priority = 90,
                 gates = {} }
local engine = Combat.new({ shim = game.combatShim(), stacks = { entries = function() return { strike } end } })
engine:setPosition("behind", 3)

local d = engine:step()
print(("position: %s %d m"):format(d.position.mode, d.position.range))
local ctx = engine:snapshot()
ctx.mob = engine:selectTarget(ctx)
local plan = engine:planPosition(ctx)
local angle = engine:relativeAngle(ctx, ctx.mob)                 -- no facing on the mob rows: unknown
local open = engine:positionalFail("behind", ctx.mob)            -- unknown never blocks

local shim = game.combatShim()                                   -- offline: an angle read, to show the gate working
shim.behindTarget = function() return false end
shim.inFrontTarget = function() return true end
local angled = Combat.new({ shim = shim, stacks = { entries = function() return { strike } end } })
local front = angled:relativeAngle(ctx, ctx.mob)
local waits = angled:positionalFail("behind", ctx.mob)

engine:setLoSGate(true)
brute.los = false                                                -- offline: a wall between you and the brute
w.runFor(250)
local blocked = engine:losFail(engine:snapshot().target)
local hold = engine:step()
```

#### Snippet: Aim at a role: Bard, DPS1, Healer1

A cast-stack entry can aim at a role instead of a name; the engine resolves it over the group of the same frame by class order. Preview a buff on the Bard and a heal on DPS1.

**Tested:** The buff aimed at Bard goes to the dirge, the heal aimed at DPS1 to the wizard (sorcerers come first).

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local Combat = require("eb.combat")
local stack = require("eb.caststack.jsonstack").holder({ entries = {
    { name = "Fixture Song", ability = "Fixture Song", group = "buff", target = "Bard", priority = 40, gates = {} },
    { name = "Fixture Mend", ability = "Fixture Mend", group = "heal", target = "DPS1", priority = 50,
      gates = { useBelowTargetHP = 100 } },
} })
local engine = Combat.new({ shim = game.combatShim(), stacks = stack })
engine:loadStack()
local ctx = engine:snapshot()
local buff = engine:selectBuff(ctx)
local heal = engine:selectHeal(ctx)
local names = {}
for _, m in ipairs(game.Group()) do names[m.id] = m.name end
print(("Bard = %s, DPS1 = %s"):format(names[buff.target], names[heal.target]))
```

#### Snippet: The combat commands, and answering one from a script

EB answers the combat commands itself: eb mez off, eb combat off, eb cures off, eb interrupts on, eb embargo tag BURN 15 and eb ho off each change EB's own engine, in the console and for the crew. A script can still take one command over with its own handler (replace = true); a second owner without replace is refused.

**Tested:** Each typed line changes the engine: mez off, casting paused, cures off, interrupt-all on, the BURN tag held for 15 seconds, the heroic part off. After the script takes eb mez over, eb mez off runs the script's handler.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script: take eb mez over (replace = true), counting what it was asked
local asked = 0
local ok = reg:attach("combat.mez", function(args)
    asked = asked + 1
    engine:toggle("mez", args.state ~= "off")
    return true, "mez " .. tostring(args.state) .. " (my script)"
end, { owner = "my-combat-helper", replace = true })
if ok then print("the script answers eb mez") end
local said = a.console("eb mez on")
local again = reg:attach("combat.mez", function() return true end, { owner = "someone-else" })   -- one owner per command
```

**Offline lines:** the lines that use `a.console` are EB's offline test world, which exists only where the example was tested: in a real script, leave them out or let the game do that part.

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
-- offline stand-in: the whole of EB for InnerSpace booted by its real boot (in game you type in the console)

-- EB's own answers: nothing to wire
local reg = eb.app.reg                                    -- the one command registry
local engine = eb.app.combat.engine                       -- EB's own engine: never build a second one
local unwired = reg:unattached({ domain = "combat" })
for _, line in ipairs({ "eb mez off", "eb combat off", "eb cures off", "eb interrupts on", "eb embargo tag BURN 15",
                        "eb ho off" }) do
    a.console(line)
end
local mezByEB = engine:moduleOn("mez")
```

*The checks:*

```lua
DOCS.check(not has(unwired, "combat.mez") and not has(unwired, "combat.embargo"), "EB answers the combat commands itself")
DOCS.eq(mezByEB, false, "eb mez off (EB's own handler)")
DOCS.eq(engine:isPaused(), true, "eb combat off")
DOCS.eq(engine:switchOn("cures"), false, "eb cures off")
DOCS.eq(engine:switchOn("interrupts"), true, "eb interrupts on")
DOCS.eq(engine:tagLive("BURN"), true, "eb embargo tag BURN 15")
```

#### Snippet: Build a cast stack from its rows

eb.caststack.jsonstack turns a cast-stack profile's rows into the entries the combat engine runs: slot order becomes priority, a row's Type becomes its group and tag.

**Tested:** Four rows build four entries in slot order (priority 99, 98, 97, 96); the summary line counts them without naming anything.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script: a profile as the stack's rows (EB reads them from the character's imported profile file)
local JS = require("eb.caststack.jsonstack")
local profile = { castStack = {
    { slot = 1, name = "Fixture Strike", ability = "Fixture Strike", type = "CA",     disabled = false, cond = {} },
    { slot = 2, name = "Fixture Burn",   ability = "Fixture Burn",   type = "CA",     disabled = false, cond = { Tag = "BURN" } },
    { slot = 3, name = "Fixture Hex",    ability = "Fixture Hex",    type = "Debuff", disabled = false, cond = {} },
    { slot = 4, name = "Fixture Flare",  ability = "Fixture Flare",  type = "CA",     disabled = false, cond = { Tag = "BURN" } },
} }
local result = assert(JS.build(profile, { class = "warden" }))
print(JS.summary(result))
for _, e in ipairs(result.entries) do
    print(("  %-22s %-14s %-4s priority %d tags %s"):format(e.name, e.ability, e.group, e.priority, tostring(e.tags)))
end
```

```lua
DOCS.eq(result.entries[4].priority, 96, "slot 4 = priority 96")
DOCS.eq(result.entries[3].tags, "DEBUFF", "a Debuff row is tagged DEBUFF")
DOCS.eq(result.entries[1].group, "dps", "a combat art runs in the dps group")
DOCS.has(JS.summary(result), "4 entries", "the summary counts")
```

#### Snippet: Switch every row with a tag

A row's custom Tag groups rows a fight switches together: setTagEnabled turns every row carrying it off or on in one call.

**Tested:** Both BURN rows go off together and come back together; the untagged row is never touched.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local JS = require("eb.caststack.jsonstack")
local result = JS.build({ castStack = {
    { slot = 1, name = "Fixture Strike", ability = "Fixture Strike", type = "CA", disabled = false, cond = {} },
    { slot = 2, name = "Fixture Burn",   ability = "Fixture Burn",   type = "CA", disabled = false, cond = { Tag = "BURN" } },
    { slot = 3, name = "Fixture Flare",  ability = "Fixture Flare",  type = "CA", disabled = false, cond = { Tag = "BURN" } },
} }, { class = "warden" })
local holder = JS.holder(result)

local ok, said = holder.setTagEnabled("burn", false)    -- case-insensitive; a third argument true matches part of a tag
print(said)
local function state()
    local t = {}
    for _, e in ipairs(holder.entries()) do t[e.ability] = e.disabled and "off" or "on" end
    return t
end
local during = state()
holder.setTagEnabled("BURN", true)
local after = state()
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(ok, true, "rows carry the tag")
DOCS.eq(during["Fixture Burn"], "off", "tagged row 1 off")
DOCS.eq(during["Fixture Flare"], "off", "tagged row 2 off")
DOCS.eq(during["Fixture Strike"], "on", "the untagged row is untouched")
DOCS.eq(after["Fixture Burn"], "on", "back on together")
DOCS.eq((holder.setTagEnabled("NOPE", false)), false, "a tag no row carries is refused")
```

#### Snippet: A reload keeps your switches

rebind swaps a freshly built stack into the same holder and carries every row's on/off state across by name, so a profile reload never undoes what a fight script switched.

**Tested:** The row switched off before the reload is still off after it, and the holder is the same object the engine holds.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local JS = require("eb.caststack.jsonstack")
local function build()                                  -- the profile as read again from its file
    return JS.build({ castStack = {
        { slot = 1, name = "Fixture Strike", ability = "Fixture Strike", type = "CA", disabled = false, cond = {} },
        { slot = 2, name = "Fixture Burn",   ability = "Fixture Burn",   type = "CA", disabled = false, cond = {} },
    } }, { class = "warden" })
end
local holder = JS.holder(build())
holder.setEntryEnabled("Fixture Burn", false)           -- a fight script switched it off
local same = holder.rebind(build())                     -- EB reloads the profile when its file changes
local burn
for _, e in ipairs(holder.entries()) do if e.ability == "Fixture Burn" then burn = e end end
print("after the reload: Fixture Burn " .. (burn.disabled and "off" or "on"))
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(burn.disabled, true, "the switch survived the reload")
DOCS.eq(same, holder, "rebind returns the same holder: never build a new one per tick")
DOCS.eq(#holder.entries(), 2, "the fresh entries are served")
```

#### Snippet: Class facts fill in what a heal row leaves out

A row says when and on whom; it does not say whether a heal is a single or a group spell. With no class facts EB builds the row from its own Target, % and # (a single-target heal at the default weight); with the class's facts the same row builds as the group heal it is.

**Tested:** Without facts the heal row builds from the row alone, as a single-target heal; with the templar's facts it builds as a group heal. Nothing is held either way.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local JS = require("eb.caststack.jsonstack")
local CF = require("eb.caststack.classfacts")
local function profile()
    return { castStack = { { slot = 1, name = "Word of Redemption", ability = "Word of Redemption", type = "Heal",
                             target = "@Group", disabled = false, cond = {} } } }
end
local bare = JS.build(profile(), { class = "templar" })
local facts = assert(CF.forClass("templar"))           -- cached: the same table every call
local full = JS.build(profile(), { class = "templar", facts = facts })
print(("without facts: %s; with facts: %s"):format(bare.entries[1].def.type, full.entries[1].def.type))
print("with facts: held " .. #full.held .. ", type " .. tostring(full.entries[1].def.type))
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(#bare.held, 0, "no facts: the row is built from its own words, not held")
DOCS.eq(bare.entries[1].def.type, "SINGLE_BASIC", "as a single-target heal: the row alone cannot say it is a group spell")
DOCS.eq(#full.held, 0, "with facts it builds")
DOCS.eq(full.entries[1].def.type, "GROUP_HEAL", "as a group heal")
DOCS.check(#CF.classes() > 20, "EB ships facts for every class")
DOCS.eq(CF.forClass("no such class"), nil, "an unknown class has none")
```

#### Snippet: Switch a tag from the engine

```lua
engine:toggle("burn", false)
local d = engine:step()

engine:toggle("burn", true)
```

#### Snippet: Write cast-stack rows by hand

Build a stack from hand-written rows of several Types and conditions, and read what came of each row: its kind, tags and priority, the rows held with a reason, an unknown Type, an empty row skipped.

**Tested:** Damage, buff, upkeep, heal, cure and rez rows build and run (a heal or cure with no class facts is built from its own Target, % and #); a buff with a health gate carries that gate; the allow-tag row is built off; a row aimed at an alias the profile never defined is held with that reason; the unknown Type and the empty row are reported.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script (pure Lua: no game needed)
local JS = require("eb.caststack.jsonstack")
local rows = {                                                    -- priority order: slot 1 first
    { slot = 1, name = "Fixture Strike", ability = "Fixture Strike", type = "CA", cond = { Tag = "BURN" } },
    { slot = 2, name = "Fixture Blast", ability = "Fixture Blast", type = "NamedCA", cond = { ["#"] = 2 } },
    { slot = 3, name = "Fixture Mend", ability = "Fixture Mend", type = "Heal", target = "@Group", cond = { ["%"] = 70 } },
    { slot = 4, name = "Fixture Cleanse", ability = "Fixture Cleanse", type = "Cure", target = "@Group", cond = {} },
    { slot = 5, name = "Fixture Revive", ability = "Fixture Revive", type = "Res", target = "@Group", cond = {} },
    { slot = 6, name = "Fixture Ward", ability = "Fixture Ward", type = "Buff", target = "@Me", cond = {} },
    { slot = 7, name = "Fixture Quick", ability = "Fixture Quick", type = "CA", cond = { ["Aggro>"] = 80, ATag = "OPEN" } },
    { slot = 8, name = "Fixture Odd", ability = "Fixture Odd", type = "Buff", cond = { ["HP<"] = 50 } },
    { slot = 9, name = "", type = "CA", cond = {} },
    { slot = 10, name = "Fixture Mystery", ability = "Fixture Mystery", type = "Wobble", cond = {} },
    { slot = 11, name = "Fixture Regrowth", ability = "Fixture Regrowth", type = "Combat", target = "@Tank", cond = { ["RW<"] = 5 } },
    { slot = 12, name = "Fixture Shield", ability = "Fixture Shield", type = "Buff", target = "*offtank", cond = {} },
}
local result = JS.build({ castStack = rows }, { class = "warden" })
print(JS.summary(result))
local byAbility = {}
for _, e in ipairs(result.entries) do byAbility[e.ability] = e end
local heldWhy = {}
for _, h in ipairs(result.held) do heldWhy[h.name] = h.why end
```

```lua
DOCS.eq(byAbility["Fixture Strike"].priority, 99, "slot 1 = priority 99")
DOCS.eq(byAbility["Fixture Blast"].tags, "NAMED_CA", "a NamedCA row is tagged NAMED_CA")
DOCS.eq(byAbility["Fixture Ward"].group, "buff", "a Buff row")
DOCS.eq(byAbility["Fixture Regrowth"].target, "PartyTank", "@Tank becomes PartyTank")

DOCS.eq(byAbility["Fixture Mend"].target, "AllParty", "aimed at the group")
DOCS.eq(byAbility["Fixture Cleanse"].tags, "CURE", "so does a cure row")
DOCS.eq(byAbility["Fixture Revive"].tags, "REZ", "and a Res row, tagged REZ")
DOCS.eq(byAbility["Fixture Odd"].def.useBelowMyHP, 50, "a buff's HP< is a gate on my own health")
```

#### Snippet: A class module of your own

Record a small class module - a heal template, a heal, a cure with its types, a rez, a stealth opener - into class facts, then build heal and cure rows that would otherwise be held.

**Tested:** The facts hold the template, the entries and the stealth openers; with them the heal, cure and rez rows build and run, and the class's own prefix names every entry.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script (pure Lua: no game needed)
local F = require("eb.caststack.jsonstack_facts")
local JS = require("eb.caststack.jsonstack")
local H = { New = function(Mx, prefix, o) return Mx end }          -- a class helper of your own: its New names the prefix
local unknown
local facts = F.record(function(M)                                  -- the class module: entries on four managers
    H.New(M, "FIXTURE", { forceNamedCA = false })
    M.Heals.DefineAbility({ name = "T_FixtureSingle", type = "SINGLE_BASIC", healWeight = 30 })   -- a heal template
    M.Heals.DefineAbility({ name = "FIXTURE_Mend", ability = "Fixture Mend", baseAbility = "T_FixtureSingle",
                            targets = "AllParty" })
    M.Heals.Enable("FIXTURE_Mend", { priority = 10 })
    M.Cures.DefineAbility({ name = "FIXTURE_Cleanse", ability = "Fixture Cleanse", type = "GROUP", tags = "CURE",
                            cureTypes = "noxious;arcane", targets = "AllParty" })
    M.Cures.Enable("FIXTURE_Cleanse")
    M.Cures.DefineAbility({ name = "FIXTURE_Revive", ability = "Fixture Revive", type = "GROUP_REZ", tags = "REZ",
                            targets = "AllParty" })
    M.Cures.Enable("FIXTURE_Revive")
    M.Dps.DefineAbility({ name = "FIXTURE_Strike", ability = "Fixture Strike", tags = "CA" })
    M.Dps.Disable("FIXTURE_Strike")
    M.Dps.SetStealthOpeners({ "Fixture Ambush" }, { "Fixture Sneak" })
    unknown = M.Dps.Enable("FIXTURE_Nothing")                       -- no such entry: false
end, { H = H })
print(("facts: prefix %s, %d entries, %d template"):format(facts.prefix, #facts.list, (function()
    local n = 0; for _ in pairs(facts.templates) do n = n + 1 end; return n end)()))

local mend = facts.byName.FIXTURE_Mend
local merged = F.effective(facts, mend)                             -- the fact with its template under it
local result = JS.build({ castStack = {
    { slot = 1, name = "Fixture Mend", ability = "Fixture Mend", type = "Heal", target = "@Group", cond = { ["%"] = 70 } },
    { slot = 2, name = "Fixture Cleanse", ability = "Fixture Cleanse", type = "Cure", target = "@Group", cond = {} },
    { slot = 3, name = "Fixture Revive", ability = "Fixture Revive", type = "Res", target = "@Group", cond = {} },
} }, { facts = facts })
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(facts.prefix, "FIXTURE", "the prefix the class helper's New was given")
DOCS.eq(facts.classOpts.forceNamedCA, false, "and its options")
DOCS.check(facts.templates.T_FixtureSingle ~= nil, "a T_ name with no ability is a template")
DOCS.eq(merged.healWeight, 30, "the heal inherits its template's weight")
DOCS.eq(F.group(facts, mend), "heal", "a Heals entry that is not kept up is a heal")
DOCS.eq(F.lineKey("Fixture Mend II"), "fixture mend", "facts and rows meet on the ability line")
DOCS.eq(facts.index.heal["fixture mend"][1], mend, "indexed by kind and line")
DOCS.eq(F.index(facts), facts, "index can be rebuilt after a change by hand")
DOCS.eq(facts.byName.FIXTURE_Strike.enabled, false, "Disable leaves an entry off")
DOCS.eq(facts.stealth.openers[1], "Fixture Ambush", "the stealth openers")
DOCS.eq(unknown, false, "Enable of a name never defined answers false")
DOCS.eq(#result.held, 0, "with the facts no row is held")
DOCS.eq(result.entries[1].group, "heal", "the heal row runs")
DOCS.eq(result.entries[2].gates.cureTypes, "noxious;arcane", "the cure took its types from the class")
DOCS.eq(result.entries[3].tags, "REZ", "the rez row runs")
```

#### Snippet: Hand a built stack to category managers

jsonstack.apply defines every built entry on a set of category managers - damage, heals, cures, buffs - and item rows on an item manager, enabling all but the ones switched off.

**Tested:** Four entries are defined: the art and the buff enabled with their priorities, the row that is off in the profile defined but not enabled, and the item kept up on you.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script (pure Lua: no game needed)
local JS = require("eb.caststack.jsonstack")
local result = JS.build({ castStack = {
    { slot = 1, name = "Fixture Strike", ability = "Fixture Strike", type = "CA", cond = {} },
    { slot = 2, name = "Fixture Ward", ability = "Fixture Ward", type = "Buff", target = "@Me", cond = {} },
    { slot = 3, name = "Fixture Slow", ability = "Fixture Slow", type = "CA", disabled = true, cond = {} },
    { slot = 4, name = "Fixture Charm", ability = "Fixture Charm", type = "Buff", isItem = true, target = "@Me", cond = {} },
} }, { class = "warden" })

local log = { Dps = {}, Buffs = {}, Heals = {}, Cures = {}, items = {}, enabled = {} }
local function manager(kind)                                     -- a category manager: define, then enable
    return { DefineAbility = function(def, disabled) log[kind][#log[kind] + 1] = def.name end,
             Enable = function(name, o) log.enabled[name] = o.priority end }
end
local managers = { Dps = manager("Dps"), Heals = manager("Heals"), Cures = manager("Cures"), Buffs = manager("Buffs") }
local itemclick = { ClearDefined = function() end, Define = function(item) log.items[#log.items + 1] = item end }
local n = JS.apply(result, managers, itemclick)
print(("defined %d: Dps %d, Buffs %d, items %d"):format(n, #log.Dps, #log.Buffs, #log.items))
```

#### Snippet: Reload a cast stack when its file changes

Join a loader to the combat plane, pin the server for a name, and let a changed profile file reload the stack - through refresh (a stamp check) or the plane's own reload - with the loader telling you each time.

**Tested:** The pinned server picks the profile; the plane casts from the loader's stack; after the file changes, refresh reloads it (two rows now) and the change callback hears it; an unchanged stamp does nothing.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local loader = require("eb.caststack.loader")
local store = { ["caststack.server.fixturae"] = "Fixture Server" }       -- this name has profiles on two servers
local settings = { get = function(key) return store[key] end }
local pinned = loader.pinnedServer(settings, "Fixturae")

local plane = require("eb.app.combat").new({ game = w.game })           -- in game: eb.app.combat
local ld = loader.new({ files = files, getenv = where, settings = settings, stat = function() return stamp end,
                        me = function() return "Fixturae", "warden" end })
loader.attach(ld, plane)                                                 -- the plane now casts from the loader
local heard, joined = 0, ld.onChange
ld.onChange = function(l) heard = heard + 1; joined(l) end
ld.load()
local first = #plane.holder.entries()

disk["stacks/Main/Fixture Server_Fixturae.json"] = profile({ "Fixture Strike", "Fixture Burn" })   -- the file changed
stamp = 2
local ok = ld.refresh()
local unchanged, why = ld.refresh()                                      -- the stamp did not move again
local again = plane.reload()                                             -- the plane's reload goes through the loader
print(plane.describe())
local stat = loader.lfsStat()                                            -- nil here; a stamp reader inside ISXLUA
```

**Offline lines:** the lines that use `w.game` are EB's offline test world, which exists only where the example was tested: in a real script, leave them out or let the game do that part.

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
-- offline stand-in: the profiles folder, in a files host of your own (in game: EB's files service and your profiles)
local w = DOCS.world()
local function profile(names)
    local rows = {}
    for _, n in ipairs(names) do rows[#rows + 1] = ('{"Type": "CA", "name": "%s"}'):format(n) end
    return '{"_v": 1, "default": "Main", "profiles": {"Main": {"sections": {"CastStack": [' .. table.concat(rows, ", ") .. ']}}}}'
end
local disk = { ["stacks/Main/Fixture Server_Fixturae.json"] = profile({ "Fixture Strike" }),
               ["stacks/Main/Second Server_Fixturae.json"] = profile({ "Fixture Other" }) }
local files = {
    read = function(path) return disk[(path:gsub("[\\/]", "/"))] end,
    list = function(dir, glob)
        local pat, out = "^" .. glob:gsub("[%.%-]", "%%%0"):gsub("%*", ".*") .. "$", {}
        for path in pairs(disk) do
            local d, name = path:match("^(.*)/([^/]+)$")
            if d == dir:gsub("[\\/]", "/") and name:match(pat) then out[#out + 1] = name end
        end
        table.sort(out)
        return out
    end,
}
local where = function() return "stacks" end
local stamp = 1
```

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(pinned, "Fixture Server", "the server pinned for this name")
DOCS.eq(first, 1, "the pinned server's profile was loaded")
DOCS.eq(ok, true, "a changed stamp reloads")
DOCS.eq(#plane.holder.entries(), 2, "the plane casts from the new rows")
DOCS.eq(unchanged, false, "an unchanged stamp does nothing")
DOCS.eq(why, "unchanged", "and says so")
DOCS.eq(again, true, "the plane's reload works through the loader")
DOCS.check(heard >= 3, "the change callback heard every load and reload")
DOCS.has(plane.describe(), "2 entries", "the plane's status line follows the loader")
DOCS.eq(stat, nil, "no file-time reader in a plain Lua")
```

#### Snippet: Recipe: script a named fight

A complete named-fight script: the boss's emote sends you to a safe spot and back, half health switches the burn rows on, a detriment on a member is cured on cue, and the boss's big cast is interrupted on cue.

**Tested:** The emote moves you out of the fire and back home with the burn held meanwhile; phase 2 turns the burn on; Member1's detriment is cured; Ashen Wail is stunned; the script ends when the boss dies.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script: the fight ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
local P = require("eb.platform")
local game, pulse = P.game(), P.pulse()
local events, nav = require("eb.events"), require("eb.nav")
local combat = eb.app.combat                                   -- EB's own combat plane: never build a second engine

local FIGHT = { boss = "the Ashen Overseer", emote = "draws in the flames", stopCast = "Ashen Wail", stun = "Fixture Stun",
                cure = "Fixture Cure", home = { x = 0, y = 0, z = 0 }, safe = { x = -20, y = 0, z = 0 }, log = {} }
combat.holder.setTagEnabled("BURN", false)                     -- phase 1: hold the burn

local cues = {}                                                -- handlers only record; the fight task acts
events.on("IncomingText", function(ev)
    if ev.text:find(FIGHT.emote, 1, true) then cues[#cues + 1] = "flames" end
end)

pulse.spawn("fight: " .. FIGHT.boss, function()
    local phase = 1
    while true do
        local b = game.Target()
        if not b or b.isDead or (b.healthPct or 0) <= 0 then break end
        if phase == 1 and b.healthPct <= 50 then               -- phase 2 at half health: burn on
            phase = 2
            combat.holder.setTagEnabled("BURN", true)
            FIGHT.log[#FIGHT.log + 1] = "phase 2"
        end
        if cues[1] == "flames" then                            -- the emote: out of the fire, then back in
            table.remove(cues, 1)
            combat.holder.setTagEnabled("BURN", false)
            local s, h = FIGHT.safe, FIGHT.home
            if nav.goPoint(s.x, s.y, s.z) then
                eb.delay(3000)
                if nav.goPoint(h.x, h.y, h.z) then FIGHT.log[#FIGHT.log + 1] = "out and back" end
            end
            if phase == 2 then combat.holder.setTagEnabled("BURN", true) end
        end
        if game.TargetCasting() == FIGHT.stopCast and game.AbilityReady(FIGHT.stun) then   -- the big cast: stop it
            game.Cast(FIGHT.stun)
            FIGHT.log[#FIGHT.log + 1] = "stunned " .. FIGHT.stopCast
        end
        for _, m in ipairs(game.Group()) do                    -- the cure on cue: a noxious detriment on anyone
            if (m.noxious or 0) > 0 and game.AbilityReady(FIGHT.cure) then
                game.Cast(FIGHT.cure, { name = m.name })
                FIGHT.log[#FIGHT.log + 1] = "cured " .. m.name
            end
        end
        eb.delay(250)
    end
    FIGHT.over = true
end)

-- offline: the fight plays out ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
local function casted(name) for _, c in ipairs(w.world.casts) do if c.ability == name then return true end end end
local function burnOn()
    for _, e in ipairs(combat.holder.entries()) do if e.ability == "Fixture Burn" then return not e.disabled end end
end
local burnAway, onFrame = nil, w.world.onFrame
w.world.onFrame = function(h) onFrame(h); if w.self.x <= -18 then burnAway = burnOn() end end   -- watch the safe spot
w.runFor(500)
w.host:emitText("The Ashen Overseer draws in the flames!", 0)
w.runUntil(function() return FIGHT.log[1] == "out and back" end, 30000)
boss.healthPct = 45
w.runUntil(function() return FIGHT.log[2] == "phase 2" end, 3000)
member.afflict.noxious = 1
w.runUntil(function() return casted(FIGHT.cure) end, 3000)
member.afflict.noxious = 0
boss.castId, boss.castName = 77, FIGHT.stopCast
w.runUntil(function() return casted(FIGHT.stun) end, 3000)
boss.castId = 0
boss.healthPct, boss.isDead = 0, true
w.runUntil(function() return FIGHT.over end, 3000)
print("fight over: " .. table.concat(FIGHT.log, " | "))
```

#### Snippet: Shape combat for one encounter

Name the encounter you are in, register an override that applies only to it - no AE near the boss, its big cast on the interrupt list - and clear it when the fight is over so the next pull is back to normal.

**Tested:** During the encounter the AE is held (disableAE switches the AE tag off) and the boss's Ashen Wail is interrupted; after the encounter is cleared the AE casts again.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local stack = require("eb.caststack.jsonstack").holder({ entries = {
    { name = "Fixture Cleave", ability = "Fixture Cleave", group = "dps", tags = "AE", priority = 99, gates = {} },
    { name = "Fixture Strike", ability = "Fixture Strike", group = "dps", tags = "CA", priority = 90, gates = {} },
    { name = "Fixture Stun", ability = "Fixture Stun", group = "dps", tags = "STUN", priority = 10, gates = {} },
} })
local engine = require("eb.combat").new({ shim = game.combatShim(), stacks = stack })   -- in game: eb.app.combat.engine

engine:setEncounter("the Ashen Overseer")                   -- where you are and what you fight
engine:addOverride({ name = "overseer", priority = 10, match = { encounter = "the Ashen Overseer" },
                     directives = { disableAE = true, interruptList = { "Ashen Wail" } } })
local d1 = engine:step()
local why = engine:passesGate(stack.get("Fixture Cleave"), engine:snapshot(), engine:snapshot().target)
boss.castId, boss.castName = 88, "Ashen Wail"               -- offline: the boss starts its big cast
w.runFor(500)                                               -- a quick art goes out at most every half second
local d2 = engine:step()
boss.castId = 0

engine:setEncounter(nil)                                    -- the fight is over: back to normal
engine:removeOverride("overseer")
w.runFor(500)
local d3 = engine:step()
print(("encounter: %s, then %s"):format(d2.reason, d3.ability == "Fixture Cleave" and "the AE again" or "?"))
```

#### Snippet: When does a combat wait end?

The instance runner's combat wait decides with a small pure rule: a fight on the group or a straggler nobody fights HOLDS the wait; a clear, or a combat flag with nothing behind it for 5 seconds, lets it go. A lone in-combat flag never holds a run forever.

**Tested:** The four cases decide fight, straggler, clear and stuck; only the first two hold the wait.

**The script:**

```lua
local HOLD = require("eb.ic.ic_hold").HOLD

-- decide(inCombat, anyHated, nearby NPCs, ms the bare flag has held)
local fight = HOLD.decide(true, true, {}, 0)
local straggler = HOLD.decide(true, false, { { id = 41, name = "a hollow skitter", dist = 12, combatMode = true } }, 0)
local clear = HOLD.decide(false, false, {}, 0)
local stuck = HOLD.decide(true, false, {}, 6000)
local early = HOLD.decide(true, false, {}, 2000)          -- not 5 s yet: a pull may still be landing

print(("in combat, nobody hated, nothing near, 6 s -> %s"):format(stuck.hold))
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
DOCS.eq(fight.hold, "fight", "someone in the group is hated")
DOCS.eq(straggler.hold, "straggler", "an NPC in combat mode nobody fights")
DOCS.eq(straggler.straggler.name, "a hollow skitter", "the straggler handed to the combat engine")
DOCS.eq(clear.hold, "clear", "out of combat")
DOCS.eq(stuck.hold, "stuck", "a bare combat flag for 5 s or more")
DOCS.eq(early.hold, "fight", "under 5 s it still counts as a fight")
DOCS.check(HOLD.holds(fight.hold) and HOLD.holds(straggler.hold), "fight and straggler hold the wait")
DOCS.check(not HOLD.holds(clear.hold) and not HOLD.holds(stuck.hold), "clear and stuck let it go")
```

#### Snippet: The pull and break rules behind a route

eb.plroutes.plan holds a route's decisions as pure functions: resolveCap turns "aggro by group" into a mob count, packDecide says whether a pack pull keeps walking or turns to fight, needBreak says when to rest or wait for a member, and goalMet says when a step is done.

**Tested:** A 3-box group caps a pack at 3, the pack turns at the cap, a member under 50% health calls a rest, and a level goal is met at its value.

```lua
local Plan = require("eb.plroutes.plan")

local cap = Plan.resolveCap("group", 1, 3)                              -- aggro_by group, 1 per member, 3 members
local keepWalking = Plan.packDecide(1, cap, 2, 25, false, false)        -- 1 mob on us, under the cap
local turn = Plan.packDecide(3, cap, 2, 25, false, false)               -- at the cap

local breaks = { hp = 50, power = 30, resume = 90, dead = true, range = 60, zone = true }
local members = { { name = "me", hp = 100, power = 100, dead = false, in_zone = true, dist = 0 },
                  { name = "Member1", hp = 40, power = 90, dead = false, in_zone = true, dist = 10 } }
local brk = Plan.needBreak(breaks, members, false)
print(brk.text)

local stepGoal = require("eb.plroutes.route").normalize({ steps = { { kind = "hunt", zone = "Fixture Vale",
    goal = { kind = "level", value = 30 } } } }).steps[1]

DOCS.eq(cap, 3, "one mob per group member")
DOCS.check(keepWalking ~= turn, "under the cap the pull goes on; at the cap it turns")
DOCS.eq(brk.kind, "rest", "a member under 50% health: rest")
DOCS.check(Plan.goalMet(stepGoal, { group_level = 30, my_level = 30, minutes = 0, kills = 0, runs = 0, aa = -1 }),
    "a level goal is met at its value")
DOCS.check(not Plan.goalMet(stepGoal, { group_level = 29, my_level = 29, minutes = 0, kills = 0, runs = 0, aa = -1 }),
    "and not before")
```

#### Snippet: Claim before a group cure

needsClaim says which combat casts need a claim; attach wraps an engine's cast so a group cure is claimed first and stands down when another box has it.

**Tested:** A group cure needs the "groupcure" claim, a damage art none; the wrapped cast waits, then casts once it wins.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local gate = require("eb.coord.combat_gate")
local Arb = require("eb.coord.arbiter")
local now = 0
local arb = Arb.new({ box = "is1", role = 10, clock = function() return now end })   -- no link: a solo box

local cureAll = { kind = "cure", target = "group", entry = { target = "AllParty", gates = { type = "GROUP" } } }   -- a group cure says so
local nuke = { kind = "dps", target = 200, entry = { target = "Target" } }
local key = gate.needsClaim(cureAll)
local none = gate.needsClaim(nuke)

-- an engine of your own with a cast(dec) method: attach claims before every cast that needs it
local engine = { sent = 0 }
function engine:cast(dec) self.sent = self.sent + 1; return true end
local detach = gate.attach(engine, arb, { now = function() return now end })
local first = engine:cast(cureAll)                         -- the claim window is still open
now = 200
local second = engine:cast(cureAll)                        -- this box won: the cast goes out
detach()
print(("%s|%s|%s: %s, then %s"):format(key.action, key.target, key.scope, first and "go" or "wait",
    second and "go" or "wait"))
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(none, nil, "a damage art needs no claim")
DOCS.eq(first, false, "the first cast waited for the claim window")
DOCS.eq(second, true, "the second cast went out")
DOCS.eq(engine.sent, 1, "the engine's own cast ran exactly once")
DOCS.eq(cureAll.sendWhy, "wait for the arbitration (collecting bids)", "the decision says why it held")
```

#### Snippet: Read a cast stack's tags as rules

An imported cast stack's ability tag and embargo tag become plain rules; imported into an engine, the tag fires and the hold works.

**Tested:** Two rows with tags give three rules; casting the trigger ability fires the tag, which casts the listener; the embargo trigger holds the bound ability.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local Import = require("eb.coord.tagimport")
local Coord = require("eb.coord.rules")
local rows = {
    { name = "Fixture Shout", ATag = "Burn", AType = "Trigger Only" },
    { name = "Fixture Strike", ATag = "Burn", AType = "Listen Only", Target = "@Group" },
    { name = "Fixture Blast", ETag = "Calm", EType = "Listen Only" },
    { name = "Fixture Jab" },                                              -- no tags: not coordination
}
local res = Import.importRows(rows)
local names = {}
for _, r in ipairs(res.rules) do names[#names + 1] = r.name end
print(("%d rules: %s"):format(#res.rules, table.concat(names, " | ")))

local now = 0
local coord = Coord.new({ me = { box = "is1", name = "Fixturae", role = "" }, clock = function() return now end })
local cast = {}
coord:onIntent(function(it) cast[#cast + 1] = it.ability end)
Import.importInto(coord, rows)
coord:feed({ kind = "cast", actor = "Fixturae", name = "Fixturae", ability = "Fixture Shout", isMe = true })
coord:add({ id = "calm-on", trigger = { kind = "chat", match = "calms" }, action = { kind = "embargo", tag = "Calm" } })
coord:feed({ kind = "chat", text = "The room calms" })
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(#res.rules, 3, "three rules from the tagged rows")
DOCS.eq(res.count.atag, 2, "two rows carried an ability tag")
DOCS.eq(cast[1], "Fixture Strike", "the tag made the listener cast")
DOCS.eq(coord:holdsCast("Fixture Blast"), true, "the embargo holds the bound ability")
```

#### Snippet: Read combat lines into records

combatlog.parse turns one line of combat text into a record - a hit, a damage-over-time tick, a heal, a ward, a miss, a death - with YOU resolved to your own name; anything else is nil.

**Tested:** Each combat line gives its kind, who, whom and how much; a chat line gives nil.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local log = require("eb.ui.monitor.combatlog")
local me = "Fixturae"
local lines = {
    "YOUR Fixture Flare hits a fixture brute for 1,200 points of heat damage.",
    "A fixture brute suffers 300 points of poison damage from Fixturae's Fixture Venom.",
    "Mendwell's Fixture Mend heals Tankard for 800 hit points (150).",
    "Mendwell wards YOU against 500 points of damage.",
    "A fixture brute tries to hit YOU, but YOU parry!",
    "You have slain a fixture brute!",
    "Tankard says, 'Pull the next one.'",
}
local recs, show = {}, {}
for i, line in ipairs(lines) do
    local r = log.parse(line, { me = me, t = i * 1000 })
    recs[i] = r
    if r then
        if r.kind == "hit" then show[#show + 1] = ("hit %d %s"):format(r.amount, r.dtype)
        elseif r.kind == "heal" then show[#show + 1] = ("heal %d (+%d over)"):format(r.amount, r.over)
        elseif r.kind == "ward" then show[#show + 1] = ("ward %d"):format(r.amount)
        elseif r.kind == "miss" then show[#show + 1] = "miss " .. r.avoid
        else show[#show + 1] = r.kind end
    end
end
print(table.concat(show, " | "))
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(recs[1].src, me, "YOUR is your own name")
DOCS.eq(recs[1].ability, "Fixture Flare", "the ability")
DOCS.eq(recs[2].src, me, "a damage-over-time tick credits its caster")
DOCS.eq(recs[3].dst, "Tankard", "the one healed")
DOCS.eq(recs[4].dst, me, "a ward on YOU")
DOCS.eq(recs[7], nil, "a chat line is not combat")
local all = log.parseAll(table.concat(lines, "\n"), { me = me, t0 = 0, stepMs = 1000 })
DOCS.eq(#all, 6, "parseAll keeps the six combat lines")
DOCS.eq(all[2].t, 1000, "and stamps them a step apart")
```

#### Snippet: Meter a fight

Feed stamped combat lines to a parser and read the live fight: damage per second per character, the top character's abilities, and who took damage.

**Tested:** Over a 10-second fight the crew does 6000 damage (600 per second), Fixturae leads, the tank took 900.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local Parser = require("eb.ui.monitor.parser")
local log = require("eb.ui.monitor.combatlog")
local parser = Parser.new({ me = "Fixturae", friends = { "Tankard", "Mendwell" } })

-- a saved fight: "<ms><tab><line>" (in game parse_feed.attach feeds the parser live)
local fight = table.concat({
    "1000\tYOUR Fixture Flare hits a fixture brute for 1200 points of heat damage.",
    "2000\tTankard hits a fixture brute for 1200 points of crushing damage.",
    "3000\tA fixture brute hits Tankard for 900 points of slashing damage.",
    "6000\tYOUR Fixture Flare critically hits a fixture brute for 2400 points of heat damage.",
    "11000\tTankard hits a fixture brute for 1200 points of crushing damage.",
}, "\n")
for _, rec in ipairs(log.parseStamped(fight, { me = "Fixturae" })) do parser:ingest(rec) end

local v = parser:current()
local top = v.bars[1]
print(("%d s: %d dps | %s %d (%d%%) | %s took %d"):format(v.durMs / 1000, v.dps, top.name, top.dmg, top.pct,
    v.intake[1].name, v.intake[1].dmg))
```

```lua
DOCS.eq(v.abilities[1].name, "Fixture Flare", "the top dealer's abilities are listed")
DOCS.eq(v.abilities[1].crits, 1, "one critical")
local named = false
for _, f in ipairs(v.foes) do named = named or f:lower() == "a fixture brute" end
DOCS.check(named, "the foe is listed (names keep the case a line gave them)")
```

#### Snippet: One fight ends, the next begins

A quiet gap longer than idleMs ends a fight; breakEncounter ends one on purpose (EB does on a zone change); snapshot lists the past fights, newest first.

**Tested:** Three fights: two split by the quiet gap, one by breakEncounter; the snapshot lists the two past fights.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local Parser = require("eb.ui.monitor.parser")
local parser = Parser.new({ me = "Fixturae", idleMs = 5000 })
parser:setFriends({ "Tankard", "Mendwell" })            -- the crew: always friends
parser:addFriend("Sparkwick")
local function hit(t, amount)
    return parser:ingest({ t = t, kind = "hit", src = "Fixturae", dst = "a fixture brute", amount = amount })
end
hit(0, 100); hit(2000, 100)                -- fight 1
hit(20000, 300)                            -- 18 s later: fight 2
parser:breakEncounter()                    -- ended on purpose (a zone change)
local third = hit(21000, 50)               -- fight 3, live

local snap = parser:snapshot()
print(("fights %d, past %d, live fight %d"):format(snap.fights, #snap.encounters, snap.current.id))
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(third, 3, "ingest answers the fight a record went into")
DOCS.eq(snap.encounters[1].id, 2, "newest past fight first")
DOCS.eq(snap.encounters[2].total.dmg, 200, "fight 1's damage")
DOCS.check(parser:isFoe("a fixture brute"), "a name with a leading 'a' is a mob")
DOCS.check(not parser:isFoe("Mendwell"), "a single word is taken for a player")
local past = parser:viewEncounter(parser.history[1])
DOCS.eq(past.total.dmg, 200, "viewEncounter reads a past fight")

parser:reset()
DOCS.eq(parser:snapshot().fights, 0, "reset forgets every fight")
```

#### Snippet: Meter the game's own combat lines

parse_feed.attach wires a parser to eb.events: each combat line that reaches ChatLine is read, counted and re-announced as a CombatEvent; a zone change ends the fight.

**Tested:** Two combat lines are counted and announced; a plain chat line is ignored; zoning closes the fight.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local Feed = require("eb.ui.monitor.parse_feed")
local Parser = require("eb.ui.monitor.parser")
local parser = Parser.new({ me = "Fixturae" })
local seen, closed = 0, nil
events.on(Feed.EVENTS.COMBAT_EVENT, function() seen = seen + 1 end)
events.on(Feed.EVENTS.ENCOUNTER, function(e) closed = e.reason end)
local detach = Feed.attach({ events = events, parser = parser, combatlog = require("eb.ui.monitor.combatlog") })

-- the game delivers lines (offline: the fake host fires ISXEQ2's chat event, then the zone events)
w.host:emitChat({ chatType = 3, message = "YOUR Fixture Flare hits a fixture brute for 1000 points of heat damage." })
w.host:emitChat({ chatType = 3, message = "YOU hit a fixture brute for 500 points of slashing damage." })
w.host:emitChat({ chatType = 8, speaker = "Tankard", message = "nice pull" })
w.frame(2)
local dmg = parser:current().total.dmg
w.host:fire("EQ2_FinishedZoning", "4")
w.frame(2)
print(("counted %d records, %d damage; fight closed: %s"):format(seen, dmg, tostring(closed)))
detach()
```

#### Snippet: Fold per-rank ability records into an ability export

An ability list arrives with one record per rank. convert folds every rank of a line into one entry - the highest held rank kept, the lowest level as when the line was learned - labels it, and masks big damage numbers in the effect text. convertText does the same from JSON text with your decoder.

**Tested:** Two ranks of the heal fold into one entry labelled heal, learned at 10 and held at 25; the damage art is labelled dps and its big number is masked.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local ex = convert.convert(doc, { anonymize = true })
local mend, smite
for _, e in ipairs(ex.abilities) do
    if e.name == "Fixture Mend" then mend = e elseif e.name == "Fixture Smite" then smite = e end
end
print(("%s: learned %d, held %d (%s), %s"):format(mend.name, mend.level, mend.topLevel, mend.rank,
    mend.labels.heal and "heal" or "-"))
local fromText = convert.convertText('{"abilities":[{"Name":"Fixture Ward","ID":7,"Level":5,"SpellBookType":0}]}',
    { decode = require("ebkit.jsontable").decode, anonymize = true })
```
