### Items, merchants and broker: Use, eat and drink

- `eb useitem <item>` uses an item now, such as a potion, food or a worn clicky: worn first, then the bags, never from the bank. It is refused while the item's own reuse timer runs.
- `eb useon <member> <item>` uses an item on a group or raid member.
- `eb consume on` keeps your worn food and drink on auto-consume. Turning it on eats or drinks one at once when its effect is not up. `eb consume status` says what is worn and whether it auto-consumes.
- `eb potion on <item>; <item>` auto-consumes the potions, elixirs, scrolls or poisons you name. `eb potion status` reads them.
- `eb scroll <name>` uses a Scroll of \<name> from the bags.

Tested pieces in Lua: [use an item when it is ready](#snippet-use-an-item-when-it-is-ready), [keep food and drink on auto-consume](#snippet-keep-food-and-drink-on-auto-consume). The *Food and drink keeper* script in the [worked example](#items-merchants-and-broker-worked-example) does it all the time, and warns when a stack runs low.

### Items, merchants and broker: What EB never takes

Every sell, destroy, transmute, salvage, extract and deposit passes the same check first. It keeps:

- **Protected items:** your protect list, every epic weapon piece and the Personal Treasure family. Only `eb protect unprotect <item>` takes a default off, and it then stays off.
- **A Krono**, always. Only `eb krono` moves one.
- **The items a box runs on**, such as recall items, the repair bot and experience potions. These are always kept.
- **An item whose details have not come in yet.** EB asks the game about a few items at a time, so a fresh look at the bags can show some items still without detail.
- **Heirloom, attuned and no-trade items**, unless the job opts in to each such flag the item carries. Selling one needs its own opt-in.
- **Spell scrolls, in a bulk run:** Expert, Master, Grandmaster, Ancient and Celestial are kept, and the T.S.E word `-keepscrolls` changes which tiers. A bulk sell never takes a spell scroll of any tier.
- **No-value items**, except from a destroy. An item the game will not transmute or salvage is refused by that act.
- **Your keep list** (`eb depot keep`) and every protected item, from a deposit.

Nothing goes without a rule, either. With no sell rule nothing is sold, with no junk tiers nothing is destroyed, and a deposit needs a kind, words or `all`. A destroy you type yourself (`eb tse destroy`) is a dry run until you add `go`.

**In Lua.** Ask the same check yourself, before a destroy or a sell:

#### Snippet: Ask the safety gate before destroying or selling

rules.canTake(action, item, ctx) is the one gate every destroy, transmute, salvage and sell goes through. It fails safe: an item whose details were not read, a protected item, or a no-trade item you did not opt in is refused, with the reason.

**Tested:** The plain junk item may go; the unread, the protected and the no-trade items are refused with their reasons.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local R = require("eb.economy.rules")
local cfg = R.load({})
local function try(item) local ok, why = R.canTake("destroy", item, { cfg = cfg }); return ok and "ok" or why end
local junk = { name = "a fixture rag", type = "Item", tier = "COMMON" }
local unread = { name = "a fixture mystery", type = "Unknown", tier = "UNKNOWN" }
local treasure = { name = "a fixture personal treasure", type = "Item", tier = "TREASURED" }
local bound = { name = "a fixture keepsake", type = "Item", tier = "COMMON", noTrade = true }
print(("%s: %s; unread: %s; protected: %s; no-trade: %s"):format(junk.name, try(junk), try(unread), try(treasure),
    try(bound)))
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(try(junk), "ok", "plain junk may go")
DOCS.eq(R.canTake("destroy", bound, { cfg = cfg, asked = { noTrade = true } }), true, "opted in by name: allowed")
DOCS.eq((R.canTake("sell", bound, { cfg = cfg })), false, "selling a bound item needs its own opt-in")
```

More tested pieces: [preview what a bulk transmute would take](#snippet-preview-what-a-bulk-transmute-would-take), [protect an item from every bulk action](#snippet-protect-an-item-from-every-bulk-action), [pick items with a filter](#snippet-pick-items-from-a-list-with-a-filter).

### Items, merchants and broker: Worked example

Three complete scripts for your bags: sell junk at a merchant, keep your food and drink going, and pause EB when the bags are full. Save one and run it as its card says.

#### Complete script: Sell junk at a merchant

A drop-in script that waits for a merchant window and sells every listed item your bags hold through the window's own rows, once per window. It answers no question it did not cause.

**Where it goes:** `InnerSpace/Scripts/eb_selljunk.lua`

**Get the file:** [examples/script-selljunk.lua](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jiimboeq2/EB-Docs/main/examples/script-selljunk.lua) (save it as eb_selljunk.lua)

**Run it:**

```text
lua eb_selljunk "Rusty Fixture Blade" "Torn Fixture Pelt"
endlua eb_selljunk
```

**Needs:**

- EB for InnerSpace's session (ISXEQ2 and ISXLUA loaded); EB itself does not have to run
- the exact names of the items to sell (only those are ever sold)
- you open the merchant window yourself (hail the merchant); the script never opens one

**Tested:** Sells the whole stack of each listed item in the bags when a window opens, leaves every other item, and sells again only at the next window.

**Verified:** tested offline: run end to end on EB's offline stand-in for the game; not run in the live game yet, so try it on one box first

```lua
-- eb_selljunk.lua - sell the items you name, whenever a merchant window is open. Twice a second it checks whether a
-- merchant window is up; when one opens it reads every listed item's stack and price in ONE read and sells each whole
-- stack through MerchantWindow.MyInventory["<name>"]:Sell. It sells again only after that window closed and the next
-- one opened. It never clicks a question (selling asks none it would answer) and reads only verified members.
--
--   lua eb_selljunk "<item name>" ["<item name>" ...]     start it with the exact item names
--   endlua eb_selljunk                                    stop it

local junk = {}
for _, name in ipairs({ ... }) do
    if tostring(name):find('["\\]') then
        echo("eb_selljunk: skipping a name with a quote or a backslash in it: " .. tostring(name))
    elseif name ~= "" then
        junk[#junk + 1] = name
    end
end
if #junk == 0 then
    echo('usage: lua eb_selljunk "<item name>" ["<item name>" ...]')
    return
end

local function split(s)
    local out = {}
    for v in (tostring(s or "") .. "|"):gmatch("(.-)|") do out[#out + 1] = v end
    return out
end

local function row(name) return 'MerchantWindow.MyInventory["' .. name .. '"]' end

local function merchantOpen() return IS.Parse("${MerchantWindow.IsVisible}") == "TRUE" end

-- one read for every listed item (its stack in the bags - NULL when there is none - and the price), then one Sell each
local function sellListed()
    local seq = {}
    for _, name in ipairs(junk) do seq[#seq + 1] = "${" .. row(name) .. ".Quantity}|${" .. row(name) .. ".PriceString}" end
    local r = split(IS.Parse(table.concat(seq, "|")))
    local sold = 0
    for i, name in ipairs(junk) do
        local qty = tonumber(r[i * 2 - 1]) or 0
        if qty > 0 then
            IS.Execute(row(name) .. ":Sell[" .. qty .. "]")
            echo(("eb_selljunk: sold %d %s (%s each)"):format(qty, name, tostring(r[i * 2])))
            sold = sold + 1
        end
    end
    return sold
end

echo(("eb_selljunk: selling %d listed item(s) at the next merchant window - endlua eb_selljunk stops it"):format(#junk))
local soldHere = false
while true do
    if merchantOpen() then
        if not soldHere then
            local n = sellListed()
            echo(("eb_selljunk: done at this merchant (%d stack(s) sold)"):format(n))
            soldHere = true
        end
    else
        soldHere = false
    end
    wait(0.5)
end
```

Also for this topic, shown in full elsewhere in this file:

- [Complete script: Food and drink keeper](#complete-script-food-and-drink-keeper)
- [Complete script: Pause EB when the bags are full](#complete-script-pause-eb-when-the-bags-are-full)

*Sell junk at a merchant* sells only the names you give it, through the merchant window you opened. It does not use EB's sell rules or your protect list, so give each item's whole name, and never one that is part of another item's name in your bags.

More tested pieces about items are in the [Lua library](#for-ai-helpers-a-worked-example).

### Items, merchants and broker: Your economy settings: eb-economy.json

EB's item rules live in `eb-economy.json`, in your EB folder. EB reads it when it starts. Every key is optional: what you leave out keeps a safe default, so a new install never sells, destroys or deposits anything.

#### Change a setting

1. Open `eb-economy.json` in your EB folder. Create it as `{ }` if it is not there.
2. Set the keys from the table below and save the file. The file is JSON, with the same groups and keys as the Lua settings in the example at the end of this section.
3. Type `eb all reload`: each box loads EB again and reads the file. A box in a run does it once the run is over.
4. Type `eb economy`. It says what EB loaded, and names the file if it does not read.

EB writes this file itself when you change a list from the console (`eb protect`, `eb depot keep`, `eb purchase add`). Do not change one between your edit and the reload, or EB writes over your edit. A file with a typo is never read as no file: EB says so, runs on the safe defaults, and does not save over it.

| Key | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bags.fullThreshold` | 3 | At this many free bag slots or fewer, EB counts the bags as full. |
| `protect.names` | none | Items nothing may sell, destroy, transmute, salvage, extract or deposit, in any case. The defaults (epic weapon pieces, the Personal Treasure family) are protected without being listed. `eb protect protect <item>` adds one. |
| `protect.removed` | none | Defaults you took off with `eb protect unprotect`. They stay off. |
| `vendor.sellList` | none | The exact item names `eb inv sell` may sell. |
| `vendor.sellJunk` | `false` | `true` lets `eb inv sell` also sell the tiers in `vendor.sellTiers`. |
| `vendor.sellTiers` | none | The tiers a junk sell may take, for example Treasured. *any* is never a sell rule. |
| `vendor.junkTiers` | none | The tiers `eb inv destroy` clears from the bags: sold when a merchant window is open, destroyed otherwise. |
| `vendor.repairBelowPct` | 40 | EB repairs when the worst worn piece is at this condition or lower. |
| `vendor.restockPresets` | none | Your restock lists, by name. Each row: the item's name, how many to keep, and for who (a class, an archetype or everyone). |
| `vendor.fuelMaxCopper` | 1000000 | The most one fuel buy may cost, in copper (1 platinum). |
| `depot.keep` | none | Items a deposit always leaves in the bags. `eb depot keep <item>` adds one. |
| `depot.depositRule` | none | An item pick for `eb depot deposit all`: only what it picks goes in. |
| `broker.maxCopper` | none | The most one broker buy may cost, in copper, when the line names no cap. With neither, nothing is bought. |
| `broker.undercut` | 1 | How many copper under the cheapest other seller EB prices your listings. |
| `broker.beatAll` | `false` | `true` prices at the cheapest other seller's price, not under it. |
| `broker.friendsFloorCopper` | 0 | EB never prices a listing under this, in copper. |
| `broker.priceDefaults` | none | A price per item, in copper: by the item's name, by `<tier>:<type>`, or `*` for the rest. EB never lists the item under it, and uses it when nobody else sells the item. |
| `broker.masters` | none | The spells to get Master scrolls of, for `eb broker masters` and `eb spells buy`. |
| `transmute.freeSlots` | 4 | The bag slots `eb transmutelevel` keeps free. Its `-keep` word overrides it. |
| `brain.vendorRuns` | off | `true` lets a box whose bags are full go to a merchant by itself. Off, an idle box never walks off. |

An item pick, as `depot.depositRule` takes it, names any of: `tiers`, `minLevel` and `maxLevel`, `flags` (`novalue`, `notrade`, `heirloom`, `attuned`), `class`, `name` (a part of the name) or `names` (exact names), `exclude`, a `stat` test, `resolve`, and `bags` or `pages`. An item must match every part you set, and a pick that names nothing is refused.

**In Lua.** The same settings as one table, with a change made while EB runs (run on EB's offline stand-in):

##### Snippet: Write the economy settings

One settings table drives every economy part; whatever you leave out takes a safe default (nothing sold, destroyed or deposited until a rule says so). eco:configure(patch) changes it while EB runs, merging a table one level deep. This is the document a settings file holds.

**Tested:** The defaults fill the gaps; a live change of the repair threshold takes effect at once.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script: the settings (every key optional)
local settings = {
    bags    = { fullThreshold = 4 },                                    -- 4 or fewer free slots = full
    protect = { names = { ["fixture charm"] = true } },                 -- never sold / destroyed / deposited
    depot   = { keep = { ["fixture arrow"] = true } },                  -- never deposited
    vendor  = { sellList = { "Fixture Pelt" }, junkTiers = { Junk = true }, repairBelowPct = 40,
                restockPresets = { food = { { name = "Fixture Bread", qty = 20 } } } },
    loot    = { method = "nbg", space = 2, rules = { ["fixture gem"] = "need" } },
    broker  = { undercut = 5, friendsFloorCopper = 1000, priceDefaults = { ["fixture ore"] = 1200 } },
    bank    = { keepFree = 2 },
    mail    = { keepFree = 1 },
    craft   = { commissions = { enabled = false } },
}
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = Fake.drive(W), me = W.me, cfg = settings })
local cfg = eco.env.cfg
DOCS.eq(cfg.bags.fullThreshold, 4, "yours")
DOCS.eq(cfg.vendor.sellJunk, false, "a default kept: junk selling stays off")
DOCS.eq(cfg.broker.beatAll, false, "a default kept")

eco:configure({ vendor = { repairBelowPct = 25 } })                     -- a live change
print("repair below " .. cfg.vendor.repairBelowPct .. "%")
```

**Offline lines:** the lines that use `DOCS`, `Fake` are EB's offline test world, which exists only where the example was tested: in a real script, leave them out or let the game do that part.

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
-- offline stand-in for the game's windows (in game EB builds the drive)
local Fake = require("economy.lib.drivefake")
local W = Fake.world()
```

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(cfg.vendor.repairBelowPct, 25, "changed")
DOCS.eq(cfg.vendor.sellList[1], "Fixture Pelt", "the rest of the vendor block is untouched")
DOCS.eq(eco:contract().bagsFull({ bagsFreeSlots = 4 }), true, "4 free is full at this threshold")
```

### Items, merchants and broker: Commands

Every command answers on this box. Put `all`, `others` or `to <who>` in front to send it to the crew, where the command allows it. In the game, `eb help depot` lists this group, and the [Commands](#commands) page has every word.

#### Merchants and repair

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `eb buy` | `eb buy "<item>" [n] [from <merchant>]`: opens the merchant in reach and buys n (1 to 200), one at a time, each purchase question answered for that item only. From: `mender`, `supplies`, `fuel`, `stones` or a merchant's name in quotes. |
| `eb purchase` | The shopping list (`add <item>`, `run`, `repeat`, `status`, `clear`), merchant spots (`grab`, `locate`, `known`, `go`) and your own buys (`expect`, `confirms`). `stop` ends the walk, the run and what is expected. |
| `eb repair` | `now` (the default): repairs at a mender in reach. `on` / `off`: repairs by itself, out of a fight, with the gear worn down and a mender in reach. `status`: the switch. |
| `eb checkgear` | The worst worn piece's condition, and what is at or under the repair line. |

#### Bags

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `eb inv` | `show` (the default): free slots and the items read. `tidy` gathers the empty slots at the end, a dry run until `go`. `move <item> to <bag>` moves one stack. `sell` and `destroy` follow your rules. Also `restock`, `trade <item> to <member>`, `quiver` and `preset` (your inventory presets). |
| `eb protect` | `protect <item>`, `unprotect <item>`, `list` (the default). |
| `eb itemsearch` | `eb itemsearch <words>`: finds an item in this box's bags, its bank and the depots read. Every other box of the crew answers with its own. |
| `eb whohas` | `eb whohas <words>`: which characters hold an item, and how many in all, as EB last read each one on this PC. `-all`: every server's characters. |
| `eb items` | The bag items of one kind (`list`, `status`, `ingots`, `familiars`, `mercenaries`, `forlorn`, `unpack`): listed, and used only with `go`. |
| `eb invdestroy` | `raws` or `resources`: says which junk raws or resources would be destroyed to free bag slots. Protected items are left alone. |
| `eb tse` | `transmute`, `salvage`, `extract` or `destroy`, then the tiers to take: the bag items of those tiers, by rule. `sell`: to the Commodities Exporter. `give <leader>`: to the leader. `saved`: the pick you kept. `stop` ends it. A destroy is a dry run until `go`. |
| `eb transmutelevel` | Levels Transmuting at a stone merchant: `level`, `scan`, `stop`, `status`. |
| `eb krono` | `count` (the default), `use`, `give <member> [n]`. |
| `eb ledger` | What every box sold, deposited, transmuted and looted, day by day: `open`, `close`, `status`, `day`, `last12`, `loot`, `clear`. |

#### Depot, bank, mail and trades

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `eb depot` | `status` (the default), `index` (reads the depot you stand at), `here`, `topup <list>`, `keep [<item> \| remove <item>]`, `deposit [all \| <kind> \| <words>]`, `everywhere` (every depot of the hall), `list <name>` (a withdraw list). |
| `eb restock` | `eb restock <list>`, `eb restock quiver` or `eb restock craftmats`: from the depot, by list. |
| `eb bank` | `status` (the default), `deposit`, `withdraw`, `coin`, and `move <from page> <to page>` in the guild bank. |
| `eb mail` | `read [all \| <subject>]`: takes the attachments. `send <character> <name words> [all \| n] [p:g:s:c]`. |
| `eb distribute` | `eb distribute <item> [n] [group \| raid \| <name>,<name>]`, `status`, `cancel`. |
| `eb trade` | `item`, `coin`, `batch` or `accept`, with one character. |
| `eb tradeq` | `eb tradeq <item> [n] to <character> [from <holder>]`, or `status`. |

#### Broker

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `eb brokerbuy` | `eb brokerbuy "<item>" [how many to hold] [the most for one, in copper]`: buys the shortfall from the cheapest listings under the cap. |
| `eb broker` | `buy <item>`, `masters`, `sweep`, `list [bags \| unlisted \| reprice]`, `listings`, `setprice`, `unlist`, `coin`, `repeat`, `replenish`, `history`, `log`, `status` (the default). |
| `eb buybest` | `gear` (the default), `spells` or `adorns`: the best this character can use, from the broker. |
| `eb spells` | `buy`: the Master scrolls of the spells named, under your cap, then scribes them. `scribe` (the default): scribes the spell scrolls in the bags. |
| `eb collections` | `list` (the default), `scan`, `fill`, `examine`, `depot`, `buy` (a plan first; `go` buys), `acquire`. |

#### Use, eat and drink

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `eb useitem` | `eb useitem <item>`: worn first, then the bags. |
| `eb useon` | `eb useon <member> <item>`: on a group or raid member. |
| `eb consume` | `on`, `off`, `toggle`, `status` (the default): the worn food and drink. |
| `eb potion` | `on`, `off`, `status` (the default) for the items named, and the auto-consume list: `list`, `add`, `remove`, `enable`, `disable`, `idle`, `apply`. |
| `eb scroll` | `eb scroll <name>`: uses a Scroll of \<name> from the bags. |
| `eb itemgate` | A worn clicky whose effect shows only in a Persona stat is not clicked again while that effect is on: `status`, `on`, `off`, `reload`. |

#### The economy itself

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `eb economy` | What EB loaded on this box: your rules, a file that does not read, the saved T.S.E, and what is under way. `stop` ends every economy job. `eb all economy` asks every box. |
| `eb proof evidence` | EB for InnerSpace: lets out, for this session, the item acts that wait for their live proof (see [Today](#items-merchants-and-broker-today-on-eb-for-innerspace)). `eb proof tested` puts the default back. |

A tested example shows a few of these answering: [the item and loot commands in this build](#snippet-the-item-and-loot-commands-in-this-build).

### Items, merchants and broker: Today on EB for InnerSpace

EB for InnerSpace sends the game only what has been proven live. Until then an act is held back: EB says so in words (*waits for the live proof run*, *held back until it is proven live*), sends nothing, and the job never says done.

#### Works at the default

- The depot: its rows, a deposit, a take.
- The bank: opening it, and reading the personal and shared bank.
- A sell through the merchant window's own rows, and the mender's repair.
- Bag items with their tier, type, level and slot, once each item's details are in.

#### Let out by eb proof evidence

- The merchant's list, its prices and its Buy, and the purchase question's Yes and No.
- The bag items' No-Trade, Heirloom and Attuned flags. Until they read, EB's own sells and T.S.E runs keep every item.
- Finding a mender or a supplies merchant by its title. Until then EB finds one only by a name that holds the word.
- The broker, moving items and coin in the bank, the guild bank, reading the mail and taking attachments, trades, and transmute, salvage and extract.

Type `eb proof evidence`: it lasts for this session, and `eb proof tested` puts the default back. `eb gate` is the doors command, not this switch.

Destroying an item and sending mail still wait for their own live proof.

### Items, merchants and broker: If something goes wrong

EB says what stopped a job in the session's console. Find the words below in its answer.

| You see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `no merchant in reach`, `no mender in reach` | Walk within 12 m. On EB for InnerSpace at the default, EB finds a mender or a supplies merchant only by a name that holds that word: open its window yourself (hail it), then type the line again. |
| `names several rows at different prices`, `whose prices do not read` | Several rows carry that name, and EB cannot tell which one you mean, so it bought nothing. Buy that row yourself: `eb purchase expect "<item>"` answers its question for you. |
| `the merchant does not sell` | Type the name as the merchant window shows it (any case). Quote a name that holds *from* or ends in a number. |
| `cost … copper, carrying …` | You carry too little coin for it. |
| `the purchase question named something else` | The game asked about another item. EB said No and bought nothing. |
| `the purchase question is up and EB may not answer it here` | Answer the question yourself, or type `eb proof evidence` and buy again. |
| `waits for the live proof run` | That act is held back on EB for InnerSpace until it is proven live (see [Today](#items-merchants-and-broker-today-on-eb-for-innerspace)). `eb proof evidence` lets most item acts out for this session. |
| `no sell rule is set - nothing sold` | Say what may go: `vendor.sellList`, or `vendor.sellJunk` with `vendor.sellTiers`, in eb-economy.json. |
| `no junk rule is set - nothing destroyed` | Set `vendor.junkTiers` in eb-economy.json. |
| `sold (the rest kept by the rules gate)` | The safety check kept the rest: protected, bound, a spell scroll, no value, or details not in yet. On EB for InnerSpace at the default the bag flags do not read, so it keeps them all: `eb proof evidence`. |
| `info not loaded (unread)` | The game has not sent that item's details yet. Wait a moment and try again. `eb inv` says how many items are still without detail. |
| `no-trade / heirloom / attuned not read` | Those flags do not read yet on EB for InnerSpace: `eb proof evidence`. |
| `not started - … is under way` | One job at a time on each box. Wait for it, or end it with the line the answer names, such as `eb economy stop`. |
| `not started - this box is in a fight` | Wait until the fight is over. A job already under way waits by itself. |
| `stopped after 600 s` | The job ran 10 minutes. See what it got done, then ask again for the rest. |
| `name the most it may cost` | Every broker buy needs a cap: `eb brokerbuy "<item>" <how many> <the most for one>`, or `broker.maxCopper` in eb-economy.json. |
| `EB never buys a Krono` | By design. Only `eb krono` moves a Krono. |
| `eb-economy.json does not read` | The file has a typo. EB runs on the safe defaults and does not save over it. Fix the typo, or rename the file, then type `eb all reload`. |
| `no spot known for` | Target the merchant and type `eb purchase grab`, or let EB open its window once. |
| `a guild deposit names its page` | Add the page, 1 to 4: `eb bank deposit guild 2 <item>`. |

## Harvesting

Gather the nodes round you, along a route or over an area, with one command or the Gather window.

### Harvesting: What harvesting does

EB gathers harvest nodes for you: the nodes round where you stand, a route you recorded, or a whole area. It walks to each node on the zone's mesh, takes only the nodes your level can harvest and your settings ask for, and leaves a node that will not give for a while before it tries again.

You start it with one console command, from the Gather window, from a quest pack's gather step, or from your own Lua script.

### Harvesting: Quick start

1. Stand near some harvest nodes, out of a fight. EB starts no harvest during a fight.

2. In that session's InnerSpace console, type:

   ```text
   eb harvest near move:15
   ```

   EB takes the nodes within 15 m of you, nearest first, and walks up to each one on the mesh. It answers `harvest near: under way`.

3. Wait for its last line. It ends after 40 pulls (one pull is one harvest), or when nothing it wants is left in reach, and says what it did: `harvest near: done - 6 pull(s); no wanted node left within 15 m`.

4. Type `eb harvest tally` to see what this session gathered: pulls, rares, pulls a minute, and each kind of node.

`eb harvest pause` holds a harvest where it stands and `eb harvest resume` goes on. `eb gatherroute stop` ends it.

**Rather use buttons?** Type `eb windows gather`, or press *Harvest* on the mini. On the Gather window's *Harvest* tab, pick how to gather and press *Start*: *What is next to me* takes the nodes in reach, and *Let the mesh pick where* walks round you, as far as *Within* says.

### Harvesting: Step by step: a gather route

A gather route is a list of stops in walking order. At each stop EB looks round, walks up to every wanted node it sees and harvests it, then walks on to the next stop.

#### Record a route in the Gather window

1. Type `eb windows gather` and open the *Routes* tab.
2. Press *New route*. The window names it *Route 1* (the next free number).
3. Walk to the first spot where nodes grow and press *Record here*.
4. Walk to each next stop, in the order you want them walked, and press *Record here* at each.
5. Press *Run* to walk the route once, or *Farm* to walk it round and round, taking every node on it.

To mark an area instead of a line of stops, walk to each of its corners and press *Corner here* (three corners or more): the route then roams inside them. A route recorded here runs from the console too: `eb gatherroute <route>`, with its name as the window shows it.

#### Make a route from the console

1. Harvest in the zone once, with the quick start or a roam. EB remembers every node it picks, zone by zone; `eb harvest known` says how many it knows here, by kind.
2. Stand where the route should start and type `eb harvest make orerun`. EB makes a route named `orerun` over the nodes it knows here, nearest first from where you stand. It does not run it yet.
3. Type `eb gatherroute list` to check it: every route EB can run, with its zone and its stops.
4. Run it with `eb gatherroute orerun`. Add `kind:ore` to take only ore nodes.
5. End it with `eb gatherroute stop`.

A route of another zone runs from anywhere: EB travels to its zone first, by its own travel, then starts it. Your own saved gather route files come in with `eb gatherroute import`.

### Harvesting: More jobs, step by step

#### Roam an area round you

1. Stand in the middle of the area.
2. Type `eb harvest roam 80 kind:ore,gem`. EB puts look points in rings within 80 m, each one a spot on the mesh, and walks them nearest first, round and round, taking only ore and gem nodes.
3. End it with `eb gatherroute stop`.

`eb harvest roam 80 patrol` walks the rings in order instead. `eb harvest cover sweep 200` walks every ring once and ends, and `eb harvest cover` visits every node EB knows in this zone, once.

#### Harvest only where you mark

1. In the Gather window, open *Where I mark*.
2. Stand on a spot and press *+ This spot*, or press *Record*, walk round the place and press it again.
3. Set *Stays within*: how far from a mark EB may go, 10 to 100 m.
4. Press *Harvest here*. EB keeps the marks as a route and harvests round them, round and round.

#### Harvest in the right zone for your level

1. In the Gather window, open *Zones*. It shows your tier, taken from your level.
2. Pick a tier to see its zones and what grows in each.
3. Pick a zone and press *Travel*: EB goes there by its own travel. From the console, `eb goto <zone>` does the same; add `bell`, `spire` or `druid` after the zone to ride that way only.
4. To come back to it later, set how to gather there and press *Save the plan*. Then `eb harvest plan go <zone>` travels there and starts that plan.

#### Gather a recipe's raw materials

1. Type `eb mats recipe "<recipe>",3`, with the recipe's name and how many you will make. EB reads the recipe's parts and lists what the bags are short of.
2. Type `eb mats list` to see what is still missing.
3. Stand where those nodes grow and type `eb mats harvest`. EB harvests the wanted nodes round you until the bags hold the list.
4. Type `eb mats clear` to empty the list when you are done.

A part no node gives, such as a refined part, stays on the list as missing, and EB says so: it never guesses which node gives what. The fuel is left off the list, because you buy it.

#### Gather the Materials list where it grows

1. In the Gather window, open *Materials*. Pick a tier, tick the materials you want and set how many of each.
2. Press *Harvest these*, or type `eb mats go`.
3. Type `eb mats status` to see where it is, and `eb mats stop` to end it.

EB travels to a zone of each material's tier and takes only the node kinds that give it. When every count is gathered, it uses Call to Guild Hall and puts the harvest in the hall's Harvesting Supply Depot. This list is the Gather window's own, kept for each character; it is not the list of `eb mats recipe`.

#### Choose which nodes EB takes

1. Stop EB in the session: `eb stop`. EB reads its harvest settings when it starts and saves over them when a switch changes, so an edit made while it runs is lost.
2. Open `eb-economy.json` in the EB folder and find its `harvest` group.
3. To never take a node, add its name to `blacklist`, in lower case, set to `true`.
4. To take only some kinds, add them to `categories`, in lower case and singular (`ore`, `gem`, `wood` ...), each set to `true`.
5. Start EB again: `lua EBIS/eb_isx_boot`.

For one run only, put `kind:<kinds>` on the command instead, for example `eb harvest near move:15 kind:ore`. Every key of the group is in [The harvest settings](#harvesting-the-harvest-settings).

#### Harvest with several boxes

1. Bring the boxes to the zone, for example with `eb all goto <zone>`.
2. Start the same harvest on all of them: `eb all harvest roam 80`.

Your own boxes never go for the same node, and each takes its own part of a roam and its own first stop on a route. That is `eb harvest courtesy`, on unless you switch it off. A box you play by hand (EB paused there) refuses a crew line that would move it, and says why.

#### Start EB's harvest from a script

1. From a script beside EB, send the line with `luacall EBISX_cmd`, for example `luacall EBISX_cmd harvest near move:15` (see [Helper scripts](#helper-scripts)).
2. From Lua inside EB, `eb.dispatch(line)` runs a line as if you typed it and gives back EB's answer.

EB's harvest engine is the [eb.economy.harvest](#module-ebeconomyharvest) module: `wantNode(node)` is the node rule and `runRoute(route, opts)` a route run, polled each tick. Give `runRoute` the option `walkToNode = true`, as `eb gatherroute` does: without it, a node more than about 6 m from a stop is refused on EB for InnerSpace and left for 90 seconds. The snippets under [Worked example](#harvesting-worked-example) show both.

#### Other ways to gather

- **Harvest as you go.** `eb harvest on` takes the nodes within about 6 m whenever you stand still, out of a fight and not casting, with one look every 2 seconds. It is off until you switch it on, EB remembers the switch, and `eb harvest off` stops it.
- **The guild hall's hirelings.** `eb hirelings` sends out the hall's gatherer, miner and hunter and takes back what they brought; `eb windows hirelings` opens their window.
- **The pack pony.** `eb packpony` summons it, hails it and answers its questions (see [Today](#harvesting-today-on-eb-for-innerspace)).

### Harvesting: Worked example

The topic's complete scripts come first: save one and run it as its card says. Shorter tested snippets follow.

*Harvest the nodes in reach* asks the game itself for the nodes round you, so it runs even when EB does not. It skips EB's rules (tiers, the blacklist, kinds and the nodes left a while); with EB running, `eb harvest near` does the same job with them. The snippets are EB's own harvest from Lua, on the offline test world. On EB for InnerSpace the pack pony waits, as [Today](#harvesting-today-on-eb-for-innerspace) says.

#### Complete script: Harvest the nodes in reach

A drop-in script that harvests the nodes within reach whose names you list, nearest first: double-click, wait for the harvest to finish, again until the node is gone, then the next. It never walks.

**Where it goes:** `InnerSpace/Scripts/eb_harvest.lua`

**Get the file:** [examples/script-harvest.lua](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jiimboeq2/EB-Docs/main/examples/script-harvest.lua) (save it as eb_harvest.lua)

**Run it:**

```text
lua eb_harvest "ore vein" "root cluster" reach=8
endlua eb_harvest
```

**Needs:**

- EB for InnerSpace's session (ISXEQ2 and ISXLUA loaded); EB itself does not have to run
- you stand within reach of the nodes (the script never moves you)
- words from the nodes' names (any part of the name, any case)

**Tested:** Empties the two listed nodes in reach, leaves the lever and the node out of reach alone, and stops trying a node that never goes away.

**Verified:** tested offline: run end to end on EB's offline stand-in for the game; not run in the live game yet, so try it on one box first

```lua
-- eb_harvest.lua - harvest the nodes around you. Twice a second, when you are not fighting, casting or moving, it
-- asks the game for the interactable actors within reach (one query into this script's own index variable, then one
-- read of the rows), picks the nearest whose name holds one of your words, and double-clicks it. It waits for the
-- harvest to finish and goes again until the node is gone; a node still there after six tries is skipped.
--
--   lua eb_harvest "<part of a node name>" ["<part>" ...] [reach=<metres>]     start it (reach: default 8)
--   endlua eb_harvest                                                             stop it

local words, reach = {}, 8
for _, a in ipairs({ ... }) do
    local r = tostring(a):match("^reach=(%d+%.?%d*)$")
    if r then reach = tonumber(r) elseif a ~= "" then words[#words + 1] = tostring(a):lower() end
end
if #words == 0 then
    echo('usage: lua eb_harvest "<part of a node name>" ["<part>" ...] [reach=<metres>]')
    return
end

local VAR = "EBH_Nodes"          -- this script's own LavishScript index:actor (never named after a game object)
local MAX_TRIES = 6
IS.Execute("declarevariable " .. VAR .. " index:actor global")

local function split(s)
    local out = {}
    for v in (tostring(s or "") .. "|"):gmatch("(.-)|") do out[#out + 1] = v end
    return out
end

local function busy()
    local s = split(IS.Parse("${Me.IsHated}|${Me.CastingSpell}|${Me.IsMoving}"))
    return s[1] == "TRUE" or s[2] == "TRUE" or s[3] == "TRUE"
end

local function wanted(name)
    local low = tostring(name):lower()
    for _, w in ipairs(words) do if low:find(w, 1, true) then return true end end
    return false
end

-- the wanted nodes in reach, nearest first: one query, then one read of up to 20 rows
local function nodesInReach()
    IS.Execute(VAR .. ":Clear")
    IS.Execute("EQ2:QueryActors[" .. VAR .. ", Interactable && Distance <= " .. reach .. ", \"ByDist\"]")
    local used = math.min(tonumber(IS.Parse("${" .. VAR .. ".Used}")) or 0, 20)
    if used == 0 then return {} end
    local seq = {}
    for i = 1, used do seq[i] = "${" .. VAR .. "[" .. i .. "].ID}|${" .. VAR .. "[" .. i .. "].Name}" end
    local r = split(IS.Parse(table.concat(seq, "|")))
    local out = {}
    for i = 1, used do
        local id, name = tonumber(r[i * 2 - 1]), r[i * 2]
        if id and id > 0 and wanted(name) then out[#out + 1] = { id = id, name = name } end
    end
    return out
end

local tries, skipped = {}, {}
echo(("eb_harvest: harvesting %s within %s m - endlua eb_harvest stops it"):format(table.concat(words, ", "), reach))
while true do
    if not busy() then
        local pick
        for _, node in ipairs(nodesInReach()) do
            if not skipped[node.id] then pick = node; break end
        end
        if pick then
            tries[pick.id] = (tries[pick.id] or 0) + 1
            if tries[pick.id] > MAX_TRIES then
                skipped[pick.id] = true
                echo("eb_harvest: skipping " .. pick.name .. " - still there after " .. MAX_TRIES .. " tries")
            else
                IS.Execute("Actor[id," .. pick.id .. "]:DoubleClick")
                echo("eb_harvest: harvesting " .. pick.name)
                wait(1)                                                     -- the harvest starts
                waituntil(function() return IS.Parse("${Me.CastingSpell}") ~= "TRUE" end, 8)
            end
        end
    end
    wait(0.5)
end
```

**Snippets:** 3 shorter tested pieces of the same topic.

#### Snippet: Decide which harvest nodes to take

eco.harvest:wantNode(node) is the node rule: never a blacklisted resource, never a tier above your level band (one tier per ten levels), and only the preferred categories when you set any.

**Tested:** At level 45 a tier-5 node is taken and a tier-6 one left; a blacklisted node and a node outside the preferred categories are left with their reasons.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local nodes = {
    { name = "a fixture vein", tier = 5, category = "ore" },
    { name = "a deep fixture vein", tier = 6, category = "ore" },
    { name = "a fixture weed", tier = 1, category = "root" },
    { name = "a fixture shrub", tier = 2, category = "root" },
}
local verdict = {}
for i, n in ipairs(nodes) do
    local want, why = eco.harvest:wantNode(n)
    verdict[i] = want
    print(("tier %d -> %s%s"):format(n.tier, tostring(want), why and (" (" .. why .. ")") or ""))
end
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
-- offline: the economy facade with a harvest config (wantNode reads only the config and your level)
local eco = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = {}, me = { level = 45 },
    cfg = { harvest = { blacklist = { ["a fixture weed"] = true }, categories = { ore = true, wood = true } } } })
```

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(verdict[1], true, "tier 5 is inside the level-45 band")
DOCS.eq(verdict[2], false, "tier 6 is above it")
DOCS.eq(verdict[3], false, "a blacklisted resource is never taken")
DOCS.eq(verdict[4], false, "a category you did not choose is left")
```

### Harvesting: How EB picks a node

Before it clicks a node, EB checks three things. It leaves a node:

- whose name (or colour) is on your `blacklist`;
- whose tier is above the highest tier your level harvests;
- whose kind is not in your `categories`, when you listed any.

A node the rules leave is never clicked. A run with `kind:<kinds>` also passes every node of another kind by.

#### Tiers

Each tier has a band of levels, and the bands overlap. You harvest up to the highest tier whose band holds your level: level 45 harvests up to tier 5, level 48 up to tier 6, and level 100 up to tier 13. Past the last band you harvest up to tier 18. A node's tier is its zone's tier, unless the game gives the node one of its own. In a zone EB has no tier for, a node with no tier of its own passes this check.

| Tier | Levels | Where its zones are |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tier 1 | 1 to 9 | Greater Faydark, Darklight Wood, Timorous Deep and the other starter areas |
| Tier 2 | 8 to 19 | Antonica, The Commonlands |
| Tier 3 | 18 to 29 | Thundering Steppes, Nektulos Forest, Butcherblock Mountains |
| Tier 4 | 28 to 39 | Enchanted Lands, Zek |
| Tier 5 | 38 to 49 | Everfrost, Feerrott, Lavastorm, Rivervale |
| Tier 6 | 48 to 59 | Desert of Flames (Sinking Sands, Pillars of Flame), Lesser Faydark |
| Tier 7 | 58 to 70 | Kingdom of Sky zones, Loping Plains |
| Tier 8 | 68 to 80 | Rise of Kunark zones, The Shadow Odyssey |
| Tier 9 | 80 to 90 | Sentinel's Fate, Destiny of Velious |
| Tier 10 | 90 to 99 | Chains of Eternity, Tears of Veeshan, the Velious additions (Withered Lands, Cobalt Scar, Obol Plains, Eidolon Jungle, Vesspyr Isles) |
| Tier 11 | 95 to 105 | Altar of Malice (Tranquil Sea, Phantom Sea) |
| Tier 12 | 100 to 109 | Terrors of Thalumbra, Kunark Ascending |
| Tier 13 | 100 to 120 | Planes of Prophecy, Chaos Descending |
| Tier 14 | 110 to 120 | Blood of Luclin, Reign of Shadows |
| Tier 15 | 120 to 125 | Visions of Vetrovia |
| Tier 16 | 125 | Renewal of Ro |
| Tier 17 | 125 to 139 | Ballads of Zimara |
| Tier 18 | 130 to 144 | Scars of Destruction, Rage of Cthurath |

#### Kinds

EB sorts nodes into seven kinds. It takes a node's kind from the zone's own list of nodes, else from words in the node's name (a vein is ore, a log is wood). In `categories`, write the kind itself in lower case; `kind:` on a command also takes the other words below.

| Kind | Words for kind: |
| --- | --- |
| Ore | `ore`, `ores`, `metal` |
| Gem | `gem`, `gems`, `gemstone`, `gemstones`, `stone`, `stones` |
| Wood | `wood`, `woods`, `lumber`, `timber` |
| Root | `root`, `roots` |
| Den | `den`, `dens`, `pelt`, `pelts` |
| Shrub | `shrub`, `shrubs`, `bush`, `bushes` |
| Fish | `fish`, `fishes` |

#### Nodes left a while

- A node whose pull was refused, a node another of your boxes is on, or a node still standing after 8 pulls is left for 90 seconds.
- A node the mesh has no way to is left for 5 minutes.
- Then EB looks at it again. `eb harvest left` lists the nodes left and when each comes back; `eb harvest left clear` looks at them all again now.
- After each pull EB waits 2.5 seconds, while the harvest plays out, before the next one.

### Harvesting: Commands

Type these in a session's InnerSpace console. Put `all`, `others` or `to <who>` after `eb` to send one to the crew. Every one answers on EB for InnerSpace, in words. In the game, `eb help harvest` shows a command's words; the [Commands](#commands) page lists every command.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `eb harvest near` | Harvests the wanted nodes round you, nearest first (the options are below). Without `move:` it takes only what is in reach, about 5 m, and says how far the nearest other node is. |
| `eb harvest roam` | Lets the mesh pick where to look: points in rings round you, 60 m unless you give a radius (at most 400), walked nearest first, round and round. `patrol` walks the rings in order. |
| `eb harvest cover` | Visits every node this box has seen in this zone, nearest first, once. `cover sweep` walks the rings round you once, 300 m unless you give a radius. |
| `eb harvest make <route>` | Makes a gather route over the nodes this box has seen here, nearest first from where you stand, without running it. Words of a node's name after the route's name narrow it. |
| `eb harvest known` | How many nodes EB knows in this zone, by kind. `known clear` forgets them. |
| `eb harvest route <route>` | Runs a route kept in your harvest settings, taking only the nodes in reach of each stop. `eb gatherroute` runs the same route and walks up to each node. |
| `eb harvest on` / `off` | Harvest as you go: the nodes within about 6 m while you stand still, out of a fight. Off until you switch it on; remembered. |
| `eb harvest status` | Whether harvest as you go is on, this session's tally, the nodes left a while, and a pause. |
| `eb harvest tally` | What this session gathered: pulls, rares, pulls a minute and each kind, then the run under way or the last one. `tally reset` counts from zero. |
| `eb harvest left` | The nodes left a while, and when each comes back. `left clear` looks at them all again. |
| `eb harvest pause` / `resume` | Holds the harvest under way where it stands, then goes on from there. |
| `eb harvest courtesy` | `on` or `off`: your boxes never go for one node, and each takes its own part of a roam and its own first stop on a route. On unless you switch it off. |
| `eb harvest log` | `on` or `off`: writes each step of a run to a file in the EB folder's logs, one a session. On unless you switch it off. With no word, it says where the file is. |
| `eb harvest plan` | Lists the Gather window's zone plans. `plan clear <zone>` clears one; `plan go <zone>` travels there and starts its plan. |
| `eb gatherroute <route>` | Runs a saved route: one of the Gather window's, an imported one, one made with `eb harvest make`, or one in your harvest settings. A route of another zone: EB travels there first. |
| `eb gatherroute farm <route>` | Walks the route round and round, taking every node on it. |
| `eb gatherroute all` | Runs every route of this zone, one after another, then over again. A route with no zone, such as one in your settings, is not in it. |
| `eb gatherroute list` | Every route EB can run, with its zone and how many stops it has. `eb gatherroute` alone says the same. |
| `eb gatherroute import` | Reads your own saved gather route files into EB's routes: all of them, or the one you name. `import old [<zone>] [overwrite]` reads your old bot's hunt routes as gather routes. |
| `eb gatherroute stop` | Ends the harvest under way: near, a roam, a cover or a route. |
| `eb mats recipe "<recipe>",3` | Makes the materials list from that recipe's parts, times 3, less what the bags hold. Two recipes with one name: give its id instead, as EB says. |
| `eb mats list` | What on the list is still missing. |
| `eb mats harvest` | Harvests round you until the bags hold the list, or no wanted node is left near you. `eb mats clear` empties the list. |
| `eb mats go` | Gathers the Gather window's Materials list where it grows, then puts the harvest in your guild hall's Harvesting Supply Depot. `eb mats status` says how it stands; `eb mats stop` ends it. |
| `eb shinies track` | Looks for new shinies near you: reports each one once, and tells the crew where it is. |
| `eb shinies on` / `off` | A switch EB keeps, with `status` to read it (see [Today](#harvesting-today-on-eb-for-innerspace)). |
| `eb packpony` | Summons the pack pony, hails it and answers its questions. During an instance run or a quest line it is held off, and sent once the run is over. |
| `eb windows gather` | Opens the Gather window. The mini's *Harvest* button does too. |
| `eb hirelings` | The guild hall's harvest hirelings: `run`, `collect`, `send`, `status` and more. `eb windows hirelings` opens their window. |
| `eb economy stop` | Ends every economy job under way, a harvest too. |

#### The options of near, roam and cover

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `move:<m>` | near: walks up to a node up to that far away, on the mesh. |
| `reach:<m>` | near: how far it looks round you, 15 m unless you give it, at most 100 (EB for InnerSpace sees 20 m at most). |
| `once` | near: one pull, then it ends. |
| `count:<n>` | near and roam: ends after that many pulls. near ends after 40 unless you give it; a roam goes on until you stop it. |
| `until:<n>:<item>` | near and roam: ends once the bags hold that many of the item. Write an underscore for each space in the item's name. |
| `kind:<kinds>` | near, roam, cover and `eb gatherroute`: takes only these kinds, for example `kind:ore,gem`. A node of another kind is passed by, never clicked. |
| a node's name | near, roam and cover: takes only nodes whose name holds these words. |
| a number | roam and `cover sweep`: the radius round you, in metres. |
| `patrol` | roam: walks the rings in order, round and round, instead of nearest first. |
| `mark:<name>` | roam: roams inside an area route of the Gather window, or round a mark or another route's first stop. Write an underscore for each space. |

The tested example below starts EB for InnerSpace the way the game does, on the offline test world, then types the harvest commands among others: each one answers in words.

##### Snippet: Which crafting, harvest and gear commands are live on this box

reg:unattached{ domain } lists the declared commands nobody answers yet on this box. On a box with the economy installed (EB for InnerSpace's boot does that) the crafting, harvest and gear commands are all attached: each typed line answers - a chore under way, a refusal in words, or a status line.

**Tested:** No craft, harvest or gear command is left waiting, and typing each of nineteen of them answers in words (never "not wired yet").

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local n = {}
for _, d in ipairs({ "craft", "harvest", "gear" }) do n[d] = #reg:unattached({ domain = d }) end
print(("craft %d, harvest %d, gear %d waiting"):format(n.craft, n.harvest, n.gear))
local lines = { "eb craft", "eb craftqueue status", "eb craftsetup", "eb recipebooks list", "eb tinker on",
    "eb writs craft", "eb luck on", "eb harvest status", "eb shinies status", "eb mats list", "eb gatherroute",
    "eb gearup self", "eb aup self", "eb adorn missing", "eb tempadorn on", "eb bestgear status", "eb gearjob",
    "eb glance", "eb transmutelevel status" }
local answered = 0
for _, line in ipairs(lines) do
    local text = a.console(line)
    if text:find("[eb", 1, true) and not text:find("does not answer on this box yet", 1, true) then answered = answered + 1 end
end
```

**Offline lines:** the lines that use `a.console` are EB's offline test world, which exists only where the example was tested: in a real script, leave them out or let the game do that part.

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
-- offline stand-in: the whole of EB for InnerSpace booted by its real boot (in game you type in the console)
local a = DOCS.app()
local reg = a.app.reg
```

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(n.craft + n.harvest + n.gear, 0, "all 19 are attached: none waits")
DOCS.eq(#lines, 19, "nineteen of them are typed here")
DOCS.eq(answered, #lines, "each typed command answers in words, none says it is not wired yet")
a.stop()
```

### Harvesting: The harvest settings

The harvest settings are the `harvest` group of `eb-economy.json`, in the EB folder. EB reads the file when it starts. Whenever a switch changes (`eb harvest on`, for example), EB saves its own copy over the file, so edit the file only while EB is stopped. If the file is not there yet, EB writes it the first time a switch changes.

| Key | What it holds | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `blacklist` | The node names (or colours) EB never takes, each set to `true`. Write them in lower case: EB lowers the node's name before it looks, but never your key. | none |
| `categories` | The kinds to take, each set to `true`: `ore`, `gem`, `wood`, `root`, `den`, `shrub`, `fish`. In lower case and singular. | empty: every kind |
| `routes` | Your own routes by name. Each route is a list of stops in walking order, and each stop has `x`, `y` and `z`. `eb gatherroute <route>` runs one. | none |
| `mats` | The list of `eb mats`: each raw material's name and how many. `eb mats recipe` writes it. | none |
| `auto` | Harvest as you go: `eb harvest on` / `off`. | `false` |
| `courtesy` | Your boxes share the nodes: `eb harvest courtesy`. | `true` |
| `log` | The harvest log file: `eb harvest log`. | `true` |
| `shinies` | The switch of `eb shinies on` / `off`. | `false` |
| `ponyAnswers` | Which reply to pick at each of the pack pony's questions, by its place in the list. | the first reply |

#### For scripts: a node and a route

- **A node** is what EB's harvest reads of one: its `id`, `name` and spot (`x`, `y`, `z`), and on EB for InnerSpace its `distance` from you. Elsewhere it may also carry its `color`, `tier` and `category`. The snippet *Decide which harvest nodes to take* shows some.
- **A route** is a list of stops in walking order, each with `x`, `y` and `z`, and a `name` if you like. The snippet *Run a gather route* keeps one in the settings' `routes`.

#### Where EB keeps the rest

- The Gather window's own routes, its settings and its Materials list are kept for each character. Its zone plans are one file for the whole install.
- The routes made with `eb harvest make`, read in with `eb gatherroute import` or kept by *Harvest here* are EB's own route store, the folder `data\ebgather_routes` in the EB folder.
- The nodes each box has seen are EB's own record, zone by zone; `eb harvest known clear` forgets a zone's.

### Harvesting: Quest steps that gather

A quest pack's gather steps use the same harvest. Each one is the command line of a step; see [Quests](#quests) for the pack itself. A step's `completed` note is its journal line for when that part of the quest is done.

| Verb | Line, and what it does |
| --- | --- |
| `HarvestQuestItem` | `HarvestQuestItem "<item>",<qty>`: the item is its own node. It harvests nodes whose name holds those words until the bags hold that many of the item. Its other forms: `"<node>,<item>,<qty>"`: harvests a named node for the item it gives.; `"<node>,!<journal line>,<max>"`: harvests until the quest's journal line holding those words is done, at most `max` times (40 when left out).; A last field of `Hail`, or of another verb, hails the node or uses that verb on it each round. The step also ends as soon as its `completed` line is done. `HarvestNear` and `HarvestItem` are the same verb. |
| `GatherMultipleUntilComplete` | `GatherMultipleUntilComplete "<item>"[,<qty>]`: harvests until the step's `completed` line is done, in rounds that each run until the bags hold `qty` (99 when left out). After the first round ends it keeps going for at most one more minute, then the pack goes on. `GatherUntilComplete` and `HarvestUntilUpdate` are the same verb. |
| `GatherNode` | `GatherNode "<node>"`: double-clicks the nearest node of that name within 30 m. It does not search or walk: put the walk to the node in the step before. A step with no name is refused. |
| `CollectShiny` | `CollectShiny "<name>"`: the same, for a shiny. |
| `GatherNodeUntilUpdate` | `GatherNodeUntilUpdate "<node>"`: double-clicks the node until the step's `completed` line is done, and stops the step after 20 seconds. A step with no `completed` line clicks once and goes on. |

#### What a gather step does

A `HarvestQuestItem` or `GatherMultipleUntilComplete` step finds the step's node in view and walks up to it on the mesh. It clicks it and reads the game's own words about it:

- **The node is gone**: it goes on to the next node.
- **The game found nothing, or gave a harvest, and the node still stands**: the same node again, up to 25 times.
- **The game said nothing, or that the node is too far away**: again, from closer. After 3 such tries the node is left for this step.
- **The bags are full**: the step stops and says so.
- **No node in view**: it roams out from the step's start (the pack's last walk before the step, else where the step began), up to 15 times, to spots where this box saw that node, else to look points in rings round the start. If the step already harvested here, it then waits up to 5 minutes for a node to come back, looking round again every 90 seconds. Otherwise the step stops and says why.

It never leaves the zone it began in.

### Harvesting: Today on EB for InnerSpace

- EB sees nodes up to 20 m round you, whatever `reach:` you give, and harvests a node from about 5 m. The runs that walk (`move:`, roams, routes and quest steps) walk up to a node first; `eb harvest near` without `move:` takes only what is in reach.
- A node's colour is not read here: a colour on your blacklist never matches, and a shiny's colour shows as `?`.
- A node's tier is the tier of its zone, as the Gather window's *Zones* tab shows it. A zone that list does not have gets no tier check.
- `eb packpony` answers that the pack pony has no proven call on this box yet.
- `eb shinies on` and `off` keep the switch, but nothing picks shinies up by itself yet: `eb shinies track` looks once each time you type it.
- An instance run's `shinies` loot step collects nothing yet.

### Harvesting: If something goes wrong

| When | What EB says, and what to do |
| --- | --- |
| The node is too far | `the nearest wanted node, <node>, is 12 m away (move:<m> walks up to it)`. Let it walk: `eb harvest near move:15`. |
| Nothing in reach | `no wanted node left within 15 m`. Walk nearer, or roam: `eb harvest roam 80`. |
| The rules leave a node | `<node> left (tier above level band)`, `(blacklisted)` or `(category not preferred)`. The nearest node is one your rules leave, so the run (on a route, that stop) ends at it. Name the nodes you want, or add `kind:`, so EB passes the others by. For the tier, harvest in a lower tier's zones (see [Tiers](#harvesting-how-eb-picks-a-node)). |
| A node is skipped | `<node> is left a while (eb harvest left)`. EB left it for 90 seconds or 5 minutes. `eb harvest left` says when it comes back; `eb harvest left clear` tries it now. |
| Another job runs | `... not started - ... is under way (eb economy stop ends it)`. EB runs one economy job at a time: let it finish, or end it first. |
| In a fight | `... not started - this box is in a fight`. Start it after the fight. A harvest already under way waits through a fight and goes on by itself. |
| No such route | `gatherroute: no route named '<route>' (eb gatherroute list)`. Check the name with `eb gatherroute list`. |
| No nodes known | `harvest make: no node is known in <zone> yet`. Harvest in the zone once first: EB records the nodes it picks. |
| A wrong kind word | `kind: takes Ore, Gem, Wood, Root, Den, Shrub, Fish`, then the word it did not know. |
| Settings change nothing | Write blacklist names in lower case and categories in lower case and singular, and edit `eb-economy.json` only while EB is stopped: EB saves over it. |
| A typo in the settings | `eb-economy.json does not read: ...`. EB runs on its safe defaults and never saves over the file. Fix the typo; `eb economy` lists any file that does not read. |
| A quest step finds nothing | `no <node> in view here, and no spot is known for it in this zone`. No such node was within 20 m, and this box has never seen one here. Put a walk to where it grows before the step, then start the step again. |
| A quest step waited | `no <node> came back in 5 minutes`. Every node near the step is taken. Start the step again later. |
| The bags are full | A quest step stops: `the bags are full ... make room, then start the step again`. Other harvest runs do not watch the bags: end them with `count:` or `until:`, or stop them with `eb gatherroute stop`. |
| The pony waits | `pack pony: held off - ...; it goes out once the run is over`. An instance run or a quest line is going on this box; EB sends the pony when it ends. |
| One box does nothing | A crew line that would move a box you play by hand (EB paused there) is refused on that box, which says why in its console. |

## Loot

After each fight EB loots the corpses and chests beside it, by your loot rules. In an instance run the lead takes every chest.

### Loot: What looting does

EB loots for you. After each fight every box opens the corpses and chests within 6 m of it and takes the drops your loot rules allow; with no rules file, the group's loot method decides. In an instance run the lead takes every chest instead, with the run's own loot steps.

### Loot: Quick start

Looting is normally on as soon as EB runs. Type these in the EB console of the session (see [the eb console](#quick-start-the-eb-console)):

1. Check it: `eb loot status`. The first line starts `loot as we go on`, then gives the reach, the method EB follows and the rules it read.
2. Fight something. When the fight ends, the box loots the corpses and chests within 6 m of it. It never walks to loot, and never loots in a fight or while dead.
3. Loot what is in reach right now: `eb loot now`.
4. Stop or start it: `eb loot off`, `eb loot on`. EB remembers the choice.

One line reaches every box: `eb all loot status`, `eb all loot off`.

### Loot: Today on EB for InnerSpace

EB for InnerSpace uses a game action only once it is proven in the live game. For loot that means:

- **A window is taken only whole.** From a free-for-all window, or the leader's own, EB takes the drops all together with the window's own Loot All. A window where a rule leaves or passes one drop is left for you.
- **These wait for their live proof.** EB says once a session that such a step waits for the live proof run, and leaves it to you:
  - taking one drop of several;
  - the Need, Greed, Request All and Decline answers of a lottery or need-before-greed window;
  - closing the window;
  - the leader's hand-out to a member;
  - Yes to the game's No-Trade question;
  - the chest summon.
- **A drop's tier, No-Trade and Lore flags do not read yet,** so a rule with a `tier`, `notrade` or `lore` condition never matches.
- **The game's Group Options window waits too.** `eb loot method` sets the method EB's own looting follows, but not yet the group's method in the game, and `eb coinsplit` only remembers your choice. Set both in the game, on the group leader.
- `eb lootdistro resolve` and `eb lootdistro assign` hand nothing out yet: no box's gear reaches them.
- A `shinies` loot step collects nothing yet.

### Loot: Step by step: write your loot rules

1. Open the EB folder (where EB Setup installed EB) and make a file named `eb-loot-rules.json` there.
2. Write one JSON object with a `rules` list. Each rule is an object: the item's name (`item`), how to match it (`match`: `exact` or `contains`) and what to do with it (`act`: `need`, `greed`, `pass`, `leave` ...). [The loot rules file](#loot-the-loot-rules-file) lists every key.
3. Save the file and type `eb loot rules reload`. EB says how many rules it read, and how many things in the file do not read as written.
4. Type `eb loot rules check`. It lists each thing a hand edit got wrong, such as a misspelled act or a tier the game never shows, and changes nothing.
5. Ask about one item: `eb loot rules show <item>` names the rule that decides it, or says that none does.
6. Fight, and watch what each box takes. To loot without your rules for a while, `eb loot rules off` switches them off for this session only.

Every box on this PC reads the same file. EB only reads it, so edit it whenever you like, then reload on every box: `eb all loot rules reload`. The snippet *Which loot rule names an item* in the [worked example](#loot-worked-example) builds the same kind of table in Lua and shows which rule wins.

> [!NOTE]
> **Your rules steer EB's own looting.** The chest step of an instance run reads no rule: it takes the chest's window whole.

### Loot: Step by step: loot a named's chest in a run

1. In the instance's route, right after the named's `encounter` step, add a loot step: its own `id`, `act = "loot"` and `op = "chest"`. The tested route below has one, with the id `n1.loot`.
2. Check where the lead stands when the step runs. The step takes every chest within 75 m, and the lead walks to each one on the zone's mesh.
3. To hear how it went, add an `announce` step whose message quotes `{{verdict.n1.loot}}`, with your loot step's own id.
4. Try the one step on the lead, standing near the chest: `eb ic teststep <zone> <step>`. `eb ic near <zone>` lists the step numbers.
5. Run the instance on the lead: `eb ic run <zone>`. The loot step's line in the console ends with its verdict, for example `loot chest: looted`.

Without a loot step the lead still takes the chests: before each `path` step it takes every chest within 75 m, and at the zone's end it sweeps 100 m. A loot step takes them at once and records how it went.

#### Snippet: Recipe: an instance route with steps, pulls and a camp spot

Write an instance file (hub, door, route steps, two encounter scripts), load it and run it end to end: the tank zones in, camps the group, walks, pulls a named, clears the trash, loots, announces and leaves by the exit door.

**Tested:** The run completes: the named is killed, the trash cleared, the chest looted, the door used once and the exit taken back to the hub.

```lua
local runner = IC.new(env)

local ok, why, report = runner:run(inst)
print(why)
for _, line in ipairs(world.lines) do
    local said = line:match("ANNOUNCE: (.*)$")
    if said then print(said) end
end
```

### Loot: Step by step: wish for an item for every member

The wish list holds items the group wants. Each one is wished for every member who does not have it yet. It steers looting through your rules file, so keep one loaded and on (`eb loot rules` says). A file whose rule list is empty is enough: every drop nobody wishes for still goes to EB's own default.

1. Put the item on the list: `eb lootdistro add <item>`.
2. Have every box check itself (its bags, its bank as EB last read it, and what it wears): `eb all lootdistro scan`.
3. On the group leader, open the wishes: `eb lootdistro sync`. It names any member not checked yet.
4. See who still lacks it: `eb lootdistro status`.
5. Take one member off an item with `eb lootdistro skip <item> <who>`, or drop the item with `eb lootdistro remove <item>`.

From then on, every 2 minutes out of a fight, each box checks itself and the leader syncs. A drop someone in this group wishes for comes before every rule: the wisher's box takes it and the others pass, and on the leader's own window the leader hands it to the wisher. The list is kept on this PC.

### Loot: Step by step: set the group's loot method

1. Pick the method, and a rarity if you like, on every box: `eb all loot method nbg treasured`. EB's own looting follows it, and EB remembers it.
2. On the group leader EB also sets it on the game's own group, at once and again whenever the group changes. On EB for InnerSpace that waits for its live proof: set it in the game's Group Options window.
3. For one instance run, put it on the run line instead: `eb ic run <zone> loot=nbg`. It comes before the instance file's own method.
4. Check it: `eb loot method` shows the method and what the group's leader set.

The words are in [Loot methods and rarities](#loot-loot-methods-and-rarities). An instance file can carry its own method too: see [Loot in an instance run](#loot-loot-in-an-instance-run).

### Loot: Worked example

The complete script for this topic first: save it and run it as its card says. Shorter tested snippets follow.

- `eb_lootall.lua` takes a loot window the moment the game opens one, by its own `leave=` and `only=` lists, not by your rules file.
- Switch EB's own looting off while it runs, so the two never act on one window: `eb loot off`. Type `eb loot on` after `endlua eb_lootall`.
- Leave out the word `all` in a group that uses lottery or need before greed. `all` sends Loot All to a window of any kind, which EB itself never does.

#### Complete script: Take loot windows by your rules

A drop-in script that takes a loot window the moment the game opens one: free-for-all windows by default, never a window holding an item on your leave list, and with an only= list just the windows that hold one of those.

**Where it goes:** `InnerSpace/Scripts/eb_lootall.lua`

**Get the file:** [examples/script-lootall.lua](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jiimboeq2/EB-Docs/main/examples/script-lootall.lua) (save it as eb_lootall.lua)

**Run it:**

```text
lua eb_lootall "leave=Cursed Fixture Idol"
endlua eb_lootall
```

**Needs:**

- EB for InnerSpace's session (ISXEQ2 and ISXLUA loaded); EB itself does not have to run
- EB's own looting off, so the two do not both act on one window

**Tested:** Takes the free-for-all window, leaves the lottery window and the window holding a leave-list item open for you, and says why for each.

**Verified:** tested offline: run end to end on EB's offline stand-in for the game; not run in the live game yet, so try it on one box first

```lua
-- eb_lootall.lua - take loot windows by your rules. It does nothing until the game says a loot window opened (the
-- loot-window event; a loot window is never polled - with no window up that read is slow), then reads the window's
-- type and every item name in ONE read and decides:
--   * a window that is not free-for-all is left for you, unless you start it with the word all;
--   * a window holding an item from leave= is left for you (EB takes a window whole, so it never takes part of one);
--   * with only=, a window is taken only when it holds at least one of those items.
-- Lists are item names separated by ';' (any case).
--
--   lua eb_lootall [all] ["leave=<item>;<item>"] ["only=<item>;<item>"]      start it
--   endlua eb_lootall                                                          stop it

local takeAny, leave, only = false, {}, nil
for _, word in ipairs({ ... }) do
    local low = tostring(word):lower()
    if low == "all" then
        takeAny = true
    elseif low:sub(1, 6) == "leave=" then
        for n in low:sub(7):gmatch("[^;]+") do leave[n] = true end
    elseif low:sub(1, 5) == "only=" then
        only = only or {}
        for n in low:sub(6):gmatch("[^;]+") do only[n] = true end
    else
        echo('usage: lua eb_lootall [all] ["leave=<item>;<item>"] ["only=<item>;<item>"]')
        return
    end
end

local function split(s)
    local out = {}
    for v in (tostring(s or "") .. "|"):gmatch("(.-)|") do out[#out + 1] = v end
    return out
end

-- the event handler runs in one go inside the game's frame: it only counts, the loop below does the work
local opened = 0
IS.AttachEvent("EQ2_onLootWindowAppeared", function() opened = opened + 1 end)

-- why a window stays open, or nil to take it
local function verdict(kind, names)
    if not takeAny and kind ~= "Free For All" then return "a " .. kind .. " window" end
    local wanted = only == nil
    for _, n in ipairs(names) do
        local low = n:lower()
        if leave[low] then return "it holds " .. n end
        if only and only[low] then wanted = true end
    end
    if not wanted then return "nothing on the only= list" end
    return nil
end

local function handleWindow()
    local head = split(IS.Parse("${LootWindow(exists)}|${LootWindow.Type}|${LootWindow.NumItems}"))
    if head[1] ~= "TRUE" then return end
    local kind, n = head[2], tonumber(head[3]) or 0
    local names = {}
    if n > 0 then
        local seq = {}
        for i = 1, n do seq[i] = "${LootWindow.Item[" .. i .. "].Name}" end
        names = split(IS.Parse(table.concat(seq, "|")))
    end
    local why = verdict(kind, names)
    if why then
        echo("eb_lootall: left the loot window open for you: " .. why)
    else
        IS.Execute("LootWindow:LootAll")
        echo(("eb_lootall: took %d item(s): %s"):format(n, table.concat(names, ", ")))
    end
end

echo("eb_lootall: waiting for loot windows - endlua eb_lootall stops it")
while true do
    if opened > 0 then
        opened = 0
        handleWindow()
    end
    waitframe()
end
```

#### Snippet: Which loot rule names an item

lootrules.parse(doc) reads a loot-rules table; bestRule(rules, name, facts) picks the rule that decides an item. The most specific rule wins: an exact name beats a "contains" text, a longer text a shorter one.

**Tested:** The exact-name rule wins for the rune; the "contains" rule takes the other shards; an unnamed item has no rule.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script: the rules a box keeps in its own loot-rules file, decoded to a Lua table
local LR = require("eb.economy.lootrules")
local d = LR.parse({
    fallback = "leave",
    rules = {
        { id = "r1", match = "contains", item = "shard", act = "greed" },
        { id = "r2", match = "exact", item = "Fixture Rune Shard", act = "need" },
    },
})
local out = {}
for _, name in ipairs({ "Fixture Rune Shard", "a cracked fixture shard", "a fixture pelt" }) do
    local rule = LR.bestRule(d.rules, name, {})
    out[#out + 1] = name .. " -> " .. (rule and rule.act or "(no rule)")
end
print(table.concat(out, "; "))
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(LR.bestRule(d.rules, "fixture rune shard", {}).id, "r2", "names compare without case")
DOCS.eq(LR.bestRule(d.rules, "a cracked fixture shard", {}).act, "greed", "the contains rule")
DOCS.eq(LR.bestRule(d.rules, "a fixture pelt", {}), nil, "no rule names it")
DOCS.eq(d.opts.fallback, "leave", "what happens to an item no rule names")
```

#### Snippet: A loot helper: read the window, apply the rules, take the lot

When the game reports a loot window, read its type and item names, let the loot rules decide, and take everything only when every item is wanted.

**Tested:** The LootOpened event arrives, both items are wanted, and the helper sends Loot All.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local LR = require("eb.economy.lootrules")
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local rules = LR.parse({ fallback = "leave", rules = { { match = "contains", item = "fixture", act = "greed" } } })
local said
events.on("LootOpened", function()
    game.NoteLoot()                                       -- tell the game layer's loot watch a window is up
    local lw = game.LootWindow()
    if not (lw and (lw.items or 0) > 0) then return end
    local items = {}
    for i = 1, lw.items do items[i] = { name = game.GetVar("LootWindow.Item[" .. i .. "].Name", "") } end
    local d = LR.decideWindow(rules.rules, rules.opts, items, LR.parseWin(lw.type), { me = game.Me().name })
    if d.act == "lootall" then
        game.Execute("LootWindow:LootAll")
        said = ("looted %d items (%s)"):format(#items, LR.actText(d.act))
        print(said)
    end
end)

-- a corpse is opened: the window appears and the game raises its loot event
w.setWindow("loot", { type = "Free For All", items = { { name = "a fixture pelt" }, { name = "a fixture fang" } } })
w.host:fire("EQ2_onLootWindowAppeared", "1001")
w.frame(2)
```

#### Snippet: The after-looting guard: destroy only by exact name

An after-looting rule (destroy, transmute, salvage) acts on an item once it is in your bags. afterBlock(rule, item) says why it would be left alone: a destroy needs the item's exact name, and No-Trade, Heirloom, Lore or attuned items are never destroyed.

**Tested:** The exact-name destroy may go; the "contains" destroy and the No-Trade item are left alone with their reasons.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local LR = require("eb.economy.lootrules")
local d = LR.parse({ rules = {
    { id = "a", match = "exact", item = "a fixture rag", act = "destroy" },
    { id = "b", match = "contains", item = "fixture scrap", act = "destroy" },
} })
local rag = { name = "a fixture rag", type = "Item", tier = "COMMON" }
local scrap = { name = "a fixture scrap", type = "Item", tier = "COMMON" }
local boundRag = { name = "a fixture rag", type = "Item", tier = "COMMON", noTrade = true }
local function verdict(it)
    local rule = LR.afterRule(d.rules, it.name)
    local why = rule and LR.afterBlock(rule, it, false, false) or "no rule"
    return why == "" and "go" or why
end
print(("exact: %s; contains: %s; no-trade: %s"):format(verdict(rag), verdict(scrap), verdict(boundRag)))
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(verdict(rag), "go", "an exact-name destroy may go")
DOCS.eq(LR.destroyOk(LR.afterRule(d.rules, "a fixture scrap")), false, "a contains text never destroys")
DOCS.eq(verdict(boundRag), "it is No-Trade", "No-Trade is never destroyed")
```
