### Loot: How EB decides a drop

For every loot window, each box goes through these in order:

1. **Not now.** Never in a fight, and never while dead. While an instance run is under way, looting as you go is held on every box: the run's own loot steps loot.
2. **Not this box's window.** A Leader Only window this box does not lead, and a window of a kind EB cannot name, are left as they are.
3. **A wish.** With your rules file loaded and on, a drop someone in this group wishes for comes first (see [the wish list](#loot-step-by-step-wish-for-an-item-for-every-member)).
4. **Your rule.** The rule that names the drop, the most specific first: an exact name beats a part of a name, then longer text wins, then a rule with more conditions, then the order in the file. A condition the window did not tell counts as not met.
5. **The fallback.** A drop no rule names gets the file's `fallback`. `need`, `greed` and `pass` are used as written; `leave` hands the drop to EB's own default.
6. **EB's own default.** With EB's default settings the drop is wanted, never needed. With no rules file, every drop comes here.
7. **Room.** A wanted drop is taken only while more than 2 bag slots are free, unless it is needed: a `need`, or a drop for this character.
8. **The window's answer.** From a free-for-all window, or the leader's own, the wanted drops are taken. A lottery or need-before-greed window gets one answer for all of it: Request All, Need or Greed when any drop is wanted, and Decline only when every drop is passed. Otherwise it is left for you, never closed.

A `leave` never declines: the drop stays where it is. A `leave` you wrote stays `leave`; EB's default never overrides a rule. What EB for InnerSpace can answer yet is in [Today](#loot-today-on-eb-for-innerspace).

### Loot: The loot rules file

#### Where it lives

- `eb-loot-rules.json` in the EB folder. Every box on this PC reads it when EB starts, and again on `eb loot rules reload`.
- With no such file, EB reads a loot rules file you already keep under the InnerSpace folder, and never writes to it.
- A file that does not read (a JSON typo) means no rules at all: EB loots nothing by itself until it is fixed, and never uses the other file instead. It says so at once, and again in `eb loot rules` and `eb economy`.

#### The file's keys

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `rules` | The list of rules, below. EB reads the first 400 and ignores the rest. |
| `on` | `true` by default. `false` switches every rule off, and EB's own default decides every drop. |
| `fallback` | What a drop no rule names gets: `leave` (the default: EB's own default decides), `need`, `greed` or `pass`. |
| `method`, `rarity` | The group loot method and rarity the group's leader sets, until `eb loot method` is typed: that choice wins. `keep`, or no method, leaves the group's own. |
| `untested`, `destroy` | `false` by default. Both must be `true` before a `destroy` rule acts. |
| `removed` | Deleted rule ids, each with the time it was deleted. For 7 days a rule with one of those ids is not read. |

#### A rule's keys

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `item` | The item's name, or part of it. Case, colour codes and curly quotes do not count, and `*` stands for any run of characters. A rule with no item is skipped. |
| `match` | `exact` (the default): the whole name. `contains`: any part of it. |
| `act` | What to do with the drop: see [Acts](#acts). `leave` by default, and a word EB does not know reads as `leave`. |
| `to` | For `assign`: a character's name, or `@` and a role (fighter or tank, priest or healer, scout, mage), a class or a subclass, such as `@priest` or `@templar`. A word without `@` is a character's name. |
| `tier` | A tier word, or a list of them: `COMMON`, `HANDCRAFTED`, `TREASURED`, `MASTERCRAFTED`, `LEGENDARY`, `FABLED`, `MYTHICAL`, `ETHEREAL`, `CELESTIAL`. Any word of the drop's tier matches, so `LEGENDARY` also takes a `MASTERCRAFTED LEGENDARY` drop. |
| `notrade`, `lore` | `yes` or `no`: the drop must be, or must not be, No-Trade (or Lore). Anything else means either. |
| `on` | `false` switches this one rule off. |
| `id` | The rule's name. A rule with no id gets one made from its text. |
| `note` | Your own note. EB does not act on it. |

EB cuts `item` and `to` at 120 characters.

#### Acts

| Act | What happens to the drop |
| --- | --- |
| `need` | Wanted, and taken even when the bags are nearly full. |
| `greed` | Wanted: taken while there is room. |
| `pass` | Not wanted. `decline` and `no` mean the same. |
| `leave` | Left where it is, never declined. `keep` and `none` mean the same. |
| `assign` | For the character in `to`. On the leader's own window the leader hands it out; on another window that character's box takes it and the others pass. `to` and `give` mean the same. |
| `destroy`, `transmute`, `salvage` | Taken, then destroyed, transmuted or salvaged in the bags (below). |

#### After looting

- A `destroy` rule acts only on the item's exact name (`exact`, no `*`), only when the file's `untested` and `destroy` are both `true`, and only once the item's details have been read.
- Nothing No-Trade, Heirloom, Lore, attuned or No-Value is ever destroyed.
- None of the three touches a protected item or one on the Keep list. Transmute and salvage skip an item that cannot be transmuted or salvaged, and No-Value items.

### Loot: Loot methods and rarities

`eb loot method` and the rules file take every spelling below; case, spaces and hyphens do not count. An instance file and the run line take the first column's words only.

#### Methods

| Word | The game's name, and other spellings |
| --- | --- |
| `leader` | Leader Only. Also `lol`, `lo`, `leader only`. |
| `ffa` | Free For All. Also `free`, `free for all`. |
| `lotto` | Lottery. Also `lottery`. |
| `nbg` | Need Before Greed. Also `need`, `need before greed`. |
| `roundrobin` | Round Robin. Also `rr`, `round robin`. |
| `keep` | The group's own method, left as it is. Also `none`, `off`, `leave`, `unchanged`. |

#### Rarities

| Word | The game's name, and other spellings |
| --- | --- |
| `all` | All items. Also `any`, `every`, `everything`. |
| `treasured` | Treasured items and above. Also `t`. |
| `legendary` | Legendary items and above. Also `l`. |
| `fabled` | Fabled items and above. Also `f`. |

Whatever the method, with EB's default settings a drop no rule names is wanted, never needed: it is taken from a free-for-all window or the leader's own, a need-before-greed window gets Greed, and a lottery window gets Request All. A member's box never touches a Leader Only window.

### Loot: Loot in an instance run

#### What a chest step does

1. Only the lead loots. On a follower's box the step's verdict is `the lead loots`.
2. It finds every chest within 75 m, nearest first, at most 8, and tries each one once.
3. A chest farther than 15 m gets one `/summon` first, when the summon is allowed. On EB for InnerSpace the summon waits for its live proof, so the lead walks.
4. The lead walks to 2.5 m of the chest on the zone's mesh, held through fights, opens it, and waits up to 3 seconds for the loot window.
5. It takes the window with the window's own Loot All, only on a free-for-all window or the leader's own. A lottery or need-before-greed window is not taken (it wants one answer for all of it), and a kind EB cannot name is left alone.
6. A drop that stayed because the lead already holds one (a Lore item) is asked of the group, and every other EB box checks itself. On the leader's own window the drop goes to the first member who lacks it (on EB for InnerSpace that waits for its live proof); on another window it is left for that member to take. A chest whose Lore drop everyone holds is skipped for the rest of the zone visit.
7. The lead walks back to where it stood.

#### The other loot passes

- Before each `path` step the lead takes every chest that appeared since, within 75 m: a trash named's, an event's.
- At the zone's end, before the members' hand-over, it sweeps every chest within 100 m.
- After a wipe, the catch-up walk skips loot steps.
- None of these reaches has a setting.

#### Keys

| Key | Where it goes, and what it does |
| --- | --- |
| `act = "loot"`, `op = "chest"` | A route step with its own `id`: the chest step above. |
| `op = "shinies"` | A loot route step that collects nothing yet. |
| `loot = "chest"` | An action in a fight phase's `do_` list: the same chest step, inside a fight's script. |
| `loot_method` | The instance file's own method, `{ method = ..., rarity = ... }`. The lead sets it as the run begins. |
| `act = "lootmethod"` | A route step with `method` and, if you like, `rarity`: the method from that step on. |
| `loot=<method>` | A word on the `eb ic run` line: this run's method. It comes before the file's own. |
| `{{verdict.<id>}}` | In an `announce` step's message: how the loot step with that id went. For a fight's `loot` action the id is `<encounter step id>.chest`. |

A method or rarity the runner does not know is refused when the file loads. Setting the method never stops a run: a box that cannot set it says so.

#### Verdicts

| Verdict | When |
| --- | --- |
| `none` | No chest in reach. Most nameds drop none. |
| `looted` | One chest, taken. |
| `<n> chests looted` | Several chests, all taken. |
| `not looted: <chest> (<why>)` | A chest EB opened but did not take, with the reason. When others were taken it follows them: `1 chest looted; not looted: ...` |
| `the lead loots` | On a follower's box. |

Every loot step counts as a success, whatever its verdict. So does a mistyped `op`: its line says `no looter for <op>`, and its verdict is `none`.

### Loot: Commands

#### Looting as you go

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `eb loot status` | Looting as you go (on or off, its reach, the method), the rules EB read, and the group's own method. `eb loot` alone does the same, and `eb lootrules` is another name for `eb loot`. |
| `eb loot on`, `eb loot off` | Looting as you go on or off. EB remembers it. |
| `eb loot now` | One look for corpses and chests in reach, now. With looting as you go off, a one-off loot of the nearest. |

#### Your rules

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `eb loot rules` | How many rules EB read, whether they are on, and the fallback. |
| `eb loot rules reload` | Reads the rules file again, and says how many rules it read and how many things do not read. |
| `eb loot rules check` | Lists what a hand edit got wrong. Changes nothing. |
| `eb loot rules show <item>` | The rule that decides an item, or that none names it. |
| `eb loot rules on`, `off` | Your rules on or off for this session. The file is left as it is. |

#### The loot method and the coin split

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `eb loot method <method>` | The method EB's own looting follows, with an optional rarity after it; on the group leader, the game's group method too. EB remembers it. `eb loot method` alone shows it, and `eb loot method apply` sets the group's method again. |
| `eb coinsplit on`, `off` | The game's even coin split: EB remembers it, and the group leader sets it in the game's Group Options window. `toggle` flips it, and `status` says it. |

#### The loot window

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `eb lootwin open` | Opens the nearest corpse or chest in reach and loots it the way looting as you go does. `eb lw` is another name for `eb lootwin`. |
| `eb lootwin claim` | Takes the open loot window whole, with its Loot All. Not in a fight, and not a lottery or need-before-greed window. |
| `eb lootwin close` | Closes the loot window. |

#### The wish list

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `eb lootdistro add <item>` | Puts an item on the wish list. `remove <item>` takes it off; `skip <item> <who>` takes one member off it. |
| `eb lootdistro scan` | This character checks itself for every listed item: its bags, its bank as EB last read it, and what it wears. |
| `eb lootdistro sync` | Every member's check on this PC opens or closes the wishes, and names who is not checked yet. |
| `eb lootdistro look <item>` | Whether this character owns the item, and where. |
| `eb lootdistro status` | The wish list, who still lacks what, and each member's last check. |
| `eb lootdistro resolve` | The Resolve auction on or off (off by default): the leader hands gear to whoever gains the most Resolve. |
| `eb lootdistro assign` | Pass Lore on or off (off by default): a Lore drop the looter already holds goes to the first member without it. |

#### Records and instance runs

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `eb ledger loot` | Who got the loot in the last 12 hours, or on a day: `eb ledger loot YYYY-MM-DD`. |
| `eb economy` | What the economy loaded on this box: your rules, and any file that does not read. |
| `eb ic run <zone> loot=nbg` | An instance run with this run's loot method. |
| `eb ic teststep <zone> <step>` | Runs one route step now, on this box. `eb ic near <zone>` lists the step numbers. |

Every command here but `eb ledger` takes a crew scope: `eb all loot off`, `eb to is2 loot now`. The tested snippet below boots EB for InnerSpace and types `eb loot status`, with the depot and broker lines beside it.

##### Snippet: The item and loot commands in this build

The loot, depot and broker commands are declared in EB's command schema, so eb help lists them and the console completes them, and EB runs the economy behind them: eb bank status, eb loot status and eb broker status each say how things stand. eb roster list names your characters from EB's own sources (never a login detail). reg:unattached shows which commands a domain still waits for.

**Tested:** eb help depot lists the commands; eb bank status, eb loot status and eb broker status answer with their state and no depot command waits; eb roster list names the characters EB knows.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script: lines exactly as you type them
local help = a.console("eb help depot")
local bank = a.console("eb bank status")
print(bank)
local loot, broker = a.console("eb loot status"), a.console("eb broker status")
local roster = a.console("eb roster list")
local waiting = a.app.reg:unattached({ domain = "depot" })
```

**Offline lines:** the lines that use `a.app`, `a.console` are EB's offline test world, which exists only where the example was tested: in a real script, leave them out or let the game do that part.

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
-- offline stand-in: the whole of EB for InnerSpace booted by its real boot (in game you type in the console)
local a = DOCS.app()
```

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.has(help, "bank", "eb help depot lists the bank command")
DOCS.has(bank, "bank (personal)", "eb bank status says how the bank stands")
DOCS.has(loot, "loot as we go", "eb loot status says whether looting runs")
DOCS.has(broker, "broker: idle", "eb broker status says what the broker is doing")
DOCS.has(roster, "character(s)", "eb roster list names the characters EB knows")
DOCS.eq(#waiting, 0, "no depot command waits for the economy")
a.stop()
```

### Loot: Loot settings

The `loot` block of `eb-economy.json`, in the EB folder, holds EB's own loot settings. EB reads the file when it starts and writes it whole when a command changes a setting, so stop EB in the session (`eb stop`) before you edit it, and start it again after.

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `reach` | How far looting as you go reaches, in metres. `6` by default. EB never walks to loot. |
| `space` | Bag slots EB keeps free. `2` by default: a drop is taken only while more are free, unless it is needed. |
| `confirmNoTrade` | `true` by default: EB may answer the game's No-Trade or Heirloom question for a drop it takes. `false` leaves such a drop. |
| `auto` | Looting as you go. It starts on, or as the auto-loot switch of loot settings you already keep under the InnerSpace folder says; `eb loot on` and `eb loot off` are remembered over both. |
| `method`, `rarity` | `leader` and `all` by default. Set them with `eb loot method`. |
| `coinSplit` | Off by default. Set it with `eb coinsplit`. |
| `resolveAuction`, `passLore` | Off by default. Set them with `eb lootdistro resolve` and `eb lootdistro assign`. |

A file that does not read is never saved over: EB runs on its safe defaults, and says so until the file is fixed.

### Loot: If something goes wrong

| What you see | What it means, and what to do |
| --- | --- |
| Nothing is looted | `eb loot status` says `loot as we go off`: it was switched off, and EB remembers that. Type `eb loot on`. |
| A rules file typo | EB says the file `does not read`, and after each fight that `EB loots nothing by itself until they do`. Fix the JSON, then type `eb loot rules reload`. `eb economy` names the file and the problem. |
| A rule does nothing | A misspelled `act` reads as `leave`, a misspelled `match` as `exact`, and a tier the game never shows can never match. `eb loot rules check` lists each one; `eb loot rules show <item>` names the rule that decides an item. |
| A condition never matches | On EB for InnerSpace a drop's tier, No-Trade and Lore flags do not read yet, and a condition the window did not tell is not met. Name the item instead, for now. |
| A destroy rule does nothing | It needs the item's exact name, the file's `untested` and `destroy` both `true`, and the item's details read. It never destroys a No-Trade, Heirloom, Lore, attuned, No-Value, protected or Keep-listed item. |
| No looting in a run | Looting as you go is held on every box for the whole run, and after a fight `eb loot status` ends with `an instance run is under way`. The run's own loot steps take the chests. |
| A chest is not taken | The verdict says `wants one answer for all of it`: the group uses lottery or need before greed, and a chest step takes only a free-for-all window or the leader's own. On the leader, set the group to Leader Only or Free For All in the game's Group Options window. |
| A chest opens nothing | `opened (no loot window)`: no window came within 3 seconds, so there was nothing for this character, or someone else took it. |
| A loot step does nothing | Its line says `no looter for <op>`: the `op` is mistyped. Make it `op = "chest"`. |
| A claim is refused | `not now - this box is in a fight`: claim after the fight. `this window wants one answer for all of it`: a lottery or need-before-greed window, which is yours to answer. |
| A wish changes nothing | No rules file is loaded (a wish steers looting only through it), the wisher is not in this group, or a member was never checked: `eb lootdistro sync` names them, and `eb all lootdistro scan` checks them. |
| Something waits | EB says a step `waits for the live proof run`: EB for InnerSpace has not proven that game action yet (see [Today](#loot-today-on-eb-for-innerspace)). It leaves that part to you. |

## Dialogs

NPC conversations, yes / no popups and reward windows: answer them from the console, a quest pack or a script, and know which ones EB leaves for you.

### Dialogs: What it does

Three kinds of game window ask your character something: an NPC's **conversation** (a speech bubble or the classic dialog window), a **yes / no popup**, and a **reward window**.

EB reads all three. It picks the conversation reply you name, takes a reward, and presses a popup only when that popup is safe to answer. You can do it from the console, from a quest pack or from a Lua script.

> [!NOTE]
> **Today on EB for InnerSpace.** Conversations work. EB accepts a group invite from your own characters by itself and answers no other popup on its own. A popup button, a reward and a quest offer's Accept are held back until they are proven in the game: `eb proof evidence` lets them out for this session. See [What runs today](#dialogs-what-runs-today).

### Dialogs: Quick start

Talk to an NPC from the console. Stand near the NPC, then type each line in that session's InnerSpace console.

1. Hail the nearest NPC you can talk to, within 15 m. EB targets it, says the game's own `/hail` and answers `hailed '<name>'`.

   ```text
   eb hail
   ```

2. Show the conversation, with its replies numbered.

   ```text
   eb dialog
   ```

3. Pick a reply by its number. EB answers `replied 2`.

   ```text
   eb dialog reply 2
   ```

To hail one NPC by its name, type `eb hail <name>`: it looks 30 m out. In the classic dialog window, `eb dialog` shows what the NPC says but not the replies' words, so answer by their number on screen.

Targeting an NPC to talk to it never starts a fight: `eb engage` (Engage what I target) leaves alone a quest giver that cannot be attacked, and on EB for InnerSpace it engages only a mob that is already fighting or aggressive.

#### The same from a script

1. Save the complete script **eb_hailreply** from the [Worked example](#dialogs-worked-example) (its *Download as file* button) as `Scripts\eb_hailreply.lua` in your InnerSpace folder.

2. Target the NPC.

3. Type this line. The script hails your target, picks the reply that holds *hollow*, then the one that holds *help*, and ends.

   ```text
   lua eb_hailreply "hollow" "help"
   ```

Give it the words of the replies you want. EB itself does not have to run for this script.

### Dialogs: Step by step

The common jobs, one action a step. Conversations: [from a script](#answer-a-conversation-from-a-script), [the moment one opens](#answer-the-moment-a-conversation-opens), [by hand with the quest helper](#let-eb-pick-the-only-reply-while-you-quest-by-hand). Popups: [yes / no](#answer-a-yes--no-popup-by-ebs-rules), [group invites](#choose-which-group-invites-eb-accepts), [rez offers](#take-a-rez-offer). Then [rewards](#take-a-quest-reward) and [a pack's talk line](#try-a-packs-talk-line-on-its-own).

#### Answer a conversation from a script

1. Get the game layer: `local game = require("eb.platform").game()`.
2. Read the conversation with `game.ReplyDialog()`. It returns nothing when none is open.
3. Find your reply. A speech bubble lists the replies' words in `options`. The classic window gives only how many there are, in `replies`, so pick that one by its number.
4. Answer with `game.ReplyChoose(n, d)`, passing back the table `d` you read: a bubble reply is clicked, a classic one is chosen.
5. Check what it returned (`sent, why`), then read the conversation again for the next part of the talk.

##### Snippet: Answer an NPC's conversation

ReplyDialog() reads the NPC conversation (the speech bubble or the classic dialog) and its reply options; ReplyChoose(n, d) picks reply n.

**Tested:** Picks the reply that offers the task, by its text, in the speech bubble.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local d = game.ReplyDialog()
if d and d.options then
    for i, text in ipairs(d.options) do
        if text:lower():find("help", 1, true) then
            game.ReplyChoose(i, d)                  -- pass the dialog back: a bubble reply is clicked, a classic one chosen
            print(("chose %d: %s"):format(i, text))
            break
        end
    end
end
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
w.setWindow("reply", { text = "Hail, traveller.", bubble = true,
    options = { "Who are you?", "I can help with that.", "Farewell." } })
```

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(d.replies, 3, "three replies offered")
DOCS.eq(w.world.windows.replyChosen, 2, "the second reply was picked")
```

##### Snippet: The classic conversation window

When an NPC opens the classic dialog (not the speech bubble), ReplyDialog.Text is what it says and its replies are listed through Replies:GetOptions. game.ReplyDialog() does both and ReplyChoose(n, d) answers.

**Tested:** Reads the classic dialog's text and its three replies, then answers with the second.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local d = game.ReplyDialog()
if d then
    print(("%s (%d replies)"):format(d.text, d.replies))
    game.ReplyChoose(2, d)
end
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
w.setWindow("reply", { text = "Classic fixture greeting.", options = { "Who are you?", "Show me.", "Bye." },
    bubble = false })
```

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(IS.Parse("${ReplyDialog.Text}"), "NULL", "the window closed once answered")
DOCS.eq(d.replies, 3, "three replies")
DOCS.eq(w.host.log.exec[#w.host.log.exec], "ReplyDialog:Choose[2]", "the second reply was chosen")
```

#### Answer the moment a conversation opens

1. Subscribe to `DialogOpened` with EB's event module (see [Events](#events)).
2. In the handler, read `game.ReplyDialog()`. The event carries only the window's id.
3. Pick and answer the reply as in the job above. Keep the handler short.
4. To watch the events arrive, type `eb event on DialogOpened`. `eb event off DialogOpened` stops it.

A standalone helper, one you start with `lua <name>`, runs in its own Lua state without EB's events. It attaches the game's own event with `IS.AttachEvent`, only notes it in the handler, and reads the window in its loop, as the complete script **eb_choicealert** does.

#### Let EB pick the only reply while you quest by hand

1. On the box you play, type `eb questhelper on`.
2. Talk to NPCs as usual. A conversation with one reply gets it picked. With several, EB says how many and leaves them for you.
3. To have the first of several picked too, type `eb questhelper on first`.
4. Type `eb questhelper` to see what it does, and `eb questhelper off` to stop it.

Standing still with no conversation up, it also clicks a quest object within 5 m, never one that moves you (a zone exit, a door, a portal, a bell, a spire or a flight). Hailing quest givers within 10 m waits for its live proof, and `eb questhelper` says so. It does nothing in a fight, while casting, moving or dead, or in a guild hall. It stays on for this character until you turn it off.

#### Answer a yes / no popup by EB's rules

1. Read it: `game.ChoiceWindow()` gives `{ text, choice1, choice2 }`, or nothing when no popup is up.
2. Answer it with `eb dialog choice 1` (or `2`). From a script inside EB, `eb.dispatch` runs the same line exactly as if you typed it; a standalone helper sends `luacall EBISX_cmd dialog choice 1` (see [Helper scripts](#helper-scripts)).
3. Read EB's answer: the button it clicked, or why it left the popup for you (see [The rules EB keeps](#dialogs-the-rules-eb-keeps)).

`game.DoChoice(n)` presses a button directly and skips those rules: use it only on a popup your script has checked itself. On EB for InnerSpace it presses nothing and answers `false` until `eb proof evidence`.

##### Snippet: Read a yes / no popup

ChoiceWindow() reads the game's yes / no popup (a rez offer, an invite, a zone-in question) - its text and both button labels - or nil when none is up.

**Tested:** Reads the popup's text and buttons; DoChoice answers false while EB holds that click back as not verified yet.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local cw = game.ChoiceWindow()
if cw then print(("popup: %s [%s / %s]"):format(cw.text, cw.choice1, cw.choice2)) end
-- DoChoice(1) presses the first button once EB has verified that click in game; until then it sends nothing
-- and answers false, so a script must not assume the popup was answered
local pressed = game.DoChoice(1)
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
w.setWindow("choice", { text = "Accept a fixture resurrection?", choice1 = "Accept", choice2 = "Decline" })
```

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(cw.choice1, "Accept", "the first button's label")
DOCS.eq(pressed, false, "held back until verified: nothing was clicked")
DOCS.check(game.ChoiceWindow() ~= nil, "so the popup is still up")
```

#### Choose which group invites EB accepts

1. Leave **Accept crew invites** on (EB Settings, Popups & Loot tab; on by default). EB then accepts a group invite from one of your own characters by itself, with the game's own `/acceptinvite`.
2. To accept a friend's characters as well, type `eb set acceptInvitesFrom <names>`. `eb set acceptInvitesFrom none` empties the list.
3. To answer every invite yourself, type `eb set acceptInvites off`.

- Your own characters are every box EB's crew hears, and every character on EB Setup's roster of this PC.
- When an invite comes from a name EB does not know, it reads the roster again, at most every 30 seconds. `eb reload invites` reads it now.
- Anyone else's invite stays on screen: EB neither accepts nor declines it.
- A box you play by hand (paused), or one where EB is stopped, answers no invite at all.
- A raid invite waits for you until its accept is proven.

#### Take a rez offer

1. Wait for the rez offer on the dead character's screen.
2. Type `eb ic acceptrez` on that box, or `eb to <who> ic acceptrez` from another one. EB says yes only to an offer that reads resurrect or revive, never to a summon.

In an instance run, the rez run sends this line to the member it rezzed. On EB for InnerSpace the yes waits for `eb proof evidence`.

#### Take a quest reward

1. Read it: `game.RewardWindow()`. Its `state` is `no_choice` (granted, nothing to pick), `choice` (pick one) or `offer` (a new quest, not a reward).
2. Nothing to pick: type `eb dialog ok`, or call `game.AcceptReward()`.
3. Pick one: name the reward with `game.AcceptReward("<name>")`, or give its row with `eb dialog choice <n>`.
4. Check the answer, `ok, why`. A quest offer is refused here: a pack's `AcceptQuest` takes it.

On EB for InnerSpace a take waits for `eb proof evidence`, and so does reading the window's title: until then `state` never says `offer`, and the `QuestOffered` event is how you know a quest was offered. A pick goes by the reward's name, which only `eb proof open` reads.

##### Snippet: Read a quest reward window

RewardWindow() tells a granted reward (no choice) from a pick-one reward and from a new quest offer; AcceptReward() takes it once EB has verified that click.

**Tested:** Reads a single granted reward; AcceptReward answers false with its reason while the click is held back.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local rw = game.RewardWindow()
if rw then print(("reward window: %s, %d granted"):format(rw.state, rw.grantedCount)) end
local ok, why = game.AcceptReward()           -- a pick-one window needs a name: game.AcceptReward("a fixture trinket")
if not ok then print("not accepted: " .. tostring(why)) end
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
w.setWindow("reward", { title = "Quest Complete", rewards = { { name = "a fixture trinket", linkId = 777 } } })
```

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(rw.state, "no_choice", "one granted reward, nothing to pick")
DOCS.eq(ok, false, "held back until verified")
DOCS.check(type(why) == "string" and why ~= "", "and it says why")
```

#### Try a pack's talk line on its own

1. Open the conversation: `eb hail`, or `eb actor <name>` to hail one NPC by its name.
2. Type the pack line after `eb action`, exactly as the pack writes it, for example `eb action ReplyDialog 2`.
3. Read EB's answer. When the line does what you want, put the same line in the pack.

Every talk line is in [Quest-pack lines](#dialogs-quest-pack-lines), and the [Quests](#quests) guide shows a whole pack.

### Dialogs: Worked example

Two complete scripts first. **eb_hailreply** hails your target and answers its conversation by words. **eb_choicealert** says when a yes / no question waits and clicks nothing; EB itself only accepts your own characters' group invites today. Both read the game themselves, so EB does not have to run. Every tested snippet of this topic follows, the ones above included.

**Worked example:** [Complete script: Hail and answer an NPC](#complete-script-hail-and-answer-an-npc), shown in full elsewhere in this file.

Also for this topic, shown in full elsewhere in this file:

- [Complete script: Tell me when a yes/no question waits](#complete-script-tell-me-when-a-yesno-question-waits)

**Snippets:** 8 shorter tested pieces of the same topic.

#### Snippet: Answer a purchase question only for your own item

The game asks "Are you sure you want to purchase X?" on some buys. confirm.asksFor(question, item) is true only when the question names exactly the item you are buying - the rule for pressing Yes; anything else is answered No or left alone.

**Tested:** The question about our own item matches; a question about another item does not.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local C = require("eb.economy.confirm")
local q = "Are you sure you want to purchase Fixture Stone?  This cannot be undone."
print(("ours: %s, someone else's: %s"):format(tostring(C.asksFor(q, "Fixture Stone")),
    tostring(C.asksFor(q, "Fixture Gem"))))
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(C.asksFor(q, "fixture stone"), true, "case does not matter")
DOCS.eq(C.asksFor("Join the fixture group?", "Fixture Stone"), false, "not a purchase question")
DOCS.eq(C.seconds(2), 20, "a wait under 5 s falls back to the default")
```

#### Snippet: Answer the purchase question in your own buy helper

When your own helper buys something, answer the game's purchase question the way EB does: confirm.new(env) over a drive that can read the question (choice.purchasePrompt) and answer it (choice.answer), expect(item) before the buy, then resolve(item) - Yes only for the exact item, No for anything else, "none" while no question is up.

**Tested:** "none" with no question up, "confirmed" for our item, "declined" for another one.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script: the two drive actions the answerer needs (in game EB's drive has them)
local question = nil
local answers = {}
local env = {
    drive = {
        ["choice.purchasePrompt"] = function() return question and { text = question } or nil end,
        ["choice.answer"] = function(n) answers[#answers + 1] = n; question = nil; return "done" end,
    },
    log = function() end,
    now = function() return 0 end,
}
local Confirm = require("eb.economy.confirm")
local c = Confirm.new(env)

c:expect("Fixture Tonic", 30)                                 -- about to buy: keep expecting it for 30 s
DOCS.eq(c:resolve("Fixture Tonic"), "none", "no question up yet")

question = "Are you sure you want to purchase Fixture Tonic?  This cannot be undone."
DOCS.eq(c:resolve("Fixture Tonic"), "confirmed", "our item: Yes")

question = "Are you sure you want to purchase Fixture Crown?  This cannot be undone."
DOCS.eq(c:resolve("Fixture Tonic"), "declined", "another item: No")
print("answered: " .. table.concat(answers, ", "))
```

**Offline lines:** the lines that use `DOCS` are EB's offline test world, which exists only where the example was tested: in a real script, leave them out or let the game do that part.

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(answers[1], 1, "1 = Yes")
DOCS.eq(answers[2], 2, "2 = No")
DOCS.eq(Confirm.seconds(2), 20, "a wait under 5 s falls back to 20")
DOCS.eq(c.expected.item, "Fixture Tonic", "what it expects")
```

### Dialogs: The rules EB keeps

Every way EB answers keeps these rules: `eb dialog`, a pack line, and EB's own brain. A popup EB will not answer stays on screen for you, and `eb dialog` or the pack step says why.

- **Never a trade, a summon or a duel.** A trade request, a summon (Call of the Hero) and a duel challenge are left for you.
- **Never money.** A popup about Krono or real money is never answered.
- **Never someone else's buy.** A buy or sell question is left to EB's own buying and selling: `eb dialog` and pack lines never answer one. A purchase question gets *Yes* only when it names exactly the item EB is buying, or the item you announced with `eb purchase expect "<item>"` (see [Items](#items-merchants-and-broker)).
- **Never a popup whose words include fast travel**, delete, destroy, betray or abandon.
- **Never a faith change.** A popup that renounces or forsakes a faith is never answered, and a pack step that meets one stops the run.
- **Group invites** are accepted only from your own characters or a name on your accept list, by EB's invite rule ([Step by step](#choose-which-group-invites-eb-accepts)). `eb dialog` and pack lines never take one.
- **Rez offers** are taken only while the character is dead, with `eb ic acceptrez`, and never a summon.
- **A known button.** EB never presses a popup on its own without knowing which button. A line you write does default to the first: `eb dialog choice` and a pack's `ChoiceWindow` with no number press button 1, and a bare `ReplyDialog` picks reply 1.
- **The popup on screen.** EB judges the popup's words at the click. A popup that is not the one that was read is left alone.

These are EB's own answers. A script that calls `game.DoChoice` skips them. To keep them, send `eb dialog choice <n>`, or check the words yourself, for example with `isFaithRenounce(text)` from the module `eb.quest.gates` and `asksFor(question, item)` from `eb.economy.confirm` (see the [Lua library](#lua-library)).

### Dialogs: Lua reads and answers

For a script that runs inside EB. Get the game layer with `require("eb.platform").game()`; every call below answers at once.

| Call | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `game.ReplyDialog()` | Reads the conversation, or returns nothing. A speech bubble gives `{ text, replies, options, bubble = true }`: `options` are the replies' words, `replies` how many there are, and `text` the replies joined with a slash. The classic window gives `{ text, replies }`: what the NPC says and how many replies, without their words. |
| `game.ReplyChoose(n, d)` | Picks reply `n`, counted from 1. Pass the table `ReplyDialog()` gave you, so a speech bubble works too. Returns `sent, why`. |
| `game.ChoiceWindow()` | Reads the yes / no popup: `{ text, choice1, choice2 }`, or nothing. |
| `game.DoChoice(n)` | Presses button 1 or 2 directly, without EB's popup rules. Returns `true` when the click went out, `false` while it is held back. |
| `game.RewardWindow()` | Reads the reward window, or returns nothing: `{ state, title, choiceCount, grantedCount, rows }`, each row `{ index, name, linkId }`. `state` is `no_choice`, `choice` or `offer`. |
| `game.AcceptReward(pick)` | Takes the reward: no argument for a granted one; for a pick-one, the reward's name or `{ prefs = { names } }`. A quest offer is refused. Returns `ok, why`. |

A read is kept for the rest of the frame (never more than 100 ms), so asking again costs nothing. An answer forgets what it changed, so the next read is fresh. On EB for InnerSpace some fields stay empty until the proof gate lets them out (see [What runs today](#dialogs-what-runs-today)).

The game's own windows are in the TLO reference ([ChoiceWindow](#tlo-choicewindow), [ReplyDialog](#tlo-replydialog), [RewardWindow](#tlo-rewardwindow)), and every call of the game layer is in the [Lua library](#module-game).

### Dialogs: Events

A window event carries only the window's id: read the window itself for the rest.

| Event | When, and what to read |
| --- | --- |
| `DialogOpened` | A conversation opened. Payload `{ id }`; read `game.ReplyDialog()`. |
| `ChoiceOpened` | A yes / no popup opened. Payload `{ id }`; read `game.ChoiceWindow()`. |
| `RewardOpened` | A reward window opened. Payload `{ id }`; read `game.RewardWindow()`. |
| `QuestOffered` | An NPC offered a quest. Payload `{ name, description, level, statusReward }`. |
| `ChoiceClosed`, `DialogClosed` | The window went away. While EB knows one is open, it checks four times a second. For a conversation, read `game.ReplyDialog()` again rather than wait for `DialogClosed`. |

Events fire on the box whose game raised them and never go to the crew by themselves. `eb event list` names EB's events and the ones this box is watching, and the [Events](#events) guide covers the module.

### Dialogs: Quest-pack lines

The lines a quest pack uses to talk, one step each. `eb action <line>` runs one on its own, and [Hails and clicks](#quests-hails-and-clicks) on the Quests page shows them in a pack.

| Line | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `HailActor <npc>,<reply>,...` | Hails the NPC (within 30 m), then picks the replies in order, by number: `1,3` is the first reply and then the third, and `1.1.1` is the first reply three times. The conversation must open within 6 s. When the talk ends before the list does, the step is done. Before it hails, it reads the journal: a work objective still open that an earlier step owns sends the run back to that step, twice a quest at most. |
| `HailThrough <npc>[,<rounds>]` | Hails and picks reply 1 each round until the talk ends: 12 rounds, or the number you give, up to 30. A reward window that opens is taken. |
| `ReplyDialog <reply>,...` | Answers the open conversation, one reply a second. A reply is a number (`1.1.1` is three clicks), `LAST_ENTRY` (the last reply), or words the reply holds, in any case; words work only where the replies can be read, in the speech bubble. `wait=<tenths of a second>` changes the gap. A bare `ReplyDialog` picks reply 1. It waits up to 2.5 s for the conversation. `ReplyNow` is the same line. |
| `ReplyClose` | Picks the conversation's goodbye reply: goodbye, farewell, leave, close or never mind. |
| `ChoiceWindow <n>` | Presses button `n` of the yes / no popup, 1 when no number, by [EB's rules](#dialogs-the-rules-eb-keeps). A faith popup stops the run. |
| `OK_Button` | Presses the popup's first button only when it reads OK, Okay, Accept or Yes, or takes a reward with nothing to pick. When nothing with an OK comes up within 4 s, the step goes on. |
| `AcceptReward [<n>]` | Takes the reward, waiting up to 8 s for the window. `n` picks row n, by its name. `AcceptNoChoiceReward` takes one with nothing to pick. |
| `AcceptQuest` | Waits up to 8 s for a quest offer and presses its Accept. |
| `AcceptDeity "<deity>"` | Says yes to that deity's prompt only when it names this deity, asks nothing more, and the character follows no other deity. It waits 30 s; `AcceptDeity "<deity>",<seconds>` sets the wait, and a last `,-continue` goes on when no prompt comes. |

While a quest line runs, EB also answers by itself: a reward with nothing to pick is taken, and so is a quest offer the line's own talk put up. A pick-one reward waits for `AcceptReward` or `eb dialog choice <n>`.

### Dialogs: Commands

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `eb dialog` | Shows the open conversation, its replies numbered. In the classic window it shows what the NPC says, without the replies' words. With nothing open: `dialog: no conversation is open`. |
| `eb dialog reply <n>` | Picks reply n. |
| `eb dialog choice <n>` | With a reward window up, takes reward n, by its name. Else presses button n of the yes / no popup, by EB's rules; 1 when no number. |
| `eb dialog ok` | Takes a reward with nothing to pick, or presses the popup's first button when it reads OK, Okay, Accept or Yes. |
| `eb dialog close` | Picks the conversation's goodbye reply (goodbye, farewell, leave, close or never mind). Refused when there is none. |
| `eb hail [who]` | Targets an NPC and says the game's own `/hail`, which only ever talks. `who` is an id, a name within 30 m, or nothing for the nearest NPC you can talk to within 15 m. |
| `eb actor <name> [verb]` | Hails that NPC (no verb, or `hail`), clicks it (`click` or `use`), or uses another of its right-click choices by name. Quote a name of several words. |
| `eb action <pack line>` | Runs one quest-pack line now, outside a pack: `eb action ReplyDialog 2`. |
| `eb questhelper on [first]` | Helps you quest by hand: a conversation's only reply is picked, and with `first` the first of several. `eb questhelper` alone says what it does, `eb questhelper off` stops it, and `eb questhelper toggle` flips it. |
| `eb event on <name>` | One console line each time that event fires, at most 4 a second. `eb event off <name>` stops it, `eb event list` names them all, and `eb event fire <name>` raises one once, as a test, to try a handler. |
| `eb purchase expect "<item>"` | For a buy you make yourself: answers "Are you sure you want to purchase \<item>?" with Yes only when it names exactly that item. It lasts 20 s, or the seconds you add after the item (5 s to 10 minutes), and as long again after each Yes. `eb purchase confirms` says what is expected. Never Yes to Krono or real money. |
| `eb ic acceptrez` | A dead box takes the rez offer on its screen: only one that reads resurrect or revive, never a summon. |
| `eb set acceptInvites off` | Turns **Accept crew invites** off; `on` turns it back on. |
| `eb set acceptInvitesFrom <names>` | Also accepts group invites from these names. `none` empties the list. |
| `eb reload invites` | Reads the roster of your characters again. |
| `eb proof` | EB for InnerSpace's proof gate: its mode, and how much waits for a live proof. |
| `eb proof evidence` | For this session, lets out what working scripts are known to use: the popup press, the reward take and the quest Accept among them. `eb proof tested` puts the default back. |
| `eb proof open` | Lets out everything that is not proven yet, the rewards' names included. Use it only while you watch the console. |

Put a crew word in front to send a line to the crew, for example `eb all dialog reply 1`. `eb event` and `eb proof` work on this box only. `eb proof` is EB for InnerSpace's own console word, so the [Commands](#commands-quests) page does not list it; every other command above is there.

### Dialogs: What runs today

EB for InnerSpace sends the game only the reads and clicks it has proven to work. One that is not proven yet is held back: the call sends nothing, answers `false`, and EB says so in words. `eb proof` shows the mode and how much waits.

| Goes out | What |
| --- | --- |
| Now | Reading the three windows. Conversation replies: `eb dialog reply`, `game.ReplyChoose`, and the pack lines `HailActor`, `HailThrough`, `ReplyDialog` and `ReplyClose`. `eb hail`. Your own characters' group invites. |
| With `eb proof evidence` | A popup button: `game.DoChoice`, so `eb dialog choice` and `eb dialog ok` on a popup, `ChoiceWindow`, `OK_Button`, `AcceptDeity` and `eb ic acceptrez`. Taking a reward: `game.AcceptReward`, `AcceptReward`, and `eb dialog ok` on a reward. A quest offer's Accept: `AcceptQuest`, and a quest line's own take. The reward window's title and its rows' `linkId`: until then `state` never says `offer`. |
| With `eb proof open` | The rewards' names, so a pick-one reward, by name or by row. Whether an NPC offers a quest, which `eb questhelper` needs before it hails quest givers. |
| Never | The popups in [The rules EB keeps](#dialogs-the-rules-eb-keeps), whatever the mode. |

- `eb proof evidence` lasts for this session; `eb proof tested` puts the default back.
- `eb proof open` lets out everything that is not proven yet. Use it only while you watch the console for errors.
- `eb gate` is not the proof gate. It is the doors command, and `eb gate open` opens a door.
- EB's brain presses no popup by itself: every popup reaches it as a plain popup, and it leaves it there. It does not act on reward windows either: a quest line, a pack line or your script takes them.

### Dialogs: If something goes wrong

| EB says | What it means, and what to do |
| --- | --- |
| `dialog: no conversation is open` | Nothing is up, or the talk already closed. Hail first (`eb hail`) and stand close. |
| `no NPC to talk to within 15 m` | `eb hail` found nobody to talk to. Walk closer, or name the NPC: `eb hail <name>` looks 30 m out. |
| `no conversation opened with '<npc>'` | `HailActor` hailed, but nothing opened within 6 s. Stand closer; the NPC may have nothing to say now. |
| `no reply holds '<words>'` | None of the replies holds those words, and the line lists them. Fix the words, or give the number. |
| `… cannot be read as words here` | The classic window: EB knows how many replies there are, not their words. Answer by number. |
| `the conversation has 3 option(s), not 5` | The number is past the last reply. |
| `… held back until it is proven live` | On EB for InnerSpace a popup press waits for the proof gate: `eb proof evidence` lets it out for this session. |
| `the reward was not taken: …` | The take waits for `eb proof evidence`, or a pick-one reward needs the rewards' names (`eb proof open`). |
| `… it is left for you` | A popup EB never answers: a trade, a summon, money, a duel or a buy that is not EB's. Answer it yourself. For a buy of your own, type `eb purchase expect "<item>"` first. |
| `… is the brain's to answer (its own rules)` | A group invite or a rez offer, which `eb dialog` never takes. See [group invites](#choose-which-group-invites-eb-accepts) and [rez offers](#take-a-rez-offer). |
| `… not one of your characters - left for you` | A stranger's group invite. Accept it yourself, or add the name with `eb set acceptInvitesFrom <names>`. |
| `… left for you (this box is paused …)` | EB answers no invite on a box you play by hand, or where EB is stopped. |
| `ic acceptrez: the yes was held back …` | The rez yes waits for `eb proof evidence`. |
| `DoChoice` answers `false` | Held back: nothing was pressed. Never assume the popup was answered. The same goes for `AcceptReward`. |
| Your handler never runs | Type `eb event on DialogOpened` and talk to an NPC. `eb status` shows each event family on its first line, for example `dialog:on`. |
| `eb gate open` opened a door | `eb gate` is the doors command. The proof gate is `eb proof`. |

## UI windows

Your own windows in EB's look: a page for one of your scripts, or a full EB window. Each one opens in a window of its own, over the game.

### UI windows: What windows are for

EB shows what it does in windows of its own: EB Main, the mini, the Master Control Panel (MCP) and the rest. Each one opens over the game, in the look the player picked.

You can add windows of your own, in one of two ways:

| Way | What it is, and who can make one |
| --- | --- |
| A script page | An HTML file beside one of your scripts. EB opens it as a window and draws its parts for you, so it needs no JavaScript. Anyone can make one: start from *My First Page*, which ships with EB. |
| An EB window | The way EB builds its own windows: a Lua side that holds everything the window shows and the buttons it allows, and a small web page that draws it. The Lua side has to run inside EB itself. A `lua` helper script runs in a Lua state of its own, and a script in the Scripts window runs in a sandbox, so neither can make one. For a window of your own, a script page is the way today. |

### UI windows: Quick start

See EB's own windows first. Type this in a session's InnerSpace console:

```text
eb windows
```

It lists every EB window by what it is for, with the line that opens it. `eb windows glance`, for example, opens At a Glance.

Then open a page of your own, from an example that ships with EB:

1. Type `eb windows scripts`. The Scripts window opens.
2. Under *Examples*, click *My First Page*, then press *Run*. Its page opens as a window of its own, in EB's look.
3. Change *Count by* on the page, or press *Bump*. The page and the script follow each other.
4. Press *Stop*. The script ends and closes its page.

To make it yours, press *Copy to my scripts*. The script and its page are copied into your scripts folder: the folder called `scripts` in EB's data folder. Edit `MyFirstPage.lua` and `MyFirstPage.html` there with any text editor, press *Reload* in the Scripts window, and run it again.

### UI windows: Give your script a page

A page is a plain HTML file beside your script. EB opens it as a window with EB's title bar and the player's theme, and keeps every part on it up to date.

1. In your scripts folder, save the page beside its script, for example `MyPanel.html` next to `MyPanel.lua`.
2. Add a page line to the script's header. Copy the one in *My First Page*'s header and change its title and file; [Script pages](#ui-windows-script-pages) lists its settings.
3. On the page, add the parts you want: elements with a `data-eb-part`. A `runner` part gives Who, Run and Stop; a `value` part with `data-eb-live` shows a value the script sends; a `button` part with `data-eb-call` calls a function of the script.
4. In the script, send each value with `script.live(name, value)`, and open the page with `script.page(1)`.
5. Write every function a button calls as a global function, above the script's loop.
6. Press *Reload* in the Scripts window, pick your script and press *Run*.

The page and the script live apart: the page opens whether the script runs or not, and closing it never stops the script. Its link in the Scripts window opens it again, and it reads the file fresh, so an edit shows at once.

*Kit Tour*, another example in the Scripts window, has every part on one page, each with a line saying what it is.

### UI windows: Step by step: build an EB window

This is how EB builds its own windows. The Lua side runs inside EB (see [What windows are for](#ui-windows-what-windows-are-for)). How it works, in three lines:

- **The Lua side holds the state:** everything the window shows, as one plain table. The page only draws it.
- **A press sends a verb:** a named action from the window's own list. Nothing else can run.
- **A quiet window costs nothing:** the state is built once and handed out again until something changes.

1. **Write the Lua side** with `ebkit.window`: an id, a `build` that returns the state, and the `verbs` a button may ask for. Call `win:touch()` whenever something it shows changes.
2. **Register it, then open it:** `P.ui().register(win)`, then `P.ui().open(win)`, where `P` is `require("eb.platform")`. Opening starts the window host when it is not running.
3. **Make its page folder** in the EB folder: `web\tools\<id>\`, named exactly like the id. The quickest start is a copy of a small shipped window, such as `web\tools\ebluck\` (the Luck window). Rename its `.js` and `.css` files to your id, change the two lines of `index.html` that load them, and set the title and size in `tool.json`.
4. **Draw it.** In `<id>.js`, call `ebk.shell()` once for the title bar, draw each state in `ebk.onState(fn)`, and send a press with `ebk.send(verb, args)`.
5. **Try it in a plain browser:** open its `index.html` from the folder. `mock.js` gives it a stand-in state and stand-in verbs, so you can work on the layout without the game. Shape its stand-in state like your build's.
6. **Open it in the game** from your code with `P.ui().open(win)`, or type `eb overlay <id>`.

Use a lower-case id: EB looks a window up by its id in lower case, so an id with capitals never opens. `eb windows <word>` opens only EB's own windows.

The tested examples for steps 1 and 2:

#### Snippet: Build a window's state

An ebkit window builds its WHOLE state as a plain table, and returns the SAME table until something changes.

**Tested:** Two state() calls give the same table and one build; touch() makes the next state() build a new one.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local W = require("ebkit.window")
local kills, builds = 0, 0
local win = W.new({
    id = "killcounter", title = "Kill Counter", about = "kills this session",
    build = function(self)                       -- called only after a change: build from your data, never the game
        builds = builds + 1
        return { kills = kills, label = kills == 1 and "1 kill" or (kills .. " kills") }
    end,
})
local a, b = win:state(), win:state()
local first = builds
kills = 3
win:touch()                                       -- "something it shows changed"
local c = win:state()
print(("builds: %d, then %d after touch"):format(first, builds))
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.check(a == b, "the same table while nothing changed: the window bridge sends nothing")
DOCS.eq(first, 1, "one build")
DOCS.eq(c.label, "3 kills", "a fresh state after touch")
DOCS.check(c ~= a, "a new table, so the bridge sends it")
```

#### Snippet: Answer a click with a verb

A window's verbs are its allow-list: a click runs one by name, answers at once, and nothing else can run.

**Tested:** reset answers "cleared", an unknown verb is refused with the list, and one that raises answers false.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local W = require("ebkit.window")
local kills = 7
local win = W.new({
    id = "killcounter", title = "Kill Counter",
    build = function() return { kills = kills } end,
    verbs = {
        reset = function(args, self) kills = 0; return true, "cleared" end,
        add = function(args, self)
            local n = W.int(args.n, 1, 100)          -- what a page sent, made safe: a whole number in 1..100, or nil
            if not n then return false, "add takes n = 1..100" end
            kills = kills + n
            return true, "added " .. n
        end,
        broken = function() error("oops") end,
    },
})
local ok, text = win:verb("reset", {})
print(("reset -> %s %s"):format(tostring(ok), text))
local okAdd = win:verb("add", { n = "4" })
local okBad, badText = win:verb("add", { n = 500 })
local okUnknown, unknownText = win:verb("unknown_verb", {})
local okRaised, raisedText = win:verb("broken", {})
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(win:state().kills, 4, "the verbs changed the data and the window rebuilt")
DOCS.check(okAdd and not okBad, "a bad argument is refused by the verb itself")
DOCS.has(badText, "1..100", "with its reason")
DOCS.eq(okUnknown, false, "an unknown verb never runs")
DOCS.has(unknownText, "add, broken, reset", "and the answer lists the verbs there are")
DOCS.eq(okRaised, false, "a verb that raises answers false")
DOCS.has(raisedText, "raised", "and says so")
```

#### Snippet: Register a window with EB's window bridge

P.ui().register(win) adds your window to the bridge at run time; P.ui().adapter(win) is what the bridge sees.

**Tested:** The window registers, and its adapter answers state() and exposes exactly the window's verbs.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local P = require("eb.platform")
local W = require("ebkit.window")
local kills = 0
local win = W.new({ id = "killcounter", title = "Kill Counter", about = "kills this session",
    build = function() return { kills = kills } end,
    verbs = { reset = function() kills = 0; return true, "cleared" end } })
local ok, why = P.ui().register(win)
print(("registered %s: %s"):format(win.id, tostring(ok)))
local adapter = P.ui().adapter(win)
local opened, whyNot = P.ui().open(win)       -- in game the window shows; offline there is no window host
kills = 2
win:touch()
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
```

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.check(ok, "registered: " .. tostring(why))
DOCS.eq(adapter.state().kills, 2, "the bridge reads the window's state")
DOCS.eq(adapter.about, "kills this session", "and what it is about")
DOCS.check(adapter.verbs.reset ~= nil and adapter.verbs.unknown_verb == nil, "only the window's own verbs")
DOCS.eq(select(2, adapter.verbs.reset({})), "cleared", "a verb through the adapter")
DOCS.check(opened or type(whyNot) == "string", "open answers whether the window showed, and why not")
DOCS.eq(type(win.clock), "function", "registering gave the window EB's clock (its spec brought none)")
```

### UI windows: Show data that changes by itself

Your health or a timer changes with no press and no `touch()`. Give such a window a `live` function: a cheap signature of what it shows, such as the health number. EB reads it at most every `liveSec`, and a new signature rebuilds the state.

1. Build from the world snapshot: the one read of the game EB makes each frame, shared by EB's brain and every window. Inside a running EB it is `eb.app.world`; call its `snapshot()`.
2. Return the value you show from `live(win)`.
3. Leave `liveSec` at 1, one look a second, unless the window has to be quicker.

The snapshot's fields (health, power, zone, where you stand, your group and more) are under [eb.world](#module-ebworld) in the Lua library. When its `inGame` is false, nothing else in it can be trusted.

The tested example makes its own snapshot with `eb.world.new`, because it runs offline. Inside a running EB, read `eb.app.world` instead, so the window adds no read of its own.

#### Snippet: Refresh a window from data that moves on its own

A live() signature is read at most every liveSec; a new signature rebuilds the state, an equal one costs nothing.

**Tested:** The window rebuilds when the snapshot's health changes and not while it stays the same.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script: a window that shows your health, built from the ONE world snapshot (never its own game reads)
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local world = require("eb.world").new({ game = game })
local W = require("ebkit.window")
local builds = 0
local win = W.new({
    id = "myhealth", title = "My Health",
    build = function() builds = builds + 1; return { hp = world.snapshot().hpPct } end,
    live = function() return world.snapshot().hpPct end,     -- cheap: the snapshot is already built this frame
    liveSec = 1,
})
local first = win:state()
w.frame(70); world.beginTick()                                -- over a second later, nothing changed
local same = win:state()
w.self.healthPct = 55
w.frame(70); world.beginTick()
local changed = win:state()
print(("hp %d after the change"):format(changed.hp))
```

**Offline lines:** the lines that use `w.frame`, `w.self` are EB's offline test world, which exists only where the example was tested: in a real script, leave them out or let the game do that part.

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world({ pulse = false, me = { healthPct = 90 } })
```

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.check(first == same, "an equal signature: no rebuild")
DOCS.eq(changed.hp, 55, "a new signature: rebuilt")
DOCS.eq(builds, 2, "two builds in all")
```

### UI windows: Put icons on rows

1. Make the icon finder once, as the window starts: `Icons.new({ require = require })`, where `Icons` is `require("eb.ui.icons.icons")`.
2. While you build the state, give each row its icon: `row.icon = icons:forAbility(name)`, or `forItem`, `forClass` or `forDetriment`.
3. On the page, draw it with `ebk.icon(row.icon)`. A name EB has no icon for gives `nil`: show the row's words alone.

The icons come from tables EB ships, not from the game, so a build may look up every row. Tested example: [Put icons on a window's rows](#snippet-put-icons-on-a-windows-rows).

### UI windows: Run EB commands from a window

A button on your window can do anything a typed line does.

1. In the verb, run the line with `eb.dispatch(line)`. It goes through EB's one command registry, exactly like a line you type.
2. Return its two answers, ok and its words, from the verb. The page's status line shows them.
3. To press one of EB Main's or the mini's own buttons, call `eb.control.act(verb, args)` with `start`, `stop`, `pause`, `preset`, `window` or `refresh`.

`eb.control.summary()` and `eb.control.toggles()` say what EB Main and the mini show. In this release a pause press with `on = false` still pauses: resume with `act("start")`. Tested example: [Press EB Main's buttons from a script](#snippet-press-eb-mains-buttons-from-a-script).

### UI windows: Keep the game smooth

Every window runs on the game's own frame, so each one keeps these rules.

- **No game reads in a build.** Build from the world snapshot or from your own data. A loop that must read the game counts its reads with `push_budget.readBudget(8)` and carries on next frame.
- **No file work in a build or a verb.** Save with `P.files().writeLater(path, text)`: EB writes the file a moment later, one file at a time.
- **A verb answers at once.** A wait inside a verb is an error. Start anything long as a task with `P.pulse().spawn(name, fn)`, or as an eb command.
- **Touch only on a real change.** An unchanged state is never sent again, and a closed window is not built at all.
- **Keep the state small.** A state over 1 MB is not sent: the page keeps the last one it had.
- **Pace a busy window** with `ebkit.push_budget`. A change that comes too soon is held, and only the newest goes out when the window is due: `hud` every 100 ms, `bar` 250 ms, `panel` 200 ms (the default), `request` 50 ms.

`P.ui().register` takes no pace yet, so a window registered with it that changes every frame sends about ten states a second. Tested example of a paced window: [Cap how often a window's state goes out](#snippet-cap-how-often-a-windows-state-goes-out).

### UI windows: Worked example

Every tested example for UI windows: the first four here, the rest a button press away. A few show parts of EB that windows use, such as the settings window's list. For a whole working window, run *My First Page* from the Scripts window (see [Quick start](#ui-windows-quick-start)).

No complete script for this topic yet; the snippets below are tested.

#### Snippet: Read the settings catalog

The settings window's catalog as data: a setting's label and range, its default, what one + press gives, how it prints, and what "Apply to All" shows when the characters differ.

**Tested:** followDistance defaults to the middle of 2..40 (21m), steps to 7 from 6, reads mixed for two characters who differ; the instance preset sets it to 6.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local S = require("eb.ui.settings.settings")
local it = S.item("followDistance")
local def = S.defaultOf(it)
local nextOne = S.step(it, 6, 1)
local values = { Tankard = { followDistance = 6 }, Mendwell = { followDistance = 8 } }
local chars = { "Tankard", "Mendwell" }
local all = S.valueFor(values, "All", "followDistance", chars)
local preset = S.preset("instance")
print(("%s = %s; 6 -> %d; All reads %s; instance preset %d"):format(it.label, S.format(it, def), nextOne,
    S.format(it, all), preset.settings.followDistance))
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(it.unit, "m", "a distance in metres")
DOCS.eq(S.snap(it, 6.4), 6, "snap keeps a number on its step (and whole)")
DOCS.eq(S.snap(it, 99), 40, "and inside its range")
DOCS.eq(all, S.MIXED, "the two characters differ")
DOCS.eq(S.baseValue(values, "All", "followDistance", chars), 6, "a press starts from the first character's value")
DOCS.eq(#S.targets(it, "Tankard", chars), 1, "Apply to one character reaches only that one")
DOCS.eq(S.step(S.item("autoLoot"), true, 1), false, "a switch flips")
DOCS.eq(S.defaults().autoLoot, false, "a switch defaults to off")
```

#### Snippet: A tour of the platform services

The target and the install folder, the eb global, the crew transport's box id, the frame loop's own status line, folders and queued saves, and the window bridge's helpers - each in one line.

**Tested:** The target is isx, eb.now is the platform clock, the transport names this box, a queued save is written by flushAll, and the window bridge gives an empty list that is sent as \[\].

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local P = require("eb.platform")
local target = P.detect()                                   -- what the environment looks like
local folder = P.root()                                     -- "." offline; the EB folder in game
local g = P.installGlobal()                                 -- fills only what is missing (EB's start made it)
local box = P.relay().session()                             -- this box's id on the crew relay
local fs = P.files()
local made = fs.mkdirs("eb-docs-notes")                    -- a folder for a helper's files
local who = P.ui().me()                                     -- nil until EB's start names the character
fs.writeLater("eb-docs-example.txt", "one queued save")    -- no disk work now
local written = fs.flushAll()                               -- a cleanup or a task writes the queue
local landed = disk["eb-docs-example.txt"]
local status = P.pulse().status()                           -- the frame loop in one line
local empty = P.ui().emptyList()
print(("%s | box %s | %d save written | %s"):format(target, box, written, status:match("^frames") or status))
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real), its files on a table
local w = DOCS.world({ me = { name = "Fixturae" } })
local disk = require("data.lib.memdisk").install()
```

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(target, "isx", "EB for InnerSpace")
DOCS.eq(type(folder), "string", "root is a folder name")
DOCS.eq(g.now, eb.now, "the eb global is the one installGlobal returns")
DOCS.eq(box, "is1", "the session name is the box id")
DOCS.eq(written, 1, "flushAll wrote the queued save")
DOCS.eq(landed, "one queued save", "the whole text, once")
DOCS.check(made ~= nil, "mkdirs answers")
DOCS.check(who == nil or type(who) == "string", "ui.me is a name or nil")
DOCS.eq(fs.pending(), 0, "nothing left in the queue")
DOCS.eq(next(empty), nil, "an empty list for a window state")
DOCS.eq(require("eb.platform.isx.services.files_isx").parent("notes/helper.json"), "notes", "the folder part of a path")
```

#### Snippet: List the items you can click

UsableItems() lists every usable item you wear or carry (bags and containers left out), with where it sits and how many; it keeps the list for 10 seconds.

**Tested:** Lists the worn blade and the tonic in the bags; the bag itself and the ore are left out.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local game = require("eb.platform").game()
local list = game.UsableItems()
table.sort(list, function(a, b) return a.name < b.name end)
local parts = {}
for _, it in ipairs(list) do
    parts[#parts + 1] = it.name .. ((it.qty or 1) > 1 and (" x" .. it.qty) or "") .. " (" .. it.where .. ")"
end
print("usable: " .. table.concat(parts, ", "))
```

#### Snippet: Tab-complete a command line

reg:complete(line, opts) returns the words that could come next and the line advanced to them.

**Tested:** pau completes to pause; after "to" it offers box ids; an onoff argument offers on and off.

**The script:**

```lua
local cands, line = reg:complete("eb pau")               -- one candidate: the line gets the word and a space
print(line)
local boxes = reg:complete("eb to ", { who = { "is1", "is2", "is3" } })

local verbs = reg:complete("eb all fo")                  -- after a scope word: verbs only
```

#### Snippet: Build a button row from the registry

reg:view(filter) lists the shipped commands of a domain in schema order: an allow-list for a window.

**Tested:** The nav view lists follow; an alias finds its command; a fresh registry reports what is not wired yet.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local reg = assert(require("eb.registry").default({ root = ".", fresh = true }))
local buttons = {}
for _, row in ipairs(reg:view({ domain = "nav" })) do
    buttons[#buttons + 1] = { label = row.verb, line = "eb " .. row.verb, help = row.desc }
end
local row = reg:command("ah")                     -- a verb, an alias or a "<domain>.<verb>" id, any case
print(("ah -> %s"):format(row.id))
local byId = reg:command("NAV.FOLLOW")
local notWired = reg:unattached({ domain = "nav" })   -- a fresh registry: no handler attached yet
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
DOCS.check(labels.follow and labels.walk, "the nav row has follow and walk")
DOCS.eq(row.verb, "autohunt", "the alias found the command")
DOCS.eq(byId.verb, "follow", "an id finds it too, any case")
DOCS.eq(#notWired, #buttons, "nothing is wired in a fresh registry")
```

#### Snippet: A console word of your own

eb.console is the console window's model: register a word it answers itself, run lines, and read what a window draws - the newest row, the word list and this box's own row.

```lua
print(("%s | %s | words: %s"):format(rolled, ran, table.concat(words, ", ")))
```

#### Snippet: The window and monitor commands in this release

Types each window and monitor command on a booted EB and reads its answer: each opens its window through the window bridge (eb ui, eb mini, eb map, eb xp, eb track, eb radar, eb meters, eb crew, eb anal, eb mybutton), lists the kept workspaces (eb battlestation) or prints its readout (eb waiting, eb crew status); eb windows lists every window with the line that opens it. **Tested:** every window and monitor command is answered; eb windows lists every window with the line that opens it.

```lua
                "eb battlestation", "eb anal", "eb meters", "eb waiting", "eb crew", "eb crew status" }

local card = a.console("eb help meters")

```
