##### Snippet: Read the world snapshot

eb.world builds ONE plain table per frame from the game layer: you, your state and your group.

**Tested:** The snapshot has your name, class, archetype, zone, health and power, the fight flag and the group.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script

local world = require("eb.world").new({ game = game })
local snap = world.snapshot()
w.self.healthPct = 40                     -- the game moves on ...
local same = world.snapshot()             -- ... but inside one frame the snapshot is the same table
world.invalidate()                        -- rebuild the table (the game layer still answers this frame's reads)
local rebuilt = world.snapshot()
world.beginTick()                         -- a new frame: the game layer reads again, the snapshot is rebuilt
local fresh = world.snapshot()
print(("%s %s (%s) hp %d power %d fighting=%s group %d"):format(snap.name, snap.class, snap.archetype,
    snap.hpPct, snap.powerPct, tostring(snap.hated), snap.group.count))
```

##### Snippet: Effect names are server requests - never poll them

Me.Effect\[n\].ToEffectInfo.Name asks the SERVER whenever it is read. Reading it for every effect every frame floods the server; read the plain fields (ID, Type) per frame and look a name up once per new effect id.

**Tested:** Polling names directly costs a server request per effect per frame; the cached way costs one per effect, once.

**The script:**

```lua
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
w.world.effects = {
    { id = 9001, name = "Fixture Ward", type = "Beneficial", icon = 11 },
    { id = 9002, name = "Fixture Haste", type = "Beneficial", icon = 12 },
}

-- the WRONG way, shown once: 10 frames x 2 effects of name reads
w.world.stats.examine = 0
for _ = 1, 10 do IS.Parse("${Me.Effect[1].ToEffectInfo.Name}|${Me.Effect[2].ToEffectInfo.Name}") end
local polled = w.world.stats.examine

-- the right way: per frame only the plain id; a name is asked once per id never seen before
w.world.stats.examine = 0
local names = {}
for _ = 1, 10 do
    local n = tonumber(IS.Parse("${Me.CountEffects}")) or 0
    for i = 1, n do
        local id = IS.Parse("${Me.Effect[" .. i .. "].ID}")
        if names[id] == nil then names[id] = IS.Parse("${Me.Effect[" .. i .. "].ToEffectInfo.Name}") end
    end
end
print(("polling names: %d server requests; cached by id: %d"):format(polled, w.world.stats.examine))
```

**Offline lines:** the lines that use `DOCS`, `w.world` are EB's offline test world, which exists only where the example was tested: in a real script, leave them out or let the game do that part.

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check (in a real script use game.HasEffect / game.MyEffectNames: they already work this way, in one read a frame)
DOCS.eq(polled, 20, "a request per effect per frame")
DOCS.eq(w.world.stats.examine, 2, "one per effect, once")
DOCS.eq(names["9001"], "Fixture Ward", "the cache maps id to name")
```

##### Snippet: Stay inside the read budget

About 8 game reads a frame: Me, Target and Group come in a few batched reads; asking again is free.

**Tested:** One frame reading Me, Target and Group twice stays at or under 8 reads; the second round costs 0.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script

game.BeginTick()                                 -- EB's pulse does this at the start of every frame
local r0 = game.GameDataReads()
local me, target, group = game.Me(), game.Target(), game.Group()
local firstRound = game.GameDataReads() - r0
local again = game.GameDataReads()
game.Me(); game.Target(); game.Group()           -- the same frame: answered from the frame's memo
local secondRound = game.GameDataReads() - again
print(("first round: %d reads, second round: %d reads"):format(firstRound, secondRound))
```

##### Snippet: Drive EB's frames yourself

With no frame loop running, pulse.frame(now) runs one frame at a time: jobs on their interval, a task's wait, the stop flag and the cleanups - the way to test a helper offline, exactly.

**Tested:** Over 10 frames of 50 ms the 100 ms job runs 5 times and the task wakes after its 250 ms wait; stop then cleanup runs the onStop handler.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local P = require("eb.platform")
local pulse = P.pulse()
local said = {}
pulse.setLog(function(line) said[#said + 1] = line end)     -- the pulse's own messages, captured
pulse.bindEb(eb)                                             -- eb.delay waits on this pulse

local runs, doneAt, cleaned = 0, nil, nil
pulse.every("count", 100, function(now) runs = runs + 1 end)
pulse.spawn("wait-a-bit", function()
    eb.delay(250)                                            -- a wait is fine inside a task
    doneAt = P.now()
end)
pulse.onStop("my.helper", function(why) cleaned = why end)

local t = 0
P.clock().use(function() return t end)
for i = 1, 10 do t = i * 50; pulse.frame(t) end
pulse.stop("test over")
local stopping, why = pulse.stopping()
pulse.cleanup()
print(("job ran %d times, task done at %d ms, stopping: %s (%s)"):format(runs, doneAt, tostring(stopping), why))
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
-- offline stand-in: a world with NO frame loop of its own (pulse = false), so this script drives every frame
local w = DOCS.world({ pulse = false })
```

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(runs, 5, "a 100 ms job over 500 ms of frames")
DOCS.eq(doneAt, 300, "the task woke on the first frame after its wait")
DOCS.eq(cleaned, "test over", "cleanup ran the onStop handler with the reason")
DOCS.eq(pulse.otherRunning(t), false, "after cleanup no EB counts as running here")
DOCS.eq(#said, 0, "no job raised and no task ran slow")
```

##### Snippet: Time a mechanic from an announcement

Center-screen announcements arrive as the Announcement event with their text and timer; schedule your answer for just before the timer runs out.

**Tested:** The announcement's 6 s timer schedules the move for 1 s before it ends, and it fires then, not before.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local events = require("eb.events")
local P = require("eb.platform")
local due, moved

events.on("Announcement", function(ev)
    if ev.text:find("Ashen Storm", 1, true) and ev.timer then
        due = P.now() + (ev.timer - 1) * 1000            -- one second of margin
        print(("move at +%.1f s"):format(ev.timer - 1))
    end
end)
P.pulse().every("storm watch", 100, function(now)       -- a job: cheap, never waits
    if due and now >= due then moved, due = now, nil end
end)

local t0 = P.now()
w.host:fire("EQ2_onAnnouncement", "The Ashen Storm gathers!", "alert", 6)   -- offline: the game shows it
w.runFor(3000)
local early = moved
w.runFor(3000)
```

##### Snippet: A moment after this, if that follows

A rule with a delay and a follow-up gate: act only when a second line comes within the window ("require"), or only when it does NOT ("block").

**Tested:** The require rules act when their follow-up line arrives; the block rule acts only when its window passes quietly.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local Coord = require("eb.coord.rules")
local now = 0
local coord = Coord.new({ me = { box = "is1", name = "Fixturae", role = "healer" }, clock = function() return now end })
local did = {}
coord:onIntent(function(it) did[#did + 1] = it.ability end)

-- 1. "Beware", then 500 ms later, if "flames" is said within 3 s: ward the group
coord:add({ id = "ward", trigger = { kind = "chat", match = "Beware" }, delayMs = 500,
            gate = { kind = "chat", match = "flames", withinMs = 3000, mode = "require" },
            action = { kind = "cast", ability = "Fixture Ward" }, scope = "self" })
-- 2. "rumbles": stand still if "calms" follows within 2 s, dodge if it does not
coord:add({ id = "stand", trigger = { kind = "chat", match = "rumbles" },
            gate = { kind = "chat", match = "calms", withinMs = 2000, mode = "require" },
            action = { kind = "cast", ability = "Fixture Stand" }, scope = "self" })
coord:add({ id = "dodge", trigger = { kind = "chat", match = "rumbles" },
            gate = { kind = "chat", match = "calms", withinMs = 2000, mode = "block" },
            action = { kind = "cast", ability = "Fixture Dodge" }, scope = "self" })

coord:feed({ kind = "chat", text = "Beware the fixture!" })
now = 600; coord:tick()                                   -- the delay is up: the gate opens
coord:feed({ kind = "chat", text = "Fixture flames rise" })
local afterWard = #did

coord:feed({ kind = "chat", text = "The floor rumbles" })    -- this time the calm line follows
now = 1200; coord:feed({ kind = "chat", text = "The floor calms" })
now = 4000; coord:tick()
local afterCalm = #did

coord:feed({ kind = "chat", text = "The floor rumbles" })    -- and this time it does not
now = 7000; coord:tick()                                  -- the 2 s window passed quietly
print("casts in order: " .. table.concat(did, ", "))
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(afterWard, 1, "the ward went up when its follow-up line came")
DOCS.eq(afterCalm, 2, "the calm line let stand act and held dodge back")
DOCS.eq(did[3], "Fixture Dodge", "with no calm line, dodge acted when its window closed")
DOCS.eq(#did, 3, "nothing else acted")
```

##### Snippet: Dry-run an instance file

Run an instance with dry = true: every step reports what it would do and nothing is sent to the game - no walk, no door, no pull. Use it to check a new file before a real run.

**Tested:** The dry run completes, prints its would-do lines, and the world records no movement and no fight.

**The script:**

```lua
local INSTANCE = {
    schema = "eb.ic/1", zone = "Fixture Hollow", short = "fixture_hollow",
    hub = { zone = "fixture_docks", door = { actor = "a fixture rift", verb = "enter" } },
    route = {
        { id = "walk", act = "path", spots = { { 0, 0, 10 }, { 15, 0, 40 } } },
        { id = "n1", act = "encounter", name = "captain_fixturo" },
        { id = "exit", act = "zoneout", via = "exit" },
    },
}
local CAPTAIN = { schema = "eb.ic/1", name = "Captain Fixturo", kind = "named",
                  phases = { { id = "pull", do_ = { { target = { "Captain Fixturo" } }, { engage = "Captain Fixturo" } } } } }

local env, world = require("instances.lib.icworld").make({ alive = { ["Captain Fixturo"] = 100 } })
env.loadInstance = function() return INSTANCE end
env.loadEncounter = function() return CAPTAIN end

local runner = require("eb.ic").new(env)
local ok = runner:run(assert(runner:load("fixture_hollow")), { dry = true })
for _, l in ipairs(world.lines) do if l:find("would", 1, true) then print(l) end end
```

##### Snippet: Save a run and resume it at a step

runner:saveRun snapshots a configured run (file, difficulty, loop window, chores, a resume pointer = a route step id, and the reuse timer) as a plain record. Store it however you like; runner:resumeRun restores it and starts at the pointer.

**Tested:** The record round-trips through decode, and the resumed run starts at step n2: the first named is never fought again.

**The script:**

```lua
local INSTANCE = {
    schema = "eb.ic/1", zone = "Fixture Hollow", short = "fixture_hollow",
    route = {
        { id = "n1", act = "encounter", name = "first" },
        { id = "n2", act = "encounter", name = "second" },
    },
}
local ENC = {
    first = { schema = "eb.ic/1", name = "Captain Fixturo", kind = "named", phases = { { do_ = { { engage = "Captain Fixturo" } } } } },
    second = { schema = "eb.ic/1", name = "Mire Queen Fixtura", kind = "boss", phases = { { do_ = { { engage = "Mire Queen Fixtura" } } } } },
}

local env, world = require("instances.lib.icworld").make({ start = "copy", reuseNow = 900,
    alive = { ["Captain Fixturo"] = 100, ["Mire Queen Fixtura"] = 100 } })
env.loadInstance = function() return INSTANCE end
env.loadEncounter = function(_, name) return ENC[name] end
local runner = require("eb.ic").new(env)
local inst = assert(runner:load("fixture_hollow"))

-- save: a single run (loop = false) to resume at route step "n2"
local record = runner:saveRun({ inst = inst, name = "evening run", loop = false, pointer = "n2",
                                between = { tse = true } })
-- the record is plain data: write it off the game thread, read it back later
local SAVED = require("eb.ic.ic_saved").SAVED
local back = assert(SAVED.decode(record))

local ok, _, report = runner:resumeRun(inst, back)
for _, l in ipairs(world.lines) do if l:find("saved run", 1, true) then print(l) end end
```

**Offline lines:** the lines that use `require("instances.lib` are EB's offline test world, which exists only where the example was tested: in a real script, leave them out or let the game do that part.

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
DOCS.eq(record.schema, "eb.icsave/1", "the record's schema")
DOCS.eq(record.reuse.fixture_hollow, 900, "the reuse timer at save")
DOCS.eq(SAVED.reuseRemaining(record, "fixture_hollow", 600), 300, "10 minutes after a save at 0 s, 5 are left")
DOCS.check(ok, "the resumed run completes")
DOCS.eq(report.verdicts.n1, nil, "step n1 was before the pointer")
DOCS.eq(report.verdicts.n2, "killed", "the run resumed at n2")
DOCS.eq(world.attempts["Captain Fixturo"], nil, "the first named was never pulled")
```

##### Snippet: One route step of each kind

A route mixes camp spots, walks, clicks, waits, a wait for an actor's death, loot, an announce and the exit. Run one of each as the tank, then hand the same steps to a member's runner: it holds on every step that would move it, because only the tank walks the route and the tank's camp spots move the group.

**Tested:** The tank's lap runs every step in order and leaves by the exit; the member holds on path, campspot and interact.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script: the tank runs the lap
local IC = require("eb.ic")
local runner = IC.new(env)
local inst = assert(runner:load("fixture_hollow"))
local ok, why, report = runner:run(inst)
print("lap: " .. tostring(why))

-- a member's runner gets the same steps and holds (the step handlers can be called one at a time)
local menv = ICW.make({ tank = false, start = "copy" })
local member = IC.new(menv)
local mctx = member:newCtx(inst)
local _, onPath = member:stepPath(inst.route[2], mctx)
local _, onCamp = member:stepCampspot(inst.route[1], mctx)
local _, onClick = member:stepInteract(inst.route[3], mctx)
print("member on path: " .. onPath)
```

##### Snippet: Add your own route step kind

runner.STEP holds the route step handlers by act and runner.ROUTE_ACTS the acts a route file may carry (a step with an act in neither is refused when the file loads). Add one entry to each and a route step with that act loads and runs: here a "ring_gong" step that clicks a gong and waits for the room's door to open. A handler returns ok, a note for the log, and false stops the run with the note as the reason.

**Tested:** The custom step runs between the built-in ones and the lap completes; a gong that is not there stops the run with the handler's reason.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script: one entry in each table adds the act (they are shared by every runner: add it once, at start)
IC.ROUTE_ACTS.ring_gong = true                               -- the loader lets a route step with this act in ...
IC.STEP.ring_gong = function(runner, s, ctx)                  -- ... and this is what the runner does for it
    if not runner.combat.find(s.gong, { alive = true }) then return false, "no gong called " .. s.gong .. " here" end
    if ctx.opts.dry then return true, "would ring " .. s.gong end
    runner.nav.interact(s.gong, "ring")
    runner.sleep(1500)                                        -- every wait goes through the env's sleep
    return true, "rang " .. s.gong .. ", the door opened"
end

local function instance(gong)
    return {
        schema = "eb.ic/1", zone = "Fixture Hollow", short = "fixture_hollow",
        hub = { zone = "fixture_docks", entrance = { loc = { 0, 0, 0 }, tolerance = 8 },
                door = { actor = "a fixture rift", verb = "enter" } },
        route = {
            { id = "gong", act = "ring_gong", gong = gong },
            { id = "walk", act = "path", spots = { { 0, 0, 12 } } },
        },
    }
end

-- offline stand-in for the game
local ICW = require("instances.lib.icworld")
local env, world = ICW.make({ start = "copy", alive = { ["a fixture gong"] = 100 } })
env.loadInstance = function() return instance("a fixture gong") end
local runner = IC.new(env)
local ok, why = runner:run(assert(runner:load("fixture_hollow")))
for _, l in ipairs(world.lines) do if l:find("ring_gong", 1, true) then print((l:gsub("^%[ic%] ", ""))) end end

local env2 = ICW.make({ start = "copy" })
env2.loadInstance = function() return instance("a missing gong") end
local runner2 = IC.new(env2)
local ok2, why2 = runner2:run(assert(runner2:load("fixture_hollow")))
print("stopped: " .. tostring(why2))
```

**Offline lines:** the lines that use `require("instances.lib` are EB's offline test world, which exists only where the example was tested: in a real script, leave them out or let the game do that part.

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.


*The checks:*

```lua

DOCS.eq(world.did("interact"), 1, "the gong was rung once")
DOCS.eq(ok2, false, "a handler's false stops the run")
DOCS.has(why2, "no gong called a missing gong here", "with the handler's own reason")
IC.STEP.ring_gong = nil
IC.ROUTE_ACTS.ring_gong = nil
```

##### Snippet: Read a fight's sensors through the world facade

Every condition in an encounter reads through runner:worldFacade(): fight timers, a curable detriment, a chat or emote line since the pull, an item in the bags, an actor's type. Here each sensor is wired to a small fake and read directly, the way a custom fn = function(ctx) action reads ctx.w.

**Tested:** The timer counts from its reset, the detriment, emote and item sensors answer what the fakes hold, and the actor's type comes from the combat interface's row.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local runner = require("eb.ic").new(env)
local w = runner:worldFacade()
w.markFight()                                    -- the pull: the fight clock starts
world.clock = world.clock + 3000
w.resetTimer("adds")                             -- what the reset_timer action does
world.clock = world.clock + 12000
print(("adds timer: %d ms since reset_timer"):format(w.timerElapsed("adds")))
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
-- offline stand-in for the game: the combat and events interfaces the sensors read through
local ICW = require("instances.lib.icworld")
local env, world = ICW.make({ start = "copy", alive = { ["Overseer of Fixtures"] = 80 } })
env.combat.detriment = function(q) return q.type == "noxious" end                 -- a noxious curse is up
env.combat.hasItem = function(name) return name == "a fixture tonic" end
env.combat.find = function(name) return name == "Overseer of Fixtures" and { name = name, type = "NamedNPC" } or nil end
local heard = { { at = 0, text = "The Overseer of Fixtures roars: the floor will burn!" } }
env.events = { chatSeen = function(match, sinceMs)
    for _, l in ipairs(heard) do if l.at >= sinceMs and l.text:find(match, 1, true) then return true end end
    return false
end }
```

*The checks:*

```lua

DOCS.eq(w.timerElapsed("adds"), 12000, "a named timer counts from its reset")
DOCS.eq(w.timerElapsed(), 15000, "the default timer counts from the pull")
DOCS.check(w.detrimentPresent({ who = "group", type = "noxious" }), "a noxious detriment is on the group")
DOCS.check(not w.detrimentPresent({ type = "elemental" }), "no elemental one")

DOCS.check(not w.chatSeen({ match = "the walls close in" }), "a line that never came")
```

**Tested:** The T.S.E runs once, for every box, while the tank is still inside the cleared copy; the loop then ends after its one lap.

```lua
local inst = assert(runner:load("fixture_hollow"))
local ok, why, report = runner:loop(inst, { laps = 1, between = { tse = true, repair = true } })
```

##### Snippet: The runner's small helpers in a custom action

eb.ic.ic_base carries what every part of the runner uses: a log line in the runner's own voice, the flat distance doors and exits are measured with, the short countdown text and how often a long wait reports. Use them in an fn = function(ctx) action so your step reads like the runner's own.

**Tested:** The custom action logs one runner line with the distance to the lever and the countdown text.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script: a custom action, the kind an encounter's phase can hold as { fn = function(ctx) ... end }
local function leverCheck(ctx)
    local x, _, z = runner.nav.here()
    local d = base.flat(x, z, 3, 4)                          -- the lever stands at x = 3, z = 4
    local left = 5400                                        -- seconds a reuse timer has left
    base.say(runner, "lever is %.1f m away (flat); reset in %s, said every %d s", d, base.short(left), base.every(left))
    return true
end
leverCheck(runner:newCtx({ zone = "Fixture Hollow", short = "fixture_hollow", route = {} }))
print(world.lines[#world.lines])
```

```lua
local runner = require("eb.ic").new(env)
```

##### Snippet: Tell a stuck combat flag from a real fight

The game's in-combat flag can stay lit with nobody fighting. The combat hold's flag watch times that bare flag: HOLD.observe counts how long it has held, and after HOLD.STUCK_MS it is called stuck so a run never waits on it forever. A real fight between looks (HOLD.hated) starts the count over.

**Tested:** The bare flag is stuck after five seconds; a real fight in between resets the count.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script: one look a second at "in combat, nobody hated, nobody near"
local f = HOLD.newFlag()
local held = 0
for t = 0, 5000, 1000 do held = HOLD.observe(f, t, true) end
print(HOLD.stuckLine(held))

local st = HOLD.newState()
HOLD.observe(st.flag, 0, true)
HOLD.observe(st.flag, 4000, true)
HOLD.hated(st)                                        -- the group was seen in a real fight between looks
local after = HOLD.observe(st.flag, 5000, true)
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
local HOLD = require("eb.ic.ic_hold").HOLD
```

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(held, 5000, "the bare flag held five seconds")
DOCS.check(f.stuck, "and is called stuck")
DOCS.eq(after, 0, "a real fight in between starts the count over")
DOCS.eq(HOLD.observe(HOLD.newFlag(), 9000, false), 0, "a look that is not a bare flag counts nothing")
```

##### Snippet: Loop one instance: wait inside until it can be reset

runner:loop runs one instance again and again (until stopped by default; laps caps it here). Looping ONE zone, the tank waits out the reuse timer INSIDE the cleared copy where the run ended, then leaves by the exit door, resets the copy from outside and goes back in. The first lap is a rerun of the copy we stand in.

**Tested:** Two laps run; the 5-minute wait happens inside the copy, every reset is done from outside, and the loop ends with "laps done".

**The script:**

```lua
local INSTANCE = {
    schema = "eb.ic/1", zone = "Fixture Hollow", short = "fixture_hollow",
    hub = { zone = "fixture_docks", entrance = { loc = { 0, 0, 0 }, tolerance = 8 },
            door = { actor = "a fixture rift", verb = "enter" } },
    route = {
        { id = "n1", act = "encounter", name = "captain_fixturo" },
        { id = "exit.walk", act = "path", spots = { { 0, 0, -38 } } },
        { id = "exit", act = "zoneout", via = "exit" },
    },
    loop = { reset = "self", rerun_first = true },      -- the defaults: until stopped, first lap a rerun
}
local CAPTAIN = { schema = "eb.ic/1", name = "Captain Fixturo", kind = "named",
                  phases = { { do_ = { { engage = "Captain Fixturo" } } } } }

-- offline stand-in: we stand inside a copy we just cleared; it can be reset in 5 minutes, and 0 after each lap
local env, world = require("instances.lib.icworld").make({ start = "copy", reuseNow = 300, reuse = { 0, 0, 0 },
    alive = { ["Captain Fixturo"] = 100 } })
env.loadInstance = function() return INSTANCE end
env.loadEncounter = function() return CAPTAIN end

local runner = require("eb.ic").new(env)
local ok, why, report = runner:loop(assert(runner:load("fixture_hollow")), { laps = 2 })
for _, l in ipairs(world.lines) do if l:find("waiting INSIDE", 1, true) then print(l) end end

DOCS.check(ok, "the loop ended cleanly: " .. tostring(why))
DOCS.eq(why, "laps done", "after the two laps asked for")
DOCS.eq(report.laps, 2, "two laps")
DOCS.check(world.said("waiting INSIDE the cleared copy"), "the timer was waited out inside")
for _, c in ipairs(world.calls) do
    if c[1] == "reset" then DOCS.eq(c[3], "fixture_docks", "every reset is done from outside the copy") end
end
```

##### Snippet: Loop windows and the reset decision

eb ic loop \<file> \[minutes\] \[difficulty\]: no minutes (or 0) loops until stopped. parseLoopArgs splits the line, loopMinutes picks the window (the command line over the file's loop.max_minutes), and decide says what the tank does between laps: reset now, wait the timer out, or end because the wait outlasts the window.

**Tested:** The line splits into file, minutes and difficulty; the three decisions come out reset, wait and end.

**The script:**

```lua
local IC = require("eb.ic")
local a = assert(IC.parseLoopArgs("fixture_hollow 480 [Heroic I]"))
print(("%s for %d min at %s"):format(a.file, a.minutes, a.difficulty))
local forever = assert(IC.parseLoopArgs("fixture_hollow"))

DOCS.eq(a.minutes, 480, "minutes")
DOCS.eq(a.difficulty, "[Heroic I]", "the rest of the line is the difficulty")
DOCS.eq(forever.minutes, 0, "no minutes = 0 = until stopped")
DOCS.eq(select(2, IC.parseLoopArgs("")), IC.LOOP_USAGE, "an empty line answers the usage")
DOCS.eq(IC.loopMinutes({ loop = { max_minutes = 90 } }, {}), 90, "the file's window when the line names none")
DOCS.eq(IC.loopMinutes({ loop = { max_minutes = 90 } }, { minutes = 30 }), 30, "the line wins")
-- decide(seconds until the copy can be reset, minutes left in the loop; -1 = uncapped)
```

**Offline lines:** the lines that use `DOCS` are EB's offline test world, which exists only where the example was tested: in a real script, leave them out or let the game do that part.

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
DOCS.eq(IC.decide(0, 60), "reset", "the timer is up: reset now")
DOCS.eq(IC.decide(600, -1), "wait", "an uncapped loop waits out any timer")
DOCS.eq(IC.decide(7200, 30), "end", "a 2 h wait past a 30 min window ends the loop")
```

##### Snippet: Chores at the end of each run

A loop's between option turns chores on (all off by default): each box's saved T.S.E first, then a repair trip when this box's gear is under 90%, then the maintenance cycle. They run once at the END of each run, inside where it ended, and a chore that cannot be done is said and skipped - it never stops the loop.

**Tested:** After lap 1 the T.S.E ran and the gear at 62% was repaired; maintenance is unwired here, so it is skipped and said.

**The script:**

```lua
local INSTANCE = {
    schema = "eb.ic/1", zone = "Fixture Hollow", short = "fixture_hollow",
    route = { { id = "n1", act = "encounter", name = "captain_fixturo" } },
    loop = { rerun_first = false },                   -- the first lap runs where we stand
}
local CAPTAIN = { schema = "eb.ic/1", name = "Captain Fixturo", kind = "named",
                  phases = { { do_ = { { engage = "Captain Fixturo" } } } } }

local env, world = require("instances.lib.icworld").make({ start = "copy", alive = { ["Captain Fixturo"] = 100 },
    upkeep = { gear = 62 } })
env.loadInstance = function() return INSTANCE end
env.loadEncounter = function() return CAPTAIN end

local runner = require("eb.ic").new(env)
local ok, _, report = runner:loop(assert(runner:load("fixture_hollow")),
    { laps = 1, between = { tse = true, repair = true, maintenance = true } })
for _, l in ipairs(world.lines) do if l:find("gear at", 1, true) then print(l) end end

local chores = report.chores[1]
```

**Offline lines:** the lines that use `require("instances.lib` are EB's offline test world, which exists only where the example was tested: in a real script, leave them out or let the game do that part.

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
DOCS.check(ok, "the loop ends after its lap")
DOCS.eq(chores.tse, "done", "the saved T.S.E ran on every box")
DOCS.eq(chores.repair, "repaired", "gear under 90%: the repair trip")
DOCS.eq(chores.maintenance, "unwired", "no maintenance runner here: skipped, said, the loop goes on")
DOCS.eq(world.did("hall"), 1, "called to the guild hall once")
```

##### Snippet: The loops' own decisions: an upgrade and a hire

The chore loops keep their choices in small pure functions you can call yourself: the trainer's next upgrade comes from YOUR priority list (exact name first, then a part of a name, and it never guesses), and the mercenary pick takes the cheapest offer of the role you ask for.

**Tested:** The trainer picks the first listed upgrade it may spend on, refuses to pick with no list, and the healer pick is the cheapest healer.

**The script:**

```lua
local Trainer = require("eb.loops.trainer")
local Mercenary = require("eb.loops.mercenary")

local trainable = { { id = "t1", name = "Fixture Ward", kind = "training" },
                    { id = "t2", name = "Fixture Bloom", kind = "aa" } }
local pick = Trainer.pickNext(trainable, { "Fixture Bloom", "Fixture Ward" }, false)   -- AA spends not allowed
local withAA = Trainer.pickNext(trainable, { "Fixture Bloom", "Fixture Ward" }, true)
local none, why = Trainer.pickNext(trainable, {}, true)
print("next upgrade: " .. pick.name)

local offers = { { id = "k1", name = "a fixture guard", role = "tank", cost = 500 },
                 { id = "k2", name = "a fixture medic", role = "healer", cost = 400 },
                 { id = "k3", name = "a fixture nurse", role = "healer", cost = 350 } }
local hire = Mercenary.pickOffer(offers, "healer")
local wrong, whyRole = Mercenary.pickOffer(offers, "utility")
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
DOCS.eq(pick.id, "t1", "AA off: the first listed TRAINING upgrade")
DOCS.eq(withAA.id, "t2", "AA on: the list's own order decides")
DOCS.eq(none, nil, "no list: nothing is picked")
DOCS.has(why, "no train list", "the trainer never guesses an upgrade")
DOCS.eq(hire.id, "k3", "the cheapest healer")
DOCS.eq(wrong, nil, "never a wrong-role hire")
DOCS.has(whyRole, "utility", "it says which role was missing")
```

##### Snippet: Build a loop's provider and see what is missing

A chore loop acts through an activities provider: overseer, trainer, mercenary and city-writ drivers plus the economy's writs and collections. eb.loops.providers.build fills every verb you do not supply with a stub that says "needs a live window" the first time it is hit, so a loop runs end to end while you bring a driver up; gaps lists what is still missing.

**Tested:** The partial trainer driver validates as incomplete, the gaps list names its missing verbs, and a stubbed verb reports itself once.

**The script:**

```lua
local Providers = require("eb.loops.providers")
local Interface = require("eb.loops.interface")

-- a trainer driver that can only read points so far
local partial = { points = function() return { training = 2, aa = 0 } end }
local notes = {}
local provider = Providers.build({ trainer = partial, note = function(m) notes[#notes + 1] = m end })

local ok, missing = Interface.validate("trainer", partial)
local gaps = Providers.gaps({ trainer = partial })
local st, why = provider.trainer.train("t1")                    -- a stub: blocked, and it says so once
provider.trainer.train("t1")
print(notes[1])
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
DOCS.eq(ok, false, "the partial driver is not complete")
DOCS.check(#missing >= 5, "validate lists every missing verb")
DOCS.check(table.concat(gaps, " "):find("trainer.train", 1, true) ~= nil, "gaps names trainer.train")
DOCS.eq(provider.trainer.points().training, 2, "the real verb is kept")
DOCS.eq(st, "blocked", "a stubbed action reports blocked")
DOCS.has(why, "no trainer window", "with the reason")
DOCS.eq(#notes, 1, "and notes the gap once, not every tick")
```

##### Snippet: A chore loop's stop flag and coin gate

Every chore loop checks its stop predicate first, on every tick: when it answers true the goal ends at once, before any action. Coin-spending steps (the overseer's buy, a mercenary hire) run only behind an explicit flag. Drive a goal yourself by calling goal:advance(brain, snapshot) once per tick.

**Tested:** The stopped goal ends on its first tick with nothing done; the mercenary goal unsuspends a suspended merc and never hires without allowHire.

**The script:**

```lua
local Loops = require("eb.loops")

-- a minimal brain for driving a goal by hand: b.sub.* adapters, b:log, b:markPointer
local function brainStub()
    local b = { sub = { nav = { travelTo = function() return "arrived" end, walkTo = function() return "arrived" end } },
                logs = {}, cfg = {} }
    function b:log(fmt, ...) self.logs[#self.logs + 1] = select("#", ...) > 0 and fmt:format(...) or fmt end
    function b:markPointer() end
    return b
end
local snap = { zone = "Fixture Docks", x = 0, y = 0, z = 0 }

local touched = false
local stopped = Loops.new({ kind = "mercenary", params = { stop = function() return true end,
    act = { mercenary = { active = function() touched = true; return "none" end } } } })
local first = stopped:advance(brainStub(), snap)

local state, hired = "suspended", false
local merc = { active = function() return state end, contactNear = function() return true end,
               offers = function() return { { id = "k1", role = "healer", cost = 400 } } end,
               hire = function() hired = true; return "done" end,
               unsuspend = function() state = "active"; return "done" end, addFromBags = function() return "done" end }
local goal = Loops.new({ kind = "mercenary", params = { act = { mercenary = merc }, role = "healer" } })
local b, status = brainStub(), nil
for _ = 1, 10 do status = goal:advance(b, snap); if status ~= "working" then break end end
print("mercenary: " .. state .. " (unsuspended)")
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
DOCS.eq(first, "done", "a stop ends the goal on its first tick")
DOCS.eq(touched, false, "nothing was read or done")
DOCS.eq(status, "done", "the mercenary pass finishes")
DOCS.eq(state, "active", "the suspended merc was brought back (free, safe)")
DOCS.eq(hired, false, "no hire without params.allowHire")
DOCS.check(Loops.describeAll().overseer ~= nil, "describeAll explains every kind and its params")
```

##### Snippet: The overseer's daily pass, and how it picks agents

eb.overseer.plan picks by the game's own rules: the order (rescues, the tutorial, plain missions in list order, then charged ones by name), the skips (the day's allowance, the player's switches) and each party - an agent whose traits the mission likes first, an agent with a trait it dislikes never unless the player's option says so. The overseer goal (eb.loops) runs ONE whole pass a bite per tick over the window driver: open the window, read both lists, turn in what is done, start the plan, shut the window it opened. Buying spends coin: only with params.buy.

**Tested:** The plain mission goes first with the agent it likes, then the charged one with its own; the agent with the disliked trait stays home; the pass turns the finished mission in, starts both, buys nothing and ends "done".

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script: the plan on its own (the rows made into EB's shapes first)
local missions, agents = {}, {}
for _, r in ipairs(missionRows) do missions[#missions + 1] = Mo.mission(r, 0) end
for _, a in ipairs(agentRows) do agents[#agents + 1] = Mo.agent(a) end
local plan = Plan.make(missions, agents, Op.defaults(), { plainLeft = 10 })
print(("plan: %d start(s), %d agent(s) left"):format(#plan.starts, plan.left))

-- and the whole pass as the goal, driven by hand (in game the brain calls goal:advance once per tick) over a driver
-- that has the base verbs only: the turn-in and the start go through its composites (collect, assign)
local started, turnedIn, bought = {}, 0, false
local ov = {
    near = function() return true end, open = function() return "done" end,
    state = function() return { finished = 1, openSlots = 2, idleAgents = 3, scrolls = 0 } end,
    missions = function() return missionRows, { at = 0, complete = true } end,
    agents = function() return agentRows, { at = 0, complete = true } end,
    collect = function() turnedIn = turnedIn + 1; return "done" end,
    addScrolls = function() return "done" end, research = function() return "done" end,
    assign = function(key, agentKeys) started[#started + 1] = key .. ": " .. table.concat(agentKeys, ", "); return "done" end,
    buy = function() bought = true; return "done" end,
}
local b = { sub = {}, logs = {}, cfg = {} }
function b:log(fmt, ...) self.logs[#self.logs + 1] = select("#", ...) > 0 and fmt:format(...) or fmt end
function b:markPointer() end
local goal = Loops.new({ kind = "overseer", params = { act = { overseer = ov }, options = Op.defaults() } })
local status
for _ = 1, 40 do status = goal:advance(b, { zone = "Fixture Docks", now = 0 }); if status ~= "working" then break end end
```

##### Snippet: Writs and collections as chore loops

The errand loop runs tradeskill writs through the economy's writs pillar (walking to the station first when one is configured); the collections loop scribes every piece it already has, from the bags and the depot. Both are brain goals: each tick does one bite, and they end "done".

**Tested:** The writ run polls until the pillar says done; the collections pass scribes the pieces once and ends.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local errands = Loops.new({ kind = "errands", params = { act = { writs = writs }, mode = "tradeskill", count = 2 } })
local e = drive(errands)
local col = Loops.new({ kind = "collections", params = { act = { collections = collections }, scope = "fixture" } })
local c = drive(col)
print(b.logs[1])
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
local Loops = require("eb.loops")

-- a brain to drive goals by hand (in game EB's brain calls goal:advance once per tick)
local b = { sub = { nav = { travelTo = function() return "arrived" end, walkTo = function() return "arrived" end } },
            logs = {}, cfg = {} }
function b:log(fmt, ...) self.logs[#self.logs + 1] = select("#", ...) > 0 and fmt:format(...) or fmt end
function b:markPointer() end
local snap = { zone = "Fixture Docks", x = 0, y = 0, z = 0 }
local function drive(goal)
    local st
    for _ = 1, 20 do st = goal:advance(b, snap); if st ~= "working" then break end end
    return st
end

-- the providers (offline: the economy's two pillars, as recorders)
local writCalls = 0
local writs = { run = function(self, opts) writCalls = writCalls + 1; return writCalls < 3 and "working" or "done" end }
local filled = {}
local collections = { fill = function(self, scope, opts) filled[#filled + 1] = scope; return "done", { added = 4 } end }
```

```lua
DOCS.eq(c, "done", "the collections pass finished")
```

##### Snippet: A route's plan helpers: skipped steps, repeats, stalls, rates

The route planner is pure: firstOnFrom skips the steps a route switched off, repeatsAt says whether a back-and-forth step goes round again at this level, stallCheck notices a run that stopped making progress, and perHour turns a count into an hourly rate.

**Tested:** Step 2 is the first one on; the repeat holds below its target level; a quiet run stalls after its limit.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local first = plan.firstOnFrom(route, 1)
local again15 = plan.repeatsAt(route.steps[2], 15)
local again19 = plan.repeatsAt(route.steps[2], 19)
local clock, stalled = { seen = {} }, nil
plan.stallCheck(clock, 0, { kills = 12, xp = 40, zone = "Fixture Vale" }, 5)          -- the first look sets the clock
stalled = plan.stallCheck(clock, 301, { kills = 12, xp = 40, zone = "Fixture Vale" }, 5)
print(("30 kills in 20 minutes = %d per hour"):format(plan.perHour(30, 20)))
```

##### Snippet: A route's actions, one bite at a time

An actions step is a list of single actions; eb.plroutes.actions runs one per call and says where it is. A go in another zone hands the zone back as need_travel; a wait counts on the snapshot's clock; a click goes to the act adapter. resolveTarget and actionTarget say what a step or an action is about without running it.

**Tested:** The go asks for travel first, the wait finishes after its seconds, the click is done, and an instance step queues one run through the instance adapter.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script

local s1, z1 = A.runAction(go, snap, deps, {})
print("go: " .. s1 .. " " .. z1)
local wait, ws = { kind = "wait", secs = 3 }, {}
local w1 = A.runAction(wait, snap, deps, ws)
snap.now = 3000
local w2 = A.runAction(wait, snap, deps, ws)
local c = A.runAction({ kind = "click", actor = "Warden Fixturo", how = "doubleclick" }, snap, deps, {})
local target = runner.resolveTarget({ kind = "actions", actions = { go } }, 1)
local inst = A.instance({ route = { recovery = {} } }, snap, { kind = "instance", ic = "fixture_hollow" }, deps)
```

##### Snippet: Write long work as a pollable job

An economy Job cuts long work into steps and runs one bite per call: a step answers "stay" (still on it), "next" (move on), "done" (finish early) or "blocked" with a reason, and keeps its progress in job.mem. Call job:tick once per tick - from a pulse job is fine, a tick never waits - until it is no longer "working".

**Tested:** The three-step job reports working for each bite, then done; a step that raises ends the job as blocked instead of breaking the frame.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script: walk to the vendor, sell three items one per tick, close the window
local sold = 0
local job = Job.new("fixture-sell", {
    function(j, ctx) return ctx.atVendor and "next" or "stay" end,
    function(j, ctx)
        j.mem.i = (j.mem.i or 0) + 1                         -- this step's own scratch
        sold = sold + 1
        if j.mem.i < #ctx.items then return "stay" end
        return "next"
    end,
    function() return "done" end,
})
local ctx = { atVendor = false, items = { "a fixture cup", "a fixture plate", "a fixture fork" } }
local trace = {}
for t = 1, 10 do
    if t == 2 then ctx.atVendor = true end                  -- the walk arrives on the second tick
    local st = job:tick(ctx)
    trace[#trace + 1] = st
    if job:finished() then break end
end
print(("sold %d of %d, then: %s"):format(sold, #ctx.items, trace[#trace]))

local broken = Job.new("broken", { function() error("the vendor window closed") end })
local bst, bwhy = broken:tick({})
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua

```

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(trace[1], "working", "the first tick waits for the walk")
DOCS.eq(trace[#trace], "done", "the job ends done")
DOCS.eq(sold, 3, "one sale per tick")
DOCS.eq(job:tick(ctx), "done", "an extra tick after the end does not restart it")
DOCS.eq(bst, "blocked", "a step that raises ends the job")
DOCS.has(bwhy, "the vendor window closed", "with the error as its reason")
DOCS.eq(job:reset().i, 1, "reset starts it over at the first step")
```

##### Snippet: One job per request: call it every tick, it resumes

Job.gate keeps one live job per key on a table you own, so an action called every tick with the same request resumes its job instead of starting over, and a different key is a separate job. Job.live finds a running one without building, Job.clear drops them, and a stop flag on holder.env.stop ends a gated job at once.

**Tested:** Three calls advance the same job; a stop ends a second one as blocked; clear forgets them.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script: an action that is safe to call every tick
local stop = false
local pillar = { env = { stop = function() return stop end } }
local function restock()
    return Job.gate(pillar, "restock:food", function()
        return Job.new("restock", { function() return "next" end, function() return "next" end, function() return "done" end })
    end):tick()
end
local a, b, c = restock(), restock(), restock()
print(("restock: %s, %s, %s"):format(a, b, c))

local sweep = Job.gate(pillar, "sweep", function() return Job.new("sweep", { function() return "stay" end }) end)
sweep:tick()
local running = Job.live(pillar, "sweep")
stop = true
local st, why = sweep:tick()
```

##### Snippet: Sell the T.S.E pick at the merchant instead

tse:sell (the T.S.E of the economy EB builds for the box) resolves the pick from the bags by the T.S.E config (a names list and/or a set of tiers), takes each pick item's adornments off and keeps them, opens the merchant in reach, sells the pick item by item through the rules-gated item action, and closes the window. With no pick configured it sells nothing. Items the game has not told the type of are never in a pick.

**Tested:** The two picked items are sold after one adornment is reclaimed; an empty config refuses to sell anything.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script: EB builds the economy once per box; the T.S.E is eco.tse
local Economy = require("eb.economy")
local eco = Economy.new({ me = { name = "Sellbox" }, log = function() end, drive = game(),
    cfg = { tse = { names = { "a fixture bracer", "a fixture ring" }, unadorn = true } } })
local tse = eco.tse
local pick = tse:resolvePick({})
local status
for _ = 1, 8 do status = tse:sell({}); if status ~= "working" then break end end
print("sold: " .. table.concat(sold, ", "))
local none, why = Economy.new({ me = { name = "Sellbox" }, log = function() end, cfg = {},
    drive = { ["bags.items"] = function() return bags end } }).tse:sell({})
local kinds = {}
for _, row in ipairs(eco.ledger:rows()) do kinds[#kinds + 1] = Model.kinds[row.kind] end
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
local Model = require("eb.economy.ledgermodel")

-- offline stand-in for the game's side of the economy (every name invented)
local bags = {
    { id = 1, name = "a fixture bracer", type = "armor", qty = 1, value = 50 },
    { id = 2, name = "a fixture ring", type = "jewelry", qty = 1, value = 20 },
    { id = 3, name = "a keepsake fixture", type = "armor", qty = 1, value = 5 },
}
local adorns, sold, open = { [1] = { { slot = 1 } } }, {}, false     -- the bracer wears one adornment
local function nameOf(id) for _, b in ipairs(bags) do if b.id == id then return b.name end end end
local function game() return {
    ["bags.items"] = function() return bags end,
    ["adorn.on"] = function(id) return adorns[id] or {} end,
    ["adorn.remove"] = function(id) adorns[id] = nil; return "done" end,
    ["merchant.isOpen"] = function() return open end,
    ["merchant.near"] = function() return { name = "a Guild Commodities Exporter" } end,
    ["merchant.open"] = function() open = true; return "done" end,
    ["merchant.sell"] = function(id) sold[#sold + 1] = nameOf(id); return "done" end,
    ["merchant.close"] = function() open = false end,
} end
```

##### Snippet: Pick items from a list with a filter

filter.pick(list, spec) keeps the items that match every criterion you set (tiers, flags, a level band, a class, a name), and tells you why each other item was skipped. An exclude list is never matched.

**Tested:** Picks the two fabled items in the level band, never the excluded one, and says why the rest were skipped.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script: a bag list in EB's item shape (name, tier, level, flags ...)
local F = require("eb.economy.filter")
local bags = {
    { name = "Fixture Gauntlets", tier = "FABLED", level = 75 },
    { name = "Fixture Greaves", tier = "fabled", level = 78 },
    { name = "Fixture Mount Training Scroll", tier = "FABLED", level = 76 },
    { name = "Fixture Bracer", tier = "TREASURED", level = 76 },
    { name = "Fixture Helm", tier = "FABLED", level = 60 },
}
local spec = { tiers = { "fabled" }, minLevel = 70, maxLevel = 80, exclude = { "mount training" } }
local picked, skipped = F.pick(bags, spec)
local names = {}
for _, it in ipairs(picked) do names[#names + 1] = it.name end
print(("picked: %s; skipped %d"):format(table.concat(names, ", "), #skipped))
```


##### Snippet: The economy's bags-full check

```lua
local fullTen = c.bagsFull({ bagsFreeSlots = 10 })              -- a world snapshot answers without a read
print(("%d free: %s; 10 free: %s"):format(free, full and "full" or "not full", fullTen and "full" or "not full"))
```

##### Snippet: Clear junk without a vendor trip

The brain's junk() frees bag slots by rule: an item whose tier is in cfg.vendor.junkTiers is sold when a merchant window is open, destroyed otherwise. With no junk rule it does nothing at all and says "done". An item whose type or tier the game has not told is never junked.

**Tested:** Without a rule nothing moves; with the Junk tier listed the two junk stacks are destroyed and the good item stays.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script, part 1: no rule configured - fail-safe, nothing is touched
local W1 = Fake.world({ bags = bags() })
local eco1 = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = Fake.drive(W1), me = W1.me })
local first = eco1:contract().junk()
DOCS.eq(first, "done", "no junk rule: done at once")
DOCS.eq(#W1.log, 0, "and nothing was sent to the game")

-- part 2: the Junk tier is junk
local W2 = Fake.world({ bags = bags() })
local eco2 = require("eb.economy").new({ drive = Fake.drive(W2), me = W2.me,
    cfg = { vendor = { junkTiers = { Junk = true } } } })
local status
for _ = 1, 20 do
    status = eco2:contract().junk()
    if status ~= "working" then break end
end
print("junk destroyed: " .. #W2.log)
```

##### Snippet: Plan a bank deposit before you make it

eco.bank:deposit{ which, filter | items | bags | all, page, dry } puts bag items in the personal, shared or guild bank. dry = true answers the plan without moving anything: what would go and what stays, with the reason (a bag, a protected item, an account valuable, info not loaded). A guild deposit needs a page, 1 to 4.

**Tested:** The dry run keeps the bag, the protected charm and the training writ; the real deposit moves the ore.

```lua
for _, k in ipairs(plan.kept) do print("kept: " .. k.item.name .. " (" .. k.why .. ")") end
```

##### Snippet: Keep a set amount of coin on you

eco.bank:coin{ keepCopper = N } opens the bank and deposits what you carry over N, or withdraws the shortfall when you carry less. Coin is counted in copper: 100 copper = 1 silver, 100 silver = 1 gold, 100 gold = 1 platinum. ledgermodel.coin turns copper into the game's words ("4p 0g 0s 0c").

```lua
end
```


##### Snippet: Reprice your broker listings

eco.broker:targetPrice says what one listing should cost: the cheapest other seller's price minus cfg.broker.undercut copper (or equal to it with beatAll), never under the friends floor or the item's own price default. eco.broker:reprice() walks every listing of yours and sets each price, accepting it only when the window reads it back.

**Tested:** 1500 from another seller becomes 1495; a market at 1100 stops at the 1200 floor; the listing is repriced.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script: the price rule
local ore = { name = "Fixture Ore" }
DOCS.eq(eco.broker:priceFloor(ore), 1200, "the item's own price default")
DOCS.eq(eco.broker:targetPrice(ore, 2000, 1500), 1495, "undercut by 5")
DOCS.eq(eco.broker:targetPrice(ore, 2000, 1100), 1200, "never under the floor")
DOCS.eq(eco.broker:targetPrice(ore, 2000, nil), 2000, "no other seller: the price stays")

-- reprice every listing of mine
local status
for _ = 1, 20 do
    status = eco.broker:reprice()
    if status ~= "working" then break end
end
for _, line in ipairs(W.log) do print(line) end
```

##### Snippet: Record and read the money and item ledger

Every sell, deposit, transmute and loot EB does is one ledger line (eco.ledger:add), kept on the PC that wrote it. day(key) sums one day, last12() the last 12 hours, status() is this box's today in one line, and command(words) answers the same words eb ledger takes (status, day \<YYYY-MM-DD>, last12, clear \<day> | all).

**Tested:** Two sales (4 items) and a deposit (30 ore) are summed for the day; clearing the day removes its file.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local ledger = eco.ledger
ledger:add({ kind = "sell", item = "Fixture Pelt", qty = 3, cp = 60, where = "Merchant Fixtel" })
ledger:add({ kind = "sell", item = "Fixture Gem", qty = 1, cp = 10000, where = "Merchant Fixtel" })
ledger:note("depot", "Fixture Ore", { qty = 30, where = "a harvest depot" })
DOCS.check(not ledger:add({ kind = "gift", item = "Fixture Pelt" }), "a kind the ledger does not know is not written")

local today = Model.localDay(NOW)
local day = ledger:day(today)
print(Model.countsText(day.sums) .. " (" .. Model.coin(day.sums.cp) .. ")")
DOCS.eq(day.sums.cp, 10060, "the day's coin, in copper")
DOCS.eq(#day.rows, 3, "three lines")
DOCS.has(ledger:status().text, "4 sold", "this box's today (counted in items)")
local ok, text = ledger:command({ "day", today })
DOCS.check(ok and text:find("4 sold", 1, true), "the eb ledger words answer the same")
DOCS.eq(#ledger:last12(NOW).rows, 3, "all three are in the last 12 hours")
```

##### Snippet: See which window actions a drive provides

The economy works through a DRIVE: one table of window actions (bags.items, merchant.sell, depot.withdraw, ...). eb.economy.drive lists every action, checks a drive against the list, and fills the gaps with honest stubs: a missing read answers empty, a missing action answers "blocked" with what it still needs. eco:driveGaps() and eco:driveReport() say the same for a built economy.

**Tested:** A two-action drive is reported with the rest missing; a stubbed buy answers blocked with its reason.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script: a drive of your own that only knows the bags
local Drive = require("eb.economy.drive")
local mine = {
    ["bags.slots"] = function() return 12, 40 end,
    ["bags.items"] = function() return {} end,
    __drive = { name = "my bag reader", proven = { ["bags.slots"] = true },
                need = { ["merchant.buy"] = "the merchant window's Buy button" } },
}
print(Drive.signature("broker.setPrice"))
DOCS.eq(Drive.kind("bags.items"), "read", "a read")
DOCS.eq(Drive.kind("merchant.sell"), "action", "an action")

local ok, missing = Drive.validate(mine)
DOCS.check(not ok and #missing == #Drive.SPEC - 2, "everything but the two is missing")

local full = Drive.withFallback(mine)
local s, why = full["merchant.buy"]("Fixture Tonic", 1)
DOCS.eq(s, "blocked", "a missing action refuses")
DOCS.has(why, "the merchant window's Buy button", "with what it still needs")
DOCS.eq(#full["merchant.offers"](), 0, "a missing read answers empty")

local report = Drive.report(mine)
DOCS.eq(report.present, 2, "two present")
DOCS.eq(report.proven, 1, "one of them proven")
```


##### Snippet: Work out which recipe a work-order step asks for

eb.economy.writs.stripVerb drops the step's leading verb and its progress; resolve() then finds the recipe: a learned answer, a known spelling fix, the exact book name, a partial fix, the name without its article, and last a loose match only when exactly one recipe fits.

**Tested:** Each kind of step text resolves the way the rules say; two loose fits pick nothing; with no book read the text itself is tried once ("unverified").

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script (pure: give it the step text and the recipe book rows)
local Writs = require("eb.economy.writs")
local book = {
    { name = "Fixture Lantern" }, { name = "Fixture Spoon" }, { name = "Fixture Longbow" },
    { name = "Fixture Ladle" },
}
local function show(text, learned)
    local recipe, how = Writs.resolve(text, book, learned)
    print(("%-38s -> %s (%s)"):format(text, tostring(recipe), how))
    return recipe, how
end
print(Writs.stripVerb("I need to create Fixture Lantern (0/6)"))
local r1, h1 = show("Create Fixture Lantern (0/6)")
local r2, h2 = show("Craft Fixture Long Bow")               -- a partial spelling fix: Long Bow -> Longbow
local r3, h3 = show("I need to create a Fixture Spoon")     -- the article comes off
local r4, h4 = show("Make Lantern")                         -- a loose match: exactly one recipe fits
local r5, h5 = show("Make Fixture L")                       -- two fit (Lantern, Ladle): none is picked
local r6, h6 = show("Make the odd thing", { ["the odd thing"] = "Fixture Ladle" })   -- learned last time
local r7, h7 = Writs.resolve("Create Fixture Bowl", nil)     -- the book did not read
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

##### Snippet: Read a skill value the way EB does

eb.economy.skills turns the game's skill text into cur / max, takes a temporary bonus off, works out the cap your levels allow, and names the state: notlearned, unreadable, level or done. Unknown is never 0.

**Tested:** The colour code is stripped (354/400, 18/560), junk does not parse, a +25 bonus comes off 57/425, the cap from levels 80 and 90 is 450, and each state comes out as the rules say.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script (pure)
local Skills = require("eb.economy.skills")
local a = Skills.parse("\\#FFFFFF354/400")          -- the game's text: a colour code, then cur/max
local b = Skills.parse("\\#22FF2218/560")           -- 18/560, not 2218/560
local junk = Skills.parse("NULL")
print(("%d/%d and %d/%d"):format(a.cur, a.max, b.cur, b.max))

local boosted = Skills.withoutBonus({ ok = true, cur = 57, max = 425 }, 400)   -- a +25 buff raised both numbers
local cap = Skills.capFromLevels(80, 90)                                       -- 5 x the higher level
local states = {
    Skills.stateOf(false, { ok = true, cur = 0, max = 400 }),     -- reads 0 and nobody said it is learned
    Skills.stateOf(true, { ok = false }),                         -- learned, but the read failed
    Skills.stateOf(false, { ok = true, cur = 12, max = 400 }),
    Skills.stateOf(false, { ok = true, cur = 400, max = 400 }),
}
print("states: " .. table.concat(states, ", "))
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(a.cur + a.max, 754, "354/400")
DOCS.eq(b.cur, 18, "the colour code came off first")
DOCS.eq(junk.ok, false, "junk does not parse")
DOCS.eq(boosted.cur .. "/" .. boosted.max, "32/400", "the bonus came off both numbers")
DOCS.eq(cap, 450, "the cap from levels")
DOCS.eq(table.concat(states, ","), "notlearned,unreadable,level,done", "the four states")
```

##### Snippet: The levelling decisions, step by step

eb.economy.skilllevel's pure rules: decide() says where a run starts (learn, unreadable, done, book or level); afterRound() says what a finished round comes to (done, again, buy, book or giveup); for Adorning, mostStockedTier() and roundFromStock() plan a round from what is on hand.

**Tested:** Each case answers as the rules say; the best-stocked Adorning tier is 2 and a round dilutes 5 and distils 4.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script (pure)
local L = require("eb.economy.skilllevel")
local r = function(cur, max) return { ok = true, cur = cur, max = max } end
local starts = {
    L.decide({ learned = false, read = { ok = false } }),                     -- never learned
    L.decide({ learned = true, read = { ok = false } }),                      -- learned, does not read
    L.decide({ learned = true, read = r(100, 100) }),                         -- capped
    L.decide({ learned = true, read = r(10, 100), bandBooksInBags = true }),  -- scribe the band's books first
    L.decide({ learned = true, read = r(50, 100), bookDone = true }),         -- craft the band's rows
}
print("starts: " .. table.concat(starts, ", "))
local again = L.afterRound({ before = r(10, 100), after = r(14, 100) })
local done = L.afterRound({ before = r(97, 100), after = r(100, 100) })
local short = L.afterRound({ before = r(10, 100), after = r(10, 100), missing = true, tripsNoGain = 3 })
local stuck = L.afterRound({ before = r(10, 100), after = r(10, 100), noGain = 1, secs = 300, tierTried = true })
print(("after a gain -> %s; capped -> %s; short -> %s; stuck -> %s"):format(again, done, short, stuck))

local tier = L.mostStockedTier({ { tier = 1, powders = 2, fragments = 30 }, { tier = 2, powders = 5, fragments = 10 } })
local plan = L.roundFromStock(5, 10, 6)
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(table.concat(starts, ","), "learn,unreadable,done,book,level", "where a run starts")
DOCS.eq(again, "again", "a gain goes again")
DOCS.eq(done, "done", "capped is done")
DOCS.eq(short, "giveup", "short of materials after 3 trips with no gain gives up")
DOCS.eq(stuck, "giveup", "two rounds with no gain give up")
DOCS.eq(tier, 2, "the tier with the most worth on hand")
DOCS.eq(plan.dilute .. "/" .. plan.distil, "5/4", "dilute 5 powders, distil 4")
```

##### Snippet: Strip old gear's adornments, keep temporary adornments up

eco.adornments:unadorn{ tiers } takes the adornments off bag items of those tiers (a protected item is never touched); tempAdorns(profile, { active = fn(slot) }) re-applies only the slots whose temporary adornment is no longer on.

**Tested:** The old vest's rune comes back into the bags and the protected treasure keeps its adornment; with the chest's temporary adornment still on, only the legs are applied; with every slot on, nothing is done.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local stripped = CW.poll(function() return eco.adornments:unadorn({ tiers = { FABLED = true } }) end)
local temp = { chest = "Fixture Flare", legs = "Fixture Spark" }
local still = CW.poll(function()
    return eco.adornments:tempAdorns(temp, { active = function(slot) return slot == "chest" end })
end)
local allOn = eco.adornments:tempAdorns(temp, { active = function() return true end })
```

##### Snippet: How EB scores a piece of gear

eco.gearup:score(item, role) ranks Resolve first, then Fervor, then Potency, then the role's main stat (fighter stamina, priest wisdom, mage intelligence, scout agility), then any weights you set in cfg.gear, with item level only breaking a tie. roleOf(me) is the character's archetype.

**Tested:** One point of Resolve outweighs any Fervor, Fervor outweighs Potency, a priest prefers wisdom, and a configured weight counts too.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local role = eco.gearup:roleOf()
local s = function(stats, ilvl) return eco.gearup:score({ stats = stats, ilvl = ilvl or 0 }, role) end
local resolve, fervor, potency = s({ resolve = 1 }), s({ fervor = 999 }), s({ potency = 999 })
local wisdom, stamina = s({ wisdom = 50 }), s({ stamina = 50 })
print(("role %s: resolve > fervor > potency > wisdom"):format(role))
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.


*The checks:*

```lua

DOCS.check(resolve > fervor and fervor > potency and potency > wisdom, "the strict order")
DOCS.check(wisdom > stamina, "a priest's main stat is wisdom")
DOCS.check(s({ haste = 10 }) > s({}), "a configured weight counts")
DOCS.check(s({ wisdom = 50 }, 90) > s({ wisdom = 50 }, 80), "item level breaks a tie")
```

##### Snippet: Turn Master scrolls into Grandmaster crafts

eco.grandmasters:plan(opts) lists each "(Master)" scroll in the bags (and, with depot = true, in the Scroll Depot) whose "(Grandmaster)" recipe is in your book; run(opts) only previews until you pass go = true, because every craft consumes a scroll.

**Tested:** Three scrolls can become Grandmaster crafts (one from the Scroll Depot), one is skipped with no recipe; without go nothing is made; with go all three are crafted.

```lua
local _, preview = eco.grandmasters:run({ depot = true })            -- no go: a preview, nothing consumed

local status = CW.poll(function() return eco.grandmasters:run({ depot = true, go = true }) end)
print(("plan: %d crafts, %d skipped; preview made %d; go made %d"):format(#plan.crafts, #plan.skipped, before, #world.made))
```

##### Snippet: Answer the economy's commands from your own economy

eb.economy.commands attaches the economy's command handlers to a registry for an economy you built: rows() are the command rows it needs, handlers(eco) the handler table, attach(reg, eco) declares any row the registry lacks and attaches every handler.

**Tested:** After attach, "eb tse" runs the economy's bulk transmute and is refused with its reason (no T.S.E is set up, so the pick names nothing), and "eb tse give" is understood and asks for the leader's name.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local Commands = require("eb.economy.commands")
local ids = {}
for _, row in ipairs(Commands.rows()) do ids[#ids + 1] = row.id end
local ok, why = Commands.attach(reg, eco)
local okT, text = reg:dispatch("eb tse")
print(("eb tse -> %s: %s"):format(tostring(okT), text))
local okG, textG = reg:dispatch("eb tse give")
```


```lua
for _, id in ipairs(ids) do have[id] = true end

```

##### Snippet: Drive the clock in a test

clock.use hands EB's clock a source you step; the clock never runs backwards - when its source steps back it holds - and seconds() is the same clock.

**Tested:** 1000, then 1000 again when the source steps back, then 3000; P.now() reads the same clock.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script: a clock you step by hand
local P = require("eb.platform")
local clock = P.clock()
local t = 1000
clock.use(function() return t end)
local a = clock.now()
t = 500                                     -- the source jumps back (a clock was set)
local b = clock.now()                       -- EB's clock holds
t = 2500
local c = clock.now()                       -- and moves on from where it held
print(("now %d -> %d (source stepped back) -> %d"):format(a, b, c))
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
-- offline stand-in for the game (only the docs runner has DOCS; in game the world is real)
local w = DOCS.world()
```

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(b, a, "never backwards")
DOCS.eq(c, 3000, "it carries on by the source's own steps")
DOCS.eq(P.now(), c, "P.now() is the same clock")
DOCS.eq(clock.seconds(), 3, "seconds() is now() / 1000")
local stamp = clock.wall()
DOCS.check(stamp == nil or type(stamp) == "number", "wall() is a number of seconds, or nil")
```

##### Snippet: Test a helper's saves without a disk

ebkit.files.memory is a files host over a table: give it to a helper's save function in a test and read back exactly what it wrote - including a failed write.

**Tested:** The save lands in the table, list and copy work on it, a forced failure is reported, and the platform's own host answers isDir and probeNative.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script: a helper's save, written against any files host
local function save(fs, state)
    return fs.write("notes/helper.json", ('{"kills":%d}'):format(state.kills))
end

local F = require("ebkit.files")
local disk = {}
local mem = F.memory(disk)                 -- in game: require("eb.platform").files()
save(mem, { kills = 3 })
local names = mem.list("notes", "*.json")
mem.copy("notes/helper.json", "notes/helper.json.old")
mem.failNext = "disk full"
local ok, why = save(mem, { kills = 4 })
print(("saved %d file: notes/%s; backup made; a failed save says: %s"):format(#names, names[1], why))
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.


*The checks:*

```lua

DOCS.check(mem.exists("notes/helper.json.old"), "copy made the backup")
DOCS.eq(ok, false, "the forced failure is reported")
DOCS.eq(mem.writes, 1, "only the good save counted")

DOCS.check(fs.isDir("notes") ~= true, "the real host has no such folder offline")
```

##### Snippet: Change one field in a JSON file another program owns

ebkit.json reads losslessly: change one value, write it back, and the rest stays exactly as it was spelled.

**Tested:** Only the edited value changes; a number spelled 1.50 and a key the script never touched come back the same.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local J = require("ebkit.json")
local file = '{\n  "scale": 1.50,\n  "theme": "bw",\n  "volume": 0.5\n}'
local doc = assert(J.read(file))
J.set(doc, "volume", J.num(0.8))                 -- numbers are kept as their text: J.num makes a new one
local out = J.write(doc)
print(out:match('"volume": [%d.]+'))
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.has(out, '"scale": 1.50', "an untouched number keeps its spelling")
DOCS.has(out, '"theme": "bw"', "an untouched string too")
DOCS.eq(J.tonum(J.get(doc, "volume")), 0.8, "the edited value")
DOCS.eq(J.write(assert(J.read(file))), file, "read and written with no edit, the file comes back byte for byte")
DOCS.eq(table.concat(J.keys(doc), ","), "scale,theme,volume", "the keys in file order")
```

##### Snippet: Save from game code without touching the disk in the frame

files.writeLater(path, text) only queues; a pulse job writes one file per slot, newest text wins.

**Tested:** Ten quick saves of the same file coalesce into one write that lands on the next flush, with the last text.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local files = P.files()
for i = 1, 10 do
    files.writeLater("helper/kills.json", '{"kills":' .. i .. '}')     -- from a job or a handler: just a queue
end
local pendingBefore = files.pending()
w.runFor(600)                                                          -- a couple of flush slots go by
print(("%d write for %d saves"):format(files.stats.writes, 10))
```

**Offline lines:** the lines that use `w.runFor` are EB's offline test world, which exists only where the example was tested: in a real script, leave them out or let the game do that part.

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
-- offline stand-in: the platform's files service over a disk in a table, and the flush job EB's boot runs for you
local w = DOCS.world()
local disk = require("data.lib.memdisk").install()
local P = require("eb.platform")
P.pulse().every("files", 250, function() P.files().flush(1) end, { prio = 90 })
```

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(pendingBefore, 1, "one queued file, not ten")
DOCS.eq(files.stats.coalesced, 9, "nine saves folded into the first")
DOCS.eq(files.stats.writes, 1, "one write")
DOCS.eq(disk["helper/kills.json"], '{"kills":10}', "the newest text won")
```

##### Snippet: Keep a helper's own config in a JSON file

Read your helper's file once at start, keep it in a table, and queue a save when it changes.

**Tested:** The config loads with defaults for missing keys; a change is saved by the next flush, not in the frame.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local J = require("ebkit.jsontable")
local PATH = "helper/lowhp.json"
local DEFAULTS = { threshold = 50, announce = true }
local function load()
    local cfg = {}
    local text = P.files().read(PATH)                  -- once, at start: never on every frame
    local doc = text and J.decode(text) or {}
    for k, v in pairs(DEFAULTS) do cfg[k] = (doc[k] ~= nil) and doc[k] or v end
    return cfg
end
local function save(cfg) P.files().writeLater(PATH, assert(J.encode(cfg))) end

local cfg = load()
cfg.threshold = 35
save(cfg)
w.runFor(300)
print(("threshold %d, saved %s"):format(cfg.threshold, disk[PATH]))
```

**Offline lines:** the lines that use `w.runFor` are EB's offline test world, which exists only where the example was tested: in a real script, leave them out or let the game do that part.

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
-- offline stand-in: the platform's files service over a disk in a table, and the flush job EB's boot runs for you
local w = DOCS.world()
local disk = require("data.lib.memdisk").install({ ["helper/lowhp.json"] = '{"threshold":40}' })
local P = require("eb.platform")
P.pulse().every("files", 250, function() P.files().flush(1) end, { prio = 90 })
```

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(load().threshold, 35, "the saved value reads back")
DOCS.eq(load().announce, true, "a key missing from the file takes its default")
DOCS.eq(disk[PATH], '{"announce":true,"threshold":35}', "the file on disk")
```

##### Snippet: Print numbers the same way everywhere

eb.compat.numstr prints 3 and 3.0 both as "3"; format and sortedkeys keep output stable on every target.

**Tested:** Whole numbers print without .0, %d takes a fractional number, and keys come out in one stable order.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local compat = require("eb.compat")
print(("%s | %s | %s"):format(compat.numstr(3.0), compat.numstr(2.5), compat.format("hp %d", 64.0)))
local keys = compat.sortedkeys({ zone = 1, [2] = "b", name = 2, [1] = "a" })
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(compat.numstr(3.0), "3", "an integral float prints as an integer")
DOCS.eq(compat.format("%d", 3.7), "3", "%d truncates instead of raising")
DOCS.eq(compat.toint(-3.7), -3, "toint truncates toward zero")
DOCS.check(compat.isint(3.0) and not compat.isint(3.5), "isint")
DOCS.eq(table.concat(compat.sortedkeys({ b = 1, a = 2 }), ","), "a,b", "strings in order")
DOCS.eq(keys[1], 1, "numbers first, then strings")
DOCS.eq(keys[4], "zone", "the last key")
```

##### Snippet: One JSON string, and the key order files use

ebkit.json.quote writes one string exactly as the codec does; ebkit.json.less is the key order every EB file is written in, so a file reads the same on every computer.

**Tested:** Quotes, backslashes and newlines are escaped; keys sort by their bytes (capitals first).

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local J = require("ebkit.json")
local q = J.quote('say "hi"\n')
local keys = { "b", "a", "B" }
table.sort(keys, J.less)
print(("%s | %s"):format(q, table.concat(keys, " ")))
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(q, '"say \\"hi\\"\\n"', "the escaped string")
DOCS.eq(keys[1], "B", "a capital sorts first")
DOCS.check(not J.less("a", "a"), "a key is not before itself")
```

##### Snippet: A JSON null, and Lua values as text

ebkit.jsontable.null keeps a JSON null through a round trip; ebkit.lua_fmt.encode writes any value as a Lua literal, and ident says whether a key can be written bare.

**Tested:** The null survives encode and decode; a table becomes a Lua literal with bare and bracketed keys.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local J = require("ebkit.jsontable")
local F = require("ebkit.lua_fmt")
local text = J.encode({ gone = J.null })
local back = J.decode(text)
local lua = F.encode({ one = 1, ["two words"] = 2 })
print(("%s | %s"):format(text, (lua:gsub("%s+", " "))))
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(back.gone, J.null, "decode gives the same null back")
DOCS.check(F.ident("one"), "a plain name is written bare")
DOCS.check(not F.ident("two words"), "a key with a space needs brackets")
DOCS.has(lua, '["two words"] = 2', "the bracketed key")
DOCS.eq(load("return " .. lua)().one, 1, "the text loads back as the same table")
```

##### Snippet: Ability names, line keys and stable files

eb.exports.util holds the naming rule EB uses everywhere for "the same ability line" - the name without its rank, lower case - and a serializer that writes the same table to the same text every time, so a saved export diffs cleanly and reads back in an empty sandbox. b64encode makes any text one clean word for a transport.

**Tested:** Every rank of the heal shares one line key; a table round-trips through serialize and deserialize; base64 round-trips.

**The script:**

```lua
-- your script
local name = "Fixture Mend IV"
print(("%s -> line '%s', rank %d"):format(name, util.lineKey(name), util.levelOf(name)))
local saved = util.serialize({ b = 2, a = { 1, 2, 3 }, note = "kept" })
local back = assert(util.deserialize(saved))
local word = util.b64encode("a line, with commas")
```

**How it was tested:** EB ran this whole file on its offline stand-in for the game and checked the result. Both exist only there.

*The offline stand-in for the game:*

```lua
local util = require("eb.exports.util")
```

*The checks:*

```lua
-- check
DOCS.eq(util.lineKey("Fixture Mend"), util.lineKey(name), "every rank shares the line key")
DOCS.eq(util.baseName(name), "Fixture Mend", "the name without its rank")
DOCS.eq(util.romanValue("XII"), 12, "a Roman numeral")
DOCS.eq(util.romanValue("Mend"), nil, "a word that is not one")
DOCS.eq(saved, util.serialize({ note = "kept", a = { 1, 2, 3 }, b = 2 }), "the same table writes the same text")
DOCS.eq(back.a[3], 3, "and reads back")
DOCS.eq(util.deserialize("os.exit()"), nil, "text that is not a table does not run as a script")
DOCS.check(not word:find(","), "base64 is one clean word")
DOCS.eq(util.b64decode(word), "a line, with commas", "and reads back")
```

### Lua library: Core modules

#### Module `commands.accounts`

Console commands for your characters: the roster, the mercenary, hirelings, a new character, the daily chores runner, and logging in and launching game sessions.
