Type them as eb \<command> in the console, send them to the crew with eb all | others | to \<who> \<command>, or run them from a script with reg:dispatch. login and launch are EB for InnerSpace's. roster, hirelings, createchar, login and launch are for this box only.

**File:** `data/eb/commands.json` in the EB folder

- `eb roster [list|status|account|window]`: Your characters, from EB's own sources: list shows this PC's boxes in their order (the lead marked) and every other character EB has seen, with class and level; status shows who is online now and where; account reads the game's own list of the characters on the account this box is logged into; window opens the Roster window.
- `eb features [what]`: The account's features - its unlocked expansions and membership unlocks - for the character on this box, in plain words: the expansions it has, the unlocks tied to no zone (a membership unlock, a pack EB's data has no zones for), the expansions it lacks, and its flags (a key your other bot keeps, such as a guild hall teleporter's friends and family unlock). Every trip uses what is kept: a zone of an expansion the account lacks is planned around and the trip says why ("needs Rise of Kunark - not on this account"); a trip to such a zone stops at once and says so.
- `eb membership [nonmember]`: This character's membership level, as the game's own Persona window shows it (All Access, Free ...), said on this box's console with what it means (a member, not a member). eb all membership asks every box: each says its own on its own console.
- `eb mercenary [cmd] [query]`: Your mercenary: summon it (one merely suspended comes back), check its buffs, status; suspend the one that is up; list shows your roster as the Persona window lists it (the current one first, each one's class, suspended or restricted said); summon \<words> brings up the one mercenary those words fit (its name, class or kind) when none is up; swap \<words> puts the one that is up away first, waits the game's minute and brings that one up. Several fitting, none fitting or a restricted one: said, nothing sent. EB never dismisses or hires one from a contact (dismiss says so).
- `eb hirelings [cmd] [band]`: The guild hall's harvest hirelings (gatherer, miner, hunter), visited in turn while you stand in your guild hall: run takes what each brought back and sends it out again, collect only takes back, send only sends out, status says what each did last, the level groups it offered and when it is due back. look walks to each one, hails it and reads its state and the levels it offers, pressing only its way out - nothing taken, nothing sent - then says which of them are in sight, the band, each one's own switches, the deposit and the auto visit (out of the hall: what each did last, no walk); stop ends a visit under way; band \<level> keeps the band every visit sends them out at, band \<hireling> \<level> that one's own (same: back to every visit's; the line's own band still comes first); send \<hireling> on or off: whether a visit sends that one out (off: what it brought is still taken, it is left in); deposit on or off: after a visit the harvest goes in the hall's Harvesting Supply Depot (on unless set off); auto on or off: a visit every 2 hours 1 minute while this box is idle in its guild hall.
- `eb createchar [spec]`: Help making a new character: with nothing after it, the steps at character select and what EB does once the character exists; with a class (and a race), the class checked against the game's own and its archetype.
- `eb tasks [run|status|list]`: This character's chores in one place: the chore loops EB has (the overseer's daily round, errands and writs, the trainer, the mercenary, the collections turn-in) and the task lists made in the Tasks window. status says how each stands and what it needs on this box; list adds the task lists; run starts the overnight chores.
- `eb tasklist [cmd] [name]`: Run a task list of the Tasks window whole on this box, step after step: a quest line (until it ends), an instance run (until it ends), a command (and the chore it starts), a wait. Stop it, see where it is, or list this character's lists. Run a list by itself on login, on a zone-in or every few hours; say the levels a list is for; pick up a list EB went down in the middle of.
- `eb login [what]`: EB for InnerSpace: log this session in from your saved logins - the box its launch named, or the box you name. With no word it says where the login is. boxes lists the box list (boxes save writes it in your logins' order); check reads the login form and types nothing.
- `eb launch [what]`: EB for InnerSpace: open game sessions that log themselves in - one box, every box of the box list, or a whole team you set up in your multiboxing tool (set \<team>). A window goes where you say (on x,y,w,h), else where the game puts it; avoid-primary keeps it off the main monitor.
- `eb persona [cmd] [arg]`: Persona - one character, several classes. open (the bare form) opens the Persona window; \<class> (or as \<class>) changes the class of the character in the world through the game's own Persona window, the class it leaves keeping what it wears first; status says the classes this character is known in (each with its level), the cast-stack profile each one loads and why, the gear kept for each, and the switches. rules lists the profile rules, numbered; rule \<server | all> \<class> \<file> says which profile file a class loads on one server or on every server (the server by its name or a short form - the first letters of its words, or the start of its name when only one server fits), rule ... clear removes it; char \<class> \<file> is this character's own rule on this server and wins over every class rule. remove \<n> takes a rule away, fix \<n> does the same and opens the Cast Stack window, later puts the Profile not found view away. gear save | restore | clear \[\<class> | all\] keeps what a class wears, puts it back on from the bags, or forgets it (nothing is taken off); bags \<digits> are the bags that hold persona gear (all: every bag); noswap on | off is Do not swap gear when changing personas; adorn on | off switches Move adornments onto bare gear (on to start), adorn recheck does the same for the gear worn now, adorn stop (or stop) ends the persona chore under way.
- `eb autologin [cmd] [rest]`: Launch profiles: named lists of boxes to log in, kept in the box list's own file on this PC (a row names a box, nothing secret). list (the bare form) names them; show \<name> its rows; dry \<name> says what start would do and does nothing; start \<name> opens this PC's rows, one session a pause apart; save makes one; set picks a PC's character set of your multiboxing tool; delete removes one; shortcut says how to make a shortcut that starts it from Windows.

#### Module `commands.broker`

Console commands for the broker and buying: price your listings, buy an item or the best upgrade, the shopping list, spell upgrades, and collections.

Type them as eb \<command> in the console, send them to the crew with eb all | others | to \<who> \<command>, or run them from a script with reg:dispatch or eb.dispatch. EB runs the economy behind them, so each one answers with a status line, a chore under way or a refusal in plain words. The Lua behind them is eb.economy.broker (reprice, buy, buyBest, buyMasters, listFromBags, addFromInventory) and eb.economy.vendor (merchant buys). Every buy answers the game's purchase question only for the exact item.

**File:** `data/eb/commands.json` in the EB folder

- `eb broker [cmd] [arg]`: The broker, for a buyer and a seller: buy an item, buy the spell scrolls of a tier (masters), put the bags up, list or unlist one listing, set its price, take the coin out of the sale boxes, reprice on a timer, and keep what was sold, bought and taken in coin.
- `eb buybest [gear|spells|adorns]`: Buy the best gear, spells or adornments the broker has for this character.
- `eb brokerbuy <item> [qty] [max]`: Buy a named item from the broker, a number of them, under a price cap.
- `eb purchase [cmd] [item]`: The shopping list (merchant and broker): add an item, run it, repeat its broker lines on a timer, show it, or clear it. Each merchant line is bought one unit at a time under the line's price cap; a "broker" line is bought up to its quantity (what the bags hold counts) from a listing between its floor and its cap; a Krono is never bought. Merchant spots kept on this PC and a walk there: grab, locate, known, go. A buy you make yourself: expect, confirms.
- `eb spells [buy|scribe] [arg]`: Spell upgrades: buy the Master scrolls you name from the broker, scribe every spell scroll in your bags, then write the ability export again - one run. scribe does the scribing and the export only.
- `eb collections [cmd] [arg]`: Collections: list what your collections still miss, scan the journal, add the collectibles in your bags (examine / fill), take pieces from the Collectible Depot, buy the missing ones on the broker, or acquire them all in one run.

#### Module `commands.combat`

The combat commands - eb combat, eb mez, eb cures, eb ho, eb cs ... - what each does, and the engine calls that do the same from a script.

Type them in the console after the console word (eb mez off), send them to the crew with a scope word (eb all mez off, eb to is2 mez off), or run them from a script with reg:dispatch("eb mez off").

EB answers the combat commands itself: each says how the engine stands or what it did. Two are still declared only: eb acs and eb rotation say "not wired yet", and reg:unattached({ domain = "combat" }) lists what waits. The engine behind the commands is scriptable - each command below names the engine calls that do its job - and a script may take over a command by attaching a handler to its id ("combat.\<verb>") with replace = true.

EB casts only through the cast stack's rows, only at a mob it may fight, and never at a guard. A cast the game does not take rests before it is tried again, and a hostile ability never goes at a citizen or a merchant.

How to answer a combat command from your own helper: 1) local reg, engine = eb.app.reg, eb.app.combat.engine; 2) reg:attach("combat.mez", function(args) engine:toggle("mez", args.state ~= "off"); return true, "mez " .. tostring(args.state) end, { owner = "my-helper", replace = true }); 3) type eb mez off - or send eb all mez off to the crew. args holds each argument by name, already read as its type (on|off arguments arrive as "on", "off" or "status").

**File:** `data/eb/commands.json` in the EB folder

- `eb combat [state]`: Turn the combat engine's casting on or off, or say how it stands.
- `eb autohunt [cmd] [list]`: Hunt by a saved list (the Auto Hunt window's): pull the nearest mob EB can win against - the list's names first, and with no names any mob it may kill, never a guard - rest, move on around where it started, along its waypoints (patrol) or inside its area (area), and stop at its kills or minutes or a zone line. No pull while anyone of the group is down (the dead check rezzes; each box releases by itself after its wait); one up again in another zone is called back; the third death in the group ends it.
- `eb cures [state]`: Automatic cures on or off: arcane, noxious, elemental, trauma and curse detriments, by priority. With several healers in the crew, one healer cures each detriment.
- `eb interrupts [state]`: Automatic interrupts and dispels on or off, for the casts and buffs being watched.
- `eb rez [state]`: Automatic rez of fallen members on or off. When several boxes could rez, one does. now rezzes a dead member at once, whatever the switch says.
- `eb ho [on|off|status|do|exclude|cancel]`: The heroic-opportunity part: on, off, its status, start one now, keep an ability out of them, or cancel a starter that is up.
- `eb mez [state]`: Crowd control on or off: mez or root the adds in the mez list's order, renew a mez before it breaks, and never touch the mob being killed or a guard.
- `eb embargo [item|ability|tag|list|clear] [name] [secs]`: Turn-taking across the crew: when one box uses an item, an ability or a tag, the other boxes hold it for some seconds. List or clear the holds.
- `eb allow <tag> [secs]`: Open an ALLOW tag for a while: the cast-stack rows that wait for it (their ATag) cast only while it is up, then it is as it was. Opening it on one box reaches the group. eb tags explains every tag; set a row's tags in the Cast Stack editor.
- `eb listen <tag>`: Fire a tag now so its LISTEN rows cast: the rows held waiting for it go once, on this box and the group. An opener row does this by itself when it casts; this is the by-hand version.
- `eb tag <name> [state]`: Switch one cast-stack tag on or off by hand: its rows are held when it is off. Nothing or status says its state. eb tags lists them and explains each; eb allow / eb embargo raise a tag for a while instead.
- `eb dnc [name]`: The do-not-cancel list: maintained spells the engine must never drop. A name puts it on the list or takes it off; nothing lists them.
- `eb stance [name]`: A fighter's stance alone: def, off, subtle, or status (eb go also sets the damage rows and the tank).
- `eb go [what]`: One word sets the part this box plays. tank: a fighter's defensive stance and its threat proc on, its offensive stance and Subtle Strikes off (the stance rows of the cast stack are switched, an effect that must go is cancelled, one that must come up is cast once when its row cannot go out now). dps: a fighter's offensive stance on, its defensive stance and threat proc off; every class's damage rows go. subtle: as dps, with Subtle Strikes on. heal: a priest's damage rows wait, so heals, cures and buffs go first. swap: tank, or from tank back to the damage preset it had last (dps or subtle). status (or nothing): what this box is set to.
- `eb assist [who] [follow] [dist]`: Fight what that one fights: tank (the group's tank - the one eb go tank names, else the group's first fighter), me (the box the line came from), a character's name, or off for no one; nothing says who this box assists now.
- `eb rogue [tank|dps|status] [name]`: A swashbuckler or brigand takes the tank's part. tank: on the rogue's box its defensive stance goes up, its taunts go first and its dehates off (read off its own ability check), and the crew heals it as the tank and points its hate buffs on the tank at it; typed on another box, the line goes to the rogue's box. dps: every row back as it was, the stance off, and the box that tanked before takes the part back. status: what this box is set to.
- `eb encounter [cmd] [name]`: The scripted encounter engine: load an encounter file and react to its mechanics (triggers, conditions, actions), list the files, say its status, switch it on or off.
- `eb setups [heroic|raid|all|status] [state]`: Whether your encounter setups run by themselves, by the kind of zone this box stands in. heroic is every zone that is not a raid zone (heroic and solo instances, overland zones, cities); raid is a zone whose name carries the game's raid tag. In a zone whose kind is on, every encounter setup installed on this box is laid on, each while its named is the mob (as eb flag autosetups on does); going into a zone whose kind is off takes them off again.
- `eb raidreact [cmd] [arg]`: Raid reactions: ready answers to a boss's moves. on and off switch every rule that reacts to a mob (its cast, its emote or its own timer) - or one, by its place in the list; status or list lists them; view or edit opens the Raid React window; test \<n> sets one off now (to see what it does); rec starts the fight scanner, where a cast is picked into a reaction. stop holds every reaction that is on until arm brings exactly those back (one switched by hand meanwhile stays as it is). timer \<n> \<every> \[\<early>\] makes that reaction also go off on its own clock in a fight - so many seconds early, every so often from the pull and from each time it was seen - and timer \<n> off takes it away. import lists your old reactions files (each zone's .react files and the older settings XML, read in your InnerSpace folders) and import \<n> | all brings their mechanics in, off; grab lists the detriments that landed on you here (EB Scanner's record) and grab \<n> makes a reaction (off) to the cast seen just before one. upload says why sharing them through the hub stays off.
- `eb mobcasts [on|off|record|watch|list]`: Watch and record what the mobs around you cast.
- `eb helpers [cmd] [arg]`: Class helpers in plain words - "when X, cast Y on Z": when someone drops under a share of health or power, is down, or is feared, stunned, mezzed or rooted; when a buff of yours is not on; when a named, an epic or the mob drops under a share; when my pet drops under a share; when my savagery is at a level; when the fight starts. list numbers them (your own first, then the ones your class tab switches on), add one, remove one by its number, on, off (all of them, or one by its number or ability - kept for this character), test one (a dry run: what it would do now and why, nothing sent), up / down (the order your own are tried in), export / import a share code, chains (the chains made in Tags & Helpers), status (the last one that went out); nothing (or window) opens the Tags & Helpers window.
- `eb classtab [option] [value]`: This character's class tab as EB's own settings. Nothing (or list) says every box of the tab EB acts on: its value, whether it is set in EB, the profile's or the default, and what EB does with it - and what it is doing now (the Warlock's Negative Void up or down, the last rotation call heard). An option alone says that one; an option and a value sets it for this character and the fight takes it at once; reset puts the profile's own box back. window opens the Cast Stack window on its Class tab.
- `eb scan [cmd]`: The fight scanner: record what the mobs cast and what lands on this box (on / off), mark the actors to watch during a fight, or clear the marks. Each detriment that lands is kept with the casts seen just before it, the mob that likely put it on (who cast those most) and its icon on this box (eb canceldet \<icon>); a mob that joins a fight already going is an add - adds says the ones seen in this zone. While recording it also keeps the lines the fights here said (a mob's words, its emotes, the warnings on the screen) as patterns - numbers read #, a name of the crew \* - and lines lists them; a player's chat and the game's own combat and loot lines are never kept. EB Scanner shows this fight or the whole zone, this box or every box (the crew's scans of the zone, asked over the relay while shown).
- `eb flag [name] [state]`: The fight's named switches (ae, pbae, encounter, nothreat, namedca, dumbfires, petassist, casting, cures, rez, interrupts, mez, ho, joust, hooffensive, face, dispel, combos, smartae, smartencounter, los, selectivecures, selectivegroupcures, autosetups, chatevents), any cast-stack tag, or one cast-stack row by its name: switch it on or off, or say what it is set to.
- `eb cs [cmd] [arg]`: The character's cast stack: show it (the Cast Stack window), archive it, share it, import a share file; camp, re-camp, clear and filter.
- `eb acs [xpack]`: Put this character's class adornment set on. The set is picked for its class, else its class group, else its archetype, at the highest level its own level allows (a set above its level still goes on when it is the only one, and the answer says the adornments above the level will not). What the bags lack comes out of the Adornment Depot in reach.
- `eb rotation [words]`: A saved rotation order: the abilities this box casts in that order, each through the checked cast (aimed and paced like any cast). save \<name>: \<ability>, \<ability>, ... keeps one (again = replaced); \<name> (or \<name> once) casts it once, on demand; \<name> start goes round and round until stop; list, status, delete \<name>; board opens the Rotation Board (every box's rotation: the caster, the ability it casts next, its role and when that is ready).
- `eb abilities [export|research|details|tracker|list] [options]`: Knowledge-book tools: export your own ability check (what to export and how, with its progress), research the next tier, an ability's details, a usage tracker, the list.
- `eb cast <ability> [who]`: Cast one ability now, by name, as a button of EB's MCP does. A row of this character's cast stack says what kind of spell it is; an ability that is no row goes only when this character has it in its own book. An attack goes only at the mob EB fights (never a guard, a merchant or a citizen), a beneficial spell on this box, and on \<member> on that group or raid member alone. It is paced like any cast of the stack: a cast the game does not take rests before it is tried again.
- `eb rebuff`: Rebuff now: every wait EB was keeping on a buff or an item is forgotten and the cast stack's buffs are cancelled so they are cast fresh, never one on the do-not-cancel list. Whatever buff is down goes out again on the next casts.
- `eb revive`: When this character is dead: release to the first revive point - EB's own release; the death window's paid instant revive is never pressed. It says the release was sent, then "up again" once this character reads alive.
- `eb autorelease [state]`: Whether this box releases by itself when it dies. on (the default): solo or a wipe releases at once; with someone else up it waits for a rez first. off: it never releases by itself and waits for a rez.
- `eb deadcheck [what] [arg]`: Every dead member in this zone (the group and the raid) gets ONE rezzer. One that already stands in reach of the body with a rez rezzes from where it stands - nobody runs (a tank in reach too; a healer only when healers go); else the send list's first kind up runs: a dirge, then a necromancer, healers when switched on, a tank last of all - of one kind the nearest to the body, never the window you play. That box runs to the body on the mesh, rezzes from its rez's max range, runs back and brings the member along (eb rezrun). Which body first: a dead healer, then a dead rezzer.
- `eb autotarget [cmd] [arg]`: The kill-first list: the mobs this box fights first, by name, top first. add puts a mob on it (and switches it on), remove takes one off, clear empties it; off leaves the list but fights what the box is pointed at (enable and disable mean on and off, as on every switch of EB; yes / no, true / false and 1 / 0 do too). The scan that finds them: radius (a candidate stands within that many metres; 30 by default), height (within that many metres above or below the box; 0 = no limit) and rescan (a pick holds that many seconds before another candidate takes its place; one that dies goes at once). scan on also looks at mobs not in a fight yet. Said alone, it says the list and the scan.
- `eb deathsave [status|propose|clear|stagger|auto] [arg]`: The group's death-save plan: who saves whom and at what health, so two saves never go out together. A death save is an emergency heal row on one member. propose makes this box's part: the group's healers (its priests, A-Z - the same order on every box) share one ladder, every healer's first save before anyone's second - with two healers, 30% and 16% for the first, 23% and 9% for the second. A planned save waits for its target to fall to its % (the row keeps its own target). status says who does what; clear drops the plan (each save as its row says, one box a member at a time); stagger \<top> \<step> moves the ladder; auto on makes it again when the group changes.
- `eb autocure [words]`: One member cured first, again and again: whenever that member carries what a cure row removes, this box cures them before anyone else. curse: only a curse cure puts them first. cursed: one curse cure on them, then the mark goes. \<member> off takes their mark off; off alone takes every mark off; nothing says who is marked. The cure rows, the selective-cure switches and the crew's claim (one box a member at a time) decide as always.
- `eb canceldet <icons>`: A detriment on me cancelled, found by its icons - one a fight says to click off. The detriment whose icon (and backdrop, when given) match is cancelled; a beneficial effect with the same icon is never touched. The Target window shows an effect's icons.
- `eb blockers [now|cycle|stop|status]`: The group's AE blockers - each class's own group ward against area damage: a druid's Tortoise Shell, a bard's Bladedance, a swashbuckler's Advance Warning, a channeler's Shield of Blackwood. now (or nothing): this box's own, cast now through the checked cast (eb all blockers: each box its own). cycle: the group's, one box after another, ten seconds apart (druids, bards, swashbucklers, channelers, A-Z) - the box it is typed on casts its own in its turn and tells the others theirs. stop ends a cycle; status says who has one and where a cycle is.
- `eb aa [value]`: The AA slider: what share of adventure XP goes to AA XP - 0 to 100, on (100) or off (0); nothing is 0 (every bit of XP to adventure levels). Sent as the game's own slider line.
- `eb castin [seconds] [ability] [who]`: One cast, later: in so many seconds (600 at most) this box casts the ability - a row of its cast stack, or its book - aimed and paced like any cast, on the member named when one is. What happened is said when it goes. list says what waits; clear drops it.
- `eb citycombat [on|off|toggle|status]`: No casting or fighting in a city unless called for. Off (the default): in a city zone this box casts nothing, picks no target and attacks nothing; a press by hand still goes, and so does a run that fights (a quest line, a hunt, an instance run). On: it fights in a city as anywhere. Kept per character.
- `eb guards [status|check]`: The guard rule on this box. A mob with a guard word in its name or title (guard, sentinel, sentry, watchman, militia, warden, protector) is never fought, pulled or caught in an area attack - except the one mob a quest step or an instance run names to kill (its words, "fifteen Blades guards", name "a Blades guard"), and only outside a city. status: what stands now. check: each damage row of the cast stack and how EB knows whether it hits an area.
- `eb readycast <ability> [seconds] [tag]`: Cast an ability the moment it is ready: this box watches its own ability for up to the seconds given (0 = now or never, 10 when unsaid, 60 at most) and casts it through the fight's own cast - a row of its cast stack, or its book - then tells the crew. An ability this character does not have is refused at once.
- `eb rezrun [who]`: This box runs to a dead member's body and rezzes them: a long way (25 m or more) first casts its in-combat speed buffs (eb deadcheck speed); out of a fight with Gather Remains in its book and the body within 100 m, Gather Remains first (the body comes, no walk); else a walk on the zone's mesh that stops half a metre inside where its rez may be cast (MAX range: 14 m for a 15 m rez), a quarter second still, then the rez from its own cast stack - the one that gets the most of the group up (a group rez) and reaches, never one tried on this body already while another may go - and the dead box is asked to take it every 3 seconds. Then, in that same moment, the walk back to where it stood.
- `eb pet [attack|backoff|assist|status] [state]`: The pet: attack my target (only a fight that is ours, or an aggressive mob - never a guard, a merchant or a citizen), back off, or assist on or off (EB then sends it at every mob it fights). status says the switch.
- `eb mount [on|off|toggle|best|status]`: Mount or dismount: on, off, toggle; status says which. best (the best mount you own) is held back until the game layer's mount swap has been proven.
- `eb joust [in|out|status] [metres]`: Step out of melee for a mechanic (out: 25 m along the line from the mob) and back in (in: 3 m), walking on the mesh. status says where this box stands.
- `eb ranged [on|off|status]`: The game's ranged auto-attack: on, off, or status. off is sent only while it is on (it stops the melee auto-attack too).
- `eb position [behind|flank|off|status] [metres]`: Where this box stands in a fight: behind (at the mob's back), flank (at its nearer side), off (where it stands), or status. Unset, the cast stack profile's Move behind mob box decides (behind). The tank - the box the mob is on, or the group's tank - faces the mob and never walks round it.
- `eb beltadorn [what]`: Put the belt rune a fight calls for on the belt, out of a fight. A word is first the item you named for it (eb set beltadorn.\<word> \<the item's name>). Stun, stifle, mez, fear and medic are rune TYPES: a rune's type is the end of its name (Adamant Defiance is Stun, Adamant Resolve Stifle, Astral Dominion Mez, Blinding Gleam Fear, Field Medic Medic), so eb beltadorn stun puts on the rune in your bags whose name ends in Adamant Defiance - typing those words does the same. With several runes of the type, the best one this character can wear: the highest level it may use, then the highest tier. Any other word is the one usable item in the bags whose name holds it; two or more are named and refused. Several words are an item's own name. status (or nothing) says what is going on.
- `eb combos [state]`: The ascension chain: on, an ascension starter that went out at a mob is followed by its combo before the other damage rows (never ahead of a heal, a cure or a rez); off, each ascension row casts where the cast stack puts it. status (or nothing) says how it stands and how many starter and combo rows the stack has.
- `eb fightto [spot]`: Walk to a spot in this zone on the zone's mesh and fight what is met on the way - a mob within 20 m that EB can win against, never a guard, a named, a heroic or an epic - then stop there. group: the others follow this box.
- `eb lazytank [on|off|status|allow|unallow] [arg]`: The lazy tank: this box holds a camp spot and takes back every mob that gets loose on someone who is not the tank - a taunt of its cast stack at that mob, sent like every cast of the fight (aimed at that mob, then back on the kill mob). The member worst off first; an area taunt first when two or more got loose. The tank is the crew's declared tank (eb go tank), else this box. A taunt is a row the class facts call one, or one this character's own ability check (eb abilities export) says raises its threat.
- `eb lazyheal [on|off|status] [arg]`: The lazy healer: in a fight (this box in it, a mob of it near, or the tank's own crew state says it fights), when the tank stands farther away than the reach, this box walks back within it - to a spot 0.7 x the reach from the tank on the line back to where it stood - by EB's one mover, with the fight walk's holds (the cast bar, another walk, a stop). In reach again, the box's own fight position is as before; out of a fight a follow does the rest.
- `eb formation [cmd] [arg]`: The raid formation: in a fight every box works out its own spot round the mob from what every box sees alike - the group's members by name, each one's role (its class off its own crew state, else the group's read), the tank, the mob and the side of it the tank holds - and walks there itself with the fight walk. The tank holds the front and faces the mob; the melee stand behind it (or on the flanks, or in front), the healers and the ranged on rings further out, every spot 2.5 m from every other one and never inside an avoid circle; a raid's groups take rings of their own.
- `eb pullplan [scan|plan|body|stop|status] [arg]`: Pull planning by the hunt's own rules (never a guard, never another player's fight, never what proved too strong). scan says the mobs this box can reach walking on the zone's mesh - a mob behind a wall is as far as the way round it - nearest that way first, and what was passed over; plan says the order to pull them in (each next the nearest to the one before); body \<name> walks at the nearest one of that name in reach until it comes for this box - never an attack - then back to where this box stood.
- `eb flagrot [cmd] [words]`: Flag rotation, for a fight's "next one takes it": marks 1 to 8, each the characters flagged on it in the order they were flagged, and the one flagged last. next flags the next one not flagged yet on that mark; again starts the mark over once every one had a turn; do \<eb line> has that character's box run the line. set / remove one, removeall, is, list, clear every mark.
- `eb intent [fire|save|list|status|delete|go] [words]`: Intents: a named list of abilities for one job (a burn, a group ward, a big heal). Fired, the first box of its scope with one of them ready casts it: the list's earliest ability any box has ready, cast by one box only.
- `eb npccast [status|on|off|toggle|list|reload] [words]`: The mobs' cast lists, answered in a fight: per zone, the mobs to watch and what to do when one of them starts a listed spell - the lists shipped in your InnerSpace scripts and your own (read only; yours deep-merged over the shipped: a mob or a spell set to false drops it, noMerge keeps yours alone). on / off (kept for this character; off by default), status, list \[\<zone>\] (each mob and spell in words: which are interrupted, which run lines), reload.
- `eb cancel <spell>`: Cancel a spell of yours that is up now (a stance, a toggle, a buff), by its name, any rank.
- `eb tagfor <tag> <secs> [allow|embargo]`: A cast-stack tag for a while: embargo holds back the rows that carry it, allow lets the rows that wait for it go - for so many seconds, then it is as it was.
- `eb curereq [cure|curse|group|cancel|clear|status] [rest]`: Cure requests: ask this box's curers for a cure that gives up after a while. cure \<member> \[kinds\]: while they carry a kind named (none named: arcane, elemental, noxious and trauma; curse; confrontfear = Confront Fear on them once), the first ready cure row that removes it goes on them - a single-target row first, else a group one - until they carry none. curse \<member>: the same for a curse. group \[kinds\] \[count \<n>\]: the group cure once, when at least n of the group (you included; 1 if not said) carry a kind named, each kind counted on its own - never on a guess. secs \<s> gives up after that long (8 if not said, at most 300); tag \<t> names it. cancel \<member or tag> drops their requests, clear drops them all, status (or nothing) lists the live ones and the last few that ended.

#### Module `commands.coord`

Coordination from the console: the ability tags of a cast stack, the claim arbiter that makes one box cure or rez, and the plain-language rules.

The same engines a script drives through eb.coord.rules and eb.coord.arbiter. EB starts the coordination on every box, so all three commands answer.

**File:** `data/eb/commands.json` in the EB folder

- `eb tags [cmd] [arg]`: The ability tags the cast stack's rows carry: list them with their switch (the default), or set one on or off - every row that carries the tag switches together.
- `eb claim [status|release] [action]`: Show who holds a claim (the cure, the rez, the group action), or release this box's claims.
- `eb rules [cmd] [arg]`: Rules in plain words: when \<something happens> do \<something> for \<who>. eb rules lists them, one sentence each, with what is wrong where a rule has a typo; add makes one, edit changes its fields, remove, enable and disable switch it, show prints one with its fields, status says what the service holds (rules, claims, holds), fired says what happened last, reload reads the saved file again, import turns this character's cast-stack tags into rules, fire sets a tag off by hand, run sets a rule off now, lift lifts a hold, words lists the words a rule may use, and builder opens the Coordination window.
- `eb chain [cmd] [words]`: Chains: step lists run beside the fight, one step a tick - cast an ability, wait, wait until a condition holds, stop unless a condition holds, say a line, fire a coordination tag, run an eb command, keep a checkpoint. save keeps one, run starts it, stop ends it (or every one), resume starts it again after the last checkpoint it passed or the one named, status says what runs and what it waits for, show its steps, delete.

#### Module `commands.core`

The commands every box answers: help, status, stop, end, pause, resume, afk and reload - typed in the console as eb \<command>, sent to the crew as eb all \<command>, or run from a script with eb.dispatch("eb \<command>").

Type a command after the console word: eb status. Put a crew word in front to send it: eb all pause (every box, this one too), eb others pause (every box but this one), eb to is2 pause (just box is2; who may also be a character, a class or an archetype). A line that reaches a box from the crew runs there and is never sent on.

How to drive EB from a script: 1. local ok, text = eb.dispatch("eb pause") runs a line exactly as if it was typed (eb.app.dispatch). 2. Read the answer text; ok is false with a plain reason for an unknown word, a bad argument, a call EB has not proven in the game yet (it says so) or a command that is not answered on this box yet. 3. eb help lists every domain; eb help \<command> prints its usage, its arguments and whether the crew may be sent it.

EB for InnerSpace answers one more console word before the commands: eb proof, the proof gate. EB sends the game only members and commands it has proven to work; a call that is held back says "held back until it is proven live" and answers false. eb proof (or eb proof \<mode>) shows or sets the mode: tested (the default: only what is proven), evidence (also what working scripts are known to use) or open (everything, for a proof run, with the console watched for errors). eb proof alone says the mode and how much waits for a live proof; eb proof list \[\<word>\] lists the steps that wait, eb proof probe \<id> runs one of them and eb proof last shows the last answer. eb gate is not this: it opens a door (eb door is the same word).

**File:** `data/eb/commands.json` in the EB folder

- `eb help [topic]`: Print the help: with no topic the command domains, with a domain its commands, with a command its usage line, its arguments, other spellings and whether it can be sent to the crew.
- `eb status [bot|crew|goal|nav|combat|patch]`: Print this box's state. bot (the default) is the version, the target, what came up at start and what did not, then the crew, combat, instance and brain lines; crew is every box this one hears; goal the instance runner and the brain; nav the walker; combat the engine; patch the quick live read after a game patch - PASS, FAIL or NOTE for the build gate, name, level, health, power, a position that follows you, the zone, the target, the actors around, the server, then the reads with no value on this build. It only reads.
- `eb stop`: The kill switch. Typed on this box's console, eb stop ends EB on this box. Sent to the crew (eb all stop) or typed as eb stopall, every box it reaches halts its brain: quests, instances, walks and goals stop, while the combat engine still keeps the character alive. eb resume starts again.
- `eb freeze`: Everything stops at once and stays stopped: the walk, the follow, a run or a quest line end (eb stop), the cast going now is cancelled, and nothing is cast until eb resume lets it all go again. Typed as eb halt too.
- `eb end <system>`: End one engine and leave the rest running: quest, ic, nav, hunt, craft, harvest, or all. irc leaves the IRC channel and server this box is on (eb irc end).
- `eb pause [state]`: Pause: goals, quests, instances and walks freeze where they are; a fight still runs in the combat engine. Pause again, or eb resume, carries on from the same place.
- `eb resume`: Carry on after eb pause or eb stopall, from where everything stopped (the same as eb pause resume).
- `eb afk [state]`: Away mode: keep the character from being logged out for idling (a keep-alive at a random time every two to five minutes), and let the crew see this box as away.
- `eb reload [module]`: Load EB again in this session without restarting the game or logging out: the client and the character stay, only EB's own scripts and data load again. With a word, one part only: nav (the mesh corrections, door lines, marks and places), invites (the roster and login results the invite reads), stack (this character's cast stack) or poi (the game's map points, read again at the next eb poi). A box in the middle of a run (an instance, a quest line, a power-level route, a queue) does not stop: it says so, keeps the ask and loads EB again by itself once the run is over; the word cancel drops that kept ask.

#### Module `commands.craft`

Console commands for crafting: the craft bot (EB Craft) - its setup queue, its runs (the queue, writs, a quest's craft steps, Auto Tinkering, Low Level Leveling), its settings - and recipe books, tinkering by its bands, crafting luck.

Type these in the console as eb \<command>, send them to the crew with eb all | others | to \<who> \<command>, or run them from a script with reg:dispatch(line) or eb.dispatch. EB runs the economy behind them, so each one answers with a run under way, a status line or a refusal in plain words. Every press in EB Craft is one of these lines, so a press and a typed line do the same thing. A crafting step that is not proven live on this box is held: a run is not started, and the answer says what waits and how to let it out for a proof run. The crafting itself is scriptable through the economy's Lua pillars (eb.economy.craft, eb.economy.writs, eb.economy.skilllevel) and the craft bot (app.economy.craftbot).

**File:** `data/eb/commands.json` in the EB folder

- `eb craft [recipe]`: The craft bot. With no word it opens EB Craft and says what the bot is doing. Runs: start (the setup queue), writs \[n\], quest \<quest>, tinker, lll, stop, pause \[on|off\]. The setup queue: add \<recipe> \[n\], remove \<recipe>, qty \<recipe> \<n>, clear, queue, save \<name>, load \<name>, queues, forget \<name>. Old saved queues: import list \[words\] shows the queue files your other craft tools left on this PC, import \<file> \[as \<name>\] saves one of them as a queue here, import all \[words\] saves every one (one a step). Settings: set \<setting> \<value> (set alone lists them), savesettings, reload; set campWhenDone on camps this character out to character select after a run that finishes (never one you stop; off by default). Also: scan (read the recipe book again), lite on|off (answer the reactions of a combine you start by hand), recipes \<words>, parse \<a writ or quest step's text>, proof on|off (EB Boxer: let its unproven crafting steps out for a proof run), shop books | sell \<item> | destroy \<item> (the named items in the bags sold to the merchant in reach, or destroyed - several split by | - never a protected one), minimize (EB Craft rolled up to its run row; eb craft brings it back). Any other words are a recipe crafted now.
- `eb craftqueue [add|start|handout|status|stop|clear] [arg]`: The setup queue - the same one as EB Craft's Queues tab: add a recipe (and how many), remove one, start it, show it, stop it, clear it, save it or load a saved one by name, or hand the finished items out. add \<recipe> \[n\] for \<who> makes it for another box (a row of its own); handout trades each recipe made for another box to it - the economy's hand-over, one recipient at a time - and that box then scribes what it got (eb to \<who> spells scribe).
- `eb craftsetup [words]`: Low Level Leveling: a new crafter from level 1 to 9, then 10 to 19 - rounds of the highest recipe at or under the tradeskill level, what is made sold or destroyed as EB Craft's Low Level Leveling tab says, until the trainer's level. start \[class\] applies the class and options then runs it; plan says what it would do; stop ends it.
- `eb recipebooks [list|scribe|plan|prices|buy] [arg]`: Recipe books: list = how many recipes this character's book holds (the book is read in the background); scribe = use every recipe book in the bags, then read the book again; plan = the books your crafting class still needs, at or under your tradeskill level; prices = the plan with each book's broker and merchant cost; buy = walk to the recipe merchant and buy then scribe the planned books.
- `eb craftjunk [list|go|add|remove] [item]`: Low Level Leveling's leftovers: the items such a run is known to make. list says which bag stacks would go and which stay; go destroys them; add and remove keep your own names beside EB's list.
- `eb tinker [arg]`: Level a secondary skill by its bands to the cap - tinkering (the default) or adorning: on = the recipes of each band (and the band's books, bought at the broker under a cap) until the skill is maxed; off = stop; no word = where it stands. eb tinker adorning on levels adorning instead. EB Craft's Auto Tinkering (eb craft tinker) is the other way: rounds of the highest tinkering recipe in the book.
- `eb writs [craft|rush|commission]`: Crafting writs as EB Craft's Writs tab says (how many, which reply takes the writ): craft = from where the tab says (the rush order agent or the work order clipboard), rush = from the rush order agent; commission = accept commissions on or off.
- `eb luck [show|on|off|reset]`: The Luck window: while a skill that levels by chance climbs (tinkering, adorning, transmuting), how many crafts, how many skill-ups, the percent and the longest dry run.
- `eb craftgm [words]`: Craft Grandmasters: the (Master) spell scrolls in your bags turned into (Grandmaster) crafts, one craft per scroll. scan (the default) says what would be crafted and what is left out and why; start crafts them; queue only puts the recipes in the setup queue (eb craft start crafts it) and never uses the depot; status says where a run stands; stop ends it (a scroll taken out and not crafted stays in your bags). A level range is the (Grandmaster) recipe's level: 131-135, 131 135, level 131-135 or one level; all (the default) is every level, and a scroll with no readable level is left out of a ranged run. depot also takes the nearest Scroll Depot's scrolls, in batches that fit your bags; nodepot is bags only.

#### Module `commands.depot`

Console commands for bags, depots, the bank, mail and repairs: depot top-ups and keep lists, the inventory hub, deposits and withdrawals, restocking, buying, handing items out, food and drink, the protect list, item search, clearing raws, transmute and salvage runs, krono, the ledger, and mending gear.

Type them as eb \<command> in the console, send them to the crew with eb all | others | to \<who> \<command>, or run them from a script with reg:dispatch or eb.dispatch. EB runs the economy behind them, so each one answers: a chore under way (a long job runs as a chore, one at a time, and eb economy stop ends it), a status line, or a refusal in plain words. A call the game layer holds back until EB has proven it in the game says so and answers false - it never says "done" for what it did not do. The Lua behind each one is named in its notes: eb.economy.inventory, eb.economy.vendor, eb.economy.depot, eb.economy.bank, eb.economy.mail and the rest of eb.economy.

**File:** `data/eb/commands.json` in the EB folder

- `eb depot [cmd] [arg]`: Depots: list what the depots in reach hold, top an item up from a depot, keep an item out of every deposit, deposit by rule, or show the depot status.
- `eb inv [cmd] [arg]`: The inventory hub: show the bags, tidy them, move one item into a bag, sell by rule, destroy junk by rule, restock, hand items over, or fill the quiver - one after another.
- `eb bank [deposit|withdraw|coin|move|status] [arg]`: The bank: deposit bag items by rule, withdraw by name or by a pick, move coin, move a guild bank page onto another, or show what the banks hold.
- `eb restock [preset] [name]`: Top up ammo, the quiver or crafting materials from the depots by a saved preset, or by an item's name.
- `eb buy [what]`: Buy from the merchant in reach: open it and buy the item, one at a time. Each purchase question is answered for that item only.
- `eb items [kind] [go]`: The bag items a use-them-all button means - status items, ingots, familiars, mercenary items, Forlorn books: listed, and used only with go.
- `eb economy`: What the economy loaded on this box: your own rules, any file that does not read, the saved T.S.E and what is under way. eb economy stop ends every chore the economy has going.
- `eb distribute <item> [qty] [who]`: Hand out some of an item to each member of the group, the raid or a list you name, one trade after another; status shows how far it got, cancel calls it off.
- `eb tradeq [text]`: Ask whichever box holds an item to hand it to another character: eb tradeq \<item> \[how many\] to \<recipient> \[from \<holder>\], or status.
- `eb trade <item|coin|batch|accept> <who> [arg]`: One trade with one character, typed: an item, coin, several items at once, or take that character's trade.
- `eb consume [state]`: Keep the food and drink slots fed: turn auto-consume on or off.
- `eb useitem <item>`: Use an item now - a potion, an elixir, food, a worn clicky - worn first, then the bags (never from the bank). Refused while the item's own reuse runs. eb all useitem \<item> uses it on every box.
- `eb scroll <name>`: Use a Scroll of \<name> from the bags: the Thaumic Scroll of \<name> first when the bags hold one, else the plain one. Refused while its own reuse runs; none in the bags is said.
- `eb useon <who> <item>`: Use an item on a group or raid member: the member is targeted, the item used, the old target put back. me is this box. Refused for someone not in the group or raid, a dead member, an item not worn or in the bags, or one whose reuse runs (the seconds left are said).
- `eb potion [state] [items]`: Auto-consume named potions, elixirs, scrolls or poisons in the bags on or off, by the game's own Auto Consume flag: on uses one at once when its effect is not up. status reads them (no names: the ones EB switched). The AUTO-CONSUME LIST keeps that flag on for its items on every box - and off while the character is idle.
- `eb itemgate [status|on|off|reload]`: The item gate: a worn clicky whose effect shows only in a Persona stat - Dragon's Temper's Whirlwind is only seen as AE auto-attack - is not clicked again while that effect is on: its cast-stack row is held off, and on again when it may be used.
- `eb protect [protect|unprotect|list] [item]`: The protect list: protect an item from every sell, destroy, transmute and deposit, take it off again, or list what is protected.
- `eb itemsearch [keep|consume] <words>`: Find an item by words, anywhere: this box's bags, its bank and the depots it read this session - and every other box of the crew answers with its own, each answer said here as it comes.
- `eb whohas <words> [all]`: Which characters hold an item, and how many in all: each character's bags and bank as EB last read them on this PC, this box's bags read now, and every crew box answering with its own count as it comes, added up.
- `eb invdestroy <raws|resources> [bags]`: Free bag slots by destroying raw materials or resources by rule (protected items are always kept). It lists what would go and destroys only with go.
- `eb tse [op] [rest]`: A transmute, salvage, extract or destroy run over the items your rule picks (protected items, Master spell scrolls and bound items you did not opt in are always kept), a sale of the pick to the Commodities Exporter, or a hand-over of it to the leader. saved runs the saved pick; stop ends a run.
- `eb krono [count|use|give] [who] [qty]`: Krono: count the ones you hold, use one, or give one to a member.
- `eb mail [read|attach|send] [arg]`: Mail: read a letter, take the attachments, or send mail.
- `eb repair [state]`: Repair your gear at a mender in reach now, or turn repairing on or off (out of a fight, with the gear worn down and a mender in reach).
- `eb ledger [sub] [arg]`: The ledger: what every box sold, deposited, unadorned, transmuted and looted, day by day. It is kept on this PC and only your own boxes see it. open and close its window (EB Ledger: the days on the left, newest first, each with its coin and its counts); status says every box's coin and counts today, one line a box, each naming its character - the boxes of this PC from the day files here, a box of yours whose ledger is on another PC asked to say its own; a day (YYYY-MM-DD) or the last 12 hours reads the rows; loot says who got the loot (each character, how many, and what); clear \<day> forgets that day and clear all forgets everything, every box's on this PC.

#### Module `commands.gear`

Console commands for gear: gear a character or the group up, adornments, gear sets, temporary adornments, the best-gear list, worn gear, the at-a-glance card, Transmuting levels.

Type these as eb \<command>, send them to the crew with eb all | others | to \<who> \<command>, or run them with reg:dispatch(line) or eb.dispatch. EB runs the economy behind them, so each one answers with a chore under way, a status line or a refusal in plain words. The work behind them is scriptable through eb.economy.gearup, eb.economy.adornments, eb.economy.gearsets and eb.economy.transmute.

**File:** `data/eb/commands.json` in the EB folder

- `eb gearup [self|group] [arg]`: Gear a fresh character from the broker: each empty slot gets the best listing for it under the cap, then the upgrades are worn. group: every box not paused gears itself up.
- `eb aup [self|group] [arg]`: Wear the upgrades in your bags, or (group) work out who in the crew should wear which spare piece and hand them over.
- `eb adorn [cmd] [arg]`: Adornment sets: put a set on (apply), put it on and buy what is missing (fill), copy a member's adornments (adopt), say where each adornment of a set is (contents, missing), keep your own sets, take adornments from the depot, buy one, strip old gear, or show the guide.
- `eb tempadorn [state] [arg]`: Temporary adornments by the Temp Adorns window's plan: put them on, a dry run, fresh ones, what is on, the status, a restock from the Adornment Depot, a find, and keep them on.
- `eb bestgear [shop|buy|goals|status] [arg]`: The best gear on the broker: a shop ranked by the stats you pick, a buy for one slot by a focus stat, the stat goals and a run toward them, or where you stand.
- `eb gearjob [cmd] [arg]`: Look at a member's worn gear (or this box's own), or run the gear job on this box: take a piece, wear it and carry the old piece's adornments across.
- `eb glance [cmd] [arg]`: At a glance: one line of this character's gear, bags and coin (card, the bare form), or a RUN - a preset's steps done on several boxes, each box its own part - with its presets, retry, stop and status.
- `eb transmutelevel [level|scan|stop|status] [arg]`: Level the Transmuting skill: level, scan the stone merchant, stop, or show where it stands.
- `eb gearset [save|adorn|equip|list|delete] [name]`: Gear sets: save what is worn (the pieces and their adornments) under a name; put the adornments or the pieces back; list the sets; delete one.
- `eb unadorn [tiers]`: Take the adornments off the bag items of the tiers named. They stay in the bags; protected items are skipped.
- `eb checkgear`: Worn gear: the worst piece's condition, and what is under the repair line.

#### Module `commands.harvest`

Console commands for harvesting: nodes near you and gather routes, shinies, crafting materials, saved gather routes, the pack pony.

Type these as eb \<command>, send them to the crew with eb all | others | to \<who> \<command>, or run them with reg:dispatch(line) or eb.dispatch. EB runs the economy behind them, so each one answers with a chore under way, a status line or a refusal in plain words. Harvesting is scriptable through eb.economy.harvest. A node the rules leave is never clicked: the route leaves it and remembers it.

**File:** `data/eb/commands.json` in the EB folder

- `eb harvest [cmd] [arg]`: Harvest: switch it on or off, show its status, take the nodes near you, or run a gather route. near takes options: once (one pull), reach:\<m> (how far it looks), move:\<m> (walks up to a node that far, on the mesh), count:\<n> (how many pulls), until:\<n>:\<item> (until the bags hold that many; an underscore is a space), and a node's name. left says the nodes left a while and when each comes back (a refused pull, or another box on it: 90 seconds; a node the mesh could not reach: 5 minutes); left clear looks at them all again. tally says what this session gathered: pulls, rares, per minute, per kind (Ore, Gem, Wood, Root, Den, Shrub, Fish, Shiny); tally reset counts from zero. log on or off writes each step of a run (start, scan, pick, walk, pull, node, mark, end) to a file in logs, one a session; no word says where it is. roam lets the mesh pick where to look: look points in rings round you (a radius in metres) or inside an area you marked (mark:\<name>: an area route of EB Gather, its corners, or a saved spot), each the mesh's own point, nearest first, round and round until you stop it, count:\<n> or until:\<n>:\<item>. cover runs once over every node this box has seen in this zone (a node's name narrows it); cover sweep \[radius\] sweeps the whole zone in rings once. make \<name> makes a gather route from the nodes seen here, nearest first from where you stand, without running it (eb gatherroute \<name> runs it). known says how many nodes are known here, by kind; known clear forgets them. courtesy on or off: your own boxes, grouped or not, never go for one node - a node another box goes for is left to it - and each box harvesting in a zone takes its own part of a roam's look points and its own start on a route (on unless set off). kind:\<kinds> (kind:ore,gem - ore, gem, wood, root, den, shrub, fish) on near, roam and cover takes only nodes of those kinds: a node of another kind is passed by, never clicked, and the next one looked at. roam \<radius> patrol walks its look points ring by ring, round and round, instead of nearest first. pause holds the harvest under way where it stands (the walk stopped, nothing pulled); resume goes on from there. plan lists EB Gather's zone plans (how, the route or name, within, the kinds); plan clear \<zone> clears one (its short name or its name); plan go \<zone> travels there first - EB's own travel, this box only - and starts its plan there.
- `eb shinies [on|off|status|track]`: Collect and track shinies: on, off, status, or track (watch for new ones and mark where they are).
- `eb mats [cmd] [arg]`: Gather the raw materials on a list. recipe \<name> makes the list from that recipe's own components (how many times: "name",3), less what the bags hold; list says what is still missing; harvest gathers what is near you until every raw on the list is in the bags; clear empties the list. go harvests EB Gather's Materials list where it grows: each material in a zone of its tier (the one you stand in when it is of that tier, else EB's own travel there first), taking only the node kinds that give it (a mineral: ore and gem nodes) until its count is gathered over what the bags held on arrival, then Call to Guild Hall and the harvest into the hall's Harvesting Supply Depot; stop ends that run where it is; status says where it is, each material gathered of its count, and how each zone ended.
- `eb gatherroute [name]`: Run a saved gather route (a route of another zone: this box travels there first, then it runs). list names the routes; import reads your own saved gather route files - all of them, or the one named - into EB's routes; import old reads the old bot's auto-hunt routes (each zone's route of named points and that zone's map) as gather routes walked in order and round again (one zone by its name; overwrite replaces a route already there); stop ends the run. farm \<route> walks the route round and round taking every node on it (wide round each stop, its own node names set aside); all runs every route of the zone you stand in, one after another, then over again from the first (a route of another zone, or one with no zone, is never in it). kind:\<kinds> anywhere among the words takes only nodes of those kinds.
- `eb packpony`: Send the pack pony out to harvest: summon it, hail it and answer its questions. While an instance run or a quest line is going on this box it is held off - said - and goes out once the run is over.

#### Module `commands.ic`

The instance commands: run or loop an instance file, see the lockout timers, reset a zone, and the instance queue, creator and run-teams commands.

Type them in the console after the console word (eb ic run fixture_hollow), run them from a script with reg:dispatch("eb ic status"), or send them to the crew: eb all ic run fixture_hollow typed on the tank runs it on every box, with the box it was typed on as the lead and the others following it.

HOW TO RUN AN INSTANCE. 1. eb ic list shows the installed instance files. 2. On the tank: eb ic run \<zone> \[difficulty\] \[option=on|off\] for one run, or eb ic loop \<zone> \[minutes\] \[difficulty\] to keep at it (0 or nothing = until you stop it). 3. eb ic status says where it is. 4. eb ic stop ends it at once; nobody moves. 5. eb lockouts shows the zone timers; eb resetzone \<zone> asks the game to reset one.

**File:** `data/eb/commands.json` in the EB folder

- `eb ic [cmd] [zone]`: Run or loop an instance file, and control the run: run, loop, stop, status, list (the installed instance files) and reload (read the files again). The box the line is typed on leads; boxes that receive it from another box follow that box: they reach the hub on their own, are zoned in by the lead's door, and never walk the route. At the door the lead on a mount or swimming comes down for a few seconds first (the fly / swim-down key), then takes the door for the group: each member takes it from where it holds, never walked to it. A run's EVAC (my own class evac, then one member by class, then an evac item - each verified by the move) learns a zone whose evac the game refuses ("... isn't so easy to escape ..."): kept on this PC, never tried there again.
- `eb lockouts [cmd] [zone]`: Show the zones this character is saved to, check one zone, or ask every character.
- `eb zoneevent <event>`: Do a zone's own event the EB way, on every box the line reaches: eb all zoneevent \<event>. EB knows Xygoz_ClickAdd (The Fabled Veeshan's Peak, the fight with Xygoz): pressed when the crew stands next to its doppelgangers, each box double-clicks the NPC that bears its own character's name within 10 m, so every copy is taken by the character it copies.
- `eb resetzone [one|all|force] [zone]`: Ask the game to reset a zone's lockout: one zone (the default), all of them, or forced.
- `eb catalog [cmd] [what]`: The NPC and door catalogue: with it on, every few seconds the NPCs and the doors around this box are noted, zone by zone - where each was seen last, how many looks saw it, the day, named or not, its level. Never a player, a pet, a mercenary or you; no look in a fight or while zoning. Kept in eb-catalog.json beside the install.
- `eb iqueue [cmd] [zone]`: The instance queue: a list of zones run one after another - add zones, start, stop, pause, resume, clear, move a row, set a row's copy, keep the queue under a name and put it back, or hand the driving to the tank.
- `eb creator [ic|quest|fight]`: Open the point-and-click creator for an instance file, a quest pack or a fight.
- `eb teams [cmd] [arg]`: Run teams: who runs with whom, and the crew at work in teams - forming a team's group, running its default run, sharing instances, quest lines or task lists out across the teams (breakouts), and running a task list with a regroup.

#### Module `commands.loot`

Console commands for loot: auto-looting and the loot rules, the group's loot method, handing drops out, the loot window, and coin splitting.

Type them as eb \<command> in the console, send them to the crew with eb all | others | to \<who> \<command>, or run them from a script with reg:dispatch or eb.dispatch. EB runs the economy behind them, so each one answers with a status line, a chore under way or a refusal in plain words. The Lua behind them is eb.economy.loot (the per-drop decision, the corpse sweep, the leader's hand-out), eb.economy.lootrules (the rules document), eb.economy.grouploot (method words) and eb.economy.auction.

**File:** `data/eb/commands.json` in the EB folder

- `eb loot [on|off|status|rules|method|now] [arg]`: Loot control: turn looting as you go on or off, show the loot status, show or change the loot rules, set the group's loot method, or loot the nearest corpse or chest in reach now.
- `eb lootdistro [cmd] [arg]`: Loot distribution: hand gear to the member who gains the most Resolve, assign drops from the leader's window, and follow the quotas each member still wants.
- `eb lootwin [open|claim|close]`: Drive the loot window by hand: open the nearest corpse's window, claim what is in it, close it.
- `eb coinsplit [state]`: The game's even coin split for the group: on or off sets it on the group leader's box, status says it.
- `eb langloot [status|list|want|sync] [arg]`: Language quests in a group: every member needs its own items - the first one examined starts the quest and the rest finish it - so each box says which quest it wants and what it holds, and the group leader's loot rules hand each item to a member still short of it.
- `eb stoponnotrade [state]`: The instance queue's No-Trade guard: with it on, the next loot window that holds a No-Trade drop pauses the queue - the run under way goes on, the next one waits (eb iqueue resume goes on).
- `eb checkloot`: The open loot window's drops, each No-Trade one marked; nothing is taken and nothing is paused.

#### Module `commands.monitor`

The combat monitor from the console: a fight's timeline and what went wrong, the crew's damage and healing meters, who the crew waits on, and the crew's status board.

The meters count what each box's own combat lines show; a box sends the crew only a short summary per fight, never its raw lines. A script meters a fight with eb.ui.monitor.parser and eb.ui.monitor.parse_feed.

**File:** `data/eb/commands.json` in the EB folder

- `eb anal [cmd] [arg]`: Fight analysis: the EB Anal window, and on the console what it opened on (the tab worth opening on, what to do to fill it, or why it did not open), then the summary of the last fight (the default), its timeline, why (what held each cast back, row by row), fix (the cast-stack rows EB will not cast) and export.
- `eb meters [show|current|export]`: The crew's damage and healing meters: show opens the window; current says this fight's numbers.
- `eb announcements [last|show|clear|status] [arg]`: The game's on-screen announcements this box got - the big lines across the middle of the screen (a quest update, a fight's next phase): the last ones, newest first, with how long ago. show on says each one here as it comes.
- `eb waiting`: Who the crew is waiting on: each box and what it is doing, this box's brain and its instance run.
- `eb crew [show|status|link] [arg]`: The crew board: show opens the At a Glance window; status says one line per box - its zone, mode, health and power. link puts several PCs in one crew: off unless you turn it on.
- `eb sessionwatch [status|list|on|off|freeze|gone] [value]`: Session watch: this PC's game sessions watched by their own crew. A session not heard for the freeze seconds froze, heard again it recovered, not heard for the gone seconds (or its EB stopped) it is gone; one box of the PC says each change on its console and raises SessionFrozen, SessionRecovered or SessionGone for your scripts.
- `eb effects [cmd] [state]`: The Effect Tracker: what effects are called and what they say they do, zone by zone, for whoever writes the zone's fight files. With no word its window opens; on records the detriments that land on you (Player), npc on the effects on the mobs you fight (NPC), off both.

#### Module `commands.nav`

The walking commands: walk to a spot, follow someone, walk to a named mark, keep routes out of a spot, hold a camp, go to a group member, record a path - the in-zone half of movement, typed or run from a script.

Every command here answers at once: a walk it starts runs on EB's frame pulse and the command says "issued", so a script can send it and carry on. A crew scope runs it on other boxes too: eb all follow Tankard, eb to is2 follow Tankard.

Movement is one thing: a walk along a route on the zone's .nav mesh, with the movement keys. Nothing here moves a character any other way - no straight run, no fallback walk, no swim across open water, no flying. A spot the mesh has no route to is not walked to: the command says why and the character stays where it is. A zone with no mesh refuses every walk, even a short step. Where the mesh joins two floors (a drop, a jump, a climb) the walk takes the link by itself: one tap of the jump key for a jump or a climb, none for a drop. A lift on record for the zone (the mesh fixes' lifts) is ridden: the walk stands on its board spot, clicks its lever or button once when it has one, stands still for the lift's wait and ride, then steps off at the exit.

Every command here is answered on EB for InnerSpace; check from a script with reg:unattached({ domain = "nav" }), which lists none of them.

How to walk the crew to a spot: 1. Save it once: eb marks set \<name> where you stand. 2. Send everyone there: eb all marks go \<name>. 3. Or have them follow you: eb others follow \<your name>. 4. A walk or a follow ends when it arrives. To end one early: eb walk stop (the walk a command started), eb follow off (a follow), eb stop (everything EB is doing on the box) - or a script calls eb.nav.stop().

**File:** `data/eb/commands.json` in the EB folder

- `eb walk [target] [fly|nofly]`: Walk to a spot in this zone over the zone's mesh, its drops, jumps and climbs on the way: x y z (or x,y,z), or the name of a route you recorded, a mark, something in sight by that name (the nearest whose name holds the words, within 80 m) or a map point. A spot the mesh has no way to is not walked to: the walk fails, says why, and nothing moves. Examples: eb walk 120,-4,388 / eb walk bank run / eb walk patrol,3 / eb walk patrol,loop. SOMETHING IN SIGHT BY ITS WORDS: an actor called exactly that first; else every word in a name, else in the title under it (eb walk broker, eb walk the nearest banker), else spread over the two (eb walk banker marcus) - an NPC before an object before a player, then the nearest; the, a, to, nearest are left out, and some words also mean others (vendor = merchant, repair = mender: data\eb\nav\actor_words.json). Nothing by those words: the walk is not made and the closest in sight are named. eb mm is the same word. eb walk stop ends the walk a command started. A route you recorded can be walked again and again: \<route>,\<times> walks it that many times (1 to 100), \<route>,loop until eb walk stop (or another walk) ends it - the first time from the point nearest you, every time after from the route's first point.
- `eb follow [who] [dist]`: Follow someone over the mesh by NAME: a crew member, or any player or NPC in range (the nearest of that name, an exact match first, case aside; when several share it, that is said once). A crew member is followed across zones: when it leaves the zone the follower walks to where it went, takes the zone line or the zone door and finds it again on the other side. Anyone else is found again by its name after a zone change, after the follower loses sight of it and after it despawns and comes back; a name not in range is looked for a short while, said once, then given up ("lost sight of \<name>", never a guess). target follows the name of what this character has targeted at that moment; an actor's number follows that one actor only and ends with the zone (EB Map's Track sends it for one that has no name or shares it). me - or nothing, in a crew line - is the box that sent the line; off ends the follow, and eb follow alone says how it stands. It only walks: nothing is targeted, attacked or cast at. It never follows a character someone is playing by hand.
- `eb marks [cmd] [name]`: Your saved places, in every zone: set one where you stand (or at x,y,z), list them all numbered by category, go to one by its name or its number (a place in another zone: the trip there first, then the walk), del one; cat files a place under a category, how makes a trip to it ride one way only, reload reads the file again.
- `eb blacklist [add|remove|list|clear] [what]`: Keep every route out of the spot where you stand (blacklist), or allow it again (greenlight). Typed as eb bl or eb blacklist it blacklists; typed as eb gl, eb greenlight or eb prefer it greenlights: eb bl add 5 puts a 5 m circle where you stand, eb gl add lifts it.
- `eb nav [cmd] [arg]`: The zone's mesh, the one mesh EB walks: status says whether it is loaded (or loading, or not in EB's mesh store); path \<x,y,z> the length of the route to a spot over the mesh and in a straight line; where whether you stand on the mesh; why how the last walk ended; door the zone's door lines; info the mesh's own notes; load and unload a zone's mesh; swimup \[ms\] \[height\] swims straight up on the spot (5 s, at most 15 s) to get out of a hole under water - given a height, only when you are well under it; badlegs lists the legs walks wedged on in this zone - each is kept a day and told to the router before every walk here, so the same wall is not walked into again after a restart (a leg wedged on twice is routed round) - and badlegs clear forgets them. There is no other mesh or mover to pick between. THE TRIP: status also says this box's trip - its state (Idle, WaitingForMesh, Planning, Moving, Arrived, Stopped, Failed) and why, the waypoint it is on of how many and the metres to go, the mesh in use, a note when it is held, nav is switched off or EB is paused - and the nav settings changed from the shipped ones. to \<x,y,z> walks there with the nav words after the spot: precision \<m> (the spot counts as reached that close; under 2 m a spot to stand on), fly / nofly, doors / nodoors (the trip clicks no door). plan \<x,y,z> plans the route and moves nothing: whole or partial, corners, metres, the work it took. stop (or end) ends the trip where it is. panel opens the Movement window; panel on makes it open by itself when a walk starts (and close when it ends), panel off stops that. off switches walking on the mesh off on this box - every walk is refused ("nav is switched off") - until on. set alone lists the nav settings changed; set \<setting> \<value> changes one, kept for this box and taken at once (the same as eb set nav.\<setting>): arrive, finalarrive, arriveheight, lookmin, lookmax, lookangle, lookslew, looktime, pathwindow, heightbias, fellbelow, avoid, avoidlead, avoidside, avoidwant, avoidbias, stuckdistance, stuckstrikes, stuckreplans, retreatback, jumptries, blockms, doors, doortries, doorradius, mesh, panel, dumppath (each plan written to this PC's nav store as nav-lastplan.local.json), the flight's flyauto, autodetour, flyfar, sightahead, followfly, and the router's nearcost, stepcost, funnelclear, ledgeclear when the router takes them. reset puts one setting - or, alone, all of them - back to the shipped value.
- `eb disperse [metres]`: Spread the group out evenly round you: typed on your box, every other box in your zone walks over the mesh to its own place on a ring of that many metres round you (no two share a place) and stops there. Nothing holds them there afterwards - a camp spot that holds a ring is eb others leash ring. Your own box does not move.
- `eb leash [cmd] [spot]`: Hold a camp: stay within some metres of a spot, walking back over the mesh whenever you are pulled or drift out. here holds where you stand; at x,y,z holds a point of this zone (the box walks there first); ring gives each box of a crew line its own place on a ring round the box that sent it; off lets go; status says where it holds. A second number is how far off it gives up: dragged farther than that, the box does not walk back (said once). In a fight the engine's own positioning stands, and the box walks back only well past the circle. A box its player walks out of the circle is never pulled back.
- `eb gate [scan|open|forget] [name]`: Doors and gates: scan lists the ones within 25 m (the zone's door lines and the live doors; a live door not on a line yet is learned on this PC), open clicks the nearest or the named one with its own verb, forget drops a door EB learned (a shipped line stays). Zone lines and teleporters are never clicked. eb door is the same command; a script opens a door with eb.nav.tryDoor.
- `eb navlink [cmd] [name]`: Record a crossing the mesh cannot find, walked once by hand: eb navlink jump (or climb, or drop) marks the near side where you stand; cross it, then say the same word again where you land and the bridge is recorded, on this PC, and the router uses it from then on. list shows this zone's bridges. start, add, undo, cancel, save and del do the same step by step and remove one. A lift or a moving platform (ride) is refused: it is a lift entry, not a bridge. A walk takes the links by itself - no key press needed.
- `eb record [start|drop|stop|save|cancel|status] [name]`: Record the path you walk as a route of waypoints (one every few metres, on a sharp turn and on a climb or a drop): start, drop a precise point where you stand, save it under a name (still recording), stop, cancel; status says how it stands. Routes are this PC's own, kept per zone. eb walk \<name> walks one over the mesh, point by point.
- `eb poi [name]`: Walk to a named point of this zone that holds every word you type: EB's own marks first, then the game's own map points (banks, mailboxes, bells, griffons, inns, zone doors). With no name it says what is known here, by kind.
- `eb gtgm <who> [dist]`: Go to a group member once, and stop within a few metres: in sight, or where the crew last heard it, or its zone first by the travel network. It runs on the box that types it only - never sent to the group by itself. eb follow does the same and keeps following.
- `eb regroup [on|off|now|status] [metres]`: Keep the group together, on the group's leader: a crew member more than 15 m away, with the group out of a fight for a minute, is called back and walks to the leader on the zone's mesh (the same walk as eb gtgm). on, off, now (call them back once), status.
- `eb face [how]`: Turn this box, where it stands: eb others face me turns the others the way this box faces (each reads the sender's heading where it sees it); target turns to the target; a number turns to that heading, in the game's own degrees (as /loc shows them). Nothing says which way this box faces.
- `eb movekeys [list|set|reset] [what]`: The game keys EB's walker holds and taps - your own binds in the game: list shows each role's key (forward, back, turn left / right, strafe left / right, jump, swim up / down, crouch, run / walk) and where it came from (yours, EB's default, set at start); set \<role> \<key> names one; reset \[\<role> | all\] puts EB's default back.
- `eb camera [reset]`: Put the game's camera back behind the character.
- `eb jump`: Jump once, with this character's own jump key (eb movekeys says which).
- `eb crouch`: Crouch, or stand up again: one tap of this character's crouch key (eb movekeys says which) - the same tap the fear walk makes.
- `eb runwalk`: Run or walk: one tap of the game's own run / walk switch with your key for it (Shift+R unless you moved it: eb movekeys set run / walk \<key>) - the same tap the fear walk makes. The game's own switch command goes instead once its live proof lets it out.
- `eb closer`: Follow closer: a metre nearer to the one this box follows now, each time (2 m at the nearest).
