- `eb farther`: Follow farther back: a metre farther from the one this box follows now, each time (20 m at the farthest).

#### Module `commands.quest`

The quest commands: the quest-line runner, power-level routes, the pack queue, the journal readers, languages, mission timers, single quest actions, NPC dialogs and the overseer.

Type them in the console after the console word, run them from a script with reg:dispatch or eb.dispatch, or send them to the crew with all / others / to. Each one answers: eb ql and eb pl say what is running (or that nothing is), eb queue the queue, eb dialog what an NPC shows. What EB cannot read yet it says in words: a journal read that is held back until it is proven in the game, a window whose elements are not captured, or a folder this host cannot list. A script can also drive quest packs and power-level routes through the Lua runners (eb.quest, eb.plroutes).

HOW TO RUN A QUEST PACK FROM A SCRIPT. 1. Bind the runner: local quests = require("eb.quest").bind(deps). 2. Load the pack and start it. 3. Call quests.step(run) once per tick from an EB task or a brain goal, handing travel, fights and loot to your nav, combat and loot. 4. Keep quests.pointer(run) after each step_done.

**File:** `data/eb/commands.json` in the EB folder

- `eb ql [cmd] [name]`: The quest-line runner: load a pack, start it, resume it, pause, cancel, skip a step, see its status, or list the packs.
- `eb pl [cmd] [route]`: Run a power-level route and steer it while it runs: start it (from a step), pause and resume it, end the step in hand, stop it, see where it is, list the routes or a route's STEPS, or show a route on EB Map.
- `eb queue [add|start|stop|status|clear] [pack]`: A queue of quest packs run one after another: add, start, stop, status, clear.
- `eb queststep [name]`: Show the active step of a quest, as the journal has it.
- `eb qsteps [name]`: List every step of a quest.
- `eb questdone [scan|upload|resync]`: Keep this character's list of completed quests: scan reads it from the journal, resync reads it again from the start.
- `eb lang [name]`: Learn a language through its quests.
- `eb linguist [what]`: Learn a language a Linguist sells - Halasian, Oggish, Ratongan, Stout or Ykeshan: the primer in the bags is used at once; else this box goes to its Linguist, walks up, buys the primer and uses it.
- `eb taskfile [run|list] [name]`: The task files that came with EB (the Tasks window's "Task files" tab): list them by folder, or run one as a quest line of its own.
- `eb missiontimer`: Show the mission and collection reset timers.
- `eb action <name>`: Run one quest pack verb by name, on its own, outside a pack.
- `eb actor <name> [verb]`: Interact with a quest actor: hail it, click it, or use one of its verbs.
- `eb dialog [reply|choice|ok|close] [n]`: Answer an NPC conversation, a choice window or a reward window, picking the allowed path.
- `eb questhelper [state] [first]`: A helper while you quest by hand on this box: a conversation that offers one reply gets it picked; with first, the first of several is always picked. Standing still with no conversation up, a quest giver within 10 m is targeted and hailed, and a quest object within 5 m is clicked - each at most once in 30 s. eb qh is the same command.
- `eb overseer [cmd] [arg]`: EB Overseer, the game's Overseer missions in one command. run: one pass now - the finished missions turned in, the rewards taken, the boxes and scrolls in the bags added, new missions started with the agents whose traits suit them (run auto: the start the pass by itself makes, with its gates). stop: the pass, the missions job, a trip and a share on this box. status: what the pass does or did, the day's allowance, the next missions done, this box's driver. window: EB's Overseer window. go: Go buy missions (the trip to an Administrator Agent, a new character's first agents, the buy, the broker when that is on, then the pass); buy: the trip and the buy; trip: the trip alone. missions / scrolls: the bags' missions added now / listed. agents, share, needs: every box's agents, the spare cards shared, who still needs what. set / options: this character's options. who, auto, spares, side, starter, brokerafter, broker cap, mark, agent: this PC's preferences and the agent it buys from. tutorial, broker, owned, lookup, help.
- `eb sharequest <quest>`: Offer quests of the journal to the group: one by its name (a mission is a quest here), or all of them, one a second. The game offers each to the members near and shares the ones it can.
- `eb hail [who]`: Hail an NPC: target it and say the game's own /hail, which only ever talks - never a double-click on something that can be fought.
- `eb special`: Click the nearest special object within 30 m (the glowing thing a zone wants clicked).

#### Module `commands.relay`

Talk to the crew from the console: put a crew word in front of any command, announce a line, put every box on the same target, invite and disband.

The way to send any command to the crew is the crew word in front of it: eb all \<command> (every box, this one too), eb others \<command> (every box but this one), eb to \<who> \<command> (the boxes named). Lines reach the other boxes over the crew relay and run there once; a relayed line is never sent on.

How to drive the crew from a script: 1. eb.dispatch("eb all pause") - every box pauses, this one too. 2. eb.dispatch("eb to is2 follow is1") - one box follows another. 3. eb.dispatch("eb announce pulling now") - one line every box shows.

Every command of this page answers; reg:unattached({ domain = "relay" }) lists any that a build leaves out.

**File:** `data/eb/commands.json` in the EB folder

- `eb relay <line>`: The written-out form of a crew line: eb relay all pause is eb all pause. The line starts with the crew word (all, others, to \<who>, or local for this box only), then the command. More words reach a set of boxes each box decides for itself: here = every box standing in this box's zone, never a paused one, this box too (eb relay here walk 10,2,30 walks them all to that spot; a box in another zone stays put); awake = every box that is not paused, so a box you play by hand is left alone (eb relay awake tse saved); stagger \[seconds\] = every box that is not paused, each in its turn - this box at once, then the others one after another, 2 seconds apart unless you say, at most 30 (eb relay stagger 3 gha go); mygroup = this character's group, this box too, and this box alone when it is in no group (eb relay mygroup rebuff).
- `eb marked [state]`: Mark this character so a crew line can pick it: eb to marked \<command> runs on every box whose character is marked. on, off or toggle sets this character's mark; status (the default) says whether it is marked and which boxes of the crew are. eb to \<name> marked on marks that character; eb all marked off takes every mark off.
- `eb ocdo <line>`: Do one line of the console command language your own MCP layout's buttons carry (!c -command who args ...) with EB's own systems: each -command whose who names this box (else the line's -cfw) runs EB's version - follow, letsgo, holdup, pause, resume, assist, jump, zone, zonedoor, special, evac, cast, cast on a player, use item, cancel maintained, accept reward and the reply buttons. A command EB has no version of is listed back, never guessed.
- `eb oc <line>`: Hand one line to the other automation running beside EB in this session: stop, pause, resume, or zonedoor \<door> - for this character's group only. It never moves a box for EB: a follow is eb follow and a camp spot is eb leash.
- `eb announce <text>`: Show one line on every box of the crew (and this one).
- `eb tgt <id>`: Target an actor on this box or on the crew. eb tgt \<id> targets that actor (a spawn id is the same on every box in the zone, so eb all tgt \<id> puts the crew on one target); eb tgt \<name> the nearest actor with exactly that name, else the nearest whose name holds the words; eb tgt me this character; eb tgt none, off or clear drops the target.
- `eb grab [loc|zone|target|npc|special]`: Where you are, in a line to paste into a quest, a route or an instance run: your spot and heading, the zone, your target, the nearest NPC or the nearest special (an object you can use) within 30 m.
- `eb invite [invite|disband|raid|leave] [who]`: Group up. With no name this box invites every crew character that is not in its group yet, in the order set in Settings > Group, up to a full group (type it on the leader; a crew line asking for it is refused, six boxes inviting each other is no group); a name invites that character; raid \<name> sends a raid invite; disband or leave takes this box out of its group, and eb all invite disband breaks the group up. It never invites a character someone plays by hand without EB.
- `eb mentor <who>`: Mentor a group member: this character drops to that member's level until eb unmentor. The member must be in this character's group and, when the crew has said the levels, below this character's level. eb all mentor \<name>: every box above that member's level mentors it; the member itself says no and sends nothing.
- `eb unmentor`: Stop mentoring: this character goes back to its own level. eb all unmentor stops it on every box.
- `eb event [on|off|list|fire] [name]`: Look at EB's events from the console: list the event names, switch a watch on or off, or fire one to test a helper.
- `eb share [what] [arg]`: Share through EB's hub, one thing at a time and only when you ask: plan \<name> shares one of your power-level plans, nogo \[zone | all\] your keep-out spots, travelactor \[\<it> | all\] your own travel objects (eb travelactor add); each gets a short code. get \<code> fetches a share by its code (a plan joins your plans under a new name, keep-out spots join your walker's avoid list, travel objects join your own - never over one of yours); list shows your shares and the ones shared with you; grant / revoke \<code> \<EB account> lets another EB account read one, or not; delete \<code>.
- `eb emote [words]`: An emote: one of the game's own by its word (bow, wave, cheer ...), or your own emote line of two words or more (the game's /emote). list names the game's emotes.
- `eb tell <who> <text>`: A tell to a character.
- `eb say <group|raid> <text>`: A line said in group or raid chat - the game's own chat (EB's crew line is eb announce).
- `eb agent <id> [line]`: A line from EB's agent server (the tool an agent program reads this box through), answered in one small file (EB for InnerSpace). The server hands it to the session through InnerSpace's relay - InnerSpace.exe relay is3 eb agent \<id> \<line> - and EB runs the line as a line from outside: never a Lua line, never sent on to the crew, never moving a box you play by hand (paused, or EB stopped there). The answer goes to agent\\\<session>.json in your EB data folder: the session, the agent's id, ok, the answer's words and the time - no character, no account. With no line it answers here and runs nothing (the agent server's list asks every session that way).
- `eb irc [cmd] [text]`: EB IRC: this box joins the IRC server set up in the EB IRC window (eb irc), leaves the channel and the server (eb irc end - also off or leave; eb end irc is the same line), opens EB IRC to set it up (eb irc window), says where it is and what it heard (eb irc status), or says a line in the channel (eb irc say \<words>). With nothing set up yet, eb irc opens the window and says what is missing. eb all irc joins every box; eb relay all end irc takes every box off.

#### Module `commands.travel`

The travel commands: go to another zone over the game's own travel network, preview the hops first, ride a zone's pads - every hop walked to on the mesh, never fast travel.

A trip rides the bells, wizard spires, druid rings, the guild hall and the zones' own pads, walking to each portal on the mesh and re-planning from wherever each ride lands. City bells never cross between the good and the evil cities. Each command answers at once; a trip runs on EB's frame pulse and the command says "issued". A hop whose portal the mesh has no route to stops the trip and says why - nothing is walked straight at it.

Fast travel is no part of a trip. It exists in one place, eb ft, and only on your own press: it is refused while a quest line, a power-level route or an instance run is going, and from any line a pack or a run sent.

Every command here is answered on EB for InnerSpace except eb hotzone; check from a script with reg:unattached({ domain = "travel" }).

How to take the crew to another zone: 1. Preview it: eb route \<zone>. 2. Go: eb all goto \<zone> - each box makes its own trip; a box that is already there stays. 3. Watch each box's status line for the hop it is on. 4. eb travelcancel pauses, resumes or cancels a trip.

**File:** `data/eb/commands.json` in the EB folder

- `eb goto <zone>`: Travel to another zone (or to a saved mark) over the game's own travel network: plan the hops, walk to each portal on the mesh, ride it, and plan again from where it lands.
- `eb route <zone>`: Preview a trip without moving: the hops, the network each rides, and which side this character travels as.
- `eb ft [dest]`: Fast travel to a place, on your own press only. Refused while a quest line, a pack step, a power-level route or an instance run is going, and from any line a pack or a run sent - each says why. Everything EB decides by itself travels in the world: bells, spires, rings, the guild hall and the zone's own pads.
- `eb transit [dest]`: The zone's own pads: with no destination, list this zone's pads and where each flies; with one, ride the pads to that station, walking to each pad on the mesh.
- `eb bell [dest]`: Travel by this zone's bell (docks, city bell, a guild hall's bell) to a place on its map; with no place, say where the bell goes. The walk to the bell is on the mesh; eb goto \<zone> rides bells for you.
- `eb travelmap [zone]`: With no place, list the places of the travel window that is open (stand at a bell, spire or ring). With a place, pick it: when no window is open the nearest bell, spire or ring is used to open one first. Travel inside the world, never the fast-travel shortcut. A ride inside the zone it starts (a griffon, a city bell to the docks) is waited out until the box lands - 40 m from where it picked, then still for 3 s; given up after 5 minutes.
- `eb gha [go|upkeep|exit|attune|porter] [dest]`: The guild hall: go calls you to it and waits for the hall, exit leaves by its door, attune ties you to the hall's travel beacon (stand near it), porter \[place\] walks to the hall's Coldborne EverPorter over the mesh, clicks it and picks the place in the list it opens (by the name the list shows, or its number; with no place the list is left open for eb zonedoor). EB never pays the hall's upkeep: upkeep says so.
- `eb zonedoor [entry]`: Pick in the zone-door list that is open on screen - an instance door, a porter, a zone's versions: its number, the place as the list names it (any case, with or without "The ", or the one entry holding the name - when two hold it nothing is picked and the entries are said), or last. It never clicks anything in the world; with no list open, or a list still showing its placeholders, it says so. eb all zonedoor 2 picks on every box that has the list open.
- `eb hub [zone]`: Take this box to the hub zone of an instance - the zone with its entrance, where the crew gathers before a run - by the zone's own transit, on foot over the mesh. eb all hub \<instance> sends every box there by its own way; nobody is led.
- `eb zoneroute [cmd] [what]`: Your stored zone routes: a way somewhere the planner does not find by itself, written down step by step and played back - each step an EB line (a goto, a walk, a door's verb, a pad ride, a bell) or a wait.
- `eb traveltest [start|stop|status|skip|report] [all|bell|druid|spire|hubs]`: The travel test: this box travels the network zone by zone and writes down what happened - a pass when it lands in the zone, a fail with the reason when it does not.
- `eb portalwait [what]`: Through a group port: after a wizard's or a warlock's Translocate (Translocator Spires) or a fury's or a warden's Circle of Growth (a druid portal), this box waits for the portal, walks up to it, opens it and picks the place on its map, then zones.
- `eb travelactor [cmd] [what]`: Travel objects a guild hall (or a zone) holds that send you somewhere: the Tunneler of Thalumbra, the Pennant of Skyshrine Loyalty, the Yon Gorroth Teleporter, the Coldborne EverPorter, the guild hall teleporters EB's travel data names (a Draconic Teleporter's rows ...), and your own - each used with its own verb, a click, a pick in the list it opens, or a hail (a tamer, a guide: hailed, its travel reply answered, the place picked on its station list).
- `eb hubs [list|destinations|add|remove] [what]`: The hub zones - where each instance is entered from, as the instance files say (each names its hub zone and its door), and your own additions.
- `eb stagger [on|off|reset|delay|leader] [arg]`: Space the crew's moves out so the boxes do not all move at once: on, off, reset, the delay in milliseconds, and who leads.
- `eb itinerary [state]`: Say the hops still ahead at every zone change: on, off; status says them now. eb route \<zone> shows the hops of a trip you have not started.
- `eb travelnet [cmd] [what]`: What EB knows of the travel network and of this server: scan the bells, spires and rings here (in a guild hall with none of its own: its portal wizard or druid), status, the places on record, merge; info = which ways this server has and what this box has; reload = read the server policy and the travel data again; allow / block \<way> and tle on | off = your own choice for this server, kept on this PC; methods = which ways this box can leave its zone by right now, and why not; stats = what the travel data holds, what this PC learned and the trips this PC made; save = the trip counts written now and one copy of every learned travel file.
- `eb zoneout [what]`: Leave this zone by its exit. The exits in sight and the ones the zone data knows are one list, best first: an exit by its own name (zone_to\_, exit_to\_, zone_exit, a guild hall's or a house's way out), then an object shown as an exit, the nearest first. eb zoneout takes the first; eb zoneout \<n> the one of that number; eb zoneout \<words> the first whose name or destination holds every word; list \[words\] shows them, numbered, saying where each comes from.
- `eb connection [list|add|remove] [what]`: Your own ways from one zone to another, kept on this PC and used by every trip at once. Stand at a zone line and eb connection add \<zone it leads to>: where you stand is where the trip walks into it. door \<its name> after the zone makes it a door clicked there; bell, spire or druid says this zone's bell, wizard spire or druid ring also goes there.
- `eb travelcancel [pause|resume|cancel]`: The trip under way: pause it, resume it, or cancel it. Typed as eb pausetravel, eb resumetravel or eb canceltravel it needs no argument. From a script, eb.nav.stop() ends the walk a trip is on.
- `eb zones [zone]`: The zones: where this box is (its portals on record, its guild hall, its lockouts), or one zone (its portals and the way there from here); browse the zones on record; teach every trip a zone the data does not name yet.
- `eb hotzone [list|count|refresh]`: Which zones carry bonus experience now: refresh reads the game's hot-zone rotation (the zone-reuse window's Hot Zones page), list says the last read - each entry, when it resets, its zones - and count how many.
- `eb zoneto <who>`: Go to the zone a crew member is in, the best way (as eb goto); in its zone already, nothing to do. In another copy of the same zone, the game's own move to a group member's copy. eb all zoneto me brings every box to your zone.
- `eb house [exit|status]`: Leave the house you stand in: EB walks to its door (the actor named house) and uses its Exit. status says whether a house door is in sight.
- `eb heartstone [rekindle|home|status]`: In the guild hall, walk to its heartstone and use Rekindle Bond; home casts Call to Home; status says whether a heartstone is in sight.
- `eb rallyflag [get|use|go|status]`: The guild's rally flag, a Tactical Rally Banner in the bags: use it, go (rekindle the hall's heartstone, then use it: what a rally asks of each box), see whether you carry one (status), or get one from the guild hall's strategist.
- `eb rally`: Rally the crew to you: plant your Tactical Rally Banner where you stand; once it stands, every other box (in the guild hall, with a flag) rekindles its heartstone and uses its own flag.
- `eb zoneclick`: Click the zone door here: the zone's own door where EB knows it, else the nearest exit, zone line or door within 30 m, else the NPC who zones you. Never in a guild hall.

#### Module `commands.ui`

Open and arrange EB's windows from the console: the mini, EB Main, the map, the xp board, the tool windows, the radar, saved layouts, the theme and anon mode.

EB's windows open in EB's own window host, outside the game. Every window command answers on this build: each opens its window through the window bridge (eb windows lists every window with the line that opens it). Where the overlay host cannot start - no socket library, or it is not running - a command that opens a window says that and opens nothing. The mini, EB Console, EB Main and the MCP open by themselves only on the crew's lead box - the lowest session the crew relay hears, or a box alone - so a small box of a crew opens nothing until you open it there (eb mini, eb console open, eb ui, eb mcp); the setting ui.open_on_load says lead (the default), all or off, and ui.miniOnLogin = false keeps the mini shut.

A window can leave the game window and come back: eb windows \<word> out puts it in a window of its own, eb windows \<word> in puts it back, max and restore size it, and click off gives the mouse back to a window that is set to let clicks through. A window's lock and click-through are kept for each window; a window that is out of the game waits docked while its monitor is gone, and goes back out when it returns.

**File:** `data/eb/commands.json` in the EB folder

- `eb mini [state] [list]`: The mini, this box's own bar: open it, close it, pick what it shows, press its Stop group or Go on, or make its switches flip for the whole group.
- `eb ui [panel]`: Open EB Main: the crew at a glance and the way into every window.
- `eb map [show|marks|path|roam|search|level] [words]`: The map window: you, the group, the zone's exits, travel and marks, the path layer and the areas you drew.
- `eb inbox [list|add|approve|dismiss|clear] [arg]`: The ops inbox of the character you play: EB lines an agent or a script proposes, waiting for you. list shows them, who proposed each and why, then the last few that ran; approve \<n> runs one on this box as if you typed it on EB Console; dismiss \<n> drops it; clear drops them all; add \<eb line> -- \<why> puts one in. eb ops is the same command; the Ops Inbox window shows the same.
- `eb site [home|account|download|docs|commands]`: EB's hub page in your web browser: the front page, your account page, the download, the docs or every EB command. eb web is the same command.
- `eb mcp [state] [button]`: Open the Master Control Panel: a button for every EB command, for the whole crew or one box, and every EB window in its Windows tab.
- `eb forwho [pick]`: Who the MCP's buttons go to: all (every box), group (your group), others (every box but this one), me (this box only), or boxes and characters by name, several with commas. With no word the For Who window opens: one click flips the pick, and the MCP shows the same pick.
- `eb windows [name]`: List every EB window by what it is for, with the line that opens each; a window's word opens it (eb windows glance). After the word: toggle, show or hide it; out, in, max or restore moves it out of the game window, back in, maximizes it or sizes it back; click off gives the mouse back to a click-through window (click on sets it); reset puts every window back at its default place and size. The same list as EB Main's Windows view and the MCP's Windows tab.
- `eb front [name]`: A game window to the front: eb front \<name> brings that character's game window forward on this PC - a quick switch between your games. Off until you switch it on.
- `eb boxes [draw|clear|off|on|status]`: Black boxes over this game window, which hide parts of it and let every click through: draw them, take them off, put them back or remove them, from the console line (or a HotBar button that runs the line).
- `eb rotationboard`: The Rotation Board: every box running a saved rotation (eb rotation), on one board - who casts what next, the part it plays, and when that ability is ready - with this box's saved rotations to start one from it.
- `eb xp [cmd] [name]`: Experience: the XP window (every box's level and how far into it, what each gained this session, its pace an hour and the time to its next level, and the XP potion each one has running) and a line a box on the console; board opens At a Glance on its XP column; reset starts the session numbers again from now; combat or quest flips the game's own combat or quest experience switch.
- `eb track [what] [key]`: Open a fight window: track = Track (what is around you), cd = Group Cooldowns (every box's long cooldowns), osa = Target (your target and every mob in the fight), with the threat readout on the console. eb osa and eb cd open their own window.
- `eb look [files|save|open|delete] [name]`: Your look as a file to share: the theme and your own colours written to \<EB>/data/looks/\<name>.eblook.json - a theme and colours only, nothing in it names anyone - and put on again by its name.
- `eb title [tag]`: This box's title bar: every EB window of this character shows a short tag beside its name and a soft strip of a colour across its top, so each box's windows are told apart at a glance.
- `eb font [area] [px]`: Text size per area on every EB window of the PC: the window titles, the tabs, the lists and rows, the buttons and the status line, each 12 to 20 px - or each window's own size.
- `eb console [cmd] [state]`: EB Console from the console line: what its EB tab shows, EB's lines in the All tab, time stamps, clear, open / close, and how it stands - the same choices its gear has.
- `eb radar [state] [where]`: What is around you: the Radar - a live picture from above, you the ringed dot, the wedge the way you face, a click on a dot targets it - opened (on) or shut (off); toggle flips it, status says what is up. track: EB Track (the list) instead; game: the radar drawn in the game window; both: the Radar and the game window's at once.
- `eb uireset [reset|popout|free|sync]`: Every window's opacity, scale, click-through and lock back to the defaults (the theme stays). popout and free say how a window leaves the game window (eb windows \<word> out); sync sends this box's theme to the crew.
- `eb mybutton [button|hotkey|alert] [arg]`: Your own buttons: the HotBar, or its editor. Your own hotkeys and alerts open EB's Keys and Alerts window.
- `eb battlestation [name]`: A workspace: which windows are open, kept under a name. save \<name> keeps the ones open now, delete \<name> forgets it, a name opens it, nothing lists them.
- `eb anon [state]`: Anon mode: every character name EB shows, in the windows and on the console, becomes Box 1, Box 2 ... (for a screenshot or a stream). eb all anon on does it on every box.
- `eb theme [name]`: The look of every EB window, from one setting: bw (Black & White, the default), jqb (JQB blue), neutral, light or accent. Every open window changes at once; eb theme alone says which one is on.

#### Module `commands.util`

Utilities from the console: settings and presets, timers, aliases, spoken announcements, exports, logs, the frame-rate readout, one stat or currency of this character, and a few chores.

Most of these answer on this build: settings, presets, timers, aliases, the debug areas, the frame readout, the log and report files, streamer mode, the stat reader, the voice (where the overlay can speak) and the update note. export, uiscan, tlocheck and grabloc answer too (11-18); each note says what it does and what a script uses instead.

**File:** `data/eb/commands.json` in the EB folder

- `eb set [key] [value]`: Read a setting (eb set \<key>) or change it (eb set \<key> \<value>); with no key it lists what is set. A value is plain text or a number, never a JSON text, never quotes or brackets.
- `eb preset [save|load|delete|list] [name]`: Save this box's settings as a named preset, load one, delete one, or list them. EB ships presets of its own (instance, openworld ...).
- `eb timer [add|list|clear] [arg]`: Named timers: add one (a name, when, and optionally an EB line to run), list them, clear. When is a time (30s, 5m, 1h30m) and every for again and again; at h:mm by this PC's own clock, every day for each day; level adv, ts or aa and a number - once this character has reached it (looked at every minute); or journal and a quest's name then the line - once that quest is done (looked at every 10 minutes).
- `eb alias [name] [expansion]`: Your own word for a whole line: eb alias \<word> \<line>. eb alias @\<role> \<who> names a box for eb to; eb alias \<word> off forgets it; nothing lists them.
- `eb tts [cmd] [text]`: A tell read out loud, and EB's voice. eb tts opens Keys and Alerts on its Alerts tab, where a tell is set to be read out loud; eb tts on or off makes that choice without a window (off drops at once what waits to be said); eb tts \<words> says the words through the overlay host's voice, one line after another.
- `eb stat [stat|currency] [name]`: One stat or currency of this character as a line: eb stat potency, eb stat currency \<name>. eb all stat potency makes every box answer for itself.
- `eb export [abilities|gear|settings|log]`: Write a snapshot to a file, each part by the command that already writes it: abilities (eb abilities export), gear (eb gearset save: what is worn now), settings (eb preset save export) or the log (eb dumplog dump).
- `eb debug [area] [state]`: Extra lines on the console, area by area (brain, combat, coord, crew, economy, nav, overlay): on or off; nothing lists them.
- `eb dumplog [dump|clear|file] [arg]`: Write what EB said this session to a file (dump), or forget it (clear).
- `eb fps [cmd] [arg]`: What EB costs: the frame rate and EB's share of a frame; framedump lists each job's time, stallcheck the ones over budget, bench measures for 30 seconds. They watch the 100-FPS rule: about 8 game reads a frame and no file work inside a frame.
- `eb uiscan [list|all] [window]`: Read one of the game's windows as EB sees it: its parts, by their names.
- `eb graphics [cmd] [value]`: The game's look on this box - what costs frames on a box you do not watch: the spell effects, glowing surfaces and scenery drawn or hidden, and the game's graphics preset and particle priority. eb gfx is the same command.
- `eb tlocheck [expr]`: Check that a game read EB depends on works here, and how long it takes.
- `eb script [cmd] [words]`: Your own scripts: Lua files in your scripts folder (and the shipped examples) whose header lines become real options in the Scripts window, with a panel, pages of their own and tests. eb script alone opens the Scripts window.
- `eb grabloc [coords] [item]`: Place an item at a spot (a house item).
- `eb trainer [list|go|train] [what]`: Your class trainer. list says this class's trainer in each city, the one this character goes to and the wares it would buy; go walks there and buys them (the errand run's trainer errand); train spends training points.
- `eb errands [cmd] [what]`: Run your errands: the chores you do after logging in or around a city. go is the errand run: to the class trainer for the wares this character does not know yet, the port spell, a first mount - then Call to Guild Hall. plan says what go would do. city says which city this character's errands go to, and picks one.
- `eb debugreport`: Write one report with what a fix needs: what came up, the windows, the frame cost and the last lines. Character names are left out.
- `eb streamer [state]`: Streamer mode: stand-in names, and chat, tells and coin hidden in the windows. eb all streamer on does it on every box.
- `eb update [check|apply]`: How EB updates: EB Setup does it, outside the game, each time it starts EB. Nothing in the game patches EB.
- `eb key [key] [press|hold|release] [seconds]`: A key on this box's game window: press (one tap, the default), hold (down - for some seconds, then let go - or until release), release. Nothing: the keys EB holds down; release alone lets go of every one.

#### Module `eb.actor`

Where a named actor stands - what eb.nav.follow re-plans toward.

**File:** `lua/eb/actor.lua` in the EB folder

- `actor.locOf(name) -> x, y, z | nil`: Find a named actor and read where it stands.

#### Module `eb.app.combat`

The combat plane EB builds once per box: the character's cast stack (a live holder), the one engine, the pump the pulse runs, and the facade every part of EB asks - "is it winnable", "engage", "set the preset".

In a running EB this is eb.app.combat: combat.holder is the character's live cast stack (switch its rows and tags), combat.engine the engine, combat.facade the views over it. EB's pulse calls combat.pump 4 times a second, so the engine runs whether or not a fight is on you (heals, buffs, upkeep out of combat too).

THE FACADE has two views of the same engine. facade.brain is pollable - ask isWinnable before a pull, engage a target, poll clear until the fight is over, set the preset for what you are doing. facade.ic is what an instance script uses: find, count, pull, engage, clearArea and the waits, all bounded, plus cure, dispel and the overrides.

The cast stack is found by the character's name in the imported cast-stack profiles EB knows about; a box with none runs the engine on an empty stack and describe() says why.

**File:** `lua/eb/app/combat.lua` in the EB folder

- `app_combat.new(o) -> combat`: Build the combat plane (EB's start does this once; a test or a tool builds its own).
- `combat.pump(t) -> decision | nil`: What the pulse calls: one engine step when it is due.
- `combat.reload() -> ok, line`: Read the character's cast stack again.
- `combat.describe() -> text`: One status line.
- `combat.icView(v) -> view`: The combat view for an instance run with several boxes.
- `combat.facade.brain.isWinnable(target) -> ok, why`: Ask before you pull. A guard is never winnable.
- `combat.facade.brain.engage(target, opts) -> "engaged" | "refused", why`: Start a fight: judge, target, one step. Then poll clear() each tick.
- `combat.facade.brain.clear() -> "fighting" | "clear"`: One engine step, then whether the fight is over. Poll it each tick of a fight.
- `combat.facade.brain.fightIsOn() -> bool`: Is a fight on?
- `combat.facade.brain.active() -> bool`: Is the facade driving a fight?
- `combat.facade.brain.setPreset(name) -> name`: Set the combat preset for what you are doing.
- `combat.facade.ic.find(name, opts) -> actor | nil`: Find an actor near you by name.
- `combat.facade.ic.count(query) -> n`: Count actors near you.
- `combat.facade.ic.cast(ability, who) -> ok, note`: Cast one ability now, through the engine's one send.
- `combat.facade.ic.pull(name, opts) -> ok, note`: Target a mob and open on it; the fight itself is engage's or clearArea's.
- `combat.facade.ic.engage(name, opts) -> ok, note`: Fight a named mob to the end. It waits, so it runs inside a task.
- `combat.facade.ic.clearArea(name, radius, opts) -> ok, note`: Clear every hostile in reach (guards and benched mobs are never touched). Inside a task.
- `combat.facade.ic.waitCombatEnd(ms, opts) -> ok, note`: Wait out a fight, stepping the engine meanwhile. Inside a task.
- `combat.facade.ic.waitActorDead(name, ms, opts) -> ok, note`: Wait for one actor to die. Inside a task.
- `combat.facade.ic.anyHated() -> bool`: The read an instance's combat hold waits on.
- `combat.facade.ic.detriment(q) -> bool`: Is a curable detriment up?
- `combat.facade.ic.cure(q) -> ok, why`: Cure now through the engine (one healer wins when several boxes would).
- `combat.facade.ic.dispel(q) -> status, why`: Strip a mob's buff now.
- `combat.facade.ic.setOverride(block, o) -> true`: A temporary manual override for an encounter; ic.clearOverride() ends it.
- `combat.facade.ic.setContext(ctx) -> true`: Tell the engine where you are and what you fight (the overrides' match).
- `combat.facade.ic.addOverride(spec) -> true`: Register a context override from an instance script.
- `combat.facade.ic.autoTarget(list) -> true`: Keep an instance's kill-first list with the facade.
- `combat.facade.ic.myHealth() -> pct`: Your health, for an instance script's checks.
- `combat.facade.ic.mobHealth(name) -> pct | nil`: A mob's health by name - the phase checks of a fight script.
- `combat.facade.ic.inCombat() -> bool`: Is a fight on you?
- `combat.facade.ic.amDead() -> bool`: Are you dead?
- `combat.facade.ic.npcsNear(radius) -> rows`: The NPCs near you.
- `combat.facade.ic.addTarget(id, name) -> ok`: Hand the engine a mob nobody is fighting.
- `combat.facade.ic.dropTarget(id) -> ok`: Take a straggler back.
- `combat.facade.ic.clearOverride() -> true`: End the manual override an encounter set.
- `combat.facade.ic.removeOverride(name) -> true`: Drop a registered override.
- `combat.facade.ic.setRules(rules) -> true`: Record which damage rules an encounter runs under, for the script's own branching and its status line.
- `combat.facade.ic.damageSource() -> name`: Which damage rules the encounter runs under right now.
- `combat.engine:step() -> decision`: The plane's engine step: the one throttle every caller shares (the pump, the brain's clear, an instance engage), so two callers in one frame never send two casts.
- `app_combat.findStack(o) -> result | nil, why`: Find and build a character's cast stack from the imported cast-stack profiles - the same rule eb.caststack.loader follows. EB calls it at start and on combat.reload().
- `combat.icView(v).pull(name, opts) -> ok, note`: The follower-aware pull of an instance run: only the lead box ever opens a fight.
- `combat.icView(v).engage(name, opts) -> ok, note`: The follower-aware engage. It waits, so it runs inside a task.
- `combat.icView(v).clearArea(name, radius, opts) -> ok, note`: The follower-aware area clear. Inside a task.

#### Module `eb.app.ic`

eb ic on a running box: start an instance run or loop as an EB task, see its status, stop it.

This is what the eb ic command runs: eb ic run \<zone> \[difficulty\] \[option=on|off\] \[loot=\<method>\], eb ic loop \<zone> \[minutes\] \[difficulty\], eb ic stop, eb ic status, eb ic list, eb ic reload. The run is an EB task over the live environment (EB's nav, combat engine and crew), shown to the brain as its goal, and ended by eb ic stop, eb stop or eb pause.

WHO LEADS. The box the line is TYPED on leads: its runner is the tank. A box that receives the run from another box (eb all ic run \<zone> typed on the tank) follows that box: it holds in the hub, is zoned in, moves only on the lead's camp spots, assists the lead's character, and refuses a run from a box whose character is not in its group.

A script reaches it as eb.app.ic and calls the same functions the command does.

HOW TO RUN AN INSTANCE FROM THE CONSOLE. 1. Put the instance folder where eb ic list shows it. 2. Bring every box to the hub zone, or let the run send each one there by its own travel. 3. On the tank, type eb ic run \<zone> \[difficulty\] (or eb all ic run \<zone> on the tank: the others follow it). 4. eb ic status says where it is; eb ic stop ends it and nobody moves. 5. To keep at it, eb ic loop \<zone> \[minutes\] - 0 or nothing loops until you stop it.

**File:** `lua/eb/app/ic.lua` in the EB folder

- `appic.new(o) -> launcher`: EB builds this once at start (it is eb.app.ic); you only need it to run eb ic in an app of your own.
- `launcher.launch(args) -> ok, text`: The body of eb ic: dispatches on cmd.
- `launcher.start(mode, rest, extra) -> ok, text`: Find the instance, load it, and start the run as an EB task.
- `launcher.stop() -> true, text`: Stop the run: every wait ends at once and nobody is moved; the lead tells the others to let go of their camp.
- `launcher.status() -> text`: One line about the current or last run.
- `launcher.find(word) -> dir, family | nil, why`: Find an installed instance under \<EB folder>/data/eb/ic.
- `launcher.list() -> ok, text`: eb ic list.
- `launcher.lockouts() -> text`: eb lockouts: the zones this character is saved to.
- `launcher.resetCommand(args) -> ok, text`: eb resetzone \[one\] \<zone> | all | force \[\<zone>\]: reset this box's own lockout of one zone (with no zone: the zone of the run in hand), or of every zone it is saved to. A reset is always this box's own: a crew word in front sends the line and each box resets itself.
- `launcher.resetZone(zone) -> text`: eb resetzone \<zone>: ask the game to reset one zone's lockout (the single-zone form of resetCommand).
- `launcher.follow(runner, inst, run) -> ok, why`: A follower's run: this box's own entry (the hub on its own, then held there until the lead's door takes it in), then held inside while the lead's camp spots, release and exit move it, zoned in again each time a loop's lead takes the group out and back. start uses it for a box that received the run from another box.

#### Module `eb.brain`

The autonomy brain: one goal at a time, advanced one bite per tick (about 4 a second), with interrupts that take over for death, a zone reset, a fight, being stuck, a member down, full bags and low health or power.

brain:pulse(now) is called every frame and ticks at most every tickMs (250 ms). A tick takes ONE world snapshot (inside the read budget) and does ONE bite of work: the highest interrupt that fires (death 100, zone reset 80, combat 70, stuck 60, group down 50, full bags 40, low health or power 30), else the active goal's advance(). While an interrupt runs the goal is frozen, untouched, and resumes from the same phase when it clears.

A GOAL is a table { name, ctx = { phase = ... }, advance = fn(self, b, snap) -> status, describe = fn(self) -> text }. advance returns "working" (call again), "done" (finished: it leaves the stack) or "blocked" (with a reason). It never waits: it calls the subsystems (b.sub.nav, b.sub.combat, b.sub.relay ...), which answer at once with their status. The built-in kinds are grind, vendor, travel, questline, harvest, craft and follow ({ kind = "grind", params = { camp = { x, y, z, radius }, maxKills } }).

The brain answers what it can by itself (rez offers, group invites, popups) and never stops to ask. A running EB keeps its brain as eb.app.brain; eb pause and eb resume pause it.

**File:** `lua/eb/brain/init.lua` in the EB folder

- `brain.new(deps, cfg) -> b`: Make a brain over a set of subsystems.
- `b:pulse(now) -> result | nil`: Call it every frame; it ticks at most every tickMs and returns at once otherwise.
- `b:pushGoal(spec) -> goal`: Start a goal on top of the current one (which resumes when this one is done).
- `b:setGoal(spec) -> goal`: Replace every goal with this one.
- `b:popGoal() -> goal`: Drop the active goal; the one under it resumes.
- `b:activeGoal() -> goal | nil`: What the brain is doing now.
- `b:pause(on, opts)`: Pause or resume the brain (goals freeze; a fight still runs in the combat engine). eb pause / eb resume.
- `b:stop(opts)`: Stop the brain until eb resume: the goals are dropped and every walk on the box ends, not only the brain's own.
- `b:attach(name, impl) -> ok, count, kept`: Hand the brain a subsystem that was built after it. The subsystem's table stays the same table, so whoever holds it sees the new functions.
- `b:status() -> text`: One line about the brain, for a window or eb status goal.
- `b:goalPointer() -> { goal, phase, kills, i, zone } | nil`: The active goal's resume point.
- `b:log(fmt, ...)`: Write a line to the brain's log (a goal calls b:log). A bad format is written as it is.
- `b:tick(now, dt) -> result`: ONE brain tick, whatever the time: a snapshot, the events, the stuck check, then one bite of an interrupt or of the goal. pulse calls it on its own schedule; call it yourself to step a brain in a test.
- `b:snapshot(now) -> snap`: The one read a tick makes.
- `b:consumeEvents(snap)`: Answer what the events subsystem reports, without stopping to ask: a rez offer is accepted (unless cfg.acceptRez is false), a group invite accepted or declined by cfg.acceptInvites, a popup given its default, a server shutdown noted.
- `b:resetStall()`: Clear the stuck watch: the time spent stalled starts again from nothing. A new goal or interrupt does this itself; call it when you take over a walk and do not want what came before to count.
- `b:trackProgress(snap, dt)`: The stuck watch: time spent trying to move without getting anywhere adds up (it never counts during a fight or while dead); the stuck interrupt fires when it passes cfg.stuckMs.
- `b:selectInterrupt(snap, idle) -> interrupt | nil`: Which interrupt takes this tick.
- `b:driveInterrupt(irq, snap) -> result`: Run one bite of an interrupt (entering it first when it just took over).
- `b:markPointer(pointer)`: Ask for the resume point to be saved; persistMaybe writes it no more often than cfg.persistThrottleMs.
- `b:persistMaybe(now)`: Hand the marked resume point to cfg.persist when it is due. Your persist function must queue the write (never write inside the frame).

#### Module `eb.brain.contracts`

What every subsystem gives the brain - nav, combat, quests, economy, events, relay, the world - and the statuses a goal reads back. Check your own subsystem against it.

THE ONE CONVENTION: every action a subsystem gives the brain is NON-BLOCKING, POLLABLE and IDEMPOTENT. A goal calls it once per tick with the same arguments; the first call starts the work and every later call reports progress, and it returns at once with a short status: "working" (still going, call me again), "done" (finished; movement says "arrived"), "blocked" (cannot go on now, with a reason as the second value). Movement adds "stuck"; combat answers "engaged" / "refused" and "fighting" / "clear"; a quest step answers "working", "step_done", "complete", "blocked", "need_travel", "need_combat" or "need_loot".

So a goal never waits: it asks nav.walkTo(...) each tick until it says "arrived", combat.clear() each tick until it says "clear", and so on. Long work lives in the subsystem; recovery (death, stuck, a fight, full bags) lives in the brain's interrupts, which freeze the goal and give it back where it was.

**File:** `lua/eb/brain/contracts.lua` in the EB folder

- `contracts.validate(name, impl) -> ok, missing`: Check one subsystem against the contract.
- `contracts.check(deps) -> report, allOk`: Check a whole set of subsystems at once.
- `contracts.stubs(note) -> { world, nav, combat, quests, economy, events, relay }`: Safe stand-ins for subsystems that are not built yet, so a brain or a goal runs (doing nothing) instead of failing. eb.brain fills every missing function from these on its own.
- `contracts.SPECS -> { [subsystem] = { function names } }`: The required functions: world snapshot; nav walkTo, travelTo, stop, progress, position, ensure; combat fightIsOn, isWinnable, engage, clear, active, setPreset; quests load, start, resume, step, pointer, stepTarget; economy bagsFull, junk, nearestVendor, sell, repair, restock, craft, lootPending, lootGrab; events poll, answer; relay send, barrier, groupState, role, amDriver, handoffToTank, catchup, evac.
- `nav.walkTo(x, y, z, opts) -> "working" | "arrived" | "stuck" | "blocked"`: (the contract) Walk to a spot in this zone over the mesh. Call it each tick until it is not "working".
- `nav.travelTo(zone, opts) -> "working" | "arrived" | "blocked"`: (the contract) Travel to another zone by the zone's own transit: bells, spires, rings, doors and the routes between zones.
- `nav.progress() -> movedMetres, state`: (the contract) How the current walk is going; the brain's stuck check reads it.
- `combat.engage(target, opts) -> "engaged" | "refused", why`: (the contract) Ask the combat engine to take a target. It refuses guards, fights it judges unwinnable, and targets its rules forbid; a goal then picks another target, it never forces one.
- `combat.clear(opts) -> "fighting" | "clear"`: (the contract) Poll while a fight is on: the goal does nothing else until it answers "clear".
- `quests.step(run) -> status, info`: (the contract) Advance a quest ONE step: "working", "step_done", "complete", "blocked", or "need_travel" (info = the zone), "need_combat" (info = the target), "need_loot".
- `relay.barrier(name, opts) -> "waiting" | "ready" | "timeout"`: (the contract) Wait for every member at a mark, one tick at a time (eb.relay.group's barrier).

#### Module `eb.caststack.jsonstack`

Turn a cast-stack profile's rows into the entries the combat engine runs, and hold them live.

A cast-stack PROFILE is the character's list of rows: what to cast (name, Type, Target) and when (its gates: encounter size, health and power windows, named-only, threat, renew-before-it-runs-out). build() turns each row into an ENTRY - slot order becomes priority (slot 1 = 99), the row's Type becomes its group and tag, its gates become the entry's gates - and holds back, with a reason, any row EB cannot run exactly as written. Nothing is guessed: a field neither the row nor EB's class facts can supply is counted, never made up.

THE ROW (what EB reads from an imported profile, and what you can write yourself): { slot, name, ability, type = "CA" | "NamedCA" | "NonNamedCA" | "Debuff" | "NamedDebuff" | "Combat" | "Heal" | "Res" | "Cure" | "CureCurse" | "PowerHeal" | "Buff" | "NonCombatBuff", target = "@Me" | "@Tank" | "@Group" | "@DPS1" | ... | a name, disabled, isItem, itemName, cond = { Tag = a custom tag, "#" = encounter size, "HP<" ..., ID = renew only when it runs out } }.

THE ENTRY (what the engine reads): { name, ability, group = "dps" | "upkeep" | "heal" | "cure" | "buff" | "item", priority, tags, target, gates, disabled, precast }. A row's custom Tag stays with its entry so setTagEnabled can switch every row that carries it.

How to write a cast stack by hand: 1) list the rows in priority order, slot 1 first, each { slot, name, ability, type, target, cond }; 2) put each row's conditions in cond (the keys are listed under ROW); 3) local result = jsonstack.build({ castStack = rows }, { class = "warden", facts = require("eb.caststack.classfacts").forClass("warden") }) and read result.held - each row it could not run as written, with why; 4) hand it to EB's holder: eb.app.combat.holder.rebind(result) (the switches carry across).

WHAT A ROW NEEDS. A row says when and on whom, so a Heal, Cure, Res or PowerHeal row is built from its own words when EB has no class fact for the ability: its Target, its % (a heal's trigger; left blank it is 80, and the entry says so) and its # (how many members must need it - two or more makes it a group spell). A spell built that way is a single-target one at the default weight, never an emergency heal. The class facts (eb.caststack.classfacts) refine it: a group spell, its weight, a cure's types.

WHAT HOLDS A ROW. A row is held, with its reason in result.held, only when EB cannot run it as written: a \* alias target that the profile's Aliases do not define (or the profile has aliases switched off) - it names nobody until an alias is defined; a condition key the cast stack has no rule for; a NonNamedCA row that can never fire; a Type Custom row for anything but Balanced Synergy; an item row that names an adornment's click effect (EB cannot use an adornment by name). Every other condition is read, and means the same on every kind of row (see ROW).

**File:** `lua/eb/caststack/jsonstack.lua` in the EB folder

- `jsonstack.build(profile, opts) -> result | nil, why`: Build a cast stack from its rows.
- `jsonstack.holder(result) -> holder`: Hold a built stack live for the engine and the switches.
- `jsonstack.summary(result) -> text`: One line for a log or a status window.
- `jsonstack.typeOf(name) -> type | nil`: What a row Type becomes.
- `jsonstack.Id(ability) -> text`: The entry-name form of an ability.
- `jsonstack.TARGETS -> { ["@Me"] = "Me", ["@Tank"] = "PartyTank", ["@Group"] = "AllParty", ... }`: How a row's Target becomes what the engine aims at: @Me, @Tank, @Group, @Raid, @DPS1-3, @Healer1-3, @Enchanter, @Bard; a plain name is kept as a player's name.
- `jsonstack.target(t, aliases) -> word | word, why | nil, why`: Read one row's Target. The reason never quotes the target itself (it may be a character's name).
- `jsonstack.isToken(word) -> bool`: Is this one of the engine's own target words (as opposed to a player's name)?
- `jsonstack.bound(v) -> number | nil`: Read a numeric condition the way the stack does: 0 means "not set".
- `jsonstack.gates(ctx, row, group, extra) -> reasons`: Check a row's conditions against the cast stack's own rules (jsonstack.HANDLED lists what each kind reads in its own builder).
- `jsonstack.finishEntry(ctx, row, e)`: Lay the engine's flat view over a built entry (id, group, ability, tags, target, gates, precast) and carry the row's tags onto it: its custom Tag (the switchable tag), an allow tag (the entry is built off until its tag is raised; "Trigger Only" casts as usual) and an embargo tag.
- `jsonstack.apply(result, M, itemclick) -> defined`: Hand a built stack to a set of category managers instead of a holder: each entry is defined (a fresh copy) and enabled unless it is off, item rows go to the item manager, and the stealth openers to the damage manager.
- `ctx:note(key, text)`: The build context a kind builder gets: write a note into result.notes, once per key.
- `ctx:gap(field)`: Count a gap in result.gaps (a field that is counted, never made up).
- `ctx:effective(f) -> fields | nil`: A class fact as one table.
- `ctx:template(name) -> def | nil`: A heal template from the class facts.
- `ctx:match(group, row, score) -> fact | nil`: Find the class fact a row's entry takes its kind-only fields from.
- `ctx:name(ruleName, fact, sameTarget) -> name, how`: Name an entry so saved edits keyed by name keep finding it.
- `ctx:precastFor(ability) -> name | nil`: The pre-cast row for an ability, during the build.
- `row = { slot, name, ability, type, target, disabled, isItem, itemName, cond = { ["#"], ["HP<"], ["HP>"], ["MP<"], ["MP>"], ["N_HP<"], ["N_HP>"], ["Aggro<"], ["Aggro>"], ["RW<"], ["%"], ID, Named, RD, ["Fervor<"], ["Fervor>"], Sav, ["D<"], ["D>"], MAX, RIE, Tag, ATag, AType, ETag, EType } }`: One cast-stack row, the shape build() reads. cond keys: "#" = at least that many mobs in the encounter (members, on a heal, cure or res row); "HP<" / "HP>" = MY health below / at or above; "MP<" / "MP>" = my power; "N_HP<" / "N_HP>" = the mob's health; "Aggro<" / "Aggro>" = my share of the mob's threat (100 = it is on me); "RW<" = renew a ward under this much absorb; "%" = a heal's trigger (the health of the member it aims at); ID = renew only when your own effect runs out; Named = named mobs only; RD = after the row casts it is not cast again for that many seconds (the row's own timer, on top of the game's recast); "Fervor<" / "Fervor>", Sav and "D<" / "D>" = a class's own resource (Fervor, Savagery, Dissonance); MAX = an attack only once the class's stacking effect is full; RIE = an item row only while the item is worn; Tag = a custom tag (the switch); ATag (+ AType "Trigger Only") = cast only while the tag is raised; ETag (+ EType) = held while the tag is raised. A value of 0, "" or false is unset.
- `result = { entries, held, unknown, skipped, gaps, notes, unused, precast, precastByKey, stealth, prefix, settings }`: What build() returns. entries = every built entry in slot order; held = { slot, name, type, why, entry } for a row built but not runnable as written; unknown = rows with no Type or one EB does not run; skipped = empty rows, separators, an @Raid copy of an @Group row, and everything below an end-of-stack fence; gaps = { field = count } that nothing could supply; notes = one line per thing worth knowing; precast = the pre-cast rows; stealth = the stealth openers.
- `jsonstack.HANDLED -> { dps = { ID, "#", Named, "Aggro<", "Aggro>", "HP<", "HP>", "MP<", "MP>", "N_HP<", "N_HP>" }, upkeep = { ID, "RW<", "MP<", "MP>" }, heal = { ID, "#", "%", "RW<", "MP<", "MP>" }, cure = { "#", "MP>" }, buff = { "Aggro<", "Aggro>", "MP>" }, item = {} }`: Which conditions each kind of entry reads in its own builder. Every kind also reads RD, HP, MP, N_HP, Aggro, Named, Fervor, Sav and D, so the only key that holds a row is one the cast stack has no rule for; a key that belongs to another kind of row changes nothing and is noted once.
- `jsonstack.TYPES -> { CA, NamedCA, NonNamedCA, Debuff, NamedDebuff = dps; Combat = upkeep; Heal = heal; Res, Cure, CureCurse, PowerHeal = cure; Buff, NonCombatBuff, UseChannelerTab = buff }`: Every row Type EB runs and the kind of entry it becomes (typeOf(name) answers one of them). Res rows carry the tag REZ, Cure CURE, CureCurse CURE_CURSE, PowerHeal POWER_HEAL, CA CA, Debuff DEBUFF, Combat COMBAT_UPKEEP; NonCombatBuff is a buff refused in combat; UseChannelerTab is a Channeler's Construct's Sacrifice, kept up on your own pet in a fight while the pet's health is at or above the Channeler tab's line.
- `jsonstack.ALIAS_UNDEFINED -> text`: The reason a row is held when it aims at a \* alias that the profile's Aliases do not define: it names nobody until one is. Match on this constant, not on the words.
- `jsonstack.ALIAS_SWITCHED_OFF -> text`: The reason a row is held when it aims at a \* alias but the profile has Enable Aliases off: it names nobody.
- `jsonstack.BLANK_HEAL_PCT -> 80`: The % a Heal or PowerHeal row gets when it has none (the value EB's cast stack loader fills in): the row casts when its target is at or under it. The entry says so (entry.from.fields) and the build notes it once.

#### Module `eb.caststack.jsonstack_live`

The live cast stack: the SAME entries every engine step, and the switches a fight script uses - one row by name, or every row carrying a tag.

The engine reads holder.entries() every step and skips any entry whose disabled flag is set, so a switch takes effect on the very next step and STAYS (nothing rebuilds the stack behind your back). Hold ONE holder per character - in a running EB that is eb.app.combat.holder - and rebind it when the profile is read again: every row's on/off state is carried across by its name.

A switch's on is true (on), false (off) or nil (flip). Each answers true and a line ("2 row(s) tagged 'burn' off"), or false and why ("no cast-stack row carries tag 'x'").

**File:** `lua/eb/caststack/jsonstack_live.lua` in the EB folder

- `live.holder(result) -> holder`: Make a holder. jsonstack.holder(result) is the same call.
- `holder.entries() -> entries`: What the engine reads each step. Read it to show a stack, or to check a row's disabled flag.
- `holder.setEntryEnabled(name, on) -> ok, text`: Switch one row on or off.
- `holder.setTagEnabled(tag, on, partial) -> ok, text`: Switch every row carrying a tag together: hold the burn rows in phase 1, open them in phase 2.
- `holder.get(name) -> entry | nil`: One entry by its name.
- `holder.rebind(newResult) -> holder`: Swap in a rebuilt stack, keeping every row's on/off state by name.
- `holder.precast() -> rows`: The stack's pre-cast rows.
- `holder.precastByKey() -> map`: The pre-cast pairs by ability, as the engine looks them up.

#### Module `eb.combat`

The combat engine: one decision per step from the cast stack - interrupts, heroic opportunities, dispels, mez, heals, rez, cures, power, upkeep, buffs, items, then the damage rotation - with guards never attacked and unwinnable fights given up.

The engine OWNS the fight. A script never casts the rotation by hand; it shapes what the engine does (switches, tags, presets, overrides, a target lock, an interrupt list) and lets the engine step. Each step reads the world once through the game layer's combat shim, picks the first category that has something to do, in a fixed order (engine.ORDER), and sends ONE cast - or holds and says why ("casting", "paused", "nothing to cast").

THE SEND GUARD. The engine watches what the game does with each cast. A cast is TAKEN when the cast bar runs or the ability goes on its recast; one the game does not take within a second is REFUSED. One send goes out at a time (the step holds "landing" until the last one is taken or judged), and at most one every half second: an instant art sent every step was a line the game could not take. A refused ability rests at that target for ten seconds, doubling for each refusal in a row up to a minute; refusals in a row at one actor rest the actor (a member is passed over by heals, cures and buffs, a mob by every target path); refusals at two targets mean the game takes nothing from this character (feigned, silenced, a state EB cannot read), so every send holds for a few seconds. A person's own order (eb rez now, eb cure now, eb cast) goes out past the rests and is judged like any send. A character that is stunned or mezzed casts nothing. eb anal why says what rests and for how long. THREE RULES NO SETTING CAN CHANGE. A guard is never selected as a target, and an AE is never fired with a guard in AE reach. A fight whose kill time stays past the limit after its grace period is given up and that mob is benched for the session. Readiness is always asked of the game, every time - an entry never carries its own recast timer.

In a running EB the engine is eb.app.combat.engine, stepped by the pulse 4 times a second; work on that one rather than building a second engine (two engines would both cast). A test or a tool builds its own with combat.new.

OVERRIDES are context-scoped changes the engine applies only while the context matches (a zone, an encounter, a mob, or a temporary manual one): turn AE, mez or heroic opportunities off, force tags, lock or assist, cap the give-up time, pause casting. With nothing matching, behaviour is exactly the default.

ON EB FOR INNERSPACE TODAY the engine's game reads cover the target, the group, hostiles, readiness, the cast bars, line of sight, your maintained spells, whether a mob is stunned or mezzed, and each member's distance. Some reads are not provided yet, and the parts that need them stay quiet (they never guess): the heroic-opportunity wheel (selectHO), "this mob has a buff to strip" (selectDispel; the on-cue engine:dispel works without it), your class's own resource reads (Savagery, Dissonance, a stacking effect at full) and the main assist's target (setAssist has no effect). A cast-stack row that needs one of them waits and says why. The engine's selection logic itself is the same on both targets.

A KNOWN LIMIT, SAID PLAINLY: the engine chooses the mob to fight (selectTarget never chooses a guard), but a damage cast goes to the game's current target. When your current target is not a fair fight - a guard you clicked, say - the engine picks another mob for its checks while its art still goes to what you have targeted. Target the mob the engine chose (game.TargetActor(engine:selectTarget(engine:snapshot()).id)) before you let it fight, and never leave a guard targeted.

How to script a fight with the engine: 1) take EB's engine (eb.app.combat.engine) - never build a second one in game; 2) shape it for the encounter: setContext / addOverride for the zone or the named, setInterruptList for the casts worth stopping, setMezList for the adds, lockTarget or the kill-first list for the order; 3) switch the cast stack's rows and tags for each phase (eb.app.combat.holder.setTagEnabled); 4) let EB's pulse step it - poll engine:activeOverride() and the decisions for your status line; 5) when the fight is over, clearOverride, clearLock and clear the lists you set.

**File:** `lua/eb/combat/init.lua` in the EB folder

- `combat.new(deps) -> engine`: Build an engine over a game layer and a cast stack.
- `engine:step() -> decision`: ONE decision: read the world, pick the first category with something to do, send its cast. A decision the aim or the send guard holds, or another box's claim takes, sends nothing and the step goes on to the next category.
- `engine:toggle(which, onOff) -> true`: Switch a category or a tag. A custom tag also switches the holder's rows that carry it.
- `engine:tagEnabled(tagList, entry) -> on`: Are these tags on right now?
- `engine:setCasting(on) -> casting`: Pause or resume the engine's casting.
- `engine:setLoSGate(on) -> on`: The line-of-sight gate.
- `engine:castNow(ability, who, opts) -> ok, text`: ONE checked cast by name, what eb cast and an MCP button's ability press do. A row of this character's cast stack says what kind of spell it is; an ability that is no row goes only when this character has it in its own book. An attack goes only at the mob the engine fights (never a guard, a merchant or a citizen), a beneficial spell on this box, and with who on that member alone. It is paced like any cast of the stack: not while the cast bar runs, the last cast lands or the send guard rests it.
- `engine:abilityHeld(line) -> bool`: Is this ability on hold by an embargo?
- `engine:mineOnMob(ctx, entry, mob) -> bool`: Is my own spell of this row still on the mob? A damage row whose Ignore Duration box is off waits for it to run out.
- `engine:isGuardMob(mob) -> bool`: Is this a guard? Guards are never targeted.
- `engine:isTooStrong(name) -> bool`: Has this mob been benched as unwinnable?
- `engine:forgetStrong()`: Forget every benched mob (after a gear upgrade, say).
- `engine:selectTarget(ctx) -> mob | nil`: Which mob the engine would choose now, without casting.
- `engine:snapshot() -> ctx`: The world as one step sees it.
- `engine:lockTarget(id) -> true`: Fight this mob first while it is a fair fight (above assist and the kill list). clearLock() ends it.
- `engine:clearLock() -> true`: End a target lock.
- `engine:setAssist(name) -> true`: Fight whatever this player is fighting. clearAssist() ends it.
- `engine:clearAssist() -> true`: Stop assisting.
- `engine:setAutoTarget(list, opts) -> true`: Give the engine a kill-first list. A non-empty list turns auto-target on by itself.
- `engine:addAutoTargetActor(name, opts) -> ok`: Add one name to the kill-first list (and turn auto-target on).
- `engine:removeAutoTargetActor(name) -> true`: Remove one name from the kill-first list.
- `engine:clearAutoTargetActors() -> true`: Empty the kill-first list.
- `engine:setAutoTargetEnabled(on) -> true`: Switch auto-target on or off without losing the list.
- `engine:setOutOfCombatScan(on) -> true`: Let the kill list start fights, not only finish them.
- `engine:setScanRadius(r) -> true`: How far the kill list looks.
- `engine:setScanHeight(h) -> true`: How far up or down the kill list looks: a mob on the floor above or below is passed over. Its height is read only while one is set.
- `engine:setRescanSec(s) -> true`: How long a pick of the kill list holds before another candidate takes its place. A pick that dies, or leaves the scan, goes at once.
- `engine:suppressAutoTarget(key) -> true`: Hold auto-target for a reason, without changing its settings.
- `engine:releaseAutoTarget(key) -> true`: Lift one hold on auto-target.
- `engine:addOverride(profile) -> ok, name`: Register a context override (replacing one with the same name). It applies only while its match does; the highest priority wins a conflicting key.
- `engine:removeOverride(name) -> true`: Drop a registered override.
- `engine:clearOverrides() -> true`: Drop every registered override.
- `engine:setContext(ctx) -> true`: Say where you are and what you fight, for the overrides' match. The zone otherwise comes from your own read.
- `engine:setEncounter(name) -> true`: Shorthand for setContext({ encounter = name }).
- `engine:setOverride(directives, opts) -> ok`: A temporary manual override, above every registered one, until clearOverride() or its time runs out.
- `engine:clearOverride() -> true`: End the manual override.
- `engine:activeOverride() -> override | nil`: Which override is in force, for a status line.
- `engine:resolveOverride(ctx) -> directives`: What the overrides would change right now, without stepping.
- `engine:setInterruptList(list) -> true`: Interrupt these casts with the stack's interrupt art (an entry tagged INTERRUPT, STUN, STIFLE or KNOCKDOWN), ahead of every other category.
- `engine:setInterruptAll(on) -> true`: Interrupt everything, not only the list.
- `engine:setDispelOn(on) -> true`: Dispels on or off (an entry tagged DISPEL or STRIP strips a named's beneficial buff).
- `engine:setMezList(list) -> true`: The mez order (entries tagged MEZ or ROOT do the mezzing; toggle("mez", false) turns it off).
- `engine:setMezRenewSec(sec) -> true`: When to renew a mez.
- `engine:setHOExcludes(list) -> true`: Keep some abilities out of heroic opportunities.
- `engine:setHOOffensiveOnly(on) -> true`: Heroic opportunities in fights only.
- `engine:raiseTag(tag, sec, why) -> true`: Raise a timed tag: rows that cast only while their tag is raised cast now; rows blocked while it is raised hold.
- `engine:tagFor(tag, sec, mode) -> true`: A timed tag in one call: raised, switched for the window, and put back when it ends.
- `engine:tagLive(tag) -> bool`: Is a timed tag raised now?
- `engine:setPrecastMap(map) -> true`: Cast one ability right before another (the stack's own pre-cast rows already do this).
- `engine:setPrecastWindow(ms) -> true`: The pre-cast window.
- `engine:setPositioning(on) -> true`: Positioning help on or off.
- `engine:setPosition(mode, range) -> true`: Where to stand for the fight. A step's decision carries it with moves = false: EB does not move in a fight for it yet, and the engine says so once per mode asked.
- `engine:after(ms, fn) -> true`: Run something later on the engine's own clock, without a timer of your own.
- `engine:findHostile(name) -> mob | nil`: Find a hostile by name.
- `engine:anyHated() -> bool`: Is anyone in the group in a fight?
- `engine:npcsNear(radius) -> rows`: The NPCs near you, in combat or not.
- `engine:addTarget(id, name) -> ok`: Hand the engine a mob nobody is fighting (a straggler); it is engaged ahead of the kill list. dropTarget(id) takes it back.
- `engine:dropTarget(id) -> ok`: Take a straggler back.
- `engine:dispel(q) -> status, why`: Strip a mob's beneficial buff now, with the stack's dispel art.
- `combat.ORDER -> { "selectInterrupt", "selectHO", "selectDispel", "selectMez", "selectHeal", "selectRez", "selectCure", "selectPower", "selectUpkeep", "selectBuff", "selectItem", "selectDps" }`: The fixed order of the categories a step tries; the first that has something to do wins the step.
- `combat.GUARD_WORDS -> { "guard", "sentinel", "sentry", "watchman", "militia", "warden", "protector" }`: A mob whose name or title contains one of these is a guard. Name your own fixtures and test mobs with care.
- `combat.TTK_MAX_MS -> 300000`: A fight whose kill time stays past 5 minutes after the 45-second grace window (combat.TTK_GRACE_MS) is given up. An override can cap it lower (ttkMax).
- `combat.killEta(hpStart, hpNow, spentMs) -> ms | nil`: How long until a mob dies at the rate it is losing health - the engine's winnability measure.
- `combat.namesGuard(text) -> bool`: The guard-word check on its own.
- `engine:passesGate(entry, ctx, mob) -> nil | gate`: Why an entry would or would not cast right now - the answer to every "why does it not cast X". The step runs it on each candidate; call it yourself to debug a stack.
- `engine:winnable(ctx, mob) -> ok, why`: The winnability check each step makes: two health readings of the same mob, the time between them, and the kill time they imply (combat.killEta).
- `engine:loadStack()`: Read the cast stack for this step: the enabled entries in stack order, and the damage entries sorted by priority. A step does it first; call it yourself before you use a category selector (engine:selectHeal ...) outside a step.
- `engine:cast(dec) -> sent`: The one place a cast leaves the engine. Send your own decision through it so it takes the same path as the engine's (the crew's one-healer arbitration, when attached, sees it too).
- `engine:runTimers(now)`: Run the callbacks engine:after scheduled that are due (timed tags end this way). The step calls it first; call it yourself only when you drive the engine without stepping.
- `engine:selectInterrupt(ctx) -> decision | nil`: The interrupt category - first in the step's order, ahead of heals.
- `engine:mobCasting(ctx) -> cast | nil`: What the kill target is casting right now.
- `engine:interruptArt() -> entry | nil`: Which art the engine interrupts with.
- `engine:selectDispel(ctx) -> decision | nil`: The dispel category (third in the step's order). setDispelOn(false) turns it off.
- `engine:dispelArt() -> entry | nil`: Which art the engine strips buffs with.
- `engine:selectItem(ctx) -> decision | nil`: The item category: worn click effects kept like combat arts, aimed at a role or a player by their target.
- `engine:itemGate(entry, ctx, who) -> nil | gate`: The item entries' own gate: an item reads its own readiness, never an ability's.
- `engine:clearStragglers() -> true`: Take back every mob handed to the engine with addTarget.
- `engine:hasStragglers() -> bool`: Are there stragglers to engage?
- `combat.U -> { splitTags, killEta, validMob, isAE, mobCount, decision, lowestOf, anyWord, lineKey, fn, call }`: The engine's small pure helpers, shared with scripts (see eb.combat.combat_util).
- `combat.ENGAGE_RADIUS -> 30`: How far (metres) the engine looks for hostiles and counts an encounter. combat.GUARD_AE_RANGE (30) is how close a guard keeps every AE entry from firing; combat.TTK_GRACE_MS (45000) the grace window before a fight is judged; combat.MEZ_RENEW_SEC (10) when a mez is renewed; combat.PRECAST_WINDOW_MS (1500) how long a pre-cast is not fired again.
- `decision = { kind, ability, target, reason, entry, sent, sendWhy, at, position, mob, itemName }`: What engine:step returns when it cast: kind = "interrupt" | "ho" | "dispel" | "mez" | "heal" | "rez" | "cure" | "power" | "upkeep" | "buff" | "item" | "dps" | "precast"; target = "Target" (the game's current target), "Me", an actor id or a role word; reason = a short why ("Member2 at 40%", "priority 97", "interrupt Fixture Blast"); sent / sendWhy = what the game answered; position = the positioning intent (eb.combat.combat_pos). A hold is { hold = true, reason, mob, position }.
- `entry.tags carries ";"-separated tags: AE, CA, DUMBFIRE, EMERGENCY, INTERRUPT, STUN, STIFLE, KNOCKDOWN, DISPEL, STRIP, MEZ, ROOT, CC, HO_STARTER, REZ, CURE, CURE_CURSE, POWER_HEAL ...`: The tags the categories look for on an entry: an AE entry is vetoed with a guard in reach and by disableAE; EMERGENCY makes a heal jump the queue; INTERRUPT / STUN / STIFLE / KNOCKDOWN mark the interrupt art; DISPEL / STRIP the dispel art; MEZ / MESMERIZE / ROOT / CC the mez arts; HO_STARTER (or HO_OPENER) the heroic-opportunity opener; REZ / CURE / CURE_CURSE / POWER_HEAL the cure-family rows. Any tag can be switched with engine:toggle.
- `{ name = part of a mob's name, hp = least health %, maxhp = most health %, checkcollision = true (only in line of sight), aggroonnotme = true (only while it is NOT on you), aggroongrouponly = true }`: One row of the kill-first list (setAutoTarget, addAutoTargetActor, an override's autoTarget.list). A plain name is the same as { name = name }. List order is the priority; every match is by part of the name, any case.

#### Module `eb.coord.arbiter`

"Only one of us does this": before a box group-cures, cures or rezzes a member, it claims the action over the crew relay; exactly one box acts, and if it fails, the next one takes over.

Each box wanting the same action (the same cure on the same member) lays down a bid and waits a short claim window (150 ms) to hear the others. The winner is decided the same way on every box - the lowest role rank, then the lowest box id - so it never depends on who was fastest. The winner acts and says so; if it never reports the cure landed within the failover time (2.5 s: it died, or the cast never went out), the others drop it and the next box acts. A box that cannot cast at all hands the claim over at once.

How to claim an action: 1. Make one arbiter per box: Arb.new{ box, role, link = relaylink, clock = P.now }. A link has ONE arbiter: asking again hands back the one that exists. 2. Each tick, ask arb:request(req). "go": cast now, then arb:acted(req, now, ttlMs). "wait": the window is open - ask again next tick. "standdown": another box has it. 3. When it landed, arb:done(req, true, now, restMs); when it did not, arb:done(req, false) (the next box takes over); when you cannot cast at all, arb:fail(req); when the need went away, arb:release(req); when this box cannot act at all (dead, zoning, held), arb:standDown() gives up everything it holds or bid for. 4. Run arb:poll(now) every tick.

**File:** `lua/eb/coord/arbiter.lua` in the EB folder

- `Arb.new(deps) -> arb`: Make this box's arbiter. With a link, bids travel to the crew and theirs reach it.
- `arb:request(req, now) -> "go" | "wait" | "standdown"`: Ask to do an action. The first ask lays down this box's bid; every later ask in the window answers the same winner as every other box computes.
- `arb:acted(req, now, ttlMs) -> true`: Say you cast it. The crew stands down; the failover clock starts.
- `arb:done(req, landed, now, restMs) -> ok`: Report the outcome.
- `arb:fail(req, now) -> ok`: Give the claim up now: you cannot cast it at all (out of power, out of range, the ability is not ready).
- `arb:release(req, now) -> ok`: Withdraw: the need went away before you acted (the member was cured by something else).
- `arb:standDown(now) -> n`: This box cannot act at all right now (dead, zoning, held): give up everything it holds or bid for, so nobody waits out a timer on a box that is not there. One line per claim.
- `arb:onClaim(e, now)`: Take in another box's bid, act, done, fail or release. A relaylink calls it for you; call it yourself only when you carry claims over your own transport.
- `arb:poll(now)`: Pump the claim windows and the failover timers. Call it every tick.
- `arb:list(now) -> { { key, action, target, scope, holder, phase, mine, bidders, leftMs } }`: Every claim this box knows of, for a status window. It only reads.
- `arb:rev() -> n`: The arbiter's change counter: a window redraws when it moves.
- `arb:statusOf(action, target, scope, now) -> "idle" | "acting" | "bidding" | "standdown" | "resting"`: Where this box stands on a claim, for a status line. It only reads: it never places a bid.

#### Module `eb.coord.rules`

Coordination in plain rules: "when the tank casts X, the healers cast Y", "when this line is said, hold that ability for 20 seconds", "a moment after this, if that follows, do this" - for one box, the group or the raid.

A RULE is a trigger, an optional delay, an optional follow-up gate, an action and a scope. The trigger is something seen on this box: an ability cast (by me, a role, a class, a character - or a mob, by the cast's name), a chat, text or emote line, a zone change, an eb.events event, a detriment on me, or a named TAG another rule fired. The action is a cast (or use, interrupt, assist, cure, joust, move, stop) for EB's combat and walker to carry out, firing a tag, raising or lifting an EMBARGO (a hold on an ability), or one crew command line.
