A rule with a typo is kept and shown with what is wrong, and never runs: coord:add answers its problems.

Rules compose: a rule's action can fire a tag that is another rule's trigger. A rule whose scope reaches the group or the raid sends ONE message over the crew relay (through eb.coord.relaylink); every box that hears it runs its own matching rules locally and never sends it on, so a rule reaches the crew in exactly one hop. Every box on the uplink hears every line, so a group-wide line carries a token made from the group's members (hashed: no name travels) and a box of another group - or in no raid, or in another raid - drops it; a rule that names a character reaches that character wherever it is.

The engine reads no game: facts come in through coord:feed (or coord:bindEvents, which feeds it from eb.events), actions go out through the coord:onIntent handler, and EB's combat asks coord:holdsCast before it casts.

Give each box the rules for its OWN abilities, and give a rule that reacts to a tag the scope "self": every box that owns the ability then acts for itself, exactly once. (A tag-reaction rule with a group or role scope that sits on every box acts twice on the boxes it reaches.)

How to coordinate the crew with a rule: 1. Make one engine per box: Coord.new{ me = { box, name, role }, link = relaylink, clock = P.now }. 2. Add rules with coord:add (the rule format below), the same list on every box. 3. Hand intents to your caster with coord:onIntent(fn) and the state its casts must respect (a tag is up, a hold starts or ends) with coord:onSignal(fn), and feed facts (coord:bindEvents(events) for chat, text and zoning; coord:feed for casts you see). 4. Run coord:tick(now) from a pulse job: it fires delayed rules, closes gates and expires embargoes and tags.

**File:** `lua/eb/coord/rules.lua` in the EB folder

- `Coord.new(deps) -> coord`: Make a coordination engine for this box. With a link it also hears the tags other boxes fire.
- `coord:onIntent(fn)`: Where actions go: your handler casts, assists or runs the crew line (usually by handing it to EB's combat or to reg:dispatch).
- `coord:onSignal(fn)`: Where the state the casts must respect goes: the rows that wait for a tag cast while it is up, a held ability is not cast. EB's own casting listens through eb.coord.act.
- `coord:add(rule) -> id, problems`: Add one rule. An embargo rule with action.bindAbility also registers the ability to hold while its tag is up.
- `coord:addAll(list) -> { ids }`: Add several rules at once (an imported list, a saved set).
- `coord:get(id) -> rule | nil`: Look up a rule.
- `coord:remove(id)`: Remove a rule.
- `coord:enable(id, on)`: Switch a rule on or off without removing it.
- `coord:all() -> { rules }`: List the rules (a rules window draws from this).
- `coord:replaceAll(list) -> { ids }`: Replace every rule at once (the saved file read again). What waited on a rule that is gone is dropped.
- `coord:rev() -> n`: The engine's change counter.
- `coord:feed(fact, now)`: Tell the engine what happened. Every enabled rule whose trigger matches starts (now, or after its delay), and a waiting gate the fact satisfies goes through.
- `coord:tick(now)`: The engine's clock: fire rules whose delay is up, close gates whose window passed (a "require" gate drops, a "block" gate acts), and expire embargoes. Run it from a pulse job every frame or two.
- `coord:holdsCast(ability, now) -> held`: The question EB's combat asks before it casts: is this ability on hold right now?
- `coord:activeEmbargoes(now) -> { { key, scope, label, until } }`: What is on hold, for a status line or a window.
- `coord:bindEvents(events) -> ok`: Feed the engine from eb.events: ChatLine becomes a chat fact, IncomingText a text fact, Announcement an announce fact, ZoningStarted and ZoningFinished zone facts. Casts are fed by whoever sees them (coord:feed).
- `coord:tagsNow(now) -> { { tag, from, at, leftMs, relayed } }`: What tags are up, for a status line or a window.
- `coord:liftHold(what, now, quiet) -> n`: Lift a hold by hand before its time is up.
- `coord:fireTag(tag, scope, ms, now)`: Fire a tag from this box yourself: it is up here, the rules that wait for it run, and ONE line tells the group (or the raid).
- `coord:raiseHold(tag, scope, ms, now)`: Raise a hold on a tag from this box yourself: held here, and said to the group (or the raid) once.
- `coord:hello()`: Say this box has joined (or come back): every box that holds something says it again, so the box knows what is on hold.
- `coord:resay(now) -> n`: Say again every hold this box raised, with what is left of it - for a box that joined, or after the group changed. One line a hold.
- `rule = { id, name, enabled, trigger = { ... }, delayMs, gate = { ... }, action = { ... }, scope }`: The rule format. trigger.kind is "cast" (with who and ability, or mob: a mob's cast by its name or number), "chat", "text" or "emote" (with match, optional chan; a chat rule also hears text lines and the other way round; emote is a mob's line or an on-screen warning), "zone" (with event "ZoningStarted" or "ZoningFinished"; none = either), "tag" (with tag), "event" (with event, an eb.events name), "det" (a detriment lands on me; type is any, arcane, noxious, elemental, trauma or cursed) or "bind" (no trigger: a standing rule that holds a row while a hold is up). trigger.who is "" or "anyone" (any actor), "self" (this box), "@npc" (a mob), a role ("tank", "healer", "mez", "@priest" = healer, "@fighter" = tank), a class or a character's name; trigger.ability may list several separated by ";", or be "\*" for any. delayMs waits that long after the trigger (at most 10 minutes); everyMs is how soon the rule may act again (default 1 s). gate = { kind, match | event | tag, withinMs (default 3000), mode = "require" (act only if it happens within the window) | "block" (act only if it does NOT) }. action.kind is "cast" or "use" (a row of this character's cast stack, by its ability's name, with an optional target), "interrupt", "assist", "cure" (what = group, single or any: one priest casts it, by claim), "joust" (dir = out, in or outback, backMs, metres), "move" (walk to x, y, z on the mesh, and back after backMs), "stop" (what = dps or all, durationMs: nothing leaves this box for a while, at most two minutes), "firetag" (with tag), "embargo" (with ability or tag, and durationMs, default 20000; or with bindAbility and tag: hold that ability while the tag's embargo is up), "lift" (with ability or tag; "liftembargo" is the same word) or "crew" (with line, one eb command line). scope names who acts: "self" (this box), "group", "raid", a role, a class, or a character or box name.
- `fact = { kind = "cast" | "chat" | "text" | "zone" | "event" | "tag", ... }`: The fact format coord:feed takes. cast: { kind = "cast", actor, name, role, subclass, ability, isMe, isNPC, castId } (a mob's cast carries its number). chat and text: { kind, text, chan, speaker }. announce: { kind = "announce", text }. zone: { kind = "zone", event = "ZoningStarted" | "ZoningFinished" }. event: { kind = "event", event = "\<name>", payload }. det: { kind = "det", type }. tag: { kind = "tag", tag, from, scope, relayed }.
- `intent = { kind, ability, target, scope, rule, name, relayed, at, line }`: The intent format onIntent hands over: kind is "cast", "use", "interrupt", "assist", "cure", "joust", "move", "stop" or "crew"; ability and target say what to cast on whom; line is the crew command for a "crew" intent; the rest of the rule's action (dir, metres, x, y, z, what, durationMs ...) comes along; rule is the rule's id, name its name and relayed is true when another box's rule set it off. Only intents meant for this box (in the rule's scope) are handed over.

#### Module `eb.economy`

The economy as one object: bags, selling, repair, restock, depots, bank, mail, broker, loot, crafting and the ledger, every part built over one table of window actions (the drive), plus the nine calls EB's brain makes between goals.

economy.new{ drive = ... } builds every part over ONE drive table - the window actions for bags, worn gear, merchants and the mender, depots, the bank, the mailbox, the broker, the loot window, trades and crafting stations (eb.economy.drive lists them all). The parts are fields of the economy: eco.inventory, eco.vendor, eco.depot, eco.bank, eco.mail, eco.broker, eco.loot, eco.auction, eco.commissions, eco.ledger, eco.craft, eco.harvest, eco.gearup, eco.transmute, eco.adornments, eco.writs, eco.grandmasters, eco.collections, eco.skilllevel and eco.tse.

EVERY ACTION IS A POLLED JOB: call it once a tick with the same arguments; it starts the work the first time, advances it a bite each call after, and answers at once with "working", "done" or "blocked" plus a plain reason. Calling with the same arguments resumes the same job; a finished job is replaced by a fresh one on the next call. Nothing waits, loops to completion or touches a file on the game thread.

FAIL-SAFE: nothing is sold, destroyed, transmuted, deposited or mailed unless a rule you configured picks it, and every pick still passes the safety gate (eb.economy.rules): protected items, items whose details were never read and bound items you did not opt in are always kept. Every buy answers the game's purchase question Yes only when it names the exact item being bought.

IN THIS BUILD the economy does not run inside EB yet: EB does not build it at start, so the item and loot commands answer "not wired yet", and the drive over the game's windows is not complete. A script can build its own economy over a drive it provides (the docs' examples run on an offline drive), and every planning call - what would be sold, kept, deposited, mailed or listed, and at what price - works on any drive.

How to run an economy job from a script: 1. Build the drive: a table of the window actions you can do (missing ones refuse with "blocked"). 2. local eco = require("eb.economy").new{ drive = drive, cfg = settings, me = snapshot, relay = crew } 3. Call the job once a tick (eco.vendor:sell(), eco.depot:topUp(rows) ...) until it answers "done" or "blocked". 4. Read what happened: eco.ledger:status(), or the job's reason when it was blocked.

**File:** `lua/eb/economy/init.lua` in the EB folder

- `settings = { bags, protect, depot, vendor, loot, broker, bank, mail, craft, transmute, harvest, gear, examineBudgetPerMin }`: The economy settings document (every key optional; economy.new and rules.load fill the safe defaults): bags = { fullThreshold = 3 } (that many free slots or fewer counts as full); protect = { names = { \["lowercase name"\] = true } } (never sold, destroyed, transmuted or deposited); depot = { keep = { \["name"\] = true } (never deposited), depositRule = a filter spec (eb.economy.filter) }; vendor = { sellList = { exact names }, sellJunk = false, sellTiers = { Rarity = true }, junkTiers = { Rarity = true } (with "novalue" for worthless items), repairBelowPct = 40, restockPresets = { name = { restock rows } }, fuelMaxCopper = 1000000 (the most one fuel buy may cost: eb restock craftmats' fuel and the craft bot's fuel step) }; loot = { method = "leader", space = 2 (free slots kept), rules = { \["name"\] = need | greed | pass | leave | take | transmute | salvage | destroy | "to:\<member>" }, autoTake = { names }, quotas = { \["item"\] = { member = count } }, owned = { member = { \["item"\] = count } }, confirmNoTrade = true, autoTakeNoTrade, keepValueCopper, rulesDoc = a loot-rules document (eb.economy.lootrules), aliases, wishers, resolveAuction = false, auction = { minResolve }, passLore, exports }; broker = { undercut = 1, beatAll = false, friendsFloorCopper = 0, priceDefaults = { \["name"\] = copper, \["tier:type"\] = copper, \["\*"\] = copper } }; bank = { depositRule, allowValuables = false, keepFree = 1 }; mail = { keepFree = 1 }; craft = { commissions = { enabled = false, allow = "fleet", names = { names } } }.
- `eco.inventory | eco.vendor | eco.depot | eco.bank | eco.mail | eco.broker | eco.loot | eco.auction | eco.commissions | eco.ledger | ...`: The parts of a built economy, each documented as its own module: inventory (bags, protect, the action gate, junk, search, trade), vendor (sell, repair, merchant buys, restock), depot (top-up, withdraw, deposit), bank, mail, broker, loot, auction (the Resolve auction), commissions, ledger (the money and item feed), and the crafting parts (craft, harvest, gearup, transmute, adornments, writs, grandmasters, collections, skilllevel, tse). The pure modules ride along on the economy table too: economy.rules, economy.drive, economy.confirm, economy.merchantread, economy.skills, economy.filter, economy.ledger (the ledger model), economy.lootrules, economy.grouploot and economy.commands.
- `economy.CONTRACT -> { "bagsFull", "junk", "nearestVendor", "sell", "repair", "restock", "craft", "lootPending", "lootGrab" }`: The names of the nine calls the brain's economy table must have (validateContract checks them).
- `economy.new(opts) -> eco`: Build the economy.
- `eco.env.lootWindowOpen() -> open`: The one shared "is a loot window up?" read every loot path uses (the game layer's loot watch when there is one, else the drive's loot.window) - never a second poll of the loot window of your own.
- `eco:contract() -> { bagsFull, junk, nearestVendor, sell, repair, restock, craft, lootPending, lootGrab }`: The brain's economy table. bagsFull(snap) -> full, freeSlots compares the free slots (from a snapshot's bagsFreeSlots, else the drive) with cfg.bags.fullThreshold; the others start or continue their job and answer a status.
- `eco:setSnapshot(snap) -> eco`: Hand the economy the latest world snapshot (the brain does this each tick).
- `eco:configure(patch) -> eco`: Change settings while it runs.
- `eco:validateContract(specList) -> ok, missing`: Check the brain's table is complete.
- `eco:driveGaps() -> missing`: Which window actions are not wired on this game yet.
- `eco:driveReport() -> report`: Every drive action: present or not, verified or not, and what it still needs.
- `economy.pillarsCovered() -> names`: The list of economy parts.

#### Module `eb.economy.adornments`

Adornment profiles: what each slot should carry, what is still missing, apply a profile or your class set, strip old gear, keep temporary adornments up.

The adornments pillar (eco.adornments). A PROFILE is { \<slot> = \<adornment name> }. Applying one gets each missing adornment from the bags, else the adornment depot in reach, else (only when you allow it) the broker under a price cap, and applies it to the slot's worn piece; a slot with nothing worn is skipped and said. Class sets live in the config (cfg.adorn.classSets) keyed by subclass, class or archetype.

How to adorn a character: 1) write the profile; 2) eco.adornments:audit(profile) shows what is missing and where it is; 3) call eco.adornments:applyProfile(profile, { broker = true, maxCopper = 50000 }) every tick until it is not "working".

**File:** `lua/eb/economy/adornments.lua` in the EB folder

- `Adornments.new(env) -> adornments`: Build the adornments pillar over an economy env.
- `eco.adornments:hasAdorn(wornItem, adornName) -> boolean`: Is an adornment already on a worn piece?
- `eco.adornments:adornInBags(adornName) -> item | nil`: Find an adornment in the bags.
- `eco.adornments:classSetFor(me) -> profile | nil`: The class set a character gets.
- `eco.adornments:audit(profile) -> missing, present`: What a profile still needs, and whether the missing adornment is in the bags.
- `eco.adornments:applyProfile(profile, opts) -> status`: Apply a profile: bags, then the adornment depot, then (allowed) the broker; a slot with nothing worn, or an adornment found nowhere under the cap, is skipped and said.
- `eco.adornments:applyClassSet(opts) -> status, why`: Apply this character's class set.
- `eco.adornments:unadorn(opts) -> status`: Take the adornments off bag items of those tiers (the adornments come back to the bags); a protected item is never touched.
- `eco.adornments:tempAdorns(profile, opts) -> status`: Re-apply only the temporary adornments that have run out.
- `profile = { chest = "<adornment name>", legs = "<adornment name>", ... }; cfg.adorn.classSets = { [subclass | class | archetype] = profile }`: An adornment profile names one adornment per worn slot (the slot words are the game's equipment slots, lower case). Class sets are profiles keyed by who gets them.

#### Module `eb.economy.bank`

The personal, shared and guild bank: deposit by rule, withdraw by name or filter, keep a coin purse, move a guild page, and read what each bank holds.

A deposit moves NOTHING without a rule (an item list, a filter, bag numbers, cfg.bank.depositRule or all = true), and every deposit keeps bags themselves, the keep list, protected items and the account valuables (familiar, mount and mercenary training items and the like) unless cfg.bank.allowValuables. The guild bank never takes a protected item, and a guild deposit names its page (1 to 4). dry = true answers the plan without moving anything. Coin is in copper (1 platinum = 1,000,000 copper).

How to bank the day's harvest: 1. Preview: eco.bank:deposit{ which = "shared", filter = { name = "ore" }, dry = true }. 2. Run it: the same call without dry, once a tick until "done".

**File:** `lua/eb/economy/bank.lua` in the EB folder

- `bank.new(env) -> bank`: Build the part (you normally use eco.bank).
- `bank.which(w) -> "personal" | "shared" | "guild" | nil`: Read a bank word.
- `bank:shielded(it, which) -> kept, why`: Is this item kept out of the bank?
- `bank:depositPlan(opts) -> picked, kept | nil, nil, why`: What a deposit would move.
- `bank:deposit(opts) -> status, info`: Put bag items in a bank.
- `bank:withdrawPlan(opts, rows) -> rows | nil, why`: What a withdraw would take.
- `bank:withdraw(opts) -> status, why`: Take items out of a bank (stops while cfg.bank.keepFree slots would not stay free).
- `bank:coin(opts) -> status, why`: Deposit or withdraw coin; keepCopper keeps that much on you.
- `bank:move(fromPage, toPage) -> status, why`: Move a guild bank page's items to another page.
- `bank:scan(which) -> { [bank] = rows }`: What the banks hold.

#### Module `eb.economy.broker`

The broker: reprice your listings against the market (never under your floors), buy by name under a price cap, buy the best upgrade for a slot, buy spell scrolls, and put bag items up for sale.

Every broker buy answers the purchase question Yes only for the exact item bought. A reprice never goes under cfg.broker.friendsFloorCopper or the item's own price default (cfg.broker.priceDefaults: by exact name, by "\<tier>:\<type>", or "\*" for everything), and a new price only counts once the window reads it back. Nothing goes up for sale until you call addFromInventory with a price; bound and protected items can never be listed.

How to keep your listings at the market price: 1. cfg.broker = { undercut = 5, friendsFloorCopper = 1000, priceDefaults = { \["my item"\] = 1200 } }. 2. At the broker, call eco.broker:reprice() once a tick until "done".

**File:** `lua/eb/economy/broker.lua` in the EB folder

- `broker.new(env) -> broker`: Build the part (you normally use eco.broker).
- `broker:settleBuy(job, name) -> "stay" | "next" | "blocked", why`: The purchase-question step every broker buy ends with (for your own buy job steps).
- `broker:priceFloor(item) -> copper`: The lowest price this item may be listed at by its own default.
- `broker:targetPrice(item, myPrice, competitorLow) -> copper`: What one listing should cost.
- `broker:reprice(opts) -> status, why`: Set the price of every listing of yours to its target price.
- `broker:buy(name, opts) -> status, why`: Buy the shortfall from the cheapest listing under the cap.
- `broker:buyBest(filter) -> status, why`: Buy the best-scoring listing for a slot (the gear scorer of eco.gearup decides).
- `broker:listFromBags(opts) -> { { id, name, qty, priceCopper, slot, tier, rarity, value, hasPrice } }`: What could go up on the broker.
- `broker:addFromInventory(id, copper, opts) -> status, why`: Put one bag item up at a price.
- `broker:buyMasters(list, opts) -> status, why`: Buy the spell scrolls of a tier you still need, each under the cap, answering each purchase question.

#### Module `eb.economy.collections`

Collections: read the journal's collections, work out the missing pieces, add the ones you have (bags, then the Collectible Depot), and plan or buy the rest.

The collections pillar (eco.collections). A SCOPE word picks the incomplete collections to work on: an exact category wins, else every collection whose name contains the word; "all", "missing" or nothing means every incomplete one. Adding a piece CONSUMES it, so only a piece the journal still misses, not already collected and not protected is ever added. Buying has three models: "confirm" (the default) counts and stops, "queue" hands back the buy list, "auto" buys on the broker - and auto refuses without a per-piece price cap. A piece already in the bags is never bought.

How to finish a category: 1) eco.collections:missing("\<category>") lists what is needed; 2) eco.collections:fill ("\<category>", { depot = true }) every tick adds what you have; 3) eco.collections:buy("\<category>", { model = "auto", maxCopper = 1000 }) buys the rest.

**File:** `lua/eb/economy/collections.lua` in the EB folder

- `Collections.new(env) -> collections`: Build the collections pillar over an economy env.
- `Collections.clean(name) -> name`: A piece name as the broker knows it.
- `Collections.usable(name) -> ok, why`: Is a missing-piece name worth acting on?
- `eco.collections:journal() -> { { name, category, level, have, missing, incomplete } }`: Read the journal's collections page.
- `Collections.scope(rows, word) -> rows, kind`: Pick the collections a scope word names. Pure.
- `eco.collections:missing(word) -> names, unresolved`: What a scope still needs.
- `eco.collections:addable(it, wanted) -> boolean`: The add rule for one bag item.
- `eco.collections:fill(word, opts) -> status, info`: Add the pieces you have: the bags first, then the Collectible Depot.
- `eco.collections:buyPlan(word, opts) -> plan, skipped`: What a buy would get.
- `eco.collections:buy(word, opts) -> status, info`: Buy the still-missing pieces by one of the three models.
- `eco.collections:needs(name) -> boolean`: The quick "keep this one" check for a harvest or loot helper.
- `colrow = { name, category, level, slots, have = { piece names }, missing = { piece names } }`: One collection as the drive reads it from the journal (drive\["collection.journal"\]()).
- `require("eb.economy.data.collections") -> { buyModels = { "confirm", "queue", "auto" }, defaultModel = "confirm", allWords = { "all", "missing", "" }, skipNames, skipIfContains, placeholder, depotKind = "collectible", depotActors, depotReachMetres, stripTrailingParen }`: The collections rules: the buy models and the default, the words that mean every collection, the names set aside, and where collectibles are kept.

#### Module `eb.economy.confirm`

The purchase question: answer Yes only when the game's "Are you sure you want to purchase X?" names exactly the item you are buying.

Some buys raise a yes / no question that must be answered, or the buy does nothing and the next one stacks a second question. The rule EB follows - and your helper should too - is never blind-confirm: Yes only for the exact item you are buying, otherwise No or leave it.

**File:** `lua/eb/economy/confirm.lua` in the EB folder

- `confirm.asksFor(question, item) -> ours`: Is this purchase question about my item?
- `confirm.seconds(asked, fallback) -> seconds`: How long a buy keeps waiting for its question.
- `confirm.new(env) -> answerer`: The purchase-question answerer for your own buy helper.
- `answerer:expect(item, seconds)`: Say what you are about to buy, just before the buy.
- `answerer:resolve(item, opts) -> "none" | "confirmed" | "declined"`: Read the purchase question, if any, and answer it for your item. Call it each tick after the buy until it answers "confirmed" or "declined", or a few ticks of "none" tell you no question came.

#### Module `eb.economy.craft`

Craft at a station: select the recipe, make sure the fuel is there, run each combine with the right reaction art, and craft a whole list of orders.

The craft pillar of the economy (eco.craft). Every call is pollable: call it every tick with the same order and it answers "working" until the order is "done", or "blocked" with a plain reason. It never walks: stand at a station first (the brain or your script walks there). While a combine runs it casts one reaction art a tick, rescuing durability first, then quality, else pushing progress.

The pillars run on a drive table: the game windows each pillar reads and pokes (eb.economy.drive names every one). On this build a running EB does not build the economy for scripts yet and the craft commands answer "not wired yet"; a script builds its own economy with require("eb.economy").new{ drive = ... }.

How to craft from a script: 1) build or get the economy (eco); 2) stand at a station that serves the recipe (craft.serves tells you); 3) call eco.craft:craftOne({ recipe = name, qty = n }, { station = device }) every tick until it is not "working"; 4) for several recipes call eco.craft:queue(orders) the same way.

**File:** `lua/eb/economy/craft.lua` in the EB folder

- `Craft.new(env) -> craft`: Build the craft pillar over an economy env. You normally use eco.craft instead.
- `Craft.serves(actorName, device) -> true | false | nil`: Does this station serve the recipe's device? Answered from EB's station data (exact names, partial names, names that must never count, and stations that serve every device). Pure: no game read.
- `eco.craft:pickArt(st, arts) -> artName | nil`: The reaction-art choice EB makes each tick of a combine: durability under 60 first, then quality under 80, else progress - always an art that is ready.
- `eco.craft:craftOne(order, opts) -> status, why`: Craft one order at the station in reach: select the recipe (always ours, even when the window still shows the last one), pull missing fuel from a fuel depot in reach, make qty of it with reaction arts, close the station.
- `eco.craft:queue(orders) -> status, why`: Craft a list of orders in turn; an order with to = \<who> is handed to that member (within trade range) when it is made.
- `order = { recipe = "<recipe name>", qty = 1, to = "<member>" }`: The shape of a craft order. recipe is the recipe book's name; qty how many to make; to (queue only) who gets each finished item.
- `drive["craft.state"]() -> { progress = 0..100, durability, quality, power, fuelOk, reaction, result = nil|"success"|"fail" }`: What the station reports during a combine, read every tick. fuelOk = false means the recipe lacks fuel (craft.fuelNeeded lists it); result says how the last combine ended.
- `require("eb.economy.data.craft_devices") -> { anyType = { { actor, within } }, devices = { { fromRecipes = { device names }, exact = { actor names }, partial = { name parts }, invalid = { names that never count }, summon = { ability, abilityId } } } }`: EB's station data, the table serves() answers from: stations that serve every device, and per device the actor names that serve it, the name parts that may, the names that must never count, and the ability that summons a portable station where there is one. Game facts only.

#### Module `eb.economy.depot`

Guild hall and house depots: top the bags up to a kept count, withdraw one item, deposit by rule with the keep list honoured.

A RESTOCK ROW is { name, qty = how many to KEEP in the bags, who = the subclass, class or archetype it is for (nothing: everyone), depot = the depot kind (else from the item: ammo, fuel, food, harvest) }. One list works for the whole group: each box takes only its own rows; rows for the same item under one "who" add up, and across different "who"s the larger target stands. Depot kinds include harvest, ammo, fuel, food, adorn, collectible and scroll. A deposit moves nothing without a rule, and the keep list (cfg.depot.keep) and protected items always stay.

How to restock a group from one list: 1. Write the rows once: { { name = "Bread", qty = 20 }, { name = "Arrows", qty = 200, who = "ranger" } }. 2. On every box, call eco:contract().restock(rows) (or eco.depot:topUp(rows)) once a tick until "done".

**File:** `lua/eb/economy/depot.lua` in the EB folder

- `depot.new(env) -> depot`: Build the part (you normally use eco.depot).
- `depot:heldInBags(name) -> n`: Count an item in the bags.
- `depot:planLines(rows) -> lines, notMine`: The restock plan for this box.
- `depot:topUp(rows) -> status`: Pull each shortfall from its depot.
- `depot:withdraw(name, qty, kind, opts) -> status, why`: Take one item out of a depot (opens it, withdraws, closes it).
- `depot:deposit(items, opts) -> status, why`: Deposit bag items into their depots, keeping the keep list and protected items.
- `depot:bagGateWorthIt() -> worth`: Is a depot trip worth it now?

#### Module `eb.economy.filter`

The one item filter: pick the items of a list that match a spec (tiers, flags, a level band, a class, a name, a stat, bags or pages), and say why each other item was skipped.

Pure Lua. A SPEC names what it takes; every criterion you set must match and the ones you leave out are ignored: { tiers = { "fabled" }, flags = { "novalue", "notrade", "heirloom", "attuned" } (any of them), minLevel, maxLevel, class = "templar", name = "\<text the name contains>", names = { exact names }, exclude = { texts never matched }, stat = { name, op = ">" | "<" | "=", value }, resolve = { op, value }, bags = { numbers }, pages = { numbers } }. An ITEM is EB's item shape: { name, tier, level, classes, stats, bag, page, noValue, noTrade, heirloom, attuned, ... }. A spec that names nothing is refused, so an empty filter never moves everything.

**File:** `lua/eb/economy/filter.lua` in the EB folder

- `filter.pick(list, spec) -> picked, skipped`: Pick the items that match.
- `filter.matches(item, spec) -> ok, whyNot`: Does one item match?
- `filter.saysWhat(spec) -> ok, why`: Does this spec say what it takes? Check it before any bulk move.
- `filter.normalize(spec) -> spec`: The canonical form of a spec (matches and pick call it for you).
- `filter.excluded(name, exclude) -> excluded`: Is this item shielded by the exclude list?
- `filter.statPasses(v, op, want) -> passes`: The stat comparison a spec's stat and resolve use.

#### Module `eb.economy.gearup`

Score gear the way EB does, wear the best pieces in the bags, fill empty slots from the broker, and plan which spare piece goes to whom in the group.

The gear-up pillar (eco.gearup). The score ranks Resolve first, then Fervor, then Potency, then the role's main stat (fighter stamina, priest wisdom, mage intelligence, scout agility), then the weights you set in cfg.gear\[role\], with item level only breaking a tie (eb.economy.gearscore: the stat lines under one key set whatever the game calls them; a piece whose stats did not read is never judged). An upgrade that is worn takes the old piece's adornments over (the gear job, eb.economy.gearswap).

How to gear up: 1) eco.gearup:aup() every tick until "done" wears the best of the bags; 2) eco.gearup:fillFromBroker { maxCopper = ... } fills empty slots; 3) for a group, gather each box's export and read eco.gearup:groupMatch(exports, { planOnly = true }).

**File:** `lua/eb/economy/gearup.lua` in the EB folder

- `Gearup.new(env) -> gearup`: Build the gear-up pillar over an economy env.
- `eco.gearup:roleOf(me) -> role`: The role a character's gear is scored for.
- `eco.gearup:score(item, role) -> number`: Score a piece for a role, by the order above.
- `eco.gearup:aup(opts) -> status, words`: Auto-upgrade: the best bag piece that outscores the worn one is put on by the gear job (the old piece's adornments carried across), then the next, until nothing in the bags is better.
- `eco.gearup:fillFromBroker(opts) -> status`: Buy the best listing for each empty slot (the purchase question answered only when it names that listing), then an auto-upgrade pass wears them.
- `eco.gearup:planGroupTrades(exports, opts) -> { { item, from, to, gain, slot } }`: Plan who should get which spare piece.
- `eco.gearup:groupMatch(exports, opts) -> plan | status`: The group trade plan.

#### Module `eb.economy.grandmasters`

Turn the "(Master)" spell scrolls in the bags or the Scroll Depot into "(Grandmaster)" crafts.

The grandmasters pillar (eco.grandmasters). plan() only looks; run() crafts only with go = true, because every craft consumes a scroll. A scroll whose Grandmaster recipe is not in your book is left, and depot scrolls come out in batches that fit the bags. It never walks: stand at the Scroll Depot for a depot run.

How to: 1) eco.grandmasters:plan({ depot = true }) and read crafts and skipped; 2) run the same options with go = true every tick until it is not "working".

**File:** `lua/eb/economy/grandmasters.lua` in the EB folder

- `Grandmasters.new(env) -> grandmasters`: Build the grandmasters pillar over an economy env.
- `Grandmasters.gmOf(name) -> ability, grandmasterRecipe | nil`: What a Master scroll becomes. Pure.
- `Grandmasters.roster(class) -> { [ability] = true } | nil`: The class's Grandmaster roster from EB's data.
- `Grandmasters.crafterFits(tsClass, advClass) -> boolean`: Which tradeskill class crafts upgrades for which archetype.
- `eco.grandmasters:plan(opts) -> { crafts = { { scroll, recipe, from } }, skipped = { { name, why } } }`: Plan a Grandmaster run - touching nothing.
- `eco.grandmasters:run(opts) -> status, info`: Craft the plan, batch by batch.
- `require("eb.economy.data.grandmasters") -> { crafterFor = { [archetype] = { tradeskill classes } }, adventure = { [class] = archetype }, roster = { [Class] = { ability names } } }`: The Grandmaster facts: which tradeskill class crafts for which archetype, each class's archetype, and each class's roster.

#### Module `eb.economy.harvest`

Harvest: decide which nodes to take, run a gather route, send the pack pony out, and track shinies.

The harvest pillar (eco.harvest). wantNode is the node rule; runRoute walks a route's stops on the mesh and harvests the wanted nodes in reach at each; packPony and trackShiny are the pony and shiny helpers. Every run is pollable ("working" / "done" / "blocked", why). The route walk needs a mesh walker in the economy (eco built with nav = ...); without one runRoute is blocked.

Config (cfg.harvest): blacklist = { \[resource name or colour\] = true }, categories = { \[category\] = true } (empty = every category), routes = { \[name\] = { { x, y, z }, ... } }. The tier band: one harvest tier per ten levels (level 1-10 = tier 1 ... 91-100 = tier 10); a node above your band is left.

How to gather: 1) put your route in cfg.harvest.routes (or pass the stops); 2) build the economy with a walker; 3) call eco.harvest:runRoute("\<name>", { loop = true }) every tick.

**File:** `lua/eb/economy/harvest.lua` in the EB folder

- `Harvest.new(env) -> harvest`: Build the harvest pillar over an economy env.
- `eco.harvest:wantNode(node) -> want, why`: The node rule: never a blacklisted resource (by name or colour), never a tier above your level band, and only your preferred categories when you set any.
- `eco.harvest:runRoute(route, opts) -> status, why`: Walk to each stop on the mesh, harvest every wanted node in reach, leave the rest (marked seen so the run never loops on one), then go on to the next stop. A stop that cannot be reached is skipped and said.
- `eco.harvest:packPony(opts) -> status`: Summon the pack pony, hail it and answer its questions to send it harvesting.
- `eco.harvest:trackShiny(opts) -> { new finds }`: Watch for shinies: each NEW one is returned once with its spot, logged, and told to the crew as one line. Call it every tick or two; it is a cheap read.
- `node = { id, name, color, tier, category, x, y, z, shiny }`: A harvest node as the drive reports it (drive\["harvest.nodeNear"\](filter)).

#### Module `eb.economy.inventory`

Your bags: what is in them, the protect list, the one gate every sell, transmute, salvage, extract, destroy and deposit goes through, junk clearing, item search and handing items to a player.

eco.inventory reads the bags through the drive (bags.items never includes worn gear) and owns applyAction - the single door every destructive or selling action passes. It asks the safety gate first (eb.economy.rules.canTake, or the keep list for a deposit), so no path can take a protected, unread or bound item, and it writes the ledger line for a finished sell, deposit or transmute.

How to clear junk safely: 1. Say what junk is: cfg.vendor.junkTiers = { Junk = true } (add novalue = true for worthless items). 2. Call eco:contract().junk() once a tick until it answers "done" - it sells at an open merchant, destroys otherwise. 3. Put anything you must keep on the protect list first: eco.inventory:protect(name).

**File:** `lua/eb/economy/inventory.lua` in the EB folder

- `inventory.new(env) -> inventory`: Build the part (you normally use eco.inventory).
- `inv:scan(budget) -> { item }`: What is in the bags.
- `inv:freeSlots() -> n`: How many bag slots are free.
- `inv:isProtected(item) -> protected, why`: Is this item protected?
- `inv:protect(name)`: Put a name on the protect list: never sold, transmuted, destroyed or deposited.
- `inv:unprotect(name) -> true, kind | false, why`: Take a name off the protect list. Only a shipped default is remembered as taken off; a name you added yourself simply leaves the list.
- `inv:applyAction(item, action, ctx) -> status, why`: Do one item action through the safety gate. The window it needs (a merchant, a depot) must already be open.
- `inv:junk(opts) -> status`: Sell (at an open merchant) or destroy the items cfg.vendor.junkTiers names. The brain's junk() calls this.
- `inv:quiver(opts) -> status, why`: Top up the ammo you hold from an open ammo depot.
- `inv:search(words, index) -> hits`: Find an item in the bags and in an index you pass.
- `inv:distribute(itemName, qty, who) -> status, why`: Hand some of an item to a player by trade.

#### Module `eb.economy.job`

The pollable job every economy action stands on: an ordered list of steps, advanced one bite per call, that never waits, never loops to the end and never touches a file on the game thread.

A Job is long work cut into steps: job:tick(ctx) runs the current step once and answers "working", "done" or "blocked" with a reason, so the brain (or your helper) calls it once per tick until it ends. A step is function(job, ctx) -> verb\[, info\], where verb is "stay" (still on this step), "next" (this step is done), "done" (the whole job finished early) or "blocked" (it cannot go on; info says why). job.mem is the current step's scratch table; it is cleared when the job moves to the next step.

ONE JOB PER REQUEST. Job.gate(holder, key, build) keeps one live job per key on any table you own, so calling the same action every tick resumes the same job instead of starting it over, and a different key is a separate job. A stop flag on holder.env.stop ends a gated job at once.

HOW TO WRITE A JOB. 1. Write each step as a function(job, ctx) that does one bite and returns "stay", "next", "done" or "blocked". 2. Keep a step's progress in job.mem. 3. Build it with Job.new(name, steps). 4. Call job:tick(ctx) once per tick (inside an EB pulse job is fine: a tick never waits) until it is not "working". 5. To make an action idempotent, wrap it: return Job.gate(self, "sell", function() return Job.new("sell", steps) end):tick(ctx).

**File:** `lua/eb/economy/job.lua` in the EB folder

- `Job.new(name, steps) -> job`: Make a job.
- `job:tick(ctx) -> "working" | "done" | "blocked", why`: Advance the job one bite.
- `job:finished() -> bool`: Has the job ended?
- `job:reset() -> job`: Start a job over (a fresh request of the same shape).
- `Job.gate(holder, key, build) -> job`: One job per request: the same key resumes the same job; a finished one is replaced by a fresh build.
- `Job.live(holder, key) -> job | nil`: Look up a request's job without building one - resume it before planning again.
- `Job.clear(holder, key) -> nil`: Drop live jobs (on a zone change or a goal switch) so the next call starts clean.

#### Module `eb.economy.loot`

Loot: what this box does with each drop, the corpse and chest sweep behind the brain's lootGrab, the leader's hand-out (quotas, the Resolve auction, Lore passing) and the group's loot method.

Each drop of a loot window gets one decision: take, assign, pass or leave. The loot-rules document (cfg.loot.rulesDoc with on = true, eb.economy.lootrules) comes first: a wish of someone in the group, then the rule that names the drop (need, greed, pass, leave, assign, or an after-looting action). A drop no rule names gets EB's own default: the per-name rule (cfg.loot.rules: need, greed, pass, leave, take, transmute, salvage, destroy or "to:\<member>"), the always-take list, a quota a member still wants (cfg.loot.quotas against cfg.loot.owned), the leader's Resolve auction, then the group's method - leader only, keep and free for all TAKE the drop (the leader hands out what is assigned and loots the rest itself; a free-for-all window is taken whole), a lottery, need-before-greed or round robin answers Greed. A leader window this box does not lead is never touched. Leave is never a decline: the drop stays where it is. A lottery or need-before-greed window takes ONE answer for the whole window (Request All, Need or Greed when anything is wanted, Decline only when every drop is passed); with nothing decided it is left for you and never closed over its drops.

Never in a fight: lootGrab answers "working" and touches nothing while this box fights. A rules file that does not read means no looting by EB at all (cfg.loot.rulesProblem says why). A drop is only taken while cfg.loot.space slots stay free (an upgrade or an assigned drop always is), a No-Trade or Heirloom question is answered only when cfg.loot.confirmNoTrade, and nothing is destroyed or transmuted unless a rule says so (the after-looting action runs on the bag item once its facts are read, through the safety rules). Every drop taken is a ledger line.

How to loot by rule after each fight: 1. cfg.loot.rules = { \["fixture gem"\] = "need", \["fixture rag"\] = "leave" }. 2. When eco:contract().lootPending() is true, call lootGrab() once a tick until it answers "done" or "empty".

**File:** `lua/eb/economy/loot.lua` in the EB folder

- `loot.new(env) -> loot`: Build the part (you normally use eco.loot).
- `loot:classify(item) -> verb`: What to do with one drop (the simple rule path).
- `loot:wishWinner(item) -> member | nil`: Who still wants this drop?
- `loot:roster() -> names`: The group, in order.
- `loot:amLeader() -> leader`: Does this box hand out the drops?
- `loot:roomFor(item, need) -> ok`: Is there room to take this drop? A drop worth at least cfg.loot.keepValueCopper also gets room.
- `loot:lootPending(snap) -> pending`: Is there something to loot? The brain's lootPending calls this.
- `loot:rulesModel() -> model | nil`: The loot-rules document in use.
- `loot:isMe(name) -> me`: Is this name me?
- `loot:winType(w) -> "leader" | "lotto" | "nbg" | "ffa" | "unknown"`: What kind of loot window is up?
- `loot:modelCtx() -> { me, sub, group, aliases, wishers }`: The loot rules' context, from the crew and the settings.
- `loot:decide(w) -> { { verb, who, need, after, rule, by } }`: Decide every drop of a window: the loot rules first, then EB's own default (see the module description).
- `loot:windowWaits() -> boolean`: Is a window waiting for this box? It reads no corpse, so it is cheap enough for every pulse.
- `loot:lootGrab(opts) -> status, why`: Open the nearest corpse or chest and resolve its loot window by rule.
- `loot:driveDrops(job, w) -> "stay" | "next"`: Drive a window drop by drop: one Loot All when every drop is wanted, there is room and nothing is to be handed out; otherwise take each drop (answering its own question when you allow it), assign it to the member its decision names and tell them over the crew relay ("loot incoming: \<item>"), or leave it. A take or an assign in flight is asked again with the same id until it ends. A window a member leaves up is taken after two looks, so it never blocks a run.
- `loot:answerWindow(job, w, mode) -> "stay" | "next"`: Answer a lottery or need-before-greed window once for all of it: Request All (lottery), Need or Greed (need before greed) when any drop is wanted, Decline only when every drop is passed. With nothing decided - or where EB may not give the answer - the window is left for you, never closed over its drops.
- `loot:takeOne(it, d, again) -> "took" | "left" | "stay"`: Take one drop, answer its No-Trade or Heirloom question when your settings allow it, and write the ledger line.
- `loot:harvestClick(opts) -> status`: Harvest the node in reach until it is gone (what lootGrab{ harvest = true } does): the game's "nothing found" on a node that still stands is the same node again.
- `loot:setMethod(method)`: Set the group's loot method; on the leader it also tells the crew ("loot method \<method>").

#### Module `eb.economy.lootrules`

The loot rules: which rule names a dropped item, what each box does with a loot window (need, greed, pass, leave, assign to a member or a role), and the guard on destroying or transmuting after looting.

Pure Lua - it reads no game and no file, so a helper or a test can ask it anything. You hand it the rules (a decoded loot-rules table), the items a loot window shows and the window's type; it answers a verb per item and the one act for the window.

A RULE is { id, on, match = "exact" | "contains", item = "\<name or text, \* is a wildcard>", act, to, tier, notrade, lore, note }. act is need, greed, pass, leave, assign (to = a member, or @fighter / @priest / @scout / @mage / a class), or an after-looting act: destroy, transmute, salvage. The most specific rule wins: an exact name beats a contains text, a longer text a shorter one, a rule with conditions one without, then list order. A condition the window did not tell (tier, No-Trade, Lore) counts as not met.

Fail-safe throughout: an item no rule names follows the fallback (leave by default), and a destroy only ever acts on an item's exact name.

**File:** `lua/eb/economy/lootrules.lua` in the EB folder

- `lootrules.parse(doc, now) -> { opts, rules, removed, ok }`: Read a loot-rules table into the shape the rest of this module takes.
- `lootrules.bestRule(rules, itemName, facts) -> rule | nil, conditionUnknown`: The rule that decides an item.
- `lootrules.decideItem(rules, opts, item, wintype, ctx) -> decision`: What this box does with one item. A wish from someone in the group comes first, then the rules, then the fallback. On a leader's window an assigned item is handed out by the leader (verb smartloot).
- `lootrules.decideWindow(rules, opts, items, wintype, ctx) -> window`: The whole window: a verb per item and the one act for the window. untested = true when the act is one EB has not verified in game yet (only Loot All is verified today).
- `lootrules.actText(act) -> text`: A window act in plain words, for a log line or a window.
- `lootrules.afterRule(rules, itemName) -> rule | nil`: Does an after-looting rule act on this bag item?
- `lootrules.afterBlock(rule, it, isProtected, onKeep) -> why`: The after-looting guard. A destroy needs an exact-name rule and readable item details, and never touches No-Trade, Heirloom, Lore, attuned or No-Value items.
- `lootrules.destroyOk(rule) -> ok`: May this rule destroy anything at all?
- `lootrules.parseAct(inp) -> act | nil`: Read an act however it is typed.
- `lootrules.parseWin(inp) -> wintype`: The window type decideWindow takes.
- `lootrules.parseTri(v) -> "any" | "yes" | "no"`: Read a rule's yes / no / any condition.
- `lootrules.normName(inp) -> text`: An item name the way the rules compare it.
- `lootrules.glob(pat, s) -> matches`: The wildcard match rules use.
- `lootrules.textMatches(rule, norm) -> matches`: Does this rule's text name this item (conditions not checked)?
- `lootrules.conditionsMet(rule, facts) -> met, unknown`: Check a rule's tier, No-Trade and Lore conditions.
- `lootrules.tierMatches(tiers, tier) -> matches`: Does an item's tier meet a rule's tier condition?
- `lootrules.moreSpecific(a, b) -> aWins`: The ordering bestRule uses.
- `lootrules.roleFits(role, subclass) -> fits`: Is a templar a priest? Is a guardian a fighter?
- `lootrules.roleArch(role) -> archetype`: The archetype a role word means.
- `lootrules.isRoleWord(role) -> isRole`: Is this @word a role (rather than an alias or a name)?
- `lootrules.targets(to, members, aliases) -> names, unresolved`: Who an assign rule hands an item to.
- `lootrules.isAfter(a) -> after`: Is this an after-looting act?
- `lootrules.fallbackOk(a) -> ok`: May this act be the fallback for items no rule names?
- `lootrules.arrivals(last, now) -> names`: Which items just arrived in the bags - when an after-looting rule should look.

#### Module `eb.economy.mail`

Mail items and coin to another character, take attachments, and open one letter by subject or sender (a quest letter opened this way starts its quest).

A send needs a recipient (one character name) AND an explicit pick (names, or a filter that says what it takes) - never "mail everything". Bound items cannot be mailed, and protected items and valuables stay unless named exactly with allowProtected. One item per letter; coin rides on the first. A letter is picked by a part of its subject (any case), its sender's WHOLE name (any case), or both; a part of a name never matches, and a key the game puts in front of a subject or name (":\<key>:") is never part of it. EB never logs a player's name it was not asked for.

How to send a crafter their materials: 1. Preview: eco.mail:send("Crafter", { names = { "Ore" }, count = "all", dry = true }). 2. Send: the same call without dry, once a tick until "done".

**File:** `lua/eb/economy/mail.lua` in the EB folder

- `mail.new(env) -> mail`: Build the part (you normally use eco.mail).
- `mail.shown(text) -> text`: A subject or name as the player sees it.
- `mail.subjectFits(want, subject) -> fits`: Does a subject fit?
- `mail.canLook(subject, sender) -> ok`: Does this search name something?
- `mail.fits(subject, sender, letter) -> fits`: Does one letter fit the search?
- `mail.pick(subject, sender, letters) -> index | nil, fits`: Choose the letter to open.
- `mail.validRecipient(to) -> ok`: Is this a character name a letter can go to?
- `mail:sendPlan(to, opts) -> picked, kept | nil, why`: What a send would mail.
- `mail:send(to, opts) -> status, info`: Mail items (and coin) to a character.
- `mail:collect(opts) -> status, why`: Take the attachments and coin of the letters that fit.
- `mail:open(subject, sender, take) -> status, why`: Open one letter (the first that fits); a quest letter starts its quest.
- `mail.isFrom(author, sender) -> bool`: Is this letter from the sender you asked about?
- `mail.canBePlayer(author) -> bool`: Could this sender be a player? Used before a sender's name is written anywhere that leaves this PC.
- `mail.fromPart(author, asked) -> text`: The " from ..." part of a mail line, keeping player names out of anything that leaves this PC.

#### Module `eb.economy.rules`

The safety gate and the settings of EB's item handling: nothing is destroyed, transmuted, salvaged or sold unless a rule says so and the item passes the fail-safe checks.

Pure Lua. canTake is the one gate every destructive action asks first, and its answer defaults to no: an item whose details were never read, a protected item (the protected list, personal treasure, epic weapon pieces), a Master-or-better spell scroll in a bulk run, and a No-Trade, Heirloom or attuned item you did not opt in by name are all refused. load() lays your settings over safe defaults, so a fresh install never sells or destroys anything until you configure it.

**File:** `lua/eb/economy/rules.lua` in the EB folder

- `rules.canTake(action, item, ctx) -> ok, why`: May this action take this item? Ask before every destroy, transmute, salvage or sell.
- `rules.load(userCfg) -> cfg`: Your economy settings over the defaults.
- `rules.defaults() -> cfg`: The safe defaults: selling junk off, nothing protected removed, an examine budget per minute.
- `rules.isProtected(item, cfg) -> protected, why`: Is this item protected?
- `rules.isTreasure(name) -> treasure`: Is this a personal treasure item?
- `rules.unread(item) -> unread`: Are this item's details unknown? An unread item is never taken.
- `rules.isMasterScroll(name) -> master`: A bulk run never touches these.
- `rules.keptByFlags(item, asked) -> kept`: Do the item's own flags keep it?
- `rules.saysWhatGoes(pick) -> says`: Does a bulk pick actually say what goes?
- `rules.isKeptFromDepot(item, cfg) -> kept`: Never deposit these: the keep list and every protected item.
- `rules.archetypeOf(subclass) -> archetype | nil`: A subclass's archetype.
- `rules.whoApplies(who, me) -> applies`: Does a restock or gear row apply to this character?
- `rules.word(s) -> word`: The comparison form rules use for class and role words.

#### Module `eb.economy.skilllevel`

Level a crafting skill by its bands (Tinkering, Adorning) and a new crafter's tradeskill level, always from the live read.

The levelling pillar (eco.skilllevel). Every round starts from a live read of the skill, so a stopped run carries on where the skill is, and an unknown read never starts or continues a run. A secondary skill is levelled band by band from EB's levelling data: each band names the books to scribe and the recipe rows a round crafts. A round that gains nothing twice, or three broker trips with no gain, ends the run with the reason. Nothing is bought unless you ask (opts.broker = true, each book under the band's price cap), and what a round made is destroyed only when you opt in (cfg.skilllevel.destroyMade = true), each item through the safety rules.

How to level Tinkering: 1) stand at a work bench with the band's materials; 2) call eco.skilllevel:level("tinkering") every tick until it is not "working"; 3) read eco.skilllevel:status("tinkering") any time to see the band and the books ahead.

**File:** `lua/eb/economy/skilllevel.lua` in the EB folder

- `SkillLevel.new(env) -> skilllevel`: Build the levelling pillar over an economy env.
- `SkillLevel.skill(id) -> skillData | nil`: A skill's levelling data, or nil when EB has none for it.
- `SkillLevel.bandFor(skill, cur) -> band`: Which levelling band a skill value is in.
- `SkillLevel.tripBooks(skill, cur, max) -> { book names }`: What a book trip would buy.
- `SkillLevel.decide(i) -> "learn" | "unreadable" | "done" | "book" | "level"`: The start-of-round decision. Pure.
- `SkillLevel.afterRound(i) -> verdict, why`: What a finished round comes to. Pure.
- `SkillLevel.mostStockedTier(tiers) -> tier`: For Adorning: the tier to level from what you have.
- `SkillLevel.roundFromStock(powders, fragments, most) -> { dilute, distil }`: For Adorning: plan one round from the bags.
- `eco.skilllevel:read(id, opts) -> read`: Read a skill the way the levelling runs do.
- `eco.skilllevel:status(id) -> { state, read, band, books, why }`: Where a skill stands right now.
- `eco.skilllevel:level(id, opts) -> status, why`: Level a secondary skill by its bands, round after round, from the live read.
- `eco.skilllevel:destroyMade(sk, round) -> status, count`: Destroy what a round made - only with cfg.skilllevel.destroyMade = true, only that round's products, each through the safety rules. The level run calls it; you rarely do.
- `eco.skilllevel:levelCrafter(opts) -> status, why`: Level a new crafter: craft the highest recipe at or under your tradeskill level, a batch a round, reading the level before each round.
- `require("eb.economy.data.skill_leveling") -> { capMultiplier = 5, noGainRuns = 2, tripsNoGain = 3, craftBands = { artisanTop = 9, archetypeTop = 19, classFrom = 20 }, skills = { { id, route, startMax, booksAhead, each (book price cap), budget, destroyMade, bands = { { from, tier, books = { names }, queue = { { recipe, id, count } }, fuel, brokerOnly } } } } }`: EB's levelling data: per skill its bands (the value a band starts at, the books it needs, the recipe rows a round crafts, its fuel, and whether its books are only on the broker), plus the rules' numbers. Game facts only.

#### Module `eb.economy.skills`

Read a crafting skill (Tinkering, Adorning, Transmuting) as cur / max, without a temporary bonus, with the cap your levels allow - and say plainly when it cannot be read.

The skill reader the levelling runs stand on. The rule: an unknown read is UNKNOWN (ok = false and the reason), never a 0, and no levelling run starts on one. The reader asks an object for the read - the game layer is one (it has Skill, SkillText, SkillAbsent and TSLevel); eb.economy.new builds one for you as eco.env.skills over the shim you give it. The pure helpers turn the game's text into numbers and name the state.

How to read a skill: local r = require("eb.economy.skills").new({ shim = game, me = function() return { level = game.Me().level } end }):read("tinkering"); use r.cur and r.max only when r.ok.

**File:** `lua/eb/economy/skills.lua` in the EB folder

- `Skills.parse(raw) -> { ok, cur, max }`: Turn the skill text into numbers; the colour code comes off first. Pure.
- `Skills.withoutBonus(r, cap) -> r`: A temporary bonus raises cur and max together; this gives the skill as it stands against the real cap.
- `Skills.capFromLevels(level, tsLevel, multiplier) -> cap`: The cap a skill can reach at your levels. Shown, never acted on alone.
- `Skills.stateOf(learned, r) -> state`: Name a skill's state from its read.
- `Skills.new(env) -> reader`: Build a skill reader over the game layer (or any object with those functions).
- `reader:read(id) -> { ok, cur, max, cap, source, absent, why, bonus }`: Read one skill live, the bonus taken off.
- `reader:readWith(fn, id) -> read`: Read through a function of your own (a test, or a value you already have), else the normal read.
- `reader:cap() -> number`: The cap your levels allow (capFromLevels over your levels).
- `reader:level() -> number | nil`: Your adventure level as the reader sees it.
- `reader:tsLevel() -> number | nil`: Your tradeskill level.
- `reader:snap() -> table`: The character snapshot the reader reads levels from.

#### Module `eb.economy.transmute`

Bulk transmute, salvage, extract or destroy a pick of bag items through the safety rules, and level the Transmuting skill on a stone merchant.

The transmute pillar (eco.transmute). A bulk run takes only what a PICK selects, and every item still passes the safety rules: a protected item, a Master or better spell scroll, a bound item (heirloom, attuned, no trade) you did not opt in by name, and an item whose details never read are always kept. A pick that does not say what goes - any tier, no bag, no kind, no flag, no resolve, the whole level range - is refused before a single item is touched. dry = true only previews, and a destroy only previews until you add go = true.

How to clear old gear: 1) preview: eco.transmute:preview({ action = "salvage", tiers = { TREASURED = true }, maxLevel = 50 }); 2) when the list is right, call eco.transmute:tse(the same pick) every tick until it is not "working".

**File:** `lua/eb/economy/transmute.lua` in the EB folder

- `Transmute.new(env) -> transmute`: Build the transmute pillar over an economy env.
- `eco.transmute:matches(item, opts) -> boolean`: Does an item fit the pick?
- `eco.transmute:preview(opts) -> taken, kept, asked`: What a run would take and keep, and why - touching nothing.
- `eco.transmute:tse(opts) -> status, info`: The bulk run: every picked item through the safety rules, one action per tick.
- `eco.transmute:levelTransmute(opts) -> status, why`: Level Transmuting: open the stone merchant, pick the cheapest stone in the currency most stones cost, buy one (the purchase question answered Yes only when it names that stone), transmute it, again - keeping cfg.transmute.freeSlots (4) bag slots free.
- `pick = { action, tiers = { [rarity] = true }, minLevel, maxLevel, bags, kind | novalue | mats, resolve, heirloom, attuned, noTrade, dry, go }`: What a bulk run takes. tiers names the rarities (the item's rarity word); minLevel and maxLevel bound the item level; heirloom, attuned and noTrade are the opt-ins for bound items; resolve = true takes only items that carry resolve. A pick must name at least one of tiers, bags, kind, a flag, resolve or a real level range.

#### Module `eb.economy.tse`

The T.S.E hand-over: a member gives its T.S.E pick to the leader before the leader's pass, and the pick can be sold at a merchant instead.

The T.S.E is the pass that breaks a chosen pick of unwanted items down - transmute, salvage, extract or destroy, by rule (eb tse). This module adds its two other ends. SELL takes each pick item's adornments off (kept), opens the merchant in reach (the guild hall's Guild Commodities Exporter, else any merchant) and sells the pick item by item, each through the economy's rules-gated item action and recorded in the ledger. GIVE is the hand-over: a member trades its pick to the leader, twelve items to a trade, within trade range, leaving out what cannot change hands (No-Trade, Heirloom, Attuned, Lore) and anything it wished for in a loot roll; a member that cannot give answers "failed" at once, so the leader never waits on it.

WHERE IT HAPPENS. At the zone's END, inside, once the run is known to be complete: members hand over, then every box runs its saved T.S.E pass (the instance runner's first chore does this after each run).

FAIL-SAFE. Nothing is sold or given without a pick (a names list and/or a set of tiers in the T.S.E config, or the items you hand in); a protected item is never unadorned; a trade only goes to the leader the trade rules allow (with no trade rules set, a group member).

THE ENV. tse.new(env) takes the economy's env: { cfg = { tse = { names, tiers }, trade = { whitelist } }, pillars = { inventory = { scan(), applyAction(item, "sell", ctx) } }, rules = { isProtected(item, cfg) }, drive = the window actions ("merchant.isOpen", "merchant.near", "merchant.open", "merchant.close", "adorn.remove", "trade.near", "trade.open", "trade.add", "trade.accept"), ledger = { add(row) }, relay = { groupState() }, tradePolicy, now, log }. Every action is a pollable Job: call it every tick until it is not "working".

**File:** `lua/eb/economy/tse.lua` in the EB folder

- `tse.new(env) -> tse`: Make the T.S.E sell and give pillar (the economy builds one; build your own over an env of your own).
- `tse:sell(opts) -> "working" | "done" | "blocked", why`: Sell the pick at the merchant in reach, adornments first taken off and kept.
- `tse:give(opts) -> "working" | "done" | "blocked", why`: The hand-over: trade the pick to the leader, twelve items a trade.
- `tse:resolvePick(opts) -> { items }`: Work out the pick from the bags.
- `tse:givePick(items, wished) -> { items }`: What a member may give.
- `tse:mayGive(to) -> allowed, inGroup`: May this member trade to that leader? (With no trade rules set: only to a group member.)
- `tse:answer() -> { state, given, at } | nil`: What the leader reads to know a member is finished.
- `tse:setAnswer(state, given) -> answer`: Record this member's give answer (give does this itself).
- `tse.plan.tradeable(it) -> bool`: May this item go to the leader at all?
- `tse.plan.merge(items) -> { { name, qty }, ... }`: Merge stacks before packing trades.
- `tse.plan.packs(items, perTrade) -> { { { name, qty }, ... }, ... }`: Split a pick into trades.
- `tse.plan.allAnswered(members, answeredAt, since) -> bool`: The leader's wait: has every member finished its hand-over?

#### Module `eb.economy.vendor`

Merchants and menders: the nearest vendor, selling by list or rule, repair when the gear needs it, buying from a merchant with the purchase question answered safely, and restocking from depots.

The brain's bags-full recovery runs sell, then repair, then restock through this part, and every merchant buy in EB goes through buyFromMerchant: the row is chosen by its exact name, a name other rows share at other prices is refused, and the game's purchase question is answered Yes only when it names the item being bought.

How to sell and repair after a run: 1. cfg.vendor.sellList = { exact names } (or sellJunk = true with sellTiers). 2. At the merchant, call eco.vendor:sell() once a tick until "done". 3. Call eco.vendor:repair() the same way: it only opens the mender when gear is at or under repairBelowPct.

**File:** `lua/eb/economy/vendor.lua` in the EB folder

- `vendor.new(env) -> vendor`: Build the part (you normally use eco.vendor).
- `vendor:nearestVendor(kind) -> x, y, z, zone, actor | nil`: The vendor to walk to. The brain walks there, then calls sell / repair.
- `vendor:sellable(items) -> items`: Which items a sell sweep would take.
- `vendor:sell(opts) -> status, why`: Open the merchant, sell what the sell rule picks, close it.
- `vendor:repair(opts) -> status, why`: Repair at the mender when the worst worn piece is at or under cfg.vendor.repairBelowPct.
- `vendor:worstCondition() -> pct | nil`: How worn is your gear?
- `vendor:buyFromMerchant(name, qty, opts) -> status, why`: Buy from a merchant the safe way.
- `vendor:restock(list) -> status, why`: Restock from depots (never buys). The brain's restock(list) calls this.

#### Module `eb.economy.writs`

Work orders (rush orders and the Work Order Clipboard): take an order, work out which recipe each step wants, craft it, hand the order in - again for as many orders as you ask.

The writs pillar (eco.writs). The clever part is which recipe a step asks for: its text loses its leading verb and its progress, then EB tries, in order, a learned answer, a known spelling fix, the exact recipe book name, a partial spelling fix, the name without its article, and last a LOOSE match - only when exactly one recipe in the book fits. A loose or unverified pick is crafted once and the step read again: it moved, the pick is learned (cfg.writs.learned) and exact next time; it did not, the next candidate is tried; none left, the run stops and names the step and every recipe it tried. It never logs a character out when done.

How to run work orders: 1) stand at the clipboard (or a rush-order giver) with a station in reach; 2) call eco.writs:run({ count = 3, kind = "clipboard" }) every tick until it is not "working".

**File:** `lua/eb/economy/writs.lua` in the EB folder

- `Writs.new(env) -> writs`: Build the writs pillar over an economy env.
- `Writs.stripVerb(text) -> text`: Clean a step's text down to the thing it asks for. Pure.
- `Writs.resolve(text, book, learned) -> recipe | nil, how, candidates`: Work out which recipe a step asks for, by the rules above. Pure.
- `eco.writs:run(opts) -> status, why`: The whole work-order loop: ask for an order, craft each short step, verify a guessed recipe, hand the order in, repeat.
- `eco.writs:workStep(job, open, drv) -> verb, why`: One bite of crafting one step - used by run(); a script calls run() instead.
- `writ = { name, steps = { { text = "Create Fixture Lantern (0/6)", have = 0, need = 6 } } }`: An active work order as the drive reports it (drive\["writ.active"\]()); a step with have < need is still short.
- `require("eb.economy.data.writs") -> { verbs = { "i need to create", "create", ... }, articles = { "a ", "an ", "the " }, conversions = { [step text] = recipe }, partialConversions = { [text part] = replacement }, agent / clipboard / fuel / recipeMerchant / exporter = { searchDistance, find = { { guild | name } } }, startWithinMetres, takeWithinMetres }`: The work-order facts the rules read: the verbs a step leads with, the articles, the known spelling fixes, and how each giver and merchant is found. A learned answer goes to cfg.writs.learned, never into this table.

#### Module `eb.events`

Subscribe to game events (chat, zoning, dialogs, loot, quest offers and updates, level and group changes) and react to them.

eb.events is one registry of event handlers. A handler you add with on() runs once per event, from EB's frame pulse - never inside the game's own event callback - so it may read the game, but it should stay short: record what happened or queue the work, and let a task do anything that waits.

Events fire on the box whose game client produced them and are never sent to the other boxes by themselves. When the crew should act on an event, the handler sends one deliberate line with events.crew().

A handler that raises is counted (events.stats.totalHandlerFailures) and stays subscribed, so one bad handler never takes the others down. The same line seen twice inside 1.5 seconds (the game often repeats a line once per chat window) is delivered once. At most events.MAX_EVENTS_PER_TICK events are delivered in one frame; a flood past that is counted and dropped, never delivered late.

EB for InnerSpace's boot attaches the game's events and ticks this registry every frame before your script runs; your script only subscribes.

**File:** `lua/eb/events/init.lua` in the EB folder

- `events.on(event, fn, opts) -> id | nil, why`: Subscribe a handler to one event.
- `events.off(event, id) -> removed`: Unsubscribe one handler.
- `events.emit(event, payload) -> delivered, failed`: Deliver one event to every handler now. Use it for your own events (a helper announcing "my buff dropped" to other helpers) or to test a handler.
- `events.tick() -> emitted, dropped`: Deliver everything the event feeds collected since the last frame. EB's pulse calls it every frame; a script never needs to.
- `events.crew(targets, line) -> sent`: Turn a local event into ONE deliberate command for the crew. Events are never forwarded by themselves; this is how a handler says "everyone pause" when it sees the named spawn.
- `events.setRelay(fn)`: Set the sender crew() uses. EB sets it to the crew relay at start; set your own in a test.
- `events.addPollFeed(def) -> ok, why`: Add your own event source that samples something every intervalMs and turns a change into events. poll() reads (cheaply) and returns a plain table; diff() compares two of them and returns the events to deliver. The first poll only sets the baseline, so a feed never fires for the state it started in.
- `events.getFeed(name) -> feed | nil`: Look up a registered feed by name (to check that your poll feed is in).
- `events.eventNames() -> { names }`: List the event names this box can deliver.
- `events.status() -> table`: A report of the event layer: each feed, how often it ran and what it cost, how many handlers each event has, and the totals (delivered, dropped, de-duplicated, handler failures).
- `events.duplicate(event, key, windowMs) -> seen`: The de-duplication check feeds use. Call it in your own handler to act once per repeated line.
- `events.EVENTS -> { CONSTANT = "Name" }`: The canonical event names. Payloads, as both targets deliver them: ChatLine { category, message, speaker, target, speakerIsNPC, channel, speakerId, targetId }; IncomingText { text, type }; ZoningStarted {}; ZoningFinished { seconds } (read the new zone from the game layer); DialogOpened { id } and DialogClosed {}; ChoiceOpened { id } and ChoiceClosed {}; LootOpened { id }; RewardOpened { id }; QuestOffered { name, description, level, statusReward }; QuestUpdated { id, name, zone, category, description, progress }; Announcement { text, sound, timer }; LevelChanged { from, to }; GroupChanged { from, to }; RaidChanged { from, to }. With eb sessionwatch on, the PC's speaking box raises SessionFrozen, SessionRecovered and SessionGone { box, name, state, was, quietS, forS, why, reporter } (SESSION_FROZEN, SESSION_RECOVERED, SESSION_GONE).
- `events.stats -> { totalEmitted, totalDropped, totalHandlerFailures, totalDeduped, totalDropGaps }`: Running totals since EB started: events delivered, dropped past the per-frame cap, handler failures, and duplicates skipped.
- `events.MAX_EVENTS_PER_TICK -> 48`: How many events one frame delivers at most.

#### Module `eb.ic`

The instance runner: load an instance file (its hub, door, route steps and encounter scripts) and run it once or in a loop - the tank zones the group in, walks the route, fights each encounter, loots and leaves by the exit door.

An instance is a FOLDER: instance.lua (the zone, the hub, the door and the ordered route STEPS) plus encounters/\<name>.lua, one fight or mechanic each, called from the route by name. Both files are pure data that only return a table. runner:load(folder) reads and checks them; runner:run(inst) runs one lap; runner:loop(inst) runs it again and again.

THE GROUP RULE. Every box reaches the hub zone by its own travel and holds there. Only the TANK walks the hub route to the door, and its one use of the door zones the whole group in. Inside, the tank walks the route alone: the group camps on the tank's camp spots and follows on the mesh only where a path step says group = "follow". The group never walks the route together, and a hub step that would move it is refused at load. A member's runner holds, waits to be zoned in and waits to be taken out; it never opens the door or takes the exit itself.

MOVEMENT. The runner moves characters only by walking the mesh (and the zone's own doors). After a death it waits for the revive and walks back from the nearest positioned step; when a box is wedged it uses the class evac chain.

FAIL CLOSED. A step the runner cannot honour stops the run with the reason (the next step assumes the last one happened). The only step that never stops a run is a chest that is not there.

THE INTERFACES. The runner does not pathfind, pick spells or read the fight itself: it calls the five interfaces it is given (nav, combat, brain, loot, upkeep - see the "env" entry). In a running EB, \`eb ic\` builds them from EB's own nav, combat engine and crew (eb.app.ic); a test or a dry run hands it its own. Every wait inside the runner uses the env's sleep and checks brain.aborting(), so a stop ends any wait at once, and a pause holds the run and moves nobody.

HOW TO SCRIPT AN INSTANCE. 1. Make a folder named after the zone's short name with an instance.lua: schema, zone, short, the hub (the hub zone, the door, where the tank stands to use it, its approach) and the route STEPS in order. 2. Write one encounters/\<name>.lua per fight or mechanic: a when gate, phases of actions, a done test. 3. Load it with runner:load(folder) and read the reason when it is refused. 4. Run it once with opts.dry = true: every step says what it would do and nothing moves. 5. Run it for real - runner:run(inst), or eb ic run \<zone> on the tank - and loop it with runner:loop or eb ic loop \<zone> \[minutes\]. 6. Read report.verdicts (and the log lines) to see what each step came to, and fix the step that stopped the run.

**File:** `lua/eb/ic/init.lua` in the EB folder

- `ic.new(env) -> runner`: Make an instance runner over its interfaces.
- `runner:load(dir) -> inst | nil, why`: Read and check an instance: the schema must be "eb.ic/1"; no hub step may move the group; every option must skip real route steps; every encounter a route step calls must load.
- `runner:run(inst, opts) -> ok, why, report`: One lap: zone in by role, then the route steps in order, then the result.
- `runner:loop(inst, opts) -> ok, why, report`: Run one instance again and again. Looping ONE zone, the tank waits out the reuse timer INSIDE the cleared copy where the run ended, then leaves by the exit door, resets the copy from outside and goes back in. The first lap is a rerun of the copy you stand in unless the file's loop.rerun_first is false. A lap that finds every named already gone ran a copy whose reset did not take: the loop ends and says so rather than cycle a cleared copy.
- `runner:newCtx(inst, opts) -> ctx`: The state of one run. Use it to call a single part yourself (runner:zoneIn(ctx), runner:runEncounter(enc, ctx)).
- `runner:runOnce(ctx) -> ok, why`: Zone in, then walk the route from ctx.opts.from (default the first step): the body of run without its header and report.
- `runner:runStep(s, ctx) -> ok, note, tag`: Run one route step by its act (see "route"), logging one line for it.
- `runner:zoneIn(ctx) -> ok, why`: The whole entry, by role. Already inside: run from here. Otherwise this box travels to the hub on its own; a member then holds until the tank's door takes it in; the tank waits for the whole group in the hub, re-sends any member still elsewhere its OWN travel (three rounds, then it goes on and says so), walks the hub route alone, checks the group is in its copy and uses the door once for everyone.
- `runner:reachHub(ctx) -> ok, why`: This box gets itself to the hub zone by its own travel (nav.travelTo); nobody is carried.
- `runner:awaitGroupIn(ctx, short, display, roundMs) -> ok, partial`: Wait until every member is in the zone; a member still missing after a round is re-sent its own travel. Members are named by role or box id in the log, never by character.
- `runner:awaitZoneIn(ctx) -> ok, why`: A member holds in the hub until the tank's door takes it in. A loop waits as long as it takes.
- `runner:walkHubRoute(ctx) -> ok, why`: The tank's own walk to the door: hub.route's steps (path, campspot who = "me", wait, interact; a wait_group step is skipped and said), else hub.approach's waypoints.
- `runner:useDoor(ctx) -> ok, why`: Stand within hub.entrance.tolerance of the entrance, then use hub.door (its actor and verb) for the whole group (who = "group"; "me" on a solo run), picking ctx.difficulty's copy.
- `runner:leaveInstance(ctx, solo) -> ok, why`: Leave by the exit door (leaveByExit), tried up to three times while still inside.
- `runner:leaveByExit(ctx, solo) -> ok, why`: One try at the exit: find the nearest zone exit within 80 m, camp the group 3 m short of it when it is further than 4 m (an exit only takes from within about 4 m, measured flat), use the exit, answer the copy picker with its last row so every box lands in the same copy, and wait up to 90 s for the zone change (using the exit again after 20 s). No exit in range: use the zone command where we stand.
- `runner:awaitOut(ctx) -> ok, why`: A member waits for the tank's exit to take it out.
- `runner:nearestExit() -> door | nil`: The exit door the runner would take from here.
- `ic.campShort(mx, mz, door, short) -> x, z`: Where the group camps before an exit: never ON the door, where everyone would push into it.
- `runner:runEncounter(enc, ctx) -> verdict`: Run one encounter: its when gate, its combat override for the fight, its phases in order with the reactive ones checked between phases and on every fight tick, then its done test.
- `runner:sweepReactive(ctx) -> nil`: Fire every reactive phase whose condition holds now (the engage action calls this on each fight tick).
- `runner:runAction(a, ctx) -> ok, note`: Do one action: one key names one call to the interfaces.
- `runner:lootOp(ctx, op, key) -> true, note`: Take loot through the loot interface and record what came. In a running EB a chest step takes every chest within 75 m, nearest first - a far one (the chest a named left out of reach, a double drop) is summoned once (game.SummonChest, /summon, when the command gate lets it out), else walked to - and the tank walks back to where it stood; a chest that will not open is said and left.
