A LORE drop that stays in the window because the tank holds one is asked of the group (every other EB box checks itself: eb others lootdistro scan \<item>): the leader's own window hands it to the first member who lacks it (the window's own hand-out, held until it is proven live), any other window leaves it for them to take, and a chest whose lore everyone holds is skipped for the rest of the visit; the window is closed.
- `runner:watchRoute(ctx) -> nil`: The run watchdog: a lead nowhere near the route - more than OFF_M (60) from the spots of the step it is on and of the next step with a place, neither moving nor getting closer for OFF_SECS (45) - goes on from the step nearest to where it stands (a path from its nearest spot): it sets ctx.jump, and the wait in hand ends, as with eb ic goto. Every wait polls it through ctx.aborting, at most once a second.
- `runner:lootWatch(ctx, s) -> verdict | nil`: Chests as they appear: before the tank walks on (a path step) every chest that appeared since - a trash named's, an event's - is taken (loot.watch, within 75 m), so none is left behind on the way. Said only when there was one. runOnce calls it before each step.
- `runner:lootSweep(ctx) -> verdict | nil`: The sweep before the way out: at the zone's end every chest within 100 m is taken (loot.sweep), before the members' hand-over and the T.S.E, so what the chests held is traded and transmuted too. zoneEnd calls it.
- `runner:announce(ctx, msg) -> nil`: Say a line (the log, and brain.report for the windows), with the run's results filled in.
- `runner:worldFacade() -> w`: The one object every condition reads through, built over the combat, nav and events interfaces. A sensor that cannot be read answers false, never a made-up true.
- `runner.evalCond(cond, w) -> holds`: Evaluate one condition.
- `runner.evalWhen(list, w) -> holds`: Evaluate a when or done list.
- `runner:recoverDeath(ctx, deadIndex, enc) -> stepIndex`: After a death: run the encounter's own on_death actions, wait for the group to be revived, then walk back from the nearest positioned step at or before the death (skipping loot and skipped steps). Nothing is moved any other way.
- `runner:recoverStuck(ctx, atIndex) -> ok, why`: When this box is wedged: the evac chain (nav.evac). Never any other move.
- `runner:betweenRuns(ctx) -> report`: The chores at the end of a run, in order: every box's saved T.S.E pass (this box waits for its own, 10 minutes at most), a repair trip to the guild hall mender when this box's gear is under 90%, then the maintenance cycle (20 minutes at most). A chore that cannot be done is said and skipped; it never stops a loop.
- `ic.parseLoopArgs(text) -> { file, minutes, difficulty } | nil, usage`: Split a loop command line.
- `ic.loopMinutes(inst, opts) -> minutes`: Which loop window applies.
- `ic.decide(secsUntil, minutesLeft) -> "reset" | "wait" | "end"`: What the tank does between laps.
- `runner:reuseLeft(inst) -> seconds`: The reuse timer, through nav.reuseSeconds.
- `runner:turnaround(ctx, minutesLeft, lap) -> true | "end", why | false, why`: The tank between laps: wait the timer out where we stand (inside, when one zone is looped), leave by the exit, reset from outside once the whole group is out, then run the chores that leave the zone.
- `ic.LOOP_USAGE -> string`: The usage line of eb ic loop.
- `ic.parseOptionFlags(text) -> flags, rest`: Take an instance's option words out of a command line: eb ic run fixture_hollow skip_bonus=off.
- `runner:optionsFor(inst, opts) -> on, unknown`: Which of the instance's options are on for a run (the file's default, flipped by the run).
- `ic.skipSteps(inst, on) -> { [step id] = option id }`: The steps a run leaves out.
- `runner:stepSkipped(s, ctx) -> why | nil`: Is this step left out of this run, and why.
- `ic.checkOptions(inst) -> true | nil, why`: The loader's options check.
- `ic.checkHub(inst) -> true | nil, why`: The loader's hub rule: hub route steps may only be path (never group = "follow"), campspot (who = "me"), wait, interact or wait_group.
- `runner:saveRun(opts) -> record`: Snapshot a configured run to keep. The record is plain data: store it off the game thread, read it back later.
- `runner:resumeRun(inst, record, over) -> ok, why, report`: Restore a saved run and start it at its pointer, saying what the saved reuse timer had left.
- `runner:stepIndexById(inst, id) -> index | nil`: A route step id to the index run's opts.from takes.
- `runner:waitCombatClear(ctx, capMs) -> ok, hold`: The instance combat wait: it holds while the group is in a fight or a straggler nobody fights is near (handed to the combat engine's own target list), and lets go on a clear or a combat flag with nothing behind it for 5 seconds. A lone in-combat flag never holds a run forever.
- `runner:anyHated() -> bool`: The fight read the combat wait uses.
- `runner:holdLook(ctx) -> look`: One step of the combat wait.
- `runner:applyOverride(ctx, enc) -> nil`: Turn an encounter's combat override on for its fight (the runner does this on entry, and clearOverride on every way out).
- `runner:clearOverride(ctx, enc) -> nil`: Turn its combat override off again.
- `runner:swimSet(ctx, dir, who) -> ok, note`: Hold or release swim-up for a water fight. The tank holds it for the group; a member's runner holds.
- `runner:swimRelease(ctx) -> nil`: Let a held swim-up go. The end of every run calls it, whatever ended the run.
- `instance.lua -> { schema = "eb.ic/1", zone, short, hub, route, encounters, rules, options, loop, variants, loot_method }`: The instance file. schema "eb.ic/1" (required); zone = its display name; short = its short name (what nav.zone() answers inside); hub = how to get in (see "hub"); route = the ordered STEPS the tank runs (see "route"); encounters = the ordered list of encounter file names (for checks and progress); rules = the rotation to arm before the first pull ("default" = the character's own cast stack); options = run options (see "options"); loop = { reset = "self", rerun_first = true, max_minutes = 0 }; variants = the difficulties the file covers; loot_method = { method = "leader" | "ffa" | "lotto" | "nbg" | "roundrobin" | "keep", rarity = "all" | "treasured" | "legendary" | "fabled" } = the group's loot method the lead sets as a run begins (see "startLootMethod"). The file only returns this table: nothing may run when it loads.
- `inst.hub -> { zone, name, difficulty, approach, route, entrance, door }`: Getting in. zone = the hub zone every box travels to first, each on its own; name = its display name (optional); difficulty = the copy the door is asked for ("\[Heroic I\]"; eb ic run ... \[difficulty\] wins); approach = the tank's sparse waypoints to the door ({ {x,y,z}, ... }, the mesh fills the gaps); route = the tank's own hub steps (wins over approach): path, campspot (who = "me"), wait, interact, wait_group (skipped); entrance = { loc = {x,y,z}, tolerance = 8 }: where the tank must stand to use the door; door = { actor = "\<door name>", verb = "\<its verb>" }.
- `inst.route[n] -> { id, act, ... }`: Every step has an id (a stable label: verdicts, announces, resume pointers and options name it) and an act: path { spots = { {x,y,z}, ... }, group = "hold" (default: the tank walks alone, the group stays camped) | "follow" (the group follows on the mesh, for bringing it into a boss room) }; campspot { name, spot = {x,y,z}, who = "group" (camp on the tank) | "me" | a role list (split part of the group) }; encounter { name = "\<encounter file>" }; loot { op = "chest" | "shinies" } (a missing chest is a success); announce { message } with {{verdict.\<id>}} filled in; zoneout { via = "exit" } (the tank takes the group out by the exit door; a member waits); wait { seconds }; wait_actor_dead { name, seconds }; interact { actor, verb } (the tank clicks); swim { dir = "up" | "stop", who }; evac (the end-of-run evac to the entrance, inside the copy); lootmethod { method, rarity } (the lead sets the group's loot method from here on - the same words as loot_method). Any step may carry when = { \<condition>, ... }: it runs only when every condition holds (else it is skipped and said).
- `encounters/<name>.lua -> { schema, name, aka, kind, spot, search, when, phases, done, on_death, kill_order, extra_targets, no_autotarget, combat_override, override_priority }`: One fight or mechanic as conditions -> actions. name = the actor the fight is about; aka = other names it goes by; kind = "named" | "boss" | "trash" | "mechanic"; spot = where the tank fights it from; when = a gate (all must hold, else the verdict is "skipped:gate"); phases = the ordered phases (see "phases"); done = a success test after the phases (false = "FAILED:done-test"); on_death = actions run on a wipe here, before the walk back (they may not move the group); kill_order = a kill-first list (extra_targets go after it); no_autotarget = true keeps this fight's names off the engine's kill-first list (neither its own step nor the walk toward it sets one); combat_override = a combat override block applied for exactly this fight.
- `enc.phases[n] -> { id, when, repeat_, once, do_ }`: A phase is { id, do\_ = { \<action>, ... } }. No when: it runs once, in order. when without repeat\_: a one-shot gate that waits (up to 2 minutes) for its condition, then runs. when with repeat\_ = true: a REACTIVE phase, checked between the ordered phases and on every fight tick, that runs whenever its condition holds - adds surfacing, a cure, a position swap. once = true makes a reactive phase fire one time per pull (an enrage, a scripted event).
- `{ actor_present = name } | { actor_dead = name } | { actor_count = { query, cmp, value } } | ...`: The conditions a when or done list may hold (a list means every one must hold): actor_present / actor_dead = "\<name>"; actor_count = { query = "\<name>", cmp = ">=" | "<=" | ">" | "<" | "==", value }; health_below / health_above = \<my health %>; mob_health_below = { name, pct }; in_combat = true | false; near_spot = { spot = {x,y,z}, within = metres }; timer_expired = { seconds, name } (since the pull, or since a reset_timer); detriment_present = { who = "group", type = "noxious", name } (true = any curable one); chat_seen = { match = "\<text>", since = seconds } (a chat or emote line this fight); mob_casting = { mob = "\<part of its name>", ability = "\<part of the cast's name>" | \<its number>, since = seconds } (that mob is casting it now - its cast bar, else the game's own "\<mob> begins casting \<ability>" line - it opens with the mob's name; a player who quotes it never counts - in the last since seconds, 5 by default, never before the pull: a reactive phase answers each cast); has_item = "\<item>" (in my bags); actor_type = { name, type }; the combinators all = { ... }, any = { ... }, not\_ = \<condition>; or a function(w) for anything else. An unknown condition is FALSE: a misspelled gate never pulls a boss.
- `{ engage = name } | { pull = name } | { clear_area = name | true, radius } | ...`: One key per action, each one call: cast = "\<ability>", who (only that role casts); target = { names } (a kill-first list); campspot = { name, spot, who }; pull = "\<name>"; engage = "\<name>", opts = { radius, reach, hpFloor, leash, chase, absentIsDead, timeoutMs } (fight it to death; reactive phases fire on its ticks); clear_area = "\<name>" | true, radius (clear a pack; true = everything attackable); cure = { who, type, name } | true; dispel = { mob, name } | true (strip a mob's buff); reset_timer = "\<timer>"; move_to = {x,y,z}; interact = { actor, verb }; wait = seconds; wait_combat = seconds (the combat-hold wait); wait_actor_dead = "\<name>", seconds; use_item = "\<item>", on, who, until\_ = { conditions }, tries, seconds, every; swim = "up" | "stop"; ability_tag = { tag, seconds, mode = "allow" | "embargo" }; announce = "\<text>"; loot = "chest" | "shinies"; wait_ready = { ability, who = "group" | "me" | \<a member>, seconds, fallback } (wait until that box has the ability ready - it casts it the moment it is, eb readycast - else the fallback goes to every box that has it ready); anchor = "\<label>" | true (keep where the tank stands - the yo-yo's out) and to_anchor = "\<label>" | true, who = "group" | "me", within = metres (walk back to it: the group camps there too; it is used up, a later walk back needs a fresh keep; none kept is said, never a failed fight) - a joust out and back, a run-out that returns to the very spot; fn = function(ctx) ... end (anything else; ctx has w, verdicts and opts).
- `inst.options[n] -> { id, label, default, skip_steps }`: A run option: { id = "skip_bonus", label = "...", default = true | false, skip_steps = { "\<route step id>", ... } }. An option that is ON skips its steps. A run flips one with opts.options = { skip_bonus = false } or by typing skip_bonus=off after eb ic run / loop. A skipped step is said, never run, never walked back to.
- `inst.blocks[<id>] -> { kind = "if" | "while" | "repeat", test, until, max, seconds }`: The gates a converted zone file puts on its steps (another bot's zone file read by EB, and the shipped copies made from such files): a step carries blocks = { "\<id>:then" | "\<id>:else", ... } and runs only inside its branch; a while or repeat runs its steps again until its until test holds (max times). A test is one of the conditions above, or the run's own: difficulty = "heroic2"; zone = { is | is_not | contains | starts | ends = "\<text>" }; group_has_class = { "\<class>", ... }; var = { name, op = "=" | "~=" | "set" | "unset", value } (a run variable a setvar step wrote); me_coord = { axis = "x" | "y" | "z", cmp, value } (where I stand); actor_near = { name, within | beyond }; engaged = { name, within = 50 } (that named is in its fight: up within the reach while I am in a fight; no name = I am in a fight); actor_at = { name, axis, cmp, value } (a living one of that name stands on that side of the line; a box whose actor rows carry no place says so and reads false); dead = true; option = { id, on }; always / never; unread = "\<what the file said>" (false, said once). An unknown test is refused at load.
- `env -> { nav, combat, brain, loot, upkeep, events, now, sleep, log }`: What the runner calls. A call may block and answer ok\[, why\] or be pollable and answer a status ("working" = call again). nav: zone(), here(), distance(x,y,z) (flat), pathTo(spots, opts), goTo(x,y,z, opts), toActor(name, opts), interact(name, verb), campSpot(name, x,y,z, who), releaseCamp(who), travelTo(zone, opts) (this box, by its own allowed travel), zoneDoor(actor, difficulty, opts), exits(radius), zoneExit(who), copyPicker(), answerCopyPicker(who, choice), reuseSeconds(zone), resetZone(which), stuck(), evac(opts). combat: find(name, opts), count(query), myHealth(), mobHealth(name), inCombat(), amDead(), setRules(name), autoTarget(list), cast(ability, who), pull(name, opts), engage(name, opts), clearArea(name, radius, opts), waitActorDead(name, ms, opts); optional: cure, dispel, detriment, anyHated, npcsNear, addTarget, dropTarget, setContext, addOverride, removeOverride, useItem, hasItem, actorType, abilityTag. brain: isTank(), role(), group() -> { { isMe, id, role, zone } }, sendToZone(id, zone), sameCopyAsGroup(), gatherToMyCopy(), paused(), aborting(), revived(), afk(on), report(ev). loot: chest(opts), shinies(opts). upkeep (the chores): tse(scope), tseBusy(), gear(), inHall(), callToHall(scope), mender(), repair(scope), maintenance(opts), maintenanceBusy(). events: chatSeen(match, sinceMs) (optional).
- `report.verdicts -> { [step id] = verdict }`: What each step came to: an encounter step's verdict ("killed", "cleared", "skipped:gate", "FAILED:\<why>", "DIED:\<why>"), a loot step's drop (or "none"). announce messages read them as {{verdict.\<step id>}}.
- `runner:begin(ctx) -> nil`: The start of a run: one header line (the zone, the copy, this box's role, DRY RUN when it is one), the rotation armed (combat.setRules with the file's rules, "default" = the character's own cast stack), the damage source said, one line per run option, and the group's loot method (startLootMethod). run and loop call it; call it yourself before runOnce when you drive a run by hand.
- `runner.STEP -> { [act] = function(runner, s, ctx) -> ok, note, tag }`: The route step handlers, by act: path, campspot, encounter, loot, announce, zoneout, wait, wait_actor_dead, interact, evac, swim, lootmethod. runStep looks the step's act up here, so a new act is one entry: STEP.ring_gong = function(runner, s, ctx) ... return true, "rang it" end, and a route step { id = "gong", act = "ring_gong" } runs it. An act with no handler is said and skipped.
- `runner:stepPath(s, ctx) -> ok, note`: The tank walks the spots on the mesh (nav.pathTo, stopping when the run stops). A member's runner holds at the tank's camp, or follows on the mesh when the step says group = "follow" (the tank first lets go of the group's camp then). A dry run only says what it would walk.
- `runner:stepCampspot(s, ctx) -> ok, note`: The tank sets a camp spot (nav.campSpot): who = "group" camps every member on it, "me" only the tank, a role list splits part of the group off. A member's runner holds: the tank's camp spots move it. A swim-up hold that was on is put back after the camp walk.
- `runner:stepEncounter(s, ctx) -> ok, note, tag`: Run the named encounter (runEncounter) and record its verdict under the step's id.
- `runner:stepLoot(s, ctx) -> true, note`: Take the loot through the loot interface (lootOp) and record the drop under the step's id.
- `runner:stepAnnounce(s, ctx) -> true, "announced"`: Say the step's message with the run's verdicts filled in (announce).
- `runner:stepZoneout(s, ctx) -> ok, note`: The tank takes the group out by the exit door (leaveInstance); a member waits to be taken out (awaitOut).
- `runner:stepWait(s, ctx) -> true, note`: Wait a number of seconds (a stop ends the wait at once; a dry run does not wait).
- `runner:stepWaitActorDead(s, ctx) -> ok, note`: Wait until an actor is dead (an event mob, a pet the boss leaves behind).
- `runner:stepInteract(s, ctx) -> ok, note`: The tank clicks an actor (a lever, a portal, a chest that needs opening) through nav.interact.
- `runner:stepSwim(s, ctx) -> ok, note`: The route act swim: the tank holds swim-up (for itself or the group) through a water fight, and lets it go.
- `runner:stepEvac(s, ctx) -> ok, note`: The end-of-run evac, inside the copy: wait for the fight to clear (a while at most), let the last loot settle, let go of any swim hold and of the group's camp, then nav.evac takes this box or the group to the entrance. A member's runner holds; the tank's evac takes it along.
- `runner:preArm(ctx, i) -> names | nil`: The next named first from its section's start: when step i is a walk (a path step) toward an encounter - the next encounter step on the route - that encounter's names go on the engine's kill-first list once (preArmNames), so a fight the walk runs into takes the named first, not only once its own step is reached. runOnce calls it before each step; each lap puts it first again. The list orders a fight that is on: it opens none.
- `runner:meetFight(ctx) -> nil`: A file's fight met in a fight: while the tank walks the route and the group fights, a mob of one of the next MEET_AHEAD (2) fights - its name, alive in reach - brings that fight's rules on for this fight: its combat override and its kill-first names, said once. They go off when the fight is over, or stay with the fight's own step once the route reaches it; meetEnd takes them off when a run or a lap ends. The waits look at it (ctx.aborting), at most once a second. The fight's phases stay with its own step.
- `runner:meetEnd(ctx) -> nil`: A met fight's rules still on when a run or a lap ends go off (run and loop call it).
- `runner:armWhenClear(ctx) -> nil`: A section's named held off while the group fought (preArm) goes on the kill-first list once the group is clear; dropped when its own fight's step is reached (that fight sets its own list). The waits look at it (ctx.aborting), at most once a second, and runOnce before each step.
- `runner.preArmNames(enc) -> names`: What a section puts first before its fight.
- `runner:stepLootMethod(s, ctx) -> true, note`: The route act lootmethod: the lead sets the group's loot method from this step on (setLootMethod); a member's runner leaves it to the lead.
- `runner:startLootMethod(ctx) -> note | nil`: As a run begins (begin calls it): the run's own pick (opts.loot, from loot=\<method> on the eb ic line) before the file's loot_method, and "keep" (either one) sets nothing. The lead sets it; a member's runner says the lead does.
- `runner:setLootMethod(ctx, method, rarity, why) -> true, note`: Set the group's loot method on the lead's box: upkeep.lootMethod sends EB's own eb loot method \<method> \<rarity> (EB's own looting follows it, and the group's leader sets it on the game's group). A member's runner, a dry run and a box with no such line each say so and send nothing; ctx.lootMethod keeps what was set.
- `runner.checkLootMethod(t, what) -> true | nil, why`: The loader's check of an instance's loot_method and of a lootmethod route step: a file the runner could not honour is refused at load.
- `runner:swimReassert(ctx) -> nil`: Put a held swim-up back on the boxes that had it (a camp walk lets the key go); campspot calls it.
- `combat.engage(name, opts) -- opts.abort() -> stopping`: What the engage and clear_area actions hand the combat interface as opts.abort: a function that answers true once the run is stopping. A combat interface that fights over many waits checks it and gives up at once.
- `combat.engage(name, opts) -- opts.onTick()`: What the engage action hands the combat interface as opts.onTick: call it on each fight tick and the encounter's reactive phases (adds surfacing, a cure, a position swap) are checked and run mid-fight.
- `w.markFight() -> nil`: Restart the fight clock (the engine does this at each pull): every named timer starts over, and chat_seen counts lines from now.
- `w.resetTimer(name) -> nil`: Start a named timer now (the reset_timer action does this): timer_expired { name = ... } counts from here.
- `w.timerElapsed(name) -> ms`: How long a fight timer has run.
- `w.detrimentPresent(q) -> bool`: The detriment_present sensor, read through the combat interface.
- `w.chatSeen(q) -> bool`: The chat_seen sensor, read through the events interface (env.events.chatSeen). Reading it never uses a line up.
- `w.mobCasting(q) -> bool`: The mob_casting sensor: the cast bar through the combat interface (combat.mobCasting - the name reads for my target, another mob's bar gives the cast's number), else the game's own cast line through the events interface (env.events.castSeen) in the last since seconds and never before the pull. Only a line that OPENS with the mob's name (or an NPC's own emote) counts: a player's say, shout or channel line that quotes it never fires the answer.
- `w.hasItem(item) -> bool`: The has_item sensor, through the combat interface.
- `w.actorType(name) -> type | nil`: The actor_type sensor: combat.actorType, else the type on the row combat.find returns.
- `runner:runEncounterBody(enc, ctx) -> verdict`: The inside of runEncounter: the tank walks to the encounter's spot, the ordered phases run with the reactive ones swept between them, then the done test. runEncounter wraps it so the encounter's combat override is always cleared, whatever ends the fight; call runEncounter, not this, unless you manage the override yourself.
- `runner:stragglers(ctx, short, display) -> { { label, zone, id }, ... }`: Who is still elsewhere - what the group wait re-sends its own travel.
- `runner:sameCopy(ctx) -> true`: Before the door: when the group stands in different copies of the hub, ask the brain to bring them into the tank's copy (brain.gatherToMyCopy - nobody walks) and wait a while; still split, the door takes the ones in the tank's copy. Solo and dry runs skip it.
- `runner:choreTse(ctx) -> note`: The first chore: every box (this box only on a solo run) runs its SAVED T.S.E pass (upkeep.tse), and this box waits for its own - it should start within seconds, then end; 10 minutes at most. Scrolls of Master quality or better are never touched (the T.S.E's own rule). It runs at the END of the run, inside, where the run ended.
- `runner:choreRepair(ctx) -> note`: The second chore: when this box's gear is under 90% (upkeep.gear), the group calls to the guild hall (upkeep.callToHall), walks to the Guild Hall Mender as a camp spot, repairs (upkeep.repair) and lets the camp go. The way back in is the next lap's own travel.
- `runner:choreMaintenance(ctx) -> note`: The third chore: run the maintenance cycle from the top (upkeep.maintenance { fromTop = true }) and wait for it, 20 minutes at most.
- `runner:waitReuse(ctx, secs) -> ok, why`: The visible reset wait, where the tank stands - inside the cleared copy when one zone is looped. It says how long is left now and then (every 2 to 60 minutes, by how long is left), and a wait of 10 minutes or more turns the brain's AFK keep-alive on for its length.
- `ic.clearedCopy(ctx) -> why | nil`: The loop's check that a reset really took. A lap whose nameds were all gone ends the loop with this reason instead of cycling a cleared copy.
- `runner:sayOptions(ctx) -> nil`: One log line per option of the instance: ON or off for this run and how many route steps it skips; an option the run named that the file does not have is said once and ignored.

#### Module `eb.loops`

The self-sustaining chore loops as brain goals: overseer, errands, trainer, mercenary and collections. Build one, hand it the activities provider it acts through, and set it on the brain.

Each loop is a brain GOAL: { name, kind, params, ctx, advance(self, brain, snapshot) }. The brain calls advance once per tick between its own interrupts (death, fights, full bags), so a loop never waits: each call does one bite and answers "working", "done" or "blocked" with a reason. ctx is the loop's resume point; an interrupt freezes it and the loop carries on from the same phase.

THE PROVIDER. params.act is the activities provider (eb.loops.interface): the window drivers the loop acts through (overseer, trainer, mercenary, city writs) and the economy's writs and collections. A loop with no provider for its domain answers blocked once and says so.

SAFE BY DEFAULT. Every loop checks params.stop first, on every tick. Spending coin (buying mission scrolls, hiring a mercenary) and using items up (unlocking mercenaries from the bags) run only behind an explicit flag. The trainer spends points only on abilities your trainList names - it never picks one itself. No loop dismisses anything, and none ever logs a character out.

LOOPING ZONES. Looping an instance is eb ic loop (eb.ic, runner:loop): looping ONE zone, the tank waits inside the cleared copy until its timer is up, then goes out, resets it from outside and goes back in, with the chores (T.S.E first) at the END of each run, inside where it ended. A LIST of zones - call the crew out and move on to the next - is the instance queue (eb iqueue), which has no runner yet.

WHAT EB CALLS A TASK. Several kinds of repeating work, each with its own home in these docs: (1) a pulse JOB - a function EB calls every frame or every N ms, which must never wait - and a pulse TASK - work in its own coroutine that may wait with eb.delay (eb.platform: pulse.every, pulse.spawn); (2) a brain GOAL - one pollable step per brain tick, with the brain's death, fight and full-bag interrupts around it (eb.brain, and the chore loops on this page: overseer, errands, trainer, mercenary, collections); (3) an instance LOOP - one zone again and again, waiting inside until its timer is up (eb.ic runner:loop); (4) a power-level ROUTE - STEPS from one level band to the next (eb.plroutes); (5) an economy JOB - an ordered list of step functions with a cursor, advanced one bite per call, that every economy action stands on (eb.economy.job); and (6) the T.S.E hand-over - at the zone's END, inside, each member gives its T.S.E pick to the leader and every box runs its saved T.S.E pass (eb.economy.tse, and the instance runner's chores).

HOW TO RUN A CHORE LOOP. 1. Build a provider for its domain (eb.loops.providers.build fills the verbs you do not have with stubs that say so). 2. Make the goal: loops.new{ kind = "overseer", params = { act = provider, dest = { zone, x, y, z }, stop = fn } }. 3. Hand it to the brain (brain:setGoal / pushGoal), or call goal:advance(brain, snapshot) yourself once per tick. 4. It answers "working" until its pass is done; "blocked" names what is missing.

**File:** `lua/eb/loops/init.lua` in the EB folder

- `loops.new(spec) -> goal`: Build a chore loop.
- `loops.installInto(brainGoals) -> { kinds }`: Teach the brain the loop kinds by name, so brain:setGoal({ kind = "trainer", params = { ... } }) builds one. Safe to call more than once.
- `loops.describeAll() -> { [kind] = text }`: The kinds, explained (for a window or a help text).
- `loops.KINDS -> { [kind] = module }`: The loop kinds and their modules: overseer, errands, trainer, mercenary, collections. Each module has advance(self, brain, snapshot), kind, start (the first phase) and preset (the combat preset the brain sets).
- `goal:advance(brain, snap) -> "working" | "done" | "blocked", why`: One bite of the loop. The brain calls this; call it yourself to drive a loop without a brain.

#### Module `eb.move`

The low-level mover the walker steers with: where you stand and face, turn to a point, hold and release the movement keys.

require("eb.move") answers the platform's movement service - EB for InnerSpace's mover below, or EB Boxer's with the same walking set (pos, heading, headingTo, face, stop, forwardOn and the turn keys). Prefer eb.nav for walking anywhere; use eb.move to face something, nudge, or read your position cheaply.

HEADINGS: EB counts headings its own way - 0 faces +Z, 90 faces +X - and converts to the game's once, inside. KEYS are your own game binds (setKeys); a key command goes out only when its state changes, and every held key is let go by stop(), by the end of a walk and when EB stops.

COST: pos(), heading() and swimming() share ONE game read a frame.

NO AUTO-RUN, NO FLIGHT: there is no auto-run key and no fly key. A character moves along a route on the mesh (eb.nav) or by a key you hold yourself for a step (forwardOn), and a walk lets every key go when it ends.

How to turn and step by hand: 1. move.face(x, z) to turn to a point (or move.faceActor(id)). 2. move.forwardOn(true) to walk, move.forwardOn(false) to stop - or move.tap("forward") for one short step. 3. Always end with move.stop(), which lets go of every key. 4. If your movement binds are not the defaults, call move.setKeys once at start.

**File:** `lua/eb/move.lua` in the EB folder

- `move.pos() -> x, y, z | nil`: Your position.
- `move.heading() -> degrees | nil`: Your facing.
- `move.headingTo(x, z) -> degrees | nil`: Which way a point lies.
- `move.turnDelta(a, b) -> degrees`: How far to turn from one heading to another.
- `move.distanceTo(x, y, z) -> metres | nil`: How far a point is.
- `move.distance2DTo(x, z) -> metres | nil`: How far a point is across the ground.
- `move.face(x, z) -> sent`: Turn to face a point.
- `move.faceHeading(deg) -> sent`: Turn to a heading.
- `move.faceActor(id) -> sent`: Turn to face an actor.
- `move.forwardOn(on) -> sent`: Hold or release forward. backOn, turnLeftOn, turnRightOn, strafeLeftOn and strafeRightOn work the same way.
- `move.turnLeftOn(on) -> sent`: Hold or release turn-left (turnRightOn for the other way).
- `move.turnRightOn(on) -> sent`: Hold or release turn-right.
- `move.backOn(on) -> sent`: Hold or release the back key.
- `move.strafeLeftOn(on) -> sent`: Hold or release strafe-left.
- `move.strafeRightOn(on) -> sent`: Hold or release strafe-right.
- `move.jump() -> sent`: Jump once.
- `move.stop(force) -> wasHolding`: Let go of every movement key. Safe any time; at most once a second it also releases every key whose state could have been lost, so nothing stays held.
- `move.held(role) -> bool`: Is EB holding a movement key?
- `move.swimming() -> bool | nil`: Are you swimming? Part of the same read as pos().
- `move.moving() -> bool | nil`: Are you moving? (its own read)
- `move.mounted() -> bool | nil`: Are you on a mount? (its own read)
- `move.setKeys(t) -> keys`: Tell EB your movement binds when they are not the game's defaults.
- `move.status() -> text`: Which keys EB holds right now.
- `move.hold(role, down) -> sent`: Hold or release one movement key by its role. forwardOn and the other \*On calls are this with a fixed role.
- `move.tap(role) -> sent`: Press and release one key by its role: a jump, one short step.
- `move.swimUpOn(on) -> true`: Hold or release swim-up for the walk in progress. stop() lets it go (the group's hold stays).
- `move.swimDownOn(on) -> true`: Hold or release swim-down (a dive). Never while the group holds swim-up.
- `move.swimHold(on) -> true`: The group's swim-up hold before a fight in deep water: swim-up stays down through every walk and stop until swimHold(false), or stop(true) when EB stops. nav.swimHold is the same, through the walker.
- `move.swimHeld() -> bool`: Is the group's swim-up hold on?
- `move.headingGame() -> degrees | nil`: Your facing as the game counts it (EB's own heading() differs from it by half a turn).
- `move.fromGameHeading(deg) -> degrees`: Convert a game heading to EB's convention.
- `move.toGameHeading(deg) -> degrees`: Convert EB's heading to the game's (the two differ by 180 degrees).
- `move.invalidate()`: Forget this frame's position read, so the next pos() reads again - after a ride lands or a zone has loaded in the same frame.
- `move.context() -> 1 | 0`: Can key input reach the game at all? nav.canMove() answers the same with a reason.

#### Module `eb.nav`

Walk the zone's mesh: to a point, to a saved spot, after an actor, to another zone by its own transit - and stop cleanly. EB's one mover.

eb.nav is the only way EB moves a character, and it moves one way: along a route on the zone's own .nav mesh, with the movement keys (eb.move). A walk plans ONE route over EB's mesh for the zone, then steers along it a frame at a time, re-planning only when it has to: stuck, a door to open, a hazard to back away from. A point within nav.SHORT_HOP metres whose straight line the mesh itself proves clear is walked without a route; a line the mesh cannot prove is planned like any other walk. There is no other mode to choose and nothing else to configure.

NO ROUTE, NO WALK: a goal the mesh has no route to - a spot past its edge, or any goal in a zone with no mesh at all, even six metres away - is not walked at. There is no straight run at it, no fallback walk and no swim across open water: goPoint answers false and says why in plain words ("no mesh: ...", "no route on the .nav: ... - the mesh has no way to this spot", "the spot is in open water the mesh does not reach (...)"), the character stays where it is, and whatever started the walk decides what to do next. A goal a few metres past the mesh's edge (within the router's 4 m snap) is walked to the mesh's nearest point.

LINKS: where the mesh joins two floors - a drop, a jump, a climb, a door - the walk goes to the take-off, faces the landing, taps the jump key ONCE for a jump or a climb, and goes on from the landing (nav.linkAction); a lift (kind 5: a mesh fixes lift, eb.nav_fixes.liftBridges / liftAt) is boarded, its actor clicked once (nav.liftClick), its wait and ride stood out, then it is stepped off at the exit.

CAVES AND RIMS: the progress along the route counts height twice over (a cave under a hill is never "near" the hill), a descent's aim is pushed out so the walk walks off a rim, arrival waits until the character is at rest (and walks back at most twice if it slid past), a partial route's end is no arrival ("the route ended N m short"), a walk knocked off the route's floor plans again from where it fell, and a wedged walk tries a door, hops a step the route goes on over, backs up and re-plans. nav.state says where a trip stands: Idle, WaitingForMesh, Planning, Moving, Arrived, Stopped (ended on purpose) or Failed; nav.last.state keeps how the last one ended.

IN THE WAY: a circle that comes up on the route ahead after the walk planned - a live blocker standing up, a circle added on the way - makes the walk plan again round it ("\<name> stands on the route ahead"). No route while a live blocker stands up, but one with it down: the walk is held where it stands, keys up, until the blocker goes down ("held (live blockers): \<name> is up - waiting for it to go down"), at most a minute, and the time held is not the walk's time budget. A solid prop is a circle only while its object stands there and is in the way (the mesh does not already wall it off, a walk does not go over it), at its radius + 0.8 m. Each "stands on the route ahead" re-plan is counted on its own (nav.AHEAD_REPLANS, 30 a walk) and never spends the stuck re-plans (stuckreplans). The route goes ROUND a circle - it keeps the object's radius + 0.8 m and takes a short way round its edge - instead of closing the ground it touches; only an object with no way round closes the polygons it covers ("no way round N avoid circle(s) (...) - routed round the ground they cover"). A circle holding the route's start or goal shrinks so that point sits 0.1 m outside it; the start's and the goal's own polygons are never closed.

A walk WAITS for the game a frame at a time, so it runs inside an EB pulse task (require("eb.platform").pulse() .spawn) or through a command (eb walk / eb follow / eb goto), never in an event handler or a frame job. Inside a task the default wait is eb.delay(0); pass opts.yield to wait your own way.

Safety is built in: a goal that stands in lava becomes its shore; twice a second a walk checks for lethal liquid and for health lost out of combat, backs away the way it came and plans round the spot. Cross-zone trips use the game's own travel network only (bells, wizard spires, druid rings, the zone's pads) - never the fast-travel map.

A walk ends with every movement key released and its outcome kept in nav.last. nav.active is the walk running now (its goal and corners, for a window) or nil.

How to walk somewhere: 1. Run your code as an EB task (require("eb.platform").pulse().spawn(name, fn)), or type a command (eb walk, eb follow, eb goto). 2. Call nav.goPoint(x, y, z) and read its ok, why. 3. Leave a walk early with nav.stop() - from anywhere, a handler included. 4. For a saved spot call nav.gotoNamed(name); for another zone nav.gotoZone(name). 5. Read how it ended in nav.last.

**File:** `lua/eb/nav.lua` in the EB folder

- `nav.goPoint(x, y, z, opts) -> ok, why`: Walk to a point in this zone over the mesh. The walk is a route on the zone's .nav and nothing else: a goal the mesh has no route to fails and says why, and nothing is walked straight at it - the character stays where it stands.
- `nav.plan(x, y, z, yield, popts) -> plan | nil, why, noWay`: Plan the route to a point without walking it: preview a walk, measure it, or check that a spot is reachable.
- `nav.pathLength(ax, ay, az, bx, by, bz) -> metres | nil, why`: How far a walk would be: the length of the mesh route between two points, not the straight distance. For ordering spots by the way there.
- `nav.pathPoints(ax, ay, az, bx, by, bz) | nav.pathPoints(from, to) -> { { x, y, z }, ... } | nil, why`: The way a walk would take between two spots, as points to draw: the planner a walk uses. The instance builder's Map view draws it, leg by leg.
- `nav.follow(who, opts) -> ok, why`: Follow a moving actor over the mesh, re-aiming the walk as it moves. Without once it keeps following until nav.stop(): when the actor leaves the zone the follower walks to where it went (on the mesh), tries the ways across in turn - the zone door, a step farther along its way - and finds it again on the other side. A zone line past the mesh's edge is said so ("the zone line is past the mesh's edge here - the mesh has no way across") and the door is tried instead; nothing walks off the mesh.
- `nav.stop(why) -> wasWalking`: End the walk or follow that is running and release every movement key. Safe to call any time, from anywhere (a handler, a command, a frame job): the walk notices on its next step and returns false, "stopped".
- `nav.hold(on, why) -> true`: Pause the walks without ending them: keys up at once, the walk waits where it stands (the time held is not counted against its time budget), and when it is let go it plans again from where it is. nav.stop() ends a walk; nav.hold keeps it.
- `nav.drop(co) -> wasActive`: End the one walk that runs on a coroutine - keys up - without raising the stop request every other walk reads. For code that runs its own walk task; nav.stop() ends them all.
- `nav.gotoNamed(name, opts) -> ok, why`: Walk (and, in another zone, travel) to a saved spot by its name.
- `nav.gotoZone(zoneName, opts) -> ok, why`: Travel to another zone over the game's own travel network: walk to the bell, spire, druid ring or pad on the mesh, open it and pick the destination, re-planning from wherever each ride lands. See eb.nav_travel.
- `nav.canMove() -> ok, why`: Can EB move this character right now?
- `nav.cmd(args, opts) -> ok, text`: The command form of the walker. save keeps a private spot by name; mark pins one your crew shares; bl and gl blacklist or greenlight the spot you stand on so routes avoid or allow it.
- `nav.swimUp(ms, yield, height) -> ok, why`: Swim up for a while - out of a hole in a lake's bed, or up to a door's height.
- `nav.swimHold(on)`: Keep swim-up held through every walk and stop until switched off (a fight in deep water).
- `nav.swimHeld() -> bool`: Is swim-up held for the group?
- `nav.last -> { ok, why, t, x, y, z } | nil`: How the last walk ended: ok, the reason, when (ms) and where you stood.
- `nav.active -> { goal, waypoints, plans, hazards } | nil`: The walk running now - its goal, its corners, how many times it planned - or nil. For a window or a status line.
- `nav.SHORT_HOP -> 10.0`: Under this many metres, a line the zone's own mesh proves clear (its raycast, on this zone's loaded mesh) is walked without asking for a route. A mesh that cannot answer, or is still loading, is no proof: the hop is planned like any walk, and with no mesh at all it fails. The other tuning values beside it: nav.FINAL (2 m, the arrival circle), nav.ARRIVE (3 m), nav.FOLLOW_RANGE (4 m), nav.STUCK_MS (2 s stuck sample), nav.REPLANS (4).
- `nav.EXACT -> 0.5`: The arrival circle for a spot to stand on (goPoint's opts.exact): half a metre instead of nav.FINAL's two. Used where a two metre circle would stop short - the mesh's own point just past a zone line.
- `nav.LINK_TAKEOFF -> 1.5`: How close across a link's take-off must be reached - or the walk be already past it - before the jump key goes out.
- `nav.linkAction(plan, st, w, px, py, pz) -> "done" | "hold" | nil`: Walk one of the mesh's links. A take-off is reached exactly (within nav.LINK_TAKEOFF across); for a jump or a climb the walk then faces the landing, holds forward and taps the jump key ONCE; a drop is walked off its edge and passed once you stand on the floor below; a landing is passed on its own floor. A walk asks it every step while its next corner is a link - call it yourself only to try a plan offline.
- `nav.onLink -> function(kind, landing) | nil`: Set it to be told each time the jump key goes out for a link: kind is "jump" or "climb", landing the corner it leads to ({ x, y, z, kind }). Nothing is told for a drop, which takes no key.
- `nav.tryDoor(px, py, pz, range, trip) -> ok, what`: Open the known door nearest a spot - what a walk that is stuck in front of a door does by itself. The click goes out through nav.doorDeps.click (EB wires the game's own door clicker at start). See eb.nav_doors for the door data.
- `nav.doorDeps -> { click = fn(door, verb, attempt) -> ok, why } | nil`: The door clicker a walk uses. door is a door record (eb.nav_doors.forZone), verb the verb it takes ("open", "use"), attempt 1 for the first try (the door's own verb) and 2 for the second (a double-click). Set it to your own table to test a door offline; nil means no door can be clicked and the walk says so.

#### Module `eb.nav_travel`

Cross-zone trips over the game's own travel network: bells, wizard spires, druid rings, the guild hall and the zones' pads, planned as hops and ridden one at a time. Never fast travel.

A trip is a list of HOPS. Inside one network (the bells, say) every zone it lists is one ride from any other, so a plan is the fewest hops from here to there; each hop walks to that zone's portal on the mesh, opens it and picks the destination, and the trip re-plans from wherever the ride really landed.

City bells cannot cross between the good and the evil cities: a ride to the other side's city does not exist, and a trip whose destination is the other side's city stops and says why. An unknown side filters nothing.

The network comes from EB's own travel data (new(deps) swaps it for your own, as the examples do). The destination pick in the travel window is the step that depends on the game's window: when it cannot be made, to() stops there and says so.

How to go to another zone: 1. Preview the trip: travel.preview(name) (or eb route \<zone>). 2. From a task, call nav.gotoZone(name) - or type eb goto \<zone>. 3. Read ok, why: a refusal names the hop that could not be taken. 4. To see the hops yourself, travel.plan(deps, from, to) answers them without moving.

**File:** `lua/eb/nav_travel.lua` in the EB folder

- `travel.new(deps) -> travel`: Use your own travel data and seams instead of EB's (a test, a tool, a private network).
- `travel.plan(d, fromShort, toShort, only) -> hops | nil, why`: The fewest hops from one zone to another.
- `travel.preview(zoneName) -> lines`: A dry run of a trip, for a status line or eb route.
- `travel.to(zoneName, opts) -> ok, why`: Make the trip: ride one hop, then plan again from wherever it landed. Only inside a task (it walks).
- `travel.ride(d, network, destDisplay, hop) -> ok, why, kind`: Ride ONE hop: walk to this zone's portal on the mesh, open it, pick the destination. Inside a task.
- `travel.graph(d) -> adjacency, skipped`: The whole travel graph, for a map or a tool.
- `travel.LABEL -> { bell_travel = "bell", wizard_spires_travel = "wizard spire", druid_rings_travel = "druid ring" }`: Plain names for the networks, for messages.
- `travel.side(d) -> side, from`: The side this character travels as: its bind city's side first, then the side its guild hall globe showed it, then the setting; an unknown side filters nothing.
- `travel.shortOf(d, display) -> short | nil`: A destination's short zone name.
- `travel\zone_connections.json -> { bell_travel = { connects_to = { { zone_name } } }, wizard_spires_travel = ..., druid_rings_travel = ..., guild_hall = ... }`: THE TRAVEL NETWORK FILE in EB's mesh store: for each network, the zones it connects. Every zone a network lists is one ride from any other zone of that network. Read once by the live deps; never written at run time.
- `travel\portal_locations.json -> { [short] = { bell_location = "x,y,z", spire_location = "x,y,z", druid_ring_location = "x,y,z", ... } }`: Where each zone's bell, wizard spire and druid ring stand: the spot a hop walks to on the mesh before it opens the portal.
- `travel\zone_names.json -> { [display name] = short name }`: Display names to short names, for typed destinations and the travel window's buttons.
- `travel\sides.json -> { zones = { [zone] = "good" | "evil" }, stops = { [menu stop] = { lands_in, side, confirmed } } }`: Which cities are on which side, and the bell menu stops that are not zones of their own (each lands in a zone). Read by eb.nav_side.

#### Module `eb.navd`

The mesh router under the walker: is this zone's mesh ready, one route, the nearest mesh point, the floor height, a straight line's clearance, lava and water under a point.

require("eb.navd") answers the platform's nav service: EB's own mesh router over EB's own mesh files, one per zone (the EBNav extension on EB for InnerSpace). eb.nav uses it for every walk; call it yourself to ask the mesh a question without moving.

A zone's mesh LOADS IN THE BACKGROUND: ready(zone) answers false, "loading" until it is in, and a zone with no mesh file says so plainly ("no .nav for \<zone> in EB's mesh store").

COST: every call here is one request to the router. A route is a whole walk's worth of work: plan it once, never every frame.

How to ask the mesh a question: 1. navd.ready(eb.zone.shortName()) - on the first ask it starts the load and answers false, "loading"; ask again on a later frame until it answers true. 2. Ask: path / pathChained for a route, nearest to snap a point onto the mesh, clear for a straight line, height / floorAt / floorsAt for floors, waterAbove and polyAt for liquid and lava. 3. Keep the answer: the mesh does not change while you stay in the zone.

**File:** `lua/eb/navd.lua` in the EB folder

- `navd.ready(zone) -> ok | false, why`: Is the mesh for this zone ready? Asking for a new zone starts its load.
- `navd.prepare(zone) -> started`: Start loading a zone's mesh ahead of time (before you zone in, or on arrival).
- `navd.loadZone(zone) -> ok, pathOrWhy`: Load a zone's mesh now, waiting for it (a tool or a test; in a script prefer prepare and ready).
- `navd.path(fx, fy, fz, tx, ty, tz) -> route | nil, why`: ONE route between two points.
- `navd.pathChained(fx, fy, fz, tx, ty, tz, closeEnough) -> route | nil, why`: The route the walker plans with: partial routes are joined end to end, still in one request.
- `navd.nearest(x, y, z, extXZ, extY) -> x, y, z, distance | nil`: Snap a point onto the mesh.
- `navd.clear(fx, fy, fz, tx, ty, tz, yTol) -> clear, t | nil`: Can the straight line between two points be walked? The mesh's own raycast. A short hop is walked without a route only when this answers true; nil is no proof and the hop is planned like any walk.
- `navd.height(x, y, z, band) -> y | nil`: The floor height at a point.
- `navd.floorAt(x, y, z, up, down) -> y | nil`: Is there a floor right under this point?
- `navd.waterAbove(x, y, z, up) -> surfaceY, lethal | nil`: Is there water (or lava) over this point?
- `navd.polyAt(x, y, z, extXZ, extY) -> flags, area, x, y, z | nil`: What kind of floor a point stands on. Pass flags and area to isLava or isWater.
- `navd.isLava(f, area, src) -> bool`: Read polyAt's answer as lava or not. eb.nav_hazard.inLava does both steps for you.
- `navd.isWater(f, area, src) -> bool`: Read polyAt's answer as water or not.
- `navd.meshWord() -> ".nav"`: The mesh's name, for a status line.
- `navd.unload()`: Drop the loaded mesh (it reloads on the next ready()).
- `navd.lib() -> true | nil, why`: Can the mesh service route at all right now?
- `navd.configure(o)`: Tell the mesh service where the zones' mesh files are. EB's start does this once; a fresh configure forgets the loaded zone. Mesh files are EB's own, one per zone, under the store's meshes folder.
- `navd.dirs() -> { folders }`: Where the mesh service looks for mesh files.
- `navd.pathFor(zone) -> file | nil`: Does EB have a mesh for this zone? (A zone without one cannot be walked by route; the walker says so.)
- `navd.loadNow(path, zone) -> ok, why`: Load one mesh file now, waiting for it. A tool's call; in a script use prepare and ready.
- `navd.source() -> "nav" | nil`: Which mesh is loaded.
- `navd.lavaBaked() -> bool`: Does the loaded mesh know where its lava is? (EB's own meshes do.)
- `navd.meshTag() -> word, source, label, line`: The words a status line shows about the mesh in use.
- `navd.notes() -> text`: The mesh's own notes, for a diagnostics window.
- `navd.stats() -> text`: Mesh statistics, for a diagnostics window. What the circles did to the LAST route planned: avoidhonoured (circles it kept off), avoidshrunk and avoiddropped (shrunk, or left out, for the route's start or goal), avoidbent (circles it went round), avoidnoway (soft circles with no way round: the ground they cover closed) and avoidrounds (the plans made again after closing it).
- `navd.histogram() -> text`: The floor kinds of the loaded mesh, for a diagnostics window.
- `navd.floorsAt(x, z, yLow, yHigh, r, max) -> { y, ... }`: All the floors stacked at one spot.
- `navd.anyFloorBetween(x, z, yLow, yHigh, solidOnly) -> bool`: Is there a floor between two heights here (is a drop really a drop)?
- `navd.swimSurfaces(x, y, z, gx, gy, gz, reach, up, max) -> { { x, y, z } }`: Where the surface of the water is between two points: the way up out of a lake toward a goal.
- `navd.pieceAt(x, y, z, reach) -> piece, x, y, z | nil`: Which piece of the mesh a point stands on. Two points on different pieces have no walking route between them until something joins them (a bridge in the corrections layer, a door, a ride).
- `navd.trisNear(x, y, z, radius, ySpan, max) -> numbers, count`: The mesh's triangles round a point, for a map window that draws the floor.
- `navd.tune(key, value) -> known`: Change one of the router's pricing settings. EB sets its own at start; leave them unless you know why.
- `navd.parsePoints(body, into) -> route`: Read route text into corners. path() does this for you; use it only to replay a route you saved as text.
- `navd.parseXYZ(body) -> { { x, y, z } }`: Read a list of points from text.
- `navd.useAvoid(mod) -> ok`: Hand the router a fuller avoid layer than its built-in one (EB's start does this when one is installed).
- `navd.avoid.addTemp(zone, x, y, z, r, h, name) -> circle | nil`: Add a circle routes stay out of, for the walk to the current goal: the hazard watch circles a spot this way, and eb.nav_places.seedAvoids pushes the blacklist.
- `navd.avoid.temps(zone) -> { circles }`: The avoid circles in force for the walk now.
- `navd.avoid.goalChanged(x, y, z) -> dropped`: Say the walk has a new goal: the circles of the last goal no longer apply.
- `navd.avoid.zoneChanged(zone)`: A new zone starts with no circles.
- `navd.avoid.reset()`: Make the next route send the circles again (after the mesh was reloaded).

#### Module `eb.platform`

One script, both EB targets: which target this is, the one clock, the frame pulse (jobs and tasks), files, settings and the log - every service a script needs, taken from one place.

EB runs the same Lua on EB for InnerSpace and on EB Boxer. A script never reaches for the target's own machinery; it asks eb.platform for a service and calls that service's methods, which are the same on both targets: local P = require("eb.platform"), then P.game(), P.pulse(), P.files() and so on.

TIME is P.now(): milliseconds that only go forward. Never use os.time in a script (it is not monotonic, and it has failed inside the game's Lua host); use P.now() for intervals and clock.wall() for a date stamp.

THE FRAME. Everything EB does runs on the game's own frame, about 100 times a second. A pulse JOB is one short call per run and must return at once; a pulse TASK is a coroutine that may wait with eb.delay(ms) without holding up the frame. Waiting anywhere else (a job, an event handler, a command handler, a window verb) raises a named error.

THE 100-FPS RULE: about 8 game reads a frame (the game layer batches them for you), no file work inside a frame (queue saves with files.writeLater), and examine-style reads (item, ability or effect details) are requests to the game's servers: read them once and keep the answer.

How to run work on EB's frame: 1. Something short and regular (watch a value, refresh a window): P.pulse().every("my.job", 250, fn). 2. Something that waits (a walk, a click then a pause, a sequence): P.pulse().spawn("my.task", fn), and inside it eb.delay(ms) or P.pulse().waitUntil(pred, timeoutMs). 3. Clean up when EB stops: P.pulse().onStop("my.helper", fn). 4. Save from game code with P.files().writeLater(path, text) - never a write inside a frame.

**File:** `lua/eb/platform/init.lua` in the EB folder

- `P.name() -> "isx" | "boxer"`: Which EB target this is. Most scripts never need to ask: the services are the same on both.
- `P.detect(env) -> "isx" | "boxer"`: Work out the target without pinning it. P.name() calls this once and keeps the answer.
- `P.use(name) -> previous`: Pin the target (tests and tools). Every service is looked up again afterwards.
- `P.get(service) -> adapter | nil, why`: Get a service by name. P.game(), P.pulse() and the other accessors are the same call.
- `P.game() -> game`: The game layer (see the game module): every game read and action goes through it.
- `P.events() -> events`: The event registry, fed by the game's own events on this target.
- `P.pulse() -> pulse`: The frame loop EB runs on: jobs that run on an interval and tasks that may wait.
- `P.clock() -> clock`: The clock service. P.now() and P.seconds() read it for you.
- `P.files() -> files`: The files host every EB module writes through, with whole-file atomic writes and a write-behind queue.
- `P.settings() -> settings`: EB's settings store: the same keys on both targets, one file per user.
- `P.log() -> log`: The log: tagged lines to the console.
- `P.ui() -> ui`: The window bridge an ebkit window registers with.
- `P.nav() -> navd`: The mesh service the walker plans on. Scripts walk with eb.nav; see the nav docs.
- `P.move() -> move`: Input and movement: face a point or an actor, stop. Scripts walk with eb.nav instead.
- `P.relay() -> relay`: The crew relay's transport on this target. Scripts use eb.relay and eb.app.crew on top of it.
- `P.root() -> folder`: Where EB is installed: the folder its data/ and lua/ live in.
- `P.now() -> ms`: THE clock. Use it for every interval, cooldown and timeout. The same clock is on the eb global as eb.now().
- `P.seconds() -> seconds`: P.now() / 1000.
- `P.installGlobal(env) -> eb`: Make the eb global scripts call. EB's start does this; it only fills what is missing.
- `P.install(target, service, adapter) -> ok, why`: Hand the platform your own service. The way to test a script offline: a clock you step, a files host over a table, a fake game.
- `P.check(target) -> report`: Check every service of a target against its contract: an empty missing list means it has every method.
- `P.reset()`: Forget the target, every loaded service and everything installed. Tests call it between cases.
- `P.pulse().every(name, ms, fn, opts) -> job`: Run fn on an interval, inside the frame. For anything that waits, spawn a task instead.
- `P.pulse().cancel(name) -> removed`: Stop a job, or end a task, by name.
- `P.pulse().spawn(name, fn, opts) -> task`: Run fn as a task: a coroutine EB resumes each frame. The place for work that waits - a walk, a sequence of clicks, a pause between casts.
- `P.pulse().running(name) -> boolean`: Is a task still running?
- `P.pulse().delay(ms) (also eb.delay(ms))`: Wait inside a task without holding up the frame.
- `P.pulse().waitUntil(pred, timeoutMs) -> true | false, "timeout" | "stopped"`: Inside a task, wait for a condition with a timeout. Every wait ends when EB stops, so a stopping EB never hangs on a task.
- `P.pulse().onStop(name, fn)`: Run your cleanup when EB stops (release what you hold, put away what you queued). Cleanups run newest first.
- `P.pulse().stop(why)`: Ask EB to stop: the frame finishes, the cleanups run, the loop ends. eb stop does the same.
- `P.pulse().status() -> text`: One line about the frame loop, for a status window or a log.
- `P.files().read(path) -> text | nil, why`: Read a whole file.
- `P.files().write(path, text) -> ok, why`: Write a whole file now, so no reader ever sees half of it (a temporary file is moved into place).
- `P.files().writeLater(path, text) -> true`: The way to save from game code: no disk work at all now. EB's flush job writes one queued file at a time, a few times a second, and EB stopping writes the rest. Saving the same file again before it is written keeps only the newest text.
- `P.files().flush(max) -> written, failed`: Write queued files. EB's flush job calls it; a script rarely needs to.
- `P.files().pending() -> count`: How many saves are still queued.
- `P.files().flushAll() -> written, failed`: Write every queued file now. EB does this when it stops; call it yourself only from a task or a cleanup.
- `P.files().mkdirs(dir) -> ok, why`: Make a folder for your helper's files. write() makes the folder of the file it writes by itself.
- `P.files().remove(path) -> ok, why`: Delete a file.
- `P.files().exists(path) -> boolean`: Is a file there?
- `P.files().list(dir, glob) -> { names } | nil, why`: The files in a folder matching a pattern.
- `P.files().copy(from, to) -> ok, why`: Copy a file (a backup: keep one per file and overwrite it, never one per edit).
- `P.log().info(tag, fmt, ...) (also debug, warn, error)`: Write one tagged line to the console: "\[info\] \<tag> \<text>". A format that does not fit its values is written as it is; logging never raises.
- `P.ui().register(win, registry) -> ok, why`: Add a window to EB's window bridge at run time; a page with the window's id can then open it.
- `P.ui().adapter(win) -> { about, state, verbs, open, close }`: The window as the bridge sees it.
- `P.ui().open(win) -> ok, text`: Show a window.
- `P.ui().emptyList() -> list`: An empty list for a window state, when the page iterates the field.
- `P.pulse().stopping() -> stopping, why`: Is EB stopping? A long task can check it between steps and end early (pulse.waitUntil already does).
- `P.pulse().otherRunning(now, freshMs) -> boolean`: The check EB's start makes so a session never runs two copies of EB.
- `P.pulse().bindEb(eb) -> ok`: Fill eb.gametime and eb.delay from this pulse when they are missing, so modules that call eb.delay wait on the right loop. EB's start does this.
- `P.pulse().setLog(fn)`: Send the pulse's own messages somewhere else (a test capturing them, a log window).
- `P.pulse().frame(now) -> tasksRun`: Run ONE frame: the due jobs, then the waiting tasks inside the frame's budget. EB's loop calls it every frame; a test drives EB offline by calling it with a clock it steps.
- `P.pulse().run(opts) -> ok, why`: EB's frame loop itself: frame after frame until EB stops, then the cleanups. EB's start runs it once; a script never calls it (a second loop would run every job twice).
- `P.pulse().cleanup()`: Run every onStop cleanup (newest first) and end every task. The loop calls it when it stops; call it yourself only in a test that drives frames by hand.
- `files.new(opts) -> fs (the module behind P.files())`: Make a second files host. P.files() is the one EB itself writes through; a fresh one is for a test, or a helper that wants its own queue.
- `files.parent(path) -> folder | nil`: The folder a path is in.
- `P.files().isDir(path) -> boolean | nil`: Is this a folder?
- `P.files().probeNative() -> boolean`: Check for EB's optional native file helper. Writes work the same without it.
- `P.ui().json() -> codec | nil`: The JSON codec for a window's own files.
- `P.ui().me() -> name | nil`: Who this window is for: the character the game layer reads.
- `win.clock() -> seconds (set by P.ui().register / adapter)`: The clock a window gets when its own spec brings none, so a window never falls back to os.time.

#### Module `eb.plroutes`

Power-level routes: a plan of STEPS (travel, hunt, instance, actions) the route runner drives a tick at a time, with breaks, goals and pull rules. Load one from the shipped catalog or write your own.

A route is a plain table (see "route"). Bind the runner to the brain-shaped adapters, load a route, start it, and call runner:step(run) once per tick; like the quest runner it answers "working", "step_done", "complete", "blocked" (with why), "need_combat", "need_loot" or "need_travel" (with a zone), and the caller does those.

THE RULES IT KEEPS. Travel and walks are mounted, on the mesh, never fast travel. Pulls are closest first. The route runs at the group's own level: a route never mentors down and never uses a chrono (the format has no such field). The runner asks the combat engine for a pull; it never drives a fight.

Each step runs while the group's level is in its band and ends at its goal (a level, a number of kills or runs, minutes, AA points) or when the group outlevels it; the next step that fits the group's level comes next.

**File:** `lua/eb/plroutes/init.lua` in the EB folder

- `plroutes.bind(deps) -> runner`: Bind the route runner to its adapters. A missing one turns the step that needs it into a clear blocked.
- `plroutes.catalog() -> cat | nil, why`: Load the shipped routes: a template to copy, and examples.
- `plroutes.resolve(cat, key) -> entry | nil, why`: Find a route in the catalog.
- `plroutes.list() -> { { id, name, code, steps, ready, note }, ... }`: The shipped routes, in short.
- `runner:load(routeTable) -> handle | nil, why`: Load a route.
- `runner:start(handle, opts) -> run`: Start a route.
- `runner:resume(handle, pointer) -> run`: Resume a route where it was.
- `runner:step(run) -> status, info`: One tick of the route: pick or advance the step, then do one bite of it (travel, hunt, actions or instance).
- `runner:pointer(run) -> { step, zone, x, y, z }`: What to keep after a step, off the game thread.
- `runner:stepTarget(run) -> { kind, zone, at, actor, ic, ready, desc }`: Where the current step wants the group.
- `runner:view(run) -> { phase, text, step, stepName, kind, zone, why }`: The run's status, cheaply.
- `route -> { schema = "eb-plroute/1", name, notes, level_of, breaks, upkeep, levelup, recovery, steps }`: A route table. level_of = whose level picks the step: "lowest" (default), "me" or "highest"; breaks = { hp = 50, power = 30, resume = 90, dead = true (wait for a rez), rez_wait, range = 60 (wait for a member further than this), zone = true (wait for a member in another zone), tell (a tell from outside the group pauses the run), tell_minutes (0 = until eb pl resume) }; upkeep = { on, bags, gear, repair, deposit } (the guild hall trip at a calm moment); recovery = { death = "carry" | "spot" | "stop", ic_tries, ic_stop, stall_min, stall_stop, trip = "stop" | "next" (a failed trip to a step's zone: stop the run, or go on with the next step) }; levelup = { export_every, trainer, potion_on, potion, hub, hub_aa, hub_bands }; steps = the STEPS, in order (at most 40).
- `route.steps[n] -> { kind = "travel" | "hunt" | "instance" | "actions", name, levels = { lo, hi }, off, ... }`: One step. travel { zone, how = "" | "bell" | "spire" | "druid", at }; hunt { zone, where = "roam" | "path" | "sweep" | "camp", at (the camp spot), radius, path, goal = { kind = "band" | "level" | "mylevel" | "kills" | "minutes" | "xphr" | "aa" | "manual", value }, pull = { mode = "single" | "pack" | "camp", aggro_by = "group" | "number", aggro_n, puller, gather, turn_hp, scan, loot, target_order = "closest" }, hunt = { names, avoid, named, heroic, epic, aggro_only }, again, again_to (go back and repeat until a level) }; instance { ic (the instance file), runs, ic_loop, ic_between = "" | "reset" | "wait", goal = { kind = "runs" } }; actions { actions = { \<action>, ... } }, each action one of go { at = {x,y,z}, zone }, click { actor, how = "doubleclick" | "hail" | "verb", verb }, pick { option | text }, transit { text = the post, tamer }, zoneout { text }, wait { secs }. Route parts are steps; the parts of an actions step are actions.

#### Module `eb.quest`

The quest-pack runner: load a quest pack, start or resume it, and advance it one step per tick - it hands travel, fights and loot back to its caller and moves on when the journal's own text says a stage is done.

A quest PACK is a data file: the quest's name, its gates and an ordered list of steps, each one command line ("HailActor Warden Fixturo,1,1", "MM 12,0,30", 'CheckQuestStep "Collect three fixture lanterns"'). The runner is a tick machine: quests.step(run) does one bounded bite of the current step and returns a status at once - it never waits. Long work (a walk, a lift ride, a wait for the journal) spans many ticks.

THE STATUSES. "working" (call again next tick); "step_done" (a step finished: keep quests.pointer(run) now); "complete" (the quest is done, or deliberately skipped); "blocked", why (it cannot go on: an unknown or refused verb, a gate it fails, a wait that ran out); "need_travel", zone (get there by the zone's own transit, then call again); "need_combat", target (pull and fight it, then call again); "need_loot" (loot, then call again). EB's brain drives a pack this way, with its own death, stuck and fight interrupts around every step.

STAGES. A pack moves on when the JOURNAL says so: a step's completed line, CheckQuestStep, WaitForQuestStep and SkipIfJournal all read the quest tracker's own objective text (open, done, or gone when the stage has moved on). The journal is never read while a zone is loading.

OPTIONAL STEPS. A step with "optional": true may fail: it gets ONE try (unless it names max_retries) and, when it cannot be done, the run goes on without it - said once in the run's log, never a failed run, a trip back or an ended route. A zone change it asks for (a bell that is not on this ring) is driven by the runner itself on the nav's own answer, so a refusal passes the step by instead of ending the line.

NO FAST TRAVEL. A pack reaches every zone the ground way: its own zone routes, then the zone's allowed transit (bells, spires, druid rings, docks, doors). FastTravel is refused inside a pack. EB never flies, in a pack or out of one: a flight-only step (FlyUp, FlyDown) stops with that reason, FlyTo walks the zone's mesh to where its chain ends, and FlyDownInto reaches its zone on the ground. A spot the mesh has no route to is a failed step, said in words.

IN AN INSTANCE. Every box reaches the hub on its own; a group member's pack waits in the hub for the tank to zone the group in, and never walks the instance's route.

THE ADAPTERS. bind(deps) ties the runner to what it reads and drives (see "deps"). A missing adapter or method turns the step that needs it into a clear "blocked", never an error.

HOW TO WRITE A QUEST PACK. 1. Write a Lua file that returns one table: schema "eb-quest/1", quest_name exactly as the journal shows it, and steps = { { type = "command", command = "\<verb> \<args>" }, ... } in order. 2. Give each step that does repeatable work (kills, clicks, gathers) its completed = "\<the journal line>" so it repeats until the journal says it is done. 3. Add the pack's own ways into its zones under zone_routes, and gates (level_required, faction_required ...) where they apply - never a fast travel. 4. Load it (quests.load), start it (quests.start), and call quests.step(run) once per tick, routing need_travel / need_combat / need_loot to your nav, combat and loot. 5. Keep quests.pointer(run) after every step_done so a stop resumes there (quests.resume).

**File:** `lua/eb/quest/init.lua` in the EB folder

- `quest.bind(deps) -> quests`: Bind the runner. Every function below is on the table this returns.
- `quests.load(path) -> handle | nil, why`: Read a pack file. It is loaded as pure data: it may only return a table.
- `quests.start(handle, opts) -> run`: Start a pack. With no pointer, a pack whose step_validation names journal lines starts at the furthest step the journal already shows, so a quest picked up halfway does not redo its first half.
- `quests.resume(handle, pointer) -> run`: Resume a pack where it was.
- `quests.step(run) -> status, info`: Advance the current step by one bite and say where it is. Call it once per tick.
- `quests.pointer(run) -> { step, zone, x, y, z }`: What to keep after each step_done so the pack can resume there. Write it off the game thread.
- `quests.stepTarget(run) -> x, y, z, zone | { actor, zone } | nil`: Where the current step wants the character, without running it - for a map, or to plan ahead.
- `quest.supported(verb) -> bool`: Can a pack say this?
- `quest.ported() -> { { verb, about, group }, ... }`: The full verb list.
- `quest.refused() -> { { verb, why, group }, ... }`: What a pack may not say, and why (grouping is the crew's job, an instance run belongs in its own file, ...).
- `<pack>.lua -> { schema = "eb-quest/1", quest_name, steps, zone_routes, fallback_travel, step_validation, ... }`: The pack file. quest_name = the quest's name as the journal shows it; steps = the ordered steps (see "steps\[n\]"); zone_routes = { \["\<zone>"\] = { { why, from = { zones } | "@guildhall", side, bind, steps = { ... } }, ... } }: this pack's own ways into a zone, tried closest first, a failed way moving on to the next; fallback_travel = steps that reach the quest's start zone; step_validation = { check_quest_steps = { { text, step } } } (where to start when the journal already shows a line). Gates: level_required, ts_level_required, faction_required = { faction, min, max }, skip_if_holding = { sibling quests }, optional, continues_later (ending with the quest still held is not a failure), repeatable. Flags: no_smart_travel (default true: no fast travel), no_flight (kept for old packs: EB never flies whatever it says), stay_mounted.
- `steps[n] -> { type = "command", command, completed, condition, skip_if_condition_false, max_retries, zone }`: One step. command = one line: a verb and its arguments; completed = the journal line that says this step's work is done (kills, clicks and gathers repeat until it is); condition = an expression read before the step starts (\${Me.Level} >= 120, \${Zone.ShortName}); skip_if_condition_false = skip the step when it reads false (a condition EB cannot read runs the step); max_retries = how often a retry may start the step over (3); zone = the zone the step belongs to. { type = "comment", description = ... } is a note the runner skips. \${...} in a command's arguments is filled from the world before the verb runs.
- `deps -> { world, nav, combat, economy, events, relay, journal, act, me, shouldStop, log }`: The adapters a run reads and drives. world.snapshot() -> { now, inGame, zone, x, y, z, level, hated, zoning, group = { count } }; nav: walkTo(x, y, z, opts), travelTo(zone, opts), stop(), progress(), position(), ensure(); combat: engage, isWinnable, clear, active, fightIsOn, setPreset; economy: lootPending(snap), lootGrab(opts) (+ merchantBuy, brokerBuy, harvest, haveItem, depotDeposit, depotWithdraw for those verbs); events: poll, answer, peek, text(sinceMs) (game text lines for the chat waits); relay: send, barrier(name), amDriver(), evac; journal: trackerRows() -> { { name, parts = { { text, progress = { current, total, complete } } } } }, questActive(name), questCompleted(name); act: the in-world seam the verbs call - hail(npc, picks, flags), reply(n), choice(n), acceptReward(n), acceptQuest(), click(spec), useItem(...), transit({ post, tamer }), zoneOut(words), actorLoc(name, range), actorFind(spec), face(x, y, z) ...; me: alignment(), bind(), deity(), tsLevel(), faction(name); shouldStop() -> true ends the run on its next tick; log(line).
- `MM x,y,z | MoveToActor <name> | FaceLoc x,z | FollowActor <name> | Mount | Dismount | StopMovement | RideLift`: Moving. MM walks the mesh to a point (x,y,z, or several joined by |); MoveToActor / FollowActor walk to an actor; FaceLoc / FaceActor turn; Mount / Dismount (LandMount is the same step: on foot); StopMovement / HoldUp stop; JumpToward jumps a gap; RideLift, UseLift and ClimbWall ride a lift or climb, a tick at a time. stay_mounted remounts before a move.
- `HailActor <npc>,<pick>,<pick>... | HailThrough <npc>[,rounds] | ReplyDialog <reply>[,<reply>...] | ChoiceWindow n | AcceptReward [n]`: Talking. HailActor hails an NPC and clicks its dialog by the picks given ("1", "3", or "1.1.1" for three clicks); HailThrough clicks the whole talk through; ReplyDialog / ReplyNow answer the open conversation, ReplyClose closes it; ChoiceWindow n answers a yes/no popup; AcceptReward \[n\] / AcceptNoChoiceReward / AcceptQuest / OK. A popup that asks the character to forsake its faith is never answered for you. REPLIES. ReplyDialog / ReplyNow take a list, answered one after another a second apart (wait=\<deciseconds> sets the gap): a number (1.1.1 is three clicks), LAST_ENTRY (the last reply) or the WORDS a reply holds, in any case ("ReplyNow Zephyl", "ReplyDialog mission"): the reply that IS the words first, else the first that holds them. Words that no reply holds block the step and list the replies - never a click on a guess. A conversation that is not up yet is waited for (2.5 s a reply). A reply window whose replies cannot be read as words is answered by number only. THE OBJECTIVE AUDIT. Before a hail the runner reads the quest's journal: a still-open WORK objective (never a go-and-see line such as "return to \<giver>") that an EARLIER step's "!journal key" of 8 letters or more owns sends the run back to that step - to its zone check first when the box stands elsewhere - instead of handing in unfinished. Twice a quest at most, then it hails anyway; said in the run's log. Never inside an authored route, for a hail run alone, or for a quest that is not in the journal.
- `ClickActor <name> | DoubleClickActor <name> | ...UntilUpdate | InteractNearby | ApplyVerb | UseItem | Examine`: Acting on the world. ClickActor / DoubleClickActor click an actor (by name, and/or at x,y,z); ClickActorUntilUpdate / DoubleClickActorUntilUpdate keep clicking until the step's completed line is done (20 s at most); InteractNearby, ApplyVerb, UseItem, UseAbility, Examine, Equip, Target, Press, ReadBook, Escort, DoorOption. Special \[Auto\] clicks the nearest special object (a glowing thing a zone wants clicked; the command is eb special) with the box standing, sees what it did and waits a zone load out; nothing in reach is tried again, then fails in words.
- `KillMobs "<mob>","",<radius>,<pulls> | KillQuestMobs ... | Pull <name> | LootAll | Leash | AvoidArea`: Fighting, handed back to the caller. KillMobs / KillQuestMobs / Pull answer need_combat with the target until the step's completed line (or the objective) is done; LootAll answers need_loot until nothing is pending. Leash and AvoidArea put fences on every pull of the run. The combat engine owns the fight: it judges what is winnable and never attacks guards.
- `CheckZone "<zone>" | TravelBell | TravelSpire | TravelDruid | Transit "<post> | <tamer>" | ZoneDoor | ZoneOut`: Changing zones, always the ground way. CheckZone runs the pack's own zone routes, then hands the zone back as need_travel; TravelBell / TravelSpire / TravelDruid / NavigateToZone name the zone's transit; Transit rides an in-zone transport to a post; ZoneDoor uses a door; ZoneOut leaves by the zone's exit; WaitForZone / WaitForZoning wait out a load; CallGH recalls to the guild hall; Evac. SmartTravelTo and TravelTo reach their zone on the ground. FastTravelFirst "\<zone>",\<place>,\<n>: with n = 0 (or none) a ground trip to the place; with n above 0 it is done at once, because the n steps written below it are the pack's own way in the world - never a jump on the map. FastTravel is refused in a pack; FlyUp / FlyDown stop (EB never flies); FlyTo walks the mesh to where its chain ends and FlyDownInto reaches its zone on the ground.
- `CheckQuestStep "<line>" | WaitForQuestStep "<quest>","<line>",<secs> | SkipIfJournal "<line>",N | QuestComplete`: Reading the journal.
