CheckQuestStep is a gate: the line must be in the quest's journal (open or done); WaitForQuestStep waits (working, never blocking) until the line shows or moves on, blocked at its time limit (or goes on with -continue); WaitForJournalStep waits for a step to complete and never fails; SkipIfJournal skips the next N steps when the line is done; SkipIf / SkipIfQuestActive / SkipIfHaveItems / SkipIfActorWithin and the other SkipIf forms skip on other facts; RepeatUntilJournal / RepeatUntilQuest go back N steps until the journal moves; CheckCompletedQuest skips a quest that is already done; QuestComplete checks the quest left the journal (the hand-in worked); MakeCurrentQuest sets which quest the journal checks read.
- `Wait <secs> | WaitFor <condition>,<secs> | WaitForActorSpawn | WaitForActorDeath | EventWaitForChat "<text>"`: Waiting, a tick at a time: Wait, WaitFor (a condition), WaitForCombat, WaitForActorNear, WaitForActorSpawn, WaitForActorDeath, EventWaitForChat / EventWaitForEmote (a line of game text), EventWaitForZoneChange, CheckActorExists. No wait is longer than an hour, whatever a pack says.
- `MerchantBuy | BrokerBuyItem | CraftItem | ScribeRecipe | HarvestQuestItem | OpenMail | TakeTurn | EndTurn`: The rest, by group: economy (MerchantBuy, BuyFromMerchant, BrokerBuyItem, CraftItem, ScribeRecipe, DumpAllToDepots, RemoveFromDepot, StartResearch, OpenMail, GetMailAttachment), gather (HarvestQuestItem, GatherMultipleUntilComplete), and the crew (TakeTurn / EndTurn: one box at a time at a world event). quest.ported() lists every verb; quest.refused() lists the ones EB refuses with the reason. QueueMissionIC \<table>\[,mark\]\[,run\]\[,wait=\<seconds>\] puts the instance run of the mission an NPC just gave in the instance queue: with mark, before the hail, it notes which missions of the table (the \_missions folder of the task folder, \<table>.lua: the NPC's missions and the run of each) the journal already holds; without it, after the hail, it waits (20 s) for ONE mission that was not held, takes the offer if one is still up, and queues its run (eb iqueue add); run starts the queue. No mission in time, two at once, a mission with no run in EB or a refusing queue: the step fails and says why. Linguist \<language> (Halasian, Oggish, Ratongan, Stout or Ykeshan) learns a language the in-world way: it sends eb linguist \<language> once - this character's Linguist, the primer bought (never over its budget) and used - and waits while the trip goes (30 minutes at most, then it stops the trip). It passes with the words of the trip, and fails, saying why, when the trip is refused (a language no Linguist sells, no Linguist to reach, a trip already going) or ends without the language. A quest that is stopped, cancelled or skipped past while its trip goes stops the trip.

#### Module `eb.registry`

The one table of eb commands: run a line as if it was typed, send it to the crew with all / others / to, answer a declared command with your own handler, and read the help and tab-completion.

Every eb command is declared ONCE, in EB's command schema (data/eb/commands.json). The console's tab-completion, the button windows, the help window, the crew relay and the brain all read this one registry, so a line a script runs with reg:dispatch behaves exactly like the same line typed in the console.

A COMMAND ROW (what reg:command and reg:view return) is a plain table: { id = "\<domain>.\<verb>", domain, verb, aliases = { words }, desc, args = { { name, type, required, default, values, help } }, scopes = { "local", "all", "others", "to" }, module, ship }. A command answers only the scopes its row lists.

A HANDLER is function(args, ctx, parsed) -> ok, text. args holds the typed arguments by name, already read as their types (whole numbers, numbers, on/off and choices in their canonical spelling). It must return at once: start long work as a task or a goal and answer "issued". ok may be true, "issued" (accepted, the work goes on) or false.

A CREW LINE: "eb all \<cmd>", "eb others \<cmd>" and "eb to \<who> \<cmd>" are handed to ctx.relay. The line that travels carries no scope word, so it runs where it lands and is never relayed again. who may be a box id (is2), a character, a class, an archetype (priest) or @archetype, or several of them joined by commas.

**File:** `lua/eb/registry/init.lua` in the EB folder

- `registry.default(opts) -> reg | nil, why`: The registry every part of EB shares. In a running EB the commands are already attached; a fresh copy (fresh = true) has none, which is what a test or a tool wants.
- `registry.new() -> reg`: A registry of your own: load a schema document into it with reg:load (tools and tests).
- `registry.decode(text) -> doc | nil, why`: Read a command schema from JSON text.
- `registry.readFile(path, fs) -> doc | nil, why`: Read a command schema from a file.
- `reg:load(doc, opts) -> ok, why`: Merge a schema document into the registry.
- `reg:command(word) -> row | nil`: Find a command by any of its names.
- `reg:attach(id, fn, opts) -> ok, why`: Answer a declared command with your handler. One owner per command: a second attach is refused unless it says replace = true.
- `reg:detach(id)`: Remove the handler of a command (it answers "not wired yet" afterwards).
- `reg:handler(id) -> fn | nil`: The handler a command has now - to wrap it: take the old one, attach yours with replace = true, call the old one from yours.
- `reg:view(filter) -> { rows }`: The commands of a domain or a module: the allow-list a window's buttons are built from.
- `reg:unattached(filter) -> { ids }`: What is declared but not wired on this box.
- `reg:dispatch(line, ctx) -> ok, text, parsed`: Run a line through the registry: parse it, hand a crew scope to the relay, and run the handler here when this box is meant (all: here too; others: never here; to: here only when the list names this box).
- `reg:complete(line, opts) -> candidates, newLine`: Tab-completion over the schema: scope words and verbs first, then a command's choices or on/off.
- `reg:help(topic, opts) -> { lines }`: The text of eb help.
- `reg:usage(word) -> text | nil`: A command's usage line.
- `reg:customerSchema() -> doc`: The whole command list as a plain table: for a help page, a button grid or a check.
- `reg:customerJson(encode) -> text`: The command list as JSON text.

#### Module `eb.relay`

Send scoped lines between boxes (all, others, to \<who>), hear every box's short state, and run what the crew sends this box exactly once.

Each box makes one relay and joins it; nothing is sent or heard before join(). R.send(line) reads the line's one leading scope word: "all" reaches every box (this one acts at once, never twice), "others" every box but this one, "to \<who>" the boxes the list names, and a line with no scope word runs only here. A line a box receives runs through onLocal and is never relayed again, so a crew line can never loop round the crew.

Every line carries a message id ("\<box>#\<n>"); a box acts on an id once however many times the line arrives. Boxes find each other by what they hear: every EB broadcasts its short state every two seconds (box id, character, zone, mode, health, power, a fight on), and R.boxes() is the roster built from it.

In a running EB the app's relay is eb.app.relay and its crew plane eb.app.crew; a helper normally sends through eb.dispatch("eb all ...") or events.crew(). Make your own relay when you build a tool or a test.

**File:** `lua/eb/relay/init.lua` in the EB folder

- `relay.new(opts) -> R`: Make this box's relay. The transport carries the lines between boxes: EB's own on each target, or an offline bus (eb.relay.events.bus) for tests.
- `R.join() -> ok`: Opt in: start sending and hearing crew lines and states.
- `R.leave()`: Leave the crew relay group this box joined: on EB for InnerSpace the transport leaves the relay group join() joined; a transport with no group of its own is unchanged. EB calls it when it stops.
- `R.send(line, sopts) -> decision`: Send one scoped line. The line may carry ONE scope word: a second one ("to is2 all pause") is refused.
- `R.onLocal(fn)`: Set the handler for lines this box should run. EB points it at its registry; a tool or a test records them.
- `R.onState(fn)`: Hear the other boxes' states as they arrive (R.boxes() keeps the latest of each).
- `R.note(fn)`: Where the relay reports what it refused or could not do.
- `R.broadcastState(fields) -> ok`: Tell every box this box's short state. EB's crew plane does this every two seconds; there is no reply - a box learns what a command did from the next state it hears.
- `R.boxes() -> { { box, state, heardAt } }`: The crew roster as this box hears it.

#### Module `eb.relay.group`

The group verbs a script uses to coordinate a crew: send to targets, wait for everyone at a mark, read the group, and know who drives an instance (the tank).

One object per box, made over its relay and the world snapshot. Every verb is non-blocking: barrier() answers "waiting", "ready" or "timeout" each time it is called, so a goal or a task calls it each tick and never hangs. In an instance the TANK alone runs the route and zones the group in; the group never walks the route on its own - amDriver() and handoffToTank() are that rule. A running EB keeps its group as eb.app.group.

**File:** `lua/eb/relay/group.lua` in the EB folder

- `group.new(deps) -> G`: Make the group verbs for this box.
- `G.send(targets, command) -> ok, why`: Send a command to the crew.
- `G.groupState() -> { count, members, leader }`: The group as this box sees it. A member in another zone has no zone (nil), never a guessed one.
- `G.role() -> "tank" | "healer" | "member"`: My role in the group (deps.role overrides it).
- `G.amDriver() -> boolean`: Am I the driver?
- `G.barrier(name, opts) -> "waiting" | "ready" | "timeout"`: A group barrier. The first call puts this box's mark on the wire; call it every tick until it is not "waiting". On "timeout" the caller decides (go on, or call the late member) - never a silent hang.
- `G.resetBarrier(name)`: Re-arm a barrier for the next objective (after a zone, a new pull).
- `G.recordMark(box, name)`: Record a member's mark. EB's crew plane calls it when a mark arrives; a test calls it by hand.
- `G.handoffToTank(payload) -> "ok" | "declined"`: Hand the drive to the tank.
- `G.catchup(who) -> "working" | "done"`: Tell stuck members to walk the route back to the group (the first answer to a member who fell behind).
- `G.evac(opts) -> "working" | "failed"`: Evacuate the group: the class with an evacuation spell casts it, in class priority, and a totem when none can.
- `group.roleOf(class) -> "tank" | "healer" | "member"`: The role of a class, without a group.

#### Module `eb.transit`

A zone's own pad networks - griffon and sokokar stations, flight paths, teleporter pads: plan the pad hops to a station and ride them, each hop walked to on the mesh.

Each pad has a place, a network, how it is opened (hail its tamer and answer the reply, or click the object) and the stations it flies to. A trip walks to the nearest pad on the mesh, opens it, picks the next station and re-plans from each landing. Cross-zone pad flights also join eb.nav_travel's network as hops.

The pad data is EB's own, per zone. new(deps) swaps in your own reads and a rider (eb.transit_ride) for tests and tools.

How to ride a zone's pads: 1. See what is here: transit.padsForZone() (or eb transit pads). 2. Preview the trip: transit.preview(station). 3. From a task, transit.to(station) walks to the first pad on the mesh, opens it, picks the station, lands and re-plans. 4. Read ok, why.

**File:** `lua/eb/transit.lua` in the EB folder

- `transit.padsForZone(short) -> pads`: The pads of a zone.
- `transit.plan(short, x, y, z, destName) -> plan | nil, why`: The pad hops from where you stand to a station.
- `transit.preview(destName, opts) -> lines`: A dry run of a pad trip.
- `transit.inZone(destName, opts) -> ok, why`: Ride the pad network to a station in this zone, re-planning from each landing. transit.to is the same call. Only inside a task (it walks).
- `transit.to(destName, opts) -> ok, why`: The same as inZone: ride the pad network to a station.
- `transit.cmd(c, opts) -> lines | ok, why`: The command form (eb transit).
- `transit.new(deps) -> transit`: Use your own reads and rider.
- `transit.contributeEdges(adj) -> added`: Add the pad flights that cross a zone line to a travel graph. eb.nav_travel calls it for you.
- `transit.resetGraph()`: Forget the pad graph built from the transit data, so the next plan builds it again (after new pad data).
- `travel\transit\<zone>.json -> { version, zone, name, pads = { { name, loc = { x, y, z }, network, method = "hail" | "click", actor, reply, dest = { { to, land = { x, y, z }, cost, zone } } } } }`: ONE ZONE'S PADS in EB's mesh store. A pad is a station (several pads can share a zone); network names its kind (griffon, sokokar, teleporter, flight path ...); method says how it opens - hail its tamer (actor) and answer the reply, or click the object; dest lists the stations it flies to, with where it lands and how long the ride takes when known. A destination in another zone is a cross-zone flight. An empty dest means not surveyed - never a dead end.

#### Module `eb.ui.monitor.combatlog`

Read one combat line into a combat record: who hit, healed or warded whom, with what, for how much.

The one place that knows the text of a combat line. "YOU" and "YOUR" become your own name, so you are one name everywhere. A line that is not combat gives nil. It reads direct hits ("\<who> \<verb> \<target> for N points of \<type> damage"), damage over time ("\<target> suffers N points of \<type> damage from \<who>'s \<ability>"), heals ("for N hit points", with the overheal in brackets), wards ("wards \<target> against N points of damage"), misses ("tries to hit \<target>, but \<how>": miss, parry, dodge, riposte, block, deflect) and deaths. It also reads the lines as the game's own chat log writes them (through eb.ui.anal.reallines): hits "for \[a critical of \]N \<type> damage", "tries to crush YOU, but misses" and the other misses, wards that "absorb N points of damage from being done to \<target>", heals "for a critical of N hit points" and "\<killer> has killed \<victim> in \<zone>". A hit whose line names nobody ("YOU are hit by \<effect> ...") gives nil: the meters credit damage by name.

**File:** `lua/eb/ui/monitor/combatlog.lua` in the EB folder

- `combatlog.parse(line, opts) -> rec | nil`: Read one line. Never raises.
- `combatlog.parseAll(text, opts) -> { records }`: Read a whole block of lines.
- `combatlog.parseStamped(text, opts) -> { records }`: Read lines that carry their own time stamp - the way to replay a saved fight exactly.
- `rec = { t, kind, src, dst, ability, amount, dtype, crit, avoid, over }`: The combat record format: t is the time in ms; kind is "hit", "heal", "ward", "miss" or "death"; src is who did it and dst who it landed on; ability is the spell or art (nil for a plain melee swing); amount is the damage or healing (0 for a miss or a death); dtype the damage type; crit true for a critical; avoid how a miss was avoided; over the overheal.

#### Module `eb.ui.monitor.parser`

A combat meter for scripts: feed it combat records and read damage, healing and damage taken per fight, per character and per ability, with fights split by a quiet gap.

The parser moves only when you hand it a record (parser:ingest); it never reads the game. A fight starts with the first hit, heal or ward and ends after 7 seconds without one (or when you call breakEncounter, which EB does on a zone change); the last 25 fights are kept so two runs can be compared.

FRIEND OR FOE: the parser has no faction read. Your own name and every name you hand it (setFriends, addFriend) are friends; a name with a space or a leading "a", "an" or "the" is a mob; a single word is taken for a player. Whoever heals or wards someone becomes a friend, and so does the one healed. Outgoing damage is a friend hitting a foe; incoming (damage taken) is a foe hitting a friend.

How to meter a fight from a script: 1. local parser = Parser.new{ me = "\<your character>", friends = { the crew's names } }. 2. Turn each combat line into a record with eb.ui.monitor.combatlog.parse and hand it to parser:ingest - or let eb.ui.monitor.parse_feed.attach do both from eb.events. 3. Read parser:current() for the fight going on, parser:snapshot() for it and the recent fights, parser:export() for a flat record to save or compare.

**File:** `lua/eb/ui/monitor/parser.lua` in the EB folder

- `Parser.new(opts) -> parser`: Make a parser.
- `parser:setFriends(list)`: Add names that are friends, whatever the name guess would say.
- `parser:addFriend(name)`: Add one friend.
- `parser:isFoe(name) -> boolean`: The friend-or-foe guess the parser uses.
- `parser:ingest(rec) -> fightId | nil`: Count one record. A record after a quiet gap longer than idleMs ends the old fight and starts a new one.
- `parser:breakEncounter()`: End the fight going on now (the next record starts a new one). EB calls it on a zone change.
- `parser:reset()`: Forget every fight.
- `parser:viewEncounter(enc, opts) -> view | nil`: One fight as a meter shows it: who did how much, the focused character's abilities, and who took how much. Rates are per second over the fight's length (at least one second).
- `parser:current(opts) -> view | nil`: The live fight.
- `parser:snapshot(opts) -> { v, me, idleMs, current, encounters, fights }`: Everything a meters window shows.
- `parser:export(which) -> record | nil`: A flat record of one fight, to save or to compare with another run.

#### Module `eb.world`

The ONE world snapshot: a plain table of you, your state and your group, built once per frame from the game layer and shared by the brain and every window.

Build it once over the game layer (eb.world.new({ game = require("eb.platform").game() })), then call snapshot() wherever you need the world. Every caller in the same frame gets the SAME table, so ten readers cost one read. A window builds its state from the snapshot, never with game reads of its own.

THE SNAPSHOT: { now, inGame, name, class, archetype ("fighter" | "priest" | "mage" | "scout"), level, zone, hpPct, powerPct, dead, hated (a fight is on you), moving, x, y, z, bagsFreeSlots, group = { count, members = { { name, zone, dead, distance, subclass, role } } }, reads, partial }. When inGame is false (character select, a zone loading) nothing else in it is to be trusted. A group member in another zone has no zone (nil), never a guess.

**File:** `lua/eb/world/init.lua` in the EB folder

- `world.new(deps) -> world`: Make the world snapshot over a game layer. A running EB has one already: eb.app.world.
- `world.snapshot(readBudget) -> snap`: The world right now, built at most once per frame.
- `world.beginTick()`: Start a new frame: the game layer's per-frame reads and this snapshot are both dropped, so the next snapshot() reads fresh. EB's pulse does it every frame; call it yourself only outside EB's pulse (a test).
- `world.invalidate()`: Drop the cached snapshot only, so the next snapshot() rebuilds it from the game layer's reads.
- `world.archetypeOf(subclass) -> "fighter" | "priest" | "mage" | "scout" | nil`: A class's archetype, the same table the crew relay uses.

#### Module `eb.zone`

The zone you are in, by the short name EB's mesh, travel network and saved spots are keyed by.

**File:** `lua/eb/zone.lua` in the EB folder

- `zone.shortName() -> short | nil`: The short name of the zone you stand in.
- `zone.inWorld() -> bool`: Are you in a zone at all?

#### Module `ebkit.jsontable`

Plain tables to JSON and back: the codec for a helper's own files, crew messages and window states. It never raises on bad input.

encode writes any plain table. Object keys come out SORTED, so the same table always writes the same text (a window's state is compared as text to decide whether anything changed). A table whose keys are exactly 1..n is an array; an empty table is written {} - give an empty LIST a metatable with \_\_tojson = function() return "\[\]" end to write \[\] instead. NaN and infinities are written as null. decode turns null into jsontable.null, so a key with no value is kept; jsontable.val(v) reads that marker as nil.

**File:** `lua/ebkit/jsontable.lua` in the EB folder

- `jsontable.encode(v) -> text | nil, why`: Write a value as JSON.
- `jsontable.decode(s, opts) -> value | nil, why`: Read JSON text. The result is the same table whether or not a tick is given.
- `jsontable.val(v) -> v | nil`: Read a decoded value with null as nil.
- `jsontable.null`: The marker decode puts where the text says null (so the key stays), and that encode writes as null.

#### Module `ebkit.lua_fmt`

Write a table as a Lua data file ("return { ... }"): stable, readable, and read back by load() with no environment. The format EB's quest and instance files use.

The same table and options always write the same text, so two saves of unchanged data are identical and a changed one diffs cleanly. Keys are bare where Lua allows (name =) and \["quoted"\] where not; nil is never written; numbers are minimal (150, 286.6 - never 150.0); a short list of plain values stays on one line.

**File:** `lua/ebkit/lua_fmt.lua` in the EB folder

- `lua_fmt.document(value, opts) -> text`: The whole text of a Lua data file. Read it back with load(text, name, "t", {}).
- `lua_fmt.encode(value, opts) -> text`: One value as a Lua literal.
- `lua_fmt.num(v) -> text`: The text a number is written as.
- `lua_fmt.ident(k) -> boolean`: Is a key a plain Lua name?

#### Module `ebkit.push_budget`

Keep windows from costing frames: cap how often each window's state goes out, and spread a big game scan over several frames with a read budget.

A window's class sets its pace: hud 100 ms (an always-on gauge), bar 250 ms, panel 200 ms, request 50 ms (it changes only on a press). A change that comes sooner than its class allows is HELD and the newest one goes out when the window is due - never a queue of old ones. A shared bucket (24 a second, bursts of 5) keeps a whole pass of windows from going out at once.

The READ BUDGET is for code that reads the game in a loop: count the reads, stop at about 8, and carry on next frame instead of costing the game its frame rate.

**File:** `lua/ebkit/push_budget.lua` in the EB folder

- `push_budget.gate(win, opts) -> g`: Put a window behind the push budget.
- `g.stats() -> { id, class, ms, polls, emits, held, overBudget, lastEmitAt }`: One window's counters: proof a window keeps its pace.
- `push_budget.report() -> { global, windows }`: The whole picture, for a perf line or a test.
- `push_budget.reset()`: Forget every gate and refill the shared bucket (tests).
- `push_budget.readBudget(max) -> rb`: A per-frame read counter for a loop that reads the game: stop when rb:ok() is false and resume next frame.
- `push_budget.CLASSES -> { hud = { ms = 100 }, bar = { ms = 250 }, panel = { ms = 200 }, request = { ms = 50 } }`: The pace of each window class.
- `push_budget.defaultClock() -> fn`: The clock a push budget uses when you give it none. In a window pass opts.clock (EB's own clock) instead.

#### Module `ebkit.window`

An EB window's Lua side: the WHOLE state it shows, built from your data, and the verbs a click may run - with no window host in it, so the same window runs on both targets and in a test.

A window is two things. Its STATE: build(win) returns a plain, JSON-able table of everything the page shows; state() returns the SAME table until something changes, so a quiet window costs nothing (the bridge only sends a new table). Call win:touch() when something it shows changed. Its VERBS: the allow-list of what a click may do; a page can run nothing else. A verb answers at once (ok and plain words), changes data and never the page's own view (which tab, which row); the window rebuilds right after it.

Build from the world snapshot (eb.world) or your own data - never with game reads of your own. Register the window with require("eb.platform").ui().register(win); gate its pushes with ebkit.push_budget.

**File:** `lua/ebkit/window.lua` in the EB folder

- `window.new(spec) -> win`: Make a window.
- `win:state() -> state`: What the page shows. Builds only after touch(), a verb, or a new live() signature.
- `win:touch()`: Something the window shows changed: the next state() builds a new table.
- `win:verb(name, args) -> ok, text`: Run one verb, then rebuild the window.
- `win:verbNames() -> { names }`: The window's allow-list.
- `win:opened()`: The first page of this window opened: runs spec.open and rebuilds. The bridge calls it.
- `win:closed()`: The last page closed: runs spec.close and forgets the built state (a closed window costs nothing).
- `window.int(v, lo, hi) -> integer | nil`: A number a page sent, made safe. Check every argument a verb takes.
- `window.str(v, max) -> string | nil`: A string a page sent, made safe.
- `window.args(a) -> table`: A verb's arguments as a table, always.

#### Module `game`

The game layer: your character, your target, actors near you, abilities, effects, items and the game's windows - read in batches and acted on. Get it with local game = require("eb.platform").game().

Every game read and action a script needs goes through this one object; it is the same on both EB targets. Reads are batched and kept for the rest of the frame: Me() answers name, level, health, power, zone, target and state from ONE read, and asking again in the same frame costs nothing. An action (target, cast, use) forgets what it changes, so the next read is fresh. EB's frame pulse starts a new frame with BeginTick(); a read is also refreshed on its own after 100 ms.

It only sends the game members EB has verified to work. A member that is not verified yet is never sent: the field it would fill keeps an honest default (nil where 0 would mislead), and an action that needs it answers false. Where a function below is held back that way, its notes say so.

Waits (WaitTarget, WaitCasting, Wait, LoadAbilities) only work inside an EB task; everything else answers at once and may be called from a handler or a frame job. Keep to about 8 game reads a frame: the reads here are batched so that a whole combat frame stays inside that.

**File:** `lua/eb/platform/isx/game/eq2.lua` in the EB folder

- `game.Me() -> me`: Your character, from one batched read per frame.
- `game.InGame() -> inWorld`: Are you in the world right now? Comes from the same read as Me(): no extra cost.
- `game.Target() -> actor | nil`: Your current target as a plain table, from the same read as Me().
- `game.ActorTarget(actorId) -> actor | nil`: What another actor is targeting - the mob behind a friendly, or the member a mob is on.
- `game.ActorPos(actorId) -> pos | nil`: Where an actor stands, its facing and its distance from you.
- `game.ActorDead(actorId) -> dead`: Is this actor dead or gone? The check a kill step or a heal waits on.
- `game.ActorHeading(actorId) -> degrees | nil`: The direction an actor faces, for "stand behind it" and "stand in front of it" checks.
- `game.ActorGuild(actorId) -> title`: An NPC's title. Held back: EB has not verified the title member yet, so this answers "" for now.
- `game.Face(x, z) -> true`: Turn to face a point on the ground.
- `game.FaceActor(actorId) -> sent`: Turn to face an actor (toward its own X and Z).
- `game.Key(action, key) -> true`: Press, hold or release a key. A held key stays down until you release it: always release what you hold, and prefer EB's movement library for walking.
- `game.TargetActor(actorId) -> sent`: Target an actor. It may not take (out of range, an object that cannot be targeted): confirm with WaitTarget, or use ClickActor for doors and other objects.
- `game.ClickActor(actorId) -> sent`: Double-click an actor the way a player does: open a door, pull a lever, hail an NPC, open a chest.
- `game.OpenLoot(actorId) -> sent`: Double-click a corpse or chest to open its loot window (ClickActor without its zone-picker bookkeeping).
- `game.WaitTarget(id, sec) -> took`: Wait until your target is the given actor. Only inside an EB task.
- `game.WaitCasting(sec) -> casting`: Wait until you are casting - the confirmation after a cast was sent. Only inside an EB task.
- `game.Wait(sec, cond) -> met`: Wait without freezing the game. Inside an EB task the frame keeps running; never call it from an event handler or a frame job.
- `game.ControlCount(actorId) -> n`: The control-cure check: is this actor feared, stunned, mezzed or rooted?
- `game.Group() -> rows`: Your group, in one batched read per frame. You are not in the list: Me() is you.
- `game.Raid(myGroupNames, refreshSec) -> rows`: The rest of the raid. Kept between refreshes, so asking every frame is cheap.
- `game.MyPet() -> pet | nil`: Your own pet. Held back: EB has not verified the pet member yet, so this answers nil for now; when you know your pet's id, PetSnapshot(id) reads it.
- `game.MyPetTargetId() -> id`: Your pet's target. Held back with MyPet (answers 0 for now).
- `game.PetSnapshot(petId, ownerName) -> pet | nil`: Read any pet by its id.
- `game.CountEngagedHostiles(radius) -> aggro, inCombat`: How many mobs are fighting you.
- `game.EngagedNamed(radius, ours) -> mob | nil`: Is a named in this fight?
- `game.EngagedMobs(radius, ours) -> mobs`: Every mob in combat with your side.
- `game.MobCasts(radius) -> casts`: Who is casting - what an interrupt helper needs. Reach and line of sight are read only for the casters.
- `game.GroupHostileNear(radius, ours) -> mob | nil`: Is anything attacking my group?
- `game.LooseHostile(radius, ours, myId) -> mob | nil`: A mob that got loose on a member - the tank's "taunt it back" check.
- `game.Lootables(reach) -> list`: Corpses and chests in reach. Open one with OpenLoot(id).
- `game.Clickables(range, max) -> list`: Doors, instance exits and other clickable objects near you - never people, pets, NPCs, corpses or you.
- `game.NearestActor(query_, range, contains) -> row | nil`: The nearest actor that matches, from one game query.
- `game.ActorsNear(query_, range, contains) -> rows`: Every actor that matches, nearest first.
- `game.EncounterMembers(id) -> set`: The mobs that came with this one. Held back: the encounter query is not verified yet, so for now the set holds only the mob itself.
- `game.SameEncounter(a, b) -> same`: Are two mobs one encounter?
- `game.LoadAbilities(timeoutSec, stallSec, batchSize, o) -> loaded`: Read your knowledge book once. Each ability's details come from the server, so the load asks a few at a time and waits between rounds. Call it once at start-up, inside an EB task; afterwards FindAbility answers with no read. One load runs at a time: a call made while one runs waits for it (its step is told that load's progress) and starts no second one, so the asks never double.
- `game.BookProgress() -> progress`: How far the book load is - what the ability export's bar shows. No read: the load keeps it as it goes.
- `game.BookCounts() -> loaded, total`: How much of the book the last load read.
- `game.BookIncomplete() -> incomplete`: Did the last book load miss anything?
- `game.FindAbility(nameOrLine) -> ability | nil`: Look an ability up in the loaded book. A line answers the rank the book keeps for it; a name the book has not loaded is looked up once in the game (detailsMissing = true). While detailsMissing is true its facts are not read yet: on EB Boxer each one (castTime, range, allowRaid ...) is nil until the game has described the ability.
- `game.AllAbilities() -> list`: The whole book, one entry per line.
- `game.AbilityLines() -> names`: The ability lines in the book.
- `game.AbilityReady(exactName) -> ready`: Can I use this ability now? Every name asked about lately is read in one batch at the first ask of a frame; the rest of the frame answers from it.
- `game.AbilityReadyNow(exactName) -> ready`: The same question as AbilityReady, always read - for the check right after a cast.
- `game.AbilityTimeUntilReady(name) -> seconds`: How long until an ability can be used again.
- `game.AbilityQueued(exactName) -> queued`: Is this ability queued? Held back: the queued member is not verified yet, so this answers false for now.
- `game.ReadyStats() -> reads, shared`: How many readiness asks the batch saved this frame.
- `game.NoteRecast(nameOrLine) -> seconds`: Measure an ability's recast right after it landed (EB does this a moment after every cast).
- `game.LearnedRecast(nameOrLine) -> seconds | nil`: The recast EB has measured for an ability.
- `game.CastIdFor(exactName) -> id | nil`: When two book entries share one name, EB casts the real spell by its id; this says which.
- `game.castMethod = "onplayer" | "direct"`: How Cast(name, { name = who }) reaches a player: "onplayer" (default) casts on them by name without touching your target; "direct" targets them, waits for the target, casts, and RestoreTarget() puts your target back.
- `game.Cast(exactName, target) -> sent`: Use an ability.
- `game.RestoreTarget()`: After a "direct" cast on a friend, put your target back on what it was.
- `game.CancelCast()`: Stop your current cast.
- `game.CastingName() -> name`: What you are casting right now (no extra read: it comes with Me()).
- `game.TargetCasting() -> name, id`: What your target is casting - the interrupt check.
- `game.Maintained() -> list`: The spells you keep up. A duration of -1 means no timer (a stance or a toggle).
- `game.CancelMaintained(name, targetId) -> sent`: Drop one of your maintained spells. Held back: the cancel is not verified yet, so this answers false for now.
- `game.MyDetrimentIcons() -> icons`: Which detriments are on you, by icon - read off the same effect rows the buff checks read (no read of its own). The fight scanner keeps the icon new on you when a detriment lands.
- `game.CancelEffect(main, back) -> ok, why`: Cancel a detriment on you, found by its icons; a beneficial effect with the same icon is never touched (eb canceldet). Held back until its live proof: until then it answers false and says so.
- `game.MobCons(rows) -> rows`: The con of each mob, for a window that colours them: one read for the ones not known yet (15 at most); a con is kept for that mob from then on, and the fight's own rows carry it. Call it from a window's refresh, never every frame.
- `game.HasEffect(name) -> up`: Is this buff on me? Each effect's name is asked of the server once and kept; your maintained spells answer too.
- `game.MyEffectNames() -> list`: The buffs on you, by name (names are learned a few per frame).
- `game.MobEffects(id) -> list`: The effects on another actor (for a dispel). Held back: an actor's effect list is not verified yet, so this answers an empty list for now.
- `game.AllowsRaid(name) -> allowed | nil`: Can this buff go on the rest of the raid?
- `game.Concentration() -> { used, max, guessed }`: Your concentration. While the game's own members are not verified, used is summed from your maintained spells and max is guessed.
- `game.ChoiceWindow() -> popup | nil`: Read the game's yes / no popup: a rez offer, an invite, a zone-in question.
- `game.DoChoice(n) -> sent`: Press a button on the yes / no popup. Held back: the click is not verified yet, so for now this sends nothing and answers false - never assume the popup was answered.
- `game.RewardWindow() -> reward | nil`: Read the quest or kill reward window: a quest OFFER, a pick-one reward, or a granted reward.
- `game.AcceptReward(pick) -> ok, why`: Take a reward. A quest offer is refused here (it is not a reward). Held back: the accept is not verified yet, so for now this answers false with the reason.
- `game.ReplyDialog() -> dialog | nil`: Read an NPC conversation and its reply options.
- `game.ReplyChoose(n, d)`: Pick a reply.
- `game.LootWindow() -> loot | nil`: The open loot window. It reads nothing while no loot window is believed up: the game's loot event (or NoteLoot) says when one opens; a quiet frame costs nothing and one idle check runs every 30 seconds.
- `game.NoteLoot()`: Tell the loot watch a loot window just opened (call it from a LootOpened handler), so LootWindow() reads it.
- `game.HOState() -> state`: The heroic opportunity window: whether it is up, the wheel's name, and which icons are still open.
- `game.Zoning() -> zoning`: Is a zone loading? Act on a new zone only once this is false.
- `game.IsForeground() -> foreground`: Is this client the window in front?
- `game.TravelMapOpen() -> open`: Is the travel map a bell, a spire or a ring opens on screen?
- `game.TravelMapPlaces() -> names`: The destinations on the open travel map. With no travel map up it answers an empty table, never an error.
- `game.TravelMapPick(i)`: Select a destination on the travel map.
- `game.TravelMapGo()`: Press the travel map's go button for the selected destination.
- `game.TravelFollowUp(pick, landing) -> what | nil`: After going, answer the zone-version picker the trip raised (only once its rows are new), or the arrival-spot map of a zone with several. On a group trip EB hands in the group's own choice, so every box of the group lands in the same copy of the zone. Only EB for InnerSpace reads the arrival-spot map; on EB Boxer landing is not asked.
- `game.GroupZoneNames() -> rows | nil, why`: Which copy of a zone each group member stands in, as the game's group window names it. Held until it is proven live (read in the gate's evidence mode).
- `game.CloseTravelMap()`: Close the travel map when it is open.
- `game.PersistentZones() -> list`: Your instance timers. Held back: the zone-timer read is not verified yet, so this answers an empty list for now.
- `game.ResetZoneTimer(zoneName) -> sent`: Reset one instance timer. Held back: not verified yet, so this answers false for now.
- `game.OpenZoneWindow()`: Open the game's zone reuse window.
- `game.ZoneReuseSeconds(zone) -> seconds | nil, why`: How long until a zone can be entered again - an instance loop on one zone waits this out inside the copy. It opens the game's zone reuse window for a moment (shut again unless it was open already), reads its Persistent Instances and Lockout pages, and keeps the answer five minutes, counting down meanwhile. Never early: the window rounds its times, so the wait is the latest the reset can be. Held back: the read is not verified yet, so for now this answers nil and why.
- `game.RepairAll()`: Repair everything you wear. Double-click a mender first (ClickActor) so its window is open.
- `game.CloseMerchantWindow() -> closed`: Close the merchant (or mender) window.
- `game.ConsumableSlot(slot) -> slot | nil`: What is in your food or drink slot.
- `game.ToggleAutoConsume(slot) -> sent`: Flip auto-consume on a food or drink slot. Turning it on eats one at once when its effect is not on you.
- `game.EquipFromBags(name) -> sent`: Equip an item from your bags.
- `game.UnequipSlot(slot) -> sent`: Take off what a slot holds. Held back: not verified yet, so this answers false for now.
- `game.GearCondition() -> pct | nil`: A quick repair check. Kept for 30 seconds (item details are a server request).
- `game.WorstCondition() -> pct | nil`: The full repair check. Item details are asked for a few items at a time and the answer is kept for 30 seconds.
- `game.HasItem(name) -> has`: Do I have this item, worn or in the bags?
- `game.HasItemExact(name) -> has`: Is this exact item in my bags? Worn gear is never seen here.
- `game.ItemReady(name) -> ready`: Can I use this item now?
- `game.UseItem(name) -> sent`: Use (click) an item.
- `game.UsableItems() -> list`: Every usable item you wear or carry, bags and containers left out. Kept for 10 seconds; names are read once per item.
- `game.Skill(id) -> cur, max | nil`: A tradeskill skill, from the Persona window - nil (unknown), never a made-up 0.
- `game.SkillText(id) -> text | nil`: The same skill as text.
- `game.SkillAbsent(id) -> false | nil`: Is the skill missing? This target can only say "it is there" (false) or "cannot tell" (nil).
- `game.TSLevel() -> level | nil`: Your tradeskill level.
- `game.Say(channel, text) -> sent`: Speak in group or raid chat.
- `game.Tell(name, text) -> sent`: Send a tell.
- `game.OnChat(fn)`: Get every chat line the moment the game raises it. That runs inside the game's own event: the function may only record or queue - never wait, never act. eb.events' ChatLine is usually the better choice: its handlers run in EB's frame.
- `game.GetVar(expr, default) -> value`: Read one member the layer does not already return. Only members EB has verified go out: any other is refused (default answered, nothing sent) and noted once - see GateSkipped().
- `game.Execute(cmd) -> ok, result`: Send one console line. It is sent as you wrote it, so use only commands and methods EB knows to work - and never put chat text or a name into it unchecked.
- `game.GateSkipped() -> list`: What this session wanted to read but EB held back.
- `game.GameDataReads() -> n`: Your read budget so far this frame - keep it to about 8.
- `game.ReadStats() -> stats`: The layer's read and command counters.
- `game.BeginTick()`: Start a new frame: every kept read is forgotten. EB's pulse calls it every frame; call it yourself only in a stand-alone script or a test.
- `game.now() -> ms`: The clock the game layer reads by (the same as eb.now()).
- `game.IsExtensionReady() -> ready`: Can the game be read at all? A stand-alone script waits for this first.
- `game.SessionName() -> name`: Which session this script runs in - the crew relay's box id.
- `game.PlaceReady() -> ok, why`: May a house item be picked up or put down by the cursor right now? The whole sequence waits for its live proof (eb proof evidence lets it out for the proof run); until then nothing is sent and the words say so.
- `game.PickUpItem(actorId, opts) -> ok, words`: Pick a house item up onto the cursor: first person, the view looking straight down, the cursor at the screen centre, then the item's Move verb (a double-click only targets it). Parking the view first keeps the item's height: it rides that far over whatever the cursor points at. Call it from a task (it waits).
- `game.PlaceItemAt(spot, item, opts) -> ok, words`: Put the item on your cursor straight down where you stand: the heading faced, first person looking down, the drop at the screen centre (EQ2:PlaceMoveableObject, then a left click), the cursor nudged 8 px right, left, up and down when the game refuses; the view is put back either way. From the floor beside a block the drop lands on its edge and is refused or slides off: stand on the block. With a height: the height an item rides over what the cursor points at is fixed when it is picked up, so a point of the view whose ray hits (where it rests) minus the height is looked for, the item goes down at the centre once and is picked up again from that point, then goes down for good; no such point in view is said and the item stays on the cursor. The height's own read (EQ2.ObjectBeingMoved.HeightOffset) waits for its live proof like the rest. Call it from a task (it waits).
- `game.PlaceView(opts) -> ok, words`: Put the camera back after a pick-up or put-down: first person, recentred (once that has its own proof), zoomed back out.

#### Module `settings`

EB's settings store: get a value with a default, change it for this session, save it once. Get it with require("eb.platform").settings().

The store is a small file (eb-settings.json) beside the EB install folder, read once and written only on save(), never in a frame. Values are plain: a string, a number or a boolean - never a JSON text inside a value. Before EB knows its folder (offline, or before the start) get() answers your default, set() keeps the value in this session and save() says why it could not write.

How to keep a helper's option between sessions: 1. Read it at start: local on = P.settings().get("myhelper.enabled", true). 2. Change it when the user flips it: P.settings().set("myhelper.enabled", false). 3. Save once - from a task or an onStop cleanup: P.settings().save().

**File:** `lua/eb/platform/isx/settings.lua` in the EB folder

- `settings.get(key, default) -> value`: Read a setting.
- `settings.set(key, value) -> true`: Change a setting for this session. save() keeps it for the next one.
- `settings.save() -> ok, why`: Write the settings file. Call it once - on stop, or from a task after a change - never every frame.
- `settings.dirty() -> boolean`: Are there unsaved changes?
- `eb-settings.json = { ["<key>"] = <string | number | boolean>, ... }`: The settings file: one flat JSON object of key and value, in the EB install folder. Keys EB itself reads: "ui.miniOnLogin" (boolean, default true: open the mini window when the character enters the world) and "caststack.server.\<character>" (string: the server folder to take that character's cast stack from). A helper keeps its own keys under its own prefix ("myhelper.enabled").

### Lua library: Advanced modules

#### Module `clock`

EB's one clock, as a service: milliseconds that only go forward, the same in seconds, a date stamp, and a stand-in for tests. Get it with require("eb.platform").clock().

**File:** `lua/eb/platform/isx/services/clock_isx.lua` in the EB folder

- `clock.now() -> ms`: The time now. Use it for intervals, cooldowns and timeouts.
- `clock.seconds() -> seconds`: The same clock in seconds.
- `clock.wall() -> unixSeconds | nil`: A date stamp. For intervals use now(): the wall clock can be set back.
- `clock.use(fn)`: Drive EB's clock yourself - the way an offline test makes time pass exactly.

#### Module `eb.app`

EB's composition root: what came up at start, and the one dispatch every typed, relayed and pressed line goes through. A running EB is eb.app; eb.dispatch(line) runs a line.

**File:** `lua/eb/app/init.lua` in the EB folder

- `app.start(S, opts) -> app`: Start EB. The boot calls this once; a script uses the app it returned (eb.app).
- `app.dispatch(line, ctx) -> ok, text (also eb.dispatch(line))`: Run a line through EB's registry, from a script, a window or the crew: the same path a typed line takes.
- `app.status() -> { lines }`: What eb status prints for this box.
- `app.meState() -> { name, subclass, zone, mode, hp, pw, combat }`: This box's one-line state: its character, zone, mode (idle, paused, ic-lead, ic-follow) and health.
- `app.crewLines(app) -> text`: The crew as this box hears it: what eb status crew prints.

#### Module `eb.app.crew`

The crew plane of a running EB: the boxes this one hears, the lead's orders to its followers, and how a line typed on one box reaches the rest exactly once.

**File:** `lua/eb/app/crew.lua` in the EB folder

- `crew.new(o) -> crew`: Make the crew plane over a relay.
- `crew.tick(t) -> sent`: The pulse job that tells the crew who and where this box is.
- `crew.peers() -> { { box, name, zone, mode, hp, pw, combat, ageMs } }`: The crew right now.
- `crew.order(who, word, args) -> ok, why`: Send an order to followers.
- `crew.onOrder(word, fn)`: Answer an order. An order nobody answers is counted and dropped.
- `crew.isMe(who) -> boolean`: Does a to-list name this box?
- `crew.nameOf(box) -> name | nil`: Which character a box plays.
- `crew.boxOf(name) -> box | nil`: Which box plays a character.
- `crew.status([t, counted]) -> text`: One line about the crew, for eb status crew.
- `crew.box() -> boxId`: Which box this is.
- `crew.wrapRegistry(reg) -> reg`: Make the registry's crew lines safe for the crew plane: a line this box sends to all is run here at once, and the copy the relay brings back is not run a second time. EB's start does this.
- `reg.relay(scope, who, line, parsed) -> ok, why (after wrapRegistry)`: The registry's crew sender once wrapRegistry wrapped it.
- `relay.send(line, sopts) -> result (while the crew plane runs a crew line)`: The relay's send, guarded by the crew plane: a line that arrived from the crew runs here, and anything it would send back out is held, so nothing echoes round the crew.
- `crew.inviteOrder(app) -> { names }`: The invite order you set in Settings > Group (kept in data\ebsettings\invite.json under EB's folder), read when eb invite is pressed. Those characters are invited first, then the rest of the crew.

#### Module `eb.app.windows`

EB Main and the per-character mini: how a running EB registers its own windows, and the control table their buttons press through.

**File:** `lua/eb/app/windows.lua` in the EB folder

- `windows.start(o) -> W`: Register and open EB's own windows. EB's start calls it.
- `windows.control(o) -> control`: The control table EB Main's and the mini's buttons press through (eb.control in a running EB).
- `eb.control.summary() -> { running, paused, preset, open }`: What EB Main's header shows.
- `eb.control.toggles() -> { eb, pause, follow, move, camp, dps, cmbt, buffs, pet, loot }`: The mini window's switch states.
- `eb.control.act(verb, args) -> ok, text`: A press on EB Main or the mini, turned into an eb command line through the one registry.

#### Module `eb.brain.goals`

The goals the brain can pursue: grind a camp, vendor, travel, run a quest line, harvest, craft and follow - each a small phase machine advanced one bite per tick.

**File:** `lua/eb/brain/goals.lua` in the EB folder

- `goals.new(spec) -> goal`: Build a goal. Each kind starts in its own first phase and sets a combat preset (grind, questline and harvest: openworld; vendor, travel and craft: afk; follow: instance).
- `goal:describe() -> text`: A goal and where it is, in one word.
- `goals.KINDS = { [kind] = { advance, start, preset } }`: The goal kinds. grind params: { camp = { x, y, z, radius }, maxKills (nil = forever), preset }. A goal of your own needs only name, ctx = { phase }, advance(self, b, snap) and describe(self).

#### Module `eb.brain.interrupts`

The seven things that take over from the goal, highest first: death, a zone reset, a fight, being stuck, a member down, full bags, and low health or power.

**File:** `lua/eb/brain/interrupts.lua` in the EB folder

- `interrupts.new(cfg) -> { interrupts }`: Build the interrupt set (brain.new does).

#### Module `eb.caststack.classfacts`

What kind of spell each heal, ward, cure, rez and power line of a class is - the facts a heal row needs to run - from EB's own data, one table per class.

**File:** `lua/eb/caststack/classfacts.lua` in the EB folder

- `classfacts.forClass(subclass) -> facts | nil, why`: A class's facts.
- `classfacts.classes() -> names`: The classes with facts.
- `classfacts.build(data) -> facts | nil, why`: Build facts from a table of your own (a class EB does not cover yet, a test).

#### Module `eb.caststack.jsonstack_facts`

Class facts from a class module: record what a class module defines, index it by ability line, and read a fact with its template.

**File:** `lua/eb/caststack/jsonstack_facts.lua` in the EB folder

- `facts.record(loader, opts) -> facts | nil, why`: Run a class module and keep what it defined.
- `M.<Heals|Dps|Cures|Buffs>.DefineAbility(def, disabled) -> def`: What a class module calls to define one entry (on a recording manager: written down, nothing cast).
- `M.<Heals|Dps|Cures|Buffs>.Enable(name, overrides) -> ok`: What a class module calls to switch an entry on, with its priority.
- `M.<Heals|Dps|Cures|Buffs>.Disable(name)`: What a class module calls to switch an entry off.
- `M.Dps.SetStealthOpeners(openers, freeLines)`: What a class module calls to name its stealth openers.
- `H.New(Mx, prefix, o)`: While record runs with opts.H, the class helper's New is wrapped so the module's prefix and options are read from its own call (and put back afterwards).
- `facts.lineKey(name) -> key | nil`: The ability-line key.
- `facts.effective(facts, f) -> fields | nil`: A fact as one table, template included.
- `facts.group(facts, f) -> group`: Which kind of entry a fact belongs to.
- `facts.index(facts) -> facts`: Index facts by kind and ability line (record does it; call it again after you change facts by hand).

#### Module `eb.caststack.jsonstack_kinds`

The per-kind entry builders jsonstack.build runs - one for damage, upkeep, heals, the cure family, buffs and items.

**File:** `lua/eb/caststack/jsonstack_kinds.lua` in the EB folder

- `kinds.dps(ctx, row, t) -> entry`: Build a damage entry.
- `kinds.upkeep(ctx, row, t) -> entry`: Build an upkeep entry.
- `kinds.heal(ctx, row, t) -> entry`: Build a heal entry (heals are weighted, not ordered).
- `kinds.cure(ctx, row, t) -> entry`: Build a rez, cure or power-heal entry.
- `kinds.buff(ctx, row, t) -> entry`: Build a buff entry.
- `kinds.item(ctx, row, t) -> entry`: Build an item entry.

#### Module `eb.caststack.loader`

Find the character's cast stack by its name, build it, and keep EB's combat casting from it - reloading when the profile file changes.

**File:** `lua/eb/caststack/loader.lua` in the EB folder

- `loader.find(o) -> result | nil, why`: The character's stack by EB's rule, without loading it into combat.
- `loader.new(o) -> ld`: One loader per character: a stable holder that loads, reloads and keeps switches across reloads.
- `ld.load() -> ok, text`: The first load.
- `ld.reload() -> ok, text`: Read the profile again; every switched row keeps its state.
- `ld.refresh() -> ok, text`: Reload only when the profile file changed (one file stat, never a read just to compare).
- `ld.describe() -> text`: One status line.
- `loader.attach(ld, combat) -> ok`: Make EB's combat cast from this loader's stack (the same holder, rebound - never replaced).
- `loader.pinKey(name) -> key | nil`: The setting to set when a character has profiles on two servers.
- `loader.install(S, opts) -> ld`: EB for InnerSpace's one call at start: load this character's stack, hand it to eb.app.combat, and reload it when the file changes (one stat every 30 s). Says one counts-only line.
- `loader.pinnedServer(settings, name) -> server | nil`: Which server's profile a character with profiles on two servers uses.
- `loader.lfsStat() -> stat | nil`: The change-stamp reader install() uses for reload-on-change.
- `ld.onChange(l)`: Called after every load and reload once loader.attach has joined the loader to EB's combat plane: it copies the loader's status line onto the plane (combat.line, combat.why). Set your own on a loader of yours to hear reloads.
- `combat.reload() -> ok, text`: After loader.attach, the combat plane's reload goes through the loader - the same rule, the same holder, every switched row kept.

#### Module `eb.combat.combat_pos`

Line of sight and positioning inside the engine: hold a cast through a wall, judge behind / front / flank, and say where to stand.

**File:** `lua/eb/combat/combat_pos.lua` in the EB folder

- `engine:planPosition(ctx) -> intent | nil`: Where to stand for this step's mob.
- `engine:relativeAngle(ctx, mob) -> "behind" | "front" | "flank" | nil`: Behind, in front or at the flank?
- `engine:positionalFail(pos, mob) -> nil | gate`: The positional gate of an entry.
- `engine:losFail(mob) -> bool`: Is the mob out of sight? (passesGate's "LoS", while the gate is on)

#### Module `eb.combat.combat_util`

The engine's small pure helpers - tags, kill time, valid mobs, AE entries, decisions - shared with scripts as combat.U.

**File:** `lua/eb/combat/combat_util.lua` in the EB folder

- `U.splitTags(list) -> tags`: A tag list as a table.
- `U.killEta(hpStart, hpNow, spentMs) -> ms | nil`: The kill time two health readings imply (combat.killEta is the same).
- `U.validMob(mob) -> bool`: Is this something to fight at all? (guards are checked separately)
- `U.isAE(entry) -> bool`: Is this an area entry (the guard veto and disableAE apply)?
- `U.mobCount(ctx, mob) -> n`: How many mobs the encounter has.
- `U.decision(kind, entry, target, reason) -> decision`: Make a decision record.
- `U.lowestOf(members) -> member, healthPct`: The member who needs a heal most.
- `U.anyWord(text, words) -> bool`: A part-of-the-name match over a word list (the guard check uses it).
- `U.lineKey(name) -> key`: The key that matches an ability's ranks.
- `U.fn(tbl, name) -> function | nil`: Does this table offer that function?
- `U.call(tbl, name, ...) -> results | nil`: Call an optional function safely - how the engine asks for reads the game may not offer.

#### Module `eb.combat.heals`

The heal, rez, cure, power, upkeep, buff and damage categories of the engine - methods on an engine object.

**File:** `lua/eb/combat/heals.lua` in the EB folder

- `engine:healChoice(ctx, entry) -> choice | nil`: How much a heal entry wants to cast, and on whom.

- `engine:selectHeal(ctx) -> decision | nil`: The heal category.
- `engine:selectUpkeep(ctx) -> decision | nil`: The upkeep category: wards and heals kept up, combat upkeep.

- `engine:selectRez(ctx) -> decision | nil`: The rez category (ahead of a top-off when the group is healthy).

- `engine:selectPower(ctx) -> decision | nil`: The power-heal category.
- `engine:selectBuff(ctx) -> decision | nil`: The buff category: an enabled, ready buff whose effect is not on you yet.

The heroic-opportunity part of the engine: open one, advance the wheel, keep the rotation from disturbing it.

#### Module `eb.compat`

Keep output and arithmetic the same on every EB target: one number formatter (3, never 3.0), a forgiving string.format, stable key order, and the 32-bit bit operations.

- `compat.format(fmt, ...) -> text`: A forgiving string.format.
- `compat.isint(x) -> boolean`: Is it a whole number?
- `compat.toint(x) -> integer | nil`: Truncate to an integer.
- `compat.sortedkeys(t) -> { keys }`: A table's keys in one stable order: use it wherever output order matters.
- `compat.maxn(t) -> n`: table.maxn.
- `compat.load(src, name, env) -> fn | nil, why`: Load Lua text. Pass {} as env to load a data file that may not reach any global.
- `compat.bit -> { band, bor, bxor, bnot, lshift, rshift, arshift, rol, ror, bswap, tobit, tohex }`: The 32-bit bit operations with signed 32-bit results, the same on every target: compat.bit.band(x, y), compat.bit.tohex(x, n) ...
- `compat.frexp(x) -> m, e`: math.frexp on both runtimes (Lua 5.4 has no math.frexp).
- `compat.getfenv(f) -> env | nil`: A function's environment, on both runtimes. Prefer passing what a function needs as an argument.
- `compat.setfenv(f, env) -> f`: Give ONE function its own environment, on both runtimes (only a function value, never a stack level). Prefer load(text, name, "t", env) for code you load yourself.

#### Module `eb.console`

The console window's model: typed lines scoped to the crew, a searchable history and output, per-box rows and tab-completion, with a state the window draws from.

**File:** `lua/eb/console/init.lua` in the EB folder

- `console.new(opts) -> C`: Make a console. With a relay it also shows the lines the crew sends here and the other boxes' states.
- `C.run(line) -> ok, text`: The Enter key: remember the line, then run it here or send it to the crew.
- `C.register(name, fn, help, ropts)`: Add a word the console answers itself (help, boxes, clear and search are built in). EB commands are not added here: they come from the registry through dispatch.
- `C.complete(partial) -> { candidates, replace }`: Completion for the console line: scope words and console words first, box ids and archetypes after "to".
- `C.historyList() -> { lines }`: The input history.
- `C.search(needle) -> { rows }`: Search the output.
- `C.since(afterSeq, max) -> { rows }`: The output rows after a row number: what a window has not drawn yet.
- `C.tail(max) -> { rows }`: The end of the output, for a window opening fresh.
- `C.clear()`: Empty the output (the history of typed lines is kept).
- `C.setScope(sc)`: Set the input's default scope (the window's scope picker).
- `C.boxes() -> { { id, self, state, heardAt } }`: The boxes the console knows.
- `C.state() -> state`: What the console window draws from.
- `C.newest() -> seq`: How far the output has got: a window keeps the last number it drew and asks since() for the rest.
- `C.vocabRev() -> rev`: Has the console's own word list changed? A window rebuilds its word list only when this moves.
- `C.vocabData() -> { { verb, help, order } }`: The console's own words (help, boxes, clear, search and any you registered).
- `C.setSelfState(st)`: Set this box's own row in the console's box list (the other boxes' rows come from the relay).

#### Module `eb.coord.combat_gate`

The claim check for combat decisions: which casts need a claim (a rez, a cure, a group cure, a dispel) and the one call that runs the claim before the cast.

**File:** `lua/eb/coord/combat_gate.lua` in the EB folder

- `gate.needsClaim(dec, engine) -> key | nil`: Does this cast need a claim, and which one? A rez is claimed per member and a cure per member. A GROUP cure (a row whose gates.type says GROUP, or a # of two or more) is "groupcure" on the group's token; a cure that is merely AIMED at the group is a single-target cure, claimed per member. A raid-wide row claims in the raid scope.
- `gate.setGroupHealClaims(on)`: Also claim group heals.
- `gate.decide(arb, dec, now) -> "skip" | "go" | "wait" | "standdown", key`: The one call before a cast: needsClaim plus request.
- `gate.acted(arb, key, now)`: After the cast went out: tell the crew.
- `gate.done(arb, key, landed, now)`: Report the outcome of a claimed cast.
- `gate.attach(engine, arb, opts) -> detach`: Make an engine claim before every cast that needs it, without changing the engine: its cast is wrapped. A decision that must stand down casts nothing this tick (the engine decides again next tick).
- `gate.setHold(engine, fn) -> true`: A coordination hold on the engine's casts (a "stop" rule: no hostile cast for a while): a cast the hold names is not sent, and the decision says why. A cast a person asked for is never held.
- `gate.onSent(engine, fn) -> ok`: Hear every cast the engine sends: the coordination's own cast facts and the cast stack's trigger tags hang on this. fn is told only of a cast that went out - first return value true.
- `engine:cast(dec) -> sent (after gate.attach)`: The engine's cast once attach wrapped it: a coordination hold first, then the claim, the cast on "go", and the crew told. false when the claim said wait or standdown: dec.sendWhy is "wait for the arbitration (...)" while the bids are collected (the step ends there) or "arbitration:\<answer>" for a stand-down (the engine goes on to its next category).

#### Module `eb.coord.cowire`

The two coordination messages on the wire: a tag (EB_Tag) and a claim (EB_Claim), and the tie-break every box computes the same way.

**File:** `lua/eb/coord/cowire.lua` in the EB folder

- `cowire.encodeTag(e) -> { fields }`: A tag message as relay arguments.
- `cowire.decodeTag(args) -> e`: Read a tag message.
- `cowire.encodeClaim(e) -> { fields }`: A claim message as relay arguments.
- `cowire.decodeClaim(args) -> e`: Read a claim message.
- `cowire.crewToken(names) -> token | nil`: The token a group-wide line carries, so a box of another group on the same uplink drops it.
- `cowire.claimKey(action, target, scope) -> key`: The one key a claim is about.
- `cowire.outranks(a, b) -> boolean`: The tie-break. It uses only what every bid carries, so every box picks the same winner.
- `cowire.winner(bids) -> bid | nil`: Pick the winner of a list of bids.
- `cowire.TAG = "EB_Tag"; cowire.CLAIM = "EB_Claim"`: The relay event names the two messages travel under.

#### Module `eb.coord.relaylink`

Carry coordination tags and claims over the crew relay, so the rules engine and the arbiter never touch the wire themselves.

**File:** `lua/eb/coord/relaylink.lua` in the EB folder

- `relaylink.new(opts) -> link`: Make a link. The engine and arbiter given this link register their own handlers.
- `link.onTag(fn, o) -> off`: Listen for inbound tags. A link has any number of listeners (the rules engine is one).
- `link.onClaim(fn, o) -> off`: Listen for inbound claims (the arbiter is one listener).
- `link.join() -> ok`: Start listening: attach both message kinds and join the relay group. Nothing is heard before join.
- `link.fireTag(tag, scope, phase, data, within) -> ok, mid`: Send one tag message to the crew.
- `link.sendClaim(e) -> ok, mid`: Send one claim message to the crew.

#### Module `eb.coord.tagimport`

Turn an imported cast stack's ability tags and embargo tags into coordination rules you can read.

**File:** `lua/eb/coord/tagimport.lua` in the EB folder

- `tagimport.rulesForRow(row, idx) -> { rules }, { notes }`: The rules for one row.
- `tagimport.importRows(rows) -> { rules, notes, count = { atag, etag } }`: Import a whole cast stack's tags.
- `tagimport.ruleKey(r) -> key, kind, who, tag, ability, target | nil`: What a tag rule IS, whoever brought it in: two rules with one key are one rule, so an import never makes the same rule twice (one buff on two members is two rules; one hold bound twice to an ability is one).
- `tagimport.idFor(r) -> id | nil`: The id an imported tag rule carries.
- `tagimport.forCharacter(rows, who) -> result`: This character's cast-stack tag rows as rules that name the character. This is what eb rules import and the Tags & Helpers window's import run.
- `tagimport.importInto(coord, rows) -> result`: Import straight into a running engine.

#### Module `eb.economy.drive`

The window actions the economy works through (the drive): the full list, a check of a drive against it, and honest stubs for the actions a drive does not have yet.

**File:** `lua/eb/economy/drive.lua` in the EB folder

- `drive.SPEC -> { "bags.slots", "bags.items", ... } drive.INFO[name] -> { kind, args, null, about } drive.GROUPS`: The action list, by group: bags (slots, items, examine, use, move, destroy, transmute, salvage, extract); equip (worn, equip, unequip); adorn (on, apply, remove, move); merchant (near, open, isOpen, offers, selectRow, selectedLabel, currency, sell, buy, repair, close); choice (purchasePrompt, answer); broker (near, open, isOpen, anywhere, search, searchType - every listing of one Item Type, read page by page, buy, examine - a listing on its own results page, turned to and back, mine, setPrice, list, unlist, add, takeCoin, close); depot (near, open, isOpen, which, contents, deposit, withdraw, close); craft (stationNear, recipes, open, isOpen, fuelNeeded, begin, state, arts, useArt, stop, close); loot (corpseNear, openCorpse, window, take, takeAll, assign, leave, confirm, close); trade (near, open, add, addCoin, accept, state, close, give); harvest (nodeNear, click); packpony (summon, hail, answer); bank (near, open, isOpen, which, contents, deposit, withdraw, coin, depositCoin, withdrawCoin, close); mail (near, open, isOpen, inbox, read, take, compose, attach, attachCoin, send, close); collection (journal, add); writ (giverNear, request, active, turnIn); commission (pending, accept, decline). drive.signature(name) shows each one's arguments.
- `item | offer | listing | lootwin | bankrow | letter | actor`: The tables actions pass. item = { id, name, qty, tier, level, rarity, type, slot, noTrade, heirloom, attuned, lore, container, value (copper a merchant pays), stats = { stat = number }, classes, adorns }; actor = { id, name, x, y, z, zone, kind }; offer (a merchant row) = { name, price = { amount, currency, coin }, priceCopper, stock }; listing (a broker row) = { id, name, priceCopper, seller, qty, slot, stats }; lootwin = { mode = "ffa" | "lotto" | "nbg" | "leader" | "free", assignable, items = { item + { who, prompt } } }; bankrow = item + { which = "personal" | "shared" | "guild", page, slot }; letter = { id, from, subject, coin, read, attachments = { { name, qty } } }.
- `drive.kind(name) -> "read" | "action" | nil`: Is this action a read or an action?
- `drive.args(name) -> { names } | nil`: The arguments an action takes.
- `drive.signature(name) -> text | nil`: An action's call line.
- `drive.validate(impl) -> ok, missing`: Does this drive have every action?
- `drive.null(note, meta) -> drive`: A drive that does nothing, honestly.
- `drive.withFallback(impl, note) -> drive`: Fill a partial drive's gaps with stubs (economy.new does this for you).
- `drive.report(impl) -> { rows, total, present, proven, missing }`: Which actions a drive has, which are proven, and what the rest still need.

- `ex:find(name) -> entry | nil, all`: Look an ability up by name, rank-insensitive.
- `ex:has(name) -> bool`: Does the character have this ability?
- `ex:labels(entryOrName) -> labels`: What an ability does and asks for.
- `ex:iter() -> iterator`: Walk the book.
- `ex:castStackCandidates() -> { entries }`: The cast-stack shortlist.
- `ex:summary() -> { total, ability, aa, ascension, byKind }`: A quick count of the book.
- `export -> { schema, meta, abilities = { entry, ... } }`: The ability export's shape. meta = { subClass, archetype, topLevel, counts = { abilities, aas, ascension }, exportedAt, gaps (what a live snapshot could not read) }. Each entry: { id, tierId, name (the line's name, no rank), line (its key), rank (the held rank's full name), level (the level the line is learned at), topLevel (the held rank's level), tier, kind ("spell" | "ca" | "gen" | "pass" | "asc"), group ("ability" | "aa" | "ascension"), book, beneficial, targetType, passive, ascension, enhance, tradeskill, labels = { positional = "front" | "behind" | "flank" | "frontflank" | "mixed", facing, threat, dehate, cure, cureTypes, ward, buff, stealth, aggro, bow, combat, heal, dps, debuff }, cast = { castTime, recast, recovery, powerCost, concentration, range, maxRange, minRange, maxDuration, radius }, dmg (the damage school), flags, usage = { type, target, derived }, effects = { up to 10 effect lines, big numbers masked } }.

#### Module `eb.ic.ic_base`

The instance runner's shared pieces: every timing and distance it uses (LIMITS), its stoppable waits, and its small helpers.

**File:** `lua/eb/ic/ic_base.lua` in the EB folder

- `base.LIMITS -> { name = number }`: Every timing (ms) and distance (m) the runner uses, for example pollMs 1000, hubRoundMs 120000 (one wait for the group in the hub), groupRounds 3, doorReach 4, exitSearch 80, exitReach 4, exitShort 3, exitWaitMs 90000, leaveTries 3, tseCapMs 600000, repairBelow 90, maintCapMs 1200000, reusePollMs 5000, longWaitSecs 600.
- `base.limits(over) -> limits`: The limits a runner uses (ic.new does this with env.limits).
- `base.waitFor(runner, ctx, pred, capMs, stepMs) -> true | false, "stopped" | "timeout"`: Wait until pred() holds, checking the stop flag on every poll. Pass the runner first.
- `base.settle(runner, ctx, fn, capMs) -> ok, why`: Run one interface call to its end, whichever way it answers. Pass the runner first.
- `base.holdWhilePaused(runner, ctx) -> stillGoing`: Hold while the brain is paused: nobody moves until it is resumed. Pass the runner first.
- `base.zoneIs(z, short, display) -> bool`: Does a zone name name this zone?
- `base.short(secs) -> text`: A countdown as a short text.
- `base.say(runner, fmt, ...) -> nil`: Write one runner log line, prefixed "\[ic\] ", through the runner's env.log. Pass the runner first. Use it in a custom action so your line sits with the runner's own.
- `base.flat(ax, az, bx, bz) -> metres`: A flat distance.
- `base.every(left) -> seconds`: The cadence of a long wait's progress line.

#### Module `eb.ic.ic_hold`

The combat-hold rule as pure functions: what holds an instance's combat wait and what lets it go.

**File:** `lua/eb/ic/ic_hold.lua` in the EB folder

- `ic_hold.HOLD -> { decide, holds, nearestInCombat, newState, next, observe, NEAR_M = 50, STUCK_MS = 5000 }`: The rule's table. NEAR_M is how near a straggler must be (metres); STUCK_MS how long a bare combat flag must last before it counts as stuck.
- `HOLD.decide(inCombat, anyHated, nearby, flagOnlyMs) -> { hold, straggler }`: One decision. A fight or a straggler holds the wait; a clear or a stuck flag lets it go.
- `HOLD.holds(hold) -> bool`: Does this decision hold the wait?
- `HOLD.nearestInCombat(nearby) -> npc | nil`: The straggler candidate.
- `HOLD.newState() -> state`: Start a new combat wait.
- `HOLD.newFlag() -> flag`: Start a watch over the "in combat, nobody hated, no NPC fighting near" condition.
- `HOLD.observe(f, now, flagOnly) -> ms`: One look for the watch. A look that comes long after the last one starts the count over (nobody was watching).
- `HOLD.hated(st) -> nil`: Tell the state the group was seen in a real fight between looks: the bare-flag watch starts over and the stuck line may be said again.
- `HOLD.stuckLine(flagOnlyMs) -> text`: The stuck-flag message.
- `HOLD.next(st, now, inCombat, anyHated, nearby) -> look`: One look in a series: it times the bare flag itself and says each one-time effect once.

#### Module `eb.loops.overseer`

The overseer loop: one whole Overseer pass - turn the finished missions in, add the mission scrolls, start missions with the agents the game's own rules pick, answer the reward windows - and buy scrolls only when you allow it.

**File:** `lua/eb/loops/overseer.lua` in the EB folder

- `overseer.estimateSuccess(mission, agents) -> percent`: How well a set of agents fits a mission, by the older amount model (a mission with trait AMOUNTS). The pass itself no longer plans with it: the game's missions name trait SETS, and the pass holds to the game's own %.
- `overseer.planAssignments(missions, agents, opts) -> assignments, leftover`: The older amount-model plan (kept for its callers): idle agents only, each used once, the hardest missions to staff first, the best agents for each by the estimate; a mission under minSuccess is skipped. The pass plans with eb.overseer.plan instead (the game's rules: liked traits first, fillers only on their options).
- `overseer.advance(goal, b, snap) -> "working" | "done" | "blocked", why`: One tick of the overseer goal (goal:advance calls it with the goal first): one bite of the pass, at most a few driver calls. The stop flag is checked first; a window EB opened is shut on the way out.

The shipped files sit in EB's mesh store; this PC's own corrections sit beside the EB install and win at the same spot. - `nav_follow.describe(st) -> text`: The follow in words.

- `nav_follow.SNAP_Y -> 8.0`: ... and this many up or down.
