#### Module `eb.nav_hazard`

The walker's safety rules as calls you can make: is a point lava, where is the shore of a pool, which zones' liquid kills - and the hazard watch every walk runs.

**File:** `lua/eb/nav_hazard.lua` in the EB folder

- `hazard.inLava(x, y, z, lavaIsFloor, nd) -> bool`: Is this point lava?
- `hazard.shoreNear(x, y, z, reach, nd, fromX, fromZ) -> x, y, z | nil`: The shore of a lava pool.
- `hazard.goalOutOfLava(x, y, z, lavaIsFloor, nd, fromX, fromZ) -> x, y, z, note | nil, why`: The rule goPoint applies to every goal: a goal in lava becomes its shore.
- `hazard.lethalZone(zone) -> bool`: Does swimming in this zone kill you?
- `hazard.setLethalZones(csv)`: Replace the list of zones whose liquid kills.
- `hazard.new() -> monitor`: Start a hazard watch.
- `hazard.sample(mon, s)`: Put one sample on the watch's track (the oldest fall off after hazard.KEEP samples, 40 seconds).
- `hazard.check(mon, now, ctx) -> hazard | nil`: Does the track show a hazard now? Honours the cooldown and the per-walk limit.
- `hazard.losing(track, now, hp) -> losing, was`: The health rule on its own (pure: no game read).
- `hazard.abort(mon, now)`: Count one abort (the cooldown and the per-walk limit start from here).
- `hazard.safeSpot(mon, x, z, was, back) -> sample, index | nil`: Where to back out to.
- `hazard.wayBack(mon, k) -> points`: The way back to a safe spot: the ground the walk stood on, point by point, which the walk's own retrace follows.
- `hazard.watch(mon, now, ctx) -> hazard | nil`: The walk's own sampler: reads your position, health, fight and swimming (at most three reads) when a sample is due, then checks. A walk calls it every step; call it from your own walking task.
- `hazard.recover(nav, mon, hz, ctx, status, yield) -> backed`: What a walk does on a hazard: keys up, circle the spot, walk back the way it came.
- `hazard.reads.health() -> percent | nil`: The watch's health read. Replace it to test the watch.
- `hazard.reads.combat() -> bool`: The watch's fight read.
- `hazard.reads.swim(px, py, pz) -> swimming, lethal`: The watch's swimming read.
- `hazard.LETHAL_ZONES -> { [short] = true }`: The zones whose liquid kills (setLethalZones replaces them). hazard.ALLOW_LETHAL stays false: a walk that has to go in says so itself with opts.allowLethal. The rule's numbers sit beside it: WINDOW_MS (5 s), LOST_HP (10), SAMPLE_MS (500), COOLDOWN_MS (8 s), MAX (3 a walk), BACK (6 m), CIRCLE_R (6 m), SHORE_REACH (40 m).

#### Module `eb.nav_marks`

Named spots: the places you save to walk back to, and the marks your crew and the map share.

**File:** `lua/eb/nav_marks.lua` in the EB folder

- `marks.set(rec) -> rec | nil, why`: Save a named spot. nav.cmd({ "save", name }) and { "mark", name } do this for where you stand.
- `marks.get(name) -> rec | nil`: One saved spot.
- `marks.resolve(name) -> zone, x, y, z | nil`: Where a named spot is.
- `marks.list(opts) -> recs`: The saved spots, by zone or kind.
- `marks.nearest(zone, x, z, opts) -> rec, distance`: The saved spot nearest a point.
- `marks.remove(name) -> ok, why`: Forget a saved spot.
- `marks.rename(old, new) -> ok, why`: Rename a saved spot.
- `marks.load(force) -> { [lower name] = rec }`: Read the marks file once; later calls answer from what was read.
- `marks.reset()`: Forget what was read, so the next call reads the file again (another box of this PC changed it).
- `marks.count() -> n`: How many marks and saved spots there are.
- `eb-map-marks.json -> { marks = { [lower name] = { name, zone, x, y, z, shared, icon, note, at } } }`: THE MARKS FILE, this PC's own (beside the EB install, never shipped, never replaced by an update): every private spot (shared false: your own bookmark) and every shared mark (shared true: the map draws it and runs can resolve it). Written whole on each change.

#### Module `eb.nav_mesh`

eb nav: the mesh itself - is this zone's mesh loaded, where do you stand on it, the route to a spot, how the last walk ended.

**File:** `lua/eb/nav_mesh.lua` in the EB folder

- `nav_mesh.status(zone) -> ok, text`: One line on a zone's mesh.
- `nav_mesh.attach(reg, deps) -> attached`: Answer eb nav on a registry. EB's start does this once.

#### Module `eb.nav_places`

Spots routes must avoid (blacklist) or may use after all (greenlight), per zone.

**File:** `lua/eb/nav_places.lua` in the EB folder

- `places.blacklist(zone, x, y, z, opts) -> rec | nil, why`: Keep walks out of a circle round a spot (a hole they fall into, a corner they wedge in). nav.cmd({ "bl" }) does it where you stand.
- `places.greenlight(zone, x, y, z, opts) -> rec | nil, why`: Allow a spot again (a greenlight inside a blacklist circle wins).
- `places.listBlacklist(zone) -> circles`: The blacklisted spots of a zone (listGreenlight for the others).
- `places.isGreenlit(zone, x, y, z) -> bool`: Is this spot greenlit?
- `places.avoidCircles(zone) -> circles`: The circles a walk in this zone routes round. Each walk takes them once, at its start - never per frame.
- `places.removeBlacklist(zone, x, z) -> ok`: Lift a blacklist circle.
- `places.removeGreenlight(zone, x, z) -> ok`: Lift a greenlight circle (the blacklist under it is in force again).
- `places.listGreenlight(zone) -> circles`: The greenlit spots of a zone.
- `places.seedAvoids(zone, navd, gx, gy, gz) -> count`: Push the zone's blacklist circles into the router for a walk to the goal. A circle that would swallow the goal is skipped (a goal is never stranded), and nothing is pushed when the goal itself is greenlit. A walk does this once, at its start.
- `places.load(force) -> { blacklist = { circles }, greenlight = { circles } }`: Read the places file once.
- `places.reset()`: Forget what was read.
- `eb-nav-places.json -> { blacklist = { { zone, x, y, z, r, note, at } }, greenlight = { ... } }`: THE PLACES FILE, this PC's own (never shipped): every blacklist circle (routes go round it, default radius 6 m) and every greenlight circle (it lifts a blacklist whose centre it covers). Circles are flat: their height is not used.

#### Module `eb.nav_register`

Wire the walking and travel commands (eb walk, eb follow, eb marks, eb goto, eb route, eb transit) onto a command registry.

**File:** `lua/eb/nav_register.lua` in the EB folder

- `nav_register.wire(reg, deps) -> reg`: Attach the nav and travel handlers. EB's start does this once; a fresh registry (tests, tools) needs it. Every handler answers at once: a walk runs on the pulse and the command says "issued".

#### Module `eb.nav_side`

The good and evil sides of city travel: which side a city is on, and whether a bell ride may cross.

**File:** `lua/eb/nav_side.lua` in the EB folder

- `side.sideOf(name) -> "good" | "evil" | ""`: Which side a city is on.
- `side.otherSide(side, dest) -> stop, why`: Would this trip end in the other side's city? Such a trip stops instead.
- `side.edgeAllowed(side, from, to) -> ok, why`: May this bell ride be taken?
- `side.resolve(info) -> side, from`: Your side, in this order: your bind city's side; else the side your guild hall globe showed you; else the setting; else unknown. An unknown side filters nothing and is never guessed.
- `side.landsIn(name) -> zone | nil`: Where a menu stop takes you (a stop is a destination of its own that lands in a zone).
- `side.sideOfMap(labels) -> side`: Read a side from what a guild hall globe offers (it shows a character its own side's cities). It knows the game's own cities by name: Qeynos for the good side, Freeport and Neriak for the evil side.
- `side.whoKey(side, bind) -> key`: The key a bell map is remembered under: maps speak for the side that read them.
- `side.noBind(bind) -> bool`: Is this character bound nowhere?
- `side.norm(s) -> text`: The form two place names are compared in.
- `side.bellLabel(zone) -> label`: What a bell's map calls a zone.
- `side.labelIs(label, dest) -> bool`: Is this button the destination?
- `side.labelMayBe(label, dest) -> bool`: Could this button be the destination?
- `side.samePlace(a, b) -> bool`: Are two names one place for a bell?
- `side.load(doc, force) -> { zones, stops }`: Load the side data (once; force to reload or to use your own document).
- `side.reset()`: Forget the loaded side data.

#### Module `eb.nav_steer`

How a walk steers along its route a frame at a time: aim a little ahead, turn and go, never cut a corner that is an action (a drop, a jump, a door, a climb). The route as the walker reads it (its arc standing on the floor every 2 m, the progress, the look and the aim) lives in eb.nav_route; eb.nav_steer hands the same functions on.

**File:** `lua/eb/nav_steer.lua` in the EB folder

- `steer.step(nav, plan, st) -> "moving" | "arrived" | "stuck" | why`: ONE step along a planned route: read where you are, aim, set the keys. A walk calls it every frame.
- `steer.steer(nav, ax, az) -> ok`: Turn toward a point and walk.
- `steer.carrotAim(nav, plan, st, px, pz, py) -> x, y, z`: Where to aim this frame.
- `steer.arc(plan) -> lengths`: The route as the walker reads it.
- `steer.isLink(w) -> bool`: Is this corner an action?
- `steer.d2(ax, az, bx, bz) -> metres`: Flat distance.
- `steer.d3(a, b) -> metres`: 3-D distance.
- `steer.linkAction(nav, plan, st, w, px, py, pz) -> "done" | "hold" | nil`: What nav.linkAction does. A take-off is reached within nav.LINK_TAKEOFF across, a jump or a climb then faces the landing and gets ONE tap of the jump key, a drop is walked off its edge, a landing is passed on its own floor.

#### Module `eb.nav_store`

Where EB's navigation data lives and the one door that reads and writes it: the mesh store that ships, and this PC's own nav data.

**File:** `lua/eb/nav_store.lua` in the EB folder

- `store.configure(o)`: Point the nav data at your own roots and files host - a test keeps everything in memory this way.
- `store.root() -> folder | nil`: Where the shipped nav data is.
- `store.localRoot() -> folder | nil`: Where this PC's own nav data is.
- `store.storePath(rel) -> path`: A shipped file's path.
- `store.localPath(rel) -> path`: A local file's path.
- `store.join(base, ...) -> path`: Join path parts.
- `store.readText(path) -> text | nil, why`: Read a nav data file.
- `store.writeText(path, text) -> ok, why`: Write a nav data file.
- `store.readJson(path) -> doc | nil, why`: Read a JSON nav data file.
- `store.writeJson(path, doc) -> ok, why`: Write a JSON nav data file.
- `store.decode(text) -> doc | nil, why`: Read JSON text the way the nav modules do.
- `store.list(dir, glob) -> names`: List a nav data folder.
- `store.fs() -> host`: The nav data's files host.
- `store.json() -> codec`: The nav data's JSON codec.

#### Module `eb.nav_swim`

Swimming on EB's walker: the swim keys, the in-the-water read, the depth rule a walk follows in the water, no dive during a fight, and the group's swim-up hold.

**File:** `lua/eb/nav_swim.lua` in the EB folder

- `swim.want(ctx) -> decision`: The swim corner decision, pure: what to do with the keys at a swim corner.
- `swim.swimming(nav, px, py, pz) -> bool`: Are you in the water? The game's own flag first, else the mesh's liquid surface.
- `swim.surfaceY(nav, px, py, pz) -> y | nil`: How high the water's surface is over you.
- `swim.inWater(nav, st, px, py, pz) -> bool`: The same question, rate-limited for a walk step.
- `swim.inCombat(nav) -> bool`: The fight read the dive rule uses.
- `swim.diveWaits(nav, t) -> bool`: Must a dive wait?
- `swim.underArrived(st, px, py, pz, gx, gy, gz, t, final) -> bool`: Has a goal under water been reached as near as the water allows?
- `swim.walkStep(nav, plan, st, w, px, py, pz) -> nil | "steer" | "spot" | "hold" | "arrived"`: One walk step in the water: sets the swim keys.
- `swim.stepSwim(nav, plan, st, w, px, py, pz) -> "moving" | "no heading"`: One step at a swim corner: walks with swim-up as needed and passes the corner.
- `swim.up(nav, on) -> sent`: Hold or release swim-up for the walk (a latched group hold stays down).
- `swim.down(nav, on) -> sent`: Hold or release swim-down - never while the group holds swim-up.
- `swim.release(nav)`: Both of the walk's swim keys up (a latched group hold stays down).
- `swim.hold(nav, on) -> sent`: The group hold (nav.swimHold calls it).
- `swim.held(nav) -> bool`: Is the group hold on?
- `swim.latches(nav) -> bool`: Does the mover latch swim-up itself?
- `swim.reassert(nav)`: After a walk ends or a stop, press the group's swim-up again on a mover with no latch of its own.
- `swim.walkState(nav) -> state`: Start a walk's swim state (goPoint does this).
- `swim.say(nav, text)`: Send a line to the walk's onStatus.
- `swim.swimUp(nav, ms, yield, height) -> ok, why`: The same as nav.swimUp.

#### Module `eb.nav_swimout`

The swimming recoveries: rise and back out when a walk is stuck in a hole under water, swim up for a while, and say plainly when a goal is in open water the mesh does not reach.

**File:** `lua/eb/nav_swimout.lua` in the EB folder

- `swimout.inOpenWater(nav, px, py, pz, x, y, z) -> bool`: Is a walk the mesh has no route for one into open water? Words only: it moves nothing. It is how a failed walk says "the spot is in open water the mesh does not reach" instead of a bare "no route".
- `swimout.crumb(trip, x, y, z)`: Drop a crumb on the walk's trail (one every few metres, the newest kept).
- `swimout.goodCrumbs(crumbs, stuckY, hx, hy, hz) -> points, metres`: The way back out of a hole.
- `swimout.stuckOut(nav, trip, gx, gy, gz, status, yield) -> handled`: What a walk does when it is stuck while swimming.
- `swimout.swimUp(nav, ms, yield, height) -> ok, why`: Hold swim-up for a while, then let go (nav.swimUp).

**File:** `lua/eb/quest/journal.lua` in the EB folder

- `J:lineState(text, questName) -> "open" | "done" | "gone" | nil, objective`: Where one journal line stands.
- `J:questActive(name) -> true | false | nil`: Is the quest in the journal?
- `J:questCompleted(name) -> true | false | nil`: Has the quest been completed?
- `J:openLines(questName) -> { lines }`: What the quest still asks for.
- `J:questRow(name) -> row | nil`: A quest's tracker row.
- `journal.lineHolds(line, text) -> bool`: The line match on its own.
- `J:rows() -> { { name, parts = { { text, progress } } }, ... }`: Every tracked quest and its objectives, as read now.
- `J:questHeld(name) -> true | false | nil`: Is the quest tracked right now? (questActive also asks the whole journal when the reader can.)

#### Module `eb.quest.quests`

The quest runner's core: the same load / bind / step / stepTarget as eb.quest, without the verb modules loaded, plus the condition view of a run.

**File:** `lua/eb/quest/quests.lua` in the EB folder

- `quests.load(path) -> handle | nil, why`: Read a pack file.
- `quests.bind(deps) -> api`: Bind the core to your adapters.
- `quests.step(run) -> status, info`: Advance the run one bite (api.step calls this).
- `quests.stepTarget(run) -> x, y, z, zone | { actor, zone } | nil`: The current step's target, read without running it.
- `quests.condEnv(run, snap) -> env`: What the run's conditions read against at this snapshot - ctx:env() gives the same for the current tick.

#### Module `eb.quest.verbs`

The pack verb registry: add your own verb, and the small parsers every verb's arguments go through.

**File:** `lua/eb/quest/verbs.lua` in the EB folder

- `verbs.register(keys, fn, about, group) -> nil`: Add a verb every pack can use (the same key registered again replaces it).
- `verbs.refuse(keys, why, group) -> nil`: Mark a verb as refused on purpose: a pack that uses it stops with your reason.
- `verbs.parse(line) -> { verb, key, rest, line } | nil, why`: Split a command line into its verb and arguments.
- `verbs.csv(rest) -> { fields }`: The usual argument splitter.
- `verbs.fields(rest) -> { fields }`: The splitter for verbs whose arguments may come as one quoted string.
- `verbs.loc(rest) -> x, y, z | nil, why`: Read a point from a verb's arguments.
- `verbs.movePoints(rest) -> { { x, y, z }, ... } | nil, why`: Read a move line's points.
- `verbs.waitArgs(rest, kind) -> { main, second, seconds, goOn }`: Read a wait verb's arguments in every shape packs write them.
- `verbs.textHolds(line, needle) -> bool`: The match a chat or emote wait uses.
- `verbs.unquote(s) -> text`: Strip a value's quotes.
- `verbs.supported(verb) -> bool`: The registry's own check (quest.supported is the same).
- `ctx:done(msg) -> "step_done", msg`: This step is finished; the pack goes on to the next one.
- `ctx:work(msg) -> "working", msg`: Still on this step; the handler is called again next tick.
- `ctx:travel(zone) -> "need_travel", zone`: Hand a zone change back to the caller (the zone's own transit).
- `ctx:combat(target) -> "need_combat", target`: Hand a pull back to the caller.
- `ctx:loot() -> "need_loot"`: Hand a loot pass back to the caller.
- `ctx:complete(msg) -> "complete", msg`: The quest is done (or deliberately skipped) here.
- `ctx:block(why) -> "blocked", why`: This step cannot go on now; the caller may recover (the same step is asked again later).
- `ctx:stop(why) -> "blocked", why`: A final stop: the run ends here (a pack that cannot be done as written).
- `ctx:retry(why) -> "working", msg | "blocked", why`: Start this step over.
- `ctx:deadline(ms) -> passed, msLeft`: A time limit for a step that spans ticks.
- `ctx:zone() -> zone`: Where the character is.
- `ctx:skip(n) -> nil`: Skip ahead: the next ctx:done jumps over n steps (what SkipIf verbs do).
- `ctx:jump(i) -> nil`: Go to another step (what RepeatUntil verbs do to loop back).
- `ctx:pos() -> x, y, z`: The character's position.
- `ctx:since(key) -> ms`: Time a phase inside a step.
- `ctx:loading() -> bool`: The mid-load test.
- `ctx:amDriver() -> bool`: Is this box the one that leads?
- `ctx:barrier(name) -> "waiting" | "ready" | "timeout"`: Wait for the whole crew at a mark (through relay.barrier; "ready" on a solo box).
- `ctx:pushRoute(steps, why) -> "working", msg`: Run a list of steps before this one is asked again (what CheckZone does with a pack's own zone routes; a step of them that fails ends that way and this step decides again).
- `ctx:log(fmt, ...) -> nil`: Write one line to the run's log (deps.log), prefixed with the quest and the step number.
- `ctx:zoneEqual(a, b) -> bool`: The zone compare every travel and journal verb uses (eb.quest.gates.zoneEqual over this run's adapters).
- `ctx:inGuildHall() -> bool | nil`: The guild hall test a zone route's "@guildhall" start uses.
- `ctx:env() -> env`: What a condition is read against - pass it to eb.quest.cond.expand or truth in your own verb.
- `ctx:truth(expr) -> true | false | nil`: Read a condition the way a step's condition and the SkipIf verbs do.
- `ctx:groupCount() -> n`: The group size a crew verb checks.
- `ctx:completedDone() -> bool`: The test a repeating verb (a kill, a click, a gather) uses to know its work is finished.
- `verbs.isComment(line) -> bool`: Is this line a comment?
- `verbs.flags(rest) -> rest, found`: Take the -flag words out of a hail ("-peaceful,Warden Fixturo,1" leaves "Warden Fixturo,1").
- `verbs.splitFields(s) -> { fields }`: The splitter the wait verbs use, so a condition like \${If\[\${Me.X} < 400,TRUE,FALSE\]} stays one field.
- `verbs.ported() -> { { verb, about, group }, ... }`: The registry's full verb list (quest.ported is the same).
- `verbs.refusedList() -> { { verb, why, group }, ... }`: The registry's refused list (quest.refused is the same).
- `verbs.dispatch(ctx) -> status, info`: Run one parsed step through its verb's handler. A refused verb or one nobody registered is a final blocked with a clear reason (never guessed, never skipped); a handler that raises is blocked with its message.
- `verbs.expandOptions(tokens) -> { numbers }`: Read a conversation step's reply list: the options to pick, one after another.

#### Module `eb.ui.settings.settings`

The settings catalog: every per-character setting EB's settings window shows - its key, label, kind, unit, range and step - plus the one-click presets and the helpers that step, format and apply a value.

**File:** `lua/eb/ui/settings/settings.lua` in the EB folder

- `S.CATALOG = { { tab, items = { { key, label, kind, unit, step, min, max, group, everyone, cycle, choice } } } }`: The settings, by tab. kind is "bool" (a switch), "num" (a number with unit, step, min and max), "cycle" (one of the values in cycle) or "choice" (one of the values in choice); group "main" shows on top and "adv" folds away. Movement: followDistance, followStop, stickStartDistance, stickStop, campEngageRange, meleeRange, stickDistance, stickCastHoldDistance, combatFollowDistance, combatFollowStop, mageSpellRange, campMeleeEngage, campMaxReturn, meleeChaseMax. Combat: expansion, autoBurnNamed, stayOnNamed, autoAttack, petAttack, faceTarget, groupCombatRange, holdBurns, burnDefaultSec, petHoldOff, mezAuto, tauntInRaid, aeTauntMobs, tauntLoose. Healing: directHealFirstBelow, healBelowThreshold, healPets, healRaid, rezHealFirstBelow, movingHealBelow, raidHealBelow, groupFirstBelow. Popups and loot: acceptRez, acceptInvites, autoLoot, lootWho, lootCorpses, remoteEnabled, remoteRequireGroup, remoteAck, lootChests, lootLottery, lootReach.
- `S.PRESETS = { { name, label, note, settings = { [key] = value }, casting, combat, stick } }`: The one-click presets: "instance" (tight follow, stick on, everything casts), "openworld" (spread out, melee holds, nothing cast until the group is fighting) and "afk" (follow only: no casting, no looting, no popups).
- `S.MIXED`: The value valueFor answers for All when the characters do not agree (format prints it as "mixed").
- `S.item(key) -> row | nil`: Look up one setting.
- `S.preset(name) -> preset | nil`: Look up a preset.
- `S.defaultOf(it) -> value`: A setting's built-in default.
- `S.defaults() -> { [key] = value }`: A full set of defaults (what a new character starts with).
- `S.snap(it, v) -> number`: Make a number fit its setting.
- `S.step(it, current, dir) -> value`: The value one press gives.
- `S.format(it, v) -> text`: A value as the window shows it.
- `S.valueFor(values, who, key, chars) -> value`: The value the window shows for its "Apply to" choice.
- `S.baseValue(values, who, key, chars) -> value`: The value a press steps from.
- `S.targets(it, who, chars) -> { characters }`: Who a press reaches.

#### Module `ebkit.json`

Lossless JSON documents: read a JSON file another program owns, change one value, write it back with every other byte as it was.

**File:** `lua/ebkit/json.lua` in the EB folder

- `json.read(text) -> value | nil, why`: Read a JSON document losslessly.
- `json.write(v) -> text`: Write a document back.
- `json.obj() -> object`: A new object.
- `json.arr(list) -> array`: A new array.
- `json.num(text) -> number`: A number for a document.
- `json.tonum(v) -> number | nil`: Read a number value as a Lua number.
- `json.str(v) -> string | nil`: Read a string value.
- `json.get(o, key) -> value`: Read a key of an object.
- `json.set(o, key, v)`: Set a key of an object. Every other key and value stays as it was.
- `json.del(o, key)`: Remove a key.
- `json.keys(o) -> { keys }`: An object's keys.
- `json.len(a) -> n`: An array's length.
- `json.at(a, i) -> value`: Read an array position.
- `json.insert(a, i, v)`: Insert into an array.
- `json.remove(a, i) -> value`: Remove from an array.
- `json.clone(v) -> copy`: Copy a document (edit the copy, keep the original).
- `json.isObj(v) -> boolean`: Is it an object?
- `json.isArr(v) -> boolean`: Is it an array?
- `json.kind(v) -> "object" | "array" | "string" | "number" | "boolean" | "null"`: The kind of a document value.
- `json.quote(s) -> text`: Write one string the way the codec does (control characters, quotes and backslashes escaped).
- `json.less(a, b) -> boolean`: The key order the codec writes objects in: the same order a browser sorts them, never the computer's locale, so a file reads the same everywhere.

## TLOs

What a script reads from the game and from InnerSpace: how to read it, when EB's game layer already has the answer, and what each read costs.

### TLOs: Reading a TLO

A TLO (top-level object) is a name the game or InnerSpace answers in a data sequence, such as `${Me.Level}`. A script on EB for InnerSpace reads one with ISXLUA's `IS.Parse`, which returns the answer as text.

Most scripts never need to. EB's game layer, `require("eb.platform").game()`, already reads you, your target, your group and the game's windows in batches, and sends the game only members EB has verified to work. Read a TLO yourself for what the game layer does not return.

- **ISXEQ2** brings the game's TLOs: `Me`, `Target`, `Actor`, `Zone`, the game's windows and more.
- **InnerSpace** has its own: the session's name, the loaded extensions, the window in front and InnerSpace's folder.
- **EB** brings two for its own use, `EBNav` and `EBDiag`. A script never reads them: they are folded at the end of the list.

### TLOs: Quick start

Read four members of `Me` in one read, and turn the answers into numbers.

1. Put every member you need into one `IS.Parse`, with a `|` between them. However many members it names, that is one read.
2. Split the answer at each `|`.
3. Turn each number into one with `tonumber`: every answer comes back as text.

Also for this topic, shown in full elsewhere in this file:

- [Snippet: Read several Me members in ONE read](#snippet-read-several-me-members-in-one-read)

### TLOs: The rules every read keeps

1. **Every answer is text.** A number reads `"100"` or `"7.500000"`, a yes or no reads `TRUE` or `FALSE`, and something that is not there (no target, a window that is not open) reads `NULL`.
2. **Test `(exists)` for `TRUE`.** It answers `TRUE` or `NULL`, never `FALSE`.
3. **`IS.Parse` gives `nil` only when it cannot read the line**, or when the answer runs past ISXLUA's 8 KB. A missing target is `NULL`, never `nil`.
4. **Several `${...}` in one `IS.Parse` are one read.** EB keeps to about eight game reads a frame so the game stays smooth. A script's own `IS.Parse` is not counted in that, and EB does not check it: keep your reads few, batch them, and read a few times a second at most.
5. **An info read asks the game's servers.** `ToEffectInfo`, `ToItemInfo` and `ToAbilityInfo` each send a request: read one once per effect, item or ability, keep the answer, and never poll it.
6. **`${Zone.Name}` changes as a zone load starts.** Read the zone once the load is over.
7. **Give your own variables names no TLO has.** Never name a LavishScript variable after a TLO.
8. **TLOs are for EB for InnerSpace.** `IS.Parse` and these TLOs exist only there. The game layer is the same on both EB targets.

### TLOs: Common jobs

#### Test whether something is there

1. Read it with `(exists)`, for example `${ChoiceWindow(exists)}`.
2. Compare the answer with `"TRUE"`. Anything else means it is not there.
3. Read its members only once it is there.

Also for this topic, shown in full elsewhere in this file:

- [Snippet: TRUE or NULL, and numbers as text](#snippet-true-or-null-and-numbers-as-text)

#### Read a member the game layer does not return

1. Find the member in the list below, and check its cost.
2. With the game layer, read it with `game.GetVar("Me.<member>", default)`. It comes back counted, and a member EB has not verified yet is never sent: you get your default.
3. In a helper's own reads, fold it into your one `IS.Parse` with the others you need.

Also for this topic, shown in full elsewhere in this file:

- [Snippet: Read one member the game layer does not return](#snippet-read-one-member-the-game-layer-does-not-return)

#### Check that a read works here, and what it costs

1. In that session's console, type `eb tlocheck <member>` (or `eb tlc`). EB tries the read on this box, and says what came back and how long it took. A read EB holds back is not sent: EB says it is held, and how to let it out.
2. With no member, `eb tlocheck` tries the reads EB itself leans on, each with its answer and its time.
3. `eb fps reads` lists EB's game reads by kind, the costliest first; `eb fps reads reset` starts the count again.

#### See what EB held back

EB holds back game reads and clicks it has not proven to work yet. With the game layer, `game.GateSkipped()` lists what this session wanted to read but EB held back, and a held-back `GetVar` sends nothing and answers your default.

Also for this topic, shown in full elsewhere in this file:

- [Snippet: What GetVar does with a member that is not verified yet](#snippet-what-getvar-does-with-a-member-that-is-not-verified-yet)

The [Lua library](#lua-library) has every tested example that reads a TLO.

### TLOs: What the cost labels mean

| Label | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| cheap | A plain read. Several of them in one `IS.Parse` still cost one read. |
| per-frame budget | It counts toward the about eight game reads EB keeps to each frame. The game layer reads it for you, batched. |
| one command | It sends the game one command, such as a query or a click, not a read. |
| one read per … | Each question, route or page is a read of its own. |
| server request | It asks the game's servers. Read it once and keep the answer; never poll it. |

The words after a label say more: what is cheap, and what is not.

### TLOs: If something goes wrong

| You see | What it means, and what to do |
| --- | --- |
| `NULL` | What you asked about is not there: no target, a window that is not open, an empty group slot. Or the member's name is not right: check it in the list. |
| `(exists)` never reads `FALSE` | It answers `TRUE` or `NULL`. Compare the answer with `"TRUE"`. |
| A number comparison never comes out right | The answer is text. Turn it into a number with `tonumber` first. |
| `IS.Parse` gives `nil` | ISXLUA could not read the line, such as a typo inside `${...}`, or the answer ran past 8 KB. Read less in one go. |
| `game.GetVar` answers your default | EB has not verified that member yet, so it sent nothing. `game.GateSkipped()` lists it, and `eb tlocheck <member>` says it is held. |
| An error on screen when you read an extension's TLO | That extension is not loaded. Read `${Extension[<name>](exists)}` first, and read its TLO only when that says `TRUE`. |
| `${Zone.Name}` names the zone you are going to | It changes as the load starts. Read it again once the load is over. |
| The game stutters while your script runs | Too many reads. Batch them into one `IS.Parse`, read a few times a second at most, and read an info read once per thing. `eb fps` says whether EB itself is the cause. |

### TLOs: Every TLO

#### TLO `Me`

**From:** ISXEQ2 (the game)

**What it is:** Your own character: health, power, level, class, state, group and raid, abilities, maintained spells, effects, equipment, bags and the game's own interface data.

**When to read it:** Prefer game.Me(): it reads the fields a script needs about you in one batch per frame, and asking again in the same frame is free. Read \${Me.\<member>} yourself only for a member the game layer does not return, through game.GetVar("Me.\<member>", default) (typed, counted, and refused when the member is not verified yet), or fold several into one IS.Parse. A raw IS.Parse is for EB for InnerSpace scripts only and is not counted in EB's per-frame budget: keep such reads few and batched.

**What a read costs:** per-frame budget (one read; several members in one read cost the same)

| Member | Type | What it reads | Cost | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ID` | int | Your actor id (the id other actors' Target.ID read when they target you). | cheap | game.Me().id. |
| `Name` | string | Your character's name. | cheap | game.Me().name. |
| `Level` | int | Your adventure level. | cheap | game.Me().level. |
| `SubClass` | string | Your subclass, lower case ("warden"). | cheap | game.Me().subclass. |
| `Class` | string | Your class ("druid" for a warden). | cheap |  |
| `Health` | int | Your health in percent, 0 to 100. | cheap | game.Me().healthPct. |
| `MaxHealth` | int | Your maximum health points. | cheap |  |
| `Power` | int | Your power in percent, 0 to 100. | cheap | game.Me().powerPct. |
| `CurrentPower` | int | Your power points now. | cheap |  |
| `MaxPower` | int | Your maximum power points. | cheap |  |
| `IsHated` | bool | TRUE while a fight is on you - the signal EB's combat follows. | cheap | game.Me().inCombat. Prefer it to InCombat, which stays lit for a while after the fight. |
| `InCombat` | bool | The game's own in-combat flag; it stays TRUE for a while after a fight ends. | cheap |  |
| `CastingSpell` | bool | TRUE while your cast bar runs. | cheap | game.Me().isCasting; the spell's name is GetGameData\[Spells.Casting\].Label (game.CastingName()). |
| `IsMoving` | bool | TRUE while you move. | cheap |  |
| `IsDead` | bool | TRUE while you are dead. | cheap |  |
| `Grouped` | bool | TRUE when you are in a group. | cheap |  |
| `GroupCount` | int | How many are in your group, you included (1 when solo). | cheap |  |
| `IsGroupLeader` | bool | TRUE when you lead the group. | cheap |  |
| `InRaid` | bool | TRUE when you are in a raid. | cheap |  |
| `RaidCount` | int | How many are in the raid. | cheap |  |
| `InGameWorld` | bool | TRUE in the world; FALSE at character select and while a zone loads. | cheap | game.InGame(). |
| `OnMount` | bool | TRUE while you are mounted. | cheap |  |
| `IsStealthed` | bool | TRUE while you are stealthed. | cheap |  |
| `IsInvis` | bool | TRUE while you are invisible. | cheap |  |
| `AutoAttackOn` | bool | TRUE while melee auto-attack is on. | cheap |  |
| `InventorySlotsFree` | int | Free slots in your bags. | cheap | The bags-full check: game.GetVar("Me.InventorySlotsFree", 0). |
| `TSLevel` | int | Your tradeskill level. | cheap | game.TSLevel(). |
| `Arcane` | int | Arcane detriments on you (also Noxious, Elemental, Trauma and Cursed, read the same way). | cheap | game.Me().arcane and the others: the cure check. |
| `NumAbilities` | int | How many abilities your knowledge book holds. | cheap |  |
| `Ability[name]` | ability | One ability by exact name (or Ability\[id,N\]): .ID, .IsReady, .TimeUntilReady, :Use, and .ToAbilityInfo with .Name, .CastingTime, .MaxRange. | cheap for IsReady / TimeUntilReady; ToAbilityInfo is a server request | Use game.AbilityReady and game.Cast: readiness of every ability you use is read in one batch a frame. The ability's name lives in ToAbilityInfo.Name, never on the ability itself. |
| `CountMaintained` | int | How many maintained spells you keep up. | cheap |  |
| `Maintained[n]` | maintained | One maintained spell: .Name, .Target (an actor), .TargetType, .Duration (-1 = no timer). | cheap | game.Maintained() reads every row in one batch. |
| `CountEffects` | int | How many effects are on you. | cheap |  |
| `Effect[n].ID` | int | An effect's id. Read it once per new effect, never every frame. | server request the first time an effect is asked about | game.HasEffect / game.MyEffectNames keep each effect's id and name for you. |
| `Effect[n].Type` | string | Beneficial or Detrimental. | cheap |  |
| `Effect[n].ToEffectInfo.Name` | string | The effect's name. | server request - read it once per effect id and keep it | Never read it for every effect every frame: that floods the server. |
| `Equipment[slot]` | item | A worn item by slot name (primary, chest, food, drink ...) or number: .Name, .ID, .Quantity, .IsReady, .AutoConsumeOn, :Use, :ToggleAutoConsume, and .ToItemInfo.Condition. | cheap for the plain members; ToItemInfo is a server request | game.ConsumableSlot, game.UseItem, game.WorstCondition. |
| `Inventory[ExactName,name]` | item | An item in your bags by exact name (Inventory\[name\] also matches part of a name): the same members as Equipment, and :Equip. Worn gear is never found here. | cheap; ToItemInfo is a server request | game.HasItemExact, game.EquipFromBags. |
| `GetGameData[key]` | gamedata | A value the game's own interface shows, read as .Label - see the Me.GetGameData\[key\] entry for the keys EB has verified. | cheap |  |
| `:QueryInventory` | method | Fill an index:item variable with your items by location: Me:QueryInventory\[MyIndex, Location == "Inventory"\]. | one command, then one read for the rows | game.UsableItems() does this for you. |
| `X` | float | Your position (also Y and Z; Loc gives all three; Heading your facing in degrees). | cheap | game.Me().x / y / z / heading. |

#### TLO `Target`

**From:** ISXEQ2 (the game)

**What it is:** Your current target - any actor member works on it.

**When to read it:** Prefer game.Target(): it comes with the same batched read as game.Me(), so it costs nothing extra. With no target every \${Target...} reads NULL - not an error - and game.Target() answers nil. Target.Target is your target's target (the implied target).

**What a read costs:** per-frame budget (shared with Me in the game layer)

| Member | Type | What it reads | Cost | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ID` | int | The target's actor id (NULL with no target). | cheap |  |
| `Name` | string | The target's name. | cheap |  |
| `Type` | string | NPC, NamedNPC, PC, Corpse, Door, Special, Me ... | cheap | A named reads Type NamedNPC: game.Target().isNamed. |
| `Health` | int | The target's health in percent. | cheap |  |
| `Distance` | float | Metres from you to the target. | cheap |  |
| `Level` | int | The target's level. | cheap |  |
| `Target` | actor | What your target is targeting (Target.Target.Name ...). | cheap |  |
| `IsDead` | bool | TRUE once the target is dead. | cheap |  |

#### TLO `Actor`

**From:** ISXEQ2 (the game)

**What it is:** Any actor in the zone: Actor\[id,N\] by id (the fast, exact form), Actor\[exactname,"Name"\], or Actor\["part of a name"\] (the nearest match).

**When to read it:** Use the game layer's actor functions - ActorPos, ActorDead, ActorHeading, ActorTarget, ControlCount - for one actor (one batched read per actor a frame), and NearestActor / ActorsNear / Lootables / Clickables to search; every search is one game query. Read Actor\[id,N\] yourself only for a member those do not return.

**What a read costs:** per-frame budget (one read per actor; a search is two reads and two commands)

| Member | Type | What it reads | Cost | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ID` | int | The actor's id. | cheap |  |
| `Name` | string | The actor's name. | cheap |  |
| `Type` | string | NPC, NamedNPC, PC, Pet, Corpse, Chest, Door, Special, NoKill NPC ... | cheap | A query term too: 'Type == "NPC" \|\| Type == "NamedNPC"' is how EB means an NPC. |
| `Level` | int | The actor's level. | cheap |  |
| `Health` | int | Health in percent. | cheap |  |
| `Distance` | float | Metres from you. | cheap |  |
| `IsDead` | bool | TRUE once dead. | cheap |  |
| `IsAggro` | bool | TRUE when the actor is aggro on you. | cheap |  |
| `InCombatMode` | bool | TRUE while it is in combat. | cheap |  |
| `IsHeroic` | bool | TRUE for a heroic mob. | cheap |  |
| `IsEpic` | int | How many groups an epic mob is meant for; 0 when it is not epic. A number, not TRUE / FALSE. | cheap |  |
| `EncounterSize` | int | How many mobs are in its encounter. | cheap |  |
| `ConColor` | string | Its con colour against you. | cheap |  |
| `Target` | actor | What the actor is targeting (Actor\[id,N\].Target.ID). | cheap | game.ActorTarget(id). |
| `ThreatToMe` | int | How much it hates you. | cheap |  |
| `Heading` | float | Its facing in degrees (X, Y, Z and Loc give its position). | cheap | game.ActorPos / game.ActorHeading. |
| `CheckCollision` | bool | FALSE when the line from you to it is clear; TRUE when something blocks it. | cheap | game.Target().los and game.MobCasts() rows carry it already. |
| `CollisionRadius` | float | The actor's size around its centre, for melee reach (CollisionScale scales it). | cheap |  |
| `AbilityCastingID` | int | The id of the spell it is casting, 0 when none. | cheap | game.MobCasts() lists the casters with their cast time (AbilityCastingTime). |
| `IsStunnedOrMezzed` | bool | TRUE while it is stunned or mezzed (IsFeared and IsRooted read the same way). | cheap | game.ControlCount(id) adds the three up. |
| `IsSwimming` | bool | TRUE while it swims. | cheap |  |
| `Interactable` | bool | TRUE when it can be clicked (a door, a lever, a chest). | cheap | A query term too; game.Clickables() uses it. |
| `IsMerchant` | bool | TRUE for a merchant or a mender. | cheap |  |
| `NumEffects` | int | How many effects are on the actor. | cheap |  |
| `:DoTarget` | method | Target it: Actor\[id,N\]:DoTarget. An object that cannot be targeted ignores it. | one command | game.TargetActor(id), then game.WaitTarget(id) to confirm. |
| `:DoubleClick` | method | Double-click it: open a door, loot a corpse, hail an NPC. | one command | game.ClickActor(id). |

#### TLO `Me.Group[n]`

**From:** ISXEQ2 (the game)

**What it is:** One slot of your group: Me.Group\[0\] is you, Me.Group\[1\] to Me.Group\[5\] the others. Any actor member works on a member who is in the zone.

**When to read it:** Prefer game.Group(): it reads every slot in one batch a frame and already turns hit points into percent. A member in another zone reads ID 0 and has no distance - check InZone before you act on one.

**What a read costs:** per-frame budget (one read for all five slots in the game layer)

| Member | Type | What it reads | Cost | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Name` | string | The member's name (empty for an empty slot). | cheap |  |
| `ID` | int | The member's actor id; 0 while the member is in another zone. | cheap |  |
| `Class` | string | The member's class. | cheap |  |
| `InZone` | bool | TRUE when the member is in your zone. | cheap |  |
| `HitPoints` | int | The member's health points now (MaxHitPoints is the maximum). | cheap | game.Group() rows carry healthPct. |
| `MaxHitPoints` | int | The member's maximum health points. | cheap |  |
| `Health` | int | The member's health in percent. | cheap |  |
| `CurrentPower` | int | The member's power points (MaxPower is the maximum). | cheap |  |
| `Distance` | float | Metres from you; NULL when the member is in another zone. | cheap |  |
| `IsDead` | bool | TRUE while the member is dead. | cheap |  |
| `Noxious` | int | Noxious detriments on the member (Arcane, Elemental, Trauma and Cursed read the same way). | cheap |  |

#### TLO `Me.Raid[n]`

**From:** ISXEQ2 (the game)

**What it is:** One member of your raid, the same members as a group slot.

**When to read it:** Prefer game.Raid(myGroup, refreshSec): it reads the raid outside your own group at most every half second. Me.RaidCount says how many there are.

**What a read costs:** per-frame budget (cached between refreshes in the game layer)

| Member | Type | What it reads | Cost | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Name` | string | The raid member's name. | cheap |  |
| `Health` | int | Health in percent. | cheap |  |
| `HitPoints` | int | Health points now. | cheap |  |
| `InZone` | bool | TRUE when the member is in your zone. | cheap |  |
| `IsDead` | bool | TRUE while dead. | cheap |  |
| `Class` | string | The member's class. | cheap |  |

#### TLO `Zone`

**From:** ISXEQ2 (the game)

**What it is:** The zone you are in: its display name and its short key.

**When to read it:** \${Zone.Name} names the NEW zone as soon as a zone load STARTS, while the zone is not playable yet: never act on it until EQ2.Zoning reads 0 (game.Zoning() false) and you are in the world (game.InGame()). EB's own libraries key everything by the short name (game.Me().zoneShort).

**What a read costs:** cheap (it comes with the game layer's Me read)

| Member | Type | What it reads | Cost | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Name` | string | The zone's display name. | cheap | game.Me().zone. |
| `ShortName` | string | The zone's short key, the name EB's nav and data use. | cheap | game.Me().zoneShort. |

#### TLO `EQ2`

**From:** ISXEQ2 (the game)

**What it is:** The game itself: whether a zone is loading, and the actor query every search runs on.

**When to read it:** Use game.Zoning() for the zoning check and the game layer's search functions (NearestActor, ActorsNear, Lootables, Clickables, the combat sweep) instead of running EQ2:QueryActors yourself.

**What a read costs:** cheap (Zoning); a query is two commands and two reads

| Member | Type | What it reads | Cost | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Zoning` | int | 0 when no zone is loading; anything else means a load is on. It reads -1 at character select. | cheap | A number, not TRUE / FALSE. game.Zoning() turns it into a boolean (-1 and no answer count as zoning). |
| `:QueryActors` | method | EQ2:QueryActors\[MyIndex, \<query>, ByDist\] fills an index:actor variable with the matching actors, nearest first; read MyIndex.Used and MyIndex\[n\].\<member>. | one command, then one read for the rows | Query terms are actor members with && \|\| ! and == != < > <= >=. EB refuses a query that names a member it has not verified. The game layer's search functions do all of this for you. |

#### TLO `ISXEQ2`

**From:** ISXEQ2 (the game)

**What it is:** The game extension itself.

**When to read it:** A stand-alone script waits for game.IsExtensionReady() (ISXEQ2 loaded and IsReady) before it reads anything. Inside EB the boot has already waited.

**What a read costs:** cheap

| Member | Type | What it reads | Cost | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `IsReady` | bool | TRUE once ISXEQ2 can answer game reads. | cheap | Extension\[ISXEQ2\](exists) only says it is loaded; IsReady says it is ready. |

#### TLO `Me.GetGameData[key]`

**From:** ISXEQ2 (the game)

**What it is:** Values the game's own interface shows, read by key as Me.GetGameData\[\<key>\].Label.

**When to read it:** Only the keys below are verified; any other key is not sent. The two cast bars come with the game layer's Me read (game.CastingName(), game.TargetCasting()).

**What a read costs:** cheap

| Member | Type | What it reads | Cost | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Spells.Casting` | string | The spell on your cast bar ("" when none). | cheap | game.CastingName(). |
| `ImpliedTarget.Casting` | string | The spell your (implied) target is casting ("" when none). | cheap | game.TargetCasting(). |
| `Self.ExperienceCurrent` | string | Your experience on the current level, as the interface shows it. | cheap |  |
| `Self.AscensionLevel` | string | Your ascension level. | cheap |  |
| `Self.MentorLevel` | string | The level you are mentored to. | cheap |  |
| `Self.BindLocation` | string | Where you are bound. | cheap |  |
| `Self.Deity` | string | Your deity. | cheap |  |

#### TLO `ChoiceWindow`

**From:** ISXEQ2 (the game)

**What it is:** The game's yes / no popup: a rez offer, an invite, a zone-in or purchase question.

**When to read it:** Use game.ChoiceWindow() (one batched read). ChoiceWindow(exists) reads TRUE or NULL. EB does not press its buttons yet: the button click is not verified, so a script must not assume a popup was answered.

**What a read costs:** cheap

| Member | Type | What it reads | Cost | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Text` | eq2text | The question, read as ChoiceWindow.Text.GetProperty\[LocalText\]. | cheap |  |
| `Choice1` | string | The first button's label (Choice2 is the second). | cheap |  |
| `Choice2` | string | The second button's label. | cheap |  |
| `IsVisible` | bool | TRUE while it shows. | cheap |  |

#### TLO `ReplyDialog`

**From:** ISXEQ2 (the game)

**What it is:** The classic NPC conversation window and its replies.

**When to read it:** Use game.ReplyDialog() and game.ReplyChoose(n, d): they read the speech bubble first and this window when it is up. The replies are listed through Replies:GetOptions into a collection variable.

**What a read costs:** cheap

| Member | Type | What it reads | Cost | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Text` | string | What the NPC says. | cheap |  |
| `Replies` | eq2listbox | The replies, listed with Replies:GetOptions\[MyCollection\]. | one command, then one read |  |
| `:Choose` | method | Pick reply n: ReplyDialog:Choose\[n\]. | one command |  |

#### TLO `LootWindow`

**From:** ISXEQ2 (the game)

**What it is:** The open loot window: its type and its items.

**When to read it:** Read it only when a loot window is open: the game's loot event (eb.events LootOpened) or game.LootWindow() tells you. Asking with no window up is slow and gets slower in a long session; game.LootWindow() never asks on a quiet frame.

**What a read costs:** cheap while a window is open; slow when none is

| Member | Type | What it reads | Cost | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Type` | string | Free For All, Lotto, Need Before Greed, Leader ... | cheap |  |
| `NumItems` | int | How many items the window holds. | cheap |  |
| `Item[n].Name` | string | The name of item n. | cheap |  |
| `:LootAll` | method | Take every item: LootWindow:LootAll. | one command | eb.economy.lootrules.decideWindow says when "lootall" is the right act. |

#### TLO `RewardWindow`

**From:** ISXEQ2 (the game)

**What it is:** The quest or kill reward window.

**When to read it:** Use game.RewardWindow(): it tells a quest offer from a granted reward and a pick-one reward. Accepting is not verified yet, so game.AcceptReward answers false for now.

**What a read costs:** cheap

| Member | Type | What it reads | Cost | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `NumRewards` | int | How many rewards it holds. | cheap |  |
| `Reward[n]` | reward | One reward row. | cheap |  |

#### TLO `MerchantWindow`

**From:** ISXEQ2 (the game)

**What it is:** An open merchant or mender window: what it sells and what it pays for your items.

**When to read it:** Read it only while the window is open (IsVisible reads TRUE). Close it with game.CloseMerchantWindow().

**What a read costs:** cheap

| Member | Type | What it reads | Cost | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `IsVisible` | bool | TRUE while a merchant window is open. | cheap |  |
| `NumMerchantItemsForSale` | int | How many rows the merchant sells. | cheap |  |
| `MyInventory[name].Quantity` | int | How many of your bag item called name you hold. | cheap |  |
| `MyInventory[name].PriceString` | string | What the merchant pays for one, as "0p,1g,20s,0c". | cheap |  |
| `:Close` | method | Close the window: MerchantWindow:Close. | one command |  |

#### TLO `EQ2UIPage`

**From:** ISXEQ2 (the game)

**What it is:** One page of the game's interface, read element by element: EQ2UIPage\[window,page\].Child\[type,full.name\].

**When to read it:** Always name the element with its full name. Never walk a window's children by number or by type: those reads are unsafe and EB refuses them. The game layer reads the heroic wheel, the travel map, the zone picker and the Persona skills this way for you.

**What a read costs:** cheap per element; batch the elements you need into one read

| Member | Type | What it reads | Cost | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Child` | eq2uipage | A named child element: .Child\[page,\_HUD.heroic\], .Child\[text,\<full name>\]. | cheap |  |
| `GetProperty` | string | A property of the element: GetProperty\[visible\], GetProperty\[LocalText\], GetProperty\[Tooltip\] ... | cheap |  |
| `NumChildren` | int | How many children a named element has. | cheap |  |
| `IsVisible` | bool | TRUE while the page shows. | cheap |  |
| `:LeftClick` | method | Click the element. | one command |  |

#### TLO `Extension`

**From:** InnerSpace

**What it is:** InnerSpace's list of loaded extensions: \${Extension\[ISXEQ2\](exists)} is TRUE when ISXEQ2 is loaded.

**When to read it:** Probe an extension BEFORE you read its TLO: reading the TLO of an extension that is not loaded prints an error on screen. EB's own nav checks its extension this way. Remember: (exists) reads TRUE or NULL, never FALSE.

**What a read costs:** cheap

#### TLO `Session`

**From:** InnerSpace

**What it is:** This InnerSpace session's name (\${Session}, "is1", "is2" ...) - the id the crew relay knows a box by.

**When to read it:** game.SessionName() reads it for you.

**What a read costs:** cheap

#### TLO `Display`

**From:** InnerSpace

**What it is:** The game window's own state.

**When to read it:** game.IsForeground() reads Foreground for you.

**What a read costs:** cheap

| Member | Type | What it reads | Cost | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Foreground` | bool | TRUE when this game window has the focus. | cheap |  |

#### TLO `LavishScript`

**From:** InnerSpace

**What it is:** InnerSpace's own information, such as the folder it runs from.

**When to read it:** Never hard-code a folder: build a path from LavishScript.HomeDirectory, or from EB's own install folder (require("eb.platform").root()). Never name a LavishScript variable after a TLO - the variable hides the TLO and every script that reads it breaks.

**What a read costs:** cheap

| Member | Type | What it reads | Cost | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `HomeDirectory` | string | The InnerSpace folder this session runs from. | cheap |  |

#### TLO `EBNav`

**From:** EB

**What it is:** EB's own mesh router, loaded as an InnerSpace extension on EB for InnerSpace. It plans routes over EB's own mesh for the zone you are in.

**When to read it:** Scripts never read EBNav directly: use eb.navd (the same as require("eb.platform").nav()) or EB's walker (eb.nav). eb.navd checks that the extension is loaded before it asks anything, loads the zone's mesh off the frame, and turns every answer into plain Lua tables. When the extension is not there it says why instead of erroring.

**What a read costs:** one read per question; a whole route is one read

| Member | Type | What it reads | Cost | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Version` | string | Which version of the router answers (eb.navd checks it once). | cheap |  |
| `Current` | string | Which zone's mesh is loaded. | cheap |  |
| `LoadAsync` | string | Start loading a zone's mesh in the background (eb.navd.prepare does this). | cheap; the load itself runs off the frame |  |
| `Poll` | string | How a background load is going. | cheap |  |
| `Path` | string | One route between two points, as a list of points (eb.navd.path / pathChained). | one read per route |  |
| `Page` | string | The rest of a very long route. | one read per page |  |

#### TLO `EBDiag`

**From:** EB

**What it is:** EB's own diagnostics, loaded as an InnerSpace extension on EB for InnerSpace: how this session ends (where the game stopped if it went down, a freeze it never comes back from), the last freeze and where the stuck thread was, and what this PC is (the system, the processor, the memory, the graphics adapters, memory integrity).

**When to read it:** Scripts never read EBDiag directly: eb fps machine, eb fps stalldump and eb debugreport show what it knows, through eb.ui.cmds.diag_native, which checks that the extension is loaded before it asks anything and keeps the answers that do not change. EB Boxer has the same built in (eb.diag).

**What a read costs:** one read per question; the machine and the earlier sessions' notes are read once

| Member | Type | What it reads | Cost | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Version` | string | Which version answers, and this process's id. | cheap |  |
| `Machine` | string | The system and its build, the processor, the memory, the graphics adapters and memory integrity (HVCI). | cheap; read once, the facts are gathered off the frame |  |
| `Hang` | string | This session's last freeze: how long, whether it was EB's own frame, where the stuck thread was. | cheap |  |

## Commands

Type a command in a session's InnerSpace console, or send it from a script: IS.Execute with luacall EBISX_cmd and the words after eb. A word in front of any command: all | others | to \<who> | local. With no word the command is for this box only.

- `local`: this box only (what a command is with no word in front)
- `all`: every box, this one too
- `others`: every box but this one
- `to`: the boxes the who names: a box (is2), a character, a class, an archetype (fighter | priest | mage | scout) or @role

What an argument takes, by its type:

- `flag`: a word that is there or not (go, -bags)
- `onoff`: on | off (some rows take status or toggle, or words of their own)
- `int`: a whole number
- `float`: a number
- `string`: free text (as the last arg it takes the rest of the line)
- `enum`: one word of a list
- `zone`: a zone: its short name or its name
- `actor`: an actor's id or name
- `item`: an item's name
- `ability`: an ability's name
- `member`: a group or raid member's name
- `coords`: x y z (three numbers, or x,y,z)
- `preset`: a saved preset's name
- `path`: a file's path

### Commands: Core / control

What every box answers: status, stop, pause and resume, help, reload.

- `eb help [topic]`: What EB's commands are: with no word the groups, with a group's word its commands, with a command's word what it does and what it takes.
  - Also typed as: `h`, `?`.
  - This box only.
  - `topic` (string; optional): a group or a command; nothing lists the groups
- `eb status [what]`: This box in a few lines: where it is, what it is doing, its health and power. crew, goal, nav or combat says that part alone; patch is the quick read after a game patch, PASS or FAIL for each read.
  - Also typed as: `s`.
  - This box only.
  - `what` (enum; optional; one of bot | crew | goal | nav | combat | patch; default bot): which part
- `eb stop`: The kill switch: stops quests, instance runs, walking and goals on this box (or the crew). The fight goes on, so you stay alive. eb resume starts again.
  - Also typed as: `stopall`, `abort`.
  - For the crew: `all`, `others`, `to`.
- `eb freeze`: Stop everything at once and stay stopped: the walk, the follow, a run or a quest line end (as eb stop does), the cast going now is cancelled, and nothing is cast until eb resume lets it all go again. eb relay mygroup freeze stops your whole group: the Stop group button of the MCP and the mini.
  - Also typed as: `halt`.
  - For the crew: `all`, `others`, `to`.
- `eb end <system>`: End one thing EB is running and leave the rest: the quest line, the instance run, a walk, the hunt, crafting, gathering - or all of them. irc leaves the IRC channel and server this box is on (eb irc end); all leaves IRC as it is.
  - Also typed as: `kill`.
  - For the crew: `to`.
  - `system` (enum; required; one of quest | ic | nav | hunt | craft | harvest | all | irc): what to end
- `eb pause [state]`: Hold quests, instance runs, walking and goals where they are (the fight goes on). Pause again, or eb resume, to go on.
  - Also typed as: `hold`, `holdup`.
  - For the crew: `all`, `others`, `to`.
  - `state` (onoff; optional; one of pause | resume | toggle | status; default toggle): pause | resume | toggle (pause when running, resume when paused) | status
- `eb resume`: Go on after a pause, or after eb stopall (the same as eb pause resume).
  - Also typed as: `letsgo`, `go!`.
  - For the crew: `all`, `others`, `to`.
- `eb afk [state]`: Away mode: EB keeps the character from being logged out for idling, and the crew sees it as away.
  - For the crew: `all`, `others`, `to`.
  - `state` (onoff; optional; one of on | off | toggle | status; default status): on | off | toggle | status
- `eb reload [module]`: Load EB again in this session - the game stays up and the character stays logged in. With a word, one part only: nav, invites, stack or poi. A box in a run keeps the ask and loads again by itself once the run is over (eb reload cancel or eb stopall drops it); eb all reload: each box decides for itself.
  - Also typed as: `r`.
  - For the crew: `all`, `others`, `to`.
  - `module` (string; optional): nothing = EB itself; nav | invites | stack | poi = that part's files, read again; cancel = drop a reload kept until a run is over

### Commands: Combat

The fight: casting on and off, cures, rezzes, interrupts, heroic opportunities, holds, the cast stack, pets, mounts, and the part each box plays (tank / dps / subtle / heal).

- `eb combat [state]`: Casting on or off on this box. Off: EB casts nothing and keeps watching. status says the stack and every switch. EB fights only what it can win and never attacks a guard.
  - Also typed as: `fight`.
  - For the crew: `all`, `others`, `to`.
  - `state` (onoff; optional; one of on | off | status; default status): on | off | status
- `eb autohunt [cmd] [list]`: Hunt by a saved list (the Auto Hunt window's): pull the nearest mob EB can win against - the list's names first, and with no names any mob it may kill, never a guard - rest, move on around where it started, along its waypoints or inside its area, and stop at its kills or minutes, a zone line, until the bags hold so many of an item, until a quest updates, or at the third death in the group (deaths:\<n>). No pull while a member is down; one up again elsewhere is called back. group: the others follow. reach:\<m>: only what can be reached within that many metres walked on the mesh, the nearest that way first; pull:body: each pull is walked at until it comes (never an attack), then back to the camp. import makes your old Auto-Hunt routes hunt lists; rename renames a list; move puts a list in a folder of yours (list and folders show them by folder). options \<list> says a list's hunt options, options \<list> \<option> \<value> sets one in the list: pulls (the abilities that open each fight, first ready first), group_hp / group_power (no pull while anyone of the group is under that %), pause_chest (no pull while an Exquisite Chest lies near), delay_after (seconds after a fight before the next pull; on = 3), prebuff (a moment for the buffs before each pull), ignore_collision (kept; EB reads no sight line).
  - Also typed as: `ah`, `hunt`.
  - For the crew: `all`, `others`, `to`.
  - `cmd` (enum; optional; one of on | off | status | list | area | route | patrol | import | rename | move | folders | options; default status): on | off | status | list | area | route | patrol | import | rename | move | folders | options
  - `list` (string; optional): a saved hunt list, then its words: kills:\<n> minutes:\<n> until:\<n>:\<item> (\_ for a space) until:quest\[:\<quest>\] deaths:\<n> reach:\<metres on the mesh> pull:body group; import: an old route's zone \[overwrite\]; rename: \<list> to \<new name>; move: \<list> to \<folder> (none: out of it); options: \<list> \[\<option> \<value>\] - pulls (abilities split by |), group_hp, group_power, pause_chest, delay_after, prebuff, ignore_collision
- `eb cures [state]`: Cure detriments by themselves (arcane, noxious, elemental, trauma, curse), the worst first; across the crew only one box cures a target.
  - Also typed as: `cure`.
  - For the crew: `all`, `others`, `to`.
  - `state` (onoff; optional): on | off | status
- `eb interrupts [state]`: Interrupt and dispel by themselves, on the casts and buffs being watched.
  - For the crew: `all`, `others`, `to`.
  - `state` (onoff; optional): on | off | status
- `eb rez [state]`: Rez fallen members by themselves; across the crew only one box rezzes a target. now: rez the dead member at once, whatever the switch says.
  - For the crew: `all`, `others`, `to`.
  - `state` (onoff; optional; one of on | off | status | toggle | now): on | off | status | toggle | now
- `eb ho [cmd]`: Heroic opportunities: on, off, status (it also says when this box cannot read the wheel yet); do starts one now; exclude lists the abilities kept out of them; cancel cancels a starter that is up (held until its live proof).
  - Also typed as: `heroicop`.
  - For the crew: `all`, `others`, `to`.
  - `cmd` (enum; optional; one of on | off | status | do | exclude | cancel; default status): on | off | status | do | exclude | cancel
- `eb mez [state]`: Crowd control: mez or root the adds and renew it before it runs out - never the mob being killed.
  - Also typed as: `cc`, `crowdcontrol`.
  - For the crew: `all`, `others`, `to`.
  - `state` (onoff; optional): on | off | status
- `eb embargo [kind] [name] [secs]`: Hold an item, an ability or a tag for some seconds so the boxes take turns: one box's use holds it on the others. list shows the holds, clear ends them. A bare tag (eb embargo \<tag> \[secs\]) holds the cast-stack rows that carry it while it is up.
  - For the crew: `all`, `others`, `to`.
  - `kind` (enum; optional; one of item | ability | tag | list | clear; default list): item | ability | tag | list | clear
  - `name` (string; optional): the item, ability or tag (quote a name of several words)
  - `secs` (int; optional): for how many seconds (30 when left out)
- `eb allow <tag> [secs]`: Open an ALLOW tag for a while: the cast-stack rows that wait for it (its ATag rows) cast while it is up, then it is as it was. One box opening it reaches the group. \`eb tags\` explains every tag.
  - For the crew: `all`, `others`, `to`.
  - `tag` (string; required): the cast-stack allow tag (one word)
  - `secs` (int; optional): for how many seconds (10 when left out)
- `eb listen <tag>`: Fire a tag now so its LISTEN rows cast: the rows held waiting for it go once, on this box and the group (an opener row does this by itself when it casts). \`eb tags\` explains every tag.
  - For the crew: `all`, `others`, `to`.
  - `tag` (string; required): the cast-stack tag to fire (one word)
- `eb tag <name> [state]`: Switch one cast-stack tag on or off by hand: its rows are held when it is off. \`eb tags\` lists them and explains each; \`eb allow\` / \`eb embargo\` raise a tag for a while instead.
  - For the crew: `all`, `others`, `to`.
  - `name` (string; required): the cast-stack tag (one word)
  - `state` (onoff; optional): on | off | status
- `eb dnc [name]`: The do-not-cancel list: maintained spells EB must never drop. A name puts it on the list or takes it off; nothing lists them.
  - Also typed as: `donotcancel`.
  - This box only.
  - `name` (string; optional): a maintained spell
- `eb stance [name]`: A fighter's stance alone: def, off, subtle, or status. (eb go also sets the damage rows and the tank.)
  - Also typed as: `ts`.
  - For the crew: `all`, `others`, `to`.
  - `name` (string; optional): def | off | subtle | status
- `eb go [what]`: One word sets the part this box plays. tank: a fighter's defensive stance and its threat proc on, its offensive stance and Subtle Strikes off. dps: a fighter's offensive stance on, its defensive stance and threat proc off; every class's damage rows go. subtle: as dps, with Subtle Strikes on. heal: a priest's damage rows wait, so heals, cures and buffs go first. status (or nothing): what this box is set to. eb all go dps sets the whole crew, each box for itself.
  - For the crew: `all`, `others`, `to`.
  - `what` (string; optional): tank|dps|subtle|heal|swap|status - any other word is a place: travel there (eb goto)
- `eb rogue [cmd] [name]`: A swashbuckler or brigand takes the tank's part. tank: on the rogue's box its defensive stance goes up, its taunts go first and its dehates off (read off its own ability check: eb abilities export), and the crew heals it as the tank and points its hate buffs on the tank at it; typed on another box, the line goes to the rogue's box. dps: every row back as it was, the stance off, and the box that tanked before takes the part back. status: what this box is set to.
  - For the crew: `all`, `others`, `to`.
  - `cmd` (enum; optional; one of tank | dps | status; default status): tank | dps | status
  - `name` (string; optional): tank: the rogue's character (nothing: this box when it is a swashbuckler or brigand, else the group's first)
- `eb assist [who] [follow] [dist]`: Fight what that one fights: tank = the group's tank (the one eb go tank names, else the group's first fighter), me = the box the line came from, a name, or off for no one. With follow, this box goes with that one too - the tank's own box stays where it is. eb relay mygroup assist tank follow is the MCP's Follow + assist tank: every box of your group goes with the tank and fights what it fights.
  - For the crew: `all`, `others`, `to`.
  - `who` (actor; optional): tank (the group's tank), me (the box the line came from), a character's name, or off (no one); nothing says who this box assists now
  - `follow` (flag; optional): follow: follow that one too (a camp spot this box holds lets go)
  - `dist` (int; optional): with follow: how many metres behind, 2 to 20 (nothing: this character's own follow distance)
- `eb encounter [cmd] [name]`: A scripted fight for a named or a raid boss - what to do when it does something: on, off, status, load one, list them. load with no name loads the setup for the named this box fights, else for the nearest named here. fights says the boss fight files EB's instance library holds for this zone; fight lays one on this box with no run going - its kill order and setting for that boss's whole fight, and its fight rules (cures, casts, lines said) answered here.
  - Also typed as: `enc`.
  - For the crew: `all`, `others`, `to`.
  - `cmd` (enum; optional; one of on | off | status | load | list | fight | fights; default status): on | off | status | load | list | fight | fights
  - `name` (string; optional): the fight's file (load with none: the one for the named you fight, else the nearest named); fight / fights: the boss's name
- `eb setups [kind] [state]`: Whether your encounter setups run by themselves, by the kind of zone: heroic = every zone that is not a raid zone (heroic and solo instances, overland, cities), raid = a raid zone. In a zone whose kind is on, every setup installed on this box is laid on, each while its named is the mob; going into a zone whose kind is off takes them off again (a setup you load by hand stays). Both off is the default: nothing is laid on by itself. Kept for this character.
  - For the crew: `all`, `others`, `to`.
  - `kind` (enum; optional; one of heroic | raid | all | status; default all): heroic | raid | all | status
  - `state` (onoff; optional): on | off | toggle (nothing: say how it stands)
- `eb raidreact [cmd] [arg]`: Ready answers to a boss's moves: on, off (all, or one by its place), status / list; view / edit opens the Raid React window; rec starts the fight scanner (pick a cast into a reaction there); test \<n> sets one off now. stop holds every reaction that is on until arm (one switched by hand stays as it is). timer \<n> \<every> \[\<early>\]: that reaction also goes off on its own clock in a fight, so many seconds early - every so often from the pull, and from each time it was seen. import lists your old reactions files and brings one (or all) in, off; grab lists the detriments that landed on you here and makes a reaction to the cast that likely put one on. Sharing them through the hub stays off (upload says so). The answers are the crew's: on or off on one box is on or off for every box.
  - Also typed as: `rr`.
  - This box only.
  - `cmd` (enum; optional; one of on | off | status | view | list | rec | edit | test | grab | import | upload | arm | stop | timer; default status): on | off | status | view | list | rec | edit | test | grab | import | upload | arm | stop | timer
  - `arg` (string; optional): test / on / off: a reaction's place in the list (or its name); timer: \<n> \<every seconds> \[\<seconds early>\] or \<n> off; import: a file's number or all; grab: a detriment's number
- `eb mobcasts [cmd]`: What the mobs near you are casting: watch it, record it, list it.
  - Also typed as: `tc`, `npccasts`.
  - This box only.
  - `cmd` (enum; optional; one of on | off | record | watch | list; default list): on | off | record | watch | list
- `eb helpers [cmd] [arg]`: Class helpers in plain words: when someone drops under a %, is down or is feared, a buff of yours is not on, the mob drops under a %, my pet drops under a %, my savagery is at a level, the game says a line ("when the game says \<words>"), or the fight starts - cast an ability on them. list numbers them (your own, then the ones your class tab switches on), add one, remove one, on / off (all, or one by its number - kept for this character), test one (what it would do now and why: nothing is sent), up / down (the order your own are tried in), export / import a share code (EBHELP1:..., also in the class's share file), chains (the chains made in Tags & Helpers, and a dry run of one); nothing (or window) opens the Tags & Helpers window.
  - Also typed as: `helper`.
  - For the crew: `all`, `others`, `to`.
  - `cmd` (enum; optional; one of list | add | remove | on | off | status | window | test | up | down | export | import | chains): list | add | remove | on | off | status | window | test | up | down | export | import | chains
  - `arg` (string; optional): add: the helper in words (when the tank drops under 40%, cast "\<ability>" on them); remove / test / up / down / on / off: its number (or its ability); export: one number, none = all your own lines; import: the code (none = this class's share file); chains: test \<n> for a dry run of one
- `eb classtab [option] [value]`: This character's class tab as EB's own settings: every box of the tab EB acts on, with its value, whether it is set in EB or the profile's, and what EB does with it; an option and a value sets it for this character (the profile file is never changed) and the fight takes it at once; reset puts the profile's box back; window opens the Cast Stack window on its Class tab. Warlock myth (Negative Void on against one mob, off against an encounter, around Dark Siphoning, Apocalypse, Absolution, Dark Nebula and Decimation), mythds, mythsay; Ranger and Assassin exploit (Exploit Weakness when the game says a weakness is seen), the Ranger's focusaim, wreakhavoc, tracingshot (each taken down once up); Brigand swath; Troubador potm, Coercer ir, Dirge cob (another player's call holds yours); Coercer pe, penocombat, peoutside; Conjuror crystal (Crystal Blast when Crystalline Destruction procs) and dimstorage, Necromancer dimstorage; Dirge confrontfear; Inquisitor verdictepic, verdictepichp, verdictnonepic, verdictnonepichp.
  - Also typed as: `classopts`.
  - For the crew: `all`, `others`, `to`.
  - `option` (string; optional): one of this character's class tab options (nothing or list: every one; window: the Cast Stack window's Class tab)
  - `value` (string; optional): on | off | toggle, the pick, the words or the number it takes; reset = the profile's own box again
- `eb scan [cmd]`: The fight scanner: keep an eye on chosen mobs - mark one, clear the marks; adds lists the mobs that joined fights here; lines lists what the fights here said (a mob's words, its emotes, the warnings), kept while recording.
  - Also typed as: `fightscan`.
  - This box only.
  - `cmd` (enum; optional; one of on | off | status | mark | clear | adds | lines; default status): on | off | status | mark | clear | adds | lines
- `eb flag [name] [state]`: The fight's named switches (ae, pbae, encounter, nothreat, namedca, dumbfires, petassist, casting, cures, rez, interrupts, mez, ho, joust, face, hooffensive, dispel, combos, smartae, smartencounter, los, selectivecures, selectivegroupcures, autosetups, chatevents, queuenext, healinterrupt), any cast-stack tag, or one cast-stack row by its name: on, off, or what it is set to. dispel: the cast stack's dispel rows; combos: an ascension starter's combo goes next; smartae: a point-blank or targeted area attack waits until 2 or more mobs stand within its radius (around me, or around its target); smartencounter: an encounter attack waits until its target's encounter has 2 or more (the profile's own counts when it has them); los: the line-of-sight check before an attack; selectivecures / selectivegroupcures: single-target / group cures only for the types switched on (stcure_arcane ... groupcure_trauma; none on: that cure is not used); autosetups: every encounter setup installed is laid on, each while its named is the mob; chatevents: the coordination rules that answer a line someone says; queuenext: while a cast runs, the next ability of the cast stack is queued in the game so it fires the moment the cast ends (on; one queued at a time); healinterrupt: an attack of EB's that is casting is cancelled when a heal or a cure of the cast stack is needed now, and that heal or cure goes at once (off).
  - This box only.
  - `name` (string; optional): a switch, a tag or a row's name; nothing lists the switches
  - `state` (onoff; optional): on | off (nothing: say how it stands)
- `eb cs [cmd] [arg]`: Your cast stack: show it, set the camp, clear it, import a cast stack file (new or old format, tags kept), filter, archive, share. profile \<name> switches the profile of this character's cast stack file EB casts from (EB's own pick, kept for this character: the file is never written; asked in a fight, it is taken once the fight is over), profile default goes back to the file's own, profile alone says which it casts from and which the file has. infuse swaps every Mount / Mercenary / Familiar Infusion row for the infusion this character holds now (one per kind, its Type and conditions kept) and saves; infuse all does it on every box, each with its own.
  - Also typed as: `caststack`.
  - This box only.
  - `cmd` (enum; optional; one of show | profile | camp | rcs | clear | import | archive | share | infuse | filter; default show): show | profile | camp | rcs | clear | import | archive | share | infuse | filter
  - `arg` (string; optional): a profile, a file or a filter; after profile: a profile's name in this character's cast stack file, or default; after infuse: all (every box)
- `eb cast <ability> [who]`: Cast one ability of this character's cast stack now, by name: the row says what kind of spell it is - an attack goes only at the mob EB fights, a heal or a buff on the member named (eb cast "Mending Touch" on Tank). A name that is no row of the cast stack is refused. eb cast stop stops casting: the abilities the game has queued are cleared and the cast going now is cancelled.
  - For the crew: `all`, `others`, `to`.
  - `ability` (string; required): the ability, in quotes when it has several words; stop = stop casting
  - `who` (string; optional): on \<member> (a heal or a buff)
- `eb cancel <spell>`: Cancel a spell of yours that is up now (a maintained spell: a stance, a toggle, a buff), by its name. Only a cancel the game took is said as done.
  - Also typed as: `unbuff`.
  - For the crew: `all`, `others`, `to`.
  - `spell` (string; required): a spell of yours that is up, by its name (any rank)
- `eb tagfor <tag> <secs> [how]`: A cast-stack tag for a while: embargo holds the rows that carry it, allow lets them go (the rows that wait for it), for so many seconds - then it is as it was.
  - For the crew: `all`, `others`, `to`.
  - `tag` (string; required): the cast-stack tag (one word)
  - `secs` (int; required): for how many seconds
  - `how` (enum; optional; one of allow | embargo; default embargo): allow | embargo
- `eb acs [xpack]`: Put this character's class adornment set on: the set for its class, else its class group, else its archetype, the highest level its own level allows - from the bags first, then the Adornment Depot in reach. A word takes only that set: an expansion, a preset, or your own family (eb adorn own). The class set in EB's settings comes first when there is one. eb all acs: every box puts on the set of its own class.
  - Also typed as: `applyclassset`.
  - For the crew: `all`, `others`, `to`.
  - `xpack` (string; optional): an expansion (RoK, TSO), a preset (TSOx2) or your own family; nothing = the set your class and level take
